Introduce WordKeywordGroup and add unit tests for keyword and group handling

This PR implements WordKeywordGroup and expands test coverage for keyword parsing and explicit group behavior. Changes include:

- Added/updated src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/model/groups/WordKeywordGroup.java
  - Implements group matching based on words in a specified field.
  - Supports splitting keywords by a custom separator or by whitespace (onlySplitWordsAtSeparator flag).
  - Respects case sensitivity option and provides add/remove methods that update the entry keyword field via KeywordList.
  - Implements equals, hashCode and deepCopy.

- Added tests for keyword parsing: src/test/java/net/sf/jabref/model/entry/KeywordListTest.java
  - Verifies parsing behavior with different delimiters, whitespace handling, duplicate suppression, bracketed terms, and formatting via getAsString.

- Added tests for explicit groups: src/test/java/net/sf/jabref/model/groups/ExplicitGroupTest.java
  - Ensures correct appending to and preservation of the GROUPS field when adding/removing groups.
  - Adds tests that prevent accidental removal when a group name appears as part of another token (addresses #2334).
  - Verifies that group matching respects whole-word/phrase boundaries (addresses #1873) and correctly handles bracketed group names (addresses #2394).

- Updated CHANGELOG.md (Unreleased) to document relevant changes and fixes.

This change fixes group-matching edge cases (brackets and partial-name matches) and improves keyword handling and test coverage to prevent regressions.

Summary:
Enable casing for entry types so the system can preserve and/or enforce a specific letter-case format (e.g., PascalCase, camelCase, kebab-case) for entry type identifiers.

What this PR does:
- Adds support for specifying and applying a casing strategy for entry types.
- Updates serialization/deserialization so entry type names are emitted in the configured case.
- Adjusts validation to accept or normalize incoming entry type identifiers according to the casing policy.
- Adds configuration option (default: preserve existing behavior) to opt into casing enforcement or normalization.
- Includes unit tests covering the new casing behavior and edge cases.

Why:
Some consumers rely on a consistent casing convention for entry type identifiers (for display, code generation, or API contracts). Allowing explicit casing control removes ambiguity and enables interoperability with external systems that expect a particular format.

Compatibility and migration:
- Default behavior preserves current casing to avoid breaking existing consumers.
- No database schema changes are required.
- When enabling a casing policy, existing entry type identifiers will be normalized on read/write according to the selected strategy; review integrations that may be sensitive to identifier changes.

How to test:
1. Enable a casing policy in configuration (e.g., camelCase or kebab-case).
2. Create and fetch entry types via API/UI and verify identifiers follow the configured case.
3. Submit entry type identifiers in different cases and verify they are accepted or normalized according to policy.
4. Run the updated unit test suite.

Notes:
- The feature is opt-in to minimize risk.
- Documentation will be updated with available casing strategies and examples.

Fix AuthorListParser#parse for two authors separated by a comma

Summary
- Fixes bug where an author field like {Hans-Joachim Habermann, Frank Leymann} was parsed incorrectly (treated as a single author containing a comma) instead of being converted to two BibTeX authors.

Background / Problem
- Some import sources (e.g. ebook.de) produce BibTeX with authors separated by a comma but without an "and". Example input:
  @book{9783110702125,
    Author = {Hans-Joachim Habermann, Frank Leymann},
    ...
  }
- The existing AuthorListParser treated this as one author (with an internal comma) rather than two authors.

What I changed
- Added a new heuristic in AuthorListParser#parse to detect the common two-author pattern when authors are comma-separated but no explicit "and" is present. In that case the parser splits into two authors and normalizes each into the expected "Last, First" form, then joins them with " AND ".
- Ensures the concrete example is converted to: {Habermann, Hans-Joachim AND Leymann, Frank}.

Tests and documentation
- Added unit tests covering the two-author comma case and a few related edge cases to ensure robustness.
- Added a CHANGELOG.md entry describing the user-visible fix.

text:
Closes #14237

Summary

This PR fixes an issue where keyboard shortcuts could not be edited from Preferences → Keyboard shortcuts. The problem was that KeyEvent instances were consumed by global application shortcuts before they reached the shortcut editor in KeyBindingsTab, so pressing keys did not update the selected shortcut and edited changes were not persisted.

What I changed

- Added a key event filter in KeyBindingsTab so the TreeTableView reliably receives key presses.
- Forward key events to the ViewModel (setNewBindingForCurrent) so the selected binding is updated immediately.
- Ensure edited shortcuts are correctly persisted by syncing the repository into GuiPreferences.
- Added/updated a JUnit test that verifies the binding update behavior.

Testing steps

1. Open JabRef → Preferences → Keyboard shortcuts.
2. Select any shortcut entry (e.g., “Close library”).
3. Press a new key combination (e.g., Ctrl+Shift+L).
4. Click Save.
5. Restart JabRef.
6. Verify that:
   - The new shortcut appears in the list.
   - The shortcut works in the application (e.g., Ctrl+Shift+L closes the library).

Notes

- UI appearance remains unchanged; this only affects event routing and persistence logic.
- JUnit coverage added to validate the fix.

- Add unit tests: ScholarArchiveFetcherTest to verify search and parsing behavior and ManageStudyDefinitionViewModelTest updated/added to ensure ScholarArchive appears in the list of available catalogs for systematic literature reviews.

text:
Add JabRefDialogService: a JavaFX-based implementation of DialogService providing consistent dialog and notification behavior across the UI.

Key features:
- Implements a wide range of dialogs: information, warning, error (with ExceptionDialog overloads), confirmations (including customizable button labels), custom dialogs and choice/input dialogs.
- createDialogWithOptOut: supports dialogs with an opt-out checkbox and a callback for handling the user choice.
- shortenDialogMessage utility to limit long dialog messages to a configurable DIALOG_SIZE_LIMIT.
- Progress support:
  - showProgressDialog wraps a Task into a ControlsFX ProgressDialog and wires cancel behavior.
  - showBackgroundProgressDialogAndWait displays a TaskProgressView bound to a StateManager to monitor background tasks, shows icons for BackgroundTask and auto-closes when no tasks are running.
- File and directory choosers:
  - showFileSaveDialog, showFileOpenDialog, showFileOpenDialogAndGetMultipleFiles and showDirectorySelectionDialog configured via FileDialogConfiguration and DirectoryDialogConfiguration (initial directory, initial filename, extension filters). The selected extension filter is propagated back to the configuration.
  - showFileOpenFromArchiveDialog opens a ZIP FileSystem and delegates to ZipFileChooser, with explicit handling of NoClassDefFoundError -> IOException.
- Notifications via JFXSnackbar with a fixed display duration and logging to SLF4J.
- Ensures PreferencesService theme CSS is applied to dialog scenes and sets application icons where appropriate.
- Misc UI improvements: resizable custom dialogs, proper dialog owner initialization, and wiring of cancel buttons to task cancellation.

This centralizes dialog behavior, error handling and theming for JavaFX dialogs used in the application.

Summary

- Introduces an improved AI chat prompt UI with a Regenerate action and enhanced prompt-history navigation, plus several AI chat reliability and notification improvements.

What changed

- Added a “Regenerate” button to the chat prompt (ChatPromptComponent + FXML) that invokes a regenerate callback to re-send the last user prompt and request a fresh model response.
  - Regeneration logic in AiChatComponent deletes the assistant responses from the end of the chat history until the last user message and then resends the last user prompt.
  - The UI shows a loading state while the regenerated reply is generated.

- Improved prompt history navigation and editing behavior (ChatPromptComponent):
  - Up/Down keys browse previous user prompts. History scrolling is only allowed when the prompt is empty or when the user is already scrolling history.
  - Editing the prompt resets history scroll state to avoid accidental overwrites.
  - Proper handling for multi-line prompts and caret position when browsing history.

- Robust error handling when sending messages to the AI (AiChatComponent):
  - Background task wraps aiChatLogic.execute and surfaces errors to the user; common HTTP errors (401/404) produce a clearer hint about API base URL settings.
  - On failure, the prompt switches to an error state offering Retry/Cancel actions.

- Notifications and ingestion status improvements (AiChatComponent):
  - Chat shows warnings when entries lack valid citation keys or when linked files aren’t PDFs.
  - Tracks ingestion statuses for linked files and surfaces processing/error/success notifications via the notifications popover.
  - Notifications button visibility is kept in sync with current notifications.

- Minor UI/UX polish and state handling (AiChatComponent):
  - The notice text is now dynamically bound to the selected AI provider and chosen chat model(s).
  - Example question hyperlinks are inserted and removed after use, and send the respective prompt when clicked.
  - Chat prompt callbacks wired: send, retry, cancel, regenerate; focus management and loading states integrated.

Files modified

- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/ai/components/aichat/AiChatComponent.java
- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/ai/components/aichat/chatprompt/ChatPromptComponent.java
- jabgui/src/main/resources/org/jabref/gui/ai/components/aichat/chatprompt/ChatPromptComponent.fxml
- CHANGELOG.md (documenting the new Regenerate button and related additions)

Why this matters

These changes make the AI chat more usable and resilient: users can quickly ask the model to reformulate or retry responses, browse and reuse previously-sent prompts, and receive clearer notifications when files are being processed or when configuration issues (e.g. API base URL) occur.

This PR improves the handling and reloading of journal abbreviation data and tightens up the parsing logic and tests.

Key changes
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/journals/AbbreviationParser.java
  - Refactor and harden the parser for abbreviation files. Better handling of whitespace, empty fields, comments and different line endings. Prevents malformed entries from causing failures and ensures consistent trimming/normalization of keys and values.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/journals/JournalAbbreviationRepository.java
  - Improved repository behavior around loading and caching abbreviation data. Ensures safe reloads when source files change and more predictable fallback behavior when mappings are missing. Better management of IO resources and error handling.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/collab/FileUpdateMonitor.java
  - Adjustments so the abbreviation repository (and other consumers) reliably pick up external changes. Fixes race conditions and makes update notifications more robust.

- Tests
  - src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/journals/JournalAbbreviationRepositoryTest.java
  - src/test/java/org/jabref/gui/journals/ManageJournalAbbreviationsViewModelTest.java
  - Updated and extended tests to cover new parsing edge cases, reloading behavior, and ensure the repository reacts to file updates as expected.

Why
- Users modifying journal abbreviation files externally or using different editors/OS line endings experienced inconsistent behavior. The parser and repository were brittle in the face of unexpected input and file changes. This PR addresses those issues and adds unit tests to prevent regressions.

Notes
- No public API changes; mostly internal refactor/bugfix and test coverage extension.
- If you have local custom abbreviation files, they should now be picked up more reliably when changed externally.

This PR updates packaging assets and build scripts for macOS and Windows releases and adjusts CI deployment workflow. Changes include refreshed icons and background images, updated entitlements, DMG setup script and README for mac packaging, the Windows post-image script, and small build/deployment configuration updates.

What changed

- CI: .github/workflows/deployment.yml — update deployment workflow (packaging/notarization steps and/or configuration).
- Build: build.gradle — build and packaging configuration tweaks.
- mac assets and scripts (buildres/mac/* and src/main/resources/icons/*):
  - Updated macOS background images (JabRef-background.png, JabRef-background-darkAqua.png).
  - Updated launcher and volume icons (Jabref-volume.icns, launcher.icns, src/main/resources/icons/jabref.icns).
  - Updated DMG setup script (JabRef-dmg-setup.scpt) and README (buildres/mac/README.md).
  - Updated mac entitlements (buildres/mac/myapp.entitlements and myapp.entitlements).
  - Updated script for converting SVGs to ICNS (src/main/resources/icons/svg2icns.sh).
- Windows: buildres/windows/JabRef-post-image.wsf — update post-image steps (installer/image customization).

Rationale

- Refresh visual assets (icons and backgrounds) for better consistency and updated branding.
- Ensure proper entitlements for macOS code signing and notarization.
- Adjust packaging scripts to reflect changed assets and to make DMG generation and Windows post-image tasks compatible with the current build process.
- Align CI deployment workflow and Gradle configuration with the updated packaging steps.

Impact and testing

- No application logic changes.
- Affects release packaging, signing, and notarization pipelines.

Suggested tests for reviewers

1. CI: Run the updated GitHub Actions deployment workflow on a test tag or draft release and confirm packaging steps complete (codesign/notarize if secrets are provided).
2. macOS: Locally build and package a DMG using Gradle and the buildres/mac scripts; verify:
   - Icons and background images render correctly in the DMG and in the app bundle.
   - Code signing uses the updated entitlements without errors.
3. Windows: Run the post-image script to confirm installer/image customization works and the icon resources are applied.
4. Verify that svg2icns.sh still produces valid .icns files from the provided SVG source.

Notes for reviewers

- Check the entitlements files carefully to ensure no unintended permission requests are included.
- CI deployment may require updated secrets for signing/notarization; coordinate with the ops/release team if necessary.
- If any packaging scripts assume specific macOS tooling versions, verify compatibility or update documentation.

This PR is focused on packaging and release assets; it should not affect runtime behavior beyond the installed app appearance and code-signing properties.

Refactor layout formatting and make export formatting configurable

This change centralizes layout-related formatting options into a new/updated LayoutFormatterPreferences class and updates the code paths that perform layout-based formatting accordingly:

- LayoutFormatterPreferences: encapsulates layout formatting options (previously scattered defaults/hardcoded values). Provides a single place to manage settings used by layout formatters.
- LayoutEntry: updated to accept and use LayoutFormatterPreferences when producing formatted output for an entry. This removes reliance on implicit/static defaults and makes formatting behavior explicit and testable.
- ExportFormat: updated export flow to construct/pass LayoutFormatterPreferences into LayoutEntry so exports honor the configured formatting preferences.

Benefits:
- Fixes inconsistencies where export formatting ignored user or configurable settings.
- Improves clarity and separation of concerns between preference storage and formatting logic.
- Prepares the codebase for future options around layout formatting without scattering changes across many classes.

Other notes:
- Minor code cleanup and javadoc improvements included.
- Backwards compatibility preserved: defaults are preserved when explicit preferences are not supplied.

- Integrates SpotBugs into the Gradle build and ensures SpotBugs output directory is ignored by git.

- build.gradle:
  - Added SpotBugs Gradle plugin (id "com.github.spotbugs" version "6.0.0-rc.2") and applied it.

- Based on: https://github.com/koppor/jabref/issues/239

- ignoreFailures is currently true to avoid breaking CI on existing findings; maintainers may want to toggle this once issues are addressed.
- No CHANGELOG entry or automated tests were added in this PR.

text:
What

This PR improves the drag-and-drop experience across the app by refining behavior, accessibility, and performance of our drag-and-drop components.

Key changes

- Smoother drag interactions: reduced layout thrashing and optimized event handling to eliminate jank during dragging.
- Better touch support: enhanced touch event handling so dragging works reliably on mobile and tablet devices.
- Improved accessibility: added keyboard support for moving items (aria attributes and focus management) and clearer ARIA live region updates for screen readers.
- More reliable drop targets: clearer visual highlighting and stricter hit testing to prevent accidental drops.
- Fixed visual artifacts: removed ghost images and flicker when dragging between lists/containers.
- Added unit and integration tests covering common drag/drop flows and keyboard interactions.
- Updated documentation: usage notes and examples for new keyboard shortcuts and touch behaviors.

Why

These changes address multiple user-reported issues with the prior drag-and-drop implementation (lag, unreliable drops on touch, and poor keyboard/screen reader support). They improve usability for mouse, keyboard, and touch users.

How to test

1. Open the components/pages that use drag-and-drop (see changed files).  
2. Verify smooth dragging with mouse: start drag, move quickly between targets, and drop.  
3. Verify touch: perform the same interactions on a mobile or emulator.  
4. Verify keyboard: focus an item, use the provided keyboard controls to move it between positions/containers, and confirm ARIA announcements.  
5. Check edge cases: rapid drags between lists, dropping outside valid targets, and canceling drag.

Notes

- No breaking API changes are expected; most improvements are internal to the drag/drop components.  
- See updated docs for keyboard shortcuts and migration tips if you extended the old drag behavior.

Root cause
The text field input handling prevented normal focus traversal on TAB/Shift+TAB and did not reliably commit the edited value before switching fields.

What I changed
- Restore normal focus traversal for single-line entry editor text fields so TAB moves focus to the next field and Shift+TAB moves to the previous one.
- Ensure the current edit is committed before transferring focus so the model always reflects the latest user input.
- Avoid inserting a literal tab character in single-line fields when the user intends to switch fields.
- Keep multi-line text components (if any) free to accept tab characters as before.

Files modified
- Entry editor UI/input handling code (focus/keyboard handling) — adjust Tab handling and commit behavior.
- Tests: add/adjust tests verifying TAB and Shift+TAB behavior and that edits are committed when focus changes.

How to verify
1. Open an entry in the entry editor.
2. Edit a single-line text field, press TAB — focus should move to the next field and the change should be saved/committed.
3. Press Shift+TAB — focus should move to the previous field.
4. Confirm no unexpected tab characters are inserted into single-line fields.

Compatibility
No public API changes. This only affects keyboard/focus behavior in the entry editor and improves UX without breaking existing behavior for multi-line inputs.

text:
Add PDF XMP import flow and improve dropped-file handling

Summary
- Implement XMP-based import when a PDF is dropped onto JabRef entries. If a PDF contains XMP metadata, the user is prompted to import one or more BibTeX records embedded in the PDF.
- Add a dedicated ImportDialog for PDF imports with options to: create a blank entry linking the PDF, create entries from XMP, create entry from PDF content, or only attach the PDF to an existing entry. The dialog can persist the chosen default behavior in preferences and offers an option to always use the selected style.
- Improve DroppedFileHandler to support linking/copying/moving/renaming files when dropped, handle PDF-specific XMP imports (creating new entries from XMP), and a convenience linkPdfToEntry API.

Details
- New/changed UI: src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/pdfimport/ImportDialog.java
  - Presents radio options for NOMETA, XMP, CONTENT, ONLYATTACH and displays any found XMP entries for preview.
  - Stores the chosen default import style in preferences and supports an "always use this PDF import style" option.
  - Exposes helper methods getChoice(), isDoNotShowAgain(), getResult(), disableXMPChoice().

- Logic/UI integration: src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/externalfiles/DroppedFileHandler.java
  - tryXmpImport(...) reads XMP from a dropped PDF and prompts the user to import embedded BibTeX entries. If the user accepts, entries are inserted into the database with generated IDs and the PDF is linked to them.
  - linkPdfToEntry(...) convenience methods added to link a PDF to a specific entry (used by MrDlib integration/comments).
  - showLinkMoveCopyRenameDialog(...) offers and persists choices for leave/copy/move/rename when adding files.
  - doCopy(...) and doMove(...) perform filesystem operations (copy uses FileUtil.copyFile) and prompt before overwriting existing files. doLink(...) manages the file list field, supports duplicate avoidance and creates undoable edits.

Behavioral notes
- When a PDF with XMP metadata is dropped, users will be prompted to import the embedded entries; they can opt to cancel, decline XMP import (in which case normal link/copy/move UI is shown), or accept and import the entries.
- The ImportDialog remembers the default import mode (persisted in preferences) and allows opting out of future prompts.
- File operations handle existing destination files by asking before overwrite and avoid re-linking when a link already points to the same absolute file.

Misc
- Error handling: reading XMP catches IOExceptions and logs/warns as appropriate.
- UI/UX: small layout and message improvements to show XMP preview and clarify options to users.

Files touched
- Added/modified: DroppedFileHandler.java, ImportDialog.java

This change improves PDF import workflows (especially for PDFs embedding BibTeX via XMP) and makes handling of dropped external files more robust and user-friendly.

Introduce StateManager and enhance GlobalSearchBar UI and search integration

Summary:
- Add StateManager to centralize GUI state: active database, active group(s), selected entries/groups, active search query, and per-database search result sizes. Provides helper methods to get/set selected entries/groups, clear/set search queries, and retrieve entries in the current database.
- Implement GlobalSearchBar providing a feature-rich, responsive search bar:
  - Delayed search execution (debounced) and bidirectional binding with StateManager.activeSearchQueryProperty().
  - Regex and case-sensitivity toggles (persisted in preferences) and a search mode toggle.
  - Validation for regular expressions using ControlsFX validators and visual feedback with IconValidationDecorator.
  - Auto-completion support with a custom popup skin that includes search option controls (regex, case-sensitive, search mode) in the popup toolbar.
  - User-friendly behaviors: expand/collapse animation on focus, keyboard handling for keybindings (clear & select first on CLOSE), clipboard X11 support, hint tooltip with formatted advanced hints, and clear/invalid-search handling.
  - Displays search results count and descriptive hints by consuming the search description (SearchDescribers) and the number of matched results from StateManager.

Notes:
- The GlobalSearchBar now relies on StateManager to keep the search query state and to show the number of results for the active database.
- The auto-completion popup uses reflection to access the underlying popup from ControlsFX (kept as a TODO to remove reflective access when possible).

Fixes #7633 — handle titles that contain curly braces around capitalized words when querying arXiv and comparing titles.

What I changed
- ArXiv fetcher: When building the search query and when comparing titles we now strip only braces that wrap capitalized words instead of removing all braces from the title. This prevents breaking titles that rely on braces for LaTeX formatting while still matching arXiv entries that have braces around capitalized terms.
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ArXiv.java: use StringUtil.removeBracesAroundCapitalizedWords(...) for query construction and title comparison.
- String utilities: added methods to support the new behaviour.
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/model/strings/StringUtil.java: added removeAllBraces, removeBracesAroundCapitalizedWords, and a helper removeSingleBracesAroundCapitalizedWords that repeatedly strips braces around capitalized words (handles nested braces like "{{Word}}" → "Word").
- Tests: added regression tests that verify findFullText works with titles both with and without curly braces around capitalized words.
  - src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ArXivTest.java: added findByTitleWithoutCurlyBracket and findByTitleWithCurlyBracket tests; updated imports to use Assertions.*.

Why
- Previously all curly braces were removed which could alter titles in unintended ways and break matching. The new approach targets the common case where authors put braces around capitalized words (e.g. {Deep} {Learning}) and removes just those braces so title matching and arXiv queries succeed while keeping other brace usage intact.

Notes
- Tests included for regression coverage.
- This addresses and closes issue #7633.

Add external-change detection and handling for .bib libraries, plus supporting view models and tests

What I changed
- Implemented a change-scanning mechanism (ChangeScanner) that parses the on-disk .bib file and produces a list of DatabaseChangeViewModel instances describing differences (metadata, preamble, strings, entries).
- Added DatabaseChangeMonitor which registers with the FileUpdateMonitor, keeps a temporary reference copy of the file, and triggers a background scan when the file on disk changes. Notable changes are delivered to registered DatabaseChangeListener objects.
- Implemented concrete DatabaseChangeViewModel types for different kinds of external modifications:
  - EntryAdd/EntryDelete/EntryChange (EntryChangeViewModel with nested FieldChangeViewModel)
  - StringAdd/StringRemove/StringChange/StringNameChange (String*ViewModel classes)
  - MetaDataChangeViewModel, GroupChangeViewModel, PreambleChangeViewModel (scanned via BibDatabaseDiff)
- Each change view model provides a description Node to show to the user and a makeChange(...) implementation that applies the accepted changes to the in-memory database with undo support (NamedCompound + specific Undoable* edits).
- DatabaseChangeMonitor runs scans in the background using BackgroundTask and TaskExecutor, and exposes methods to mark external changes as resolved or to update the reference copy.
- AppendDatabaseAction was updated to reuse OpenDatabase.loadDatabase for opening/importing files in the background and merge imported content (entries, strings, groups, content selectors) into the currently open library with proper undo edits and setting of automatic fields.
- OpenDatabase now centralizes loading logic and runs post-open migrations and keyword/special-field syncing when requested.
- Extended/added many localized strings for the external changes UI and related actions (JabRef_en.properties).
- Added unit tests for core database operations and diffs:
  - BibDatabaseTest: extensive coverage for entry/string insertion/removal, duplicate detection, event posting, string resolution (including circular dependencies), and other behaviors.
  - BibDatabaseDiffTest: tests verifying comparison of empty databases and of entries that are equal by content even when different instances.

Why
- Users need a reliable way to detect and review external modifications to a .bib file (for example when another program or another instance modifies the file). This change introduces scanning, user-facing descriptions, and the ability to accept/reject and apply those external changes with undo support.
- Centralizing database-opening logic (OpenDatabase) avoids duplicated parsing code and ensures consistent post-processing (migrations, special-field syncing).
- The tests increase confidence in database behavior, string resolution, and diffing.

Notes / Potential follow-ups
- ChangeScanner currently uses a DummyFileUpdateMonitor when parsing the on-disk file to avoid interfering with the real monitor; consider passing a real monitor if nested monitoring is desired.
- The rename logic for strings logs and refuses to rename if the target name already exists; UX around conflicts could be improved (offer alternatives/merge strategies).
- Additional UI wiring is required to present the list of DatabaseChangeViewModel objects to the user and to hook accept/reject actions into the rest of the application (these changes implement the model and background plumbing).

- Localization: src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties

Summary:
This PR implements restoration capabilities for the shared database. It adds the end-to-end restore workflow so backups can be applied to the shared DB in a controlled, auditable, and repeatable way.

- Service/background job that performs the restore steps and handles long-running work

- Unit and integration tests covering success, failure and edge cases
- Documentation updates describing how to trigger and monitor restores and expected behavior

1. Trigger a restore via the provided endpoint/CLI with a known backup reference.
2. Observe the restore job is scheduled and moves through progress states.
3. Verify data from the backup is applied to the shared database.
4. Confirm proper logging and error reporting on both successful and failed runs.

Why this change:
Enables safe recovery and management of the shared database by providing a tested, auditable restore path and tooling to monitor and handle restores.

text:
Summary

This PR adds support for regular expressions in the global search feature.

What changed

- Global search now recognizes and executes regular expressions supplied by the user.
  - Queries wrapped in forward slashes are treated as regex (for example: /foo.*bar/i).
  - A UI toggle was added to explicitly enable regex mode (so plain queries can still be used).
- Query parsing and validation for regex input were implemented.
  - Invalid regexes now produce a helpful error message rather than failing silently.
  - Input validation prevents obviously catastrophic patterns (basic safeguards for performance).
- Server/search layer updated to accept and safely evaluate regex queries where supported; otherwise falls back to literal searching.
- UX improvements: the search field shows a regex indicator when regex mode is active and displays validation errors inline.

Why

- Some users need flexible pattern matching across the codebase and other searchable resources; supporting regexes allows more powerful queries than simple substring or wildcard searches.
- Validation and safeguards reduce risk of expensive or unsafe searches.

Compatibility and behavior

- Plain text searches continue to work exactly as before.
- If a user enters an invalid regex, the system will indicate the error and will not run the search as a regex; the user can choose to run the literal text instead.
- Performance safeguards may reject extremely complex patterns; a clear message explains why and suggests alternatives.

Tests

- Unit tests added for regex detection, parsing, validation, and fallback behavior.
- Integration/E2E tests ensure the UI toggle, indicator, and inline error messages work as expected.

Notes

- No data migrations required.
- Future work: support for additional regex flags via UI, and more advanced pattern-safety heuristics.

text:
Fix and improve XMP/Dublin Core metadata export and extraction

What I changed
- XmpExporter: Fixed generation of Dublin Core (dc:) metadata when exporting entries to XMP. Ensures correct mapping of common BibTeX fields (author, editor, title, journal/booktitle, year/date, doi, isbn, url, keywords, language) to Dublin Core elements and avoids duplicate/empty entries.
- DublinCoreExtractor: Improved extraction logic to read dates (falling back from date to year), handle multiple creators (authors/editors) correctly, and normalize fields such as journal vs booktitle. Also made parsing more robust for missing or malformed values.
- XmpUtilWriter: Updated writing utilities to produce well-formed RDF/Dublin Core elements, handle special characters/encoding, and ensure arrays (e.g. dc:creator) are written consistently.
- Tests: Updated/added unit tests (XmpExporterTest) and example resource (article_dublinCore.bib) to cover the corrected mappings and round-trip behavior for common fields.

Why this change
- Previous XMP export produced incorrect or incomplete Dublin Core metadata in some cases (missing date, duplicated creators, incorrect field mappings). That caused interoperability issues with tools that consume XMP/Dublin Core metadata.
- The changes make XMP output conform more closely to expected Dublin Core semantics and improve robustness when reading/writing metadata.

Notes for reviewers
- Focus on the mappings in XmpExporter and the fallback logic in DublinCoreExtractor for date and creator handling.
- Tests demonstrate expected XMP output for an example article and validate that special characters and arrays are handled properly.
- No public API changes beyond improved/export behavior; this is an internal fix to exporter/extractor logic.

Fix tab navigation in Entry Editor: pressing Tab in the last TextField of a tab now moves focus to the next tab (fixes #11937).

What I changed
- Added a changelog entry noting the fix.
- Implemented tab navigation plumbing in EntryEditor: EditorTextField.setupTabNavigation(...) is called from the constructor to wire a predicate that detects the last field in the currently selected tab and a Runnable that selects the next tab.
- Implemented EntryEditor.isLastFieldInCurrentTab(TextField) to determine whether a given text field is the last shown field in the active FieldsEditorTab.
- Added an event filter to EditorTextField to intercept the Tab key: when the predicate reports this is the last field, the nextTab selector is invoked and the Tab event is consumed.
- Exposed a setup method on EditorTextField (setupTabNavigation) to provide the predicate and the next-tab action.
- Set control IDs for various field editors so fields can be identified: CitationKeyEditor (display name), PersonsEditor (field name), and SimpleEditor / SimpleEditor.createTextInputControl now receive the Field and set the input ID accordingly. MarkdownEditor signature adjusted to pass Field into createTextInputControl.

Notes
- The logic relies on field IDs and Field.getDisplayName() to match the text field control to the underlying Field. This enables reliable detection of the last visible field in a tab.
- No behaviour changes beyond the intended Tab navigation fix.

text:
Update CHANGELOG.md: add detailed Unreleased section

This PR updates the CHANGELOG.md with the new "Unreleased" section documenting notable additions, changes, fixes and removals since v6.0-alpha2. Key highlights included in the entry:

- Added a setting to control citation relations local storage TTL (default: 30 days) and improved citation relations caching via offline storage.
- Release distribution improvements: added Linux arm64 images.
- New fetchers and integration endpoints: EuropePMC ID-based fetcher; initial "cite as you write" endpoint; LOBID as an alternate ISBN fetcher.
- UX improvements: warning on adding duplicate entries to an active library; success dialogs for "Copy to" indicating cross-reference inclusion; toggle for absolute/relative file paths; automatic selection of appropriate identifier tab and clipboard prefill when creating entries; "Open example library" button on Welcome tab.
- Entry creation and import improvements: merged New Entry / Import by ID / New Entry from Plain Text into a single "Create New Entry" tool; option to create entries from Bib(La)TeX source; batch fetching for multiple entries; support for Refer/BibIX import; added monthfiled to default fields for resolving BibTeX-Strings.
- New tooling and commands: introduced the jabkit application (with verbs moved from the graphical app) and a new jabkit "pseudonymize" command.
- AI and accessibility: AI chat responses now support markdown rendering and copying; added initial OpenAI/Mistral/HuggingFace/Google/Ollama/GPT4All provider integrations earlier in the changelog and references to AI features.
- LibreOffice/OpenOffice integration: more CSL bibliography header/body format options, including "Bibliography Heading" and better style handling and previews.
- Miscellaneous: dark title bar support on Windows; focus-running-instance behavior when starting additional instances; progress output and exit code behavior for toolkit check-consistency command (non-zero exit on issues for CI use); multi-file import support; option to hide File Annotations tab when empty.

Fixes and removals documented:
- Various bug fixes (e.g. convert-to-biblatex date fallback, tab dragging exception, path checks in library properties, document viewer and PDF import behaviors, fulltext search tab issues, etc.).
- Removed ability to change internal preference values, removed MySQL/MariaDB and Oracle support, and removed library migrations (users must use JabRef 6.0-alpha.1 to perform migrations).

See the Unreleased section in CHANGELOG.md for the complete list of added/changed/fixed/removed items and links to the related issues and PRs.

text:
Add JabRefPreferences: a comprehensive singleton implementation of PreferencesService that centralizes application preferences using java.util.prefs. This class defines and documents preference keys, supplies a defaults map, provides getters/setters and typed retrieval (String, boolean, int, double, Optional), and implements persistence operations (import/export, flush, clear, deleteKey). Key features include:

- Centralized default values for many preference domains (UI, preview, proxy/SSL, OpenOffice, citation keys, file handling, import/export, cleanup, telemetry, grobid, etc.).
- Typed preference accessors and convenience methods for lists and series of preferences (putStringList/getStringList/getSeries/purgeSeries).
- Language-dependent default handling and language selection logic.
- Caching and lazy initialization of domain-specific preference objects (General, Telemetry, DOI, Owner, Timestamp, Groups, EntryEditor, Remote, Proxy, SSL, CitationKeyPattern, PushToApplication, ExternalApplications, MainTable/Column preferences, Internal, Appearance, File, AutoLink, ImportExport, Preview, SidePane, Cleanup, GUI, Search, XMP, NameFormatter, AutoComplete, SpecialFields, MrDlib, ProtectedTerms, Importer, Grobid).
- Conversion utilities for serializing/deserializing lists with escaping and helpers to parse/serialize custom entry types and citation key patterns.
- Integration points with other components via EasyBind listeners to automatically persist changes from preference objects back to the preference store.
- Support for importing legacy jabref.xml preferences and an option to export preferences (used for memory-stick mode), plus TrustStoreManager integration to clear custom certificates when preferences are cleared.

This class provides the main preferences backbone for JabRef, enabling storage, retrieval and migration of a wide range of application settings and exposing them through typed preference objects used across the application.

text:
Fix repeated escaping of % sign (fixes #2451)

What I changed
- Prevent double-escaping of the percent sign when running the LaTeX cleanup multiple times by only escaping unescaped % signs.
- Extracted and replaced several string-based regex replaceAll calls with precompiled java.util.regex.Pattern instances for clarity and performance.
- Improved handling of LaTeX cleanup steps (removing redundant braces, moving numbers/operators into math mode, and dollar-sign handling) by using named Patterns.
- Added unit tests to ensure percent signs are escaped only once (including in numeric contexts) and updated existing tests.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md with the fix.

Why
- Previously, the formatter used a blind replace("%", "\\%") which re-escaped already-escaped percent signs (\% -> \\%). This resulted in repeated escaping when the formatter ran multiple times. The new regex only matches % not preceded by a backslash or another % and replaces it with \%.

Tests
- Added tests escapePercentSignOnlyOnce and escapePercentSignOnlnyOnceWithNumber to verify correct behavior.

- Fix for issue #2451
- CHANGELOG entry added

Summary

Fixes an issue where customImporterTabViewModel was duplicated when exporting Preferences, which could lead to duplicated importer tabs after import or app restart.

What was happening

- The Preferences export included a UI view model (customImporterTabViewModel) that should not be exported or was exported more than once.
- As a result the exported preferences contained duplicate entries and importing or reloading preferences produced duplicated importer tabs in the UI.

What this change does

- Prevents customImporterTabViewModel from being exported as part of Preferences (filters out transient UI view model state during export).
- Adds a deduplication check during import/merge so existing custom importer tab models are not added twice if an export mistakenly contains duplicates.
- Adds tests that assert a single customImporterTabViewModel is present after export/import and that importing exported preferences does not create duplicate tabs.

Why this is safe

- This only affects transient/UI state that should not be persisted across export/import; persistent importer definitions remain unchanged.
- Backwards compatibility is preserved: imports that previously contained duplicates are handled by the deduplication logic.

How to verify

1. Create or configure custom importer tabs.
2. Export Preferences.
3. Import the exported Preferences (or restart the app if export/import path triggers reload).
4. Confirm that each custom importer tab appears only once and no duplicates are present.

Notes

- If an earlier exported file already contains duplicates, importing it after this fix will not create additional duplicates; the deduplication step will clean it up.
- Tests included to prevent regressions.

text:
Fix legacy linked-file paths that included the file directory name (Fixes #8991)

Summary
- Adds a backward-compatible workaround in FileHelper.find to handle old JabRef file links that include the file directory as a leading path element inside the stored filename. If the file is not found by resolving the given filename against the provided directory, we additionally check whether the filename starts with the directory name and, in that case, try resolving it relative to the directory's parent (using resolveSibling).

What changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/util/FileHelper.java
  - Improved JavaDoc for find(...).
  - If the direct resolution doesn't exist, detect legacy filenames that start with the current directory name and try resolving them relative to the directory's sibling (workaround for old JabRef behavior).

- src/test/java/org/jabref/model/util/FileHelperTest.java
  - Added unit tests (using @TempDir) to cover:
    - finding a file in the same directory
    - finding a file when the filename starts with the directory name (legacy case)
    - ensuring correct behavior when nested subdirectories exist
  - Minor formatting and import adjustments.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added an entry describing the fix for linked files that contained parts of the main file directory.

Why
- Some older JabRef installations stored linked-file names containing parts of the main file directory. These links could no longer be opened after changes to path handling. This patch restores the ability to open such legacy links while keeping the newer, correct resolution behavior.

Tests
- Unit tests added to verify the new behavior and prevent regressions.

Notes
- This is a targeted compatibility workaround and should not affect normal, modern path resolution behavior.

text:
WIP: Fix for undoing deletion/cutting multiple entries (workaround for #796)

What this does:
- Fixes a bug where undoing a deletion/cut that contains multiple entries only reverted the first entry. The root cause was that when the first entry is re-inserted, that insertion created and pushed a NamedCompound into the UndoManager, which interrupted and effectively destroyed the outer compound that represented the multi-entry undo.
- Implements a workaround: each entry in a multi-entry undo now has its own NamedCompound. This prevents inner insertions from killing the main compound so each entry is properly restored.

Why this approach:
- The change is a pragmatic workaround that ensures all entries are restored. It avoids the main compound being invalidated by nested insertions registering their own undo compound.

Tradeoffs / known limitations:
- Because each entry gets its own NamedCompound, the user must perform Undo (Ctrl+Z) once per entry. Ideally a single Undo would revert all entries at once; that remains a potential future improvement.

Status and checklist:
- CHANGELOG.md updated.
- Changes outlined in this PR description.
- Tests: none added for this behavior (TODO).
- Current tests pass.

References:
- Issue: #796

Notes:
- Marked WIP because this is a workaround and a better approach to preserve single-step undo for multiple entries should be investigated later.

What changed:
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ArXiv.java
  - When building the arXiv query and when comparing titles, the entry title is now normalized via StringUtil.removeBracesAroundCapitalizedWords(...) to strip braces used to protect capitalization in BibTeX titles.

  - Added removeAllBraces(String) to remove all brace characters from a string.

Motivation:
- Many BibTeX entries use braces to preserve capitalization in titles. Previously these braces could cause the arXiv fetcher to fail to match titles. The new normalization improves matching and reduces false negatives when searching arXiv.

Extend and fix RIS importer

This PR improves RIS import coverage and robustness by mapping many additional RIS tags to JabRef fields, fixing tag recognition, and updating tests and changelog.

Key changes
- Extended RIS tag handling: treat T2, J2, JA as secondary/journal title; JO, J1, JF as journal title; support A2/A3/A4 as authors and ED as editor; accept Y2 in addition to Y1/PY/DA for year parsing; accept L2/LK in addition to UR for URL; accept IS/AN/C7/M1 for number; accept AD/CY/PP for address; handle M3/DO as DOI; and more mappings (C3 -> eventtitle, N1/RN -> note, ST -> shorttitle, C2 -> eprint with eprinttype=pubmed, TA -> translator).
- Added mappings for non-standard RIS tags into custom fields (archive_location, call-number, archive, number-of-volumes, original-title, reviewed-title, status, section, refid).
- Added FieldName.SHORTTITLE constant.
- Minor refactor: renamed local BibEntry variable from b to entry for clarity; preserved month handling.
- Improved DOI handling via addDoi(...) where applicable.

Tests and resources
- Updated expected .bib test files to reflect the new mappings and normalization (several RisImporterTest*.bib files changed).
- Added a new test case RisImporterTest7 with corresponding .ris and .bib resources and registered it in the parameterized test list.

Other
- CHANGELOG.md updated to mention the RIS import fixes and extensions.

These changes increase compatibility with a wider range of RIS exports (Scopus, PubMed, etc.) and should reduce manual cleanup after import.

text:
Summary

This PR brings a collection of UI and interaction improvements to the main JabRef window, library tabs and the main table. The changes focus on better drag & drop behavior, background task visibility, entry import workflows and improved tab / editor handling.

Key changes

- Improved drag & drop across the application (JabRefFrame, MainTable)
  - Adds a temporary "Open files..." drag indicator tab when dropping .bib files on the window/tab area.
  - Support opening .bib files by dropping them onto the frame or onto the indicator tab.
  - Accepts and handles dragging selected entries between tabs (uses local dragboard ENTRIES format).
  - MainTable supports file drops on rows (import files, link/copy/move files to entries depending on drop position and modifier keys).

- Background tasks UI
  - Toolbar progress indicator showing overall background progress and providing a popover with a TaskProgressView of background tasks.
  - Tooltips dynamically reflect whether tasks are running or done.

- Entry-from-ID popover
  - Adds an "Import by ID" button in the toolbar that shows a PopOver to create an entry from an identifier.

- Improved key binding handling
  - Global and per-table key handlers for many actions (new entry types, navigation between libraries, selection shortcuts, copy/cut/paste/delete, Enter to edit, etc.).
  - macOS paste workaround to avoid double-paste with CodeArea.

- Tab and LibraryTab enhancements
  - Better tab title and tooltip generation including modification asterisk logic, path fragments for uniqueness, shared DB info, and mode name.
  - Persisted divider positions and entry editor divider position; side pane visibility handling.
  - Autosave and Backup managers are started/stopped appropriately for opened databases.
  - Database loading lifecycle with loading animation and post-open actions (OpenDatabaseAction.performPostOpenActions).

- Main table & data handling
  - MainTable supports keyboard jump-to-search (type to jump to entries based on first sorted column).
  - Selection handling integrates with global StateManager so cut/copy/paste and other actions operate on the correct tab.
  - Copy/Cut/Paste operations use the centralized clipboard manager; paste/import performs duplicate checks and uses ImportHandler.
  - Row factory wiring for double-click to edit and rich context menus.
  - Persistence of visual state (columns, sort order) restored from preferences.

- Indexing and fulltext integration
  - IndexingTaskManager used to index linked PDFs and updated when entries are added/removed or when file links change.

- Miscellaneous
  - Notification pane (DatabaseNotification) for inline DB notifications.
  - Various refactorings to use EasyBind, DefaultTaskExecutor and subscribe to state changes in a safer way.

Why this change

These improvements make opening libraries, moving entries between libraries, adding files, and monitoring background tasks more intuitive and reliable. They also ensure that UI state (tab titles, splitters, backgrounds tasks view) is consistent and persisted.

Compatibility and notes

- No public API changes are intended for external modules; changes are internal to GUI code.
- The PR wires several features to existing preference switches (autosave, fulltext indexing, groups auto-assign, confirm delete) and keeps behavior conditional on those preferences.
- No new tests are included in this change-set.

If you want, I can split this into smaller PRs (drag&drop, background tasks popover, main table improvements) to ease review.

Refactor and improve automatic file-linking flow and user feedback

What changed
- AutoLinkFilesAction now receives a DialogService directly instead of a JabRefFrame (constructor and call site updated in JabRefFrame).
- The background Task now returns an AutoSetFileLinksUtil.LinkFilesResult instead of a list of entries.

- Localization: added messages for file-search problems, moved/added keys for finished message and "Changed %0 entries." to support new user-facing notifications.

Why
- Decouples the action from the main frame by using DialogService directly, making the action easier to test and reuse.
- Provides clearer user feedback for error cases and when no files are found, and reports how many entries were changed when links are added.
- Collects and surfaces file-related exceptions so users know to inspect the error log.

text:
Add automated file-linking feature and background task support

This PR implements an "Automatically set file links" action to detect and attach external files (e.g. PDFs) to selected BibTeX entries.

Key changes:
- Add AutoLinkFilesAction: a SimpleCommand that validates preconditions (active database + selected entries), runs the linking as a background Task, shows a progress dialog, and reports results to the user. The action binds an informative status message and uses the TaskExecutor to run the work off the FX thread.
- Add AutoSetFileLinksUtil: encapsulates the file-discovery/linking logic. It uses FileFinders (constructed from AutoLinkPreferences) to find associated files in the configured file directories, filters out already-linked files (using Files.isSameFile checks), builds LinkedFile entries with relative paths, and collects undoable edits (UndoableFieldChange wrapped in NamedCompound). UI updates to add files to entries are executed on the JavaFX thread.
- Error handling and user feedback: IOExceptions encountered during file search are collected and logged; the user receives warnings if problems occur or if no files were found; on success the user is notified of how many entries were changed.
- Integrates with existing UndoManager: NamedCompound edits are ended and pushed as a single undoable edit when changes exist.
- Localization: includes new/used resource strings for labels and user messages (e.g., "Automatically set file links", "Finished automatically setting external links.", result messages).

Notes:
- The implementation ensures UI responsiveness by running expensive IO on background threads and scheduling UI updates on the FX thread.
- The action respects configured file directories, file type selection, and autosaves undo information so changes can be reverted.

This change provides a convenient, undoable way to autolink local files to bibliography entries using the user’s file-directory configuration and autolink preferences.

Skip integrity checks for verbatim fields (file, url, etc.)

What changed
- AmpersandChecker and HTMLCharacterChecker now skip fields that are marked with FieldProperty.VERBATIM, preventing false positives for values such as file names and URLs that legitimately contain '&' or HTML-encoded sequences.
- AmpersandChecker was refactored to a stream-based implementation and a small helper (getUnescapedAmpersandsWithCount) that counts unescaped '&' occurrences (taking backslash-escaping into account) and reports per-field counts.
- HTMLCharacterChecker was simplified to a stream-based implementation that filters out verbatim fields.
- Added parameterized tests in AmpersandCheckerTest and HTMLCharacterCheckerTest to verify that verbatim fields do not trigger integrity messages.
- CHANGELOG.md updated to mention the change.

Why
This fixes false-positive integrity warnings for ampersands and HTML-encoded characters in verbatim fields (e.g., URLs or file paths). See discussion: https://github.com/koppor/jabref/issues/585#issuecomment-1735461242 and related references.

Notes
- Implementation uses FieldProperty.VERBATIM to identify verbatim fields.
- Tests cover examples for FILE and URL fields to ensure no warnings are produced.

Summary

This PR improves the user friendliness of automatically detected (auto-linked) files in the entry editor's Files tab by making the action to accept an auto-found file more visible and giving the filename a subdued appearance until it is accepted.

What I changed

- UI/UX
  - Move the accept (link) button to the far left of each file row so it is more prominent and easier to find.
  - Swap the icon for automatically linked files from a briefcase-check to a link-with-plus (LINK_PLUS) which better communicates the meaning.
  - Give filenames of automatically detected files reduced opacity (70%) until they are accepted, making their status visually distinct.

- Code
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/LinkedFilesEditor.java
    - Added a PseudoClass for the opacity state and subscribe to linkedFile.isAutomaticallyFoundProperty() to toggle the pseudo-class on the filename Text node.
    - Use EasyBind to react to the automaticallyFound property.
    - Make the accept button visible and managed only when the file is automatically found; moved the accept button to the left of the info area.
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/icon/IconTheme.java
    - Replaced AUTO_LINKED_FILE icon from BRIEFCASE_CHECK to LINK_PLUS.
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/Base.css
    - Added .file-row-text:opacity style to render file names at 70% opacity using derive(-jr-search-text, 70%).
  - CHANGELOG.md
    - Added a user-facing entry describing the change.

Motivation

The previous layout and icon made it less obvious that a file was automatically detected and that the user needed to explicitly accept linking. These changes make the action clearer and the file status easier to understand at a glance. This addresses and fixes issue #3607.

Testing

- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance. Confirmed:
  - Auto-detected files show the link-with-plus icon on the left and the filename is visually subdued until accepted.
  - The accept button only appears (and is managed) for auto-detected files.
  - After accepting, filename opacity returns to normal and behavior is unchanged for already-linked files.

Other

- Screenshots demonstrating before/after are included in the issue/PR.
- CHANGELOG updated for end users.

Fixes: #3607

Summary

Remove cloning of entries before insertion so newly imported entries are the same instances that get stored in the database and bound to the UI.

What changed

- Removed unnecessary cloning in importCleanedEntries. Entries are now inserted directly into the database and then processed (generateKeys, setAutomaticFields).

Why

Cloning the entries prior to insertion meant the objects inserted into the database were different instances than the ones kept by the import flow/UI. As a result the entry editor and main table were not correctly bound to the newly added entries. By inserting the original instances, UI bindings work correctly and newly created entries are displayed/edited as expected.

Related

- Follow-up to #11724
- Closes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref-issue-melting-pot/issues/656

This PR continues the work on making preferences observable (follow-up to #9135). Main changes:

- GeneralPreferences
  - Embed the Language preference inside GeneralPreferences (observable ObjectProperty).
  - GeneralTabViewModel now reads/writes language via preferencesService.getGeneralPreferences().getLanguage()/setLanguage() and listens to changes. Changing language now updates persistent prefs and triggers language-dependent defaults and Localization.

- PreferencesService / JabRefPreferences
  - Removed legacy getLanguage()/setLanguage() from the PreferencesService API; language is now provided via GeneralPreferences.
  - JabRefPreferences constructs GeneralPreferences with the current language and registers an EasyBind listener on languageProperty to persist changes and update Localization.
  - Refactored getLanguage() implementation inside JabRefPreferences to derive language from stored ID.
  - Minor refactors: renamed getOrCreateUserId() -> getTelemetryUserId(), return type change for determineMainFileDirectory.
  - GUI prefs persistence updated: lastFilesOpened and file history handling now use ListChangeListener and the new FileHistory structure.

- FileHistory
  - Reworked FileHistory to be an observable list by extending ModifiableObservableListBase<Path>, exposing list semantics (add/get/remove/size) and a static factory FileHistory.of(List<Path>).
  - Integrates with GuiPreferences: GuiPreferences now stores a FileHistory and JabRefPreferences persists RECENT_DATABASES via ListChangeListener.
  - Updated codepaths that used getHistory()/getFileAt() to use the new API (stream/list semantics).
  - Updated FileHistoryTest accordingly.

- Metadata differences localization
  - MetaDataDiff now produces an EnumSet<Difference> instead of localized strings (separates business logic from UI/localization).
  - MetadataChangeDetailsView maps MetaDataDiff.Difference values to localized strings for display.

- Misc refactors and cleanups
  - RelatedArticlesTab: use preferencesService.getGeneralPreferences().getLanguage() for MrDLibFetcher.
  - JabRefFrame: use prefs.getGuiPreferences().getFileHistory() and access lastFilesOpened via gui preferences; clear edited files now manipulates the observable list directly.
  - Small cleanups in FieldFormatterCleanup and FieldFormatterCleanups equals/toString implementations and other minor improvements (e.g. use of toList()).

Notes/Impact:
- API change: PreferencesService no longer exposes direct getLanguage()/setLanguage(); callers must use getGeneralPreferences(). This is a breaking change for code using the old methods.
- FileHistory is now observable and integrates directly with GuiPreferences; persistence always writes the RECENT_DATABASES list (empty list handling preserved).
- MetaDataDiff no longer returns localized text; UI layer must map enums to strings (done in MetadataChangeDetailsView).

Tests:
- Updated FileHistoryTest to work with the new FileHistory implementation.

Manually tested in running JabRef.

text:
Refactor preferences, file history and metadata diffs; modernize several implementations

This PR contains a set of related refactorings and cleanups across the preferences, file history and metadata-diff code paths plus a few small API-modernizations and bugfixes.

Highlights

- FileHistory redesigned
  - FileHistory now extends ModifiableObservableListBase<Path> and behaves like an observable List<Path>.
  - Factory: FileHistory.of(List<Path>) creates instances.
  - Deprecated/removed methods: getHistory(), getFileAt(int), isEmpty() were removed; use standard List methods (size(), get(index), isEmpty(), add/remove, iteration) instead.
  - Call sites updated (FileHistoryMenu, JabRefPreferences, tests).
  - FileHistoryTest updated to use the new list API.

- Preferences / language handling
  - GeneralPreferences now owns a Language property (getLanguage(), setLanguage(), languageProperty()).
  - JabRefPreferences now supplies the language to GeneralPreferences and listens to changes on generalPreferences.languageProperty(), persisting LANGUAGE and updating Localization and language-dependent defaults when changed.
  - Removed the old cached language handling from JabRefPreferences.
  - PreferencesService interface no longer exposes getLanguage()/setLanguage() and clearEditedFiles(); callers should use GeneralPreferences and GuiPreferences instead.

- GUI preferences and persistence
  - GuiPreferences now stores lastFilesOpened as ObservableList<String> and exposes a FileHistory instance (fileHistory) for the recent-file menu.
  - JabRefPreferences.getFileHistory() uses FileHistory.of(...) and JabRefPreferences.storeFileHistory(...) persists the entire list (empty list is persisted correctly by putting LAST_EDITED when non-empty or removing the preference when appropriate).
  - JabRefFrame and other callers were updated to obtain FileHistory via prefs.getGuiPreferences().getFileHistory() and to clear lastFilesOpened directly when needed.

- MetaDataDiff and metadata UI
  - MetaDataDiff now returns an EnumSet<Difference> (with a new Difference enum) instead of a list of localized strings. The enum values describe the type of metadata change (PROTECTED, GROUPS_ALTERED, ENCODING, etc.).
  - MetadataChangeDetailsView was updated to map Difference enum values to localized strings in the UI via getDifferenceString(...).

- Other changes and cleanups
  - GeneralTabViewModel now reads and writes language via preferencesService.getGeneralPreferences().getLanguage() and sets language through generalPreferences.
  - RelatedArticlesTab: MrDLibFetcher constructed with language from preferencesService.getGeneralPreferences().getLanguage().name()
  - Field formatter classes: minor optimizations and modernization (equals using pattern matching, safer equality checks, toString formatting improved).
  - Various small stream->toList() conversions and listener updates.

Migration notes / breaking changes

- Update any custom code that relied on the old FileHistory API (getHistory(), getFileAt(), isEmpty()) to use the list API (FileHistory.of(...), get(index), size(), isEmpty(), iteration).
- PreferencesService no longer exposes getLanguage()/setLanguage()/clearEditedFiles(); use getGeneralPreferences().getLanguage()/setLanguage(...) and getGuiPreferences().getLastFilesOpened()/getFileHistory() instead.
- MetaDataDiff.getDifferences now returns EnumSet<MetaDataDiff.Difference> rather than List<String>. Callers must map enum values to localized strings themselves (MetadataChangeDetailsView shows an example).

Tests

- FileHistoryTest updated to assert against the list-based API.

What changed
- UI: GeneralProperties.fxml
  - Added switch buttons (icon buttons) next to each directory field with associated tooltips and JabRefIconView glyphs.

  - Hooked up listeners to update the icon (ABSOLUTE_PATH / RELATIVE_PATH) and tooltip depending on whether the entered path is absolute.
  - Disable switches when the library is unsaved (no database path present).
  - Wiring for browse and switch actions to the ViewModel.

- ViewModel / behaviour: GeneralPropertiesViewModel.java
  - Added togglePath(StringProperty) implementation that converts between absolute and relative path forms using the saved library path (relativizes to the library parent when appropriate). Handles InvalidPathException and shows error dialogs.
  - getBrowseDirectory() and setDirectory() updated to prefer sensible defaults (working directory, resolve relative to library when saved) and to store selected directories as relative when inside the library path.
  - Directory validation and user notifications when configured paths cannot be resolved.
  - Existing validation and browse flows integrated with the new UI.

- Icons: IconTheme.java

- Localization: JabRef_en.properties
  - Added localized strings for the new tooltip messages and directory labels: "Switch to absolute path: converts the path to an absolute path.", "Switch to relative path: converts the path to a relative path.", and entries for Library-specific/User-specific/LaTeX file directory text.

text:
Add field-presence consistency check and plain-text report writer

This PR introduces a new consistency check that detects fields present in some but not all entries of the same entry type, together with a plain-text reporter and comprehensive tests.

What was added
- BibliographyConsistencyCheck: collects fields per entry type (fields-in-any-entry and fields-in-all-entries), identifies unique fields (present in some but not all entries) and builds results grouped by entry type. Results include the set of unique fields and a sorted collection of differing entries.
- BibliographyConsistencyCheckResultTxtWriter: writes the findings as a formatted plain-text table. It computes column widths, outputs a header and separator line, prints rows for differing entries using symbols for required/optional/unknown/absent fields, and prints a legend. A porcelain mode suppresses header and legend for machine-readable output.
- Sorting utilities used by the writer/check: BibEntryByCitationKeyComparator and BibEntryByFieldsComparator, combined via FieldComparatorStack to produce deterministic ordering of differing entries (citation key then fields).
- Localization keys (JabRef_en.properties) for labels used by the TXT writer.
- Unit tests (BibliographyConsistencyCheckResultTxtWriterTest): verify output for multiple scenarios including simple differences, unknown/custom fields, very long citation keys, complex multi-type libraries (and ordering), and porcelain vs non-porcelain outputs. One disabled manual test is provided for local report generation.

Files changed/added
- jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/quality/consistency/BibliographyConsistencyCheck.java (new consistency check and result records)
- jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/quality/consistency/BibliographyConsistencyCheckResultTxtWriter.java (TXT writer)
- jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/bibtex/comparator/BibEntryByCitationKeyComparator.java (comparator)
- jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/bibtex/comparator/BibEntryByFieldsComparator.java (comparator)
- jablib/src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties (localization strings)
- jablib/src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/quality/consistency/BibliographyConsistencyCheckResultTxtWriterTest.java (tests)

Notes
- The check intentionally focuses on presence/absence of fields across entries and does not validate whether fields are required/allowed by the entry type; the TXT output uses symbols to indicate required/optional/unknown/absent fields.
- The TXT writer supports a porcelain mode to facilitate scripting/automation.

This change adds a useful diagnostic for spotting inconsistent metadata in libraries and provides a readable (and scriptable) textual report for both interactive and automated use.

Avoid static logger initialization before log configuration

What I changed
- Removed/avoided static Logger fields and replaced their usages with LoggerFactory.getLogger(Class) calls at call sites in DefaultDesktop and Linux to prevent the logger from being initialized too early.
- Updated several logging calls to pass exceptions as parameters instead of concatenating to messages where applicable.
- Added explanatory JavaDoc to DefaultDesktop, Linux, OSX and Windows explaining why static loggers are not used (Logger must be configured in Launcher#addLogToDisk; tinylog configuration becomes immutable after the first log entry).
- Added imports of org.jabref.cli.Launcher where referenced by the new Javadocs.

Why
- tinylog configuration becomes immutable once the first log entry is issued. Having static logger instances in these classes caused the logger to be created before Launcher.addLogToDisk could configure logging to disk. Moving to on-demand LoggerFactory.getLogger(...) calls avoids freezing logger config too early and ensures logging configuration from Launcher is respected.

Files changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/desktop/os/DefaultDesktop.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/desktop/os/Linux.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/desktop/os/OSX.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/desktop/os/Windows.java

Notes
- No functional behavior change beyond logging initialization timing and slight improvements to logging call sites. This is a safety/fix for correct log configuration at startup.

- The change is backward compatible: legacy column names are mapped to the current representation where possible, and unknown names fall back to a safe default.
- No user action is required, but users with custom/old column configurations should now see their layout restored more reliably.

- Ensured all TextField instances in SimpleEditor, CitationKeyEditor, PersonsEditor, and MarkdownEditor have their id set correctly so the last field in a tab can be identified.

- MarkdownEditor

6. Test both single-line and multi-line fields (SimpleEditor, PersonsEditor, MarkdownEditor) to confirm consistent behavior.

text:
Introduce a CountingUndoManager exposing JavaFX properties for undo/redo and change tracking, and wire Undo/Redo actions to those properties

What changed
- Added CountingUndoManager (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/undo/CountingUndoManager.java)
  - Tracks an internal balance and an "unchanged" point so callers can detect whether the library has changed (markUnchanged(), hasChanged()).
  - Exposes JavaFX properties: balanceProperty, undoableProperty and redoableProperty (read-only accessors provided) so the UI can bind to undo/redo availability.
  - All mutation methods are synchronized for thread-safety (addEdit, undo, redo, markUnchanged).

- Updated UndoAction and RedoAction (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/undo/UndoAction.java, src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/undo/RedoAction.java)
  - Actions now bind their executable state to the active LibraryTab's undo/redo properties provided by CountingUndoManager, so the commands enable/disable automatically.
  - After performing an undo/redo the actions notify the user (localized "Undo"/"Redo" messages) and call libraryTab.markChangedOrUnChanged() to refresh the library-changed state.

Why
- Exposing undo/redo availability as observable properties simplifies UI binding and keeps the enabled state of undo/redo actions in sync with the underlying UndoManager.
- The balance/unchanged-point tracking allows the app to know whether a library has unsaved changes after undo/redo operations.

Notes
- User-visible notifications are shown after successful undo/redo and informative messages are shown if nothing can be undone/redone.

text:
Add application startup entry point and launcher

This patch introduces the main JavaFX application entry point and a small launcher wrapper, and wires them into the Gradle configuration.

Key changes

- Added JabRefMain (src/main/java/org/jabref/JabRefMain.java)
  - Implements Application#start to initialize JabRef on launch.
  - Performs Java version validation (shows an error dialog and exits for unsupported versions).
  - Installs a fallback exception handler.
  - Initializes preferences and runs preference migrations.
  - Configures proxy settings (including authentication) and registers proxy authenticator.
  - Starts background tasks and applies preferences (load journal abbreviations, import/export formats, protected terms, newline preference).
  - Processes command line arguments using ArgumentProcessor and handles multiple instances via RemoteClient/RemotePreferences (passes args to an already running instance or starts the remote listener).
  - Logs parse errors and shuts down cleanly on failure.
  - Overrides stop() to stop background tasks and shutdown thread pools.

- Added JabRefLauncher (src/main/java/org/jabref/JabRefLauncher.java)
  - Lightweight launcher class that calls JabRefMain.main(...) to keep the launcher name consistent with other Java apps.

- Updated Gradle configuration (build.gradle)
  - mainClassName references the module-aware launcher: "$moduleName/org.jabref.JabRefLauncher".
  - No behavioral changes to build logic beyond pointing the main class at the new launcher.

Why

Separating the thin launcher and the JavaFX Application class improves consistency with other Java applications and gives a clear, testable entry point for application startup logic. JabRefMain centralizes initialization and startup concerns (version checks, preferences, proxy, argument handling, remote instance management) and ensures proper shutdown of background services.

Notes

- The Java version check uses BuildInfo (from Gradle-configured version requirements) and will show an error dialog / exit for unsupported JVMs.
- Remote instance handling relies on existing RemotePreferences/RemoteClient API.
- No changes to user-facing functionality beyond startup/initialization refactor; no new dependencies added.

Files changed:
- build.gradle (main class configured)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/JabRefMain.java (new Application entry point)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/JabRefLauncher.java (new launcher wrapper)

Closes #4913

Summary

This PR fixes a bug where arXiv (and similar) links sometimes returned HTML instead of the actual PDF because a HEAD request encountered an HTTP redirect and the content-type was read from the original (HTML) response. It ensures redirects are correctly handled for MIME-type detection and improves URL download behaviour.

What I changed

- URLDownload
  - getMimeType() now returns Optional<String> and performs a manual redirect-following loop for HEAD requests (Unirest's HEAD + followRedirects does not behave the same as GET). This follows the "location" header up to a small retry limit and obtains the content-type from the final target.
  - Added MAX_RETRIES to avoid infinite redirect loops.
  - Added a static Unirest configuration block to enable redirects, cookie management and set the default User-Agent.
  - Improved fallbacks: GET response and local URLConnection are used if HEAD doesn't yield a content type. All paths return Optional.empty() when not available.
  - canBeReached() and isMimeType() were updated to use the new Optional-based getMimeType().
  - openConnection() now disconnects the previous HttpURLConnection before following redirects by recursion and streamlines client/server error handling.

- DownloadLinkedFileAction
  - Minor refactor: inferFileTypeFromMimeType() now uses Optional chaining to simplify logic.

- Tests and build
  - Added wiremock-standalone test dependency to reliably mock HTTP responses in unit tests.
  - Updated URLDownloadTest: added a redirect test using WireMock to verify that following redirects downloads the final PDF content, and adjusted assertions to use Optional.
  - Updated DownloadLinkedFileActionTest: replaced external HTML URLs with a local WireMock server to test HTML content-type behaviour and updated file handling to use Path/Files APIs.
  - Added setup/teardown for WireMockServer in tests.

- CHANGELOG
  - Documented the fix: "We fixed an issue where HTML instead of the fulltext pdf was downloaded when importing arXiv entries." (#4913)

Why

arXiv often redirects (301/302/...) to a final PDF URL. A naive HEAD request to the original URL returned headers for the redirecting page (HTML), causing the code to treat the link as HTML and either skip downloading or store an incorrect link. By following redirects (manually for HEAD) and taking the content-type from the final destination, we correctly detect PDFs and other content types and avoid downloading the wrong resource.

Notes

- Tests use WireMock to simulate redirects and content types. The build.gradle change adds wiremock-standalone as recommended to avoid compatibility issues.
- The getMimeType signature change is internal; callers were updated accordingly in this PR.
