Summary:
Fixes a bug where citation keys on existing/imported entries were unintentionally overwritten during import.

What was happening:
- The import logic always regenerated and assigned a citation key for entries, even when an entry already had a user-provided key. This caused existing citation keys to be lost during import.

What this change does:
- Update import flow so citation keys are preserved when an entry already contains a key.
- Only generate or replace a citation key when the entry has none (or when an explicit overwrite option is requested).
- Add unit/integration tests that cover importing entries with existing keys and ensure they are not changed.
- Ensure duplicate-key detection still runs and only triggers when appropriate (no silent overwrites).

Why this is safe:
- Preserves user-provided data and avoids surprising data loss on import.
- Keeps existing behavior for key generation when entries lack keys.

Testing:
- New tests added for import scenarios with and without existing citation keys.
- Manual import verification to confirm keys are retained unless overwrite is intentional.

Notes for users:
- No migration required. If you relied on the previous (incorrect) behavior of always regenerating keys, you can still force overwrite via the explicit overwrite option where applicable.

Files changed (high level):
- Import handler/logic: guard to skip key generation when a key exists.
- Tests: added cases for preserving citation keys on import.
- Minor docs/comments clarifying import behavior.

Summary:
Convert stored and displayed absolute file paths to relative paths in the Recent Files feature when the files are located inside the current project/workspace.

Why:
- Improve portability of recent-file lists across machines and repository moves.
- Reduce exposure of absolute user or system paths in the UI.
- Keep Recent Files consistent with project-relative workflows.

What changed:
- When adding a file to Recent Files, if the file is under any known workspace/project root, store its path relative to that root instead of an absolute path.
- On load, resolve stored relative paths back to absolute paths using the currently available workspace roots. If resolution fails (file not under any workspace), fall back to the stored absolute path.
- UI now displays relative paths where available; the full absolute path is shown on hover/tooltip for clarity when needed.
- Added a migration/compatibility step: existing absolute entries are converted to relative when a matching workspace root is found during load.
- Edge cases handled: multiple workspace roots (prefer the matching root), remote/URI locations and symlinks (resolved according to existing path resolution rules), and missing files (kept in the list but shown as unavailable).

Tests and docs:
- Unit and integration tests added/updated to cover storing, loading, resolution, UI display, and migration behavior.
- Documentation updated to mention the new relative-path behavior and the fallback rules.

Notes:
- Behavior is intentionally conservative: we only convert to relative when a clear workspace root can be identified; otherwise absolute paths remain untouched.
- No changes to user-facing settings; behavior is automatic and backward-compatible.

Summary

Fixes #6541 — avoid marking the library as modified when opening Library > Library Properties. The change removes an event trigger that previously set the saving/dirty status when save actions metadata was read or written.

Problem

Opening Library Properties caused a comment like the following to be added to .bib/.sav and triggered a postChange event, which made the UI show the library as modified (unsaved):

@Comment{jabref-meta: saveActions:disabled;
all-text-fields[remove_unicode_ligatures]
date[normalize_date]
month[normalize_month]
pages[normalize_page_numbers]
;}

This was caused by calling postChange() inside MetaData.setSaveActions(...), which made the application think the database changed simply by reading/updating metadata for the save actions.

What I changed

- Removed the postChange() call from setSaveActions in src/main/java/org/jabref/model/metadata/MetaData.java so that setting saveActions no longer fires the global change event.

Summary

This PR renames the provider label for OpenAI to OpenAI (or API Compatible) in the AI preferences provider dropdown and updates the AI summary processing message to show the model selected by the user. The AI chat footer/provider indicator was also adjusted to reflect the updated label when using an OpenAPI / API-compatible endpoint.

This PR fixes several issues in the entry editor and related areas:

- Reactivates next/previous entry shortcuts when the entry editor is active (default changed to Alt+Up / Alt+Down). This restores the behavior reported in #4104.
- Preserves focus inside text fields when switching between entries in the entry editor. When switching entries, the previously focused field is restored after the editor content is reinitialized.

  - Capture the currently focused child field name before rebuilding the editor UI and restore focus via Platform.runLater after the new content is set.

Summary
- Add unified, extensible context menus and supporting infrastructure for field editors.

What this PR does
- Introduces ContextMenuAddable interface to represent editor controls that can expose additional "add" operations through their context menu.
- Adds EditorMenus and several context-menu actions (including ClearField) to provide consistent actions across editors.
- Adds ProtectedTermsMenu to allow managing protected terms (used e.g. for journal names) from the editor context menu.
- Refactors field editor classes to use the new context-menu infrastructure: EditorTextField, EditorTextArea, SimpleEditor, PersonsEditor and JournalEditor now integrate the new menus.
- Introduces EditorValidator to centralize validation logic for editor fields.
- Adds FieldEditors factory to centralize creation/initialization of various field editor controls.
- Refactors JournalEditor to move logic into JournalEditorViewModel and to integrate protected-terms handling and improved behavior for journal abbreviation management.
- Updates FieldsEditorTab to use FieldEditors and to hook up the new editor capabilities.
- Small model change in InternalBibtexFields to support the updated editor behavior.

Why
- Provides a consistent user experience across different field editors (same clear/add/protected-terms options available where applicable).
- Makes it easier to extend context menus in the future by centralizing menu construction and editor capabilities.
- Separates UI and logic for the journal editor (ViewModel), improving maintainability and testability.
- Consolidates validation logic into a single place.

Impacts
- User-facing: new context menu entries (Clear field, Protected Terms and other addable actions) in various editors; improved journal editing UX.
- Code: refactors and API additions are internal to GUI/editor components; should not affect external APIs beyond editor creation.

Notes for reviewers
- Focus on: context menu construction (EditorMenus), correctness of ClearField and ProtectedTermsMenu actions, the JournalEditor ⇄ JournalEditorViewModel split, and integration in FieldsEditorTab.
- No functional tests included in this PR; manual testing of editor context menus and journal abbreviation/protected terms workflows recommended.

Add ArXiv fetcher implementation, supporting paged and id-based searches and fulltext PDF discovery

- Implement ArXiv fetcher (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ArXiv.java)
  - Implements FulltextFetcher, PagedSearchBasedFetcher, IdBasedFetcher and IdFetcher<ArXivIdentifier>.
  - Builds queries for the arXiv API, strips accents from queries and supports id_list filtering.
  - Calls the arXiv Atom API, handles 400 responses by parsing returned error entries, and wraps failures in FetcherException.
  - Parses Atom XML results into an ArXivEntry inner class which extracts title, authors, abstract, published date, categories, DOI, journal ref, primary category and PDF link.
  - Converts ArXivEntry to BibEntry (sets eprint, eprinttype, eprintclass, date, DOI, abstract, title, authors, keywords and linked PDF files).
  - Provides performSearchPaged using ArXivQueryTransformer to transform lucene queries and filters results by start/end year.
  - Provides performSearchById, findIdentifier and getTrustLevel (PREPRINT).
  - Includes a small debug print of the constructed query.

- Extend and reuse string utilities (src/main/java/org/jabref/model/strings/StringUtil.java)
  - Utility methods used by the fetcher are included/available: accent stripping, brace handling and line break unification.
  - Added helper removeAllBraces and removeBracesAroundCapitalizedWords to normalize titles for matching.

- Add comprehensive unit tests for the ArXiv fetcher (src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ArXivTest.java)
  - Tests for findFullText by DOI, eprint (with and without arXiv: prefix), title, author+title combination and various failure cases.
  - Tests for performSearchById with multiple ID formats (old style hep-ex, modern 4- and 5-digit ids, version suffixes, and URL inputs) and malformed/empty ids.
  - Tests for phrase search, boolean AND search and matching titles that contain curly braces and accented characters.
  - Verifies conversion to BibEntry and returned fields (date, authors, eprintclass, DOI, journal reference and file link).

Notes:
- The fetcher removes accents from user queries before calling the arXiv API to avoid problems with accented characters.
- The code contains a temporary System.err.println(query) for debugging the constructed query.

text:
Summary

This PR fixes an issue where the magnifier (search) icon did not follow JabRef's color scheme and stayed black despite being configured as purple in code. The root cause was that the toolbar/search icon was provided as a non-colorable raster asset; it has been replaced with a vector-based icon and its fill is now bound to the application's icon color so it respects theme and color-scheme changes.

What I changed

- Replaced the raster magnifier asset with a colorable SVG/vector icon.
- Updated the icon registration/loading so the magnifier is returned as a colorable graphic (SvgIcon/Glyph) instead of an ImageView of a PNG.
- Bound the icon's fill/fillProperty to the application/theme icon color value so it updates dynamically with theme changes.
- Adjusted CSS variables / styles where needed to expose the color used for toolbar/search icons.
- Added a small unit test verifying that the icon manager returns a colorable magnifier icon (and that its color property can be modified).

Why this fixes the issue

Raster images (PNGs) do not support tinting through CSS/fill and therefore will not inherit or change color when the theme changes; converting to a vector/SVG icon allows us to programmatically or via CSS set the icon's fill, making it follow the JabRef color scheme.

Manual testing performed

- Verified the magnifier icon is purple in the default theme (matches code configuration).
- Switched between light/dark themes and verified the icon color updates accordingly.
- Confirmed the icon color changes when the toolbar/icon color setting is changed.

Checklist

- [x] Change in CHANGELOG.md described
- [x] Tests created for changes (icon manager unit test)
- [x] Screenshots added (showing icon in different themes)
- [x] Manually tested changed features in running JabRef
- [ ] Check documentation status (created issue if help page needs update)

Notes

If there are other places using a PNG magnifier (or other raster icons) that should follow the theme as well, those can be migrated in a follow-up PR using the same pattern.

Switch LaTeX→Unicode normalization to NFC and add tests for ordinal superscripts

What I changed:
- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/strings/LatexToUnicodeAdapter.java: use Normalizer.Form.NFC instead of NFKC. This prevents compatibility decomposition that would strip or collapse styled Unicode characters (e.g. mathematical italic letters and superscripts).
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/layout/format/LatexToUnicodeFormatterTest.java: update the expected output for \textit{text> to the corresponding mathematical-italic Unicode characters, and add new tests that verify conversion of ordinal superscripts (1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 9th) produced by \textsuperscript{...}.

Why:
- NFKC performs compatibility decomposition which can normalize away visual/stylistic Unicode characters produced by the LaTeX→Unicode conversion. Switching to NFC preserves those characters so the converter can return stylized Unicode (superscripts, mathematical italic glyphs) as expected.

Notes:
- This PR is a follow-up to issues/PRs referenced in the original report (issues #2596 and PR #2601) and adds tests that reproduce and assert the desired behavior for ordinals and textit output.

This PR refactors the entry editor field editors and context-menu handling to support both single-line and multi-line text inputs and to centralize journal-abbreviation access.

Key changes
- Introduced ContextMenuAddable interface to defer context menu creation using Supplier<List<MenuItem>> (reduces allocations when scrolling with entry editor open).
- Added EditorTextField (a single-line text input) that implements ContextMenuAddable. It implements smart TAB behavior (Tab/Shift+Tab traversal and Ctrl+Tab to insert a tab) and integrates with the custom context-menu mechanism.
- EditorTextArea now implements ContextMenuAddable and its addToContextMenu method was made consistent (signature and override).
- Generalized validation: EditorValidator now accepts javafx.scene.control.TextInputControl (works for both TextArea and TextField) instead of only EditorTextArea.
- Context menus generalized to accept TextInputControl instead of TextArea: EditorMenus, ClearField, ProtectedTermsMenu and associated callers updated.
- Field editors updated to support single-line fields:
  - InternalBibtexFields: added a SINGLE_LINE_FIELDS set and isSingleLineField(fieldName) helper.
  - FieldEditors.getForField now accepts a JournalAbbreviationRepository and returns editors that can be single-line when appropriate. It also computes isSingleLine once and passes it to relevant editors.
  - SimpleEditor and PersonsEditor now create either EditorTextField or EditorTextArea based on isSingleLine and use TextInputControl everywhere. A legacy SimpleEditor constructor retained for compatibility.
  - AutoCompletionTextInputBinding usage updated to work with TextInputControl.
- Journal abbreviation handling refactor: replace JournalAbbreviationLoader + JournalAbbreviationPreferences usage with a JournalAbbreviationRepository passed through constructors and methods (FieldEditors, JournalEditor, JournalEditorViewModel). JournalEditorViewModel now calls repository methods directly.
- FieldsEditorTab updated to pass journalAbbreviationLoader.getRepository(...) instead of passing loader and preferences separately.

Why
- Support for single-line editors (e.g. author, year) improves UX by using text fields where appropriate.
- Unifying on TextInputControl simplifies validators and context menus and reduces code duplication.
- Deferring context menu creation saves allocations and improves performance when scrolling large tables.
- Centralizing journal abbreviation access as a repository simplifies code and avoids passing loader + preferences around.

Notes
- API changes: FieldEditors.getForField signature changed (now takes JournalAbbreviationRepository and reordered params) and some editor constructors changed accordingly. Internal code updated to match these changes.
- No behavior changes intended other than the improved single-line handling and context-menu allocation optimization.

Improve backup comparison to consider timestamps and add tests

What changed
- BackupManager.backupFileDiffers(Path): Now checks the last-modified time of the latest backup and the current file before comparing contents. If the backup is not newer than the current file, it is treated as non-different. If timestamps cannot be read, the method logs the error and returns false (no warning). Content comparison still uses Files.mismatch when the backup is newer.
- Added import of java.nio.file.attribute.FileTime where needed.

Why
- Previously any existing .bak file could cause a perceived difference even when it was older than the current file. By requiring the backup to be newer than the original before doing a content comparison, we avoid false positives and unnecessary warnings to the user.

Tests
- Updated existing test to use local Path variables for test resources.
- Added two tests:
  - bakFileWithNewerTimeStampLeadsToDiff: asserts that a newer .bak containing changes is detected as different.
  - bakFileWithOlderTimeStampDoesNotLeadToDiff: sets the .bak file timestamp to very old and asserts it is NOT considered different even if contents differ.

Notes
- IOExceptions when reading timestamps are logged and the method conservatively treats the backup as non-different (no warning) except for content comparison errors where true is returned to force user investigation.

Summary:
Fixes incorrect parsing of author metadata imported from ACM sources. The previous parser produced broken author lists in a number of real-world ACM records (merged names, lost suffixes, incorrect splitting around affiliation markers and conjunctions).

What I changed:
- Reworked the ACM author parsing logic to robustly split author lists while preserving name components (given, middle, family, suffix) and affiliation markers.
- Normalized separators (commas, semicolons, the word "and", and common parenthetical affiliation patterns) before tokenization to avoid splitting inside names.
- Added handling for common edge cases: "et al.", last-name-first formats, hyphenated/accented names, and suffixes like Jr./Sr./III.
- Added unit tests and updated example fixtures that cover previously failing cases and a variety of real ACM author strings.

Why this matters:
- Fixes numerous bugs where multiple authors were concatenated or incorrectly split, resulting in bad metadata in downstream systems.
- Improves fidelity of imported author data without changing the public author model or APIs.

Testing:
- New unit tests cover the problematic records and edge cases.
- Ran parser across existing ACM fixtures to verify no regressions.

Notes:
- No breaking API changes. Performance impact is negligible.
- If you have sample ACM records that still parse incorrectly, please attach them to the PR for further tuning.

- MalformedURLException and download errors are handled with user-facing dialogs.

Re-adds the UI display for group hit counts when the count is zero. Previously empty groups could appear without any hit indicator, causing confusion and making it hard to tell which groups had been considered but had no results.

What this change does:
- Restores the rendering of the group hits indicator/badge for groups with zero hits.
- Adjusts the component logic so a 0 value is treated as a valid count (not falsy/omitted).
- Adds/updates tests to cover zero-count rendering and ensures snapshots reflect the restored UI.
- Small CSS/accessibility tweaks to ensure the zero-count badge is visible and announced to screen readers.

Why:
- Improves discoverability and consistency of the groups list by clearly indicating groups that had no hits instead of leaving them visually ambiguous.
- Addresses user reports/bug where empty groups appeared without any hit marker.

4. Run unit/integration tests and confirm the new/updated tests pass and snapshots are correct.

Notes/risks:
- Change is localized to group hits rendering logic; low risk for unrelated areas.
- Accessibility: zero-count indicators include an aria-label so screen readers announce the count.

Group and keyword merging improvements

- GroupMerger
  - Broaden separator recognition to accept commas and semicolons (regex changed to "[;,]\s*").
  - Trim input group strings before processing.
  - Trim each parsed group token before deduplication so that semantically identical groups with extra whitespace are merged correctly.
  - Preserve joining with the existing GROUPS_SEPARATOR (", ").

- KeywordMerger
  - Added separator detection logic to infer the actual keyword separator character from the provided keyword strings.
  - If both sides provide a separator and they differ, an IllegalArgumentException is thrown to prevent merging with ambiguous separators.
  - When a separator is detected, it is set on bibEntryPreferences before merging; the merge then uses that delimiter.
  - detectSeparator enforces that only one non-alphanumeric, non-whitespace separator is present in a string and throws IllegalArgumentException if multiple different separators or no valid separator are found.

Notes/Risks
- KeywordMerger now throws IllegalArgumentException on mixed or missing separators in inputs; callers should be prepared to handle these errors.
- Group merging now normalizes whitespace around items which may change the deduplication behavior for inputs that previously included extra spaces around group names.

Summary

Fix module declarations for the lsp4j modules to address JPMS-related build and runtime issues.

What I changed

- Added/fixed module-info.java files across the lsp4j modules.
- Corrected module names and ensured exports/opens reflect the actual public API surface.
- Added/adjusted requires and requires transitive entries so dependent modules can resolve necessary types.
- Resolved split-package and visibility problems that caused runtime linkage errors on the module path.
- Updated the build configuration to compile modules on the module path and included necessary automatic-module fallbacks where appropriate.
- Ran and updated unit tests to reflect the module changes.

Why this is needed

Projects using the Java module system (Java 9+) were encountering compilation or runtime failures due to incomplete or incorrect module descriptors. These fixes make lsp4j modules resolvable on the module path, maintain proper encapsulation, and avoid accidental exposure of internal packages.

Compatibility and migration notes

- These changes are intended to be source-compatible; public APIs have not been changed, only their module declarations.
- If you previously relied on accessing internal packages via the classpath, you may need to move to the classpath or adapt to the encapsulation enforced by JPMS.
- Consumers on Java 8 are unaffected.

Testing and verification

- Build the project with -p (module path) to verify module resolution.
- Run the test suite to confirm no regressions.
- Manual verification: start any LSP servers/clients that depend on these modules and confirm no linkage exceptions occur.

Notes

If you see any unresolved modules or split-package warnings after merging, please report them with the specific module and package names so they can be addressed.

Summary:
Add a separate launcher to fix extension import when running JabRef as a snap.

What this change does:
- Adds a dedicated launcher used by the browser extension to perform imports without launching a second JabRef instance.
- Prevents the extension from passing CLI options to a newly spawned JabRef process, which previously produced a long list of parsing errors.

Why:
The browser extension (JabRef-Browser-Extension#165) and the snap packaging caused an extra JabRef process to be started when importing from the extension. That produced spurious CLI parsing errors (reported on Gitter and in issue #5537). Providing a separate launcher avoids starting a new instance and removes those errors.

Testing / Verification:
- Manually tested in a running snap build of JabRef: triggering an import from the browser extension now succeeds without the CLI parsing errors previously observed.

Related issues:
- Fixes #5537
- Fixes JabRef/JabRef-Browser-Extension#165

Notes:
- No automated tests or changelog entry included in this PR.
- Packaging may need to include the new launcher in the snap; please ensure snap metadata is updated accordingly if required.

Fixes an issue where saving a library could trigger a "metadata changed" message even though nothing was changed. The root cause was missing or incorrect equals/hashCode/toString implementations in several metadata-related classes which made metadata comparisons report spurious differences.

What I changed

- Implemented proper equals/hashCode/toString methods and fixed equals logic where needed:
  - FieldFormatterCleanup: corrected equals signature/logic

- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/metadata/MetaData.java

Metadata equality checks are used to determine whether anything meaningful changed before saving. text:
This PR contains several related improvements to preferences handling and BibTeX entry serialization, plus associated tests and UI wiring.

Key changes
- JabRefPreferences
  - Added utility methods to store/retrieve string arrays (putStringArray/getStringArray) and other helpers used by preference-backed features.
  - Improved special-field handling (putBracesAroundCapitals / non-wrappable fields) and exposed getters/setters for default encoding.
  - Added/initialized many default preference values (value delimiters, newline, external file types, encoding, etc.) and logic to update special field handling.
  - Implemented import/export of preferences (XML) and memory-stick mode export on flush.

- BibEntryWriter
  - Reworked writing logic to honor modified vs unmodified entries (write original serialization when unchanged, reformat only when changed).
  - Field names are written in lower case (consistent biber-style choice) and aligned: the value column is padded to align values based on the longest field name present.
  - Required fields, optional fields and remaining fields are written in the intended order; remaining fields are sorted alphabetically.
  - Key formatting and comma/newline handling refined to match expected output.

- LatexFieldFormatter
  - Uses preferences for value delimiters and string-resolution behavior (RESOLVE_STRINGS_ALL_FIELDS and DO_NOT_RESOLVE_STRINGS_FOR).
  - Normalizes newlines and supports wrapping/bracing logic (putBracesAroundCapitals) before formatting.
  - Improved parsing and safe handling of # string labels and brace checking.

- FileTab (preferences UI)
  - Exposed UI elements for newline separator and value delimiter selection; storing the newline preference updates Globals.NEWLINE immediately.
  - Wires resolve-strings radio buttons and autosave settings to preferences.

- Tests
  - Added/updated BibEntryWriterTest covering many scenarios: serialization, round-trip parsing/writing (with/without extra newlines), camel-cased original fields resulting in lower-case output, month special syntax (#mar#), multiple writes without modification, and alignment when adding longer fields.

Why
- Enforces consistent field-name casing and aligned output for better readability and compatibility (biber-style lower-case field names).
- Makes formatting behavior configurable via preferences (delimiters, string resolution, braces, newline style).
- Ensures we only reformat entries that were actually modified, preserving original formatting where possible.
- Adds tests to prevent regressions in serialization and preferences-driven formatting behavior.

Notes
- Some method/parameter names retain older spellings (e.g., intendation) to preserve compatibility with existing calls.
- Preference-related defaults and external file-type handling are centralized in JabRefPreferences; callers should use these APIs to read/write preferences.

Summary: Remove all field saving options and simplify BibTeX serialization logic. This PR removes related preferences and GUI controls, simplifies the field formatter and writer, and updates tests and the changelog to reflect the new behavior.

Key changes:
- General
  - Remove field saving customization options (sorting, user-defined order, include empty fields, wrap fields, same-column spacing).
  - Entries are only reformatted on save if they were changed during the session (no mandatory reformat of the entire database).
  - Field keys are written in lower case and an equals sign is appended to the field key position (i.e., "field = value").
  - Indentation/alignment is computed per entry (based on the longest field name in that entry) instead of a global alignment.

- JabRefPreferences.java
  - Remove constants and default preferences for WRITEFIELD_ADDSPACES, WRITEFIELD_SORTSTYLE, WRITEFIELD_USERDEFINEDORDER, WRITEFIELD_WRAPFIELD, INCLUDE_EMPTY_FIELDS and their defaults.

- BibEntryWriter.java
  - Remove complex field-order modes and caches. Always write required fields first and remaining fields afterwards.
  - Avoid rewriting entries that have not changed by using the parsed serialization.
  - Compute indentation per entry and write the equals sign together with the field key.
  - Simplify field display name handling and remove global max field length usage.

- LatexFieldFormatter.java
  - Remove wrap-on-write behavior and the WRITEFIELD_WRAPFIELD preference usage. Field content formatter always delegates to the parser without optional wrapping.

- FileTab.java (GUI)
  - Remove UI controls related to the removed field saving options: include empty fields, same-column spacing, wrap fields, and the field order radio/user-defined order controls.
  - Adjust loading and storing of preferences to no longer reference removed keys.

- Tests (BibEntryWriterTest.java)
  - Update expectations to the new formatting style (lower-case field names, equals appended early, per-entry alignment).
  - Ensure tests set BibTeX mode explicitly where needed and add a new test for adding a field with longer name to verify per-entry alignment.

Changelog: Document removal of field saving options and the change to only reformat modified entries.

Rationale: As decided in issue #116, remove the historic field saving options to reduce complexity and maintain a single, consistent serialization style.

text:
Integrate SpotBugs static analysis and address reported issues

What this PR does:
- Adds SpotBugs integration to the project build and CI so static analysis runs automatically.
- Adds a SpotBugs configuration and baseline/exclude file (spotbugs-exclude.xml) to suppress known/legacy findings.
- Fixes a number of high- and medium-priority SpotBugs findings (NPE risks, resource leaks, incorrect equals/hashCode patterns, concurrency issues, and unsafe casts).
- Updates CI pipeline to run SpotBugs and fail the build on new high/medium severity issues to prevent regressions.

Files/changes of note:
- Build configuration: added SpotBugs plugin configuration and report settings.
- config/spotbugs-exclude.xml (or equivalent): baseline exclusions for legacy findings we will triage later.
- Multiple source files updated to fix bugs flagged by SpotBugs (null checks, try-with-resources, synchronization or atomic usage, and type-safety fixes).
- CI pipeline script updated to include SpotBugs step.

How to run locally:
- Maven: mvn spotbugs:check (or mvn -Dspotbugs.failOnError=true spotbugs:check)
- Gradle: ./gradlew spotbugsMain spotbugsTest
- Reports are generated under target/spotbugs* or build/reports/spotbugs/ depending on the build tool.

Notes & follow-ups:
- The baseline/exclude file is intentionally conservative to avoid noisy failures on this initial rollout. We should incrementally remove exclusions and address findings in follow-up PRs.
- Prioritize remaining warnings by severity and potential runtime impact.
- If you see a SpotBugs change that looks suspicious, please call it out so we can ensure fixes are correct and well-tested.

Summary

This PR adds a small set of example questions to the AI Chat UI to help users quickly try the chat feature. It introduces a compact visual row with a label "Try with examples" and three clickable example prompts. Clicking any example sends the prompt into the chat input flow.

- UI (FXML)
  - Added an HBox after the chat history that contains:
    - A label (exQuestionLabel) with the text "Try with examples".
    - Three Hyperlink elements (exQuestion1, exQuestion2, exQuestion3) with example prompts:
      - "What is the goal of the paper?"
      - "Which methods were used in the research?"
      - "What are the key findings?"
  - Consolidated FXML imports for brevity (<?import javafx.scene.control.*?> and <?import javafx.scene.layout.*?>).

- Stylesheet (Base.css)
  - Added styles for the new elements:

- Java (AiChatComponent.java)
  - Added FXML fields for the three hyperlinks and the label.
  - Added initializeExampleQuestions() to wire the FXML label/text values (keeps current behavior but centralizes initialization).
  - Added three @FXML handlers (sendExampleQuestion1Prompt, sendExampleQuestion2Prompt, sendExampleQuestion3Prompt) which call onSendMessage(...) with the corresponding example text.

Why

- Improve discoverability and first-run experience of the AI chat by providing immediate example prompts that users can click to test the feature without having to type a question.

Notes / Limitations

- The three example questions are currently hardcoded in the FXML (not generated by the AI model). If desired in the future, they can be made configurable or localized.

- Backward compatible: normal behavior is preserved for valid configurations.
- No data migrations required.
- If additional edge cases are discovered, follow-up PRs can extend handling and tests.

text:
Enhance MetaData handling and event propagation

This change extends the MetaData class with several features and improvements to better manage database metadata and to control event propagation:

Key additions
- Centralized EventBus (eventBus) to post MetaDataChangedEvent and GroupUpdatedEvent when metadata changes.
- Ability to enable/disable metadata event propagation via setEventPropagation(boolean) to avoid event loops during save operations.
- Listener management API: registerListener(Object) and unregisterListener(Object).
- setEncoding(Charset, ChangePropagation) overload to control whether setting encoding should post change events.
- Group tree handling: setGroups now subscribes to descendant changes and posts GroupUpdatedEvent when groups change.
- Content selector support via a ContentSelectors field and convenience methods: getContentSelectors(), getContentSelectorList(), addContentSelector(...), clearContentSelectors(...), getContentSelectorValuesForField(...).
- Per-user LaTeX file directory support (laTexFileDirectory) with getLatexFileDirectory / setLatexFileDirectory / clearLatexFileDirectory and read-only accessor getLatexFileDirectories().
- Per-user file directories remain supported (userFileDirectory) with read-only access via getUserFileDirectories().
- Unknown metadata storage (unkownMetaData) and accessor putUnknownMetaDataItem / getUnknownMetaData() to preserve unsupported meta entries.

Other notes
- Most mutating setters post a MetaDataChangedEvent to notify listeners; postChange() respects the event propagation flag.
- Defensive null checks (Objects.requireNonNull) were added for many setters to prevent invalid state.
- equals(...) and hashCode() implementations compare relevant metadata fields to allow reliable equality checks.
- Some maps are returned as unmodifiable views to prevent external modification.

This PR centralizes metadata eventing and extends metadata capabilities (content selectors, LaTeX dirs, unknown metadata) while providing mechanisms to avoid unwanted event loops during save operations.

Add JSTOR fetcher and tests

This PR introduces a new fetcher for jstor.org and integrates it into the application:

- Added JstorFetcher (implements SearchBasedParserFetcher and FulltextFetcher). Features:
  - Builds search URLs against JSTOR's open search endpoint and supports complex queries (authors, title, journal, year ranges / single year parameters).
  - Downloads citation exports from JSTOR's citation/text endpoint and parses returned BibTeX using the existing BibtexParser.
  - Implements full-text discovery by scraping the entry page and extracting the PDF link.
  - Returns TrustLevel.META_SEARCH.
- Registered JstorFetcher in WebFetchers so it is available among search-based fetchers and meta fulltext fetchers.
- Added unit tests (JstorFetcherTest) covering searchByTitle and fetchPDF. Tests use a mocked ImportFormatPreferences and include disabled year-search tests because JSTOR does not support searching by year alone.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to mention the new JSTOR fetcher.
- Added Johannes Theiner to AUTHORS.

Notes:
- The fetcher uses Jsoup and URLDownload for HTML parsing and HTTP fetching.
- The implementation relies on JSTOR’s open search and citation endpoints and may be affected by changes to JSTOR’s site structure or endpoints.

Update CHANGELOG and enhance BasePanel functionality

This PR includes two main changes:

1) CHANGELOG.md
- Adds/updates the 'Unreleased' changelog section with many notable changes, fixes and removals. This documents recent feature additions (groups saved in the groups field, DOI pasting in main table, integrity checks, UI improvements, additional import/export and cleanup options) and a comprehensive list of fixes and removed features.

2) src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/BasePanel.java
- Refactored and extended many BasePanel responsibilities and UI actions.
- Enhanced clipboard handling: paste action now robustly detects available clipboard flavors and can parse string-flavor BibTeX entries for pasting between JabRef instances or from editors/browsers.
- Improved save flow: saveDatabase now handles encoding problems more gracefully (shows problem characters, offers encoding change, supports commit/cancel), registers save actions for undo, and commits/cancels SaveSession correctly.
- Added SaveSelectedAction to save selected entries to a new file with overwrite confirmation.
- Added SearchAndOpenFile helper to locate and open associated files automatically (with preference checks and extension/type handling).
- Improved file update monitoring: fileUpdated now runs a ChangeScanner, handles file locking, and shows a FileUpdatePanel via SidePaneManager when changes are detected.
- Autocompletion & search: instantiateSearchAutoCompleter, SearchAutoCompleteListener and AutoCompleteListener keep search and content autocompleters up to date when entries change.
- Group updates: GroupTreeListener schedules group UI refreshes with a small debounce via JabRefExecutorService to avoid excessive updates.
- Undo/redo and edit lifecycle: Ensures current editor stores edits before undo/redo, keeps undo history in sync, and marks the base as changed appropriately.
- Many UI actions wired/organized (copy, cut, delete, paste, edit, save, export to SQL, generate keys, cleanup, merge, open URL/external files, manage previews/groups, special field toggles, back/forward navigation, etc.) with improved error handling and user feedback.

Overall, this PR documents the current Unreleased changes and consolidates several BasePanel improvements to clipboard handling, saving, file discovery, autocompletion, group updates and external-change handling.

Fix LaTeX cleanup behavior and add tests

What I changed
- Improved LatexCleanupFormatter to avoid removing braces and escapes that are meaningful for LaTeX semantics. Specifically:
  - Preserve braces used to protect capitalization (e.g., single-letter capitals) instead of stripping them unconditionally.
  - Correctly handle escaped braces and backslashes so LaTeX commands are not corrupted by cleanup.
  - Avoid overzealous removal of nested or adjacent braces/commands that led to incorrect output.
- Added unit tests in LatexCleanupFormatterTest covering nested braces, single-letter capitalization protection, escaped braces and LaTeX commands to prevent regressions.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md with an entry describing the fix.

Why this matters
The previous cleanup could produce invalid or semantically changed LaTeX when it removed braces or escapes that were intentionally used by the author. These changes ensure the formatter conservatively removes only truly redundant braces while preserving LaTeX constructs that affect output (capitalization and commands).

Notes for reviewers
- The logic changes are confined to net.sf.jabref.logic.formatter.bibtexfields.LatexCleanupFormatter and its tests.
- Please run the test suite to verify all new and existing tests pass.

Add MainTableColumnModel to represent columns in the main table and encapsulate all column-related metadata and behavior.

Key points:
- Introduces MainTableColumnModel class with properties: type (Type enum), qualifier (String), width (Double), and sortType (TableColumn.SortType).
- Adds Type enum for supported column types (INDEX, EXTRAFILE, FILES, GROUPS, GROUP_ICONS, LINKED_IDENTIFIER, NORMALFIELD, SPECIALFIELD, LIBRARY_NAME, MATCH_CATEGORY) with name/displayName and ICON_COLUMNS set for icon-only columns.
- Default column widths: ICON_COLUMNS use ColumnPreferences.ICON_COLUMN_WIDTH, others use ColumnPreferences.DEFAULT_COLUMN_WIDTH. Default sort type is ASCENDING.
- getDisplayName() resolves human-readable names using FieldsUtil.getNameWithType and FieldFactory.parseField to avoid showing type hints (e.g., prevents "(Custom)" from appearing for OrFields). ICON_COLUMNS and INDEX use their displayName directly.
- getSortCriteria() builds a list of SaveOrder.SortCriterion for all fields in an OR-field qualifier. Sort order respects current sortType (ASC/DESC).
- parse(String) factory method parses stored column names using ':' as qualifier delimiter and handles default parsing rules for NORMALFIELD, SPECIALFIELD, and EXTRAFILE.
- Proper equals, hashCode and toString implementations based on type and qualifier.
- Uses Injector to obtain CliPreferences and UndoManager where needed.

This class centralizes column naming, parsing and UI-related metadata to simplify handling of table columns and preference migration.

text:
Refactor and harden ClipBoardManager

What I changed
- Refactored ClipBoardManager to improve thread-safety and overall reliability when interacting with the system clipboard.
- Centralized and better-encapsulated clipboard access to avoid shared mutable static state.
- Added explicit handling for common clipboard-related exceptions (e.g. IllegalStateException / UnsupportedFlavorException) so the app no longer crashes when the system clipboard is unavailable or temporarily locked.
- Ensured clipboard reads/writes that interact with JavaFX occur on the JavaFX Application Thread (using Platform.runLater / appropriate scheduling) to avoid threading issues.
- Improved logging and error messages to make clipboard failures easier to diagnose.
- Minor API cleanup and input validation to avoid NPEs when null/empty content is passed.

Why this change
- Users reported intermittent crashes and lost clipboard operations when the system clipboard was busy or unavailable.
- The previous implementation relied on shared static access and sometimes performed clipboard operations off the UI thread, causing race conditions and hard-to-debug failures.

Notes for reviewers
- The functional behavior (copy/paste semantics) is unchanged; this PR focuses on robustness and safety.
- Review the exception handling and thread scheduling to ensure it matches other GUI code patterns in the project.
- If there are platform-specific clipboard quirks we should also test on Windows/macOS/Linux to confirm behavior is correct.

Summary

This PR improves the export workflow, enhances notifications and theming, and updates localization strings.

What changed

- Export flow (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/exporter/ExportCommand.java)
  - Builds the file-save dialog with available exporters (sorted by name) and last-used defaults (extension + working directory).
  - Supports exporting either all entries or only the selected entries (ExportMethod.EXPORT_ALL / EXPORT_SELECTED).
  - Sets the global file directory context so exporters/formatters can resolve linked files correctly before export.
  - Runs the actual export on a background task to avoid blocking the UI.
  - On success, displays a notification with an action button to reveal the exported file in the file manager ("Reveal in File Explorer").
  - Persists the last used export extension and working directory in preferences.
  - Improved error handling: logs the problem, notifies the user, and shows an error dialog on failure.

- UI / Theming (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/Base.css, src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/Dark.css)
  - Adjusted and extended CSS theme variables and defaults to make colors and components more consistent.
  - Tweaks for toolbar, tooltip, notification and list/table visuals.
  - Dark theme adjustments to match the base theme changes.

- Localization (src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties)
  - Added/updated strings used by the export flow and notifications, e.g. "Export operation finished successfully." and "Reveal in File Explorer".

Changelog

- Mentioned in CHANGELOG.md: Added support for multiple messages in the snackbar and fixed visibility issues with the notification bar.

Why

- Export was switched to a non-blocking background task so large exports do not freeze the UI.
- Notifications now provide feedback and quick access to the exported file.
- Theming and localization updates provide a more consistent and user-friendly experience.

Notes / Follow-ups

- The export implementation temporarily sets a global preference (fileDirForDatabase) so formatters can resolve file links during export. This is noted in the code as an ugly hack; consider refactoring to avoid reliance on global mutable state in a follow-up.
- Ensure the extension handling and Path mutation (FileUtil.addExtension) behave as intended on all platforms; tests/manual verification are recommended.

Fixes #7452 — avoid downloading HTML when expecting a PDF and notify the user

What I changed
- ExternalFileTypes::getExternalFileTypeByMimeType: strip any MIME type parameters (the ";..." part) before mapping to the enum. This makes detection conform to the MIME type specification (see MDN) and matches the values in StandardExternalFileType.java.
- Added a notification via the status bar when a downloaded file is detected as HTML so the user is informed that the link did not return a PDF but an HTML page.

Why
- Previously mime types with parameters (e.g. "application/pdf; charset=UTF-8") were not matched against the expected enum values, causing incorrect handling. In some cases users thought they had downloaded a PDF but actually saved an HTML page (e.g. an access/redirect page).

Other notes
- Tests were added to cover the changed behavior.
- CHANGELOG updated and changes manually tested in a running JabRef build.
- Screenshots showing the problem and the new warning are included in the PR description.

Summary

Add an automated PR comment and a workflow job that encourages/ensures contributors assign themselves to the referenced issue when opening a PR. This reduces the race condition where external contributors immediately open a PR and other contributors assign the issue to themselves before the PR author can.

What I changed

- .github/ghprcomment.yml
  - Added a PR-hygiene comment template “Ensure that contributor is assigned (fails if not commented on issue)” that reminds authors to assign issues to themselves and links to CONTRIBUTING.md.

- .github/workflows/on-pr-opened-updated.yml
  - Added a new job ensure_assignment (name: Ensure that contributor is assigned (fails if not commented on issue)) to run on PR opened/updated events.
  - The job is gated with: if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != 'JabRef/jabref' so it only runs for PRs from forks (external contributors).
  - When updating the issue assignees the job now queries the issue labels. If a label starting with "good" is present, the assignment update is performed normally (failures are not silenced). If that label is not present, the API call is performed in a "silent" mode (errors are ignored) to avoid hard failures when adding an assignee isn’t possible.
  - The issue-assignee update uses the repository variable instead of hardcoding JabRef/jabref where applicable.

Why this was necessary

- When an external contributor opens a PR immediately after fixing an issue, they cannot yet add themselves as an assignee on the issue. That can let others assign the issue to themselves before the PR author has a chance to do so.
- Posting a friendly automated comment and enforcing assignment for relevant issues reduces that unwanted behavior while still being permissive for certain issue types (labelled with "good...").

Behavior notes

- The workflow runs for PRs from forks (external contributors) only.
- If the issue has a label beginning with "good" (e.g. "good first issue"), the assignment update is treated strictly and failures will surface. For issues without such a label, any failure to add an assignee will be ignored to avoid breaking the workflow.
- The PR comment text links to CONTRIBUTING.md and politely requests that the contributor assign the issue to themselves.

Files changed

- .github/ghprcomment.yml
- .github/workflows/on-pr-opened-updated.yml

Checklist

- [x] Adds helper message to remind contributors to assign issues to themselves
- [x] Runs only for PRs from forks to target external contributors
- [x] Avoids hard failures for non-"good" labelled issues by silencing API errors where appropriate

This change aims to reduce accidental issue-ownership conflicts while staying friendly and non-blocking for most cases.

- Added a context menu on event log entries with the following actions: 'Copy' (copies the selected text or the full entry if nothing is selected) and 'Copy All' (copies all visible log entries).

- Improves usability for troubleshooting and sharing logs by making it easy to copy entries.

1. Open the Event Logs view.

3. Select part of a log entry, right-click and choose 'Copy' — verify only the selection is copied.
4. Right-click anywhere in the logs list and choose 'Copy All' — verify the clipboard contains all visible entries.
5. Select text and press Ctrl/Cmd+C — verify copy still works.
6. Test keyboard navigation and screen-reader announce of the menu.

Notes
- On touch-only devices where right-click is not available, the existing long-press or selection behavior is unchanged.
- No breaking changes to existing APIs or persisted data.

Add unified “Send” functionality (As Email / To Kindle) and related preferences

Summary
- Introduces a new Send menu/submenu integrated into the Tools menu and the main table right-click menu, offering two actions: “As Email” and “To Kindle”.
- Centralizes email-sending logic in an abstract SendAsEMailAction to share common behavior between concrete actions.

What’s new / changed
- New Send actions
  - SendAsEMailAction (abstract): shared implementation for creating a mailto: URI, gathering attachments from selected entries, opening attachment folders when requested, and invoking Desktop.mail() via BackgroundTask.
  - SendAsStandardEmailAction: populates the email body with BibTeX source for the selected entries (uses writer/formatters) and uses the configured email subject.
  - SendAsKindleEmailAction: sends attachments to the configured Kindle email address and is only enabled when entries with linked files are selected.

- UI / menus
  - A new “Send” submenu (Send → As Email / To Kindle) is added to the Tools menu and to the entry right-click context menu.
  - The toolbar/menu action registrations are wired to existing ActionFactory infrastructure and key binding support.

- Preferences and validation
  - External programs preferences (ExternalTab) now expose fields for: email subject, Kindle email, and an option to automatically open folders of attached files.
  - ExternalTabViewModel and ExternalApplicationsPreferences store and validate these settings (validation messages shown when necessary).
  - The ExternalTab FXML updated to include Kindle email, subject, and the auto-open checkbox.

- Behavior details
  - When creating an email, attachments are collected from the selected entries’ linked files (resolving against configured file directories).
  - For email clients that don’t support mailto attachment parameters (e.g., Outlook), the preference to open containing folders will open and select the files so users can attach them manually.
  - Errors in creating or launching the email are reported via the DialogService; tasks run off the FX thread.

Files touched (high level)
- New/changed classes: SendAsEMailAction, SendAsStandardEmailAction, SendAsKindleEmailAction
- Menus & integration: JabRefFrame (createSendSubMenu), RightClickMenu (createSendSubMenu)
- Preferences: ExternalTab.fxml, ExternalTab, ExternalTabViewModel, ExternalApplicationsPreferences
- Actions registry: StandardActions (added SEND items / labels)

Notes for reviewers
- The mail creation uses java.awt.Desktop.mail and constructs a mailto: URI; attachment handling is implemented via non-standard mailto parameters for clients that support them, with the fallback of opening folders when configured.
- UI strings and localization keys are included/used where appropriate.

This change implements issue/feature #6186 (integrate mail actions under a Send menu and provide Kindle email preference).

Extend RIS import with multiple fields and improved mappings

This PR expands and fixes the RIS importer to recognize many more RIS tags and map them to appropriate BibEntry fields (or to custom fields when no direct BibTeX equivalent exists). Key changes:
- Extended tag -> field mappings: T2/J2/JA/JO/J1/JF -> journal; AU/A1/A2/A3/A4 -> authors; ED -> editor; IS/AN/C7/M1 -> number; AD/CY/PP -> address; UR/L2/LK -> url; Y2 (added) -> year; M3/DO -> DOI (uses addDoi); C3 -> eventtitle; N1/RN -> note; ST -> shorttitle; C2 -> eprint + eprinttype=pubmed; TA -> translator.
- Added mappings for tags without direct BibTeX equivalents to custom fields: AV -> archive_location, CN/VO -> call-number, DB -> archive, NV -> number-of-volumes, OP -> original-title, RI -> reviewed-title, RP -> status, SE -> section, and ID -> refid.
- Added FieldName.SHORTTITLE constant.
- Small refactor: local BibEntry variable renamed from b to entry and month handling kept intact.
- Tests: added RisImporterTest7 (.ris + expected .bib) and updated several expected .bib output files to reflect the improved mappings; updated the parameterized test list and adjusted RisImporterTestDoiAndJournalTitle.ris (ED tag -> editor mapping).
- CHANGELOG updated with a brief entry and issue references (#3634, #2607).

This improves RIS import fidelity for a wider range of RIS tag variants and preserves unmapped information in custom fields when appropriate. Manual and automated importer tests were updated accordingly.

Add Save Order and Save Actions UI to Library Properties

This PR integrates the save-order configuration and field-formatter save actions into the Library Properties dialog so users can view and edit per-library export/save settings from the same place where encoding, file directories and protection are configured.

What changed
- Added SaveOrderConfigDisplay.fxml to define the save-order UI (radio buttons for export order, and editable comboboxes for primary/secondary/tertiary sort criteria plus descending checkboxes).
- Wire up SaveOrderConfigDisplayView into LibraryPropertiesDialogView so the dialog shows and edits the library's SaveOrderConfig. The dialog loads the existing config from MetaData or falls back to the global preference default and writes changes back to MetaData on OK (clearing the metadata entry if it matches the default).
- Added a FieldFormatterCleanupsPanel instance to the Library Properties dialog to show and edit per-library save actions (formatters). The panel initializes from MetaData, supports adding/removing/recommending formatters and shows formatter descriptions.
- FieldFormatterCleanupsPanel now includes ProtectTermsFormatter (initialized with Globals.protectedTermsLoader) among available formatters.
- Updated LibraryPropertiesDialogView.storeSettings() to persist save-order and save-action changes and to mark the base as changed when relevant settings differ from previous values.

Behavior notes
- If the user resets the save order to the default, the SaveOrderConfig is removed from the library metadata.
- If save actions are cleared or match defaults, the metadata save actions entry is cleared to avoid storing redundant defaults.
- Changes to save order, save actions, encoding, file directories, protection, etc. cause the library to be marked as changed so the UI correctly prompts for saving.

Files touched (high level)
- Added: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/SaveOrderConfigDisplay.fxml
- Updated: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/libraryproperties/LibraryPropertiesDialog.fxml
- Updated: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/libraryproperties/LibraryPropertiesDialogView.java (hooked-up save order + field formatter panel)
- Updated: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/cleanup/FieldFormatterCleanupsPanel.java (add ProtectTermsFormatter and related UI initialization)

This change improves discoverability and convenience by centralizing library export/save configuration in the Library Properties dialog.

text:
Summary
- Fix performance issue when saving large .bib files by optimizing date parsing. Related to #7265.

What I changed
- CHANGELOG.md: added an entry noting the fix for saving large .bib files (#7265).
- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/Date.java:
  - Replaced repeated on-the-fly creation and trial-parsing of many DateTimeFormatter instances with a single pre-built composite formatter (SIMPLE_DATE_FORMATS) built via DateTimeFormatterBuilder.appendOptional.
  - Added a NORMALIZED_DATE_FORMATTER constant and simplified getNormalized() to use it.
  - Parsing now short-circuits empty strings and returns Optional.empty().
  - Parsing uses Locale.US and a consolidated set of supported formats (covers variants like 2009-1-15, 9/15, September 1, 2015, 15.1.2015, 2015, Jan, 2020, etc.).
  - Reduced the number of exceptions thrown during parsing (previous code relied on trying multiple formatters and catching DateTimeParseException repeatedly), which improves performance when processing many dates.

Why
- When saving large bibliographies, the previous parsing approach created many DateTimeFormatter instances and relied on exceptions for flow control, causing substantial overhead. The new approach builds a single optional-pattern formatter once and reuses it, avoiding excessive exception creation and improving save performance.

Notes
- Behavior preserved for supported formats; unsupported/empty inputs still result in an empty Optional.
- Tests and manual testing were performed as noted in the issue checklist.

Summary of changes

This PR contains a set of improvements and bug fixes across the import/parsing pathway and the entry editor source tab. Main highlights:

Source editor (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/SourceTab.java)
- Added/updated the source editor (CodeArea) setup and behavior:
  - Workaround for problematic input methods via a custom InputMethodRequests implementation and handling committed IME text.
  - Listens to global save keybindings while editing source and stores/parses the source when a save is triggered (SAVE_DATABASE, SAVE_ALL, SAVE_DATABASE_AS).
  - Validates source edits and surfaces parser/validation warnings via the DialogService.
  - Search highlighting integration: highlights active search query matches in the source tab.
  - Ensures source changes are persisted (storeSource) when the tab loses focus or a save keybinding is used.
- storeSource now parses the edited BibTeX using BibtexParser and applies field/type/citation-key changes via Undoable edits (NamedCompound), with robust handling of warnings/errors and user feedback.

Import pipeline and UI (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/importer/ImportAction.java)
- Refactored automatedImport to run parsing/merging in a background task (BackgroundTask.wrap) and improved error handling and user notifications.
- For unknown format imports, the code now shows proper notifications in JavaFX thread and handles the Grobid opt-in flow for PDFs (resetting available import formats when needed).
- The import worker collects ImportFormatReader.UnknownFormatImport results, merges them to a single ParserResult, and then either opens results in a new tab or shows the ImportEntriesDialog in the current library.
- Improved reporting of import failures: distinguishes between no entries found vs importer-thrown exceptions and presents appropriate messages to the user.

Open database flow (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/importer/actions/OpenDatabaseAction.java)
- Loading/opening database files is done with background tasks to avoid blocking the UI.
- Working directory is set based on the opened file. Backups are checked and restoration dialog shown when needed.
- Shared database handling improved (SharedDatabaseUIManager), with appropriate error handling and fallbacks (clearing database path and shared id on connection errors).
- Added telemetry tracking when new databases are opened.
- performPostOpenActions moved/available to run migration/post-open checks (e.g. entry type migrations).

Import formats and detection (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/ImportFormatReader.java)
- resetImportFormats signature updated to accept importer- and general-preference objects and repopulate the list of importers; built-in importers are re-initialized in a stable order.
- importUnknownFormat improved to try all registered importers and keep the most promising result (by number of entries), and to fallback to treating the file as BibTeX via OpenDatabase.loadDatabase if all importers fail.
- Added convenience APIs: import by CLI id, import from string, and functional helper for importing while testing recognition functions.

BibTeX parsing robustness (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/BibtexParser.java)
- Many robustness fixes and parsing improvements:
  - Detects and preserves the new-line separator used by the input.
  - Parses and restores JabRef metadata and custom entry types found in @comment blocks more safely.
  - Better handling of EOF and malformed/corrupted entries (warnings instead of hard failures) to allow continuing parsing.
  - Improved bracket/quote parsing (parseBracketedTextExactly, parseQuotedFieldExactly) and safer whitespace handling.
  - parseFieldContent improved to correctly handle concatenation (#), raw string tokens, numeric values and to use FieldWriter.BIBTEX_STRING_START_END_SYMBOL for unresolved tokens.
  - Improved key-fixing heuristics (fixKey) to try to recover corrupted citation keys and provide clearer parser warnings.
  - Added helpers for parsing single entry from string and other small utility improvements.

Localization resource
- No functional changes to the l10n file other than ensuring relevant messages exist for import/open/source parsing errors and dialogs (used by the new/updated UI flows).

Why these changes
- Make importing and opening files more robust and responsive (background tasks, better error handling, fallback strategies).
- Improve user experience when editing raw BibTeX source in the entry editor: better IME support, save integration, validation and informative warnings.
- Harden BibTeX parsing to tolerate and report malformed inputs while still extracting as much as possible.

Testing notes
- Manual testing of importing various formats (including PDFs) and the Grobid opt-in flow is advised.
- Verify editing the source tab: losing focus and pressing save should persist changes, and parser warnings should appear in dialogs when appropriate.
- Exercise opening databases (including shared DB cases) and confirm background loading and warning dialogs for parse issues.

text:
Improve library properties validation and directory handling

This PR enhances the Library Properties dialog by adding robust validation, debounced directory checks, and better path resolution and browse behavior.

Main changes:
- Validate-and-store per-tab: LibraryPropertiesViewModel.storeAllSettings() now validates each PropertiesTab before storing. Settings are only saved for tabs that pass validation and the method returns a combined success flag so the dialog only closes when all tabs are valid.
- Debounced path validation: GeneralPropertiesViewModel adds a PauseTransition to debounce validation notifications for directory path fields (library-specific, user-specific, LaTeX). This prevents spamming the user with immediate notifications while they type.
- Relative path resolution: Relative directory paths are resolved against the library file location (when available). Empty paths are allowed (treated as defaults). Non-resolvable or non-existing paths trigger a notification using dialogService.
- Better browse initial directory: The directory browse dialogs now pick a sensible initial directory (working dir or a resolved existing file directory) and fall back to the working directory if resolution fails, notifying the user.
- Encoding and database mode handling: GeneralPropertiesViewModel correctly disables encoding selection for shared databases and reads/writes encoding, mode, and file-directory metadata as before.
- Minor UI improvements: properties tabs are wrapped in ScrollPane and AbstractPropertiesTabView instances get size bindings and a "propertiesTab" style class.
- Localization: Adds/uses a new message for non-existing paths: "The path for %0 ('%1') does not exist." in JabRef_en.properties.

Notes:
- The save button action in LibraryPropertiesView already closes the dialog only when storeAllSettings() returns true.
- No public API breaking changes.

This improves UX by providing timely, non-intrusive validation and by making directory path behavior more predictable and resilient.

Adds a searchable and filterable interface for user preferences, allowing users to quickly find settings by keyword and narrow results by category/status (e.g., modified, default, reset). Improves discoverability and efficiency when managing preferences.

What I changed:
- Added a search input that filters preferences in real time (case-insensitive, partial matches across keys, labels, and descriptions).
- Implemented filter controls to show/hide categories and states (All, Modified, Default, Reset).
- Highlighted matched text in results for better context.
- Kept existing preference editing, reset, and save flows intact.
- Implemented debounce on search input and optimized rendering to avoid performance regressions with large preference sets.

Files/areas touched:
- Preferences UI components (search box, filter controls, result list)
- Preference rendering logic (matching, highlighting)
- Styling for new controls and highlight states
- Unit and integration tests for search/filter behavior

- Added unit tests for matching logic and filter behavior.
- Added integration tests to ensure search + filters interact correctly with preference editing and reset flows.
- Manual testing performed for keyboard accessibility, focus behavior, and performance with large datasets.

Notes for reviewers:
- Search is currently client-side; if preferences grow very large we may consider server-side search/pagination.
- Accessibility: controls are keyboard navigable and include ARIA labels; please flag any issues.
- No migration or backend changes required.

Release notes:
Users can now quickly find preferences using the search box and refine results with filters (Modified/Default/Reset).

text:
Fix crash when editing date fields in biblatex library mode (fixes #8747)

Summary:
- Prevents an uncaught exception that occurred when editing an entry's "date" field in biblatex library mode by improving parsing and validation logic and wiring the editor to the preferences-based validator.

Root cause:
- The date editor could throw an uncaught DateTimeParseException (or other parsing exceptions) when encountering dates in unexpected formats, and the editor lacked configured validation in some code paths.

What I changed:
- CHANGELOG.md: Added entry describing the bugfix.
- DateEditor.java: Inject PreferencesService and configure EditorValidator so the date editor is validated according to user preferences.
- FieldEditors.java: Pass PreferencesService through when constructing DateEditor instances.
- DateEditorViewModel.java: Broaden the catch from DateTimeParseException to Exception so non-standard/legacy date parsing falls back to Date.parse(...) when necessary.
- TemporalAccessorPicker.java:
  - Added defensive null handling when converting TemporalAccessor -> LocalDate.
  - Improved StringConverter.fromString so it tries defaultFormatter.parse(...) and falls back to Date.parse(...); blank input returns null.
  - Preserve user-typed text in the editor when the value is invalid (to avoid clearing typed-but-invalid input).
  - Ensure temporalAccessorValue is updated before returning the LocalDate in the internal converter.

Why this fixes the issue:
- Parsing is now tolerant of a wider range of date formats and falls back to the shared Date parser rather than letting exceptions bubble up. The editor is also validated via PreferencesService to present validation errors instead of causing uncaught exceptions. Preserving the editor text avoids losing user input for invalid dates.

Risk/Compatibility:
- Parsing behavior is more permissive and will accept additional date formats via fallback. Validation is now enabled for date editors across code paths. These are intended fixes and should be backward-compatible.

Related issue: #8747 (https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/8747)

Summary

This PR implements support for deleting temporary files on application exit when JabRef is started with the --deleteWhenClosing=<path> argument. It addresses leftover temp files created by the browser extension by scheduling deletion of the provided path on shutdown. Closes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/11048.

What changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/cli/JabKit.java
  - Added parsing for the --deleteWhenClosing=<path> CLI argument inside processArguments().
  - Introduced a static Optional<String> to hold the delete path and schedule a BackgroundTask on the SHUTDOWN_EXECUTOR that calls Files.deleteIfExists(Path.of(path)). Failures are logged.
  - Ensures this deletion happens during shutdown so temporary files are removed when JabRef exits.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ACMPortalFetcher.java
  - Refactored the fetcher to support paged searches (implements PagedSearchBasedFetcher).
  - Added getURLForQuery, performSearchPaged and helper methods to build ACM search URLs and transform Lucene QueryNodes to query strings.
  - Kept/updated the parser provider to ACMPortalParser.

- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ACMPortalFetcherTest.java
  - Added unit tests for performSearchPaged and updated existing parser test assertions.
  - Added a spy-based test to assert expected behavior for performSearchPaged.

- .vscode/settings.json
  - Added "java.compile.nullAnalysis.mode": "automatic" (editor config change).

- jabref
  - Updated to referenced subproject commit (submodule pointer change).

Why

Browser extension usage can create temporary files that were not cleaned up when JabRef closed. This change makes it possible to request deletion of such a temp file at shutdown by launching JabRef with --deleteWhenClosing=/path/to/temp, improving resource cleanup and preventing stale temp files.

Testing

- Unit tests for the ACM fetcher were added/updated.
- Manual testing of the new --deleteWhenClosing behavior was performed (file deletion scheduled at shutdown). Errors during deletion are logged as warnings.

Notes

- The shutdown deletion runs as a BackgroundTask on the dedicated SHUTDOWN_EXECUTOR and uses Files.deleteIfExists to avoid exceptions if the file is already gone.
- The PR also contains refactoring and tests related to the ACM fetcher (paged search support).

- Fixes issue: https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/11048

text:
Summary

Fixes an issue where icons from Material Design Icons were not recognized by our icon loader/components.

What I changed

- Normalize icon identifiers so common naming styles (kebab-case, snake_case, and camelCase) map to the same canonical name used by the loader.
- Add an alias map for renamed/deprecated Material icons so older names still resolve to the correct glyph.
- Upgrade the Material Design Icons dependency to the latest compatible version to pick up missing glyph metadata.
- Improve unit and integration tests to cover a representative set of Material icons (including hyphenated and renamed icons).
- Update documentation for the icon component explaining accepted name formats and the aliasing behavior.

Root cause

The icon lookup expected a single name format but Material Design Icons uses a variety of naming styles and some icons were renamed across versions. That caused some icons to not be found at runtime.

Testing

- Added unit tests that assert icons resolve correctly for kebab-case, camelCase, and previous/deprecated names.
- Manual verification in the local Storybook/demo: verified a sample list of problematic icons renders correctly after the change.
- Ran full test suite and linting; all pass.

Migration/Notes

- Developers should reinstall dependencies (npm/yarn install) due to the dependency bump.
- No changes required to existing code calling the icon component; old names will continue to work via the alias map.

If you want, I can add a CLI script to regenerate aliases from the upstream icon metadata for easier maintenance in the future.

Summary
- Added a small CLI tool GenerateCharacterTable that prints a LaTeX document (two-column supertabular) listing all characters from the converter. The output shows code point, Unicode symbol, printed \symbol{n} and the LaTeX replacement/code so mappings can be visually inspected.

What I changed
- New file: src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/cli/GenerateCharacterTable.java
  - Prints a ready-to-compile LaTeX file enumerating entries in HTMLUnicodeConversionMaps.

- Updated: src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/util/strings/HTMLUnicodeConversionMaps.java
  - Fixed and improved many LaTeX replacement strings (escaping, using more appropriate LaTeX commands and math/text context). Examples of fixed cases include degree sign, double prime, therefore, not-subset, and many punctuation/diacritic entries.
  - Corrected improper escaping for several ASCII punctuation mappings (plus, period) and for \textit/other macros.
  - Added a hair-space mapping (U+200A) and other spacing adjustments (en/quad/others).
  - Cleaned up and commented-out a few dubious or redundant mappings (Cyrillic entries, some L-midot entries) and added missing diacritic/multi-letter mappings for various code points.
  - Added mappings for subscript digits and signs, and for several typographic ligatures (ff, fi, fl, ffi, ffl) with a note that LaTeX usually handles them.
  - Adjusted entries for degree Celsius, script/blackboard letters, ell, and other math/symbol entries to use more robust LaTeX commands.
  - General comment and formatting cleanups inside the map to make entries clearer and more consistent.

- Updated test: src/test/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/layout/format/HTMLCharsTest.java
  - Updated expected output in a test to reflect changed mapping: the test now expects Oogon & imath for the input "\\k{O}\\i" (previously used Lmidot).

Notes
- This change is intended to make it easier to visually verify every mapping and uncover incorrect or awkward LaTeX replacements.
- The generated LaTeX document depends on fonts/packages to render all glyphs; some symbols may still require tweaking of packages or fonts.
- Related to issue #1761 (not fully addressed here). A sample PDF (CharGen5.pdf) was used for manual verification.

Testing
- Manually tested the changed features; unit test adjusted accordingly.

If you want I can:
- Add a small README or usage note for the CLI tool (how to run and compile the output .tex), or
- Break the large map edits into smaller commits grouped by character ranges to ease review.

- File type inference for downloads: try MIME type first and fall back to URL extension when needed.
- XMP metadata writing: write XMP metadata to local PDFs using a background task.
- Validation: a file-exists validator warns if a linked file cannot be found (online links are considered valid).
- Integration with existing services: uses LinkedFileHandler, ExternalFileTypes, TaskExecutor, DialogService, FilePreferences, XmpPreferences and BibDatabaseContext; provides observables for UI binding.
- User interaction improvements: confirmation dialogs for overwrite and delete actions and error dialogs for failure cases; logging for debug/error conditions.

Overall this adds comprehensive UI-facing support for managing and downloading linked files in entries, with background execution and safe user interactions.

Introduce a JavaFX-based DialogService implementation and centralize backup restore UI logic behind a dialog service interface.

Summary of changes
- Add FXDialogService: a DialogService implementation that creates and shows JavaFX/ControlsFX dialogs (information/warning/error/confirmation/custom dialogs, input dialogs, file/directory choosers, cancelable progress dialogs, exception dialogs, printing dialog, notifications). It wraps platform dialogs so they work on top of Swing windows and exposes file chooser configuration handling.
- Add BackupUIManager: helper for all user dialogs related to BackupManager. The restore-backup prompt now accepts a DialogService, constructs the localized message and triggers BackupManager.restoreBackup when the user confirms.
- Update OpenDatabaseAction: when a backup is detected while opening a file, call BackupUIManager.showRestoreBackupDialog(frame.getDialogService(), fileToLoad) so the frame’s configured DialogService is used instead of instantiating a new FXDialogService.
- Keep compatibility at startup: JabRefGUI still uses new FXDialogService(mainStage) to show the restore dialog for last-edited databases during startup (before the main frame’s DialogService is available). FXDialogService has a deprecated default constructor for backward compatibility.

Motivation
- Decouple UI dialog presentation from business logic by using a DialogService interface. This enables reusing and mocking dialog behavior (for testing) and ensures a single consistent dialog implementation across the app.
- Centralize backup-related user interaction in BackupUIManager to avoid duplicated dialog logic and to make behavior easier to change and test.

Other notes
- The changes use ControlsFX dialogs for exception and progress handling.
- No change to localization resources.

This PR is primarily a refactor to improve separation of concerns and testability of dialog interactions.
