Refactor and cleanup: journal abbreviation data structures, deduplicate temp-file creation, and update tests

Summary of changes:
- FileUpdateMonitor
  - Removed duplicate getTempFile implementation and consolidated it as a single private static synchronized method.
  - Created temporary files via Files.createTempFile with deleteOnExit and added logging on failure.
  - Minor reordering of fields and updated Javadoc return type from File to Path for getTempFile(String key).

- AbbreviationParser
  - Replaced List<Abbreviation> with a Set<Abbreviation> (HashSet with initial capacity 5000) to naturally deduplicate entries.
  - Removed explicit contains() check since Set.add() ensures uniqueness.

- JournalAbbreviationRepository
  - Big refactor: replaced multiple lookup maps and a SortedSet with a single HashSet of Abbreviation (initial capacity 16000).
  - Added helper methods isMatched and isMatchedAbbreviated to perform case-insensitive matching against name, ISO and Medline forms.
  - Rewrote lookup methods (isKnownName, isAbbreviatedName, getAbbreviation, getNextAbbreviation, getMedlineAbbreviation, getIsoAbbreviation) to use stream-based searches on the set and Optional.map where applicable.
  - addEntry now uses Set.contains to detect duplicates, logs and replaces existing entries (preserves behavior of overwriting duplicates but no longer stores separate lower-cased keys in maps).
  - API changes:
    - addEntries now accepts a Collection<Abbreviation> instead of List<Abbreviation>.
    - getAbbreviations now returns an unmodifiable Set<Abbreviation> instead of a SortedSet.
  - Note: This removes any deterministic ordering previously provided by a SortedSet and replaces fast map lookups with linear searches over the set. This reduces memory used for multiple maps and simplifies duplicate handling, but changes iteration/order semantics and lookup performance characteristics.

- Tests
  - Updated expected content in ManageJournalAbbreviationsViewModelTest to reflect new ordering/handling of duplicate entries.
  - Removed a test that relied on sorting (JournalAbbreviationRepositoryTest.testSorting) and adjusted tests that expected deterministic ordering of results.

Why
- Simplifies and reduces memory overhead by removing multiple maps used solely for case-insensitive lookups and consolidating data into one set.
- Ensures duplicates are handled consistently via the Set and centralizes matching logic.
- Removes duplicated code (getTempFile) and clarifies return types.

Potential impact
- Lookups are now linear-time over the set instead of constant-time map lookups; this is a trade-off for reduced memory usage and simpler code.
- Ordering of abbreviations is no longer guaranteed (previous SortedSet ordering removed). Tests relying on sorted order have been updated/removed accordingly.
- Public API changes: addEntries(Collection) and getAbbreviations() returning Set may require callers to be updated if they relied on SortedSet behavior.

Summary

Refactor and bugfixes for the full-text retrieval and linked-file workflow. The FindFullTextAction no longer performs direct file/link creation and UI updates itself; instead it delegates creation and validation to the LinkedFileViewModel and runs retrieval in a background task. Error handling, UI refresh and null-safety around selection are improved.

What I changed

- FindFullTextAction
  - Moved full-text retrieval into a background task to avoid blocking the UI and to support cancellation/progress handling.
  - Delegates creation/attachment of the resulting file/link to LinkedFileViewModel instead of manipulating linked files directly.
  - Adds null/selection checks and better exception handling; displays appropriate error messages when retrieval fails or when no entry is selected.

- LinkedFileViewModel
  - Centralized validation and creation logic for linked files (filename sanitization, path handling, file type detection) so callers can reuse consistent behavior.
  - Exposes a clear API for attaching a downloaded file to an entry and refreshing the UI model.
  - Improves null-safety and error reporting for invalid file operations.

Why

- Separating concerns makes the code easier to test and maintain (FindFullTextAction handles orchestration and UI interactions while LinkedFileViewModel owns file/link concerns).
- Running network/file operations off the UI thread improves responsiveness and avoids UI freezes.
- Centralizing validation reduces duplication and prevents subtle bugs (e.g. invalid filenames, null pointer conditions, or missing UI refresh).

Risks / Backwards compatibility

- This is an internal refactor with no public API changes expected. Existing behaviors are preserved but more robust.
- Callers that bypass LinkedFileViewModel for linked-file creation may miss the new validation; ideally they should be updated to use the model.

Notes

- The changes include improved user feedback when retrieval fails and ensure the file list view is refreshed after attaching a file.

This PR adds a new integrity check that detects unescaped ampersands (&) in BibEntry fields and reports them in the Integrity Check window. It also includes tests and localization entries and registers the new checker with the existing integrity checks.

What I changed

- Added AmpersandChecker (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/integrity/AmpersandChecker.java)
  - Scans all fields of an entry and counts unescaped ampersands by checking the number of preceding backslashes (even count means the ampersand is unescaped).
  - Produces an IntegrityMessage with a localized message "Found %0 unescaped '&'" per affected field.
- Registered the checker in IntegrityCheck so it runs with the other entry checkers (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/integrity/IntegrityCheck.java).
- Added unit tests for the checker covering allowed (properly escaped) and disallowed (unescaped) inputs (src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/integrity/AmpersandCheckerTest.java).
- Added localization strings for English and German (src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties, JabRef_de.properties).
- Added a short entry to CHANGELOG.md about the new integrity check.

Files touched

- NEW: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/integrity/AmpersandChecker.java
- UPDATED: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/integrity/IntegrityCheck.java (registered new checker)
- NEW: src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/integrity/AmpersandCheckerTest.java
- UPDATED: src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties
- UPDATED: src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_de.properties

- The checker counts ampersands where the number of consecutive backslashes immediately before the ampersand is even (including zero), treating those ampersands as unescaped. Ampersands preceded by an odd number of backslashes are considered escaped.
- The integrity message includes the number of unescaped ampersands found in a field.
- Tests cover a variety of combinations of backslashes and ampersands to validate counting logic.

Fixes

- Fixes #8948
- Fixes https://github.com/koppor/jabref/issues/585

Additional notes

- If the message string is changed, please also update the unit tests which assert the exact message text.

Summary

This PR refactors and enhances the entry preview / entry editor experience and preferences handling. It introduces a PreviewPanel with persistent preview preferences, improves drag-and-drop file linking in both the preview and the entry editor, refines tab management in the entry editor, and adds associated keybindings and actions for cycling/copying previews. Several related improvements and fixes around focus, divider persistence and auto-completion indexing were included.

Main changes

- Add PreviewPanel and integrate preview viewer
  - New PreviewPanel component that hosts PreviewViewer and handles layout updates, context menu actions and keybindings (copy preview, next/previous preview layout).
  - PreviewPanel supports drag-and-drop of files onto the preview to link/copy/move files to the entry using ExternalFilesEntryLinker.
  - Preview cycling and the currently selected preview style are stored and loaded via preferences.

- Persist preview preferences in JabRefPreferences
  - Store/load preview cycle, current preview position, preview style and preview panel divider position.
  - PreviewPreferences class introduced to represent preview-related preferences and provide a builder for updates.
  - JabRefPreferences now exposes getPreviewPreferences() and storePreviewPreferences(...) and integrates preview defaults.

- Entry editor improvements
  - EntryEditor now supports drag-and-drop on the editor area with user-configurable behavior (move/copy/link) using FileDragDropPreferenceType and ExternalFilesEntryLinker.
  - Tabs in the entry editor are recalculated when the edited entry changes type or content; selection and focus handling refined (notifyAboutFocus, remember focused child field etc.).
  - Easier navigation via key bindings (next/previous panel, next/previous entry, close, help), and buttons for generating cite keys and switching fetchers.

- FieldsEditorTab changes
  - FieldsEditorTab embeds a PreviewPanel alongside fields (SplitPane) so previews appear inline in the entry editor tabs.
  - Layout logic for compressed vs regular field arrangements separated and row/column constraints computed based on FieldEditor weights.
  - Field editors created via FieldEditors.getForField(...) and bound to entries; focus restoration after rebuild.

- BasePanel integration and actions
  - BasePanel wires preview-style actions (NEXT_PREVIEW_STYLE / PREVIOUS_PREVIEW_STYLE) to the entry editor to allow cycling preview styles from the main panel.
  - Ensures split-pane divider positions are persisted per mode (entry editor), keeps change monitor lifecycle management and improves search/autocomplete initialization.

Bug fixes and improvements

- Save/restore of entry editor divider position based on BasePanelMode to avoid splitter jump.
- Better handling of selection/focus when switching tabs and when editing entries (prevent losing focus, restore focused field after tab rebuild).
- Autosuggestion providers and search auto-completer are properly initialized and indexed on startup/entry events.
- Drag-and-drop behavior uses user preferences to decide between move/copy/link and prevents accidental CPU-heavy file searches unless enabled.
- Context menus and fetcher menus assembled dynamically and shown from toolbar controls.
- Minor stability and logging improvements where exceptions are caught and reported.

- Manually verified downloads against current arXiv endpoints.

- No API changes to callers; behavior is backward compatible and improves robustness.
- If any further edge cases with auth/cookies arise, we can extend the redirect handling to carry specific credentials as needed.

Summary:
Enable dragging selected entries from the main table and dropping them onto other open (inactive) library tabs to import those entries into the target library.

What changed:
- Implement cross-tab entry drag & drop
  - JabRefFrame: added drag handlers on the scene and on each tab so dragging can be detected and handled for both bib files and entry objects. When entries are dropped on an inactive tab, the target tab receives the entries and imports them. Dropping bib files on a tab opens those files.
  - LibraryTab: each tab now gets a unique ID (for identifying the target tab during drop). Added dropEntry(List<BibEntry>) which delegates to the main table to import entries.
  - MainTable: added dropEntry(List<BibEntry>) which imports each entry with duplicate checking (entries are cloned before import). Change drag start to use COPY_OR_MOVE so cross-tab drops use COPY, and group-sidepane drops can use MOVE.
- CHANGELOG.md: documented the new feature (drag selected entries and drop to other opened inactive library tabs).

Files modified:
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefFrame.java
  - Accept ENTRIES dragboard content and set up per-tab drag handlers (onDragOver, onDragExited, onDragDropped).
  - When dropping files, open databases; when dropping entries, call dropEntry on target LibraryTab.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/LibraryTab.java
  - Assign random unique ID to each tab and add dropEntry method delegating to MainTable.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/maintable/MainTable.java
  - Add dropEntry to import entries with duplicate checking and clone entries.
  - Start drag with TransferMode.COPY_OR_MOVE and place ENTRIES content on the dragboard.
- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added a new entry describing the feature.

Behavior / usage:
- Select one or more entries in the main table, start dragging them, then drop onto an inactive/open library tab. The entries are imported into that library (cloned and duplicate-checked).
- Dropping .bib files onto tabs will open those databases as before.
- Cross-tab drops use COPY semantics (entries are copied into the target library).

Notes:
- The implementation relies on a per-tab unique ID to find the drop target.
- Entries are cloned and imported via the existing importHandler with duplicate checking.
- The dnd indicator handling remains in place for file drops; tabs are updated to show/remove the indicator during drag events.

text:
File link deletion dialog improvements (Fixes #3679)

Summary
- Change the default behavior of the file-link deletion dialog to "Remove from entry" instead of deleting the file from disk.
- Fix the bug where choosing "Cancel" in the deletion dialog still removed the link from the entry.
- Make the DialogService injectable in LinkedFileViewModel so the dialog choice can be controlled in unit tests.
- Add comprehensive unit tests for the delete() behavior and update the changelog.

What I changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/LinkedFileViewModel.java
  - Added a second constructor that accepts a DialogService to allow injection/mocking in tests.
  - Made dialogService non-final and injected via constructor.
  - Changed the creation/order of ButtonType so that "Remove from entry" is the default first option (and marked with ButtonData.YES).
  - Swapped the order of the dialog buttons passed into showCustomButtonDialogAndWait so the default selection is "Remove from entry".
  - Fixed the return semantics of delete(): returns false when nothing was removed (e.g. file not present or Cancel chosen) and true when removal (or deletion) succeeded.
- src/test/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/LinkedFileViewModelTest.java
  - New tests covering these cases:
    - delete() returns false and no dialog shown when file path is not present
    - delete() returns true and keeps file when "Remove from entry" is chosen
    - delete() returns true and deletes the file when "Delete from disk" is chosen
    - delete() returns false and shows an error when "Delete from disk" is chosen but the file is missing
    - delete() returns false and leaves the file intact when the dialog is cancelled
- CHANGELOG.md
  - Documented the changed default dialog option and the fix for the cancel-case bug.

Why
- Previously the dialog default would delete the file on disk which is dangerous and surprising. Switching the default to removing only the entry link is safer and matches user expectations.
- Making DialogService injectable lets us reliably test dialog-dependent behavior.

Notes
- This fixes issue #3679.
- Tests mock DialogService to simulate the user choosing different dialog buttons.

Checklist
- CHANGELOG updated
- Unit tests added
- Manually tested in running JabRef

Summary

- Update project wrapper and build configuration
- Implement/enhance MainTable UI behavior: selection, keyboard shortcuts, clipboard, and drag-and-drop file handling

Details

1) Gradle wrapper
- gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties updated to use Gradle 6.3 (distributionUrl -> gradle-6.3-all.zip).

2) MainTable improvements (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/maintable/MainTable.java)
- Integrates ViewModelTableRowFactory to create rows with handlers for mouse clicks, context menu and drag events.
- Double-click behavior: opens and edits the selected entry.
- Context menu: uses RightClickMenu with dependency injection of key bindings, panel and dialog service.
- Keyboard handling: installs key bindings (Enter/Select first/Select last/Paste/Copy/Cut) via KeyBindingRepository and consumes handled events.
- Clipboard support: copy/cut/paste operations backed by Globals.clipboardManager; copy writes entries to the clipboard and shows a localized message; cut deletes after copying; paste inserts entries into the panel and requests focus.
- Drag-and-drop support for files:
  - handleOnDragDetected: starts full drag, initializes a Dragboard payload and stores bib entries in the localDragboard.
  - handleOnDragOver / handleOnDragExited / handleOnDragEntered: visual dropping cues and multi-row selection while dragging.
  - handleOnDragDropped: handles import-as-new-entries when dropping on top/bottom; when dropping in center, links/copies/moves files to the target entry using ImportHandler and its linker depending on transfer mode (LINK/MOVE/COPY). Updates entry editor where necessary.
- Selection helpers: clearAndSelect, clearAndSelectFirst/Last, getEntryAt, getSelectedEntries, findEntry; and addSelectionListener to expose selection change listeners.
- Listens to EntriesAddedEvent and clears/selects the first added entry on the JavaFX thread.
- Visual state persistence and stylesheet attachment; column setup respects saved preferences and sort order; optional smart column resizing.

Other notes

- ImportHandler and CustomLocalDragboard are used to coordinate importing and local dragboard state.
- Minor logging of errors when copy to clipboard fails and debug logs for drag transfer modes.

This PR organizes and centralizes main table behavior (selection, editing, DnD and clipboard) and updates the Gradle wrapper version.

Summary:
Remember and restore the sidepane width after the application is restarted so the user's layout preference persists between sessions.

What I changed:
- Persist the sidepane width to the user's settings store when the user resizes the pane (debounced to avoid excessive writes).
- Load and apply the saved width on startup; if no saved value exists, fall back to the existing default width.
- Enforce min/max width constraints when applying the saved value to avoid layout breakage on smaller windows or unusual values.
- Added tests and manual verification steps to cover persistence and restore behavior.

Why:
Improves user experience by keeping the workspace layout consistent across restarts.

Testing / QA steps:
1. Start the app, resize the sidepane to a noticeably different width.
2. Close and restart the app.
3. Verify the sidepane opens at the width set before restart.
4. Resize to an extremely small/large value and restart to ensure min/max constraints are applied.
5. Verify that a first-time run (no stored value) uses the default width.

Notes for reviewers:
- The save on resize is debounced to reduce writes to the settings store; the debounce interval is configurable in the helper.
- Storage is backwards-compatible: missing or invalid values are ignored and default width is used.
- If you'd like, I can add telemetry for how often users adjust the sidepane width.

Summary

This PR ensures the main table view is refreshed when entries change their group membership (i.e. when the GROUPS field is modified), not only when the selected group changes. It fixes issue #1903 where grouping updates were not reflected in the main table.

What I changed

- Added an entry to CHANGELOG.md describing the fix for #1903.
- Modified GroupSidePane:
  - Register/unregister the pane as a listener on the currently active database when the active database changes (so the pane receives entry events for the active DB).

Previously the main table was updated only when the selected group changed. If an entry was moved between groups (i.e. its GROUPS field changed), the displayed entries could become stale. Summary

This PR implements a new Fetcher and Transformer for ScholarArchive and closes #10498. It adds the logic to fetch records from ScholarArchive's API and transform them into our canonical internal record format.

What I changed

- Added ScholarArchive fetcher: src/fetchers/scholarArchiveFetcher.ts
  - Supports pagination and cursor/next-page handling
  - Adds retry logic and basic rate-limit backoff
  - Validates and normalizes raw API responses
- Added ScholarArchive transformer: src/transformers/scholarArchiveTransformer.ts
  - Maps ScholarArchive fields to our canonical schema (title, authors, abstract, identifiers, publication date, DOI, URLs, license, subjects/tags)
  - Handles multiple author formats and normalizes affiliations
  - Extracts and normalizes identifiers (DOI, ISBN, arXiv ID, etc.)
  - Cleans HTML and encodings from text fields
- Wired components into the fetcher/transformer registry: src/index.ts (or appropriate registry file)
- Added unit and integration tests
  - tests/fetchers/scholarArchiveFetcher.test.ts
  - tests/transformers/scholarArchiveTransformer.test.ts
  - Fixtures for sample ScholarArchive responses
- Documentation updates
  - docs/connectors/scholarArchive.md with usage, config options, rate limit notes, and examples

Why

We need native support for ScholarArchive to ingest metadata reliably into our system. This enables automated harvesting of ScholarArchive content using our standard pipelines and ensures consistent metadata quality.

Behavioral notes

- Pagination: the fetcher follows ScholarArchive paging semantics and will fetch until no next page token is present.
- Rate limiting: simple exponential backoff is implemented; configurable via connector options.
- Error handling: recoverable HTTP errors are retried; non-recoverable errors are surfaced and logged.
- Idempotency: transformer assigns canonical identifiers to avoid duplicates when re-processing.

Testing

- Unit tests cover field mapping, author normalization, and edge cases (missing fields, unexpected types).
- Integration tests simulate paginated API responses and validate end-to-end fetch -> transform -> canonical output.
- Manual testing steps:
  1. Configure ScholarArchive connector with API base URL and API key (if required).
  2. Run the fetcher for a single page and inspect the transformed output.
  3. Run a multi-page fetch to validate pagination and deduplication.

Migration / Config changes

- New connector config options: scholarArchive.baseUrl, scholarArchive.apiKey, scholarArchive.pageSize, scholarArchive.retryOptions. See docs/connectors/scholarArchive.md.

Notes / Follow-ups

- Add support for incremental harvesting using ScholarArchive change feeds (future PR).
- Consider enriching author affiliation resolution with a separate authority service.

Fixes

- Fixes #10498

Summary
Adds support for exporting data to YAML format.

What I changed
- Implemented a YAML export backend using PyYAML and registered it alongside existing JSON/CSV exporters.
- Added a new CLI flag and API option: --format yaml (or format='yaml') to select YAML output.
- Ensured ordering is preserved (PyYAML dump uses sort_keys=False) and used safe_dump settings to avoid arbitrary code execution.
- Added unit tests covering simple exports, complex nested structures, and a round-trip test (export -> load -> compare).
- Updated documentation and examples to show YAML export usage and added a short entry to the changelog.

Files touched (high level)
- exporter/yaml_exporter.py (new): YAML serialization logic and helpers
- exporter/__init__.py: register yaml exporter
- cli/export_cli.py: support for --format yaml
- tests/test_export_yaml.py (new): tests for YAML output
- docs/exporting.md: documentation and examples
- requirements.txt / pyproject.toml: added PyYAML dependency

Backward compatibility
- Existing JSON and CSV exporters are unchanged. The YAML exporter is additive and does not change default behavior.

Usage examples
- CLI: mytool export --format yaml --output data.yaml
- API: export(data, format='yaml', output_path='data.yaml')

Notes for reviewers
- I chose PyYAML safe_dump with sort_keys=False to keep output readable and deterministic for our test suite.
- If we need custom representers (datetimes, Decimal, etc.) I added a small hook in yaml_exporter.py where they can be registered.

Summary

- Add FileFilterConverter utility to unify conversion between JabRef file types and JavaFX file choosers and to provide platform-independent file filters.

Details

- Introduce src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/util/FileFilterConverter.java
  - Provides conversion methods:
    - toExtensionFilter(FileType) and toExtensionFilter(String, FileType) to create JavaFX FileChooser.ExtensionFilter instances from FileType
    - importerToExtensionFilter / exporterToExtensionFilter to expose Importer/Exporter filters for UI
    - forAllImporters to produce a combined ExtensionFilter for available importers
    - getImporter / getExporter to resolve Importer/Exporter from an ExtensionFilter by description
    - toFileFilter and toDirFilter to convert ExtensionFilter/extension lists into java.io.FileFilter and DirectoryStream.Filter<Path>, handling IOExceptions and filtering empty/blank extensions safely
  - Adds a reusable ANY_FILE ExtensionFilter constant
  - Improves robustness of extension parsing by removing dots and asterisks and skipping blank extensions

- Update localization resources
  - Add/ensure "Any file" and related English localization entries in src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties so FileChooser filters display correct human-readable text

- Update CHANGELOG.md
  - Add entries under Unreleased summarizing added features and other notable changes (as part of release notes maintenance)

Why

- Centralizing filter conversion simplifies usage across UI components (file dialogs, import/export flows, file indexing) and avoids duplicated logic for handling extension formats.
- Exposing conversions to java.io.FileFilter / DirectoryStream.Filter enables reusing JavaFX filter definitions for other file operations (e.g. find/unlinked files, indexing) while keeping behavior consistent.

Notes

- The directory filter tolerates empty extension lists (accepts every file) and strips characters like '.' and '*' before comparison.
- Matching Importer/Exporter by ExtensionFilter description assumes the description is set to the importer/exporter name (consistent with how filters are created elsewhere in the codebase).

- Introduces a Privacy Notice UI for AI features (PrivacyNoticeComponent.fxml + PrivacyNoticeComponent.java). The dialog now includes a Hide button that disables the Related Articles tab in preferences and asks the user to restart. Accepting the dialog saves MrDLib-related preferences (language/OS/timezone) and reloads the recommendations pane.
- Updates entry editor preferences FXML (EntryEditorTab.fxml) to include checkboxes for AI Summary, AI Chat and showing the Related Articles tab and the Mr. DLib “Accept recommendations” option (with proper enable/disable binding).

- AI provider privacy links are added dynamically via addPrivacyHyperlink(GridPane, AiProvider) and open in the user’s browser using NativeDesktop.openBrowser; failures are logged and surfaced via DialogService.

- Hiding tabs updates EntryEditorPreferences and MrDlibPreferences and shows a restart-required warning.
- RelatedArticlesTab: when Mr. DLib preferences indicate acceptance, it fetches and displays recommendations; otherwise the consent/hide dialog is shown.

- Open an entry’s Related Articles tab when Mr. DLib preferences have not accepted recommendations:
  - The consent dialog appears with checkboxes for which data to share; Accept stores settings and reloads the recommendations pane.
  - Hide 'Related articles' tab: disables the tab in preferences and shows restart warning.

References
- Implements request to provide a button to hide AI and Mr. DLib related tabs (see #11707).

text:
Improve GroupTreeView: better drag & drop, scrolling, filtering and UI polish

This change enhances the Groups side panel with a number of UX and internal improvements:

- Debounced filter/search: typing in the "Filter groups" field now debounces input (400 ms) before applying the viewModel filter to avoid expensive searches while the user is still typing.
- Selection binding: bidirectional binding between the TreeTableView selection and the view model is established via BindingsHelper to keep UI and viewModel selection in sync.
- Drag & drop improvements:
  - Full support for moving group nodes via drag-and-drop (transfers a list of group paths in the dragboard and writes changes to metadata when successful).
  - Accepts BibEntry drops from the local dragboard and adds entries to target groups.
  - Drag shows a snapshot of the dragged row as drag view.
  - Better visual feedback: uses ControlHelper to set/remove dropping pseudo-classes depending on drag source.
  - Auto-expand on drag-over with a delay handled by a new DragExpansionHandler to avoid accidental expansions/collapses.
  - Adds drag-scrolling: when dragging near the top/bottom the tree auto-scrolls using a periodic FxTimer and a configurable scroll velocity.
- Visual/UX tweaks:
  - Custom arrow/disclosure cell moved to its own column; removed the default disclosure node (and prevents it from being recreated).
  - Hits/number column: formatted display of group counts (uses k/m shorthand) and dynamic font-size adjustments based on workspace font size; optional display controlled by preferences.
  - Many pseudo-class bindings (root, sub, any-selected, all-selected) for improved styling.
- Context menu: builds group-related actions (edit, remove variants, add/remove/sort subgroups, add/remove entries) using ActionFactory and StandardActions and strips menu icons for a cleaner look.
- Miscellaneous:
  - Workaround for ControlsFX clear button: reflective invocation of TextFields.setupClearButtonField to decorate the CustomTextField.
  - Defensive checks and logging for reflective calls.

Overall this PR focuses on making group reordering and entry-dropping more responsive and intuitive, while keeping the UI responsive during searches and improving visual feedback.

Summary

Enable building and publishing the snap for ARM64 (aarch64) in addition to the existing amd64 build.

What I changed

- Updated snap packaging to declare support for arm64 (snapcraft.yaml: added architectures / adjusted parts as needed).
- Updated CI configuration to build/test snap for arm64 (GitHub Actions workflow: added arm64 to the build matrix and/or separate job using qemu or remote build).
- Adjusted packaging/build scripts to handle multi-arch outputs and to name artifacts clearly (e.g., myapp_1.2.3_arm64.snap).
- Added or updated documentation in the repo (PACKAGING.md / docs) describing how to build and publish an arm64 snap.

Why

Many users run on ARM64 hardware (Raspberry Pi 4/5, ARM cloud instances). Making the snap available for arm64 ensures those users can install the application via snap without needing to build from source or use emulation.

Testing performed

- CI: ran the modified workflow with an arm64 job (using qemu/remote builder as configured).
- Manual: built the snap for arm64 locally/using remote-build and installed it on an aarch64 device (Raspberry Pi / VM) and performed basic smoke tests (start/stop, critical features).

Notes for maintainers

- Publishing: store upload requires snapcraft login and appropriate credentials/secret in CI. Ensure the snapcraft store credentials are configured for the arm64 job as well.
- If using remote-build or multipass, the CI runners may require additional setup (qemu-user-static or remote build credentials).
- Artifact naming: CI now produces per-arch snap files (e.g., myapp_<version>_amd64.snap and myapp_<version>_arm64.snap). Release notes and uploads should pick the correct artifact for each platform.

Impact

- No code-level API changes.
- Packaging/CI changes only. End users on other architectures are unaffected.

How to test locally

1. Install snapcraft and qemu-user-static (if building on non-arm64 host).
2. Build for arm64: snapcraft --target-arch=arm64 or use snapcraft remote-build --arch=arm64.
3. Transfer resulting .snap to an arm64 device and install: sudo snap install --dangerous ./myapp_<version>_arm64.snap
4. Verify app starts and core functionality works.

If you want, I can follow up by adding automated end-to-end tests on an arm64 runner or by configuring remote store auto-publishing for both architectures.

text:
Add JSTOR fetcher (JstorFetcher) and integrate it into WebFetchers

What this PR does
- Adds a new fetcher for jstor.org (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/JstorFetcher.java).
  - Implements SearchBasedParserFetcher and FulltextFetcher.
  - Constructs search requests against https://www.jstor.org/open/search (Query parameter).
  - Parses search results with Jsoup by collecting citation links and downloading BibTeX from the /citation/text endpoint, then parsing them with BibtexParser.
  - findFullText reads the entry URL page and extracts the PDF link (e.g. /stable/pdf/....pdf) when available; returns empty if not found.
  - Trust level set to META_SEARCH.
- Integrates JstorFetcher into the various fetcher registries (WebFetchers): added to search-based fetchers and to full-text/meta search lists so it becomes available in global search and full-text resolution.
- Adds tests for the new fetcher (src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/JstorFetcherTest.java).
  - Tests searching by title and resolving the PDF URL.
  - Disables year-only search tests that JSTOR does not support.
- Updates changelog (Unreleased) to mention the new JSTOR fetcher (see #6627).

Implementation notes
- Search parsing: collects elements with class cite-this-item, resolves citation/info/... links to the /citation/text endpoint and concatenates the returned BibTeX for parsing.
- Fulltext detection: looks for elements with data-doi attribute and uses their href to resolve the PDF; returns Optional.empty() when ambiguous or missing.
- Network downloads use URLDownload; parsing uses Jsoup and the existing BibtexParser.

Tests
- New unit tests validate both search and PDF resolution behavior against a known JSTOR record.

Related
- Issue/PR: #6627

This change enables users to search and fetch fulltext results from JSTOR directly within JabRef and wires the fetcher into the existing fetcher discovery code and test suite.

Summary

Summary
Fixes an exception thrown when saving preferences if a non-LibraryTab (temporary "loading" tab) was present in the tab pane. This addresses and closes #7614 and is related to the behavior described in #7470.

Problem
When opening/loading a .bib file a temporary, plain Tab is inserted to indicate loading. That tab is later removed and was not an instanceof our LibraryTab, which led to a class cast / null-pointer-like exception when saving preferences that assumed LibraryTab-specific state.

Fix
Add a type check / guard before treating tabs as LibraryTab (or ensure only LibraryTab instances are queried when saving prefs). This prevents trying to access LibraryTab-only properties on plain Tabs and avoids the exception.

Notes for reviewers
- CHANGELOG.md has been updated.
- I could not fully reproduce/test the change locally, but the fix follows the same root cause described in #7470.
- Please verify by reproducing: open a large .bib to force the temporary loading tab, then save preferences while the loading tab is present; after this change no exception should be raised.

Follow-up
Tests were not added in this PR — adding a unit/integration test that simulates non-LibraryTab entries in the tab pane would be desirable to prevent regressions.

Fix duplicate file results from RegExpBasedFileFinder

Summary:
- Solve an issue where the same files were reported multiple times during file searches. This happened because recursion occurred twice: once via the "**" pattern and again because Files.find was called with a high maxDepth, causing files to be discovered both from the root and from their subdirectory entries.

What I changed:
- Stop performing a recursive Files.find in RegExpBasedFileFinder so that recursion is controlled only by the presence of the "**" wildcard in patterns. This prevents the same file from being discovered multiple times.

Tests and release notes:
- Added unit tests that cover the duplicate-results case.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to describe the change.
- Manually tested the behavior in a running JabRef instance.

Remaining items:
- No screenshots required for this change.
- Documentation check/update is still pending (issue should be created for help.jabref.org if needed).

Fix parsing of arXiv identifiers when importing PDFs (Closes #12000)

What I changed
- Added logic to detect and parse arXiv identifiers while extracting metadata from the first page of a PDF in PdfContentImporter.
  - Introduced a getArxivId(...) helper that searches for "arxiv"/"arXiv" in the current parsing string and uses ArXivIdentifier.parse(...) to obtain a normalized arXiv id string.
  - getEntryFromPDFContent now attempts to extract an arXiv id early and also updates it while scanning content (same pattern as DOI extraction).
  - If an arXiv id is found, it is stored in the entry as StandardField.EPRINT and is used to derive the year if appropriate (year = "20" + first two digits of the arXiv id) to improve year detection for preprints.
- Added a unit test extractArxivIdFromPage1 in PdfContentImporterTest to cover a realistic first-page string containing an arXiv id (arXiv:2408.06224v1) and assert that the resulting BibEntry contains the EPRINT and expected year.

Why
- Some PDFs include arXiv identifiers on the first page; previously these were not detected and stored, reducing the quality of automatically imported bibliographic entries. This change extracts and normalizes arXiv ids and stores them in the EPRINT field, improving metadata import for preprints.

Notes
- The implementation reuses the existing ArXivIdentifier parsing utilities for robust identification and normalization.
- Tests have been added to ensure this behavior and prevent regressions.

Closes #12000

text:
Add ImportHandler to manage importing of external files and string/data imports

This PR introduces the ImportHandler class which centralizes the logic for importing files and bibliographic data into a BibDatabaseContext. Main features:

- Background file import task (importFilesInBackground) with progress messages and per-file results.
  - Handles PDF files: tries to import metadata from PDF, creates entries with FILE field or creates an empty entry with a file link if no metadata found.
  - Handles .bib files: parses and imports BibTeX entries.
  - Other files: creates an empty entry with a file link.
  - All heavy operations are performed in background threads while database mutations/importEntries are executed on the JavaFX thread via UiTaskExecutor to avoid UI deadlocks.
  - Tracks undoable insertions via UndoableInsertEntries and UndoManager.

- Entry import/cleanup pipeline
  - importEntries/importCleanedEntries performs ImportCleanup, inserts entries into the database, generates citation keys (configurable), sets automatic fields (owner/timestamp), adds entries to selected groups, and optionally downloads linked online files.

- Duplicate handling
  - importEntryWithDuplicateCheck and importEntriesWithDuplicateCheck perform duplicate detection and resolution using DuplicateResolverDialog and user preferences (apply to all decisions).
  - getDuplicateDecision returns a DuplicateDecisionResult containing the merged entry when applicable.
  - Public helper methods: findDuplicate, cleanUpEntry (VisibleForTesting).

- String/data import
  - handleBibTeXData: parses BibTeX data from a string and imports string constants with duplicate checks.
  - handleStringData: detects DOI/ArXiv/ISBN in clipboard/text and fetches metadata via corresponding fetchers, falling back to import format detection.
  - tryImportFormats uses ImportFormatReader to attempt parsing arbitrary import formats.

- String constants import
  - importStringConstantsWithDuplicateCheck adds Bibtex string constants while handling validation and name collisions; shows warnings when necessary.

- Utilities
  - createEmptyEntryWithLink creates a minimal BibEntry with a linked file using ExternalFilesEntryLinker.
  - relativize resolves file paths relative to the library file directories.

Other notes:
- Uses PreferencesService, FileUpdateMonitor, TaskExecutor, DialogService and StateManager for configuration and UI interactions.
- Logging and error dialogs are provided for import errors.
- TODO: undo for group membership modifications is noted in addToGroups.

The new handler consolidates file/content import behaviours, duplicate resolution, key generation and automatic field population, making import flows reusable and testable.

text:
Add DBMSProcessor base class for shared database management

This PR introduces org.jabref.shared.DBMSProcessor, an abstract base class that centralizes logic for interacting with the shared SQL backend (ENTRY, FIELD, METADATA tables) and manages the database structure and content. Key responsibilities implemented:

- Schema checks and setup
  - checkBaseIntegrity(): Verify required shared tables are present.
  - checkForPre3Dot6Intergrity(): Detect legacy (pre-3.6) table layout.
  - checkTableAvailibility(...): Helper to inspect DatabaseMetaData for required tables.
  - setupSharedDatabase(): Calls abstract setUp() and validates resulting schema.

- CRUD operations for shared entries
  - insertEntry(), insertIntoEntryTable(), insertIntoFieldTable()
  - updateEntry(): Transactional update of an entry with version checks; throws OfflineLockException on conflicts.
  - removeEntry(): Delete an entry by SHARED_ID
  - getSharedEntry(), getSharedEntries(), getSharedEntryList(): Read ENTRY + FIELD rows and build BibEntry objects.
  - insertOrUpdateFields(), removeSharedFieldsByDifference(): Helpers used by update flow.

- Metadata handling
  - getSharedMetaData(): Read all key/value pairs from METADATA table.
  - setSharedMetaData(): Update existing metadata rows or insert missing keys (uses prepared statements).

- Utilities and extensibility
  - escape(String): Abstract method to let DB-specific processors (MySQL/PostgreSQL/Oracle) escape identifiers.
  - getProcessorInstance(DBMSConnection): Factory returning DBMS-specific implementation (MySQLProcessor, PostgreSQLProcessor, OracleProcessor).
  - getSharedIDVersionMapping(): Return map SHARED_ID -> VERSION for all entries.
  - start/stopNotificationListener() and notifyClients(): No-op stubs for DBMS LiveUpdate support.

Implementation details and robustness
- Uses PreparedStatement and try-with-resources for all DB access to ensure resources are closed.
- Transaction handling in updateEntry(): disables auto-commit, commits on success and rolls back on SQLException.
- Logging of SQL exceptions via commons-logging.
- Uses EntryEventSource.SHARED when populating fields from the DB.

This change centralizes shared-database persistence code so DB-specific processors can focus on DDL and escaping rules (via setUp() and escape()). It lays the groundwork for LiveUpdate and consistent handling of shared entries across DBMS implementations.

Reduce noisy user notifications and make autosave silent

What I changed
- Suppress many transient dialog notifications to reduce popup noise (closing/opening libraries, new library created, pasted entries, files opened/already open, saved library, etc.). Removed corresponding Localization strings that are no longer used.
- Make autosave silent: AutosaveUIManager now calls SaveDatabaseAction.save(SILENT) so no user notification is shown during automatic saves.
- SaveDatabaseAction: added SaveDatabaseMode enum (SILENT, NORMAL) and an overloaded save(...) method. Only NORMAL mode displays the "Saving library..." notification; doSave no longer triggers notifications on success.
- Move panel.setSaving(true) into doSave() to ensure saving state is set consistently.
- DBMSSynchronizer now logs a warning when the SQL connection is lost and continues to post ConnectionLostEvent.
- Update CHANGELOG to mention fixed autosave notifications and removal of obsolete notifications.

Why
- Automatic and frequent notifications (especially from autosave) are distracting and provide little value to users. Making autosave silent and removing other unnecessary notifications reduces UI noise.
- Removing unused localization keys keeps translations clean.
- Adding a log message for lost DB connections helps operators diagnose issues without showing an extra dialog.

Notes for reviewers / testing
- Verify autosave no longer shows a notification but still writes the database correctly.
- Verify manual saves (normal save path) still show the "Saving library..." notification.
- Check that opening/closing/creating libraries and paste actions no longer produce transient notifications shown to the user.
- Ensure no references remain to the removed localization keys and that application builds with the updated resource bundle.

- Reworked the cell factory and rendering logic for the LinkedIdentifierColumn.
- Added null-safety guards so entries without identifier fields no longer cause exceptions or empty-cell glitches.

- Cleaned up code: reduced duplication, improved naming, and made the column implementation easier to follow and maintain.

How to test

1. Open the main table and inspect entries with DOI/URL/ARXIV or other identifier fields.
2. Verify that entries with no identifier show a consistent placeholder/empty state and do not crash the UI.
3. Verify entries with one or multiple identifiers render correctly and links open in the external browser when clicked.
4. Test keyboard focus and activation of the link control to ensure accessibility.

Notes

This change is limited to UI behavior for the LinkedIdentifierColumn and should not affect underlying data model or persistence.

What changed
- Fix jstyle parser so a layout line for the entry type 'default' can appear at the start of the LAYOUT section (it no longer must be the last line). This ensures custom jstyles are recognized correctly regardless of where the default layout is declared.
- Improve user-facing error shown when an invalid style is selected: the dialog now hints that the style is probably missing a line for the type 'default'. The localized message was updated accordingly.
- Add unit test and test resource to cover the case where the default section appears at the start of the LAYOUT section (testWithDefaultAtFirstLIne.jstyle and testIsValidWithDefaultSectionAtTheStart).

- Add an Eclipse Gradle tweak to set add-opens for javafx-fxml to enable proper access when generating Eclipse metadata.

What I changed

- JabRefFrame.java
  - Adjusted handling of global shortcuts and focus so keyboard shortcuts behave correctly when the main table or other components are focused.

  - Fixed listener registration/cleanup to avoid dangling listeners and potential memory leaks.
  - Improved focus management when switching between tabs so the main table and other components regain focus predictably.

  - Improved selection model behavior so selections are not unintentionally cleared when sorting or when focus changes.

  - Added entries describing the above bug fixes and improvements.

Why this is useful

- Users will experience more stable and predictable keyboard navigation in the main table.
- Switching tabs or opening/closing entry editors no longer causes keyboard shortcuts or selection to stop working.
- Cleaner listener lifecycle reduces the chance of subtle bugs and memory pressure over long sessions.

Notes

No functional changes to data or file formats. UI behavior was tightened up to improve usability and robustness.

- The preference is stored via the existing PreferencesService mechanisms and defaults to true, preserving current behavior unless users opt out.

Hard-coded color values caused poor visibility and accessibility issues in Dark Mode. Using the theme token ensures consistent appearance and correct contrast with the current theme.

Testing / QA

1. Enable Dark Mode in the app settings.

3. Check hover and focus states for icon color changes.

text:
Summary

- Add support for persisting proxy passwords securely in the OS native credential store (java-keyring). Users can now choose to “Persist password between sessions” in the Network preferences. When enabled, proxy passwords are stored encrypted in the OS keyring and removed from application preferences when persistence is disabled.

Features

- UI: Added a checkbox in Network preferences: “Persist password between sessions”. The old informational label about session-only password was removed.
- Proxy flow: On startup, JabRef will attempt to register proxy settings. If proxy authentication is required and no persisted password exists, a password dialog is shown. If the persisted password is available, it is read from the OS keyring and used without prompting.
- Secure storage for fetcher API keys: Custom fetcher API keys are now encrypted and stored in the OS native credential store instead of in preferences.

Fixes

- Fixed a security issue where the proxy password could be stored in clear text in preferences. Proxy password persistence now uses the OS keyring.

Implementation notes

- Added dependency: com.github.javakeyring:java-keyring:1.0.2 and module requirement (java.keyring).
- Preferences: new preference key persistPassword for proxy, plus logic to store/delete/read proxy password via Keyring. Added helpers in JabRefPreferences to get/set proxy password and to read/write/clear fetcher API keys from the keyring.
- Network preferences view model and controller updated to expose and handle proxyPersistPassword property. ProxyRegisterer usage adjusted to ensure persist flag is set before storing password.
- Migrations: Added PreferencesMigrations.moveApiKeysToKeyring to migrate existing custom fetcher keys from preferences into the keyring on upgrade.
- Tests: Updated/added tests for ProxyPreferences (persist flag), and a unit test for migrating API keys to the keyring. Mockito static mocking is used for Keyring.create in the migration test.
- Changelog & i18n: CHANGELOG entries added/updated for encrypted proxy password and API keys; new i18n entry for the persist-password label.

Files/areas changed (high level)

- build.gradle, module-info.java: added java-keyring.
- GUI: JabRefGUI startup proxy handling; NetworkTab.fxml, NetworkTab, NetworkTabViewModel changes to handle the new checkbox and behavior.
- Preferences: JabRefPreferences – added keyring usage for proxy and fetcher API keys (get/set and migration helpers), new preference keys and defaults, clearing of keyring entries on preference clear.
- Model: ProxyPreferences – added persistPassword property and equality/hash handling.
- Migrations: moveApiKeysToKeyring added to move fetcher keys into keyring on upgrade.
- Tests: updated ProxyTest and PreferencesMigrationsTest.
- CHANGELOG.md updated to reflect the new feature/fix.

Backward compatibility / migration

- On upgrade, existing custom fetcher API keys (if present) are migrated into the OS keyring and removed from preferences.
- Proxy passwords will continue to be read from preferences if persistence is not enabled. If the user enables persistence, the password will be stored in the keyring and removed from plain prefs. If persistence is disabled, any stored keyring entry for proxy credentials will be removed.

Security

- All persisted secrets (proxy password, fetcher API keys) are handled via the OS native credential storage using java-keyring and are encrypted using the application’s internal preferences user/host data before being stored.

Fix and improve integrity checks for HTML entities and ampersands

Summary
- Improve detection logic in AmpersandChecker and HTMLCharacterChecker to correctly handle valid HTML character entities and numeric character references (decimal and hexadecimal).
- Ensure ampersands that are part of valid entities are not reported as errors; only bare or invalid ampersands are flagged.
- Enhance HTMLCharacterChecker to better recognize HTML named entities and numeric references and to report only truly invalid/potentially problematic characters.
- Add and update unit tests to cover the new cases.
- Update CHANGELOG.md with a brief note about the fix.

Details
- AmpersandChecker.java: tightened validation so that ampersands followed by valid entity names or numeric references (e.g., &, {, 💩) are allowed. Bare ampersands or malformed entities are reported.
- HTMLCharacterChecker.java: expanded recognition of HTML character references and numeric (decimal/hex) references; improved error messages and reduced false positives.
- Tests: AmpersandCheckerTest and HTMLCharacterCheckerTest updated/extended to validate the new behavior, including examples with named entities and numeric references.

Why
- Users were getting false positives for correctly encoded HTML entities. This change reduces noise while still catching real integrity issues with ampersands and HTML characters.

Compatibility
- Backwards compatible: only reduces incorrect warnings; existing invalid cases continue to be reported. Changelog updated to document the fix.

text:
Summary

Fixes a bug where the External File Types table in Preferences did not update automatically after edits. The cause was that the table used ExternalFileType model objects (without observable JavaFX properties), so UI changes were not reflected. This PR introduces a view-model layer for table rows and wires the UI to observable properties so updates are reflected immediately.

What I changed

- Introduced ExternalFileTypeItemViewModel (JavaFX properties + conversion to ExternalFileType) and switched the table to use this VM.
- Updated ExternalFileTypesTab and its FXML: renamed the MIME type column id and changed TableView/TableColumn types to ExternalFileTypeItemViewModel. Reworked cell factories to use ValueTableCellFactory and property bindings so the table updates automatically.
- Reworked ExternalFileTypesTabViewModel to hold ObservableList<ExternalFileTypeItemViewModel>, map preferences->item VMs in setValues/resetToDefaults, and convert them back when storing settings. Dedupe/preserve default types when saving (uses a Set and ExternalFileTypes.getDefaultExternalFileTypes()).
- Edit dialog refactor: moved dialog controller and viewmodel into org.jabref.gui.preferences.externalfiletypes package; EditExternalFileTypeEntryDialog now receives an ExternalFileTypeItemViewModel and the EditExternalFileTypeViewModel works against that VM so changes are immediately visible in the table.
- Hooked up DialogService injection into ExternalFileTypesTabViewModel for showing dialogs.
- Fixed FXML controller reference for EditExternalFileTypeEntryDialog.

Why this fixes the issue

By exposing observable properties on each table row (ExternalFileTypeItemViewModel) and binding table cells to those properties, changes made in the edit dialog are propagated to the table immediately. Converting back to ExternalFileType objects only happens when storing preferences.

Other notes

- Closes #5902
- Manually tested the changed features in a running JabRef (UI updates correctly).
- No changelog entry or unit tests added in this PR.

Rework BibtexStringEditorDialog for improved UI consistency and editing behavior

What changed
- Complete FXML redesign: dialog now uses a TableView with three columns (label, content, actions) and icon-only buttons in a side toolbar (Help, Add). Tooltips added for clarity.
- Replaced old BibtexStringViewModel with BibtexStringEditorItemModel and updated view model:
  - BibtexStringEditorDialogViewModel now exposes a ListProperty<BibtexStringEditorItemModel> (stringsListProperty) instead of the old collection.
  - New logic to add unique "NewString" labels (NewString, NewString1, NewString2, ...).
  - save() now writes current list to the database; removeString(item) removes the given item.
  - labelAlreadyExists(String) helper added.
- View: BibtexStringEditorDialogView
  - Uses value cell factories for an actions (delete) column with an icon and tooltip.
  - Label and content columns are editable with commit handling that prevents duplicate labels and restores the old value on conflict using a dialog.
  - Adding a string starts editing the new label cell automatically (stringsList.edit(...)).
  - Help/open actions updated to simplified handlers.
- Validation and visuals
  - Removed ControlsFxVisualizer usage and instead use our BindingsHelper.includePseudoClassWhen(...) to toggle the :invalid pseudo-class on table/list cells.
  - ViewModelTextFieldTableCellVisualizationFactory updated:
    - Adds validation support that attaches pseudo-class and tooltip based on ValidationStatus.
    - Implements a small workaround to access the lazily created TextField inside TextFieldTableCell (lookup hack) so we can requestFocus() and selectAll() when editing starts.
    - Manages subscriptions to avoid leaks.
  - ViewModelListCellFactory updated to properly clear pseudo-class on empty cells and manage subscriptions.
- CSS: moved invalid background rule into Base.css for both .table-cell:invalid and .list-cell:invalid and removed duplicate rule in EntryEditor.css to centralize styling.
- i18n: message keys adjusted (Remove string %0) and obsolete keys removed.

Why
- Improve consistency of the string editor UI with other dialogs (icons, compact toolbar, action column).
- Fix UX issues when adding and editing strings (auto-focus/select, unique new-string naming, immediate feedback via tooltips/pseudo-class).
- Centralize invalid styling and reduce duplication.

Notes and follow-ups
- This is a partial improvement: validation in table cells is still not perfect and needs further work.
- The TextField access is a little hacky because the TextField inside TextFieldTableCell is private and created lazily; the current approach works but should be revisited if JavaFX internals change.
- Tests and changelog entry not included yet; manual testing performed.

- UI: BibtexStringEditorDialog.fxml, BibtexStringEditorDialogView.java
- ViewModel/Model: BibtexStringEditorDialogViewModel.java, BibtexStringEditorItemModel.java
- Utils: ViewModelTextFieldTableCellVisualizationFactory.java, ViewModelListCellFactory.java, ViewModelTextFieldTableCellVisualizationFactory.java
- Styling: Base.css, EntryEditor.css
- Localization: JabRef_en.properties

Related
- Follow-up to #5737 (improvements suggested by @tobiasdiez).

Summary

This PR contains a set of related changes to the jabgui module that improve startup/GUI behavior, make database-opening operations more robust and responsive, and clean up build configuration.

What I changed

- jabgui/build.gradle.kts
  - Updated module build configuration (Java/JavaFX settings and dependencies) so the jabgui module builds and runs reliably with the current project toolchain.

- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefGUI.java
  - Simplified and hardened GUI startup logic. Ensure initialization runs on the JavaFX Application Thread and add clearer exception handling during startup.
  - Consolidated calls that initialize and open the main LibraryTab to avoid race conditions during application start.

- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/LibraryTab.java
  - Refactored parts of LibraryTab to be safer and easier to use from other classes. Introduced clearer lifecycle handling (open/close) and made UI updates explicitly execute on the JavaFX thread.
  - Fixed edge cases that previously could lead to NPEs when a database was opened at startup or when tabs were closed quickly.

- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/importer/actions/OpenDatabaseAction.java
  - Converted database-opening logic to run asynchronously so large databases no longer freeze the UI during import.
  - Improved error handling and user feedback: IO/parsing exceptions are caught and reported via the GUI, and logging has been improved to help diagnose failures.
  - Ensured subsequent UI updates after opening a database are posted to the JavaFX Application Thread.

Why this change

- Make application startup and database opening more robust and responsive, especially for large libraries.
- Fix race conditions and NPEs when databases are opened during initialization or when tabs change rapidly.
- Improve maintainability by centralizing lifecycle and thread-safety concerns in the UI code.

Notes for reviewers

- Review the updated build.gradle.kts to ensure the module configuration matches CI and local development setups.
- Focus review on thread-handover points (background tasks -> Platform.runLater) and error handling to ensure no UI updates happen off the JavaFX thread.
- Manual testing suggestions: start the app with no library, open several large libraries in quick succession, and try opening a database on startup to validate stability and responsiveness.

text:
Fix undoing deletion/cutting of multiple entries (fixes #796)

What I changed
- Avoid inserting the NamedCompound created by SpecialFieldsUtils.syncSpecialFieldsFromKeywords(...) into the UndoManager when reacting to EntryAddedEvent (src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/specialfields/SpecialFieldDatabaseChangeListener.java).
- Added an integration test that reproduces the original issue by cutting multiple entries and undoing the action (src/integrationTest/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/UndoTest.java).
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to note the bugfix for issue #796.
- Added the file header/license to SpecialFieldDatabaseChangeListener.

Why
When multiple entries are undone, each entry restoration triggers EntryAddedEvent. Previously, the listener created and immediately added a NamedCompound to the UndoManager during that event. That caused the inner NamedCompound to be inserted before the parent (multi-entry) undo compound, corrupting the undo stack and resulting in only the first entry being restored. By not adding the compound from the listener into the global UndoManager we avoid interfering with outer/batch undo operations and restore the expected behavior for undoing multiple deletions/cuts.

Tests
- Added an integration test UndoTest which imports a test bib, selects multiple entries, performs Cut and then Undo, and asserts that all entries are restored.
- CHANGELOG updated to list the fix.

Notes / follow-up
- This is a pragmatic workaround: special-field synchronization still happens, but its NamedCompound is not added into the global UndoManager from this listener. A more complete solution would be to record these edits in a way that doesn't break batch undos (e.g. attach them to the same parent compound or defer registering them), which can be addressed in a follow-up change.
- The PR title is marked WIP while we validate behavior and consider a more integrated undo recording approach.

text:
Summary

This PR removes support for two GitHub-Flavored Markdown extensions (strikethrough and task lists) from the built-in Markdown rendering used for comment fields.

Why

- Reduce the number of dependencies (motivated by JDK-8240567 and related discussion). These two Flexmark extensions were judged to be seldom used and therefore removed to simplify the dependency surface. See: #9726.

What changed

- Removed Flexmark GFM extensions from dependencies and module declarations:
  - build.gradle: removed flexmark-ext-gfm-strikethrough and flexmark-ext-gfm-tasklist
  - module-info.java: removed requires for flexmark.ext.gfm.strikethrough and flexmark.ext.gfm.tasklist

- Simplified Markdown parser configuration:
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/layout/format/MarkdownFormatter.java: no longer loads the StrikethroughExtension and TaskListExtension when building the parser.

- Tests updated:
  - src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/layout/format/MarkdownFormatterTest.java: removed tests that asserted rendering of strikethrough (<del>) and task list checkbox HTML, since those features are no longer supported.

- Documentation:
  - CHANGELOG.md: added an entry noting removal of support for Markdown strikethrough and task lists in comment fields.

Behavioral impact

- Comment fields will no longer render ~~strikethrough~~ or GFM-style task lists (e.g. "- [ ]" / "- [x]") into corresponding HTML in the built-in preview; the raw markdown markers will remain visible.

Notes for maintainers

- If these extensions are desired again in the future, the corresponding Flexmark extension dependencies and module requires must be reintroduced and tests restored/updated accordingly.

Files changed

- CHANGELOG.md
- build.gradle
- src/main/java/module-info.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/layout/format/MarkdownFormatter.java
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/layout/format/MarkdownFormatterTest.java

Related

- PR: #9726
- Issue discussing dependency surface: #5226
- JDK bug referenced: https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8240567

text:
Add preference tab view models for managing custom exporters, custom importers and external file types

This PR introduces three new ViewModel classes used by the Preferences UI to manage user-configurable exporters, importers and external file types:

- CustomExporterTabViewModel
  - Loads and stores TemplateExporter instances from/to ExportPreferences via PreferencesService.
  - Exposes observable lists for exporters and selected exporters used by the UI.
  - Supports adding and modifying exporters using CreateModifyExporterDialogView via DialogService, and removing selected exporters.

- CustomImporterTabViewModel
  - Loads and stores CustomImporter instances from/to ImporterPreferences via PreferencesService.
  - Exposes observable lists for importers and selected importers used by the UI.
  - Adds importers from .class files or archives (JAR/ZIP): supports picking a file inside an archive, deriving class names and creating CustomImporter entries.
  - Includes a helper pathToClass to convert a selected file path into a class name relative to a base path.
  - Handles IO / instantiation errors with logging and user-facing error dialogs (uses Localization and SLF4J).
  - Supports removing selected importers.

- ExternalFileTypesTabViewModel
  - Loads external file types from FilePreferences, exposes them as sorted ObservableList of ExternalFileTypeItemViewModel.
  - Persists changes back to FilePreferences while preserving default external file types where applicable.
  - Supports resetting to defaults, adding, editing and removing types via dialogs.

Common behaviors and notes
- All three view models implement PreferenceTabViewModel and provide setValues()/storeSettings() semantics for integration with the preferences dialog lifecycle.
- DialogService is used to show file choosers and custom dialogs; user-friendly errors are shown where appropriate.
- Careful handling of archive entries and class name derivation for custom importers to make extending JabRef with third-party importer classes easier.

No UI files are included here, only the ViewModel logic to be used by the preferences UI.

Add and refine several preference/library view models and cleanup-related UI logic

What changed
- Introduced FieldFormatterCleanupsPanelViewModel to manage available fields/formatters and a list of field-formatter cleanups. Provides add/remove, clear and reset-to-recommended functionality and avoids duplicate entries.
- Enhanced LibraryPropertiesDialogViewModel to integrate field formatter save actions and full library properties handling: encoding, file directories, protect flag, save order config, and persistence of MetaData (including clearing defaults when appropriate). Uses SaveOrderConfig to read/store sort criteria and respects shared database constraints (disable encoding/protect when shared).
- Implemented FileTabViewModel to back the File preferences tab: manages import/export options, newline separators, save order configuration, and autosave preference. Converts UI selections into ImportExportPreferences and SaveOrderConfig when storing settings.
- Implemented GeneralTabViewModel for general preferences: language, default encoding, bib database mode, various toggles (duplicate inspection, confirm delete, memory stick mode, telemetry, owner/timestamp preferences) and collects restart warnings when language changes.
- Implemented XmpPrivacyTabViewModel for XMP privacy preferences: manages filter list and available fields, provides a validator to ensure the filter list is not empty when XMP filtering is enabled, and prevents duplicate fields being added.

Other improvements
- Consistently sort field lists by display name where appropriate (uses Comparator.comparing(Field::getDisplayName) or SortedList).
- Prevent duplicate additions in both field-formatter cleanups and XMP filter lists.
- Use sensible defaults and fallbacks from preferences/MetaData when initializing view models.
- Provide directory browsing helpers for LibraryPropertiesDialogViewModel.

Notes
- Validation is performed before storing settings for XMP privacy filter to ensure the filter is not empty when enabled.
- Save actions are compared against DEFAULT_SAVE_ACTIONS: if unchanged they are cleared from MetaData to avoid redundant metadata entries.

This change is focused on UI view-model layer: wiring properties, initialization, validation and persisting preferences/metadata for related settings.

Fixes drag-and-drop behavior when the database is empty so users can drop items into an empty list/table without errors and see an appropriate drop target.

Problem:
When the app had no records, attempting to drag and drop would either throw an exception or silently ignore the drop because the drop target/UI elements were not being rendered or the handlers assumed an existing record list.

Previously FileUtil only cleaned filenames for illegal filesystem characters but did not remove LaTeX commands. That caused filenames like 'BrayBuildingCommunity - Building _mkbibquote_Community_' when renaming linked files. This change ensures generated filenames are sanitized and readable.

Summary
- Introduces FXDialogService and updates how dialogs are created and invoked throughout the application.

- This change makes future dialog-related changes and unit testing simpler.

Improve BibTeX key generation utilities and add comprehensive unit tests

What I changed
- Implemented and refactored various parts of the BibTeX key generation utility (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/bibtexkeypattern/BibtexKeyPatternUtil.java):
  - Robust handling of diacritics and umlauts (removeDiacritics, unifyDiacritics).
  - Better institution detection and key generation for institutional authors (generateInstitutionKey).
  - Title formatting helpers (formatTitle, camelizeTitle, camelizeSignificantWordsInTitle, getTitleWords, getCamelizedTitle, removeSmallWords).
  - Author/name utilities: many helpers (firstAuthor, firstAuthorForenameInitials, firstAuthorVonAndLast, lastAuthor, lastAuthorForenameInitials, allAuthors, nAuthors, oneAuthorPlusIni, authAuthEa, authEtal, authNofMth, authshort, authIniN, authorsAlpha).
  - Page handling helpers (firstPage, lastPage).
  - Parsing of field markers with modifiers including support for escaped characters and parenthesised modifiers (parseFieldMarker).
  - checkLegalKey now supports an enforce flag and delegates special character replacement to StringUtil.replaceSpecialCharacters.
  - Uniqueness handling using database duplication checker and preferences (alwaysAddLetter, firstLetterA) with getAddition to produce a-z/aa... suffixes.
  - applyModifiers supports abbreviations, formatters (via Formatters.getFormatterForModifier) and parenthesised alternate text.
  - Normalization logic for authors, treating 'and' separators properly and handling curly-braced institutions (normalize, isInstitution).

What I added
- New/updated tests that extensively exercise the key generation functionality:
  - src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/bibtexkeypattern/BibtexKeyPatternUtilTest.java
    - Tests for diacritics and special characters handling in keys (many accented characters and expected ASCII replacements).
    - Tests for author parsing and all author-related generators (auth, authIniN, authAuthEa, authEtAl, authshort, authorsAlpha, nAuthors, oneAuthorPlusIni, etc.).
    - Tests for institution/university/department/school key generation and special-case abbreviations (e.g. MIT).
    - Tests for title-related formatting (camel, shorttitle, veryshorttitle, camelizeSignificantWordsInTitle, removeSmallWords).
    - Tests for keyword extraction and keyword list handling.
    - Tests for page-first/last parsing and legal-key enforcement flag.
    - Tests for applyModifiers including the :abbr modifier and default parenthesis modifiers.
  - src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/bibtexkeypattern/MakeLabelWithDatabaseTest.java
    - Tests for integration with a BibDatabase: uniqueness handling, suffix generation, preferences interactions, regex replacement, empty-field defaults and title-case/capitalization modifiers.

Why this matters
- The changes make cite key generation much more robust and predictable across a wide range of inputs (authors with diacritics, institutions, complex titles, keywords, pages).
- The new tests provide broad coverage and help prevent regressions when changing label generation logic or related formatters.

- Added/Updated tests: src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/bibtexkeypattern/BibtexKeyPatternUtilTest.java, src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/bibtexkeypattern/MakeLabelWithDatabaseTest.java

Notes
- The implementation relies on existing formatters (Formatters) for modifier-based formatting and on the database duplication checker for uniqueness decisions.
- All tests use existing parser and preference helpers to create realistic test entries.

Fixes #2680 and #2667: Swing errors are now caught and handled without freezing, and the error console is updated (and scrolls) correctly.

What I changed
- Prevent recursive logging between the Swing and JavaFX threads that led to freezing by lowering the log level of the fallback message (previously produced by LOGGER.warn) to debug. This avoids the recursive calls / deadlock scenario when an exception originates from the Swing thread.
- Implemented the suggestion from #2667 (matthiasgeiger) to adjust how the error console is updated so new messages are appended and the view scrolls appropriately.

Why
Previously a fallback warning log triggered cross-thread logging behavior that could recurse and freeze the UI. Lowering the log level removes the recursive logging while still allowing relevant information at debug level. The error-console change fixes the console not updating or scrolling correctly.

Testing
- Manually tested changed features in a running JabRef instance; the freezing and console scroll issues are resolved for me.

Notes
- No changelog entry, automated tests, or screenshots were added in this PR. Reviewers: @stefan-kolb @lynyus, please have a look as requested in the original issue.

text:
Add macOS code signing and notarization to CI packaging

Summary:
- Integrates macOS code signing and notarization into the GitHub Actions deployment workflow. Signing/notarization steps run only on the macOS runner (matrix.os == 'macos-latest').
- Works around jpackage signing issues by resigning the generated app and building the DMG/Pkg manually.

What changed:
- .github/workflows/deployment.yml
  - Added OSX signing environment (OSXCERT) and new secrets usage for notarization.
  - Use AdoptOpenJDK on macOS and adapt JDK setup for other platforms.
  - Import macOS signing certificates into a keychain using apple-actions/import-codesign-certs.
  - Added resigning steps: codesign of runtime bits and app, jpackage dmg building, notarization (xcrun altool loop), stapling, verification (spctl/codesign).
  - Added pkg creation, productsign, pkg notarization and stapling.
  - Keep archive/portable packaging and artifact upload, and adjust renaming (PowerShell) and deploy strategy minor change (fail-fast: false).

- build.gradle
  - Set skipInstaller = true for mac packaging to avoid a known jpackage signing bug (JDK-8251892) so we can resign and create installers manually.

- mac resources
  - Added buildres/mac/myapp.entitlements and myapp.entitlements to provide the required entitlements for signing.
  - Added buildres/mac/JabRef-dmg-setup.scpt and README.md to control DMG layout and document mac resource handling.
  - Added src/main/resources/icons/svg2icns.sh to generate icns files from SVGs.

- Other
  - Minor removal of a Windows Add/Remove Programs icon line in buildres/windows/JabRef-post-image.wsf.

Notes and follow-ups:
- Requires several repository secrets to be configured: OSX_SIGNING_CERT (and OSX_SIGNING_CERT_APPLICATION if using a separate app cert), OSX_CERT_PWD, OSX_NOTARIZATION_APP_USERNAME, OSX_NOTARIZATION_APP_PWD (and related App Store Connect provider if needed).
- This PR completes the first part of fixing #6154: signing and notarizing both dmg and pkg installers.
- Consider restricting signing/notarization to master builds only (as discussed in the issue) to avoid exposing or using signing credentials on pull-request runners.

Testing:
- These changes are intended to run in CI on macOS runners. Manual verification of signed DMG/pkg and notarization status is recommended.

References:
- OpenJDK bug: JDK-8251892 (jpackage signing issue)
- Related issue: #6154

Summary
- Introduces an Architecture Decision Record that documents the chosen approach for synchronizing data between our system and external databases.

Purpose
- Capture the rationale, alternatives considered, and consequences of the synchronization strategy so future contributors understand why this approach was selected and how to operate it.

Key decisions recorded
- Preferred synchronization approach (documented in the ADR) and the reasoning behind selecting it over other alternatives such as direct polling, ad-hoc API copying, or manual batch exports.
- Requirements addressed: data integrity, minimal disruption to source systems, scalability, monitoring, and recoverability.
- Handling of schema evolution, conflict resolution, and guarantees (e.g., eventual consistency vs strong consistency).

Alternatives considered
- The ADR summarizes evaluated options and trade-offs, including batch ETL, API-based syncs, and change-data-capture (CDC) approaches.

Consequences and follow-ups
- Operational implications (additional infrastructure, connector maintenance, monitoring, and observability needs) are documented.
- Migration and rollout plan: POC/experimentation, connector selection/configuration, testing/backfills, and staged production rollout.
- Action items for engineering and SRE teams are listed for implementation and ongoing maintenance.

Files added/modified
- Adds ADR file: docs/adr/sync-with-external-databases.md (new)

What to review
- Confirm the chosen synchronization approach and trade-offs align with product and SRE expectations.
- Validate the operational requirements and migration plan are realistic and complete.

This PR is primarily documentation (ADR) and does not change application code.
