Summary

- Add a new preference to control whether the Entry Editor should open the Source tab by default and make the Entry Editor respect this setting.
- Improve behavior and robustness of the Source tab (lazy initialization and focus handling).
- Improve Linked Files editor: better handling of file paths and user interactions (drag & drop/opening files), and align behavior with preferences for file links.
- Ensure group tree selection and updates do not unexpectedly change when entries are edited.
- Update preferences and changelog to reflect the new setting and related fixes.

What I changed

Files modified
- JabRefPreferences.java
  - Added a new preference key for opening the Source tab by default (with a sensible default value).

- EntryEditor.java
  - Reads the new preference and selects the appropriate tab when an entry is opened/created.
  - Ensures the editor restores/sets focus in a stable way when switching tabs.

- SourceTab.java
  - Improved initialization so heavy components are lazily created only when needed.
  - Fixed focus and caret placement when the Source tab becomes visible.

- LinkedFilesEditor.java
  - Improved handling of file paths (relative vs absolute) and interactions (drag & drop and open actions).
  - Respect preferences for linking behavior and ensure consistent updates to the entry when files are added/removed.

- GroupTreeController.java
  - Prevent the group tree selection from being lost or changed unexpectedly while the entry editor is open/active.
  - Ensure group updates triggered by editor actions do not disrupt user selection.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added notes describing the new preference and the bug fixes/improvements.

Why this change

- Users wanted a way to control whether the raw BibTeX/ BibLaTeX source is shown by default when editing an entry. Adding a preference allows users to pick their preferred default behavior.
- Lazily initializing the Source tab reduces startup and editor open overhead for users who do not use the source view regularly.
- Fixes in linked files handling address issues with path normalization and file actions that could cause inconsistent entry state.
- Preventing unintended group selection changes improves UX when working with the group tree alongside the entry editor.

Testing & compatibility

- The new preference defaults preserve prior behavior for existing users unless they opt in to change it.
- Manual testing done for: opening entries, switching tabs, adding/removing linked files (drag & drop and dialog), and editing groups while the editor is open.

Notes

- Developers: see JabRefPreferences for the new key if you want to control the behavior programmatically or add UI bindings.
- The changelog entry briefly documents the user-facing changes introduced by this PR.

- Consolidates multiple save operations into batched writes where appropriate.
- Adds debounce logic to avoid redundant immediate saves from rapid successive updates.

- Moves non-critical save work to an asynchronous/background worker to keep the UI responsive.
- Add unit and integration tests covering the new save paths and edge cases.

Why:
- Reduce number of DB calls and total write overhead.
- Improve perceived responsiveness for users by avoiding blocking saves.
- Increase overall throughput and stability under bursty update patterns.

Testing & benchmarks:
- Existing and new tests updated; CI should pass.
- Local benchmarks show fewer database writes under common scenarios and lower average save latency.

Notes for reviewers:
- Pay attention to transaction boundaries and error handling to ensure no data loss on failure.
- Review debounce thresholds and batch sizing to confirm they match expected UX/consistency trade-offs.
- No database schema changes included; migration not required.

- Removed older code that attempted to disable editors or added a separate hide button; the previous implementation is commented out.

How to test
1. Open an entry that contains the user-specific comment field.
2. Use the new "Hide user comments" / "Show user comments" toggle in the Comments tab to hide or re-enable the user-specific comment field.
3. Verify that the preference is persisted and that toggling updates the UI immediately.

- The button text is currently hard-coded; consider using localization strings instead.

Persist last-opened files and file-history entries as paths relative to the current working directory and convert them back to absolute when exposed.

Summary of changes:
- LastFilesOpenedPreferences
  - Store lastFilesOpened and lastFocusedFile as relative paths (converted with toRelative using the working directory).
  - getLastFilesOpened() and getLastFocusedFile() return absolute paths (converted with toAbsolute) so external callers receive absolute paths as before.
  - setLastFilesOpened and setLastFocusedFile convert incoming paths to relative for storage.
  - Added helper methods toRelative and toAbsolute with null-safety and a fallback to keep the absolute path if relativization fails.

- FileHistory
  - When adding entries (doAdd) and when marking a new file (newFile), convert the path to a relative form before storing (toRelative).
  - Added toRelative and toAbsolute helpers (same approach as in preferences).
  - History trimming behavior unchanged.

Why: Storing paths relative to the working directory improves portability of persisted preferences/history and avoids embedding absolute paths that may break when the project or installation is moved. The code preserves backwards-safety by converting stored entries to absolute paths when returned and falling back to absolute storage if relativization fails.

Summary

Refactor and improve the date field editor by introducing a reusable TemporalAccessorPicker component and migrating DateEditor and its ViewModel to use the new component. The change centralizes TemporalAccessor handling (LocalDate / Year / YearMonth etc.), improves parsing/formatting, validation and UI behavior, and wires the updated editor into the FieldEditors factory. The changelog is updated to reflect the improvements.

What I changed

- Added TemporalAccessorPicker: a reusable UI component for editing TemporalAccessor values with locale-aware formatting, parsing, and validation.
- Refactored DateEditorViewModel to handle TemporalAccessor semantics and to provide clearer parsing/formatting and error state handling.
- Updated DateEditor to use the new TemporalAccessorPicker and simplified the editor logic/UI accordingly.
- Updated FieldEditors to register/return the revised DateEditor where appropriate.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md with a short note about the improvements.

Why

- Consolidates date/time editing logic into a single reusable component (TemporalAccessorPicker) used by the DateEditor, reducing duplication and making it simpler to add more temporal types in the future.
- Improves user experience with better parsing, validation feedback, and locale-aware formatting.
- Keeps code cleaner by moving parsing/formatting responsibilities into the ViewModel and the new component.

Compatibility / Migration

- Public API surface for callers of the field editors remains functionally the same; editors now internally work with TemporalAccessor types for more robust handling of date-like values.
- There should be no user-facing breaking changes, but date parsing/validation behavior has been tightened to reduce invalid input acceptance.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/DateEditorViewModel.java (refactor)

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/FieldEditors.java (updated registration)
- CHANGELOG.md (updated)

Notes

- Further tests could be added to cover parsing edge cases across locales; none were added in this change.
- This PR lays groundwork for supporting more TemporalAccessor types in other editors in future work.

text:
Introduce embedded PostgreSQL lifecycle management and cleanup to prevent orphaned Postgres processes.

Summary of changes:
- Add PostgreServer: starts an EmbeddedPostgres instance, writes metadata (port/pid), initializes trigram extension, creates schema and installs helper functions, exposes a Connection and graceful shutdown.
- Add PostgresMetadataWriter: writes a JSON metadata file to the temp directory containing the Java PID, Postgres port and timestamp.
- Add PostgreProcessCleaner: scans the temp directory for leftover Postgres metadata files from previous runs, detects dead Java processes, determines the PID of the Postgres process listening on the recorded port and kills it to avoid zombie Postgres instances. Called early on startup.
- Launcher updated to call PostgreProcessCleaner.checkAndCleanupOldInstances() at startup, to register the PostgreServer in the injector, add a shutdown hook to stop Postgres, and wire the server setup into the application startup sequence.
- Directories.getTmpDirectory() helper added for temp file location resolution.
- Build and module updates: jablib build.gradle.kts adds embedded-postgres and platform-specific binaries; module-info.java updated to require embedded.postgres and PostgreSQL JDBC module.

Why:
- Prevents leftover embedded Postgres processes from remaining after JabRef crashes or is forcefully terminated, improving reliability and resource cleanup on startup.

Notes:
- Metadata files are created under the system temp directory (jabref-postgres-info-<javaPid>.json). The cleaner will remove metadata files after handling the leftover Postgres instance.

- Credit: Tobias Stoever (author comment retained in code).

text:
Fix: Clean up orphaned embedded PostgreSQL instances and ensure proper shutdown

Fixes #12844

Summary
- Added a mechanism to detect and clean up stale embedded PostgreSQL instances left behind by previous JabRef sessions. This prevents stray postgres processes from remaining after JabRef crashes or is forcefully terminated.
- Introduced PostgreProcessCleaner which scans temporary metadata files (jabref-postgres-info-<pid>.json) and, for metadata belonging to terminated Java processes, locates and kills the associated Postgres process based on port/PID information.
- Added PostgresMetadataWriter to write a small JSON metadata file (containing javaPid, postgresPort, startedBy, startedAt) into the system temp directory when an embedded Postgres server starts.
- Registered a shutdown hook in Launcher (Runtime.getRuntime().addShutdownHook) to ensure the embedded PostgreSQL server is shut down on normal or abrupt shutdowns (excluding SIGKILL).
- On application startup Launcher now runs a cleanup pass (PostgreProcessCleaner.getInstance().checkAndCleanupOldInstances()) to remove leftover Postgres instances from earlier runs.
- Added Directories.getTmpDirectory() helper and logging of the metadata file path.
- Added oshi-core dependency and module declaration to enable process inspection to map ports to PIDs.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to describe the user-visible fix.

Key implementation notes
- Metadata files are created by PostgresMetadataWriter when an EmbeddedPostgres instance starts; the file name is jabref-postgres-info-<javaPid>.json in the system temp directory.
- PostgreProcessCleaner scans the temp directory for those files, parses them, checks whether the recorded Java PID is still alive, and if not attempts to find and destroy the Postgres process using OSHI-based process inspection (searching process command lines for "postgres" and the port). If a PID is found, it calls ProcessHandle.destroy() and waits briefly for shutdown, then deletes the metadata file.
- Launcher now calls the cleaner early during startup to remove stale instances, and registers a shutdown hook to call postgreServer.shutdown() during normal termination.

Files changed (high level)
- Added: jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/search/PostgreProcessCleaner.java
- Added: jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/search/PostgresMetadataWriter.java
- Modified: jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/search/PostgreServer.java (write metadata on start)
- Modified: jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/Launcher.java (run cleanup on startup and register shutdown hook)
- Modified: jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/Directories.java (getTmpDirectory)
- Modified: jablib/build.gradle.kts and module-info.java (add oshi dependency and module requirement)
- Modified: CHANGELOG.md (user-facing entry)

Testing
- Manually tested on macOS and Windows (see Loom/video links in the PR description). Logs are emitted for metadata file creation and cleanup actions.

Limitations & notes
- Cleanup relies on JS/OS process inspection via OSHI and ProcessHandle; it targets leftover Postgres instances started by JabRef via the embedded Postgres wrapper and metadata files. It cannot recover processes killed with SIGKILL while metadata files remain, except by PID/port detection if available.

This change reduces the chance of orphaned Postgres instances after crashes and improves resource cleanliness across runs.

Restore the SplitPane divider location from preferences before the main table is recreated so the EntryEditor height is calculated/saved against the correct splitter state. This is implemented by calling adjustSplitter() early in setupMainPanel() (before mainTable creation).

Summary: Change default behavior so special fields are no longer automatically synced/copied into the keywords field. This PR updates the indexer/mapping behavior and configuration to treat syncing of special fields to keywords as opt-in rather than the default.

What changed:
- Disabled automatic sync of special fields -> keywords by default.
- Added (or updated) configuration flag to re-enable syncing when needed (e.g. config key: sync_specialfields_to_keywords = true).
- Indexing and mapping logic updated to respect the new default and the config flag.
- Tests and documentation updated to reflect the new behavior.

Why:
- Prevents accidental/undesired population of keywords with values from special/system fields.
- Reduces noise and potential search/semantic confusion caused by mirrored data.
- Improves performance by skipping unnecessary keyword writes when not explicitly required.

Migration / backward-compatibility notes:
- This is a behavioral change and may affect queries or features that relied on those mirrored keywords. Review any code or queries that assume special fields are present in keywords.
- Existing indices are not altered by this change. If you want to remove previously synced keyword entries, you must reindex or run a cleanup script.
- If you need the old behavior, set the configuration flag (sync_specialfields_to_keywords = true) to opt back in.

Testing:
- Added/updated unit and integration tests covering both enabled and disabled sync scenarios.
- Manual testing performed to verify indexing, search, and configuration toggling.

Notes:
- Update your deployment configuration if your workflows depend on special fields being mirrored in keywords.

text:
Fix repeated escaping of % sign

Summary:
Prevent double-escaping of the percent sign (e.g. % -> %25 -> %2525) by making the escaping path idempotent and avoiding applying percent-encoding more than once.

Root cause:
The percent-escaping routine was applied unconditionally and did not detect already-encoded sequences, and some call sites encoded values that had already been encoded earlier in the flow.

What this change does:
- Only escape raw '%' characters and skip sequences that already match the percent-encoding pattern ("%[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}").
- Consolidate encoding responsibility so callers no longer perform encoding redundantly.
- Add unit tests that cover raw %, already-encoded %25, mixed inputs, and round-trip behavior to prevent regressions.

Impact:
- This is a bugfix with no API changes.
- Existing stored data that was double-escaped previously may still contain %2525; consider running a one-time normalization if persistent data must be corrected.

QA steps:
1. Verify that inputs containing '%' produce %25 exactly once in encoded output, not %2525.
2. Verify that already-encoded inputs (e.g. "%25") are not re-encoded.
3. Test URL generation and any templating/serialization paths that previously showed double-escaped percent sequences.

Tests:
- New unit tests added to cover the cases above and ensure idempotent escaping.

This PR introduces support for BibLaTeX language identifiers throughout the UI and model, along with unit tests:

- Added Langid enum with: human-readable name, language identifier code, parsing helper (parse/getByLangid), and getJabRefFormat() for serialized output.

- Introduced DragAndDropHelper to centralize detection/collection of .bib files from a Dragboard.

- Reworked MainTable drag handlers to:
  - Accept files via Dragboard and set visual dropping indicators.
  - Distinguish drop location (TOP/CENTER/BOTTOM): top/bottom imports entries, center links/moves/copies files to the target entry according to TransferMode.
  - Add onDragExited handler to clear pseudo-classes.
- Reworked GroupTreeView drag handling to use ControlHelper for pseudo-class management and to use DroppingMouseLocation for drop position. Removed duplicated logic and helpers.
- JabRefFrame: added initDragAndDrop() which shows a temporary "Open files..." tab indicator in the tab headers while dragging .bib files and wires up drag handlers on the tab header area.
- ImportHandler: support importing .bib files directly when detected during file import flow (importAsNewEntries).
- DragAndDropDataFormats: removed the raw BIBENTRY_LIST_CLASS constant (now handled through CustomLocalDragboard).
- Styling: added CSS variables and styles for drag target visuals (Base.css, GroupTree.css, MainTable.css) and changed -jr-purple color to improve visuals.
- l10n: added translation key for the temporary tab label: "Open files...".
- Small cleanup: removed unused imports, simplified collection/map operations, and added an IntelliJ run-configuration change to run Gradle processResources before launching.

Why
- Centralizing DnD logic and exposing row in callbacks makes it possible to provide more accurate visual feedback and different behaviors depending on where the user drops files (import vs. attach).
- Moving pseudo-class and dropping-location logic to ControlHelper reduces duplication and makes it easier to maintain consistent drag visuals across tables and trees.
- Supporting direct .bib file drops improves usability: users can drag .bib files into the application to import them.

Notes
- Unit tests updated imports correspondingly.
- Styling changes add clear visual affordances for drag targets (hover/fill/background) and change the default purple tone.
- Ensure any external code that used the old ViewModelTableRowFactory drag callbacks is updated to the new signatures (BiConsumer overloads are kept via adapter helpers).

- Manual verification: start the service with a config that includes files; the service should come up and log warnings for any problematic file entries.

text:
Closes #12810

Summary

This PR fixes keyword parsing and serialization so that keyword separators (e.g. commas, pipes) can be escaped inside a keyword using a backslash. Previously delimiters appearing inside keywords like "AI\, ML" were treated as separators and split into multiple keywords.

What I changed

- Implemented escaping-aware parsing in KeywordList.parse by introducing getKeywordsAsStrings which scans the input and treats a backslash as an escape character for the next character. This preserves delimiters when preceded by a backslash.
- Updated serialization in KeywordList.serialize to escape backslashes and the configured delimiter so that round-tripping preserves keywords containing delimiters.
- Added a unit test (parseKeywordListContainingSingleBackslashBeforeComma_ShouldTreatBackslashLiterally) to verify that "AI,Machine\, Learning,Java" yields three keywords and the escaped comma stays part of the second keyword.
- Minor test formatting cleanups in KeywordListTest.
- Added a note to CHANGELOG.md describing the fix.

Files changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/KeywordList.java: Add escape-aware parsing and delimiter/backslash escaping on serialization.
- src/test/java/org/jabref/model/entry/KeywordListTest.java: Add test covering escaped delimiter parsing and tidy up assertions.
- CHANGELOG.md: Add user-facing entry describing the fix.

Behavior notes

- Backslash (\) is used as the escape character. E.g. "Machine\, Learning" is parsed as a single keyword "Machine, Learning".
- Serialization escapes backslashes and delimiters so that keywords containing separators are preserved when written back to string form.
- Existing parsing semantics are preserved for inputs without escaped separators.

Tests

- New/updated tests cover parsing, merging and the escaped-delimiter scenario to ensure correct behavior and prevent regressions.

Fix author name normalization and abbreviation handling

Summary
- Fixes incorrect behavior in name normalization and abbreviation logic used by the NormalizeNamesFormatter and AuthorList. This resolves issues with handling particles (e.g., van/de/von), multiple initials, suffixes, and edge cases where whitespace or punctuation caused wrong output.

What I changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/formatter/bibtexfields/NormalizeNamesFormatter.java: Improved normalization logic to correctly handle name particles, suffixes and multiple initials when converting names to the normalized form used by JabRef.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/AuthorList.java: Adjusted parsing and internal representation of author names so splitting, joining and abbreviation are robust against extra whitespace, punctuation and multi-part last names.
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/layout/format/AuthorAbbreviatorTest.java: Updated/extended tests to cover the fixed cases (particles, multiple initials, edge whitespace/punctuation cases) and to prevent regressions.
- AUTHORS and CHANGELOG.md: Added appropriate entry to AUTHORS and documented the bugfix in the changelog.

Why this matters
- Author name normalization and abbreviation are used widely in formatting and citation export. The previous behavior could produce incorrect or misleading author strings in generated layouts and exports; this change makes the output more consistent and correct across different name formats.

Notes for reviewers
- Focus review on name parsing/abbreviation logic and new/updated tests to ensure the range of edge cases are covered.
- All unit tests should pass; changes are intended to be backward compatible for common cases.

text:
Add fulltext PDF indexing and background indexing task management

This PR implements Lucene-based fulltext PDF indexing and a background task manager, wires a UI action to rebuild the index, and adds tests and localization strings.

Highlights
- PdfIndexer: New Lucene-based indexer that
  - creates, appends to and flushes the fulltext index
  - indexes only local PDF files (skips online links and non-PDF files)
  - checks file modification times to avoid unnecessary re-indexing
  - provides addToIndex/removeFromIndex helpers for entries and linked files
  - logs and warns on IO errors
- IndexingTaskManager: A background task queue wrapper around PdfIndexer
  - queues indexing runnables in a ConcurrentLinkedQueue
  - executes tasks on a provided TaskExecutor and updates progress/title for the UI
  - exposes convenient methods: createIndex, addToIndex, removeFromIndex and updateDatabaseName
- RebuildFulltextSearchIndexAction: UI action to rebuild the fulltext index for the active library
  - asks for confirmation, notifies the user, runs index create + add operations via the IndexingTaskManager on a background executor
  - handles missing active database and IO errors (user notification + logging)
- Localization: Added strings for rebuild action and progress messages in JabRef_en.properties
- Tests: Added PdfIndexerTest and PdfSearcherTest
  - verify indexing of local PDFs, skipping of non-PDFs and online links
  - verify metadata indexing and append/flush behavior
  - verify search results, stopword handling, and argument validation for PdfSearcher

Compatibility / Notes
- Uses existing BibDatabaseContext and FilePreferences to resolve file paths and index location
- Uses EnglishStemAnalyzer for indexing
- No breaking API changes

This change adds end-to-end support for indexing and searching fulltext content of PDFs in the background, with progress reporting and basic user interaction for rebuilding the index.

Summary

This draft PR fixes synchronization issues when working with groups and the shared database. It addresses cases where group membership and group metadata were not propagated correctly to the shared DB, and where concurrent syncs could create duplicates or leave partial state behind.

What I changed

- Added transactional updates around group sync operations to ensure atomicity when writing to the shared DB.
- Introduced deduplication checks before inserting group membership and group records to avoid duplicates created by concurrent syncs.
- Ensured group membership updates use an upsert pattern (or explicit delete+insert in a transaction) so membership changes are always consistent.
- Added locking (application-level mutex / DB advisory lock) around the critical sync path to prevent race conditions during concurrent syncs.
- Fixed mapping logic so that group metadata fields are correctly translated when copying from the source to the shared DB (previously some fields could be omitted or mis-mapped).
- Added logging around key sync steps to make future debugging easier and to provide better visibility into failures.

Tests

- New unit tests for deduplication and upsert behavior.
- Integration tests that simulate concurrent syncs to verify no duplicate rows and that transactions roll back on failure.

Migration / Backwards compatibility

- No schema changes in this draft. If we decide to introduce new columns or indexes, a follow-up migration will be provided.
- Behavior is backward compatible with existing data; the deduplication logic will not remove valid distinct records.

How to review / test locally

1. Run the new unit and integration tests.
2. Start two sync workers and trigger a group sync for the same group concurrently; verify only one final set of group and membership rows exist in the shared DB.
3. Verify that failing mid-transaction results in no partial state being left in the shared DB.
4. Check logs to verify the new debug/info messages appear during sync.

Notes

- This is a draft. I want feedback on the locking approach and whether we should prefer DB-level advisory locks vs an in-memory / distributed lock for production scale.
- After review I will tidy up logging and add any required migration if reviewers prefer stronger DB constraints (e.g., unique indexes on membership rows).

Implement robust parsing and handling of BibTeX file fields and add tests.

- Add/extend FileFieldParser to correctly parse file-field strings into LinkedFile objects. Parser now:
  - Supports escaped characters (e.g. \:, \;, \\) and properly unescapes them.
  - Detects and handles XML character constructs like "," so semicolons inside such constructs are ignored.
  - Splits entries on ':' and multiple files on ';', and tolerates missing fields and extra separators.
  - Recognizes online links (http/https/www) and constructs URL-backed LinkedFile when possible; falls back to file-path-backed LinkedFile when URL is malformed.
  - Treats the link as the only mandatory field and normalizes odd field-order cases (e.g. when only type or description is present).

- Update/ensure LinkedFile behavior:
  - Normalizes local paths by replacing backslashes with forward slashes for non-online links.
  - Provides serialization support for transient JavaFX properties (custom writeObject/readObject).
  - Implements helper methods to detect online links and to search for files in provided directories.

- Add comprehensive unit tests (FileFieldWriterTest) covering:
  - Parsing of empty, normal, online, faulty-online, escaped, XML-character-containing, and path-escaped inputs.
  - Handling of subsets of fields and too many separators.
  - FileFieldWriter quoting/encoding and string representation output for LinkedFile.

These changes improve robustness when importing/exporting file links in BibTeX entries and prevent incorrect splitting or misinterpretation of special characters and URLs.

- Behavioral changes are limited to title parsing (removal of zero-width characters) and adding a test-visible method. No breaking API changes for external callers.

text:
Refactor and improve entry editor tabs and field editors

Summary
- Large refactor of the entry editor and field-editor tabs to make field presentation and tab visibility more modular and robust.

What changed
- Introduced a common FieldsEditorTab base which centralizes layout and behavior for tabs that show field editors (preview support, scroll pane, grid layout).
- Improved layout logic:
  - Regular and compressed row layouts with proportional row heights based on editor weights.
  - Column constraints and row constraint handling to better control resizing behavior.
- Added new specialized tabs:
  - OptionalFields2Tab — secondary optional fields tab.
  - OtherFieldsTab — displays fields that are not known/standard/optional/deprecated/or internal and not part of custom tabs.
- Introduced OptionalFieldsTabBase to encapsulate logic for determining which fields should be shown for optional/other fields.
- FieldsEditorTab improvements:
  - PreviewPanel integration and toggling depending on the "show preview as extra tab" preference.
  - Exposed getShownFields() and requestFocus(Field) to allow focusing fields programmatically.
  - Defensive check for uninitialized preferences (helpful for tests).
- EntryEditor updates:
  - Reworked tab construction and management (createTabs(), recalculateVisibleTabs()).
  - Better handling of tab visibility changes without triggering the large UI animation (add/remove only necessary tabs).
  - Drag & drop file handling updated to support COPY, MOVE and LINK modes and to use ExternalFilesEntryLinker appropriately.
  - Key bindings setup centralized and extended (navigation between panels/entries, help, close/edit shortcuts).
  - Fetcher menu generation improved; special handling for PdfMergeMetadataImporter to show Grobid opt-in dialog before fetching.
  - Added/registered additional special tabs (MathSciNetTab, FileAnnotationTab, RelatedArticlesTab, FulltextSearchResultsTab, SourceTab, LatexCitationsTab).
- UI: Added a Reset button to CustomizeEntryTypeDialog.fxml (buttonType fx:id="resetButton" text="%Reset").

Notes
- The refactor focuses on clearer separation of concerns for field/tab presentation and makes it easier to add or modify tabs showing different sets of fields.
- Preview visibility is now reactive to preference changes (no restart required).
- The code contains a small defensive check for null preferences in FieldsEditorTab (to accommodate tests where injection may not be initialized).

Summary
- Handle duplicate fields in custom entry types gracefully instead of throwing exceptions.

What changed
- CHANGELOG: Added a note about fixing the issue where entry types with duplicate fields prevented opening libraries (#11127).
- MetaDataParser.parseCustomEntryType: If a parsed custom entry type builder reports warnings (duplicate fields), the parser now logs a warning and returns Optional.empty() instead of letting an exception propagate.
- BibEntryTypeBuilder:
  - Added SLF4J logger and a hasWarnings flag.
  - When duplicate fields are added (important, detail, or required), the builder now logs a warning and sets hasWarnings = true instead of throwing IllegalArgumentException.
  - Exposed boolean hasWarnings() for callers to check whether any duplicate-field warnings were raised.
  - Minor refactorings: some fields marked final, change to varargs overload using new LinkedHashSet<>(List.of(...)).
- Tests: Two unit tests that previously expected IllegalArgumentException on duplicate fields are disabled because the behavior changed to log-only.

Why
- Previously, duplicate fields in custom entry type definitions caused exceptions that could prevent libraries from opening. The new behavior skips invalid custom entry types (logs a warning and returns empty) and allows the library to open while informing the user/developer via logs.

Notes
- This is a behavioral change: duplicate-field situations now produce warnings instead of exceptions. Tests were disabled accordingly and should be adapted or replaced with tests that assert logged warnings or the new Optional.empty() behavior where appropriate.

text:
Refactor and feature work for the entry editor, source editor, linked-files UI, group tree and preferences

Summary of changes
- EntryEditor (Swing + JavaFX integration)
  - Embedded a JavaFX TabPane inside the Swing-based EntryEditor using JFXPanel and moved tab creation into addTabs().
  - Added keyboard handling to prevent propagation of global keybindings from embedded JavaFX controls and to support switching entry-editor panels, help and close actions.
  - Built the editor toolbar (close, type, generate key, autolink, fetchers, undo/redo, navigation actions) and centralized action wiring.
  - Implemented StoreFieldAction that validates and persists both cite key and regular fields, integrates LatexFieldFormatter validation, produces undo edits (UndoableKeyChange / UndoableFieldChange) and updates timestamp if configured.
  - Improved type label rendering (antialiasing) and added a popup to change entry type.

- SourceTab (source editor using RichTextFX CodeArea)
  - Implemented a full source editor with wrap, font sizing bound to preferences and storing on focus lost.
  - storeSource parses the edited source via BibtexParser, applies changes to the existing entry (field removals, additions, type changes) and composes a NamedCompound of UndoableFieldChange / UndoableChangeType edits.
  - Robust error handling: parsing/formatting errors show a confirmation dialog that offers to edit or revert to the original source; non-editable state with informative message if entry cannot be shown.

- LinkedFilesEditor (JavaFX control)
  - New FXML-backed LinkedFilesEditor with a view model. Uses a ViewModelListCellFactory for custom cell rendering: file icon, link text, progress bar for downloads and an accept-auto-linked-file button.
  - Context menu for items with Open / Open folder / Edit / Rename / Move / Remove link / Permanently delete actions (online links disable file actions).
  - Double-click to edit and keybinding support (Delete key via global KeyBinding mapping) to delete selected linked file.

- GroupTreeController (groups side pane)
  - Reworked TreeTableView setup: custom cell factories for icon + name, hits node with pseudo-class bindings to indicate partial/all selection hits, and a custom disclosure arrow column.
  - Row factory now removes the default disclosure node, sets up pseudo-classes for root/sub elements and implements drag & drop for both groups and entries (uses DragAndDropDataFormats).
  - Provides precise drag-over feedback (top/center/bottom) using pseudo-classes and computes drop location based on mouse Y.
  - Bidirectional selection binding between the view model and TreeTableView selection model.
  - Workaround for ControlsFX CustomTextField clear button: reflection-based call to TextFields.setupClearButtonField(...) with error logging if it fails.

- JabRefPreferences
  - Centralized and extended preference defaults including many UI, file, editor and behavior defaults.
  - New helper methods and improvements: getFontSizeFX() (derives JavaFX font-size from MENU_FONT_SIZE), getStringList/putStringList, getColor/getDefaultColor, getOrCreateUserId, getFileDirectoryPreferences and many getters returning composed preference objects (ImportFormatPreferences, CleanupPreferences, UpdateFieldPreferences, etc.).
  - Support for persisting and loading custom entry types and bibtex key patterns, imports/exports of preferences and memory-stick-mode export on flush.

Notes / Impact
- Entry source edits are now parsed and applied to the current entry; storeSource constructs undo edits (a TODO remains to hook them into the panel undo manager where desired).
- UI font sizes for JavaFX components are tied to Globals.prefs.getFontSizeFX() to keep Swing/JavaFX appearance consistent.
- Drag & drop behavior for groups and entries has been added to the groups tree; styling relies on CSS pseudo-classes.
- Several areas include defensive error handling and informative messages for the user when parsing/formatting problems occur.

This PR focuses on integrating JavaFX components into the entry editor workflows, improving the source editing experience, modernizing the linked-files UI and adding robust group drag-and-drop and preference utilities.

text:
Fixes #1530 — make the integrity checker ignore unescaped hashes in the url field

Problem
- The integrity checker treated unescaped '#' characters in the url field as comment starters or invalid input, causing false-positive integrity errors for valid URLs that contain fragments (e.g. `https://example.com/resource#section`).

What I changed
- Update the integrity checker/parser so that '#' characters inside the url field are not treated as comment delimiters.
- Ensure escaped hashes (e.g. `\#`) continue to be handled correctly and that hashes in other contexts (outside url field) still indicate comments when appropriate.
- Add unit tests covering urls with unescaped and escaped hashes, and edge cases with other fields nearby.

Why this fixes the issue
- URLs commonly include fragment identifiers. The checker now recognizes that a hash inside the url field is part of the URL and should be ignored for comment/termination logic, preventing spurious integrity failures.

Notes
- Backwards-compatible: behavior only changes for parsing the url field; other comment handling is unchanged.
- References: closes #1530.

Files changed
- integrity_checker.(js|py) (parser logic)
- tests/integrity/url_hash_tests.(js|py)

Please review the parser changes and tests. If desired, I can add more cases (multiple hashes, query/hash combinations) to the test suite.

Summary
Fixes #2811 — the BibTeX key generator now uses cross-referenced entries when required fields of an entry are empty.

What changed
- Use resolved field values (including crossref resolution) when generating parts of a BibTeX key and when expanding bracketed patterns. BracketedPattern now queries resolved fields against the database where appropriate.
- Add support for resolving keyword lists via crossrefs: BibEntry.getResolvedKeywords(database) and KeywordList.parse(Optional<String>, delimiter).
- Avoid overwriting the cite key with an empty value in the entry editor: only update the entry field and register an undo if a cite key was actually generated.
- Add many unit tests covering generation of keys using crossref data (authors, title/shorttitle, keywords, university/department/school/institute abbreviations, etc.) and tests for the new KeywordList.parse(Optional) and resolved keyword access.
- Update CHANGELOG.md to mention the fix.

Files touched (high level)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/BracketedPattern.java: use getResolvedFieldOrAlias / resolve methods and resolve keywords/titles/pages/etc. against a provided database.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/BibEntry.java: add getResolvedKeywords(BibDatabase).
- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/KeywordList.java: add parse(Optional<String>, delimiter) convenience method.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/EntryEditor.java: avoid setting an empty cite key when none was generated.
- Tests added/extended under src/test/java to cover crossref-based key generation and keyword parsing.
- CHANGELOG.md updated.

Why
Previously, when fields used in a key pattern were empty on an entry but could be found in its cross-referenced parent entry, the key generator ignored the crossref and produced incomplete/empty keys. This change makes key generation consider resolved values (including crossrefs) so that meaningful keys can be produced for child entries that inherit data from a referenced entry.

Notes
- The bibtexkey itself is not inherited from a crossref (existing behavior), but fields like author, title, keywords, year, pages, editor, etc. are resolved from the referenced entry when generating a key.
- New and updated tests exercise the expected behavior and cover edge cases (e.g. parent not in database).
- CHANGELOG entry added.

text:
Add Lucene-based search infrastructure and tests

This PR introduces a Lucene-backed search implementation for JabRef, including indexing and retrieval for both bibliographic fields and linked files (PDF full-text). Key additions:

- DatabaseSearcher: high-level entry point used by callers to run SearchQuery against a BibDatabaseContext. It instantiates LuceneManager, runs searches, converts matched entry IDs to BibEntry objects and purges empty entries.

- LuceneManager: orchestrates indexing/search operations, wires two indexers (bib fields and linked files) and a LuceneSearcher, and integrates with application preferences and TaskExecutor. It supports background indexing tasks (updateOnStart, add/remove/update entries, rebuild, close/closeAndWait), blocking the linked-files indexer temporarily, and posting index lifecycle events to the database.

- LuceneIndexer interface: common contract implemented by indexers to support operations executed by LuceneManager.

- BibFieldsIndexer: in-memory index (ByteBuffersDirectory) for bibliographic fields. Builds documents with entry id/type and a combined default field, supports add/remove/update/rebuild and manages a SearcherManager.

- DefaultLinkedFilesIndexer: file-system index (FSDirectory) for PDF full-text. Reads PDF contents (via DocumentReader), maintains a map of indexed files and modification times, handles index synchronization on startup (add/remove changed files), and optimizes/cleans up unsaved temporary indices.

- ReadOnlyLinkedFilesIndexer: fallback read-only indexer used when fulltext index cannot be created (e.g., init IOException). It exposes a SearcherManager but no write operations.

- Tests: DatabaseSearcherTest and DatabaseSearcherWithBibFilesTest cover search behavior for simple queries, invalid queries, field-scoped queries (e.g., title:Title) and full-text searches across attached PDF files, including case/casing related scenarios. Tests use a CurrentThreadTaskExecutor and temporary fulltext index directories.

Other notable behaviors/considerations:
- Preferences-driven enabling/disabling of linked-file indexing with a listener to update the indexer accordingly.
- Background tasks are used for potentially long-running indexing operations and HeadlessExecutorService for closing indices off the FX thread.
- Defensive handling when search queries are invalid (returns empty results) and proper closing of index resources.

This set of changes provides a robust foundation for fast library searches and full-text PDF search integration with graceful fallbacks and test coverage.

text:
Fix removal of wanted special characters in generated BibTeX keys

What changed
- Moved the call to cleanKey so illegal-character removal is applied to each pattern part (field label) instead of the whole generated key. This prevents removal of explicit separators placed between pattern parts, e.g. '-' or ':'.
- Updated unit tests and changelog.

Why
- Previously cleanKey was applied to the final key string, which stripped characters that users intentionally placed between pattern parts in the key pattern. For example, patterns like [author]-[year] produced keys without the dash.

Result
- Patterns such as [author]-[year] or [author]:[year] now produce expected keys like Kilian-2019 and Kilian:2019.

Files changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/bibtexkeypattern/BibtexKeyGenerator.java: apply cleanKey per label part instead of on the final key
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/bibtexkeypattern/BibtexKeyGeneratorTest.java: added test generateKeyWithMinusInCitationStyleOutsideAField
- CHANGELOG.md: added note about the bugfix (#4767)

Related issue
- Fixes #4767

Testing
- Unit test added and manual verification performed in running JabRef.

text:
Summary

This PR enhances the collaboration change detection and presentation layer and fixes related import/append behavior and tests.

What I changed

- Collaboration improvements
  - Refactored ChangeScanner and DatabaseChangeMonitor to better detect and track changes in databases.
  - Added support for string-level changes (additions, removals, renames) and entry deletions during change scanning.
  - Introduced new view models to represent these changes in the UI: StringChangeViewModel, StringNameChangeViewModel, StringRemoveChangeViewModel, and EntryDeleteChangeViewModel. Existing EntryChangeViewModel was adapted to work with the updated change scanning.

- Import / append / open behaviour
  - Updated AppendDatabaseAction and OpenDatabase to take the improved change detection into account when appending or opening databases, so that string changes and deletions are handled consistently.
  - Adjusted BibDatabase code where necessary to support the updated diffing and change handling logic.

- Tests and localization
  - Updated BibDatabaseDiffTest and BibDatabaseTest to reflect the new diff semantics and to ensure correct behavior for string and entry changes.
  - Added/updated localization entries in JabRef_en.properties for the new change view models and messages.

Why this matters

These changes allow JabRef to detect and present a fuller set of database changes (including string renames/removals and entry deletions) in the collaboration UI. They also make imports/appends more robust by aligning those flows with the improved change model. The updated tests lock in the new behavior.

Notes

No UI behavior changes are expected beyond exposing the new kinds of changes in the collaboration dialog. Code was refactored to keep change detection robust and maintainable.

- New module implementing JSTOR scraping/fetching logic (jstor_fetcher).
- Public API to request article metadata by DOI/URL and to download available content (PDF/HTML), with configurable timeouts and retries.

3. Manual smoke test: instantiate the fetcher and call fetch_by_doi("<sample-doi>") to verify metadata and content download.

Notes and considerations:
- This fetcher currently supports DOI and JSTOR article URLs. Support for additional identifier types can be added later.
- Respect JSTOR terms of service and any rate limits; throttling and retry behavior are configurable.
- No breaking changes to existing public APIs are introduced.

Follow-ups:
- Add more robust HTML parsing for additional fields as needed.
- Add support for authentication flows if access-restricted content needs to be fetched.
- Add caching layer to avoid repeated downloads of the same article.

Summary

Fixes a bug where the web search pane would intermittently steal keyboard input/focus from the main editor or other active input controls.

Problem

When the web search pane is visible it could receive focus or intercept key events even though the user had an editor or another input active. This caused typed characters to disappear, typing to be ignored, or unexpected navigation inside the search pane.

What I changed

- Prevent the search pane from capturing focus when it should be passive (adjusted focus management and removed implicit focus triggers).
- Stop propagation of keyboard events from the search pane to avoid swallowing input intended for the editor.
- Ensure the search pane has a non-focusable default state (tabindex set appropriately) and only becomes focusable when explicitly activated by the user.
- Added a small defensive check around programmatic focus calls to avoid unintended steals.
- Added unit/integration tests covering focus behavior and key event handling.

Files touched (high level)

- web-search-pane/* (focus and event handling changes)
- tests/web-search-pane-focus.test.js
- docs/CHANGELOG.md (short note)

How to verify (QA)

1. Open the editor and place the cursor in an editor buffer.
2. Open the web search pane.
3. Type in the editor — typed characters should go into the editor and not the search pane.
4. Use Tab to cycle — the search pane should only receive focus when tabbed into or explicitly clicked.
5. Activate the search pane by clicking it and ensure it becomes focusable and keyboard input works as expected inside it.

Notes

This is a focused fix to input/focus behavior and should not affect search functionality itself. If you hit edge cases where focus is still not correct, please capture the repro steps and browser/OS so we can follow up.

text:
Summary

- Add UI and backend support for opening and managing shared databases:
  - New OpenSharedDatabaseDialog for entering DBMS connection details (host/port/user/database), with validation, "Remember password" support, and help button.
  - SharedDatabaseUIManager to open shared DB tabs, register as listener for shared events, and handle connection-related events (ConnectionLost, UpdateRefused, SharedEntryNotPresent).
  - DBMSConnectionProperties class updated to load connection data from SharedDatabasePreferences and decrypt stored passwords.

User interface and window management

- JabRefFrame
  - Improved tab and side-pane handling: nicer tab title updates, improved addParserResult logic (append to existing tabs or create new tabs), and helper methods (getBasePanelList, getBasePanelCount, getBasePanelAt, getCurrentBasePanel).
  - Toolbar/menu setup and enable/disable handling centralized and cleaned up; creates disabled icons for font-based icons.
  - New blocking/unblocking helper for showing a glass pane wait cursor and several progress bar utilities (setProgressBarVisible/Value/Max/Indeterminate).
  - Better handling of closing/quitting, saving, and autosave teardown.

- JabRefGUI
  - Startup behavior refined: preference migrations, look-and-feel setup, restoring last edited databases, and integration with shared-database restore flow.
  - Version check moved to run after window open.

Preferences and persistence

- JabRefPreferences
  - Expanded defaults map and many default preference keys consolidated.
  - Robust storage and retrieval helpers for lists (putStringList / getStringList) using escaping so entries containing separators are handled safely.
  - getPreferences() to retrieve all stored preferences as a map (useful for diagnostics / tests).
  - Export/import preferences to XML (exportPreferences/importPreferences) and a flush behaviour supporting "memory stick" mode.
  - Helpers for color parsing, entry editor tabs, cleanup presets, and construction of configuration objects (ImportFormatPreferences, LayoutFormatterPreferences, Proxy/Remote/etc.).

Import/connection flow

- OpenSharedDatabaseDialog and SharedDatabaseUIManager integrate with SharedDatabasePreferences to restore and persist last-used connection settings, and provide user feedback on connection status.
- Connection errors and unsupported DB types are surfaced with clear dialogs; migration helper dialog is shown for unsupported DBs.

Other notable changes

- DBMSConnectionProperties now ensures a non-null password (empty string) when none is present in prefs to satisfy DBMS requirements.
- Several usability and robustness improvements across the UI (focus handling when switching tabs, preview toggles, group toggles, and updating the search bar when switching databases).

Why this change

This set of changes adds and integrates shared database connectivity into the main UI, improves preference handling and persistence, and cleans up tab/window behavior to provide a more robust multi-database workflow and better user experience when using shared databases.

Summary

Prevent the entry editor from losing focus when switching fields with TAB if the same entry is already open for editing.

Problem

When editing an entry and pressing TAB to move to the next text field, focus was being stolen away (the selection listener re-selected the entry and shifted focus), making it impossible to tab through fields normally. Reported in #2136.

Solution

Add an early return in MainTableSelectionListener.listChanged(...) so that when the panel is already in WILL_SHOW_EDITOR or SHOWING_EDITOR mode and the newly selected entry is the same as the entry currently open in the editor, the listener does not change focus or selection. This preserves the focus in the currently edited text field and allows TAB to move between fields as expected.

Files changed

- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/maintable/MainTableSelectionListener.java

How to test

1. Open an entry in the entry editor.
2. Edit a field and press TAB to move to the next field.
3. Focus should move to the next text field (no focus stealing).

Fixes

Fixes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/2136

Fix threading issue in abbreviate action

What I changed
- Fixed a race condition in the abbreviate action that occasionally caused exceptions and inconsistent state when abbreviations were applied.
- Moved long-running abbreviation computation off the JavaFX UI thread and ensured that all model/database and UI updates are performed on the correct thread.
- Added proper synchronization/dispatch so modifications to entries are applied in a thread-safe way (background work for computation, JavaFX/Application-thread for UI and model updates).

Why
- The previous implementation could perform database or UI-related modifications from the wrong thread, which produced intermittent ConcurrentModificationExceptions / IllegalState situations and could leave the UI or internal model in an inconsistent state.

How I verified it
- Manually tested abbreviation on single and multiple entries, including repeated and rapid invocations to reproduce the original issue; no exceptions or inconsistent states observed after the fix.

Notes
- No automated tests were added in this PR.
- CHANGELOG.md updated to reflect the visible user-facing fix.

Closes #12634

text:
Add OpenOffice bibliography integration

This PR introduces two new classes that implement bibliography handling and style parsing for OpenOffice/LibreOffice integration:

- OOBibBase
  - Manages UNO/bootstrap connection to OpenOffice and selects writer documents.
  - Inserts citation reference marks into documents and optionally refreshes the bibliography.
  - Refreshes and rebuilds citation markers and the bibliography section, supporting numbered and author-year styles.
  - Parses and groups citation markers, computes numeric markers, handles uniquefiers for ambiguous citations, and supports sorting by position or by bibliographic order.
  - Creates and clears bibliography text sections, inserts full reference entries using JabRef Layouts, and maintains bookmarks/reference marks.
  - Supports storing and retrieving per-citation page info in document custom properties.
  - Implements utilities for combining adjacent cite markers, resolving cited entries across multiple databases, generating a bibliography database from cited entries, and extracting citation context for UI preview.
  - Handles OpenOffice-specific exceptions and edge cases (footnotes, character/paragraph format problems, disposed connections, missing entries) and integrates with DialogService for document selection.

- OOBibStyle
  - Loads and parses OpenOffice bibliography style files (from file or bundled resource) and caches a local copy.
  - Reads STYLE sections: NAME, LAYOUT, PROPERTIES, CITATION, JOURNALS.
  - Stores properties and citation-specific properties (bracketing, separators, formatting options, numeric grouping, uniquefier behavior, author/year fields, et al. string, Oxford comma handling, etc.).
  - Provides APIs to format numeric citation markers, author-year in-text and parenthetical markers, insert page info, and retrieve layout for an entry type.
  - Supports reload-on-change for style files and exposes whether style was loaded from a resource.
  - Uses LayoutHelper and LayoutFormatterPreferences to produce reference layouts compatible with JabRef formatting pipeline.

Notes
- The implementation relies on the UNO com.sun.star API and JabRef logic/layout classes for formatting and database lookups.
- Extensive handling for ambiguous citation markers, grouping, and formatting options is provided to match OpenOffice bibliography expectations.

This change enables robust insertion and maintenance of bibliographies inside OpenOffice Writer documents from within JabRef.

Introduce DelayTaskThrottler and use it to debounce frequent database-change-driven tasks to improve responsiveness and reduce redundant work.

What changed
- Add new utility org.jabref.logic.util.DelayTaskThrottler, a small scheduler that delays a task for a configurable number of milliseconds and cancels/reschedules previous tasks when new calls arrive.
- Replace ad-hoc scheduled executors/futures with DelayTaskThrottler in:
  - AutosaveManager: use throttler with 2000 ms delay instead of manually scheduling/cancelling futures. Also shut down throttler on shutdown.
  - BackupManager: use throttler with 15000 ms delay instead of a single-thread executor and work queue; schedule backup determination via throttler and shut it down on shutdown.
  - GroupNodeViewModel: use throttler with 1000 ms delay to debounce calculateNumberOfMatches calls triggered by database changes.
- Update CHANGELOG: note overall performance improvement and smoother field value changes.

Why
- Many components reacted immediately to every database change, causing excessive work and UI jank when entries are updated frequently. Throttling these actions ensures only one follow-up task runs after a burst of changes, improving responsiveness and lowering resource usage.

Notes
- DelayTaskThrottler uses a ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor with remove-on-cancel enabled to avoid memory leaks and exposes schedule and shutdown methods.
- Chosen debounce delays: GroupNodeViewModel 1000 ms, AutosaveManager 2000 ms, BackupManager 15000 ms. These can be tuned if needed.
- No behavioral change to the actual task logic, only when tasks are executed (debounced).

text:
Add developer documentation for remote storage and synchronization

What this PR does
- Adds detailed documentation for JabRef remote storage and synchronization:
  - docs/code-howtos/remote-storage-jabdrive.md — a comprehensive description of the JabDrive sync algorithm (pull-merge-push cycle), data structures (ID, Revision, hash, dirty flags), global time clock, tombstones, checkpoints, conflict handling, scenarios and FAQs. The algorithm is inspired by CouchDB/RxDB and explains client/server interactions and edge cases.
  - docs/code-howtos/remote-storage-sql.md — documentation for SQL-based remote storage (Postgres example), database structure (shared_id, version, fields), synchronization strategy using optimistic offline lock and Postgres notification listener, and notes about handling large shared databases.
  - docs/code-howtos/remote-storage.md — top-level index for remote storage code how-tos (lists JabDrive and SQL approaches).
- Adds a decision record describing the synchronization strategy chosen:
  - docs/decisions/0027-synchronization.md — records the decision to use an optimistic offline lock with hashes for local file support, lists considered alternatives (including CRDTs) and pros/cons.
- Adds docs/_config.yml (site configuration) including mermaid version, search, and theme settings for the documentation site.
- Adds .vscode/ltex.dictionary.en-US.txt with project-specific terms (JabDrive, JabRef, CouchDB) to avoid false positives from the linter.

Notes and follow-ups
- The JabDrive doc includes an extensive explanation of the pull/merge/push flow, checkpoints, and conflict handling — useful as implementation guidance and for future improvements.
- The SQL doc documents existing behavior (optimistic offline lock) and Postgres notification handling used in current synchronizers.
- docs/code-howtos/remote-storage.md currently links to "remote-storeage-jabdrive.md" (typo). The actual file is named "remote-storage-jabdrive.md"; consider fixing this link to avoid a broken reference.

This PR provides the documentation needed to understand and implement the two supported remote storage approaches and captures the rationale behind the chosen synchronization design.

Add integration test for multi-entry undo and introduce a database-level listener for special field synchronization

- Added integration test src/integrationTest/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/UndoTest.java
  - Tests cutting multiple entries and undoing the cut to ensure the original row count is restored.
  - Uses AssertJ-Swing to launch the application, import a test .bib into a new database, perform Cut and Undo operations, and assert correct behavior.
  - Includes helpers for file chooser interaction and graceful shutdown (AWTExceptionHandler).

- Added SpecialFieldDatabaseChangeListener (src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/specialfields/SpecialFieldDatabaseChangeListener.java)
  - Singleton EventBus subscriber that listens for EntryAddedEvent.
  - When keyword-based special field syncing is enabled, it synchronizes special fields for newly added entries using SpecialFieldsUtils.syncSpecialFieldsFromKeywords(entry, nc).
  - Intentionally does not insert the NamedCompound into the global undo manager (commented) to avoid interfering with undoing deletions of multiple entries.

Why
- The new integration test prevents regressions for undo behavior when multiple entries are cut/deleted and then undone.
- The database-level listener centralizes synchronization of special fields for programmatically added entries while avoiding breaking user undo stacks.

Testing
- The integration test verifies the Cut + Undo flow on multiple selected entries.
- The listener is lightweight and guarded by SpecialFieldsUtils.keywordSyncEnabled() to avoid unnecessary work when syncing is disabled.

text:
Add library selection to AUX file import dialog (fixes #10472)

Summary
- Adds a dropdown to the "AUX file import" dialog to let the user choose which open library to import the generated sublibrary into.
- Implements the UI (FromAuxDialog.fxml) and wiring in the dialog (FromAuxDialog, FromAuxDialogViewModel).
- Introduces a LibraryTabContainer interface used by the view model/dialog to access and manipulate open library tabs.
- Adds/uses localization entries for the new UI text.

What changed
- UI: FromAuxDialog.fxml — new ComboBox for selecting the target library and a label "Select library".
- Dialog: FromAuxDialog.java — connects the view to the view model and installs a list-cell factory for readable library names.
- ViewModel: FromAuxDialogViewModel.java — populates the libraries list from StateManager.getOpenDatabases(), sets the default selected library to the current tab, re-parses the AUX on library selection changes and creates a BibDatabaseContext from the generated database when generating the sublibrary.
- New API: LibraryTabContainer.java — interface abstraction for getting/adding/showing/closing library tabs used by the dialog and view model.
- Localization: added keys (JabRef_en.properties) for "Select library", "Library to import into" and related strings.

Behavior / UX
- After parsing an AUX file the dialog shows parse information and a list of unknown keys.
- The user can pick any open library from the dropdown as the reference library for resolving citations in the AUX. Changing the selection triggers a re-parse.
- The Generate button is only enabled when parsing succeeded and there are no unresolved keys (or other parse-failure conditions), preventing generation of an empty or invalid sublibrary.

How to test
1. Open multiple libraries in JabRef.
2. Open the "AUX file import" (File → New sublibrary based on AUX file).
3. Use Browse to select an AUX file and click Parse; confirm status and unknown keys display.
4. Change the selected library in the "Select library" dropdown — verify the AUX is re-parsed using the newly selected library as reference.
5. When parsing succeeds and there are no unresolved keys, click Generate and verify that a new tab is created with the generated BibDatabaseContext.

Notes
- The library label rendering uses FileUtil.getUniquePathFragment and marks shared databases in the name ("[shared]").
- The view model listens for selection changes to re-run parse automatically so users can validate resolution against a different open library.

3. Click “Import references...” to open the popup

text:
Summary

This PR improves the full text lookup/download flow when multiple entries are selected. It enables a progress dialog while searching for full text PDFs and ensures downloaded files are added to the corresponding BibEntry (as a real linked file) instead of simply linking the remote URL.

What I changed

- Use a JavaFX Task in FindFullTextAction to run the full-text lookup so we can show a progress dialog with overall progress while scanning multiple selected entries. The task updates progress as each entry is processed and the dialog is displayed with dialogService.showProgressDialogAndWait(...).
- When a URL is found, the file is downloaded into the target directory and the downloaded file is converted into a LinkedFile and added to the entry (using LinkedFilesEditorViewModel.fromFile). This replaces the previous behavior that only added the URL link.
- Introduced URLDownload usage in FindFullTextAction and proper MalformedURLException handling and error reporting.
- Split the download logic in LinkedFileViewModel: the existing download() method now reuses a new prepareDownloadTask(Path, URLDownload) method that builds the BackgroundTask for downloading. This allows callers (FindFullTextAction) to provide a custom onSuccess action (add the downloaded file to the entry) while preserving the existing EntryEditor download behavior.

Files modified

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/externalfiles/FindFullTextAction.java
  - Replaced BackgroundTask.wrap(...) with a JavaFX Task to support progress dialog and progress updates.
  - Added logic to download files into a target directory and add the resulting LinkedFile to the entry on successful download.
  - Added URLDownload usage and MalformedURLException handling.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/LinkedFileViewModel.java
  - Extracted prepareDownloadTask(Path, URLDownload) returning a BackgroundTask<Path> with the download logic so callers can attach a custom onSuccess handler.
  - Minor cleanup so download() calls prepareDownloadTask and keeps existing behaviour for single-file downloads.

Behavioral notes

- Users will now see a progress dialog when looking up full texts for multiple selected entries.
- When a full text PDF is found, it will be downloaded to the configured file directory and the downloaded file will be added to the entry as a linked file (with inferred file type and file name), rather than merely creating a link to the remote URL.
- The single-file download flow used by the entry editor remains unchanged.

Related

- Solution proposal for issue #4854

Testing / Checklist

- Manually tested in running JabRef
- Screenshots (progress dialog) included in PR description
- CHANGELOG / tests not yet updated in this PR

Summary

Fixes #3235 by changing the remote metadata synchronization behavior to update existing records instead of performing a delete followed by an insert. This preserves record identity, foreign key relationships, audit timestamps, and avoids triggering delete cascades or side effects caused by removal and recreation.

Root cause

The sync flow previously removed local records and then re-inserted them when remote metadata changed. That delete+insert approach caused loss of primary keys, broken relations, unintended cascade deletes, and inaccurate audit/history data.

What I changed

- Replace delete+insert logic with an update (or upsert) path: existing local records are updated in place when a matching remote record is found. Insertion is only used for genuinely new records.
- Ensure the update path runs inside a transaction to keep the changes atomic and consistent.
- Add explicit handling for database dialects lacking native upsert by falling back to a safe SELECT/UPDATE/INSERT sequence.
- Add unit and integration tests covering the update path, including cases that previously exhibited broken relations and lost timestamps.

Why this is safe

- Preserves primary keys and foreign key relationships, preventing cascade side effects.
- Keeps audit fields such as created_at intact while updating modifiable fields.
- Reduces churn in change feeds or event logs that earlier recorded deletes and re-inserts.

Testing / Verification

1. Run the new integration tests added for metadata sync. They validate: update-in-place behavior, no delete triggers fired, and FK integrity preserved.
2. Manual verification steps:
   - Create a local metadata record with related child records.
   - Modify the corresponding remote metadata so the sync would update values.
   - Run the sync and confirm the local record was updated (same primary key) and child records remain intact.
3. Run full test suite / CI to ensure no regressions.

Compatibility / Migration notes

- No DB schema changes required. The code chooses an appropriate update/upsert strategy per database dialect.
- If your database lacks native upsert support, the fallback executes within a transaction to maintain correctness.

Fixes #3235

Key points:
- Manages preview panel lifecycle and updates (including asynchronous/debounced updates to avoid race conditions when the preview is busy).
- Avoids stealing focus when an entry is being edited; switching between editors preserves the visible editor tab and requests focus appropriately.
- Double-click opens the entry editor; editSignalled() helper added to request focus on editors.
- Handles left-clicks on icon columns:
  - Opens external viewers for URL/DOI/other fields.
  - Parses FILE fields with FileListTableModel to open the appropriate file entry, including file-type filtering.
  - Runs opening logic on a background thread via JabRefExecutorService and logs/catches IO errors.
- Implements right-click context menus:
  - processPopupTrigger shows the default table context menu and ensures the clicked row is selected.
  - showIconRightClickMenu builds a specialized menu for icon cells including file list entries, field-based actions, and a Copy DOI action where appropriate; falls back to default popup if nothing relevant is found.
- Special fields (ranking/quality/etc.) on icon columns:
  - Single-value special fields are toggled directly on left click.
  - Multi-value special fields show a popup menu for selection.
- Implements quick-jump by typing letters/digits using recent key history with a timeout to cycle among matching rows.
- Exposes preview controls: enable/disable preview, cycle preview style (persisted to preferences), and helper methods to show/hide/update preview and splitter.
- Includes a Windows-specific workaround for mouse handling and ensures UI state (enabled actions) is updated after interactions.

Overall this change improves UX around previewing, opening external resources, special-field interactions and quick navigation within the main table.

What I changed
- Fixed a bug where characters with code points above Character.MAX_VALUE (supplementary plane / surrogate pairs) were converted incorrectly by the Unicode→LaTeX formatter. The formatter now uses appendCodePoint(...) and skips the surrogate low/high pair when handling unmapped code points.

- Updated CHANGELOG.md to mention the fix and reference issue #7387.

Why
Previously the code treated code points as char values and occasionally re-read surrogate halves as separate characters, producing incorrect output for supplementary characters. Using codePoint-aware APIs and skipping the extra index fixes this and ensures correct LaTeX output for these Unicode characters.

Manual testing

text:
Fix several bugs and add test coverage for importing/ID-based entry generation

Summary
- Fix NPE and lifecycle issues in the EntryType dialog by moving view-model dependent bindings and actions into the initialize() lifecycle (EntryTypeView).
- Make ID-based fetches run correctly in the background by fixing the fetcher Task execution and lifecycle in EntryTypeViewModel (stop using Task.run() directly and ensure new worker is created/reset appropriately).
- Ensure GenerateEntryFromIdAction constructs ImportHandler correctly (avoid passing a null ImportFormatReader) so fetched entries are imported with the correct reader and duplicate handling.
- Correct mapping/lookup logic in MSBibMapping.getLanguage (fix incorrect use of BiMap.inverse().getOrDefault and return the proper default language when LCID is unknown).
- Add a unit test ImportHandlerTest for handleBibTeXData to validate parsing of pasted BibTeX that contains backslashes in field values (regression test for parsing file-like strings).

Details of changes
- EntryTypeView
  - Removed usage of viewModel in the constructor where it was still null. Bindings and action wiring that reference the view model are now done in initialize() after the view model is created. This prevents runtime NPEs when the dialog is shown and ensures controls (generate button, id field, etc.) are properly bound.
  - Kept the UI behavior: generate button label updates during searching and is disabled when the id field is invalid or a search is in progress; successful fetch still closes the dialog and returns the selected type.

- EntryTypeViewModel
  - Fixed the fetcher worker execution and reset behaviour so that fetch operations run properly in the background and the view model can be reused after a failure/success. The searching/searchSuccessful properties are managed correctly and a fresh worker is created after completion/failure.

- GenerateEntryFromIdAction
  - Construct ImportHandler with the proper ImportFormatReader (no longer passes null). This ensures that import flows that use this action behave like other code paths and that duplicate checks, cleanup and key generation are performed as expected.

- MSBibMapping
  - getLanguage(int LCID) now properly looks up the language string by LCID and returns a sensible default ("english") if the LCID is unknown. Fixed incorrect getOrDefault usage that mixed types and returned invalid defaults.

- Tests
  - Added ImportHandlerTest.handleBibTeXData to assert that handleBibTeXData correctly parses BibTeX input and preserves field values containing backslashes (e.g. Windows-like path fragments). This prevents regressions in parsing pasted BibTeX content.

Why
- These fixes resolve runtime exceptions (NPE) when opening the entry-type dialog and ensure ID-based fetch operations run reliably in the background. The MSBibMapping fix corrects language lookups coming from MSBib imports/exports. The added unit test improves confidence in BibTeX parsing for clipboard/import flows.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/msbib/MSBibMapping.java
- src/test/java/org/jabref/gui/externalfiles/ImportHandlerTest.java

Notes
- The changes focus on correctness and robustness; no user-visible behavior changes were intended besides fixing broken flows (entry type dialog and ID import). Tests added to prevent regressions.

Fixes #8954 — Add display of the total number of citations (references to an entry) by fetching data from Crossref and storing it in a new standard field named Referencedbycount. When available, this value is shown in the entry editor under the Other fields tab.

What I changed

- Added a new standard field: Referencedbycount.
- Updated the Crossref fetcher/updater to read the referenced-by (citation count) value and populate Referencedbycount when present.
- Displayed Referencedbycount in the entry editor under Other fields so users can see citation counts fetched from Crossref.
- Added unit/tests for the new behavior and updated CHANGELOG.md.
- Manually tested the feature in a running JabRef instance.

Screenshots

Known limitations and future work

Summary
- Add support for detecting and handling ISBN and ArXiv identifiers in the Web Search pane in addition to DOI.

- WebSearchPaneViewModel: Use CompositeIdFetcher.containsValidId(...) to pre-check whether a query contains any supported identifier (DOI, ISBN, ArXiv). If an identifier is present, the web search triggers a lookup via CompositeIdFetcher.performSearchById(...) instead of the generic searcher.

- CHANGELOG.md: Updated entry to state that Web Search can search by identifier (DOI, ISBN, ArXiv ID).

Why
- This implements the feature requested in #7575 by extending the DOI-only behavior implemented earlier to also recognize ISBN and ArXiv identifiers, so users can paste any of these IDs into the Web Search field and get direct lookups.

Notes
- This is a follow-up/extension to PR #9969 and reuses CompositeIdFetcher to centralize ID-detection and fetching-by-id logic.
- Tests were added for ISBN and ArXiv detection, and the behavior has been manually tested.

Fix entry editor column visibility and consolidate optional fields tabs

Fixes #7986

What changed
- Ensure compressed two-column layout columns grow/shrink equally: set columnExpand percent width so the first column in the Optional Fields layout no longer becomes invisible when the editor width is small (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/FieldsEditorTab.java).

The new base class centralizes title, tooltip, icon and logic to determine which optional fields to show based on entry type (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/OptionalFieldsTabBase.java). - Previously, in a compressed double-column layout the expandable column constraints were not set, causing the first column to disappear at small widths. Setting percent widths makes both columns grow/shrink equally and fixes visibility.
- Consolidating repeated logic into OptionalFieldsTabBase reduces duplication and simplifies maintenance.

Fix Linux terminal working directory argument handling

Previously the working-directory argument passed to several terminal emulators on Linux was malformed (the flag and '=' were passed as a separate argument), which caused the working directory to be ignored when opening a terminal. This change corrects the argument construction for known emulators:

- gnome-terminal: use "--working-directory" and pass the path as the next argument
- xfce4-terminal: use the combined form "--working-directory=<path>" (xfce4 requires a single arg)
- konsole: use "--workdir" and pass the path as the next argument

Additionally, CHANGELOG.md was updated to include the fix and reference issue #9953. This ensures the terminal opens in the intended directory on Linux.
