This PR fixes and hardens the journal abbreviation action and documents the change in the changelog.

What I changed:
- AbbreviateAction.java
  - Prevents NullPointerExceptions and other errors when there is no active database or no selection. The action now correctly checks preconditions and exits early if there is nothing to process.
  - Ensures the abbreviation work is executed off the JavaFX UI thread (runs in a background task) to avoid blocking the UI for large datasets, while UI updates are marshalled back to the FX thread.
  - Improves selection handling so the action consistently abbreviates either the selected entries or, when appropriate, the entire database according to the user's context.
  - Adds clearer logging and error handling for unexpected cases.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Adds an entry describing the fix and the improved behavior for the journal abbreviation action.

Why this change:
- Users could experience application freezes or crashes when running the abbreviation operation on large libraries or when no entries/database were available. This change makes the action more robust and improves the user experience by preventing UI blockage and handling edge cases gracefully.

Notes:
- No user-facing behavior changes besides improved stability and responsiveness. Existing workflows for abbreviating journals remain the same.
- If desired, follow-up improvements could add a progress indicator or allow cancelling long-running abbreviation operations.

Fixes incorrect author parsing when the string "and" appears — either as a conjunction separating multiple authors or as part of an author's name. The previous implementation split too aggressively on "and", producing broken author lists in many real-world cases.

- Updates the author-parsing logic to only treat "and" as a separator in appropriate contexts (e.g., as a standalone separator between names) and to preserve it when it is part of a single author's name.
- Improves whitespace and punctuation handling so mixed separators (commas, ampersands, and/AND) are handled consistently.
- Adds unit tests for several edge cases, including:
  - "John Doe and Jane Roe"
  - Names that include the substring "and" (e.g. "Anderson", "Smith and Wesson" as a single organization)
  - Multiple authors with/without commas
  - Mixed separators and extra whitespace

- This is still WIP: more international name edge cases should be added (prefixes/suffixes, non-English conjunctions), and we should consider performance on very large author strings.
- Feedback welcome on additional cases to cover and any preferred parsing heuristics.

Testing:
- Added and updated unit tests covering the cases above. All new tests pass locally.

Fixes #12215

Problem
- When multiple files were attached, the tooltip and context menu in the "Linked File" tab removed the first underscore (_) from file names. File paths were correct internally and files opened correctly, but the displayed text lost the underscore.
- Root cause: JavaFX treats a single underscore as a mnemonic (shortcut key) indicator when rendering text.

Solution
- Escape underscores for display: update ControlHelper.truncateString() to replace single underscores (_) with double underscores (__) before the text is shown in the UI. This preserves the visual underscore while keeping internal file paths untouched.

Testing
- Manually verified that tooltips and context menu entries now show underscores correctly.
- Screenshot of the fix has been attached to the PR.

Notes
- This change only affects UI display (escaping underscores); no change to file paths or file-opening behavior.

Summary

This PR refactors and fixes scripts/syncLang.py. It introduces a proper CLI (argparse), improves file/path handling (pathlib when available), clarifies and fixes duplicate/missing/obsolete key handling, and reorganizes many methods to make the script easier to use and maintain. This change addresses and fixes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/3573.

Key changes

- Add argparse-based CLI with subcommands: "markdown", "status", "update" and a new "print" command (print missing|obsolete|duplicates, optional -f/--file).
- Add PathFinder (uses pathlib when available) to locate repository base and resource paths (falls back gracefully if pathlib is not available).
- Replace ad-hoc argv parsing with structured subcommands and shared arguments (e.g. -e/--extended).
- Rename and reorganize methods for clarity:
  - Keys.duplicates -> Keys.find_duplicates
  - SyncLang.update -> SyncLang.update_properties
  - Several helper methods renamed: __read_file_as_lines -> __read_lines_from_file, __check_properties -> __compare_properties, etc.
- Add and centralize printing helpers (print_missing_keys, print_obsolete_keys, print_duplicate_keys and a generic __print_keys).
- Improve duplicate handling and formatting via Keys.format_key_and_value and more consistent use of Keys helper methods.
- Use set operations for missing-key detection for simplicity and performance.
- Allow status_create_markdown to accept a custom filename and improve markdown/IO handling.
- More consistent logging and an explicit extended_logging flag (set_extended_logging_enabled).
- Minor docstring and type clarifications and cleanup.

Usage examples

- Create markdown: python ./scripts/syncLang.py markdown
- Show status: python ./scripts/syncLang.py status [-e]
- Update localization files: python ./scripts/syncLang.py update [-e]
- Print missing/obsolete/duplicates: python ./scripts/syncLang.py print missing|obsolete|duplicates [-f file]

Compatibility notes

- argparse is imported (requires Python 2.7+ on the Python2 side). PathFinder uses pathlib and requires Python 3.4+; if pathlib is not available the script logs and falls back to previous behavior.

Fixes

- Resolves issue #3573 (see linked issue for details).

Summary:
Fixes an issue where highlighted text in the entry preview was rendered incorrectly or persisted across previews.

What was happening:
- Highlights could appear in the wrong positions or remain visible after updating the preview.
- The highlight state was not being reset properly and the DOM updates could apply highlight classes to stale nodes.

What I changed:
- Reset highlight state before re-rendering the entry preview to avoid leftovers from previous renders.
- Apply highlight classes only to freshly computed ranges and ensure mapping between model indices and DOM nodes is correct.
- Hardened rendering to avoid applying highlights to already-escaped HTML or inserting invalid markup.
- Added tests to cover highlight rendering and state reset on preview updates.

How to verify:
1. Open an entry preview and perform a search or trigger highlighting.
2. Change the entry content or re-open a different entry; highlights should update and not persist incorrectly.
3. Verify highlight positions match search terms and no extraneous markup appears in the DOM.

Notes:
- This is a behavioral fix; no UI changes other than correct highlight display.
- If you see any edge cases (complex nested tags or multi-node ranges), please report them with steps to reproduce.

Summary
Fixes an issue where saving files to network-mounted volumes (SMB/AFP/NFS) on macOS could fail or produce errors.

Root cause
The existing save implementation used an atomic-write strategy that created temporary files on a different volume or relied on a local-only write path. That caused cross-volume rename/replace (EXDEV) failures and coordination problems when the destination was a network drive.

What I changed
- Detect network-mounted volumes and avoid the failing atomic-write path for those destinations.
- Use a safer fallback: create the temporary file in the same directory as the target and/or use FileManager.replaceItemAt(_:withItemAt:) when appropriate so replaces succeed across network shares.
- Add NSFileCoordinator-based coordination around writes to network volumes to reduce conflicts with other clients.
- Centralized the logic in FileIO/SaveManager so the behavior is automatic and transparent to callers.

Behavioral notes
- For local volumes the original atomic save is preserved.
- For network volumes the implementation falls back to a same-directory temp + replace strategy (or coordinated non-atomic write) to avoid EXDEV errors. This keeps saves reliable on network shares, though in rare cases a non-atomic write may briefly show a partial file if another client reads the file during the write. The replace strategy minimizes that window.

Tests and verification
- Added unit tests that simulate cross-volume saves by using separate temp directories and verifying the save no longer errors on rename/replace.
- Manually verified saving to SMB shares on macOS in QA.

Compatibility
No public API changes. This is a bugfix; update is safe to ship.

Notes for reviewers
Focus on FileIO/SaveManager changes and the new volume detection logic. I included comments that explain why atomic writes fail on network drives and how the fallback avoids EXDEV/coordination issues.

Summary

This PR adds and documents Architectural Decision Records (ADRs) for the project and provides an ADR template and index entry for the docs site. It collects decisions made about formatting ADRs, translations, changelog style, BibTeX special fields, YAML parsing for study.yml, and chat message rendering.

What I changed

- docs/decisions/0000-use-markdown-architectural-decision-records.md
  - Choose MADR (Markdown ADRs) as the ADR format.
- docs/decisions/0006-only-translated-strings-in-language-file.md
  - Decide to keep only translated strings in language files (Crowdin-compatible).
- docs/decisions/0007-human-readable-changelog.md
  - Adopt Keep-a-changelog format with free-form bullet points.
- docs/decisions/0019-implement-special-fields-as-separate-fields.md
  - Implement special BibTeX fields as explicit separate fields (not keywords).
- docs/decisions/0020-use-Jackson-to-parse-study-yml.md
  - Choose Jackson for parsing study.yml into DTOs.
- docs/decisions/0036-use-textarea-for-chat-content.md
  - Use a TextArea (ExpandingTextArea from GemsFX) for chat message content.
- docs/decisions/adr-template.md
  - Provide ADR template (Jekyll front matter + MADR structure) for future ADRs.
- docs/decisions/index.md
  - Index entry for the Decision Records section and guidance to use the template.

Why

- Captures and makes explicit architectural and design decisions so contributors can find rationale and consequences easily.
- Standardizes ADR format (MADR) and provides a template to streamline future records.
- Decisions reflect trade-offs made for localization workflow (Crowdin usability), changelog readability, BibTeX data model, reliable YAML parsing into Java DTOs, and pragmatic UI choices prioritizing text selection/copying and implementation effort.

Implications and follow-ups

- Translation workflow: Keep-only-translated-strings requires tooling or processes for translators to detect untranslated strings; see ADR-0001 reference.
- Code/implementation tasks to follow-up: implement special fields as separate fields in the persistence/GUI layers and ensure any formatters/cleaners handle them; add Jackson dependency where study.yml parsing is required; ensure chat UI uses ExpandingTextArea as noted.
- Docs/site: Jekyll front matter is included for correct ordering/navigation under "Decision Records".

Testing & Validation

- These are documentation-only changes with no runtime behavior changes by themselves.
- Implementation decisions (e.g., Jackson dependency or special fields) should be validated via follow-up PRs with code, tests, and reviews.

Who should review

- Docs maintainers
- Localization/translation maintainers
- UI/UX owners (chat rendering)
- Core/format maintainers (BibTeX handling)

Notes

- ADRs reference rationale, considered alternatives, and consequences to aid future maintainers.
- If you want an ADR split, updated, or expanded, use the provided adr-template.md as basis.

Moved the cleanKey logic into the field-case handling so that desired special characters (such as '-' and ':') are no longer stripped from generated citation keys. This fixes issue #4767.

- Relocated cleanKey to the field-case context so it no longer clears wanted special characters used by key patterns.
- Added tests covering the new behavior (ensuring [author]-[year] and [author]:[year] produce Kilian-2019 and Kilian:2019 respectively).
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to describe the change.
- Manually tested the feature in a running JabRef instance.

Result
Key generation now preserves '-' and ':' when included in patterns, matching user expectations and the referenced issue.

Enhance KeywordsEditor: support drag-and-drop reordering, smarter sorting and improved paste/edit behavior

What I changed
- Implemented drag'n'drop support to reorder individual keyword tags (mouse-drag a tag to reposition it).
- Added automatic alphabetical sorting behavior: the editor detects if the tag list is already sorted and keeps it sorted when appropriate. A flag is used to preserve explicit user reordering.
- Improved paste handling: Ctrl/Cmd+V (Paste key binding) now parses clipboard contents using the configured keyword separator and inserts multiple keywords at once.
- Double-click on a tag opens it for editing (tag is removed and its text copied to the editor).
- Added a context menu on each tag with Copy, Cut and Delete actions. Copy/Cut copies the tag text to clipboard and shows a notification; Cut also removes the tag.
- Commit-on-separator: typing the configured keyword separator in the tag editor commits the current input as a tag.

Implementation notes
- The tag view factory now builds tag Labels with mouse and drag event handlers (startDrag, dragOver, dragDropped, dragDone) and visual feedback on drag enter/exit.
- Uses KeywordList parsing and the view model's string converter to create new Keyword items when pasting or typing.
- Uses Guava's Comparators.isInOrder to detect whether tags are alphabetically ordered.
- Clipboard and notifications are handled via ClipBoardManager and DialogService; UndoManager and preferences are passed into the view model as before.

User-visible effect
- Users can reorder keywords by dragging tags.
- Pasting a comma/semicolon/etc. separated list of keywords (depending on your configured separator) will add multiple tags.
- Tags are easier to edit and manage via double-click and context menu actions.

Improve GroupTreeView UI and drag-and-drop behavior

This change enhances the groups side panel with a number of UI and interaction improvements:

- Reworked tree table layout: separate columns for main content, hit counts, and custom expansion arrows (disclosure node removed and replaced by a dedicated expansion column).
- Hit count cell: formatted number display (k/m), tooltip with full count, and responsive font-size adjustments based on workspace font size to avoid layout issues for large counts.
- Search field: added a clear button decorator (using a reflective fallback for ControlsFX) and debounced filtering (400ms) to avoid running expensive searches for every keystroke.
- Drag & drop: improved handling for dragging groups and entries (start, over, drop, exit), including auto-expansion while hovering (with a delay) and visual dropping pseudo-classes. Drag-scrolling while dragging is implemented with a periodic timer and heuristics to compute scroll velocity.
- Selection & interaction fixes: multi-selection binding between view and view-model, prevention of right-click selection when entries are selected, and support for expanding parents when programmatically selecting a node.
- Context menu: rebuilt context menu items wired to view-model actions and keybindings; menu items are stripped of graphics for consistent styling.
- Misc: defensive reflection handling when decorating the search field (logs errors on failure), improved formatted number helper, and general code cleanup around drag/selection logic.

These changes improve usability, performance and visual consistency of the groups panel, especially for large group hierarchies and during drag-and-drop operations.

Summary

- Add a localization synchronization script and a consistency test to help keep translations aligned with code changes.
- Update CONTRIBUTING.md with guidance for localization and how to run the new tooling and tests.
- Improve the PR template to remind contributors about localization-related checks.

What I changed

- .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md: Added checklist items and guidance to ensure contributors verify localization/translation changes and run localization checks when relevant.
- CONTRIBUTING.md: Documented the localization workflow, how to run the syncLang.py script, and how to run the localization consistency test locally. Added instructions for translators and maintainers to help reduce mismatches between resource bundles and code.
- scripts/syncLang.py: New script to synchronize localization/resource bundle keys across language files and help identify missing or obsolete keys.
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/l10n/LocalizationConsistencyTest.java: Added/updated unit test that verifies consistency of localization keys between code and translation files, failing the build when inconsistencies are detected.

Why

Keeping localization strings consistent across languages is error-prone when adding, removing, or renaming keys. This change introduces tooling and documentation to automatically detect and surface these issues early (locally and in CI) so translators and developers can address them before they reach users.

How to use / Developer notes

- To check translations locally: run scripts/syncLang.py (see CONTRIBUTING.md for invocation details).
- Run the new LocalizationConsistencyTest as part of the test suite; CI will also execute it and fail when mismatches exist.
- When adding or removing UI strings, update translations and run the sync script / test to ensure everything is aligned.

Files changed

- .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md
- CONTRIBUTING.md
- scripts/syncLang.py
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/l10n/LocalizationConsistencyTest.java

- ColumnPreferences: added a private default constructor with hardcoded default column models, a static getDefault() factory, and setAll(ColumnPreferences) to copy values into an existing instance.
- MainTablePreferences: added a private default constructor, static getDefault(), and setAll(MainTablePreferences) to copy fields into an existing instance.

Added helper methods getMainTablePreferencesFromBackingStore(...) and getMainTableColumnPreferencesFromBackingStore(...) to load preferences while falling back to defaults when nothing is stored.

Benefits:
- Centralizes default configuration in code, avoiding scattered hardcoded strings.
- Ensures existing preference objects remain the same instance (preserving listeners/bindings) by copying data into them.
- Makes preference loading more robust: when stored column names are absent, defaults are used.

Add ScholarArchive fetcher and integrate it into search fetchers

This PR introduces a new web fetcher for scholar.archive.org and integrates it into the application search ecosystem. Main changes:

- Implement ScholarArchiveFetcher
  - New class org.jabref.logic.importer.fetcher.ScholarArchiveFetcher implementing PagedSearchBasedParserFetcher.
  - Builds API requests to https://scholar.archive.org/search with JSON response format and paging (from, size) and sets Accept: application/json.
  - Parses JSON results into BibEntry objects, mapping fields such as title, journal (container_name), doi, issue, language, publisher, year, volume, abstract, url, date, authors (contrib_names) and issns.
  - Chooses entry type (InCollection, Book, Article) based on release_type.
  - Throws ParseException on unexpected JSON format.

- Add ScholarArchiveQueryTransformer
  - New transformer to convert Lucene queries to Scholar Archive query syntax (handles author, title, journal, year and year ranges and logical operators).

- Register fetcher
  - Add ScholarArchiveFetcher to the search-based fetcher set in WebFetchers so it appears among available search sources.

- Tests and test updates
  - New unit test org.jabref.logic.importer.fetcher.ScholarArchiveFetcherTest to validate fetcher name and a sample performSearch result assertion.
  - Update org.jabref.gui.slr.ManageStudyDefinitionViewModelTest to include "ScholarArchive" in the expected catalog list and factor test setup into a helper method.

- Changelog
  - Document the addition of scholar.archive.org as a new fetcher in CHANGELOG.md.

Notes/Behavioral details:
- The fetcher uses ScholarArchiveQueryTransformer to translate search queries and supports paged searches.
- JSON parsing is defensive (uses optX methods) and will throw a ParseException if the expected structure changes.

Summary

Add a WebView pooling/preloading facility to reduce UI freezes when creating WebView instances and fix the perceived lag when selecting an entry after a fresh start (#8446).

What I changed

- Added org.jabref.logic.util.WebViewStore
  - Maintains a queue of preloaded JavaFX WebView instances.
  - Provides init() (and init(Configuration)) to preload instances on the JavaFX thread using Platform.runLater.
  - Provides get() to obtain a WebView from the store (falls back to creating a new WebView if none are available) and ensures more instances are scheduled when the pool drops below a minimum threshold.
  - Includes a Configuration record with default values (4 preloaded, 2 minimum).
  - get() throws IllegalStateException if the store was not initialized.

- Initialized the WebViewStore at application startup in JabRefGUI (WebViewStore.init()).

- Replaced direct new WebView() usages with WebViewStore.get() in:
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/MathSciNetTab.java
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preview/PreviewViewer.java

- Updated CHANGELOG.md to mention the fix for the startup-selection lag (issue #8446).

Other small change

- Minor whitespace cleanup in JabRefMain.

Why this change

Creating JavaFX WebView instances can be expensive and block the UI when done on demand. By preloading instances on the JavaFX thread and reusing them, the UI no longer stalls when a view is constructed for the first time, which addresses the reported lag on fresh start (#8446).

Notes / Caveats

- WebViewStore must be initialized at application startup before any call to WebViewStore.get(); this is done in JabRefGUI.
- Preloading is scheduled on the JavaFX thread via Platform.runLater, so the actual construction occurs asynchronously.
- The store may still create a new WebView if none are available immediately.

- Modified: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/MathSciNetTab.java

Fixes #3235 — update remote metadata rows instead of truncating and reinserting the whole table.

What I changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/shared/DBMSProcessor.java
  - Removed the TRUNCATE TABLE call that wiped the METADATA table.

text:
Closes #11999

Summary
- Reintroduced "best" title selection when merging candidate entries. Previously titles were effectively last-wins and could result in poor title choices when multiple candidates existed.

What I changed
- Updated mergeCandidates to merge all field candidates as before, then select and override the merged title with the best title candidate.
- Added a helper method calculateTitleScore that ranks title candidates using several heuristics: file path endings, titles that end with dot + characters (likely file extensions), and the number of words in the title (favoring longer/more descriptive titles).

Why
- This fixes a regression where title candidates were simply overwritten in a last-wins manner. The new scoring heuristics choose a more appropriate title automatically.

Testing and notes
- Manually tested the changed behavior in a running JabRef instance.
- Screenshots demonstrating the behavior have been added to the PR description.
- No automated tests were added in this change (see checklist). Please review the heuristics in calculateTitleScore for edge cases and suggest additions if needed.

- calculateTitleScore and the heuristics used to score titles

text:
Fix bug preventing external group metadata changes from being merged

What I changed
- Fixed group-diff construction: GroupDiff.compare now constructs GroupDiff(originalGroupRoot, newGroupRoot) (previously the arguments were reversed).
- Adjusted GroupDiffTest to expect the corrected ordering.
- When applying a metadata change in MetaDataChangeViewModel, ensure the database metadata keeps the original groups root (group changes are handled separately by GroupChangeViewModel). This prevents accidental overwrites/inconsistencies when merging external metadata changes.
- Added a CHANGELOG entry describing the fix.

Why this fixes the bug
- The reversed ordering in GroupDiff led to incorrect handling of group differences. Coupled with applying metadata wholesale, this caused external group metadata changes not to be merged correctly. Fixes #5555 — remove unnecessary status popups and suppress notifications during autosave.

What I changed
- Suppress notifications shown during autosave: AutosaveUIManager now calls SaveDatabaseAction.save(SILENT) instead of producing UI notifications.
- Introduced SaveDatabaseAction.SaveDatabaseMode (SILENT, NORMAL). The original save() delegates to save(NORMAL) to preserve previous behaviour; SILENT avoids status popups while still performing the save.
- Removed many obsolete dialogService.notify(...) calls that produced transient status popups in normal workflows:
  - BasePanel.insertEntry: removed 'Added new' notification
  - JabRefFrame.removeTab: removed 'Closed library' notification
  - FromAuxDialog: removed 'New library created' notification
  - NewDatabaseAction: removed 'New ... library created' notification
  - OpenDatabaseAction: removed notifications for 'File is already open', 'Files opened' and 'Opened library'
  - MainTable.paste: removed 'Pasted' notification
  - SharedDatabaseUIManager: removed simple 'Connection lost.' notify (replaced by dialog interaction)
- DBMSSynchronizer: added a warning log when the SQL connection is detected as lost and the ConnectionLostEvent is posted.
- Removed the corresponding localization strings from JabRef_en.properties for the deleted notifications.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to mention the autosave notification fix and removal of obsolete notifications.

Rationale
- Many small transient status popups created noise and disturbed workflows (especially autosave). Autosave should be silent; other transient messages that clutter the UI were removed in favor of less intrusive UX or explicit dialogs where appropriate.

Notes
- No automated tests were added.
- Changes were manually tested in a running JabRef build.
- See issue #5555 for discussion.

text:
Summary

Ensure the undo and redo toolbar and menu buttons are enabled and disabled correctly based on the document history state.

Problem

Undo/Redo controls sometimes remained enabled when there was nothing to undo/redo (or vice-versa). The UI did not always react when the history stack changed (for example after programmatic edits, document switches, or certain modal interactions), which led to confusing and inconsistent UX.

What this change does

- Make the toolbar and menu undo/redo controls listen to the canonical history state instead of stale cached state.
- Query the commands/history (canUndo / canRedo) on relevant events and update the enabled/disabled state accordingly.
- Wire up history change events so the UI updates immediately after edits, undo/redo operations, document switches, and programmatic changes.
- Ensure both toolbar buttons and menu items share the same state logic so they remain consistent.
- Add unit/integration tests covering the common edge cases (programmatic edits, document change, modal interactions).

Why this is better

- Eliminates inconsistent button/menu states and reduces user confusion.
- Keeps toolbar and menu in sync with the actual undo/redo availability.
- Prevents invalid operations by disabling controls when no action is possible.

Testing notes / How to verify

1. Open a document and make an edit; verify Undo becomes enabled and Redo is disabled.
2. Click Undo; verify Redo becomes enabled and Undo disables if no further undo remains.
3. Perform programmatic edits (e.g., paste via command/API) and verify the controls update immediately.
4. Switch between documents with different history stacks and confirm controls reflect the active document.
5. Open/close modal dialogs that perform edits and verify controls update after the dialog closes.

Risk / Rollback

- No public API changes. Low risk. If regressions are found, revert the UI wiring that subscribes to history events.

Notes

- Shared logic was centralized to avoid duplication between toolbar and menu implementations.
- Small test coverage added to prevent regressions in the future.

Add OttoBib ISBN fetcher and integrate it into the ISBN fetcher chain

- Added IsbnViaOttoBibFetcher which fetches BibTeX from https://www.ottobib.com/isbn/{isbn}/bibtex using Unirest.
  - Validates the ISBN, posts the request, parses the returned BibTeX, and returns the first BibEntry if any.
  - Sets the isbn field on the returned entry explicitly (ottobib does not include it in the response).

  - Adds debug logging for each fallback step.

- Uses Unirest (com.mashape.unirest) to perform the HTTP requests and the existing BibTeX parser to parse responses.
- Network or parse issues are wrapped into FetcherException so callers can handle failures uniformly.
- No changes to public APIs beyond adding the new fetcher implementation and integrating it into the existing IsbnFetcher flow.

Summary

Fixes issue #12188 by sanitizing generated filenames to remove LaTeX commands and other unsafe characters that may be introduced when filenames are derived from plot titles, labels, or other LaTeX-containing strings.

What I changed

- Added a filename sanitization routine used when generating filenames automatically.
- This routine removes LaTeX commands (backslashes and command names), braces, dollar signs, and other TeX-specific tokens; collapses/mapping whitespace into underscores; and strips or replaces characters that are unsafe or problematic in filenames (path separators, control chars, etc.).
- Normalizes repeated underscores and trims leading/trailing underscores to produce clean readable names.
- Ensures that user-provided explicit filenames are left unchanged.

Why this change

Automatically generated filenames could contain LaTeX commands (for example "\alpha", "{\mathbf{x}}", or math delimiters "$...$") which produced filenames with backslashes, braces, or other undesirable characters. Those filenames could be invalid on some platforms or simply ugly and hard to read. This change produces safe, predictable filenames while preserving meaningful text from titles/labels.

Examples (before → after)

- "$\alpha + \beta$" → "alpha_plus_beta"
- "Figure {\bf 1}: E=mc^2" → "Figure_1_E_mc2"
- "\mathrm{temperature}/K" → "temperature_K"

Compatibility

- Backwards compatible for user-supplied filenames: if a filename is explicitly provided by the user, it is not altered by this sanitization.
- Automatic filenames now follow the sanitized format; this may change the exact generated filename compared to previous behavior, but results are safer and more portable.

Tests

- Added unit tests covering typical LaTeX patterns, whitespace handling, repeated underscores, and edge cases (empty or all-removed names).

Related

- Fixes: #12188

Notes

- If additional filename normalization rules are desired (different replacement characters, maximum length limits, locale-specific rules), they can be added behind the same utility function.

text:
Add theme sync and custom theme support with live reloading

Summary
- Introduces an option to follow the OS light/dark preference and a way to select/import custom CSS themes from the Preferences -> General tab.
- Implements live CSS reloading for both the base stylesheet and additional theme CSS so theme changes (including external file edits) are applied immediately without restarting JabRef.

Key changes
- UI
  - Preferences -> General: added "Visual theme" control, "Use System Preference" checkbox, fields/buttons to pick a custom theme file and a "Get more themes..." link (GeneralTab.fxml, GeneralTab.java).
  - Spinner/text handling and validation for font size, theme path and remote port are wired up in the view model.

- Theme handling
  - New/updated ThemeManager to manage base and additional stylesheets, register listeners for OS theme changes (using OsThemeDetector), monitor CSS files via FileUpdateMonitor and apply live updates to Scene and WebEngine instances. Ensures graceful degradation if custom theme files are removed.

- Preferences & persistence
  - WorkspacePreferences extended to hold Theme and themeSyncOs state.
  - JabRefPreferences: added THEME and THEME_SYNC_OS defaults and storage handling so theme selection and "sync with OS" preference are persisted and available across sessions.
  - GeneralTabViewModel reads/writes the preferences and performs validation; UI bindings reflect preferences live.

- Misc
  - The General preferences view was refined to disable theme-related controls when "Use System Preference" is active, and to only enable custom-theme controls for ThemeTypes.CUSTOM.
  - Web preview styling is updated when theme changes (ThemeManager installs styles into WebEngine instances).

Why
- Allowing users to sync JabRef’s theme with their operating system improves UX and accessibility (automatic dark/light selection).
- Custom theme import + live reloading enables faster theme iteration and easier theming for power users.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/general/GeneralTab.fxml
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/general/GeneralTab.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/general/GeneralTabViewModel.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/theme/ThemeManager.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/preferences/JabRefPreferences.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/preferences/WorkspacePreferences.java
- build.gradle (JavaFX version & related build settings)
- resources: l10n additions for the new UI strings

Notes
- Theme switching now reacts to OS theme changes when the new "Use System Preference" option is enabled.
- Custom CSS files are watched and reloaded when changed; if a custom file is removed while running, ThemeManager degrades gracefully.
- No manual restart is required when changing themes or font-size settings (applied live).

text:
Re-introduce preview-style switching and refactor preview handling

Summary
- Re-added the ability to cycle through different preview styles (next/previous) [#5221].
- Moved preview-cycle logic out of BasePanel and into the EntryEditor / EntryEditorTab / FieldsEditorTab / PreviewPanel, cleaning up responsibilities and removing preview-specific imports from BasePanel.
- PreviewPanel now uses JabRefPreferences and is responsible for reading/storing PreviewPreferences and cycling the preview layout.
- EntryEditor delegates next/previous preview style actions to its tabs; EntryEditorTab provides no-op hooks that FieldsEditorTab overrides to switch the embedded PreviewPanel.
- Restored context-menu items for "Next preview layout" and "Previous preview layout" and wired them to the new methods.
- Fixed PreviewPreferences.Builder naming/logic (typos and correct cycle position wrapping) and made JabRefPreferences.getPreviewPreferences resilient to invalid stored cycle indices.

Files changed (high level)
- CHANGELOG.md: documented re-introduced feature.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/BasePanel.java: removed preview cycle methods and added actions to trigger next/previous preview styles.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/EntryEditor.java: added next/previous preview methods that forward to tabs.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/EntryEditorTab.java: added protected next/previousPreviewStyle hook methods (no-op default).
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/FieldsEditorTab.java: moved PreviewPanel field to private, override hooks to call previewPanel.next/previous and updated PreviewPanel construction to pass JabRefPreferences.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preview/PreviewPanel.java: refactored to accept JabRefPreferences, initialize from preferences, store updated PreviewPreferences, implement next/previous/cycle logic and re-enable context menu items.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/preferences/JabRefPreferences.java: improved getPreviewPreferences to guard against out-of-range stored cycle position.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/preferences/PreviewPreferences.java: fixed builder variable name typos and corrected cycle positioning/wrapping logic.

Notes
- Behavior: cycling previews updates PreviewPreferences and shows a notification when the style changes. If the stored cycle index is invalid (e.g. after removing layouts), it falls back to 0.
- This change centralizes preview preference handling in PreviewPanel/JabRefPreferences and decouples BasePanel from preview-specific state.

- Implemented several improvements to how custom export name formatters are managed and looked up, following suggestions from @koppor in #1695.

Key changes
- Replaced direct usage of Globals for resource loading in ExportFormat with JabRefMain to avoid referencing Globals from logic package.
- Introduced new API on LayoutFormatterPreferences to encapsulate operations on custom export name formatters:
  - clearCustomExportNameFormatters()
  - putCustomExportNameFormatter(String formatterName, String contents)
  - getCustomExportNameFormatter(String formatterName) -> Optional<String>
- Replaced direct map access in LayoutEntry and ExportFormat with the new LayoutFormatterPreferences methods. This uses Optional to make the presence check more explicit and avoid potential NPEs.
- Renamed several local variables (e.g. className -> nameFormatterName) to make it clear these identifiers represent name formatter names rather than class names.
- Updated NotFoundFormatter usage and formatter loading code to consistently use the formatter name variable.

Why
- Encapsulating map operations in LayoutFormatterPreferences improves encapsulation and makes future changes to storage safer and clearer.
- Using Optional for lookup results makes intent explicit and simplifies presence checks.
- Removing Globals usage from logic package aligns with project structure and removes an unnecessary dependency.

Files changed
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/exporter/ExportFormat.java
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/layout/LayoutEntry.java
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/layout/LayoutFormatterPreferences.java

Backward compatibility
- Public API of LayoutFormatterPreferences changed by removing direct access to the map and adding accessor/mutator methods; callers should use the new methods. This change was applied to affected internal call sites in this PR.

Notes
- These changes are primarily refactorings and small behavioral improvements; no change to exported formats/behavior is expected beyond more robust handling of custom name formatters and resource loading.

Summary
Fixes charset detection to correctly identify UTF-16 (both LE and BE) and other multibyte encodings that were previously misdetected.

Problem
The previous detection logic treated inputs containing NUL bytes or certain byte patterns as binary/unknown or as single-byte encodings. That caused UTF-16-encoded files (and some other multibyte encodings) to be misclassified, losing correct text processing and downstream behavior.

What I changed
- Added BOM-aware handling so UTF-16LE/UTF-16BE (and UTF-32 where present) are detected by their BOMs.
- Improved heuristics to distinguish valid UTF-16 streams with interleaved NUL bytes from true binary data when BOM is absent (e.g., checking likely ASCII/Unicode ranges and surrogate validity).
- Extended detection rules to better handle other multibyte encodings and avoid false positives for binary when zero bytes are valid.
- Reordered checks to prefer explicit BOM and strong multibyte signatures before falling back to binary heuristics.
- Added unit tests and sample fixtures for UTF-16LE/BE files (with and without BOM) and edge cases that previously failed.

Compatibility and impact
- Public API unchanged; callers will see corrected charset labels for affected inputs.
- Behavior change is intentional and fixes incorrect detections; callers that relied on the old incorrect behavior should update accordingly.
- Performance overhead is negligible — checks are lightweight and limited to the sample buffer used for detection.

Testing
- New unit tests cover BOM-present and BOM-absent UTF-16, surrogate pair validation, and mixed-content edge cases.
- All existing tests updated and passing.

Notes
- If you have specific corner-case files that still misdetect, please add them as test fixtures so we can refine heuristics further.

Fixes #2336: ensure clean shutdown by properly initializing and registering the BackupManager.

What I changed
- BackupManager now registers itself as a listener in its constructor so it cannot be missed during setup.
- The backup manager is always initialized, even for shared databases or when a DB has no filepath yet.
- Minor refactorings and cleanup around backup manager initialization and related code paths.

Why
- The symptom was that shutdown wasn't working reliably; I suspect the BackupManager was sometimes not registered as a listener which prevented proper shutdown handling. Initializing and registering it deterministically fixes that.

Notes
- This resolves the reported problem for me during manual testing. I don't have a definitive root-cause trace beyond the registration timing, but these changes make shutdown behavior reliable.
- No other behavioral changes intended beyond more robust backup manager initialization and slightly cleaner code.

- The illegal reflective access warnings from Byte Buddy noted when running tests in IntelliJ were observed during debugging but are not addressed by this PR (they stem from underlying libraries and Java internals). See issue #5602 for context.

Adds a search history feature to the global search field and exposes it via the field's right-click context menu.

text:
Introduce MainTableFormat, a TableFormat<BibEntry> implementation that centralizes the main table column configuration. Key points:

- Manages a dynamic list of MainTableColumn instances and exposes helper accessors: getColumnCount(), getColumnName(int), getColumnValue(BibEntry, int), getTableColumn(int), and getColumnIndex(String).
- Implements updateTableFormat() to (re)build the table layout from preferences and the provided BibDatabase. The rebuild flow:
  - Clears existing columns.
  - Adds a numbering column and optionally a file column.
  - Adds a URL/DOI icon column, honoring the PREFER_URL_DOI preference to determine which icon/field (DOI first or URL first) to prioritize.
  - Adds an arXiv icon column when enabled.
  - Adds any extra file columns defined in LIST_OF_FILE_COLUMNS.
  - Adds special icon columns (ranking, relevance, quality, priority, printed, read) if SPECIALFIELDSENABLED and the individual SHOWCOLUMN_* preferences are enabled. These are constructed via SpecialMainTableColumnsBuilder.
  - Adds the normal BibTeX fields configured in COLUMN_NAMES. Support for multi-field column definitions (e.g., "author/editor") is provided by splitting on FieldName.FIELD_SEPARATOR.

- Uses Globals.prefs and JabRefPreferences constants to drive which columns are displayed.
- Uses IconTheme icons for the various icon columns and delegates construction of specialized columns to SpecialMainTableColumnsBuilder.

Other notes:
- getColumnIndex performs a case-insensitive comparison and returns the last occurrence index (or -1 if not found).

This change centralizes column-building logic and makes the main table layout responsive to preferences and database schema.

Summary

This draft implements a first pass at fixing synchronization between groups and a shared database. The main idea is to propagate group metadata update events from the LibraryTab to the GroupTreeViewModel so the groups view refreshes when group metadata changes come from other clients/threads.

What I changed

- Added a new ObjectProperty<MetaData> groupsTreeChanged to LibraryTab and publish GroupUpdatedEvent changes into it. The property is updated on the JavaFX thread when a GroupUpdatedEvent is received.
- GroupTreeViewModel now observes the active tab's groupsTreeChanged property and triggers a refresh (via initRefreshListener -> onActiveDatabaseChanged) when non-null metadata is observed. This simulates a database change to force reloading the group tree. (A debug System.out.println is present in the listener.)
- Converted GroupTreeNodeViewModel from a class to a record to simplify code and remove boilerplate accessors. Updated all usages accordingly (replaced getNode() calls with node()).
- Updated undoable group edits (UndoableAddOrRemoveGroup, UndoableModifySubtree, UndoableMoveGroup) to use the new record accessor methods.
- Minor cleanups in OptionalObjectProperty (imports) and a couple of other imports.
- Added a unit test (MetaDataDiffTest.metadataWithColoredGroupsShowsDiff) to assert that colored group metadata differences are detected by MetaDataDiff.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/LibraryTab.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/groups/GroupTreeNodeViewModel.java (converted to record)

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/groups/UndoableModifySubtree.java

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/util/OptionalObjectProperty.java
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/bibtex/comparator/MetaDataDiffTest.java (new test)

Notes / TODOs

- This is still a draft. The current approach simulates a full database change to force a refresh; a more targeted update propagation would be preferable.
- The code contains a System.out.println used for debugging in GroupTreeViewModel; that should be removed or replaced by logging once the approach is finalized.
- Performance and correctness of the event wiring (and whether additional event-source checks are required) need to be verified in manual testing with shared DB setups.

Closes
Fixes #11232

Fixes an issue where the "Copy to clipboard" custom export was not selected when the file extension was uppercase (for example ".MD" instead of ".md").

Root cause

The code matched file extensions against custom export keys using a case-sensitive comparison, so uppercase extensions failed to match existing lowercase export keys.

What I changed

- Normalize file extensions to lowercase before doing the custom-export lookup and selection.
- Ensure the selection logic for the "Copy to clipboard" export uses the normalized extension.
- Added unit tests covering uppercase and mixed-case file extensions to prevent regression.

Testing / QA

- Unit tests added for ".MD", ".Md", and ".md" matching a configured custom export.
- Manual verification: open an asset with an uppercase extension and trigger Copy to Clipboard -> the appropriate custom export is now pre-selected.

Risk / Impact

This change is backward compatible and only affects how file extensions are matched (making it case-insensitive). No other behavior is changed.

Why:
Some fields (identifiers, certain metadata fields, etc.) are intended to be single-line. Users or imports could introduce newlines that break output formatting or metadata expectations. This change guarantees single-line values for those fields across input and output.

Notes:
- There are 7 failing tests reported in the PR description, but they also failed on master before this change and appear unrelated to this fix. The failing tests are included in the PR body for visibility.

Summary

This PR replaces the use of org.hisp.dhis:json-tree for parsing nested JSON in the JabLS language server with Jackson's JsonNode API. The JSON-handling ADR (docs/decisions/0051-handle-nested-json-paths.md) is updated to choose Jackson, code in ExtensionSettings now uses ObjectMapper/JsonNode.at with safe fallback values, and build/module configuration is updated to remove the json-tree dependency and add jackson-databind.

What I changed

- docs/decisions/0051-handle-nested-json-paths.md: Reworked the ADR to select Jackson and included a compact example using JsonNode.at(...).asBoolean(...).
- jabls/src/main/java/org/jabref/languageserver/ExtensionSettings.java: Replaced org.hisp.dhis.jsontree usage with com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper and JsonNode.at. Added JsonProcessingException handling and logging.
- jabls/src/main/java/module-info.java: Removed requires org.hisp.dhis.jsontree; added requires com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.
- jabls/build.gradle.kts: Removed implementation("org.hisp.dhis:json-tree").
- .jbang/JabLsLauncher.java: Added a direct DEPS entry for jackson-databind and removed a json-tree DEPS line.
- build-logic/src/main/kotlin/org.jabref.gradle.base.dependency-rules.gradle.kts: Removed the extra-java-module mapping for org.hisp.dhis:json-tree.

Rationale

- Jackson's JsonNode.at supports nested paths directly, returns sensible defaults (via asBoolean/etc.) when nodes are missing, and is compact and readable. It avoids adding a specialized JSON-tree dependency.
- Keeps parsing robust: code now catches JsonProcessingException and logs parsing failures instead of throwing at call sites.

Files modified (high level)

- docs/decisions/0051-handle-nested-json-paths.md
- jabls/src/main/java/org/jabref/languageserver/ExtensionSettings.java
- jabls/src/main/java/module-info.java
- jabls/build.gradle.kts
- .jbang/JabLsLauncher.java
- build-logic/src/main/kotlin/org.jabref.gradle.base.dependency-rules.gradle.kts

How to test

1. Build the project (Gradle) and ensure the jabls module compiles.
2. Start the JabLS language server (or run the jbang launcher) and send settings payloads containing nested jabref.consistencyCheck and jabref.integrityCheck fields.
3. Verify that ExtensionSettings picks up enabled/required/optional/unknown and integrity settings correctly when present, and that missing fields fall back to the current defaults without throwing exceptions.
4. Confirm there are no unresolved module requirements for org.hisp.dhis.jsontree and that jackson-databind is available at runtime for the jabls module.

Notes

- This is a follow-up to #13910 and addresses the discussion about JSON parsing approach.
- No behavioral changes are intended other than switching the underlying parser implementation; parsing should be more robust and introduce no new runtime exceptions for absent nested paths.

- [x] I own the copyright of the code and license under MIT
- [x] Manually tested changes in a running environment
- [/] Added unit tests (n/a)
- [/] Updated CHANGELOG or user documentation (n/a)

Summary:
Improve the import workflow and make BibTeX parsing more robust. This PR refactors parts of the import UI/actions, improves format detection and parsing in the importer core, fixes several edge cases (encoding/BOM, empty input and escaped/nested braces), and adds/updates a user-facing localization string.

Key changes:
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/importer/ImportAction.java
  - Refactor import action logic to better separate UI concerns from import logic.
  - Ensure the import process opens or offers the imported database reliably and handles the result consistently.
  - Improve error handling and user feedback when an import fails or yields no entries.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/importer/actions/OpenDatabaseAction.java
  - Improve behavior for opening databases produced by import actions (including opening in new tabs and reusing existing views where appropriate).
  - Make the action more tolerant to varied import outcomes and coordinate with the ImportAction changes.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/ImportFormatReader.java
  - Improve format detection by more reliably sniffing file contents and handling BOM/encoding cases.
  - Harden stream reading to avoid NPEs and to properly preserve content for downstream parsers.
  - Add clearer error propagation so UI can inform users about format/encoding issues.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/BibtexParser.java
  - Fix parsing issues for several edge cases, including escaped characters, nested braces and concatenated strings.
  - Handle empty or whitespace-only inputs without throwing exceptions.
  - Better handle leading BOM and non-UTF8 inputs by cooperating with ImportFormatReader.
  - Increase robustness against malformed entries to prevent the whole import from failing.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/SourceTab.java
  - Ensure the source view reflects imported content correctly and is synchronized with the parsing improvements.
  - Improve UI resilience when showing raw sources from different encodings and when an entry has problematic source text.

- src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties
  - Add/update translation keys used by the improved import/error messages so users get clearer feedback when imports fail or encoding is ambiguous.

Motivation:
Users reported imports failing silently or producing unusable databases when files contained BOMs, non-UTF-8 encodings, escaped/braced content, or when import actions returned unexpected results. This PR addresses those issues by making both the parsing logic and the UI actions more robust and better coordinated.

Compatibility and testing:
- Changes are backwards compatible for normal import flows.
- Error messages and import dialogs are improved but existing settings remain unchanged.
- Manual testing performed for common BibTeX files (including files with BOM, nested braces, and string concatenation). Please review edge cases and run existing import tests.

Notes for reviewers:
- Pay attention to the cooperation between ImportFormatReader and BibtexParser around encoding/BOM handling.
- Review the UI changes in ImportAction/OpenDatabaseAction to ensure they match expected user flows (open new tab vs reuse).
- Localization key changes are small but verify strings make sense in context.

Introduce structured preferences for the main table columns and wire them into the GUI preferences.

Summary of changes:
- Add ColumnPreferences to encapsulate a table of MainTableColumnModel instances and the column sort order. Provides observable lists, setters/getters, defaults (including DEFAULT_COLUMN_WIDTH and ICON_COLUMN_WIDTH), and a private default constructor with the app's default column layout.
- Add MainTablePreferences to hold ColumnPreferences and BooleanProperties for resizeColumnsToFit and extraFileColumnsEnabled, with defaults and property accessors.
- Integrate column and main-table preferences into JabRefGuiPreferences:
  - Add constants for column-related preference keys (COLUMN_NAMES, COLUMN_WIDTHS, COLUMN_SORT_TYPES, COLUMN_SORT_ORDER) and for autosize/extra file columns.
  - Implement getMainTablePreferences(), getMainTableColumnPreferences() and getSearchDialogColumnPreferences() to read from the backing store (with fallbacks to defaults) and to register listeners that persist changes when columns, widths, sort types or sort order are modified.

  - Use the main table column sort order when building a SelfContainedSaveOrder for the export configuration.
- Ensure backward compatibility and robustness: parsing handles NumberFormatException and invalid values by falling back to defaults and logging errors.

Summary
- Add support for the biblatex langid field as an optional field in the entry editor (dropdown + parsing + storage). This enables storing the language identifier for entries so formatting/processing tools can adapt to the entry language. Closes #10868.

What changed
- New model: added Langid enum (model/entry/Langid.java) containing biblatex language identifiers, parsing helpers and a method to produce the JabRef stored format.
- Entry API: added BibEntry#setLangid(Langid) to set the field using the new enum.
- UI: added LanguageEditorViewModel (gui/fieldeditors/optioneditors/LanguageEditorViewModel.java) and wired it into FieldEditors so langid appears as an option editor in the entry editor for applicable fields/modes.
- Entry types: added StandardField.LANGUAGEID to relevant biblatex entry type definitions (model/entry/types/BiblatexEntryTypeDefinitions.java) so langid is available/visible where appropriate.
- Field handling: marked LANGUAGEID as a not-text field in FieldFactory so it is treated consistently with other special fields.
- Minor: made databaseMode field in MonthEditorViewModel final for consistency.
- Tests: added tests for Langid parsing and lookups (model/entry/LangidTest.java), tests for LanguageEditorViewModel (gui/fieldeditors/optioneditors/LanguageEditorViewModelTest.java), and updated BibEntry types tests to use StandardField.LANGUAGEID (model/entry/BibEntryTypesManagerTest.java).
- Changelog: updated CHANGELOG.md mentioning langid support.

Notes for reviewers
- The LanguageEditor uses Langid.parse and a StringConverter to convert between displayed strings and enum values. Empty/blank input maps to null.
- Langid.getJabRefFormat wraps the identifier in the same quoting/wrapping the project uses for similar fields.
- UI screenshot and manual testing were performed (see PR description attachments).

Testing
- Unit tests added and updated to cover parsing, conversion, and integration into entry type definitions.

If anything else should be exposed in the UI or if more langid variants need adding, I kept the enum centralized so it can be extended easily.

text:
Add ClipBoardManager for cross-platform clipboard handling and integrate into Globals

- Introduce ClipBoardManager to centralize clipboard operations (system clipboard and X11 primary selection).
  - addX11Support(TextInputControl): support primary selection for X11 (copies selected text to primary and pastes on middle click).
  - getContents()/getContentsPrimary(): read text from system clipboard and fall back to primary clipboard when available.
  - setContent/setPrimaryClipboardContent/setHtmlContent: write plain text, HTML (with plain fallback) and synchronize system and primary clipboards.
  - setContent(List<BibEntry>): serialize BibEntry objects to BibTeX and place them on the clipboard using DragAndDropDataFormats.ENTRIES.
  - extractData(): extract BibEntry data from clipboard; supports direct serialized entries, raw BibTeX parsing, DOI detection and fetching, and importing unknown formats via ImportFormatReader.
  - Robust error handling and logging for clipboard I/O, parsing and fetcher errors.

- Update Globals
  - Add static IMPORT_FORMAT_READER to provide import functionality used by ClipBoardManager.
  - Instantiate a default ClipBoardManager as Globals.clipboardManager so it can be accessed/injected where needed.
  - Keep other existing global singletons and background task initialization unchanged.

Notes
- ClipBoardManager uses AWT for primary selection access (allowed via @AllowedToUseAwt).
- DOI-based clipboard content will trigger a fetch via DoiFetcher; failures are logged and return empty results.
- Parsing of pasted BibTeX uses BibtexParser with configured import preferences.

This change centralizes clipboard logic, improves cross-platform clipboard behavior (notably Linux X11 primary selection), and enables richer paste behavior (BibTeX, DOI, import formats, HTML) throughout the GUI.

Summary

- Validate the configured main file directory in the File preferences tab and notify the user if it doesn't exist or is not a directory.
- Surface download errors to the user instead of failing silently when a download / write operation throws an IOException.
- Update CHANGELOG to mention the fix.

What changed

- FileTab.java
  - Added validation in validateSettings(): verifies that the path in the main file directory field exists and is a directory. If invalid, an error dialog is shown and the method returns false (preventing invalid settings from being accepted).
  - Added necessary imports for java.nio.file and JOptionPane.

- DownloadExternalFile.java
  - When an IOException occurs while downloading/writing a file, show an error dialog with a localized error message instead of only logging a warning. This gives immediate feedback to the user about the failure.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added an entry documenting the fix: downloads no longer fail silently when an invalid directory is selected.

Rationale

Previously an invalid main file directory could be saved silently, and download write errors were only logged, leaving users unaware of the problem. These changes improve UX by validating directory settings up front and by presenting clear error dialogs for download/write failures.

Compatibility

No public API changes. Behavior changes are limited to user-visible validation and error reporting in the GUI.

text: Introduce shared-database synchronization core: add DBMSProcessor (abstract) and DBMSSynchronizer to manage interaction between a local BibDatabase and an external SQL-backed shared database. DBMSProcessor encapsulates low-level DB operations (insert/update/delete entries and fields, metadata read/write, table-structure checks and setup) and provides DBMS-specific escaping and processor instantiation for supported types (MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle). It implements batched retrieval, prepared-statement usage, transaction handling for updates, and safeguards such as version checks and OfflineLockException handling. DBMSSynchronizer wires synchronization to the application via a Guava EventBus: it listens for local entry/meta events (add, remove, field change, metadata change), pushes local changes to the shared DB, pulls remote changes into the local database, applies metadata and save-actions, and handles initialization/migration of legacy DB schemas. The synchronizer also includes connection health checks and events for connection loss or refused updates. Error handling and logging have been added/extended around SQL operations and metadata parsing. The changelog has been updated (Unreleased) to record recent additions.

Improve field resolution, alias/date handling and LaTeX->Unicode conversion for main table columns and BibEntry

Summary
- MainTableColumn now uses resolved field values (including string resolution and crossref lookups) when determining the column value to display. Name columns are formatted with MainTableNameFormatter and converted from LaTeX to Unicode. The column header and icon handling remain unchanged. Why
- Correctly displaying values in the main table requires resolving string values and crossref aliases, and supporting bibtex/biblatex aliases and date->year/month extraction makes field access more robust.
- Caching LaTeX-free conversions reduces repeated work and avoids converting the bibtex key.
- isResolved enables UI elements (e.g. group highlighting or resolved-field color coding) to detect when a displayed value is from a resolved/aliased source.

Notes
- Behavior change: callers that previously inspected raw entry fields may now see resolved values when using the new APIs that accept a BibDatabase. The raw getField(...) remains available.
- No UI changes were made in this commit beyond using the resolved values and Unicode formatting for names.

text:
Fixes #8907 — Remember Sidepane width after restart

Summary
- Fixes an issue where the Sidepane (groups, web search, OpenOffice) width was not preserved after restarting JabRef when the window size/state changed (e.g. maximized -> restarted).

Problem
- Previously we stored the SplitPane divider position and re-applied that position on startup. When the app was restarted from a different window state (e.g. minimized or different width), the divider position produced a different absolute sidepane width, resulting in an apparent loss of the saved width. Also, the side pane was configured as non-resizable with its parent which caused that persisted relative divider position to result in a constant (wrong) width.

What I changed
- Store and persist the absolute sidepane width (sidePane.widthProperty()) instead of the relative divider position.
- On startup, compute and apply the divider position from the stored absolute width by dividing the stored width by the current SplitPane width (prefsWidth / splitPane.getWidth()).
- Wrap the initial setDividerPosition call in Platform.runLater to ensure the main stage is showing and the SplitPane size is available before computing/calculating divider positions.
- Replace the EasyBind subscription on the divider position with a subscription on sidePane.widthProperty() so preference updates track the actual pixel width.
- Added a short user-facing changelog entry.

Notes
- Manually tested the behavior (maximized -> restart, different window sizes) and confirmed the sidepane width is now preserved across restarts.
- No automated tests were added in this PR.

text:
Add automatic download of linked online files when creating entries from identifiers (DOI, arXiv, etc.)

What this does
- Implements an option to automatically download linked online files (e.g. PDFs reachable via DOI or URL) when a new entry is created from an existing identifier. The feature is controlled by a new preference: Preferences → Import and Export → "Download linked online files".
- When enabled, ImportHandler will trigger downloads for all online LinkedFile objects of the newly created entry by invoking LinkedFileViewModel.download(). Downloads are executed via the TaskExecutor.

Why
- Users expect attached fulltext files to be fetched automatically when creating an entry from an identifier. This implements that behavior while keeping it opt-in via preferences.

Main changes
- New preference checkbox in the Import & Export preference tab and binding in ImportExportTabViewModel to FilePreferences.shouldDownloadLinkedFiles().
- ImportHandler now accepts a TaskExecutor and, after importing a fetched entry, will download any online linked files if the preference is enabled.
- Propagate TaskExecutor to several classes and constructors (EntryTypeView/EntryTypeViewModel, LibraryTab, MainTable, BibtexExtractorViewModel, ImportEntriesViewModel, UnlinkedFilesDialogViewModel, GenerateEntryFromIdAction, etc.) so background downloads use the app task executor.
- Updated ImportHandlerTest to use CurrentThreadTaskExecutor for deterministic testing.
- CHANGELOG entry announcing the new option.

Notes for reviewers
- Constructor signatures changed in multiple GUI classes to accept TaskExecutor; callers were updated accordingly. Pay attention to DI / injection and make sure no call site was missed.
- The preference is opt-in by default (reads from existing FilePreferences). Existing behavior remains unchanged unless the new preference is enabled.

Fixes
- Fixes #9756
- Fixes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref-issue-melting-pot/issues/127

Add title-based formatters and extensive bracketed-pattern tests

This change introduces several new title-formatting tools and integrates them into the existing formatter infrastructure:

- Implemented CamelFormatter and CamelNFormatter (casechanger)
  - CamelFormatter: capitalizes and concatenates all title words (Camel case)
  - CamelNFormatter: same behavior but limited to the first N words (Camel case - n letters max)

- Implemented ShortTitleFormatter and VeryShortTitleFormatter (casechanger)
  - ShortTitleFormatter: returns the first 3 non-function words of a title
  - VeryShortTitleFormatter: returns the first non-function word of a title

- Registered the new formatters in Formatters
  - Added getTitleChangers() and included the title changers in getAll()
  - Ensures modifiers such as camel, camelN, shorttitle and veryshorttitle are available via bracketed patterns

- Added localization strings for the new formatters and descriptions in JabRef_en.properties

- Added/updated comprehensive tests (BracketedPatternTest)
  - Extensive coverage for author/editor markers, regex/replace modifiers, truncate chaining, camel/camelN, shorttitle and veryshorttitle modifiers
  - Tests for edge cases: von name prefixes, braces and LaTeX-to-Unicode conversions, institution abbreviation extraction, long page numbers, unresolved crossref handling, and regex modifiers with special characters

No breaking changes to existing formatters are expected; this primarily extends available formatting and citation-key pattern capabilities and ensures behavior via the new unit tests.

Summary:
Adds a reliable way to reset proxy preferences to their default values and fixes issues where proxy settings would become inconsistent between UI and persisted storage.

What I changed:
- Implemented resetProxyPreferences() that restores default proxy configuration and clears any cached runtime proxy state.
- Added a "Reset to defaults" control in the Proxy Preferences UI and wired it to the new reset logic.
- Ensured the reset operation updates both the in-memory state and the persistent storage (preferences file / database) so UI and backend remain in sync.
- Added unit tests for the reset logic and an integration/e2e test that verifies the UI control resets settings and that changes persist after restart.
- Fixed a bug where partial/invalid proxy values could leave the application in a broken state by validating values before saving and reverting to defaults on reset.

Why this change:
Users were experiencing confusing behavior when proxy preferences were changed — settings could appear to be applied in the UI but would not be persisted, or the app would retain stale cached values. Providing a clear reset action and fixing the persistence/pathology makes preferences predictable and recoverable.

How to test:
1. Open Preferences -> Proxy.
2. Change proxy fields to non-default values and save.
3. Verify values are persisted after app restart.

text:
Refactor layout/formatter configuration and export handling

This patch introduces a centralized LayoutFormatterPreferences class and integrates it into the export/layout pipeline. Main changes:

- Add LayoutFormatterPreferences to encapsulate: NameFormatterPreferences, JournalAbbreviationPreferences, FileLinkPreferences and JournalAbbreviationLoader, plus support for per-export custom name formatters.
- ExportFormat now accepts LayoutFormatterPreferences (and SavePreferences) and passes the preferences to LayoutHelper when loading .layout/.begin.layout/.end.layout files so formatters have access to required preferences and loaders.
- Implement loading of custom name formatters from a companion "<layout>.formatters" file in ExportFormat.readFormatterFile(), expose them through LayoutFormatterPreferences, and ensure they are cleared after the export (layoutPreferences.clearCustomExportNameFormatters()).
- Add a performExport overload that accepts a Path and delegates to the String-based implementation.
- Improve encoding/save workflow in performExport and finalizeSaveSession (use specified encoding if possible, fall back otherwise, flush/close writer and commit output file, and warn on encoding issues).
- LayoutEntry now accepts LayoutFormatterPreferences (prefs) and uses it when instantiating formatters that require external preferences (e.g. JournalAbbreviator, FileLink, WrapFileLinks) or when resolving user-defined name formatters.
- Option-field handling changed: if the option text starts with a backslash (\), it now resolves the referenced field value from the entry; otherwise it uses literal text from the layout. This allows distinguishing between text and field resolution in optional fields.
- Added robust parsing of formatter method calls via parseMethodsCalls, and expanded mapping of formatter names to concrete LayoutFormatter implementations (fall back to NotFoundFormatter for unknown names).
- Various minor logging and error handling improvements.

These changes make layout formatters more configurable, enable export-specific name formatters, and streamline how formatter preferences are provided and used during export.

text:
Add module descriptor (module-info.java) and align module metadata with Gradle configuration

This change introduces an open module descriptor for org.jabref (src/main/java/module-info.java) to enable Java Platform Module support while still allowing reflection for frameworks that require it (JavaFX, Afterburner, ControlsFX, etc.). The module-info declares explicit module-level dependencies (requires) and service loader contracts (uses/provides) to match the project’s runtime and build-time dependencies configured in build.gradle.

Key points:
- Declare required modules for core functionality: JavaFX, Swing, SQL, HTTP, JAXB/JSON/YAML (Jackson), Lucene, PDFBox, Antlr, JDBC drivers (Oracle, PostgreSQL, MariaDB), H2 MVStore, and various 3rd-party libs used across the project.
- Register and expose service provider implementations via provides (examples: ikonli handlers/providers, Afterburner resource/injection hooks, tinylog GuiWriter, MariaDB authentication/credential plugins, and JDBC driver provisioning for PostgreSQL).
- Use uses declarations for service loader consumers (e.g., ikonli, MariaDB credential plugin, JGit factories, Lucene codec/query parser hooks) so implementations can be discovered at runtime.
- Keep module open to allow reflection-based frameworks (Afterburner, Jackson, JavaFX, ControlsFX, mvvmFX, etc.) to operate without additional --add-opens flags during development.
- Align module names to the artifacts declared in build.gradle so the module descriptor is consistent with the dependency graph and the jlink/jpackage configuration.

This improves clarity of module dependencies, aids modular runtime packaging (jlink/jpackage), and prepares the project for stricter modularization while preserving compatibility with reflection-based libraries.

text:
Re-add FormatChars support and legacy formatter name compatibility

Summary
- Restore backward compatibility for legacy LayoutFormatter names (including FormatChars) by replacing the previous reflection-based factory with an explicit name->formatter mapping.
- Make getOptionalLayout an instance method and adapt usages accordingly.
- Small refactor and parsing fixes in LayoutEntry.
- Remove a couple of unused constants in Globals and GUIGlobals.

What changed
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/layout/LayoutEntry.java
  - Replaced getLayoutFormatterByClassName (reflection) with getLayoutFormatterByName: a large switch that maps many legacy/alternate formatter names to their current implementations. This restores support for FormatChars and other renamed formatters (FormatChars -> LatexToUnicodeFormatter, HTMLToLatex/HtmlToLatex, UnicodeToLatex/UnicodeToLatexFormatter, etc.).
  - getOptionalLayout is now an instance method (getOptionalLayout) and is used in doOptionField.
  - Minor parsing/variable-scope cleanups: moved blockEntries declaration, created local LayoutEntry le variable inline, removed some commented markers.
  - Added imports for various formatters used by the mapping (HtmlToLatexFormatter, UnicodeToLatexFormatter, OOPreFormatter, etc.).
  - Unknown/unsupported formatter names now return a NotFoundFormatter(name), preserving previous behavior for missing formatters.

- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/Globals.java
  - Removed unused FILETYPE_PREFS_EXT constant.

- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/GUIGlobals.java
  - Removed unused PE_HEIGHT constant.

Motivation
- Avoid fragile reflection-based instantiation of formatters and make it possible to rename/relocate formatter classes while keeping backward compatibility for saved exports and custom layouts. This is an alternative approach to PR/issue #1114.

Notes / TODO
- CHANGELOG.md entry not yet added.
- No tests added for these changes yet; they should be created to cover legacy-name mappings and behaviors.
- The commit keeps many deprecated Author* formatters mapped for compatibility. The old Author* formatters are documented as deprecated in the help; consider removing them in a future cleanup.

Risks
- The switch-based mapping is large and must be kept in sync with actual formatter classes. New formatters need to be added to this mapping if they should be addressed by legacy names.

This change aims to restore compatibility for existing user configurations that reference legacy formatter names (notably FormatChars) while removing the reliance on reflective class loading.

Fix editing and saving of keyboard shortcuts (#14237)

Summary
- Fixes an issue where keybindings could not be edited and persisted via the preferences UI.

What I changed
- CHANGELOG.md: Added an entry describing the fix for editing/saving keybindings.
- KeyBindingsTab.java: Improve key event handling for the keybindings table. The table now consumes key pressed events and forwards them to the view model via an event filter to ensure key presses are captured reliably when editing bindings.
- KeyBindingsTabViewModel.java: Simplified and corrected storeSettings(): the preferences keybinding repository is now cleared and populated with the current UI repository entries, and the restart warning is always added. This ensures edits are written into GuiPreferences correctly.
- Tests:
  - Updated KeyBindingsTabModelTest expectations to reflect the corrected behavior when resetting/modifying bindings.
  - KeyBindingViewModelTest: added DisabledOnCIServer to two tests (marked flaky on CI), added an import and assertion helper, and added a new test verifyStoreSettingsWritesChanges that mocks GuiPreferences and verifies a changed binding is persisted as expected.

Notes
- The change to event filtering ensures key events are not swallowed by other handlers and that setNewBindingForCurrent receives the full KeyEvent. The storeSettings change consistently writes the UI repository into preferences rather than conditionally replacing or attempting to compare repositories, which resolves the bug where changes were not saved.

Summary

Fix a bug where metadata changes coming from external group sources were not being merged into existing groups, causing metadata updates to be ignored or lost.

What I changed

- Updated the merge logic for external groups to properly merge the metadata map instead of skipping or replacing it incorrectly.
- Implemented a deep-merge behavior for metadata so new keys are added, existing keys are updated, and explicit null values are handled as intended (treated as removal only when explicitly supported).
- Added unit tests that cover: adding new metadata keys, updating existing keys, removing keys, and handling empty/null metadata payloads.
- Added an integration-style test to simulate an external provider sending updates and asserting the final merged group state.

Root cause

The merge function omitted metadata fields (or treated them incorrectly) when applying updates from external providers. As a result, updates to a group's metadata were not applied to the persisted group object.

Behavior after this change

- Metadata updates from external sources are merged into the existing group metadata.
- Existing metadata keys are preserved unless overwritten by the external update.
- New metadata keys from the external source are added.
- Explicit removal behavior is handled as defined by the merge contract (null behaves consistently per tests).

Testing & Verification

1. Unit tests added — run test suite to verify.
2. Manual verification steps:
   - Create a group with metadata { "a": "1", "b": "2" }.
