Fixes #12000 — Correctly parse arXiv identifiers when importing PDFs that contain an arXiv id.

Summary
- Resolves a bug where arXiv identifiers embedded in PDF filenames, metadata, or URLs were not recognized or were parsed incorrectly during import.

What I changed
- Implemented robust arXiv id extraction logic to handle common formats:
  - New-style ids: 1234.5678 and with version suffixes (1234.5678v2)
  - With "arXiv:" prefix (arXiv:1234.5678v2)
  - Old-style ids (hep-th/9901001 and variants)
  - Full arXiv URLs (https://arxiv.org/abs/1234.5678v2)
- Updated the PDF import flow to attempt arXiv id extraction from filename, embedded metadata, and any found URLs before falling back to manual entry.
- Normalizes parsed ids to a canonical form (e.g. 1234.5678v2 or hep-th/9901001) for storage.
- Added unit tests covering all supported patterns and several edge cases (missing prefix, uppercase/lowercase, stray whitespace).

Files changed (high level)
- src/import/arxiv_parser.py — new/updated parsing logic and normalization
- src/import/pdf_importer.py — integration to use parser during PDF import
- tests/test_arxiv_parser.py — unit tests for parser
- tests/test_pdf_importer.py — integration tests for import flow

How to verify
1. Run test suite: tests now include cases for all supported arXiv id formats.
2. Manually import sample PDFs with filenames or metadata containing:
   - "paper-1234.5678.pdf" -> arXiv id should be 1234.5678
   - "arXiv:hep-th/9901001.pdf" -> arXiv id should be hep-th/9901001
   - A PDF with URL https://arxiv.org/abs/1234.5678v3 in metadata -> arXiv id should be 1234.5678v3

Notes
- This change is backward-compatible: if no arXiv id is found, import behavior is unchanged.
- No database migrations required.

Summary
- Adds a new ottobib fetcher that retrieves bibliographic entries from ottobib.org by ISBN and returns BibTeX (and parsed metadata).

What this PR does
- New module: ottobib fetcher implementation (src/fetchers/ottobib_fetcher.*)
- Public API: OttobibFetcher.fetch(isbn) (returns BibTeX string and normalized metadata object)

- Error handling: clear errors for invalid identifiers, network failures, and empty responses
- Tests: unit tests with mocked HTTP responses and an integration test covering a real fetch
- Docs: usage examples and brief docs added (docs/fetchers/ottobib.md)

- Input: ISBN (10 or 13), single or in a small batch depending on caller support
- Output: BibTeX string and parsed metadata; callers may choose which to use
- Robustness: handles common edge cases (invalid ISBN, 404/no results, transient network errors)

Compatibility and migration
- No breaking changes to existing fetcher APIs
- New component is opt-in and can be used by registering the fetcher or calling OttobibFetcher directly

Testing
- Run the test suite (pytest) to execute the new unit and integration tests

Future work
- Add bulk-fetch optimization and more resilient rate-limit handling
- Add support for other identifier types if needed

Add global search across libraries and show library context in results

This PR implements a global search feature across all open libraries and improves how search results are presented and interacted with.

Key changes
- Add GlobalSearchBar to trigger searches across all open libraries from the main UI.
- Implement GlobalSearchResultDialog to display search results in a dedicated dialog with actions such as navigate to entry, open containing library, and copy citation keys.
- Add LibraryColumn to the main table view model so search results and table rows can show which library an entry belongs to.

Behavior and UX
- Searches are executed across all open databases and results include the library name in a dedicated column.
- Results dialog supports keyboard navigation and double-click to open or focus the entry in its library.
- Long-running searches are run asynchronously and can be cancelled (progress feedback shown in the UI).

Compatibility and testing
- Existing workflows for single-library searches remain unchanged.
- Tested navigating from results to entries, opening libraries, and copying citation keys.

Notes
- The changes are focused on UI and model plumbing; no changes to file formats were made.

Summary

This PR updates and reorganizes documentation related to remote storage and synchronization, and makes small site/config and dictionary updates to support the new/updated pages.

What changed

- docs/code-howtos/remote-storage.md: Reworked the main remote storage how-to page to act as an overview and entry point for specific backends.
- docs/code-howtos/remote-storage-jabdrive.md: Added a new how-to describing the JabDrive remote storage backend (usage, setup and troubleshooting steps).
- docs/code-howtos/remote-storage-sql.md: Added a new how-to for the SQL-based remote storage backend (configuration, schema notes and best practices).
- docs/decisions/0027-synchronization.md: Updated the ADR about synchronization to clarify behavior/assumptions and to reflect current design decisions.
- docs/_config.yml: Updated site configuration so the new/updated documentation pages are included in the generated site (navigation/order/metadata adjustments).
- .vscode/ltex.dictionary.en-US.txt: Added domain-specific terms to the ltex dictionary to avoid false positives from the spellchecker while authoring docs.

Why

These changes improve discoverability and usability of remote storage documentation by splitting backend-specific guidance into dedicated how-tos and by clarifying synchronization design in the ADR. The site config and dictionary changes support the new content and make editorial work smoother.

Notes for reviewers / testing

- Review the new how-to pages for technical accuracy and completeness for each backend (JabDrive and SQL).
- Verify the ADR changes represent the intended synchronization behavior and constraints.
- Build the docs site locally (Jekyll/MkDocs as used in this repo) to confirm pages are included in navigation and that links render correctly.
- Spellcheck/linguistic reviewers: the updated ltex dictionary prevents incorrect suggestions for the included terms.

No runtime/application code was changed; this is documentation-only.

Recommended reviewers: docs maintainers, synchronization/remote-storage owners.

text:
Add comprehensive unit tests for BibtexParser (BibtexParserTest.java).

This test suite exercises parsing behavior across many realistic and edge cases, ensuring correct interpretation of BibTeX input and ParserResult handling. Key areas covered:

- Basic parsing: fromString, singleFromString, and parse produce expected BibEntry objects and types, cite keys, and field values.
- Whitespace and formatting: entries with leading/trailing whitespace, newlines, spaces between tokens, parentheses instead of braces, and uppercase keywords are parsed correctly.
- Field formats: values in braces, in quotes, numeric values without delimiters, concatenated values (including date concatenation), and fields with escaped braces or quotes are handled as expected.
- Special characters: bibtex keys with special characters and entries with unknown or very long types map to UnknownEntryType with normalized names.
- Combining repeated fields: multiple author/editor fields are concatenated into a single value in the expected format.
- Strings, preambles, and comments: @string and @preamble are recognized (including concatenation); comments and text outside entries are ignored; duplicate strings warn and only keep one.
- File field handling: ensures multiple spaces in file field are preserved while other whitespace normalization (newlines/tabs -> single space) occurs in general fields.
- Encoding/header handling: header lines with encoding are ignored and result.getEncoding() is null.
- Robustness and warnings: duplicate bibtex keys are detected; missing cite keys and unmatched bracket cases produce warnings and appropriate behavior (ignored or partial results as expected).
- Big numbers: very large numeric field values are parsed as strings and preserved.
- Accents: accented characters in fields are preserved.

Notes:
- Several tests are annotated @Ignore for known/unstable cases (e.g., keywords concatenation, certain bracket mismatch behaviors, file-field tab/newline normalization, month field edge-case). These reflect currently accepted deviations or unresolved issues.
- A test asserts BibtexParser constructor throws NPE when initialized with null.

Overall, these tests significantly increase coverage of parser edge cases and help guard against regressions in BibTeX parsing behavior.

Add background ID-fetch action and improve fetch-by-ID UI/workflow

This PR introduces a dedicated GenerateEntryFromIdAction that performs identifier-based lookups in a background task (BackgroundTask + TaskExecutor) and improves the user interaction and error handling when importing entries by ID.

Key changes
- New GenerateEntryFromIdAction:
  - Executes ID-based fetches in a BackgroundTask (off the UI thread) and reports progress via the task UI.
  - On success, imports the fetched BibEntry using ImportHandler.importEntryWithDuplicateCheck.
  - On failure shows a localized message explaining the likely cause (client vs. server) and offers to add a new entry manually.
  - Ensures the entry-from-ID PopOver is hidden after the operation.
- EntryTypeViewModel improvements:
  - Manages an internal FetcherWorker Task for ID searches and exposes searching/searchSuccessful properties and validation for the ID field.
  - Stores the last selected fetcher in preferences and provides a method to stop an ongoing fetch (cancel the Task when running).
  - On successful fetch imports the result via ImportHandler (with duplicate checking) or, if nothing found, prompts the user to add an entry manually.
  - Resets worker state and focus flags after operations, and shows appropriate dialogs for client/server errors.
- Localization:
  - Uses existing localized messages (e.g. "Failed to import by ID", "Empty search ID") for consistent user-facing text.

Why
- Running fetches on the background thread keeps the UI responsive and provides a unified user experience for import-by-ID flows.
- Centralizing import logic via ImportHandler with duplicate checking avoids duplicated code and ensures consistent behavior.
- Better error handling and user prompts make it clearer to users what went wrong and offer an immediate fallback (add entry manually).

Notes
- GenerateEntryFromIdAction leverages TaskExecutor / BackgroundTask, while EntryTypeViewModel currently uses an internal Task subclass. Future work could harmonize both approaches (e.g. using BackgroundTask/TaskExecutor everywhere) for consistency.

Summary

Refine the "File exists" warning dialog when renaming linked files to provide clearer choices and reduce accidental overwrites.

What this PR does

- Replaces the simple yes/no overwrite confirmation with a richer dialog offering four options: Replace, Keep both, Provide alternative file name, and Cancel.
- When Keep both is chosen, a non-conflicting filename is suggested (using FileNameUniqueness.getNonOverWritingFileName) and shown as a tooltip on the Keep both button so users see what the new filename will be.
- Provide alternative file name opens the existing name prompt flow so users can enter a custom name.
- Improve dialog title and content for clarity and add corresponding English localization entries.
- Add a helper DialogService API to show custom dialogs where specific tooltips can be attached to buttons, and implement it in JabRefDialogService.

Implementation notes

- LinkedFileViewModel.performRenameWithConflictCheck now: checks for an existing file, computes a suggested non-conflicting filename, builds ButtonType options (Replace, Keep both, Provide alternative, Cancel), builds a map of tooltips (shows the suggested filename for Keep both), and calls dialogService.showCustomButtonDialogWithTooltipsAndWait to present the options. The result is handled accordingly (overwrite, use suggested name, ask for alternative, or cancel).
- DialogService interface: adds showCustomButtonDialogWithTooltipsAndWait(Alert.AlertType, String title, String content, Map<ButtonType,String> tooltips, ButtonType... buttonTypes).
- JabRefDialogService: implements the new API, creating a dialog, setting content, registering tooltips on the dialog buttons (using Platform.runLater to attach them), and returning the pressed ButtonType.
- Error handling: rename IO errors are reported with an error dialog as before.

Files changed

- CHANGELOG.md: user-facing changelog entry describing the improved File exists warning.
- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/DialogService.java: added new API method to allow tooltips on custom dialog buttons.
- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefDialogService.java: implemented the new API and the tooltip attachment.
- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/LinkedFileViewModel.java: use the new dialog to present Replace / Keep both / Provide alternative / Cancel and apply suggested unique filenames.
- jablib/src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties: added new localization keys used in the dialog.

Notes

- This implements the behavior requested in issue #12565 (Refine file exists warning).
- Manually tested in running JabRef; screenshots showing the new buttons and the tooltip are attached in the PR.
- No automated tests were added in this PR.

Closes: #12565

Fixes #8747 — Prevent uncaught exception when editing date fields (e.g. in biblatex library mode).

What I changed
- Wire validation into the DateEditor: DateEditor now receives PreferencesService and configures EditorValidator to show validation status instead of causing an uncaught exception.

  - Handle null/blank input safely.
  - Catch DateTimeParseException and fall back to Date.parse(...).map(Date::toTemporalAccessor) so legacy date formats are accepted.

- Minor cleanup: use diamond operator in DateEditorViewModel StringConverter.
- Add CHANGELOG entry describing the fix.

Why
Editing the date field could trigger an uncaught exception in certain modes/inputs. The changes ensure input parsing is tolerant, validation is hooked up to the editor, and invalid input does not crash the UI. This also enables negative dates in the chooser (requested behavior).

Notes
- Manual testing performed and screenshot added in the original issue/PR description.
- Follow-up to #9314.

text:
Fix export-to-clipboard selection for custom exporters with uppercase extensions (#6285)

What I changed
- Fix: custom exports with uppercase file extensions can now be selected in "Copy -> Export to Clipboard". This resolves #6285 and is reflected in CHANGELOG.md.
- Exporter detection: ExportToClipboardAction now matches exporters by FileType (using StandardFileType/UnknownFileType) instead of comparing raw extension strings. This allows case-insensitive matching of extensions.
- StandardFileType improvements:
  - Added HTML alias (htm) and clarified extension normalization (lowercase without dot).
  - Replaced the old factory method with fromExtensions(...) which attempts to map provided extensions to a known StandardFileType and otherwise returns an UnknownFileType.
- New UnknownFileType: represents file types not present in StandardFileType, normalizes and lowercases extensions, and implements equals/hashCode for reliable comparisons.
- Dependency injection & robustness for clipboard export:
  - ExportToClipboardAction now receives ExporterFactory, ClipBoardManager and TaskExecutor (instead of using Globals directly).
  - Call sites were updated (JabRefFrame, RightClickMenu).
  - Background task execution now uses the injected TaskExecutor and shows/logs errors on failure.
  - Clipboard operations use the injected ClipBoardManager.
- Minor cleanup/bugfixes:
  - TemplateExporter now uses StandardFileType.fromExtensions(...) when creating exporters from an extension string.
  - Removed a noisy rethrow in export logic and improved error logging.
  - Added @Override annotation to CopyCitationAction.execute().

Migration notes
- ExportToClipboardAction constructors changed and now require ExporterFactory, ClipBoardManager and TaskExecutor. Call sites must provide these (already updated in this PR).

Why this matters
- Users with export formats that use uppercase file extensions (e.g. .XML/.RTF) can now export to the clipboard without issues.
- The FileType normalization and UnknownFileType make exporter detection more robust and case-insensitive.
- Error handling and DI improvements make the clipboard export flow more testable and reliable.

Summary

This PR improves handling of regular expressions in the global search bar. It adds validation for the regular expression mode, provides visual feedback when the entered regex is invalid, and prevents running searches with invalid regex patterns.

What I changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/search/GlobalSearchBar.java
  - Added a regex validator (FunctionBasedValidator) bound to the search field.
  - Added visualization using ControlsFxVisualizer with an IconValidationDecorator to show an error icon when the regex is invalid.
  - Before performing a search, the code now checks the validator status and displays "Invalid regular expression" in the results area instead of performing the search when the regex is invalid.

- src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/Base.css

Why

Previously, enabling regular expression mode in the global search allowed users to enter invalid regex patterns which could lead to confusing results or errors. With this change, invalid regex input is detected early, the user gets clear visual feedback and a message, and the search is not executed until the expression is valid.

Related issue

- Fixes #5349

Notes

- Manually tested in a running JabRef build.
- No automated tests were added in this PR.
- A small UI/CSS adjustment was included for label padding in the search field.

text:
Fix downloading of arXiv PDFs and improve URL download robustness

This PR addresses an issue where arXiv imports could download HTML pages instead of the actual PDF and hardens the URL download logic. Key changes include:

- Fixes
  - Fixed importing from arXiv where HTML (landing page) was downloaded instead of the fulltext PDF (CHANGES updated).

- URLDownload improvements
  - getMimeType() now returns Optional<String> and tries to follow redirects for HEAD requests (manually follows Location headers up to MAX_RETRIES) to determine the real content type (prevents misdetecting original URLs that redirect to PDFs).
  - Falls back to GET and to URLConnection when HEAD fails; returns Optional.empty() if no content type is discovered.
  - Introduced MAX_RETRIES constant and a static Unirest configuration block (followRedirects, enableCookieManagement, default User-Agent).
  - canBeReached() simplified to use a HEAD request status check.
  - isMimeType() updated to use the Optional result.
  - openConnection(): ensure HttpURLConnection is disconnected before recursion, and simplify HTTP error handling to distinguish client vs. server errors correctly.
  - Minor typo fix in Javadoc.

- API impact
  - getMimeType() signature changed from String to Optional<String>. Callers were updated accordingly (e.g. inferFileTypeFromMimeType and isMimeType).

- Tests and dependencies
  - Added wiremock-standalone as a testImplementation dependency and updated tests to use WireMock for deterministic HTTP responses.
  - Updated tests to handle Optional<String> for MIME type and added a redirectWorks integration test that verifies redirects and PDF downloads.
  - Updated DownloadLinkedFileAction tests to use WireMock for HTML content scenarios and improved temp dir usage and cleanup (start/stop WireMock server in setup/teardown).

- Misc
  - Small refactors: use Optional.flatMap in inferFileTypeFromMimeType, code cleanups and imports adjustments.

This change improves reliability when downloading files from providers that return intermediate redirects (like arXiv) and adds tests to prevent regressions.

Notes:
- Resolves issue #2581
- Instructions to test: run the fetcher with sample ISBNs and verify that ebook.de and chimbori.com are tried first; when they fail or return no metadata, ottobib is requested and parsed.

Summary:
Adds automatic cleanup for leftover embedded PostgreSQL processes started by JabRef and ensures the embedded Postgres is shut down on application exit. Also updates the changelog and adds the OSHI dependency used to inspect running processes.

What this PR changes:
- Adds PostgreProcessCleaner (jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/search/PostgreProcessCleaner.java): scans the temp directory for Postgres metadata files, checks whether the originating Java process is still alive, and if not attempts to find and kill the leftover Postgres process (using OSHI to inspect processes and by PID) and removes metadata files.
- Adds PostgresMetadataWriter (jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/search/PostgresMetadataWriter.java): writes metadata about started embedded Postgres instances to a temp JSON file (filename pattern: jabref-postgres-info-<javaPid>.json) containing javaPid, postgresPort, startedBy and startedAt.
- Calls PostgresProcessCleaner.getInstance().checkAndCleanupOldInstances() early in Launcher.main to remove stale Postgres instances from previous crashes
- Registers a shutdown hook in Launcher.main to call postgreServer.shutdown() so the embedded Postgres is stopped on normal shutdown
- Calls PostgresMetadataWriter.write(port) when PostgreServer successfully starts so cleanup data is available
- Adds Directories.getTmpDirectory() helper used by PostgresMetadataWriter
- Adds OSHI dependency (com.github.oshi:oshi-core:6.8.1) and requires com.github.oshi in module-info to allow process inspection
- Updates CHANGELOG.md with a note about fixing leftover Postgres processes after crashes (#12927)

Implementation details / notes for reviewers:
- Metadata files are written into the OS temp directory using the name prefix jabref-postgres-info- and the current Java PID as suffix.
- The cleaner checks each metadata file: if the recorded javaPid is not alive, it checks whether the recorded Postgres port is open and tries to determine the Postgres process PID by searching process command lines for "postgres" and the port number (via OSHI). If found and alive, the process is destroyed and the metadata file deleted.
- A short wait (1500 ms) is used after sending destroy to allow Postgres to exit.
- OSHI is used to enumerate OS processes. The module-info and build files were updated accordingly.

Changelog:
- CHANGELOG.md notes that we fixed an issue where Postgres processes remain running after JabRef crashes or is forcefully terminated (#12927).

Why:
This prevents orphaned embedded Postgres instances from lingering after JabRef crashes or is killed, which otherwise could consume resources and block ports on subsequent launches.

Compatibility / follow-ups:
- OSHI is already added as a runtime dependency; please verify packaging and module usage for all target platforms.
- The process-matching logic uses simple substring matching on the command line; if necessary, we can make this more robust per-platform later.

text:
Summary

This PR implements a targeted workaround for intermittent SSL errors that occur when fetching DOI metadata (e.g., from CrossRef/DataCite). The error manifested as TLS/SSL verification failures which caused DOI lookups to fail and downstream workflows to break.

What I changed

- Added a robust DOI fetcher that: 
  - retries transient network/ssl errors with exponential backoff,
  - falls back to a configurable, temporary relaxed TLS verification mode only as a last resort,
  - logs detailed diagnostic information when an SSL verification failure occurs.
- Introduced a configuration flag (DOI_VERIFY_SSL=true by default) to control TLS verification for DOI requests. The flag can be set via environment variable or app config.
- Added unit tests and an integration-style test (mocked DOI provider) to assert retry behavior and the fallback path.
- Documented the workaround and security implications in the README and config docs.

Why this approach

- Retries handle transient network/TLS flakiness without weakening security.
- The relaxed verification fallback is opt-in and disabled by default; it is intended as a temporary mitigation for environments with broken/misconfigured local CAs or middleboxes. It allows the service to continue functioning while a proper CA/certificate fix is implemented.
- Detailed logging makes it easier to diagnose and remove the workaround later.

Security notes

- DOI_VERIFY_SSL=false disables SSL certificate verification for DOI fetches and should only be used as a temporary emergency measure in trusted network environments.
- Prefer to fix the underlying CA/certificate issues and re-enable verification as soon as possible.

Testing

- Unit tests cover retry/backoff logic and correct behavior of the verification flag.
- A mocked integration test simulates SSL verification failures to ensure the fallback activates when configured.

Deployment / Rollout

- Default behavior is unchanged (verification enabled).
- If you need to enable the workaround in production, set DOI_VERIFY_SSL=false or update the config, and monitor logs for SSL diagnostics to track the root cause.

If you want, I can split the retry logic and the verification-fallback into separate PRs to keep scope smaller.

Fix AuthorList parsing for comma-separated names and add tests

- Bugfix: Correctly handle comma-separated author lists in AuthorListParser. The parsing logic was refactored to better distinguish between:
  - multiple commas (e.g. entries separated by commas, possibly with affixes like "Jr"), and
  - the ambiguous single-comma case (e.g. distinguishing "Lastname, Firstname" from "Firstname Lastname, Firstname2 Lastname2"). For the single-comma case we now count spaces and treat strings with three spaces as two separate authors (replacing ", " with " AND "). This fixes cases where authors were incorrectly collapsed into a single author.
- Reorganized conditional checks to centralize the comma-count handling and preserve existing rules for "and", braces and semicolons.
- Tests: Expanded and split tests for author parsing into separate parameterized suites for single-author and multiple-author scenarios (AuthorListParserTest). Added concrete test cases that cover name affixes and complex multi-author strings (including examples like "Ali Babar, M., Dingsøyr, T., Lago, P., van der Vliet, H.").
- Normalization tests: Converted a NormalizeNamesFormatterTest case to a parameterized test and added an extra scenario (Hans-Joachim / Leymann) to improve coverage.
- Changelog: Added an entry noting a related fix (ISBN fetcher returning two authors expected).

These changes improve robustness of author name parsing and increase test coverage to prevent regressions.

What this does
- Makes the font size used in several JavaFX parts of the UI configurable via the existing 'Menu and label font size' preference.

  - Groups tree (group panel)
- Adds a small mapping helper in JabRefPreferences.getFontSizeFX() that subtracts 3 from the menu/font preference to account for JavaFX’s default font baseline vs Swing.
- Moves a private helper (getSourceString) in SourceTab (no behavior change).
- Updates CHANGELOG.md to mention the change.

text:
Refactor and centralize action handling; update UI parts to use the new Actions API

What this PR does
- Introduces/uses a centralized Actions construct to manage action identifiers and common action wiring.
- Updates BasePanel and JabRefFrame to use the new Actions API instead of ad-hoc action strings, reducing duplication and improving consistency when creating menus, toolbars and wiring event handlers.
- Adapts GroupsPrefsTab to the updated action wiring and preferences usage so group-related preferences and commands are handled correctly.
- Improves null-safety and lifecycle handling when panels and frames are created/destroyed, preventing potential NPEs when actions are invoked while the GUI is being torn down.

Why this change
- Centralizing action definitions makes it easier to maintain and reuse actions across different parts of the GUI (main window, panels, preference tabs).
- This reduces subtle bugs caused by inconsistent action identifiers and duplicate wiring.
- The changes also make it straightforward to add/rename actions and ensure that all callers are updated in a single place.

Files changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/actions/Actions.java: new/updated central action definitions and helper methods for creating/binding actions.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/BasePanel.java: updated to use Actions and improved lifecycle handling when registering/unregistering actions.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefFrame.java: updated menus/toolbar to use centralized Actions and improved null-safety during frame teardown.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preftabs/GroupsPrefsTab.java: adapted to the new action API and fixed preference read/write behavior.

Testing
- Manual testing of menus, toolbar buttons and groups preference tab was performed to verify actions are correctly created and invoked, and no regressions occur when opening/closing databases or the main window.

Notes
- No behavioral changes to existing user-facing commands are intended; this is primarily a refactor to simplify action management and make the codebase more maintainable.

text:
Paste & copy linked PDF files across libraries

- Implemented copying of linked PDF files when pasting entries that were copied from another library. When entries are copied (Copy/Cut) the source BibDatabaseContext is stored and used during paste to locate and copy PDF files referenced by the pasted entries from the source library's default file directory into the current library's default file directory. After copying the files, the entries are imported with duplicate checking.

Details
- LibraryTab.copyEntry() now saves the source BibDatabaseContext (copiedBibDatabaseContext) so paste can determine the original file directory.
- LibraryTab.pasteEntry(): after parsing clipboard contents and creating entriesToAdd, the code attempts to find PDF files referenced by each entry in the source database's default file directory. If a source PDF is found, it is copied into the current library's default file directory (replacing existing files). Missing source directories or files are logged and warned via logger.
- The importHandler.importEntriesWithDuplicateCheck(...) is called after copying to add the entries to the current database.

Robustness & error handling
- If the source library has no configured default file directory, a warning is logged and the paste aborts (no entries are imported).
- Individual file copy failures are caught and logged (IOException), but do not abort importing of other files/entries.

Related classes
- New/updated copy-to-folder flow in gui.copyfiles: CopyFilesAction, CopyFilesTask and CopyFilesDialogView handle the "Copy linked files to folder..." action, perform the copy work in a background Task and present a results dialog (with a generated .log file). CopyFilesTask writes a timestamped log and collects per-file results for user feedback.

Notes/limitations
- Only linked files with file type "pdf" are considered during the paste-entry copy step.
- The paste operation requires the source library to have a configured default file directory in its metadata. If not present, files are not copied and a warning is emitted.
- Files are copied with StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING (existing files in the destination will be overwritten).

This change improves portability when moving entries between libraries by attempting to automatically transfer associated PDFs, reducing manual file management after pasting entries.

text:
This pull request contains a large set of UI, preferences and behavior improvements and fixes across the application. Highlights:

- UI / Main Window
  - Improved main window behavior and layout: new toolbar structure, task progress indicator (clickable popover showing background tasks), and improved tab handling.
  - Drag & drop: visual "Open files..." drop indicator tab and full drag-and-drop support for opening/importing .bib files.
  - Keyboard handling: centralised key binding handling for library navigation, entry creation shortcuts and search focus.
  - Telemetry prompt: show a delayed non-intrusive prompt asking users if they want to share anonymous usage statistics.

- Main table and interactions
  - MainTable: improved keyboard navigation (type-to-search on sorted column), selection helpers (select first/last), refined drag-and-drop for files (import, link, move, copy depending on drop location and modifier), and better context menu integration.
  - RightClickMenu: refactored creation of the right-click menu and copy submenus, including citation/preview-specific copy items.

- Special fields and keywords
  - Added SpecialFieldsPreferences abstraction and helper method isKeywordSyncEnabled(), and used it across keyword and special-field flows.
  - ManageKeywordsViewModel: improved logic for listing, adding/removing keywords across selected entries and synchronizing with special fields when enabled.
  - SpecialFieldAction / SpecialFieldViewModel: encapsulate special-field changes, undo support and user notifications.

- Preferences & Settings
  - JabRefPreferences / PreferencesService: many getters/setters and internal caching updated to support newly added preferences (main table columns, preview settings, special fields, auto-linking, etc.).
  - TableTabViewModel: improved preferences UI backing model for the main table columns, special fields columns, extra file columns, name format and validation.
  - New methods for storing/loading custom exporters, entry types, preview cycles and other persisted settings.

- Import / Parsing
  - ParserResult: improved handling of to-open-in-tab flag, path/file handling and migration tracking.
  - Import flows: ImportCleanup use in paste/import and improved import inspection for adding entries to open tabs.

- Misc fixes and polish
  - Various fixes referenced by the changelog: task progress display, title/tab handling, autosave/backup wiring, better preview & name-format handling, and numerous stability and UX improvements.

This PR brings many smaller behavioral improvements and refactorings to better separate preferences logic from UI, improve drag & drop and keyboard UX, and add a clearer and more robust special-fields/keyword synchronization model.

text:
Summary

- Introduce Path-based database path access and improve backup/autosave handling.

What I changed

1) Model: BibDatabaseContext
- Added getDatabasePath() which returns Optional<Path> for the database file location.
- Deprecated getDatabaseFile() in favor of the Path-based API (keeps backward compatibility but encourages the new API).
- Kept existing file-directory resolution logic (getFileDirectory) but made database-path handling consistent with the new Path API.

2) BackupManager
- Migrate backup logic to use Path throughout (determineBackupPath now uses bibDatabaseContext.getDatabasePath()).
- getBackupPath(Path) returns a .sav backup Path derived from the original Path.
- performBackup/save/restore/delete now operate on Path and use NIO (Files, StandardCopyOption).
- Use a single-threaded ThreadPoolExecutor with an ArrayBlockingQueue(1) to serialize backups and reject redundant concurrent backup submissions (prevents overload when many change events are fired).
- Track running BackupManager instances and provide start(BibDatabaseContext)/shutdown(BibDatabaseContext) helpers to manage lifecycle and to delete backup files when a database is closed normally.
- Added checkForBackupFile and restoreBackup helpers.
- Improved logging and error handling around IO / save failures.

3) UI / Frame changes (JabRefFrame)
- Added getBasePanelList() and helper methods to make it easier to iterate all open BasePanels.
- Added addTab(BibDatabaseContext, boolean) convenience overload that constructs a BasePanel and registers autosave/backup when a tab is opened.
- Updated tab title handling and unique path generation by using Path-aware collection of database file paths (collectDatabaseFilePaths / getUniquePathParts / updateAllTabTitles).
- Minor housekeeping: centralize enabling/disabling actions and improved startup/teardown interactions for autosave and backup managers (Hooks to start/stop BackupManager/AutosaveManager when tabs are opened/closed).

Why

- Using Path instead of File for database paths modernizes the API and avoids repeated File->Path conversions in backup and file utilities.
- The executor/queue change prevents heavy backup load when many database-change events fire in rapid succession; redundant backup tasks are rejected/logged instead of piling up.
- Centralized lifecycle management (start/shutdown and runningInstances tracking) ensures backup files are cleaned up when a database is closed normally and reduces the chance of leftover .sav files.
- Convenience methods in JabRefFrame simplify tab management and make it easier to wire autosave/backup to the UI lifecycle.

Notes / Compatibility

- getDatabaseFile() still exists but is marked @Deprecated; existing code will continue to work. New code should prefer getDatabasePath().
- Backup files now use Path-based operations; behavior of .sav backups remains unchanged (extension and basic semantics preserved).

If you want me to split this into smaller commits (API change, BackupManager refactor, UI changes) or add unit tests for backup path handling and backup-task rejection, I can prepare that.

This PR enhances the EntryEditor with several usability improvements and new behaviors:

- Add drag & drop support for files onto the entry editor. Dropped files are processed according to the drop TransferMode: COPY (copy to file dir and attach), MOVE (move & rename into file dir and attach), or LINK (add a link). - Rework tab management: createTabs centralizes all built-in tabs (preview, required/optional/other fields, comments, user-defined tabs, multiple provider tabs, source tab, LaTeX citations, fulltext search results). adaptVisibleTabs updates visible tabs without reordering artifacts and respects user-configured tabs and the "show preview as extra tab" preference. The source tab can be shown by default via preferences.
- Add and wire up editor-specific key bindings (panel navigation, entry navigation, help, unfocus/close editor) via KeyBindingRepository.
- Add small utility methods and improvements: setFocusToField (selects the tab that contains a field and focuses it), nextPreviewStyle/previousPreviewStyle for cycling preview styles, and live updates of the type label when the entry type changes.

These changes improve entry editing workflows (file attachment, fetching metadata, navigation and preview handling) and make the editor more responsive to user preferences.

Fix charset detection and handling for UTF-16 and other mismatches

Fixes: #8895, #8870

What this PR does
- Fixes charset detection logic in Importer: stop incorrectly treating certain detected charsets as the default and improve handling of ASCII detection.
- Make reader creation more robust: use a CharsetDecoder that replaces malformed input so files that declare the wrong encoding (e.g., declare UTF-8 but are actually Windows-1252) do not fail to be read — undecodable bytes are replaced with the replacement character instead of throwing.
- Adjusted Importer.getReader(InputStream) signature (no longer throws IOException) and updated related call sites.
- Adds tests and test resources for UTF-16 (with and without header) and for a case where the declared encoding mismatches the actual bytes (Windows-1252 bytes with a UTF-8 header).
- Update CHANGELOG to document behavior where unreadable characters get replaced and how to find them via Integrity Check.

Files changed (high level)
- Core behavior: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/Importer.java, src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/BibtexImporter.java
- Tests: src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/BibtexImporterTest.java and new test resource src/test/resources/.../encoding-windows-1252-but-utf-8-declared--decoding-fails.bib
- Chore: CHANGELOG.md, build.gradle, external-libraries.md, and bundled ICU jars in lib/

Notes
- This approach replaces unreadable characters (no user-facing warning currently). The replacement behavior is intentional to allow import even when the declared encoding is wrong; users can find suspicious replacement characters using the Integrity Check.
- Build/dependency updates: JavaFX bumped to 18.0.1 and several libraries updated; icu4j-charset removed in favor of the bundled/managed ICU fork (lib/icu4j.jar and source).
- The change still needs verification on Windows as noted in the original issue.

Tests
- Added parametric tests for UTF-16 BE (with/without header) to assert both content and metadata (encoding) are detected correctly.
- Added a test demonstrating that a wrong declared encoding leads to replacement characters instead of a decoding failure.

text:
This PR contains a set of improvements, bug fixes and small feature additions across multiple modules. The changes focus on developer tooling, robustness of import/parsing logic, formatting utilities, and networking reliability.

Main highlights:

- Developer tooling (new jbang launchers and helpers)
  - Added utilities for cloning and checking out PRs and launching JabRef-related tools: .jbang/CheckoutPR.java, .jbang/CloneJabRef.java, .jbang/JabKitLauncher.java, .jbang/JabLsLauncher.java, .jbang/JabSrvLauncher.java. These simplify local development and debugging of services.

- AI summarization
  - jablib/.../GenerateSummaryTask.java: improved error handling and resilience for the summarization task, with better handling of null/missing fields and clearer failure propagation.

- BibTeX and import robustness
  - jablib/.../BibtexParser.java: hardened parsing for malformed or unusual BibTeX input (better handling of line continuations, comments and edge cases), reducing silent parsing failures.
  - jablib/.../INSPIREBibtexFilterReader.java: improved reader for INSPIRE-exported BibTeX, normalising fields and types more reliably.
  - jablib/.../PdfContentImporter.java: improved PDF text extraction and metadata fallback handling to increase success rate for importing data from PDFs.
  - jablib/.../URLDownload.java: added configurable timeouts, stronger error handling and retry logic for more reliable downloads (including SSL/proxy scenarios).

- Formatting and name handling
  - jablib/.../UnprotectTermsFormatter.java: fixed logic around unprotecting terms so braces are handled correctly (including nested cases) and no longer produce malformed output.
  - jablib/.../NameFormatter.java: better handling of international names and diacritics, improving formatting consistency across name styles.

- Citation key and bibliography utilities
  - jablib/.../CitationKeyGenerator.java: improved uniqueness and collision-avoidance logic, better sanitisation of generated keys and handling of missing fields.
  - jablib/.../BstFunctions.java: bug fixes and small improvements to BibTeX style functions used during layout/formatting.

- Linked file handling
  - jablib/.../LinkedFileHandler.java: improved path resolution for linked files (relative vs absolute), more robust handling of remote/portable links and fixes to prevent NPEs when metadata is incomplete.

Other notes:
- Most changes emphasize defensive coding, clearer error messages and fewer silent failures.
- No breaking API changes are intended; behaviour is tightened to be more robust and predictable.

This PR should reduce import/parsing failures, improve key generation and formatting correctness, and provide a better developer experience with the added jbang tools.

Add ClipBoardManager to centralize clipboard handling and X11 primary-selection support.

- Add ClipBoardManager that encapsulates both JavaFX system clipboard and the AWT/X11 primary selection clipboard (primary). The default constructor wires real system instances; an alternate constructor accepts Clipboard, AWT Clipboard and ImportFormatReader for easier testing and dependency injection.
- Provide addX11Support(TextInputControl) to enable primary-selection behavior in text inputs: selected text is copied to the primary selection and middle-click pastes from primary.
- Implement getContents() and getContentsPrimary() with fallbacks and error logging; setContent variants for plain text, HTML, and List<BibEntry>.
- When placing BibEntry lists onto the clipboard, serialize using BibEntryWriter (with LatexFieldFormatter) and store under DragAndDropDataFormats.ENTRIES and as a string so other consumers can use it.
- Implement extractData() that retrieves entries from the custom ENTRIES data format or handles string data by: detecting DOIs and fetching entries via DoiFetcher, trying to parse BibTeX with BibtexParser, or delegating to ImportFormatReader.importUnknownFormat() as a fallback.
- Add robust error handling and logging for parse/fetch/import failures and character-encoding safe parsing of byte streams.

This change centralizes clipboard logic, adds X11 primary selection support, improves testability, and provides rich clipboard handling for BibTeX entries and DOIs.

This PR fixes issue #2336 by restoring correct shutdown behavior. Previously the application could hang or leave background workers running when a shutdown was initiated. That prevented clean restarts and caused resources to remain locked.

- Corrected the shutdown sequence to ensure services transition through the proper states before termination.
- Fixed a race condition around the shutdown flag/state check by adding synchronization and explicit state transitions.

- Improved signal handling so external termination signals (SIGINT/SIGTERM) trigger the same clean shutdown path.
- Added unit and integration tests that reproduce the original failure and assert successful graceful shutdown.

Testing & verification

1. Run the new shutdown integration test suite: it should now pass.

No API changes. This is a bugfix; no migration steps are necessary.

Notes

Summary

Refactors JabRefDialogService to simplify and harden dialog handling across the application. The change centralizes common dialog setup, improves owner/stage handling and threading behavior, and cleans up the API to reduce nullability and raw-type usage.

Motivation

Dialogs were occasionally losing focus, showed incorrect modality or caused unexpected behavior when invoked from non-JavaFX threads. The previous implementation also contained some raw types and scattered null checks which made the calling code more error-prone and harder to maintain.

What I changed

- Centralized dialog creation and configuration logic inside JabRefDialogService for consistent behavior across the app.
- Ensured dialogs are always created/shown on the JavaFX Application thread (internal helper to runLater if needed) to avoid thread-related issues.
- Improved owner/stage detection and explicitly sets the owner for new dialogs so modality and focus work reliably.
- Replaced several nullable-return patterns with Optional where appropriate to make the intent clearer for callers.
- Removed raw type usages and added type-safe generics for dialog-related methods.
- Added defensive null checks and better logging to aid debugging when dialog creation fails or when no owner stage is available.
- Kept public API stable where possible; small cleanup resulted in a couple of improved method overloads (backwards-compatible alternatives/deprecations added where necessary).

Testing

- Manually tested the most common dialog flows (preferences, import/export, warnings) to verify modality, focus and that dialogs appear on top of the main window.
- Verified no threading exceptions when invoking dialogs from background tasks.

Notes

This PR targets stability and maintainability of dialog handling and should reduce intermittent UI issues related to dialogs. If you rely on any very specific undocumented behavior from the previous implementation, please call out the case so it can be handled or a compatibility shim added.

Why this change

These changes address stability issues (crashes and NPEs) that occurred when closing or switching databases while previews were rendering, reduce memory usage caused by retained WebView resources, and improve user experience by avoiding needless re-renders and supporting external link opening.

Testing

- Manually tested switching between entries, closing databases, and opening/closing the preview pane to confirm there are no crashes or memory spikes.
- Verified that links in the preview open externally and that unchanged previews are not reloaded.

Notes

If desired I can split the thread-safety/resource-cleanup and the hyperlink/performance changes into separate commits/PRs for easier review.

Summary

Handle arXiv 301 redirect that returned an HTML page instead of the expected PDF, which caused arXiv downloads to fail (see #4913).

What I changed

- Update the arXiv download logic to properly follow HTTP redirects and verify the final Content-Type before treating the response as a PDF.
- If the response Content-Type is text/html, follow the redirect(s) and request the final PDF resource so a proper PDF is returned instead of HTML.

Why

arXiv sometimes responds with a 301 redirect which resulted in an HTML response being treated as a PDF download. By following redirects and validating the final content type we avoid attempting to process HTML as a PDF and restore correct download behavior.

Notes

- This fixes GitHub issue #4913.
- Changes were manually tested against arXiv downloads. No user-facing UI changes.

Closes #4913.

Improved detection of long DOIs within text (fixes #7256).

What I changed
- Updated the DOI extraction regex in src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/identifier/DOI.java to avoid including trailing punctuation when a DOI appears at the end of a sentence or before commas/semicolons. The suffix pattern was tightened from (?:[^\s]+) to (?:[^\s,;]+[^,;(\.\s)]) so that DOIs are not captured with trailing ",", ";" or "."/whitespace, while still allowing dots inside DOI suffixes (e.g. 10.1007/...-9.1234).
- Added/extended tests in src/test/java/org/jabref/model/entry/identifier/DOITest.java to cover DOIs followed by period, comma, semicolon and to cover long DOIs containing dots and short DOIs followed by punctuation.

Why
- Previously DOI extraction could include trailing punctuation when the DOI appeared at the end of a sentence or directly before "," or ";", producing incorrect DOI strings. The updated regex fixes these edge cases.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/identifier/DOI.java
- src/test/java/org/jabref/model/entry/identifier/DOITest.java

- New tests validate extraction for examples such as: "... doi:10.1007/s10549-018-4743-9.", "...doi:10.1007/s10549-018-4743-9,", "...doi:10.1007/s10549-018-4743-9;something" and DOIs containing trailing dot segments like "10.1007/...-9.1234".

Closes
- Fixes #7256

text: Fix AuthorListParser#parse so it correctly handles inputs with exactly two authors separated by a comma. Problem: when two authors were provided in a comma-separated form the parser would mis-split the string (treating the comma inside or between names incorrectly) and produce incorrect author entries. Change: update the parsing logic to detect the two-author comma case and split on the correct delimiter (preserving commas that are part of a single author name), and fall back to the existing logic for other cases. text:
Summary

This PR makes the "Lookup a DOI and try again." text in the Citation Relations tab a clickable hyperlink that performs a DOI lookup. When clicked, the placeholder changes to "Looking up DOI..." and the app tries to fetch an identifier via CrossRef. If a DOI is found it is written into the entry and the citation relations search is retried; if no DOI is found the user is notified and the placeholder resets. Errors during the lookup now show appropriate dialogs for client/server errors or other failures.

What I changed

- UI: Replaced the static placeholder text with a TextFlow containing a Hyperlink in CitationRelationsTab so users can click to start a DOI lookup.
- Behavior: On click, runs a background CrossRef lookup and shows "Looking up DOI..." as a placeholder. On success, sets the DOI field on the entry and restarts the relations search. If no DOI is found, shows a notification "No DOI found".
- Error handling: Added handleIdentifierFetchingError to display user-friendly dialogs for FetcherClientException and FetcherServerException and to log unexpected failures.
- Localization: Split the original single placeholder string into two separate localization keys so the label and hyperlink are localized independently.
- Changelog: Added an entry describing the enhanced Citation Relations behavior.

Files modified

- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/citationrelationtab/CitationRelationsTab.java
- jablib/src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties
- CHANGELOG.md

How to test

1. Open the entry editor for an entry without a DOI.
2. Switch to the Citation Relations tab.
3. You should see the sentence split into text + a clickable hyperlink "Lookup a DOI and try again.".
4. Click the hyperlink.
   - The placeholder should change to "Looking up DOI...".
   - If a DOI is found, it will be written to the entry and the citation relations search will be re-run and populate results.
   - If no DOI is found, a notification "No DOI found" is shown and the placeholder resets.
5. Test error behavior by simulating a fetcher client/server error (if possible) and confirm the dialogs are shown.

Notes

- The lookup uses the CrossRef fetcher and runs in a background task so the UI remains responsive.
- The change also improves diagnostic messages on failures and logs exceptions.

Closes

Closes #13234

Summary

Fixes #8747 — Prevent an uncaught exception when editing the "date" field in biblatex mode with invalid input. The change validates editor input and makes date parsing more robust so that clicking away with an invalid date no longer throws a NullPointerException.

What I changed

- Updated CHANGELOG.md to document the bugfix.
- DateEditor
  - Added PreferencesService parameter and configured EditorValidator to show validation status for the date editor.
- DateEditorViewModel
  - Broadened the catch during parsing fallback so non-DateTimeParseException parse errors also use the Date.parse fallback.
- FieldEditors
  - Pass PreferencesService into DateEditor instances (timestamp and date fields) so editor validation can be configured.
- TemporalAccessorPicker
  - Handle null TemporalAccessor in getLocalDate() to avoid NPEs.
  - Make string-to-temporal parsing resilient: only attempt parsing for non-blank strings, catch DateTimeParseException, and fall back to Date.parse(...).
  - Preserve the original editor text when the value is invalid (so invalid input is not cleared unexpectedly).

Rationale

- The bug occurred when an invalid date input was typed and the user clicked away: the UI attempted to derive a LocalDate from a null TemporalAccessor and caused an uncaught NPE. In addition, parsing fallbacks were not robust enough for various invalid inputs. Adding validation and defensive checks prevents the exception and improves UX (showing a validation icon rather than crashing).

Testing

- Manually verified in running JabRef:
  - Typing invalid input into a date field now shows the validation indicator and no exception occurs when clicking elsewhere.
  - Pressing Enter still clears input where expected.

Notes

- No automated tests added in this PR.
- The changelog entry describes the fix for end users.

Fixes: #8747

Fix RFC fetcher compatibility with draft identifiers (Fixes #7305)

Summary
- The RFC fetcher previously always prefixed identifiers with "rfc" when an RFC-like prefix was missing. This broke lookups for IETF draft identifiers that begin with "draft" (case-insensitive), producing incorrect URLs.

What I changed
- Added a DRAFT_PREFIX constant and updated getUrlForIdentifier so that the fetcher does NOT add the "rfc" prefix when the given identifier starts with "draft".
- Added unit tests covering draft behavior:
  - performSearchByIdFindsEntryWithDraftIdentifier (positive case for a draft id)
  - performSearchByIdFindsNothingWithValidDraftIdentifier (negative case)
- Updated CHANGELOG.md with a short note about the fix.

Why
- To support IETF draft identifiers (e.g. draft-fielding-http-spec) and avoid producing invalid datatracker URLs by incorrectly prepending "rfc".

Testing
- New unit tests were added and pass. The change was also manually tested against draft example IDs; screenshots were provided in the original issue.

Fixes: #7305

Add full-text PDF fetchers for SpringerLink and Wiley

What I changed
- Added SpringerLinkFetcher implementing FulltextFetcher
  - Attempts to resolve a full-text PDF for a BibEntry using its DOI
  - First tries the direct content/pdf URL pattern (https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/<doi>.pdf)
  - Falls back to fetching the article page (https://link.springer.com/article/<doi>) and heuristically searching the HTML for links ending in .pdf (href/src)
  - If a PDF URL is found and returns a PDF content-type, downloads it to a temporary file and returns a file:// URL
  - Uses timeouts, content-type checks, and logs debug/info/warn messages
  - Returns TrustLevel.PUBLISHER

- Added WileyFetcher implementing FulltextFetcher
  - Uses the Wiley TDM API to resolve a PDF for an article DOI
  - Reads TDM client token from environment variable WILEY_TDM_TOKEN (skips if not set)
  - Requests the API; if the API returns a PDF directly, download to temp and return
  - Otherwise parses JSON response with Jackson to find any text node containing ".pdf" (recursive search), follows that URL and attempts to download the PDF
  - Downloads valid PDFs to a temporary file and returns a file:// URL
  - Uses timeouts, content-type checks, logging, and returns TrustLevel.PUBLISHER

Shared/implementation details
- Both fetchers implement FulltextFetcher.findFullText(BibEntry) and throw IOException/FetcherException on errors
- Both write downloaded PDFs to temporary files and return the temporary file URL
- Helper method copyStream used to stream response bodies to disk
- Robust logging and status/content-type checks to avoid false positives
- WileyFetcher adds a dependency on Jackson for JSON parsing

Notes and considerations
- WileyFetcher requires the environment variable WILEY_TDM_TOKEN to be set for TDM API access
- Temporary files are left to the OS; callers may want to clean them up or move them into the library database as appropriate
- Heuristic HTML/JSON scanning for ".pdf" may produce false positives in edge cases; however content-type checks and download verification mitigate that

- jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/FulltextFetcher.java (interface for full-text fetchers)
- jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/fulltext/SpringerLinkFetcher.java
- jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/fulltext/WileyFetcher.java

This change provides publisher-backed full-text retrieval for Springer and Wiley content based on DOI, improving JabRef's ability to find and download PDFs automatically.

Add "Auto-Link Files" feature and integrate into UI

This PR introduces an automation feature to detect files on disk and automatically attach them as file links to bibliography entries. Changes include:

- UI integration: JabRefFrame now exposes the new action in the Tools menu (and where appropriate), enabling users to run the auto-link operation from the GUI.
- New action: AutoLinkFilesAction implements the user-facing action, handles selection context (selected entries or whole library), prompts where necessary, and runs the auto-linking task in the background with progress reporting.
- Core utility: AutoSetFileLinksUtil contains the logic for scanning configured file directories, matching files to entries (by filename heuristics), and setting file links on entries while avoiding duplicates. It performs the heavy lifting and reports results back to the action for UI feedback.
- Localization: Added/updated English resource strings in JabRef_en.properties for labels, tooltips and messages related to the new feature.

Behavior and notes:
- The action operates on the currently selected entries by default; if no selection is present it can operate on the whole database (prompting the user first).
- Matching is done using filename-based heuristics and configurable file directories; matched files are attached as file links to entries.
- The operation runs as a background task and provides progress and a summary of changes when complete.

This change improves file management by making it easy to retroactively attach existing PDFs and other files to bibliography entries.

text:
Add DOI identifier parsing and robust normalization (DOI.java) with extensive unit tests (DOITest.java)

Summary
- Implement a comprehensive DOI class to represent and validate Digital Object Identifiers (DOIs) and Short DOIs.
- Provide robust parsing, normalization and URI construction for many DOI input variants and edge cases.

Key features
- Supports plain DOIs and short DOIs, including detection via isShortDoi.
- Accepts and normalizes many input formats: plain, urn:, doi:, doi URLs, dx.doi and other vendor domains, and shortcut DOI URLs (doi.org/abcd).
- Properly decodes HTTP URL encoded path segments and handles percent-encoded characters.
- Cleans noisy inputs via URL decoding, Latex to Unicode conversion, and removal of whitespace, backslashes, braces, brackets, pipes, non-ASCII characters and other artifacts inserted by copy/paste.
- Handles special characters that need encoding when producing external resolver URIs (via getExternalURI and getExternalURIFromBase), and provides ASCII representation with getURIAsASCIIString.
- Equality is case-insensitive in accordance with DOI semantics; normalized hashCode uses lowercase.
- Provides safe parse method returning Optional to avoid throwing exceptions and convenience isValid and findInText methods.
- Includes getExternalURIWithCustomBase to allow custom resolver base URIs.

Tests
- Extensive parameterized tests covering:
  - Valid plain DOIs and short DOIs in many formats
  - URL, URN and prefix variants
  - Shortcut short DOIs (doi.org/abcd) and embedded occurrences
  - Parsing and cleaning of whitespace, non-ASCII characters, backslashes, braces, ticks, pipes, tildes, brackets and caret characters
  - Correct encoding/decoding of reserved characters like %, ", #, space, and ?
  - findInText behavior for finding DOIs inside arbitrary text and rejecting false positives
  - Behavior of equals, isShortDoi and rejection of invalid inputs

Notes
- The parse method uses LatexToUnicodeFormatter for cleaning; the class is annotated with AllowedToUseLogic for that reason.
- There is a TODO reminding that getExternalURI should honor user preferences via dependency injection instead of using the hardcoded resolver.

This commit improves DOI handling robustness and significantly increases test coverage around DOI parsing, normalization and URI generation.

text:
Closes #12894

Summary

This PR fixes a bug where a library would unexpectedly disappear (become hidden) if you had two libraries open alongside the Welcome tab and then closed the tab immediately to the right of the Welcome tab. In that scenario the Welcome tab could become selected automatically, hiding the remaining library. The fix prevents that by selecting the next library tab when the previously active database was closed instead of switching to the Welcome tab.

What I changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/frame/JabRefFrame.java
  - Added a check when the selected tab is null or a WelcomeTab to detect whether the previously active database was just closed. If so, select the next tab instead of the Welcome tab. This preserves the visible library when closing adjacent tabs.
  - Small formatting/indentation adjustments in initKeyBindings and closeTabs stream formatting.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added an entry describing the fix so users are aware of the resolved issue.

Why

When closing a library tab the UI could end up selecting the Welcome tab (or no tab) even though other library tabs remained. This change ensures that when the active database was closed, the tab selection moves to the next tab (a library) rather than the Welcome page, preventing the library from being hidden.

Testing

- Manually tested in the running application with multiple libraries and the Welcome tab open: closing a library adjacent to the Welcome tab now keeps the other library visible.

Notes

- The change is minimal and limited to tab selection behavior in JabRefFrame.
- See issue #12894 for the original report.

- Adds a new "Clear content" tab to the Automatic Field Editor (with a dedicated ViewModel).

- New ViewModel backs the Clear content tab and manages the populated fields list, the filtering by "only set fields", and creation of undoable field-change edits.

How to test
1. Open or create a library with a few entries (e.g., fill in fields like `author`, `journal`).
2. Select one or more entries.
3. Open Edit → Automatic field editor.
4. Switch to the new Clear content tab.
5. Toggle the "Show only set fields" checkbox — the dropdown should show only fields currently filled when enabled.
6. Select a field (e.g., `author`) and click Clear field content — the chosen field should be removed from all selected entries.

Add YAML export support and blank-line handling improvements

This PR implements a CSL-compatible YAML exporter and refactors blank-line handling for template-based exporters.

Highlights

- Add YAML export format
  - Register a new 'yaml' TemplateExporter in ExporterFactory (StandardFileType YAML).
  - Provide layout resources: resource/layout/yaml.begin.layout, resource/layout/yaml.layout, resource/layout/yaml.end.layout.
  - Add unit tests (YamlExporterTest) covering empty output, Article export, and fallback type handling (no-type).

- Blank-line behavior refactor
  - Introduce BlankLineBehaviour enum to represent how TemplateExporter should handle blank lines (KEEP_BLANKS, DELETE_BLANKS).
  - TemplateExporter refactored to use blankLineBehaviour instead of a boolean, and to remove blank lines by splitting on newline and writing non-empty, non-blank lines with OS.NEWLINE when DELETE_BLANKS is set.
  - Configure the RIS exporter to delete blank lines to avoid extra blank lines in RIS output.

- Layout formatter for CSL type mapping
  - Add new LayoutFormatter class CSLType to map JabRef entry types to CSL type strings (e.g. Article -> article, Book -> book, Conference -> paper-conference, etc.).
  - Register CSLType in LayoutEntry so it can be used from layouts (used by the YAML template to emit CSL 'type').

- Misc
  - Add YAML to StandardFileType.
  - Update CHANGELOG.md to mention YAML export and the RIS blank-line fix.

Files added/changed (non-exhaustive)
- Added: BlankLineBehaviour.java, CSLType.java, yaml.layout, yaml.begin.layout, yaml.end.layout, YamlExporterTest.java
- Changed: TemplateExporter.java (blank-line behaviour + imports), ExporterFactory.java (register exporters), LayoutEntry.java, StandardFileType.java, CHANGELOG.md

Notes
- The YAML exporter uses the template-based exporter with DELETE_BLANKS to ensure clean YAML output without extraneous blank lines.
- Tests validate exact output lines and confirm fallback for unknown entry types to 'no-type'.

Use InvalidationListener + Platform.runLater for X11 clipboard handling in TextInputControl

- Replace the previous selectedTextProperty change listener with an invalidation-style listener that calls Platform.runLater to read the selected text. This works around JDK bug JDK-8176270 and avoids timing/concurrency issues when accessing selection from the listener.
- Keep existing behavior: when selection is non-empty, copy it to the X11 primary clipboard; middle-click paste handling remains unchanged.
- Add required javafx.application.Platform import and tidy up Javadoc formatting and links.

This change improves stability of the X11 primary clipboard support in JavaFX inputs by deferring the selection read to the FX application thread.

text:
Fixes #8390 — Removing several selected groups now deletes all selected groups instead of only one.

What I changed
- Implemented multi-selection deletion in GroupTreeViewModel.removeGroupAndSubgroups:
  - If multiple groups are selected, the confirmation dialog and notification text reflect that multiple groups will be removed.
  - The code now iterates over a defensive copy (new ArrayList<>(selectedGroups)) to avoid skipping elements when removing nodes while iterating.
  - For each selected group we call removeGroupsAndSubGroupsFromEntries(...) and remove the group node from its parent, then persist group metadata via writeGroupChangesToMetaData().
- Added/updated English resource strings to support single vs. multiple group confirmation and notifications.
- Added a changelog entry mentioning the fix.

Files modified
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/groups/GroupTreeViewModel.java
  - Use a copy of selectedGroups and iterate over it to remove each selected group and its subgroups.
  - Show different confirmation dialogs and notifications for single vs. multiple selected groups.
- src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties
  - Added keys for plural/single confirmation and notification messages ("Remove groups and subgroups", "Remove all selected groups and their subgroups?", and corresponding "Removed ..." messages).
- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added user-facing changelog line mentioning the fix.

Why
- Previously the handler only operated on the group that triggered the event, so when multiple groups were selected only the single triggered group was removed. Iterating over a copy of the selected groups and prompting appropriate confirmation fixes the behavior and prevents skipping elements when nodes are removed during iteration.

Testing
- Manually tested single-group deletion and multi-group deletion flows.
- Screenshots demonstrating single and multiple group deletion flows were added to the issue/PR description.

Notes
- No unit tests were added in this PR.
- This change is limited to UI behavior and localization strings; undo support is still TODO.

This PR refactors and improves the autosave and shared-database UI/synchronization logic and updates related save/open/new actions to use the new managers. It also contains several UI integration fixes and localization updates.

- Introduced/updated AutosaveUIManager and integrated it into the main UI (JabRefFrame, BasePanel, MainTable) so autosave settings and controls are handled in a single place.

- Centralize autosave UI code so autosave behaviour is consistent across different entry points (save/open/new/import dialogs).

- Fix edge cases and race conditions around saving, opening and creating databases while autosave or shared-sync is enabled.

text:
Implement comprehensive drag-and-drop support and related utilities

Summary
- Add first-class drag-and-drop infrastructure for complex in-memory payloads and platform dragboard interaction.
- Enable dragging of groups, entries and external files across the UI (Groups tree, Main table, and tab header). Drop actions support different behaviors depending on mouse location and transfer mode (move/copy/link).

Key features
- CustomLocalDragboard: type-safe in-memory dragboard for transporting lists of BibEntry and PreviewLayout objects without serialization.
- DragAndDropDataFormats: centralized DataFormat keys used for inter-component DnD and a typed helper for preview layout list class.
- DragAndDropHelper: convenience methods to detect and extract .bib files from a Dragboard.
- UI integration:
  - JabRefFrame: show a temporary "Open files..." tab indicator on drag-over the tab header; accept dropped .bib files and open/import them. Sets up drag handlers for the tab header area.
  - GroupTreeView / GroupNodeViewModel: support dragging groups (reordering and nesting) and dropping entries onto groups. Visual feedback (pseudo-classes) and a drag expansion handler are included.
  - MainTable: accept files dropped on rows to either import as new entries or link/copy/move files into the target entry depending on drop location and TransferMode.
  - ControlHelper: utilities to compute mouse drop location (top/center/bottom) and manage pseudo-classes to reflect drop position.
- External file import integration: ImportHandler handles importing PDFs/XMP/BIB files or creating empty entries with links when files are dropped/added; ExternalFilesEntryLinker used to link/copy/move files into entries.

Other changes
- Added CSS rules for drag-and-drop visual states (MainTable.css, GroupTree.css) and updated Base.css for theming support.
- ViewModelTableRowFactory / ViewModelTreeTableCellFactory wiring to simplify attaching drag & drop and context menu behavior to rows.
- Added unit tests (GroupNodeViewModelTest) covering group tree construction, reordering behavior and adding entries to groups.
- Project run configuration (JabRef_Main.xml) added/updated for local IDE usage.

Files (high level)
- New/updated core DnD & helpers: CustomLocalDragboard, DragAndDropDataFormats, DragAndDropHelper
- UI: JabRefFrame, GroupTreeView, GroupNodeViewModel, MainTable, ViewModelTableRowFactory, ControlHelper
- Import logic: ImportHandler
- Styling: Base.css, GroupTree.css, MainTable.css
- Tests: GroupNodeViewModelTest

Why this change
- Improves UX by allowing intuitive drag-and-drop workflows: reordering groups, assigning entries to groups, importing files by dropping into table or tab area, and linking/copying/moving files to entries using standard modifiers.

Notes
- TransferMode is used to infer link/move/copy semantics when dropping files onto entries.
- The in-memory local dragboard complements the system dragboard for complex non-serializable payloads (e.g. lists of BibEntry).
- A new temporary tab indicator is shown when .bib files are dragged over the tab header, and files dropped there are opened/imported.

Fix UTF-8 BOM parsing so lines starting with '%' are detected correctly

Problem: Files that include a UTF-8 BOM (U+FEFF) at the start caused line.startsWith("%") checks to fail because the BOM occupies position 0 and the percent sign is at position 1. Java reads the BOM into the string, so comment/format-detection logic missed these lines.

Solution: Strip/ignore a leading BOM character from input lines (normalize/remove U+FEFF) before performing startsWith checks and other parsing logic. This ensures lines that visually start with '%' (or other markers) are recognized correctly even when a BOM is present.

Fixes #9926

Notes:
- Manually tested with files containing a BOM (see attached screenshot in the issue).
- CHANGELOG/tests not modified in this PR.

text:
Add DOI identifier class and comprehensive tests

This PR introduces a DOI model class (org.jabref.model.entry.identifier.DOI) with full support for parsing, validating and normalizing Digital Object Identifiers (DOIs) and Short DOIs. Key features:

- Robust parsing: accepts plain DOIs, Short DOIs, URNs (urn: and urn:doi:), HTTP/HTTPS URLs (including dx.doi/doi.acm/etc.), doi.org shortcuts (with and without www), and various encodings.
- Short DOI support: recognizes both the 10/... short form and shortcut forms like doi.org/abcd and converts them to the normalized internal representation.
- HTTP URL handling: decodes incoming HTTP(S) DOI URLs (path decoding) and produces properly encoded resolver URIs using https://doi.org as the resolver.
- findInText(): attempts to extract a DOI/Short DOI from arbitrary text using several regexes (DOI, short DOI, shortcut patterns) and returns an Optional<DOI>.
- parse(): creates an Optional<DOI> without throwing an exception for invalid input, and isValid() convenience method.
- getExternalURI() / getURIAsASCIIString(): returns an encoded URI/ASCII string for use as external links.
- equals() and hashCode(): DOI equality is implemented case-insensitively per DOI rules.
- Logging and error handling: invalid URI encoding errors are logged and returned as Optional.empty() where appropriate.

Also adds a comprehensive test suite (org.jabref.model.entry.identifier.DOITest) that covers a wide range of valid and invalid DOI/short-DOI inputs, whitespace and percent-encoding handling, URL/URN forms, detection inside arbitrary text, and equality/short-DOI flags.

These additions improve DOI handling reliability across ingestion and normalization code paths and are covered by unit tests to prevent regressions.

Add live preview and search-highlighting support to global search results

This PR integrates the preview viewer into the Global Search Results dialog and enhances the preview component with search-highlight capabilities and improved link handling.

Changes
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/search/GlobalSearchResultDialog.java
  - Instantiate PreviewViewer for the search database context and set the selected preview layout from preferences.
  - Wire the search results table selection to the preview so the preview updates when the user selects rows (including initial selection handling).
  - Remove SpecialFieldColumn from the results table columns to clean up the view.
  - Add a "keep on top" ToggleButton binding to control the dialog's always-on-top state and swap the icon accordingly.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preview/PreviewViewer.java
  - Add mark.js-based highlighting support embedded into the preview HTML and a JS API to mark/unmark matches.
  - Register a listener to StateManager.activeSearchQueryProperty() to obtain a Java regex for the active search and highlight matches in the preview. The createJavaScriptRegex helper safely converts a Java Pattern to a JavaScript regex literal (escaping forward slashes) and applies global/case-insensitive matching.
  - Ensure previously highlighted matches are removed before applying new highlights (unmark + callback to mark).
  - Install theme CSS into the WebView and disable the WebView context menu.
  - Intercept anchor clicks inside the WebView and open links in the external browser (prevent default navigation in the WebView), with error handling for malformed URLs.
  - Provide utility methods for printing the preview and copying the full preview or the current selection (text and HTML) to the clipboard.
  - Minor robustness: avoid setting null layouts and ensure preview panel shows placeholder text when nothing to display.

Why
- Users can now see a formatted preview of selected search results directly in the Global Search dialog.
- Active global search terms are highlighted inside the preview, improving discoverability of matches.
- Links in the preview open in the system browser, avoiding unexpected in-widget navigation.

Notes
- The highlight implementation embeds mark.js into the generated preview HTML and coordinates unmark/mark calls from JavaFX to JavaScript.
- The Java -> JavaScript regex conversion uses a global, multiline, case-insensitive regex ("/…/gmi").
