text:
Add ConflictRules utility to detect three-way BibEntry conflicts

Summary:
- Introduces ConflictRules, a final utility class with static methods to detect entry-level and field-level conflicts between base, local, and remote BibEntry instances during a three-way merge.
- Returns Optional<ThreeWayEntryConflict> for entry-level conflicts and boolean results for field-level checks.

Key behaviors handled:
- Entry-level conflict detection (detectEntryConflict):
  - New entry added on both sides (base == null && local != null && remote != null): compares fields of both additions and reports a conflict if fields conflict.
  - One side deleted while the other modified (base != null): flags conflict when one side removed the entry and the other changed it.
  - Both sides modified (base != null && local != null && remote != null): only considered conflict if there are conflicting fields.

- Field-level conflict detection (hasConflictingFields):
  - Treats differing entry type changes (both changed to different types) as conflict.
  - Aggregates all fields present in base, local, and remote, and checks each for:
    - modifiedOnBothSidesWithDisagreement: both modified from base and local != remote
    - oneSideDeletedOneSideModified: one removed the field while the other modified it
    - addedOnBothSidesWithDisagreement: both added the field (absent in base) with differing values

API / helpers:
- detectEntryConflict(BibEntry base, BibEntry local, BibEntry remote): Optional<ThreeWayEntryConflict>
- hasConflictingFields(BibEntry base, BibEntry local, BibEntry remote): boolean
- entryTypeChangedDifferently(BibEntry base, BibEntry local, BibEntry remote): boolean
- modifiedOnBothSidesWithDisagreement(String baseVal, String localVal, String remoteVal): boolean
- oneSideDeletedOneSideModified(String baseVal, String localVal, String remoteVal): boolean
- addedOnBothSidesWithDisagreement(String baseVal, String localVal, String remoteVal): boolean
- notEqual(String a, String b): boolean

Implementation notes:
- The class is non-instantiable (private constructor throws UnsupportedOperationException).
- Uses streams to collect the union of all fields across entries to ensure all relevant fields are checked.
- Handles null entries/fields gracefully and uses Objects.equals for comparisons.

This change centralizes conflict-detection rules for three-way merging of bibliographic entries, making merge planning and conflict reporting consistent and testable.

text:
Fixes #2680 and Fixes #2667: Proper Swing error handling and prevent UI freeze

Summary
- Fixes two related issues where exceptions thrown on the Swing Event Dispatch Thread (EDT) were not being handled properly and could cause the UI to freeze.

What I changed
- Centralized and improved error handling for code executed on the EDT: all top-level event handlers are wrapped so exceptions are caught and routed through the error handling path instead of being uncaught.
- Ensured any UI updates and error dialogs are always invoked on the EDT (using invokeLater) to avoid deadlocks and illegal threading operations.
- Moved long-running or blocking work off the EDT (SwingWorker/background executor) so an exception in background work cannot block the UI.
- Avoided using invokeAndWait from the EDT to prevent freezing; converted blocking patterns to non-blocking alternatives where appropriate.
- Improved logging of caught exceptions (stack traces are preserved) and show a user-friendly error notification without freezing or leaving UI components disabled.

Tests and verification
- Added tests and manual verification steps that reproduce both reported problems and confirm the fixes.
- Manually tested typical user flows that previously triggered freezes and error dialogs to ensure responsiveness is restored.

Notes for reviewers
- No public API changes; this is strictly internal behavior and robustness work for the UI layer.
- Focus review on concurrency boundaries: EDT wrapping, background task transitions, and error-dialog invocation paths.

Issues closed: Fixes #2680, Fixes #2667

text:
Summary
Move context-menu creation to lazy (late) initialization using Supplier so context menus are instantiated only when actually requested (on user right-click), rather than for every visible field during rendering.

Motivation
Profiling showed that creating context menus for every visible editor field had a measurable memory and performance cost (context-menu related objects accounted for ~40% of memory in the measured scenario and ~8% of CPU time when scrolling through 50 entries). Because these menus are rarely used while merely browsing, deferring creation eliminates that overhead.

What I changed
- Replace eager instantiation of context menus with Suppliers that create the menu on first use (on right-click).
- Update checkstyle version in the Gradle build to allow {@link ...} in javadoc for otherwise-unused classes.

Results (measured)
- Memory footprint when scrolling 50 entries: context-menu related memory went from ~40% to negligible in the profiled scenario.
- Performance impact went from ~8% to essentially zero when merely scrolling/browsing (menus are no longer created until needed).

Testing
- Manually tested in a running JabRef by scrolling through 50 entries and by invoking context menus. Behavior matches expectations: no menu objects are created until a menu is requested.

Notes
- This follows the suggestion discussed in issue #3335 (thanks to Tobias Diez for the hint).
- No automated tests were added in this PR.

- [ ] Tests created for changes

text:
Implements new title-based modifiers requested in issue #11367

What this PR adds
- New modifiers that can be used in citation key / file name patterns: camel, camelN, shorttitle, veryshorttitle.
- Four new Formatter classes: CamelFormatter, CamelNFormatter, ShortTitleFormatter, VeryShortTitleFormatter (under logic/formatter/casechanger).
- Integration into Formatters: a new getTitleChangers list and registration in getAll; parsing logic for modifiers in getFormatterForModifier updated to handle camel and camelN forms and explicit shorttitle / veryshorttitle.
- English localization strings added (JabRef_en.properties).
- Unit tests added to BracketedPatternTest to cover [:camel], [:camelN], [:shorttitle], [:veryshorttitle] usages.

Behavior summary
- camel: returns the title with each word capitalized and concatenated (e.g. "camel title formatter" -> CamelTitleFormatter). Used as [title:camel].
- camelN: same as camel but limits to the first N words concatenated; parsed from the modifier suffix (e.g. [title:camel1], [title:camel4]). If no numeric suffix is given the plain camel behavior is used.
- shorttitle: returns the first 3 non-function words of the title (ignores small/function words).
- veryshorttitle: returns the first non-function word of the title.

Tests
- Added parameterized tests for camel, shorttitle and veryshorttitle as well as a test for camelN in BracketedPatternTest. Examples in tests demonstrate expected outputs.

Notes / follow-ups
- User documentation at docs.jabref.org (citation key pattern modifiers) needs updating to document the new modifiers.
- CHANGELOG entry and additional language translations are not included in this PR.

References
- Implements feature discussed in: https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/11367

Summary

Fixes an issue where the library UI would disappear after closing and re-opening a browser tab. Users reported that the library panel/state was lost when a tab was closed, causing confusion and lost context.

Root cause

The library visibility/selection state was kept only in memory and not persisted across tab close/reopen. When the tab was closed the in-memory state was lost and the app initialized without restoring the previous library state.

What this change does

- Persists library visibility and selection state to storage so it can be restored when the app reloads.
- Rehydrates the library state during app/component initialization so the panel remains visible (and selection restored) after closing and re-opening a tab.
- Adds safe save-on-unload handling and cleans up listeners to avoid leaks.

Tests and verification

- Added unit tests to verify persistence and rehydration logic.
- Added a manual/end-to-end test scenario to confirm library remains visible after closing and reopening a tab.

Impact

- Backwards compatible: no migration needed. Users will retain their previous library state automatically after this update.
- Small storage usage for persisting only the needed library state.

Notes

If any environment has strict storage/privacy requirements, the persisted storage key/location can be changed or made configurable.

Summary

This PR adds the JabLS (BibTeX Language Server) module and wiring, plus the implementation to read extension settings from the (possibly nested) VS Code settings JSON. It also includes a jbang launcher for running the language server and records the decision to use Jackson for nested JSON paths.

What’s included

- Add .jbang/JabLsLauncher.java
  - Simple entry point to run the JabLS server via jbang (delegates to org.jabref.languageserver.cli.ServerCli).

- Add jabls module build and module-info
  - jabls/build.gradle.kts: new module configuration and dependencies for LSP4J, Guava, SLF4J and test logging.
  - jabls/src/main/java/module-info.java: exports/opens for the language server packages and adds a require on com.fasterxml.jackson.databind (Jackson) as well as other libraries (Gson, lsp4j, slf4j).

- Add settings parsing implementation
  - jabls/src/main/java/org/jabref/languageserver/ExtensionSettings.java
    - New ExtensionSettings class with default values and copyFromJsonObject(JsonObject) which uses Jackson's ObjectMapper and JsonNode.at("/path") to safely read nested settings and apply fallback values.
    - Errors while parsing are logged via SLF4J.

- Documentation decision
  - docs/decisions/0051-handle-nested-json-paths.md: documents the design decision to use Jackson for nested JSON path access, with reasoning and comparison to other approaches.

- Build logic updates
  - build-logic/src/main/kotlin/org.jabref.gradle.base.dependency-rules.gradle.kts: contains module mappings/patches used by the build to support the modules used by JabLS and other parts of the project.

Why

- Jackson's JsonNode.at(...) was chosen for concise, safe access to nested JSON settings with fallback values (no exceptions for missing paths). The decision doc explains the alternatives and tradeoffs.
- Providing a jbang launcher makes it easy for developers/contributors to run the language server during development.

Behavioral notes

- Default extension settings remain as before; when provided by an editor client the new copyFromJsonObject method will override defaults where appropriate.
- Parsing errors are logged but do not crash the language server; settings remain at defaults when parsing fails.

Developer notes

- The jabls module now requires Jackson on the module path (com.fasterxml.jackson.databind) and lsp4j dependencies; ensure IDE/build tool resolves those modules correctly.

Summary

This PR adds a dedicated Snap launcher to fix extension import when running JabRef as a snap. Instead of launching another full JabRef instance (which caused CLI parsing errors seen in the logs), we install a small wrapper that directly starts the JabRef module entry point.

What I changed

- Added snap/local/JabRef-launcher: a small shell wrapper that invokes the snap-provided Java runtime and starts the module main class org.jabref/org.jabref.JabRefLauncher.
- Updated snap/snapcraft.yaml:
  - Remove the original bin/JabRef from the jabref part install.
  - Add a new jabref-launcher part that dumps the local launcher into bin/JabRef in the snap.

Why

When the browser extension tries to import into a running JabRef snap, the previous launcher logic caused a new instance to be spawned and produced a list of CLI parsing errors. Providing a separate launcher that invokes the module directly prevents spawning another instance and removes those errors.

Related issues

- Fixes #5537
- Fixes https://github.com/JabRef/JabRef-Browser-Extension/issues/165

Testing

- Manually tested running JabRef and the browser extension import flow; confirmed the extension can import and the CLI parsing errors no longer appear.

Notes

- No changelog or automated tests were added in this PR.

Closes #12585

Summary
- Remove duplicate groups and keywords when merging entries.
- GroupMerger:
  - Split groups on comma or semicolon (previously only comma).
  - Trim individual group names before deduplication.
  - Join final groups using the canonical separator ", ".
- KeywordMerger:
  - Detect the separator character used in the provided keyword strings.
  - Enforce a single consistent separator across inputs (throws IllegalArgumentException if multiple different separators are detected or if no valid separator is found).
  - Set the detected separator in BibEntryPreferences and delegate to KeywordList.merge(...).

Behavioral notes and rationale
- Deduplication and trimming prevent duplicate entries that differ only by surrounding whitespace.
- Accepting semicolons for group splitting increases robustness when users used a different delimiter.
- Explicit separator detection for keywords avoids ambiguous merges when different separators are mixed; the current implementation fails fast (throws) to make the issue visible. If preferred, we can change this to fall back to a default separator instead.

Testing
- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance (screenshot attached in the issue/PR).
- No unit tests were added in this PR; recommended follow-up is to add tests covering group deduplication and keyword separator detection/edge cases.

Follow-ups / open questions
- Should KeywordMerger fall back to a default separator instead of throwing when no separator is found or when inputs use different separators?
- Add unit tests for these cases and update CHANGELOG.md.

Implementation details
- GroupMerger now uses regex "[;,]\s*" to split and trims input before deduplication.
- KeywordMerger counts non-alphanumeric non-whitespace characters to detect the separator and ensures a single separator character is used for merging.

text:
This PR implements support for fetching BibTeX from ottobib and integrates it into the ISBN lookup fallback chain.

Key changes
- Add new fetcher IsbnViaOttoBibFetcher that retrieves BibTeX from https://www.ottobib.com/isbn/{ISBN}/bibtex. The fetcher uses Jsoup to read the HTML page and extracts the BibTeX from the <textarea>, then parses it with BibtexParser.
- Update IsbnFetcher to try ebook.de first, then chimbori.com, and finally ottobib when previous fetchers return nothing.
- Update URLDownload.USER_AGENT to a newer Firefox 68 user agent string.

Tests and fixes
- Add IsbnViaOttoBibFetcherTest with various ISBN cases (short/long ISBNs and authors formatting). 
- Update WebFetchersTest to exclude IsbnViaOttoBibFetcher from the ID-based fetchers list exposed to users (consistent with other special ISBN fetchers).
- Fix and adapt existing tests for ebook.de and chimbori fetchers (updated expected dates, ISBNs, URLs, page counts and formatting fixes). Several small expected values changed to match current upstream data.

Motivation
- Ottobib serves BibTeX inside an HTML textarea, so previous approaches that expected a plain-text response failed. This fetcher correctly extracts the textarea content and parses it.

Notes
- Tests were added/updated and manual testing of the changed features was performed. This is a follow-up to #5125.
- CHANGELOG.md has not been updated in this PR.

text:
Refactor and enhance main application window (JabRefFrame)

This PR contains a focused set of improvements and refactorings to the main application frame (JabRefFrame). Key changes include:

- Drag & drop: add a robust drag-and-drop experience for opening .bib files. A temporary tab indicator is shown while dragging and files are opened on drop. Listeners are registered only when a proper TabPaneSkin is available.
- Key bindings: centralize and extend keybinding handling. Many new / existing entry creation shortcuts are executed directly from the frame and a macOS-specific paste workaround for CodeArea/TextField is applied.
- Telemetry prompt: implement delayed telemetry opt-in prompt (shown after 60s) with the ability to toggle collection and not ask again. The preference is stored via TelemetryPreferences.
- Background tasks UI: improve the toolbar task indicator and add a pop-over with a TaskProgressView. Indicator tooltip and clip/size logic adjusted for determinate/indeterminate states.
- PopOvers: add reusable PopOver handling for the Import-by-ID dialog and the background tasks view.
- Tab / side pane behavior: better handling for adding/removing the side pane from the SplitPane, persist divider position, and subscribe to side pane width updates.
- Tab lifecycle & autosave: attach AutosaveManager and BackupManager when opening new libraries; shutdown autosave/backup on close; track telemetry event when a new DB is opened.
- Quit/close flow: improved quit() and closeTab() flows — wait for background tasks, confirm saving or deleting empty entries, convert/close shared DBs, and properly shutdown autosave and backup managers.
- Menu & toolbar wiring: build menus and toolbar with ActionFactory and register reconfigurables (push-to-application), plus improved creation and management of the New Entry From ID button.
- State binding: better binding between TabPane and application state (openDatabaseList, activeDatabase, active search query, focus owner) so actions operate on the correct database and UI state is synchronized when switching tabs.
- Misc: small fixes like clipping the progress indicator label, ensuring selection/focus handling when switching tabs, and background task wait dialog on quit.

Why:
These changes improve usability (drag & drop, clearer background-task feedback, reliable keyboard shortcuts), robustness (proper lifecycle and shutdown of autosave/backup, safer quit behavior), and telemetry handling (respectful opt-in flow).

Testing:
- Manual verification of drag-and-drop open for .bib files (indicator appears/disappears, files open on drop).
- Verified entry creation keyboard shortcuts work and macOS paste workaround prevents double-paste.
- Telemetry prompt shows once after startup when configured to ask and persists the choice.
- Background tasks popover displays running tasks and retains completed tasks.
- Opening/closing libraries registers/unregisters autosave and backup; quitting waits for long-running background tasks and prompts to save modified libraries or delete empty entries.

No behavioral changes to high-level features were intentionally introduced; most edits are wiring/UI improvements and lifecycle fixes.

text:
Add ImportHandler to centralize importing of external files and string data.

- Provides importFilesInBackground(...) to process PDFs, .bib files and arbitrary files in a background task; extracts BibTeX from PDFs, parses .bib files, or creates empty entries with file links; reports progress/messages on the JavaFX thread and aggregates results for the UI; integrates with UndoManager.
- Uses ExternalFilesContentImporter and ExternalFilesEntryLinker to import content and attach/relativize files according to FilePreferences.
- Implements importEntries / importCleanedEntries to run ImportCleanup, insert cloned entries into the database, generate citation keys, set automatic fields and add entries to selected groups; supports optional download of online linked files.
- Adds duplicate-aware import flows: importEntryWithDuplicateCheck, importEntriesWithDuplicateCheck, findDuplicate, handleDuplicates and getDuplicateDecision using DuplicateResolverDialog and user preferences for applying decisions to all entries; cleanUpEntry is exposed @VisibleForTesting.
- Supports handling pasted BibTeX data (handleBibTeXData), importing string constants with duplicate checks (importStringConstantsWithDuplicateCheck), and importing by identifier or unknown formats (handleStringData and tryImportFormats) with fetchers for DOI, arXiv and ISBN.
- Includes error handling and logging for IO, parse and import exceptions and surfaces user-facing messages via DialogService.
- Notes/TODO: group-change undo is not yet implemented (TODO in addToGroups). Background tasks deliberately run UI operations on the FX thread to avoid deadlocks.

This class consolidates import logic, respects user preferences and integrates with existing services (StateManager, DialogService, TaskExecutor, FileUpdateMonitor, UndoManager).

Summary

- Adds a new preference that allows JabRef to follow the operating system’s light/dark theme preference.
- When enabled, the application automatically switches between the light and dark themes according to the OS setting and updates immediately when the OS preference changes.

What I changed

- Preferences UI
  - Preferences -> General -> Appearance: added a 'Use System Preference' checkbox. When checked, the Visual theme combobox and custom theme controls are disabled.
  - Files: GeneralTab.fxml, GeneralTab.java, GeneralTabViewModel.java

- Theme handling
  - Integrated jSystemThemeDetector to detect the OS theme and listen to changes; ThemeManager now uses it to pick light/dark when the new preference is enabled.
  - Files: ThemeManager.java

- Preferences and persistence
  - Added a themeSyncOs property to WorkspacePreferences and a stored preference key (THEME_SYNC_OS) in JabRefPreferences. Preference defaults to false.
  - Files: WorkspacePreferences.java, JabRefPreferences.java

- Build & module updates
  - Added dependency com.github.Dansoftowner:jSystemThemeDetector and module require for com.jthemedetector.
  - Updated external-libraries.md with the new library and license.
  - Files: build.gradle, module-info.java, external-libraries.md

- Misc
  - Updated CHANGELOG.md and localization string for the new checkbox label.
  - Files: CHANGELOG.md, JabRef_en.properties

Behavior notes

- Default: the new "Use System Preference" option is off, preserving current behavior.
- When enabled, the app overrides the selected theme and applies Theme.light() or Theme.dark() depending on the OS preference. The setting is persisted and can be toggled in Preferences.
- The change reacts to OS appearance changes at runtime via a registered listener.

Testing

- Manually tested on macOS and Windows. The theme follows the OS appearance and updates when the OS setting changes.

Related

- Closes #8729
- Based on prior work in #9263

Summary

This PR stores sensitive credentials (proxy passwords and custom fetcher API keys) in the native OS credential store instead of keeping them in plain-text preference values. It integrates the java-keyring library to access the OS keyring and adds migration code to move existing API keys into the keyring.

User-facing changes

- New checkbox in Preferences → Network: "Persist password between sessions". When enabled the proxy password is stored in the OS credential store and reused across sessions; when disabled the password is kept for the current session only (and the keyring entry is removed when toggled off).
- On startup, if proxy authentication is enabled and the password is persisted, JabRef will read the password from the keyring. If the password is not persisted or missing, the user is prompted for the proxy password.
- Custom API keys (web fetcher keys) are migrated to the OS credential store by the migration routine. Old preference entries for API keys are removed.
- UI text updated: new resource entry for the persist-password label and changelog entry added.

Implementation details

- Adds new dependency: com.github.javakeyring:java-keyring:1.0.2 and module-info entry (requires java.keyring).
- ProxyPreferences: added persistPassword boolean property with getters/setters and included in equals()/hashCode().
- Network preferences UI: NetworkTab.fxml includes a CheckBox (proxyPersistPassword); NetworkTab/ViewModel bind and persist the value.
- JabRefPreferences:
  - Implements getProxyPassword() and setProxyPassword(...) to interact with the keyring when persist flag is set. Passwords are encrypted/decrypted with the existing Password helper using the internal preferences (user@host) before writing to keyring.
  - getFetcherKeysFromKeyring(...) and storeFetcherKeysToKeyring(...) are added to read/write fetcher API keys in the keyring. clearCustomFetcherKeys() removes keys during preferences clear.
  - Listeners: when persist flag changes to false, the proxy credential is removed from the keyring.
- PreferencesMigrations: adds moveApiKeysToKeyring(...) to migrate legacy fetcher keys into the keyring and remove the old preference key.
- JabRefGUI: improved proxy setup flow — if password is persisted and present, register proxy; otherwise prompt for password and register when provided.
- NetworkTabViewModel/NetworkTab: refactored storing logic to set persist flag before storing password so setProxyPassword() can react accordingly. checkConnection() uses ProxyRegisterer.register to temporarily apply test settings and restore them afterwards.

Tests

- Updated tests to reflect new properties and keyring behavior:
  - ProxyTest updated to include persist flag and verify it in the object.
  - PreferencesMigrationsTest added testMoveApiKeysToKeyRing which mocks Keyring.create() and verifies the migration writes expected entries and deletes the old preference key.

Changelog

- CHANGELOG.md updated describing the new option to encrypt and remember the proxy password and storing custom API keys in the OS credential store.

Notes and failure handling

- If the keyring is unavailable or operations fail, JabRef logs warnings and falls back to previous behaviour (using defaults or prompting the user). The code handles PasswordAccessException to detect missing entries in the keyring and logs appropriate messages.

Related issues / PRs

- Implements: fixes #8055 / follow-up to #9652 and related items (see PR description).
- Depends on: #10004 (as noted in the PR meta).

If you want, I can split migrations, preferences logic, and UI changes into smaller PRs for easier review.

This PR improves drag & drop across the main table, group tree and tab headers and adds visual feedback so users can see what will happen when they drop files or entries. It also fixes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/5017.

Main user-facing changes
- Open .bib files by dropping them onto the tab header: a temporary "Open files..." tab appears while dragging. Dropped .bib files are opened as databases.
- Improved row-level drop indicators: rows show distinct visual states for dropping at TOP / CENTER / BOTTOM. The CENTER state indicates linking files to an entry; TOP/BOTTOM indicate creating/importing new entries between rows.
- Different drop actions are applied depending on the drop location within a row:
  - TOP / BOTTOM -> import entries (create new entries from dropped file(s))
  - CENTER -> attach/link files to the target entry (supports MOVE / COPY / LINK transfer modes)

Implementation highlights
- New utility class DragAndDropHelper to detect .bib files in a Dragboard (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/DragAndDropHelper.java).
- Visual styling and colors added/adjusted in Base.css, GroupTree.css and MainTable.css (introduces -jr-drag-target and -jr-drag-target-hover styling and pseudo-class rules).
- Tab drop indicator implemented in JabRefFrame.initDragAndDrop. It observes the TabPane skin, captures drag events on the tab header area and shows a temporary localized tab label ("Open files...").
- MainTable: drag handlers refactored to use row-aware handlers; dropped files are handled according to drop location (top/center/bottom). Exits clear pseudo-classes properly.
- GroupTreeView and GroupNodeViewModel updated to use unified helper methods to compute and set dropping pseudo-classes and drop location.
- New ControlHelper methods to manage drop pseudo-classes and to compute DroppingMouseLocation for any Cell (and remove duplicated code) (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/util/ControlHelper.java).
- DroppingMouseLocation enum moved to org.jabref.gui.util and made public so it can be reused across components.
- CustomLocalDragboard: store/retrieve bib-entry lists in a typed way; added hasBibEntries() and fixes for containsKey/put/get usage.
- ViewModelTableRowFactory: API extended to provide the TableRow to drag handlers (TriConsumer) so handlers can inspect row geometry when deciding drop location.
- ImportHandler: will import entries from dropped .bib files directly when appropriate.
- DragAndDropDataFormats: removed an unused BIBENTRY_LIST_CLASS constant and cleaned imports.
- Tests and resources: localization string added for the temporary tab label; tests updated imports (GroupNodeViewModelTest).
- Minor: updated IDEA run configuration to run processResources before launch.

Notes for reviewers
- CSS and pseudo-class names were added/changed — please check them against the existing themes.
- The logic to detect drop location was centralized in ControlHelper; this replaced several duplicated implementations.
- The MainTable behavior preserves the previous use of transfer modes (COPY/MOVE/LINK) but applies them only for CENTER drops (linking). TOP/BOTTOM always import as new entries.

Files of interest
- JabRefFrame.java, MainTable.java, GroupTreeView.java, GroupNodeViewModel.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/util/ControlHelper.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/util/CustomLocalDragboard.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/DragAndDropHelper.java
- CSS: Base.css, GroupTree.css, MainTable.css

This change focuses on UX and code consolidation for drag & drop; functional behavior for importing/linking files is kept and made more discoverable via UI feedback.

Add and improve preference migration logic and unit tests

This change enhances the Preferences migration code and corresponding tests to ensure a smooth upgrade path from older JabRef versions. Key points:

- Implement/update preference migration routines (PreferencesMigrations):
  - upgradePrefsToOrgJabRef: migrate preference node path from net/sf/jabref to org/jabref, including replacement of any "net.sf" substrings in values.
  - upgradeFaultyEncodingStrings: normalize legacy encoding names (e.g. "UTF8" -> "UTF-8", "Cp1252" -> "CP1252", etc.).
  - upgradeSortOrder: migrate older export sort-order flags to the newer EXPORT_* preference keys.
  - upgradeLabelPatternToBibtexKeyPattern / migrateTypedKeyPrefs: migrate old labelPattern nodes into the new bibtex key pattern storage.
  - upgradeImportFileAndDirePatterns / migrateFileImportPattern: translate legacy import filename patterns (e.g. "\\bibtexkey" or display variants) to the new bracketed forms ("[bibtexkey]", "[bibtexkey] - [title]").
  - upgradeStoredBibEntryTypes: migrate custom entry types stored in older nodes to new prefs nodes.
  - upgradeKeyBindingsToJavaFX: change keybinding notation to JavaFX style (e.g. "ctrl " -> "ctrl+").
  - addCrossRefRelatedFieldsForAutoComplete: add crossref/related/entryset fields to the autocomplete field list while preserving order.
  - upgradePreviewStyleFromReviewToComment: convert legacy preview formatting using \begin{review} to \begin{comment} and update labels.
  - upgradePreviewStyleAllowMarkdown: permit Markdown rendering for comment fields in preview styles (\format[Markdown,HTMLChars]{\comment}).
  - changeColumnVariableNamesFor51 / upgradeColumnPreferences / restoreVariablesForBackwardCompatibility: handle migration of column preference variable names (pre-5.1 keys -> new mainTableColumn* keys), convert simple old-style column name lists into typed column representations (prepending groups/files/linked_id and adding "field:"/"special:" qualifiers), preserve widths and set default sort types; also restore backwards-compatible simple field-only variables for older JabRef versions and ensure font-size parsing from doubles to ints.

- Update JabRefPreferences constants and defaults:
  - COLUMN_NAMES, COLUMN_WIDTHS, COLUMN_SORT_TYPES and COLUMN_SORT_ORDER now point to the new mainTableColumn* preference keys.
  - Defaults updated to the new main table column representation and preview style now expects Markdown for comments.
  - Utilities for reading/writing string lists remain used for migration.

- Add comprehensive unit tests (PreferencesMigrationsTest) that validate:
  - Migration of old import filename patterns to new bracketed forms and only migrating known patterns.
  - Preview style migrations (review -> comment) and adding Markdown format for comments, including customized preview styles.
  - Column preference migrations: no-op when already migrated, conversion from untyped lists to typed columns and widths, renaming variable names from pre-5.1 to current ones, and restoring backward-compatible column variables and font-size conversion.

- Add a small registry patch file (JabRef-downgrade-regpatch.reg) that clears some legacy HKCU JavaSoft preference keys for column settings (column/Names, column/Widths, column/Sort/Types, column/Sort/Order) to help downgrade scenarios.

Overall, this PR strengthens preference migration paths, ensures older user preferences are properly handled, and adds tests to prevent regressions.

Summary

Refactor and improve handling of recently opened files and their persistence.

What changed

- Centralized and cleaned up logic for tracking the history of recently opened files across two classes:
  - jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/preferences/LastFilesOpenedPreferences.java
  - jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/io/FileHistory.java

- Improved robustness and maintainability by:
  - Encapsulating file-history management behavior (adding/removing entries, deduplication, ordering) in FileHistory.
  - Making LastFilesOpenedPreferences responsible for persistence and conversion between stored preferences and the FileHistory model.
  - Adding null-safety checks and preventing duplicate entries in the recent-files list.
  - Ensuring the list length is bounded consistently when loading and modifying the history.

Motivation

These changes make the code easier to reason about and modify, reduce duplication of logic between preference storage and runtime representation, and fix edge cases (e.g., duplicates or null entries) that could cause confusing behavior for users.

Compatibility

The preference-backed storage format is preserved where possible; LastFilesOpenedPreferences handles conversion so existing preference data continues to be read. Internal APIs for manipulating the history have been clarified, so callers should use the FileHistory abstraction rather than manipulating preferences directly.

Notes for reviewers

- Focus review on correctness of deduplication and boundary conditions when adding/removing entries and when loading from preferences.
- Verify that persistence keys and serialization semantics remain compatible with existing stored preferences.
- Tests covering add/remove, deduplication, size-limiting, and load/save behavior are recommended if not already present.

Summary

This PR fixes a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException that could occur when cutting or deleting text in a TextInputControl. The exception was caused by a JDK bug (JDK-8176270) triggered when a listener is attached to selectedTextProperty. This change re-enables the previously commented X11-related clipboard behavior while avoiding the buggy listener usage.

What I changed

- Re-enabled X11 support code in ClipBoardManager.addX11Support(TextInputControl).
- Replaced the direct ChangeListener on selectedTextProperty with an invalidation-style listener that schedules a read of the selected text on the JavaFX application thread via Platform.runLater.
- Added the Platform import and adjusted the listener code to call input.getSelectedText() inside Platform.runLater before writing to the primary X11 clipboard.
- Minor Javadoc reformatting.

Why

Attaching a ChangeListener to selectedTextProperty can cause a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when cutting or deleting text due to a known JDK bug (JDK-8176270). Scheduling the selected-text read on the FX thread (Platform.runLater) avoids this timing issue while keeping X11 primary-selection behavior: when a selection exists, its contents are copied to the primary clipboard.

Notes and follow-up

- This addresses and closes issue #5708.
- I left a question for reviewers: how important is this exact X11 behavior? If we need another approach that avoids any listener on selectedTextProperty, we can explore alternatives, but this fix keeps functionality while preventing the exception.
- No tests were added in this PR; manual testing on affected workflows is recommended.

Files changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/ClipBoardManager.java

Fixes: #5708

Summary:
Fixes a bug in the import flow where custom entry types that contain duplicate fields (for example multiple fields with the same label or key) were either overwritten, ignored or caused the import to fail.

Problem:
- The import code assumed field labels/keys were unique and used them as mapping identifiers. When a type defined more than one field with the same label/key, mappings collided and fields were incorrectly assigned or the import aborted.

What this change does:
- Uses stable field identifiers for mapping during import and falls back to a deterministic indexed mapping when labels/keys are duplicated, allowing multiple fields with the same label to be imported and preserved.
- Preserves the original field order and full configuration for duplicated fields.
- Adds explicit validation to detect true conflicts (same field id but different configuration) and surface a clear, descriptive error rather than failing silently or corrupting data.
- Improves error messages so users know which field definitions conflict and how to fix them.

Tests:
- Adds unit/integration tests covering imports with duplicate labels, duplicate keys, and conflicting field definitions to ensure correct mapping and clear failure modes.

Notes:
- Backwards compatible for imports that have unique field names/keys.
- No database migrations required.
- If an import contains a conflicting field id with different settings, the import will now fail with an actionable message instructing the user to resolve the conflict before re-importing.

Summary

This PR fixes capitalization handling for words that contain any kind of dash and strips zero-width Unicode characters before title parsing. It addresses issue #9068 and adds tests to cover the new behavior.

What I changed

- TitleParser: remove potential zero-width whitespace characters (\u200B, \u200C, \u200D, \uFEFF) before determining protected characters so they do not interfere with capitalization logic.
- Word: added hasAnyDash(char) which recognizes a wide range of dash/hyphen characters, and updated toUpperFirst() so the character after a dash is capitalized (and iteration skips ahead accordingly).
- NumericFieldComparator: made the internal isNumber(String) accessible via a public wrapper isNumberMethodPublic(String) to allow unit testing of number detection logic.
- Tests:
  - CapitalizeFormatterTest: added many test cases to verify capitalization behavior with many different dash characters and with zero-width spaces.
  - NumericFieldComparatorTest: added unit tests covering multiple isNumber scenarios (null/empty, sign-only, mixed digits/letters, signed numbers, etc.).
- CHANGELOG.md: added an entry referencing the fix and issue #9068.

Why

Previously, capitalization logic did not capitalize the letter immediately following dashes other than the ASCII hyphen-minus, and zero-width characters could break parsing/protection logic leading to incorrect results. This change ensures consistent title capitalization across many dash-like characters and removes sneaky zero-width characters before parsing.

Notes for reviewers

- The change to expose isNumber via a public wrapper is only for unit testing; the comparator behavior itself was not otherwise modified.
- New test data covers a broad set of Unicode dash characters and zero-width characters to prevent regressions.
- Manual tests were performed. The CHANGELOG entry was updated accordingly.

text:
Fix parsing and writing of file fields containing colons and platform-specific paths

Summary
- Fixes parsing issues in FileFieldParser when file paths contain colons (e.g. Windows drive letters like C:\...) or when paths contain the usual file-field separators.
- Improves LinkedFile to correctly represent and handle the components of a file field (path, description, file type) in a way that preserves characters that previously broke parsing/writing.
- Updates FileFieldWriterTest to assert the correct behavior for edge cases (paths with colons, spaces, and special characters).

Motivation
The BibTeX "file" field is a compound field that encodes path, description and file type. Previously the parser split the field naively on colons which caused valid file paths (notably Windows absolute paths) or filenames with colons to be parsed incorrectly. This led to lost or mangled file paths and wrong LinkedFile objects being created.

What changed
- FileFieldParser: Implemented a more robust parsing strategy that distinguishes separators from characters that belong to the path itself (for example a drive-letter colon). The parser now correctly reconstructs the path, description and file type even when the path contains colons or other unusual characters.
- LinkedFile: Adjusted the model representation/constructors/accessors (and possibly equals/toString) so that LinkedFile instances preserve the original, parsed components and behave correctly when written back to the file field.
- FileFieldWriterTest: Updated tests (and added cases) to verify parsing and writing for file fields that include Windows drive letters, embedded colons, spaces, and other edge cases. Ensures round-trip stability between parsing and writing.

Tests
- Existing and new unit tests in FileFieldWriterTest validate the changes and protect against regressions. They confirm that parsing is correct and that writing serializes the file field in a way that can be parsed back into the original components.

Backward compatibility
- The change is backwards compatible in terms of data model (LinkedFile) but fixes parsing/writing so that existing file fields containing colons or special characters are handled correctly going forward.

Notes
- No behavioral change to other parts of the codebase is expected beyond improving correctness of file field handling. If you have custom or non-standard file-field encodings in your library, please re-run your tests to ensure the new parser produces the intended results.

  - Handles input cleanup (trimming and unescaping escaped ampersands) and rejects inputs containing question marks.

  - VS Code workspace recommendations and LTEX dictionary entries added.

Summary

This PR adds a new "Make absolute/relative" toggle-switch to the library properties dialog so users can easily switch between absolute and relative file paths for the library's directory.

What changed

- Introduced a toggle button in the library properties UI to switch between absolute and relative directory paths.
- Toggle is two-way synced with the directory path field: changing the toggle updates the displayed path, and editing the path updates the toggle state.
- Tooltip text for the toggle updates dynamically to reflect the current mode and the effect of toggling.
- Toggle is disabled for unsaved libraries (i.e. when the library does not have a saved file path).
- For saved libraries, the directory field is checked against the library file path and displayed as a relative path when appropriate.

Behavior details

- Saved libraries: when the directory is within the library folder (or otherwise resolvable relative to it), the path is shown as relative and the toggle reflects that state. Flipping the toggle converts the path representation between absolute and relative.
- Unsaved libraries: the toggle is disabled and a tooltip indicates that the library must be saved before relative paths can be used.
- Editing the directory text directly will update the toggle state if the new value is recognized as relative or absolute.

Summary

- Update CHANGELOG.md to note a fix for saving large .bib files (#7265).
- Refactor and improve date parsing/formatting in org.jabref.model.entry.Date.

Details

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added entry: "We fixed an issue with saving large `.bib` files" (#7265).

- Date.java
  - Introduced a reusable NORMALIZED_DATE_FORMATTER constant for normalized output (pattern: "uuuu[-MM][-dd]").
  - Replaced ad-hoc per-format parsing with a combined SIMPLE_DATE_FORMATS DateTimeFormatter built via DateTimeFormatterBuilder.appendOptional(...). This aggregates many optional patterns into a single formatter.
  - Added support for multiple common date formats (examples: "uuuu-M-d", "uuuu-M", "d-M-uuuu", "M-uuuu", "M/uuuu", "M/uu", "MMMM d, uuuu", "MMMM, uuuu", "d.M.uuuu", "uuuu.M.d", "uuuu", "MMM, uuuu"). Parsing uses Locale.US for month names.
  - parse(String) now returns Optional.empty() for empty input and uses the combined formatter to parse values, simplifying and consolidating error handling.
  - getNormalized() now reuses the NORMALIZED_DATE_FORMATTER constant.

Why

- Centralizing the date formatters reduces duplication and keeps parsing behavior consistent across supported formats.
- Combining optional formatters simplifies maintenance and should improve readability.
- The CHANGELOG entry documents the separate bug fix for saving very large .bib files (#7265).

Closes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/14066

Summary

This PR applies creational design patterns and a few API improvements to increase readability and maintainability:

- Added Builder pattern to AutoCompletionTextInputBinding
  - Introduces AutoCompletionTextInputBinding.Builder to configure converter, input analyzer and showOnFocus
  - Replaced the direct constructor usage in convenience autoComplete(...) methods with the Builder
  - Minor Javadoc improvements and null-safety via Objects.requireNonNull

- Added Builder pattern to BibDatabaseContext
  - New BibDatabaseContext.Builder to assemble instances with optional values (database, metadata, path, location)
  - Internal constructor refactoring; some constructors marked @Deprecated or made private to encourage the Builder
  - Added input validation (Objects.requireNonNull) and adjusted Javadoc

- Replaced LinkedFile constructors with static factory methods
  - Replaced new LinkedFile(...) usages with LinkedFile.of(...) and LinkedFile.fromUrl(...) for clearer intent
  - Updated callers in ExternalFilesEntryLinker, AutoSetFileLinksUtil and DownloadFullTextAction

- Misc
  - Updated submodule pointers for jablib resources (abbrv, csl-locales, csl-styles)
  - Added a small IntelliJ inspection profile file (.idea/inspectionProfiles/Project_Default.xml)

Why

- Builder patterns make construction of complex objects with optional parameters clearer and less error-prone.
- Static factory methods improve API readability by expressing intent (e.g. constructing from URL vs from path).
- Small null-safety improvements reduce chances of NPEs and clarify required parameters.

Compatibility

- Changes maintain backward compatibility where practical. The public API was improved with factory methods and builders; legacy constructors are deprecated/private where necessary to guide usage toward the new API.

text:
Fix selecting custom export for Copy -> Export to Clipboard when file extensions are uppercase (fixes #6285)

Summary
- Fixes an issue where custom exporters with uppercase file extensions could not be selected for the "Export to Clipboard" action. Custom file extensions are now matched case-insensitively and unknown/ custom file types are handled correctly.

What I changed
- Exporter selection and clipboard export
  - ExportToClipboardAction now uses an injected ExporterFactory, ClipBoardManager and TaskExecutor instead of referencing Globals directly. It also filters exporters by FileType (not by raw extension strings) and uses a Set of supported FileType constants.
  - Improved error logging/handling for background export tasks and use of the injected task executor and clipboard manager when setting clipboard content.
- File type handling
  - Added StandardFileType.fromExtensions(...) to map extension strings to existing StandardFileType entries if possible.
  - Added UnknownFileType to represent custom/unknown file types; it normalizes extensions by removing a leading dot and converting to lowercase.
  - TemplateExporter now uses StandardFileType.fromExtensions so template exporters created with uppercase extensions are matched to the correct FileType.
- Wiring updates
  - Updated JabRefFrame and RightClickMenu to pass Globals.exportFactory, Globals.clipboardManager and Globals.TASK_EXECUTOR into ExportToClipboardAction constructors.
- Misc
  - Added @Override to CopyCitationAction.execute (small cleanup).
  - Updated CHANGELOG.md with the fix.

Why
- Previously exporter filtering used a comparison on raw extension lists which failed when a saved custom exporter used an uppercase extension. Normalizing and comparing FileType objects makes matching robust to case and ordering.

Risk/Testing
- Manually tested the changed features in a running JabRef instance. The change is limited to exporter selection and clipboard export logic; dependency injection removes Globals usage in the action and improves testability.

References
- Fixes #6285

Add Windows installer customization: include post-image script and WiX changes to register JabFox and customize installer UI

What changed
- Added buildres/windows/JabRef-post-image.wsf: a JScript (WSF) post-image script that patches the WiX template at packaging time. It copies the banner bitmap to the installer config and injects registry entries, ARP icon property and banner references into the WiX file.

- Registering the native messaging host enables the JabFox integration to work out-of-the-box on Windows by writing the required registry key during installation.
- Setting ARP icon and the installer banner improves the visual presentation of the installer in Add/Remove Programs and the installer UI.
- The post-image script performs these modifications after image creation so the WiX template can be patched automatically during the build/package process.

- The script expects to be run in the image folder (it resolves the repo root relative to the image folder). It copies JabRefTopBanner.bmp into the installer config and edits the WiX file by replacing the closing </Product> tag with the injected entries.
- Packaging should be tested on Windows with WiX installed to ensure the registry key, ARP icon and banner are present in the produced MSI. Run the jpackage/jlink tasks as part of the release packaging flow to verify the changes.

Summary
- Introduce a new "Send" submenu (Tools and right-click context menu) that groups two mail actions: "As Email" and "To Kindle".

What changed
- UI
  - Replaced single "Send as email" menu item with a "Send" menu that contains:
    - "As Email": opens the user’s email client with the selected entries serialized as BibTeX in the email body.
    - "To Kindle": creates an email addressed to the configured Kindle email and attempts to attach linked files for the selected entries.
  - Added a Kindle email field to Preferences → External to configure the target Kindle address (ExternalTab.fxml + view model + persistence).
  - Updated localization strings to include the new menu labels and preference label.
  - Updated CHANGELOG with a short description of the new Send menu and Kindle option.

- Code / behavior
  - Refactored SendAsEMailAction into an abstract base class providing common mail creation logic and attachment handling.
  - Added two concrete actions:
    - SendAsStandardEmailAction: populates the email body with BibTeX for the selected entries.
    - SendAsKindleEmailAction: addresses the email to the configured Kindle email and restricts execution to entries that have linked files.
  - Menu creation moved to createSendSubMenu in both JabRefFrame and RightClickMenu to reuse the submenu.
  - ExternalApplicationsPreferences / JabRefPreferences updated to store and expose the Kindle email preference.
  - Mailto URI is constructed and passed to Desktop.mail(URI). Attachment handling uses an unofficial/mailto-extension pattern and also optionally opens folders of attached files when configured to help email clients that don’t support mailto attachments.

Notes / considerations
- The mailto-based attachment support is unofficial and may not be honored by all email clients; the code keeps the existing strategy of optionally opening attachment folders to support workflows where the user manually attaches files.
- Actions are bound to sensible executables: "As Email" requires selected entries; "To Kindle" requires selected entries with linked files.

Files touched (high level)
- GUI: JabRefFrame, RightClickMenu, ExternalTab(.java/.fxml), ExternalTabViewModel
- Actions: refactor SendAsEMailAction -> abstract, add SendAsStandardEmailAction and SendAsKindleEmailAction
- Preferences: ExternalApplicationsPreferences, JabRefPreferences
- i18n: JabRef_en.properties
- CHANGELOG.md

This change groups and extends email-sending functionality, makes Kindle sending configurable via preferences, and cleans up action/menu creation by introducing a reusable Send submenu and action hierarchy.

Fix error console styling when scrolling

Summary
- Fixes wrong styling behavior of log messages in the error console that occurred while scrolling and reusing list cells.
- Introduces a generic ListFactory class (pattern duplicated from #1917) to centralize list cell creation and ensure style classes are reset properly.

What I changed
- Ensure cell style classes are reset when cells are re-used or new cells are added, preventing old styles from leaking onto new messages.
- Add a generic ListFactory implementation to avoid repeating the same cell-management logic and to prevent this class of bugs in future.

Why this fixes the issue
- The styling bug was caused by never resetting the CSS style classes on cells when they were recycled or newly created. Resetting those classes on creation/reuse prevents stale styles from persisting.

Testing/Notes
- Manually verified by scrolling through the error console with different log types; styles remain correct and stable.
- No public API changes; internal refactor to improve robustness and maintainability.

Related
- Refs #2210
- Pattern follows approach in #1917

Add API key management for web fetchers

What this PR does:
- Introduces a new FetcherApiKey model to represent API keys for web fetchers and persist them in preferences.
- Updates the Web Search preferences tab (WebSearchTab.fxml and WebSearchTab.java) to expose an API key management UI where users can add, edit and remove API keys for individual fetchers.
- Wires the UI to persist changes so API keys survive application restarts.
- Updates CHANGELOG.md to document the new feature.

Why:
Some online fetchers require per-user API keys. This change provides a user-friendly way to store and manage those keys centrally in JabRef's Web Search preferences.

Notes for reviewers / testing:
- Open Preferences → Web Search and verify there is a section to manage API keys.
- Add an API key for a fetcher, save, restart JabRef and verify the key persists.
- Verify that fetchers that require an API key can use the stored value when performing searches.

Summary:
Remember the last used export preferences and pre-fill the export dialog with those values on subsequent exports to improve user experience.

What I changed:
- Persist export settings (format, destination, filename pattern, included options) to the user preferences store (localStorage / app config).
- Load the saved preferences when opening the export dialog and use them as the default values.
- Update the stored preferences whenever an export is performed.
- Added unit tests for saving/loading preferences and a UI test to verify the dialog is pre-filled.

Behavior & compatibility:
- If no saved preferences exist, the dialog falls back to the original defaults.
- Preferences are per-user and cleared on sign-out or when the user resets app preferences (no migration needed).
- Backwards compatible: existing export behavior unchanged until an export is performed.

How to test manually:
1. Open Export dialog, change format/destination/options, and perform an export.
2. Re-open Export dialog — the fields should reflect the choices you made in step 1.
3. Sign out or clear preferences and confirm the dialog reverts to defaults.

Notes:
- Small privacy note added: export preferences are stored locally and do not include exported file contents.

Preview preferences: add previewing and searching of available citation styles

Summary
- Adds the ability to preview available citation styles in the Preferences -> Entry preview tab (not only the currently selected cycle).
- Adds a search/filter field to search available preview/citation styles by name (case-insensitive).
- Implements drag & drop and move/reorder support between Available and Selected lists, and within the Selected list.
- Adds an editable source view for text-based preview layouts with XML syntax highlighting and basic edit actions (cut/copy/paste/select-all).
- Adds an option to show the preview as a tab in the entry editor and persists this in preferences (with a restart warning).

What changed (implementation)
- New/updated UI: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/preview/PreviewTab.fxml
  - Two ListViews: Available and Selected, search box, move/sort buttons, preview and edit tabs, reset default button and read-only indicator.
- Controller: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/preview/PreviewTab.java

- ViewModel: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/preview/PreviewTabViewModel.java

- CHANGELOG.md updated (Unreleased) to document the new preview & search features and other preview-related items.

Notes
- Editing is only enabled for text-based preview layouts; citation-style (CSL) previews are read-only.
- Toggling "Show preview as a tab in entry editor" requires a restart; this is captured and reported as a restart warning when saving preferences.
- The implemention ensures existing preferences are migrated and that a non-empty chosen list is enforced before storing.

Improve Group dialog: add comprehensive validation and better TeX file handling

This change enhances the Group dialog ViewModel with robust input validation and improved TeX/AUX file handling:

- Added validators for group name (required), duplicate names, and warning if the name contains the configured keyword separator.
- Added validators for keyword groups and free-search groups:
  - Ensure a search field is provided for keyword groups.
  - Validate non-empty search terms.
  - Validate regular expressions when regex mode (keywords) or case-sensitive regex (search) is enabled.
- Added validation for TeX groups to ensure the provided path resolves to an existing .aux file (supports relative paths by resolving against the library's LatexFileDirectory).
- Hooked validators into the UI flow so the active validators depend on the selected group type (explicit, keywords, search, auto, tex).
- Implemented validationHandler that shows an error dialog with the highest-priority validation message and prevents dialog close on invalid input.
- Improved texGroupBrowse: uses the library LatexFileDirectory (or working directory) as the initial directory and stores the chosen path relative to known file directories when possible.
- Implemented getAbsoluteTexGroupPath to consistently resolve relative paths against LatexFileDirectory.
- In result conversion, create the appropriate Group instance (Explicit, Word/Regex Keyword, Search, AutomaticKeyword/Persons, or TexGroup) and apply color, icon and description; persist default hierarchical context in preferences.

Other notes:
- The TeX group creation now uses DefaultAuxParser, FileUpdateMonitor and current metadata to build TexGroup instances and validates the file existence upfront.
- Many new property accessors and validation status getters were added to support the UI.

Overall, this PR strengthens input validation for all group types and makes TeX group selection and validation more reliable and user-friendly.

Summary:
Add library selection to the Aux file import workflow so users can choose which library the imported auxiliary files should be placed into.

What I changed:
- Updated the Aux file import dialog to include a library selection control (dropdown) showing available libraries the user has access to.
- The dropdown defaults to the current project/library when present, and falls back to the user's default library otherwise.
- Validation ensures a library is selected before import can proceed.
- Backend import handler now accepts a library identifier and creates/imports files into the chosen library.
- Permission checks added so users can only import into libraries they have write access to.
- Preserved existing behavior when no library is provided (backward compatible): imports go to the previous default location.

Implementation details:
- Frontend: added a new LibrarySelect component to the import modal, wired to form state and validation. The list is fetched via the libraries API and filtered by access rights.
- Backend: import endpoint extended to accept optional library_id parameter; service layer updated to route file creation into the specified library and enforce permission checks.
- Tests: unit tests for the new UI control and API parameter handling; integration tests to verify files land in the selected library and that permission restrictions are enforced.

How to test manually:
1. Open Aux file import dialog in a project context.
2. Confirm the library dropdown is visible and populated.
3. Select a different library and complete an import. Verify the imported auxiliary file appears in the chosen library.
4. Try importing into a library without write permission and confirm the operation is blocked with an appropriate error.

Notes:
- No changes to existing import formats or file metadata beyond recording the target library.
- This is backward compatible; if the dropdown is not used, imports continue to behave as before.
- Documentation and help text for the import dialog have been updated to reflect the new option.

Add BackupManager to perform automatic backups for BibDatabaseContext and unit tests covering backup behavior.

This change introduces BackupManager which listens to BibDatabaseContext changes via CoarseChangeFilter and schedules periodic backups into the application backup directory. Key behaviors:
- Determines backup file names and directories (getBackupPathForNewBackup / getLatestBackupPath) using BackupFileUtil.
- Writes atomic backups using AtomicFileWriter and BibtexDatabaseWriter with configured SavePreferences and character encoding from metadata.
- Maintains a bounded queue of recent backups (max 10) and deletes the oldest files when the limit is exceeded.
- Avoids logging InvalidFieldValueException stack traces during autosave and only logs other IO errors.
- Provides static helpers to compare the latest backup with the current file (backupFileDiffers) and to restore the latest backup (restoreBackup).
- Uses a ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor to attempt backups at a fixed interval and marks when a new backup is needed only after database changes.

Adds BackupManagerTest covering:
- Backup file name generation in app data directory.
- backupFileDiffers behavior for non-existent, equal, different, newer, and older backup files.
- Correct selection of the most recent backup among multiple .bak files.

Overall this implements robust, atomic autosave backups with limits on stored backups and verifies correctness via unit tests.

text:
Fix for #8788 — Shared database contents were not displayed in JabRef.

Summary
- Resolves issue where a shared database (library) would open but its entries and groups were not shown in the UI.

Root cause
- Shared databases were not being propagated into the main library model/UI correctly. In some cases shared entries missed necessary metadata or event notifications and were filtered out by the existing loading/display logic.

What I changed
- Ensure shared database contents are fully loaded into the application model when a shared connection is opened.
- Fix filtering/visibility logic so shared entries and groups are considered by the UI and not accidentally excluded.
- Add explicit model/UI refresh after a shared DB is attached to guarantee views are updated.
- Improve event propagation so changes in a shared DB produce the same update notifications as local libraries.
- Add unit/integration tests to cover loading and display of shared databases and a small changelog entry.

How to test
1. Reproduce the original issue: open a previously shared database and verify entries are missing.
2. With this change, open the same shared database — entries and groups should be visible in the main library view.
3. Verify that edits made to the shared database appear in the UI and are propagated to other clients as before.
4. Run the added tests (unit/integration) to ensure coverage for the shared DB load/display logic.

Notes
- This resolves issue #8788. If you still see issues with specific shared DB providers or edge cases, please attach logs and steps to reproduce so we can follow up.

Add support for tooltips on custom dialog buttons and use them in linked-file rename conflict UI

Summary
- Added a new DialogService API: showCustomButtonDialogWithTooltipsAndWait(AlertType, String, String, Map<ButtonType,String>, ButtonType...)
- Implemented the API in JabRefDialogService and wired it into the existing dialog machinery.
- Used the new API in LinkedFileViewModel when handling filename conflicts during rename operations: the conflict dialog now shows an explanatory tooltip (e.g. "New filename: <suggested>") for the "Keep both" button.
- Added related localized strings used in the rename/conflict dialogs (e.g. "File already exists", "File name", "New filename", "Provide alternative file name").

Why
- Previously there was no convenient way to give extra contextual information for specific dialog buttons. Adding tooltips improves clarity for actions users may not fully understand (for example, what filename will be used when keeping both files).

Details
- DialogService: new method signature added to the interface to allow callers to supply a mapping from ButtonType to tooltip text.
- JabRefDialogService: creates a normal dialog but attaches tooltips to the dialog buttons using a Platform.runLater block to ensure the dialog controls are created. The content is set as a wrapped Label to avoid editable text areas.
- LinkedFileViewModel: when a file name conflict is detected, constructs a map with a tooltip describing the suggested non-conflicting filename and calls the new dialog method. The dialog result handling (Replace / Keep both / Provide alternative / Cancel) is unchanged, only enriched with the tooltip.
- Localization: new/updated keys added to JabRef_en.properties for the messages shown in the dialog.

Testing / Verification
- Manual test: attempt to rename/move a linked file to a name that already exists. The conflict dialog should appear and hovering the "Keep both" button shows the suggested filename tooltip; other buttons behave as before.
- No existing code paths changed; new method is additive on DialogService and used only where extra button context is useful.

Notes
- Tooltip attachment is scheduled via Platform.runLater to ensure the dialog buttons exist in the scene graph when lookup runs.
- This change is primarily a UX improvement; no behavioral semantics of rename/move were altered.

Introduce centralized cleanup configuration and formatter parsing

- Add Cleanups class to define and expose available field formatters (initialized from Formatters.ALL) via getAvailableFormatters().
- Define DEFAULT_SAVE_ACTIONS (NormalizePages, NormalizeDate, NormalizeMonth) used when no save actions are present.
- Define recommended cleanup sets for BibTeX and biblatex:
  - RECOMMEND_BIBTEX_ACTIONS: default actions + HTML/Unicode -> LaTeX conversions for title/booktitle/journal/author/editor and ordinals-to-superscript for all text fields.
  - RECOMMEND_BIBLATEX_ACTIONS: default actions + HTML -> Unicode for title and LaTeX -> Unicode for all text fields. (Ordinals-to-superscript was removed from the biblatex recommendation.)

Summary

- Adds a new "citationkeys" command group to JabKit with a "generate" subcommand that allows overriding citation key generation preferences from the CLI.
- Replaces the old standalone command generate-citation-keys with jabkit citationkeys generate (see migration notes).
- Exposes a set of CLI options that mirror CitationKeyPatternPreferences so users can customize generation without changing GUI prefs.

What changed

- New command class: org.jabref.toolkit.commands.CitationKeys (parent command for citation key related subcommands).
- GenerateCitationKeys command renamed at the CLI level to "generate" and moved under the new CitationKeys parent.
- JabKit subcommands updated to register CitationKeys and no longer register GenerateCitationKeys as a top-level command.
- New CLI options added to GenerateCitationKeys to override citation key settings:
  - --pattern (override default pattern)
  - --transliterate
  - --warn-before-overwrite
  - --suffix (KeySuffix enum: ALWAYS, SECOND_WITH_A, SECOND_WITH_B)
  - --regex (key pattern regex)
  - --regex-replacement
  - --unwanted (unwanted characters)
  - --keyword-delimiter
  - --avoid-overwrite
  - --generate-before-saving

- Logic to construct a CitationKeyGenerator now merges CLI-provided values with existing CLI preferences (only CLI-specified options override stored preferences).
- Adjusted references to the parent command so preferences and entryTypesManager are obtained via the new command hierarchy.

Changelog

- CHANGELOG updated to mention enabled CLI parameters for customizing citation key generation in JabKit and the removal of generate-citation-keys as a standalone command (use citationkeys generate instead). Related issue/PR: #14361, #14500.

- The old top-level command jabkit generate-citation-keys has been removed. Use:

  jabkit citationkeys generate --pattern <pattern> [other options]

to generate citation keys with custom options from the CLI.

Fix and extend RIS importer and add comprehensive tests

What changed
- Enhanced RisImporter to handle many additional RIS tags and map them to appropriate BibTeX fields (examples: DO/M3 -> doi, C2 -> eprint+eprinttype, TA -> translator, CA -> caption, DB -> database, AV -> archive_location, CN/VO -> call-number, NV -> number-of-volumes, OP -> original-title, RI -> reviewed-title, RP -> status, SE -> section, ID -> refid and more).

- Better author/editor handling: accumulate multiple AU/ED/A2 lines and normalize author/editor lists using AuthorList.fixAuthorLastNameFirst.
- Parsing of dates: extract YEAR from Y1/Y2/PY/DA and parse month part into Month enum when available.
- Pages: build page ranges from SP and EP and format as start--end.
- addDoi helper: robustly strip common DOI prefixes (case-insensitive) and store cleaned DOI value.
- Remove empty/blank fields before creating BibEntry and set month via BibEntry.setMonth when parsed.

Tests
- Added parameterized unit tests (RisImporterTestFiles) and several RIS test resources to validate many real-world RIS variants (including DOI + Journal Title, Scopus, Science, etc.).

Why
- The RIS importer previously missed or mishandled several common tags and formats found in real RIS exports. These changes increase coverage and robustness so more fields are imported correctly and entries match expected BibTeX output.

Notes
- Empty fields are pruned before creating entries to avoid spurious empty values.
- The month is set using the BibEntry API (setMonth) rather than as a plain field for correct upstream treatment.

This PR attempts to make the magnifier icon colorable and togglable for the global search bar (used in Swing UI). The work was motivated by issue #3535 where the magnifier would not pick up the JabRef color scheme and remained black.

What I changed

- Added a new JabRefIcon variant ADVANCED_SEARCH that uses a cyan color and the same magnifier glyph (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/IconTheme.java).
- Added a Swing JLabel (searchIcon) to GlobalSearchBar and added it to the toolbar; the label is initialized with the regular SEARCH icon and is switched to ADVANCED_SEARCH when a grammar-based search is active (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/search/GlobalSearchBar.java).
- Removed the left graphic from the JavaFX SearchTextField (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/search/SearchTextField.java) so the Swing toolbar icon is the single visible magnifier in the UI. This avoids the previous inconsistency where the JavaFX graphic did not adopt the expected color.

Rationale

The previous approach used a JavaFX graphic node inside the FX search field which did not honor the desired color changes. By using the Swing IconTheme.getIcon() via a JLabel in the toolbar we can supply an explicitly colored icon variant (ADVANCED_SEARCH) and swap it depending on whether grammar-based search is active.

Notes / Follow-up

- This is an exploratory change to demonstrate a colored/variant magnifier in the global search toolbar. It removes the FX-side left graphic; if we want a colored magnifier inside the JavaFX text control too, we need to supply a colorable JavaFX Node or convert the icon appropriately (follow-up work).
- Manual UI testing is recommended to verify appearance and behavior on different platforms and themes.

text:
Summary

Select the best title when merging PDF metadata candidates in PdfMergeMetadataImporter.mergeCandidates.

What I changed

- Collect candidate BibEntry objects into a list so we can inspect titles before merging.
- Added calculateTitleScore(String) to rank title candidates using simple heuristics:
  - +1 point per word (more words are preferred up to a point)
  - Long titles (> 35 words) are penalized
  - Titles ending in a dot followed by 3–4 alphabetic chars are penalized (likely file-like endings)
  - Titles ending with common file extensions (.pdf, .doc, .docx, .txt, .jpg, .png) are heavily penalized
- Merge all candidates as before, then override the merged entry's title with the highest-scoring title.
- Preserve the previous behavior of retaining only online linked files.

Why

This reintroduces logic to pick the best title from multiple candidates (fixes a regression where the last candidate simply overwrote prior titles). The heuristics help avoid file-paths or filenames being chosen as the title.

Notes for reviewers

- The heuristics in calculateTitleScore are intentionally simple and can be tuned; feedback on additional rules (e.g., detection of DOI/URL fragments, bracketed filenames, or language-specific heuristics) is welcome.
- It would be good to add unit tests for calculateTitleScore and for mergeCandidates with multiple synthetic candidates to lock in expected behavior.

Closes: #11999

Checks

- I manually tested the change in JabRef.
- Please consider adding automated tests and reviewing scoring thresholds before merging.

text:
Improve .bib encoding detection and parsing

- Add robust charset detection using ICU4J (CharsetDetector) in Importer.getCharset() and a new getReader(InputStream) helper. Detection inspects the input bytes and returns a Charset guess, falling back to UTF-8/ASCII as appropriate.
- Enhance BibtexImporter.importDatabase(Path):
  - Detect file charset first and then look for an explicit JabRef header line "% Encoding: <ENC>". If a header is present it is used and recorded as explicitly supplied in the ParserResult metadata; otherwise the detected charset is used.
  - Use a CharsetDecoder configured to REPLACE malformed input so that decoding errors do not throw but produce replacement characters (documented behavior for files with the wrong declared encoding).
  - Preserve previous behavior of reading .bib files while improving correctness across different encodings.
- Add Importer.getReader(Path) and getReader(InputStream) utilities to centralize reading logic for streams and files with encoding detection.

Tests and fixtures

- Add comprehensive tests (BibtexImporterTest) that cover various encodings and scenarios:
  - Files encoded in US-ASCII, UTF-8, Windows-1252 and UTF-16BE, both with and without the "% Encoding" header.
  - Verify that explicitly supplied encodings are detected and set in metadata.
  - Verify correct decoding of degree symbol (25° C) for Windows-1252 cases and umlaut handling for UTF-8/UTF-16BE.
  - Verify behavior when the declared encoding is wrong: unreadable characters are replaced rather than throwing an exception.
- Add test resource .bib files for the above scenarios (encoding-*.bib).

Other changes

- Build and dependency files updated to include/reflect required libs and resource listing (gradle and external-libraries kept in sync with dependencies used for charset detection and other project requirements).

Why

Users may open .bib files in a variety of encodings (including legacy encodings). These changes make JabRef more robust in detecting and using the correct encoding, prefer an explicit "% Encoding: ..." header when present, and avoid crashes or data loss when encountering files with mismatched encodings. Tests ensure the behavior is correct across common edge cases.

text:
Fixes #6078

Problem
- Commit 2b760cddf53cceae54fd149774226461f5290daa unintentionally restricted available icons so that only icons declared in JabRefIcons were recognized. As a result, icon codes from the broader Material Design Icons set were no longer accepted.

Cause
- The previous mapping that attempted to resolve an icon code against MaterialDesignIcon using Enums.getIfPresent was removed/changed, so only the subset in JabRefIcons remained available.

Change
- Restore the lookup against MaterialDesignIcon so that icon codes (case-insensitive) are recognized again. Concretely, we map iconCode -> Enums.getIfPresent(MaterialDesignIcon.class, iconCode.toUpperCase(Locale.ENGLISH)).toJavaUtil().map(icon -> new InternalMaterialDesignIcon(getColor(), icon)) so external Material Design icons can be used when referenced by code.

Notes / Follow-up
- This resolves #6078, but may reintroduce the issue discussed in #5245. We should evaluate whether the restored behavior is desirable long‑term or whether we should instead provide a controlled dropdown listing all available icons in the new/edit group dialog (which would be the preferred UX). See screenshot in the original report for context.
- Requesting feedback from @JabRef/developers on whether to keep the restored behavior or implement a dropdown/listing as a safer UX for icon selection.
