Add 'Make absolute/relative' toggle-switch to library properties

Summary:
- Adds a toggle control in the Library Properties dialog labeled Make absolute/relative that lets users switch how library file paths are stored and displayed (absolute vs. relative to project base).

Behavior and UI:
- The toggle is placed next to the path list in the library properties pane with a short tooltip explaining its effect.
- Flipping the toggle converts all paths for the selected library between absolute and relative forms and updates the preview immediately.
- Conversion uses the current project base path to compute relative paths.
- If conversion may break references (missing files or different drive letters), the UI shows a warning and allows the user to cancel or proceed.

Implementation notes:
- Introduces path conversion helper functions and integrates them into the library properties save flow.
- Existing import/export and storage code updated to use normalized paths produced by the conversion helpers.
- No automatic conversion is performed on load; paths remain as stored unless the user toggles the option.

Tests and QA:
- Unit tests added for the conversion helpers and edge cases (already-relative paths, absolute roots, cross-drive paths, symlinks where applicable).
- Manual QA performed to verify UI behavior and that no data is lost during conversions.

Compatibility and migration:
- Backwards compatible: libraries keep their current path form until the user explicitly toggles the switch.
- No database or file-format migration required.

Notes and future work:
- Added tooltips and a short inline explanation for first-time users.
- Possible future enhancement: batch-convert multiple libraries or a project-wide setting for preferred path mode.

Add Snap packaging for JabRef

What this PR adds
- snap/snapcraft.yaml: Snapcraft configuration for the "jabref" snap (base: core18, confinement: strict). Defines two apps:
  - jabref: main application (command: bin/JabRef)
  - browser-proxy: helper script (command: lib/jabrefHost.py) used for native messaging
  Features include: desktop/wayland/legacy plugs, home and removable-media access, network-bind, opengl, and system-files plugs for registering native messaging hosts.
  The snap reads its version from the bundled JabRef.cfg during the build and sets _JAVA_OPTIONS to point $SNAP_USER_DATA as the user home.
  The "jabref" part pulls the portable Linux distribution from the builds server, stages x11-utils, updates the native messaging host JSON to point to the snap-provided browser-proxy, and removes the original upstream launcher.
- snap/local/JabRef-launcher: A small launcher script placed into snap/bin/JabRef that executes the modular Java runtime from the snap and starts org.jabref.JabRefLauncher with passed arguments.
- snapcraft organizes the JabRef-launcher into bin/JabRef so the snap app uses the new launcher.

Why
- Provide an official Snap package so JabRef can be installed and confined on Ubuntu and other Snap-enabled distributions.
- Replace upstream launcher paths with snap-friendly locations and ensure native messaging hosts point to the snap helper.
- Use a minimal launcher to start the modular Java runtime packaged inside the distribution archive.

Notable implementation details
- The snap pulls the prebuilt portable distribution (https://builds.jabref.org/master/JabRef-5.1-portable_linux.tar.gz) as part of the jabref part.
- override-build extracts and sets the snap version from lib/app/JabRef.cfg and rewrites native messaging host JSON files to reference "/snap/bin/jabref.browser-proxy".
- The launcher uses $SNAP/lib/runtime/bin/java and module path (-p) to launch the application module org.jabref/org.jabref.JabRefLauncher.
- Confinement is set to strict; the snap declares multiple interfaces that may need to be connected after installation depending on the environment (desktop, removable-media, native messaging file writes, etc.).

How to build and test locally
1. Install snapcraft (if not installed).
2. From the repository root run: snapcraft
3. Install the produced snap locally (example): sudo snap install --dangerous jabref_<version>_amd64.snap
4. Run the app: snap run jabref
5. If native messaging integration is required, connect appropriate interfaces and ensure the host JSON files are written to the expected system locations (may require admin privileges or manual setup).

Notes and follow-ups
- Confirm the exact upstream portable tarball/version to use for releases, and consider switching to a released artifact rather than master build artifacts for stable releases.
- Verify which native messaging host paths require write access on target systems and whether additional snap interfaces or hooks are required for automated registration.

text:
Add CI deployment workflow and packaging support for cross-platform releases

This PR adds a complete build-and-deploy pipeline and supporting packaging resources to produce installers and portable bundles for Linux, Windows and macOS.

Key changes

- .github/workflows/deployment.yml
  - New GitHub Actions workflow that builds on a matrix (ubuntu/windows/macos).
  - Checks out full history, runs GitVersion and sets up JDK (AdoptOpen/Setup Java) per OS.
  - Builds runtime images with jlink and packages installers with jpackage.
  - macOS: rescinds and re-signs app binaries, produces DMG and signed/ notarized PKG; staples notarization ticket.
  - Creates portable archives for each platform and uploads build artifacts.
  - Deploys built binaries to builds.jabref.org via rsync when deployment secrets are present.
  - Uses secrets for API keys, signing certificates and notarization credentials.
  - Restores Gradle cache to speed up CI runs.

- build.gradle
  - Project configured to use Java 14/15 for compilation and packaging.
  - Application main class set and modularity patches for non-modular jars applied.
  - jlink and jpackage configuration for Windows, Linux and macOS with platform-specific options (icons, resources, installer options, file associations, vendor info, etc.).
  - Force-merge and merged-module tweaks to ensure jlink works with non-modular dependencies.
  - Tasks to generate ANTLR/XJC sources, bundle LibreOffice libs, pre-download dependencies, and run specialized test tasks.
  - Dependency update check with rules to ignore release candidates and other incompatible versions.

- macOS resources and signing
  - Added entitlements files (buildres/mac/myapp.entitlements and myapp.entitlements).
  - DMG setup AppleScript (JabRef-dmg-setup.scpt) and background images for DMG layout.
  - ICNS launcher / volume icons and README explaining DMG scpt and icon generation.

- Windows resources
  - JabRef-post-image.wsf to patch WiX-generated installer config (adds registry entries for browser extension and banner config).

- Icon tooling
  - svg2icns.sh helper script to generate .icns files from SVGs.

Why

These changes automate building, signing and distributing JabRef across all major desktop platforms from CI. It centralizes packaging logic in Gradle (jlink/jpackage) and ties it to a GitHub Actions pipeline that produces artifacts and (optionally) deploys them to builds.jabref.org.

Notes / Requirements

- macOS signing & notarization require secrets: OSX signing certs, notarization credentials and correct APP IDs/provider.
- jpackage must be available (BADASS_JLINK_JPACKAGE_HOME) for local runs or CI mac runner.
- Windows packaging requires WiX on the runner to build MSI installers.
- The workflow expects several repo secrets (SpringerNatureAPIKey, AstrophysicsDataSystemAPIKey, IEEEAPIKey, OSX certs, build server SSH key).

This PR focuses on CI packaging and deployment plumbing and on the platform-specific resources required to build installers. Please verify secrets and runner prerequisites before enabling automatic deploys.

Fixes issue #834 — Ignore non-displayable fields when computing field-name indentation during BibEntry writing.

What changed
- BibEntryWriter: getLengthOfLongestFieldName now considers only displayable fields when computing the longest field name used for alignment. This prevents writable-only or otherwise non-displayable internal fields from affecting the visual indentation of an entry.
- InternalBibtexFields: mark the key field as non-displayable and non-writable (it is handled specially when rendering/writing entries).
- Tests: refactored test setup by adding generateArticle1234() and added testSerializationOfNonDisplayableFields which verifies that a non-displayable writable field (e.g. __markedentry) does not influence the alignment/padding of displayed fields. Existing serialization test was adjusted to use the new helper.

- This is a quick fix to match how entries are shown in the UI; a longer-term fix is tracked in issue #574.

Summary

This PR implements several enhancements and bug fixes related to the global search UI, main table library column, and related model accessors. It also updates the changelog entries for recent features and fixes a small typo.

What changed

- Global Search
  - Added a separate search bar for the global search window (CHANGELOG updated).
  - The global search result dialog is now created lazily and reused instead of being recreated every time (GlobalSearchBar).
  - Double-clicking an entry in the global search results now: opens the corresponding library tab, clears the global search query, selects the entry in the main table, and closes the search window (GlobalSearchResultDialog).
  - Improved behavior for keeping the search window on top and persisted sizing: stage always-on-top is bound to the view model, and window height/width are saved/restored via Stage shown/hidden events instead of raw scene window handlers (GlobalSearchResultDialog).
  - Fixed preview update on selection change and corrected listener variable naming.

- Main table / Library column
  - Renamed the table view model property method to bibDatabasePathProperty() and added a getBibDatabaseContext() accessor (BibEntryTableViewModel).
  - LibraryColumn now uses bibDatabasePathProperty() to display the library (LibraryColumn).

- CHANGELOG
  - Added changelog items for the separated search bar and double-click behavior.
  - Added entries for BibTeX String copy/paste support and the new langid field.
  - Fixed a typo in the "Keywords field" changelog line.

Why

- Reusing the global search dialog reduces unnecessary recreation and preserves state where appropriate.
- Double-click support makes it faster to navigate from search results to the main table and the correct library tab.
- Exposing the BibDatabaseContext and clearly naming the path property improves API clarity for UI code.
- UI behavior improvements ensure the search window sizing and keep-on-top behavior are applied reliably.

Files touched (high level)

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/search/GlobalSearchBar.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/search/GlobalSearchResultDialog.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/maintable/BibEntryTableViewModel.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/maintable/columns/LibraryColumn.java
- CHANGELOG.md

Notes

- No behavioral changes to search results themselves—this PR focuses on dialog lifecycle, selection behavior, and UI polish.
- If other code referenced the old bibDatabaseContextProperty() method, it should be updated to bibDatabasePathProperty() or use the new getBibDatabaseContext() getter as appropriate.

Add Binaries GitHub Actions workflow to build, package and publish releases and PR artifacts for JabRef across Linux, macOS (Intel/ARM) and Windows.

What this workflow does
- Name: Binaries — triggered on pushes to main/main-release, tag pushes, pull_request events (opened/synchronize/reopened/labeled), merge_group and manual workflow_dispatch (with boolean 'notarization' input).
- Concurrency and cancellation to avoid duplicate builds for the same ref/event.

Key job flow
1. conditions: Determine whether to run builds/uploads and notarization based on event type, labels, repository owner, secrets and workflow inputs.
   - Skips early-access workflow for non-JabRef owners.
   - Requires label "dev: binaries" for PR uploads (except for certain label exceptions like "automerge").
   - Checks presence of BUILDJABREFPRIVATEKEY and other secrets; sets outputs used by downstream jobs.
2. build: Matrix build across: ubuntu-22.04 (amd64), ubuntu-22.04-arm (arm64), windows-latest, macos-13 (intel) and macos-14 (arm64).
   - Fetches full git history, runs GitVersion.
   - Sets up JDK, Gradle and (on Linux) pigz.
   - Optionally publishes JabLib to Maven Central when upload secrets are present and running on linux amd64.
   - Assembles the project, prepares merged jars/modules, and runs jpackage to produce installers and runtime images.
   - macOS: signs and builds dmg/pkg (when signing secrets are present), renames with version and suffix.
   - Linux/Windows: creates portable archives (tar.gz / zip) and repacks .deb for Debian compatibility.
   - Builds and packages JabKit similarly.
   - Uploads artifacts either to builds.jabref.org via rsync (preferred) or to GitHub Actions artifacts when upload is disabled/skipped.
   - Checks remote disk usage before rsync and installs rsync on needed runners (brew on macOS, choco on Windows).

3. comment-on-pr: If event is a pull request and upload-to-builds-jabref-org==true, posts a comment linking to the merge build on https://builds.jabref.org/pull/<PR_NUMBER>/merge (tagged as download-link). This job waits for the builds to be available.

4. notarize: Separate job (can be rerun independently) that runs sequentially for macOS platforms when notarization is required.
   - Downloads macOS artifacts from the workflow artifact store and uses xcrun notarytool + stapler to notarize and staple dmg/pkg, then uploads notarized artifacts to builds.jabref.org.

Notes and safeguards
- Uses secrets extensively: signing keys, macOS signing certs, notary password, and buildJabRefPrivateKey for uploading. If secrets are missing, uploads are skipped and jobs adapt accordingly.
- Provides outputs from build (major, minor, branchname) to other jobs so artifacts are correctly named and uploaded.
- Includes logic to avoid uploads for merge queue branches, and to only notarize when requested or for tag builds.
- Uses artifact uploads as fallback when rsync/upload to builds.jabref.org is disabled.

Why this change
- Centralizes cross-platform binary build, packaging, signing and distribution workflows.
- Enables reproducible releases and per-PR build previews on builds.jabref.org.
- Separates notarization into a re-runnable job to mitigate macOS notary timeouts.

How to trigger
- Push to main or main-release, create a tag, or open/update a PR. For PR uploads, add label "dev: binaries" or use a non-PR event. Manual run available via workflow_dispatch with optional notarization=true.

Add LinkedFileViewModel to manage linked file operations in the entry editor.

This view-model centralizes UI logic for a linked file and provides:
- Properties and bindings: downloadProgress, downloadOngoing, isAutomaticallyFound, isOfflinePdf, icon binding, and accessors for link/description.
- Validation: a warning validator that checks whether non-online files exist in the configured file directories.
- File actions: open, openFolder, edit, delete (with dialog to remove from entry or delete from disk), rename (prompt or suggestion) with overwrite/conflict checks, moveToDefaultDirectory, move+rename, and helper methods to check whether a generated name/path matches the current one.
- Download support for online links: checks SSL handshake (with user confirmation on certificate errors), prepares a BackgroundTask for downloads (maintaining/ restoring SSL defaults), infers file type from MIME or URL, ensures filename uniqueness, writes the downloaded file into the configured file directory and replaces the entrys link with a relative LinkedFile. Progress is reported via downloadProgress and the download is executed through TaskExecutor.
- PDF metadata handling: extracts metadata via multiple importers (verbatim, embedded, XMP, Grobid, content) and shows a merge dialog to replace the entry with merged metadata when the user accepts.

Implementation details:
- Integrates with LinkedFileHandler, PreferencesService, DialogService, TaskExecutor and database context to resolve paths and create suggested filenames.
- Uses URLDownload/FileDownloadTask for fetching remote resources and FileNameUniqueness to avoid overwriting files unintentionally.
- Includes logging for error conditions and reports user-facing messages via DialogService.

Behavior notes:
- Remote (online) links cannot be renamed or moved locally.
- Download and file operations surface errors and confirmations to the user when appropriate.

- Fixes an issue where the main table was not updated when grouping changed (issue #1903).

Notes
- The listen method is synchronized to be thread-safe.
- No other UI behavior was changed.

- Removed unnecessary '!important' declarations and cleaned up redundant rules.
- Added a small utility class to normalize font rendering for console output.

Testing:
- Manual verification across light/dark themes, window resize, and toggling the console open/closed.
- Verified that messages wrap correctly and scroll behavior is stable.
- Ran existing style/unit tests; updated snapshots where appropriate.

Notes:
- No functional changes to error handling or logging were made — this is purely styling cleanup.
- If you see any remaining edge cases on specific screen sizes, please add screenshots and steps and I'll follow up.

Add ADR-007: Provide a human-readable changelog

Summary:
This PR adds ADR-007 which documents the decision to adopt a human-readable changelog for the project. The ADR captures the motivation, rationale, chosen format, alternatives considered, and consequences of the decision.

Why:
A clear, human-readable changelog improves discoverability of user-facing changes, makes release notes accessible to non-developers, and provides a stable source for release communications and audits.

Decision and scope:
- Establish a canonical CHANGELOG.md (Markdown) organized by release with standard sections (Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, Security).
- Use PR metadata and short release-note snippets submitted with PRs as the primary input; provide guidance and a lightweight automation script/CI job to generate or validate entries.
- Document contributor guidelines for how to write changelog entries and how entries are curated.

Alternatives considered:
- Relying solely on autogenerated commit logs or third-party tools without a curated changelog.
- Manual-only maintenance without any automation.
The ADR explains why a curated, machine-assisted changelog was chosen.

Consequences and follow-ups:
- Adds slight maintenance overhead and a new contributor workflow (including guidance in CONTRIBUTING.md).
- Follow-up work: add generation/validation tooling, update CI to run validations, and retroactively populate recent releases as needed.

Files added:
- docs/adr/007-provide-human-readable-changelog.md

Notes on rollout:
The ADR should be reviewed and approved by maintainers. After approval, implement the tooling and update contributor docs before the next release to trial the new process.

- Users now see progress while the application searches for full-text PDFs.
- Download logic is centralized and reusable (prepareDownloadTask), reducing duplication.

- Invalid URLs are handled gracefully with an error dialog.

  - preferencesImportFailsWithoutFilePath: runs `preferences import` and asserts the command fails and prints an instantiation error
  - preferencesExportFailsWithoutFilePath: runs `preferences export` and asserts the command fails and prints an instantiation error

- Tests run locally: ./gradlew :jabkit:test --tests PreferencesTest

Notes
- These tests focus on expected behavior given the current PicoCLI setup (error on subcommand instantiation). If the CLI wiring is changed to use static/top-level subcommand classes in the future, the tests can be extended to cover successful import/export flows.

Notes
- If you want a different default configuration, update the default preferences provider used by MainTablePreferences.
- If additional preference fields are added later, remember to include them in the reset logic.

Summary

This PR contains two related sets of changes: updates to the changelog and a number of improvements and fixes to the EntryEditor GUI component.

CHANGELOG
- Added Unreleased notes for:
  - Integrity check for fields that store BibTeX keys (e.g. crossref and related)
  - Tracking which entry a downloaded file belongs to
  - Support for downloading multiple entries in one action

EntryEditor (src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/entryeditor/EntryEditor.java)
- Added support for additional field extras, including CROSSREF: the editor now returns the crossref extra component (FieldExtraComponents.getCrossrefExtraComponent) so cross-reference fields get the appropriate controls.
- Source panel / parsing improvements:
  - getSourceString now uses LatexFieldFormatter.buildIgnoreHashes to format source output consistently.
  - storeSource uses BibtexParser to robustly parse edited BibTeX source and provides clear error handling: if parsing fails the user is shown an explanation and offered to edit or revert the source.
  - lastSourceAccepted/lastSourceStringAccepted tracking ensures the editor behaves correctly after failed parses.
- Field storage and validation improvements:
  - Storing of cite keys and regular fields now performs validation (legal key checks, LatexFieldFormatter formatting) and gives visual feedback (valid/invalid background colors).
  - Cite key changes use panel.getDatabase().setCiteKeyForEntry and produce appropriate duplicate/empty-key warnings.
  - Undo grouping is handled for field changes that trigger automatic timestamp updates: when timestamp update is enabled, timestamp updates are included in the same NamedCompound undo as the original change.
- Keyboard and focus handling:
  - setupJTextComponent establishes consistent key bindings (store, next/previous panel, help, save, next/previous tab) and sets explicit focus traversal keys for text components.
  - Focus listeners ensure edits are stored when fields lose focus.
- Auto-link/file handling:
  - FileListEditor is tracked per tab where present; the AutoLinkAction will use the current fileListEditor and call autoSetLinks() (with a warning if none is available).
- UI/behavior tweaks and bug fixes:
  - Better handling of switching entries (storeCurrentEdit, unregister/register listeners when switching entries).
  - Ensure table selection/visibility is updated when the source is refreshed or keys are generated.
  - Improved TypeLabel rendering (antialiasing) and context menu for changing entry type.

Why this change
- Make the entry editor more robust and user friendly when editing raw BibTeX source and when working with fields that reference other entries (crossref, related).
- Provide clearer validation feedback and better undo behavior when automatic timestamp updates are active.
- Support new integrity checks and file-download tracking described in the changelog.

Notes
- The changelog has been updated to reflect the high-level user-visible changes in the Unreleased section.
- The EntryEditor changes are focused on behavior, validation, parsing and UI interactions; no external API or data-model changes were introduced.

Add a Linux .desktop template for packaging (buildres/linux/JabRef.desktop).

This commit introduces a desktop entry template that will be used during the build/package step to generate the final JabRef .desktop file for Linux distributions. The file contains the standard keys needed to show the application in desktop menus and associate mimetypes, while using placeholders that the build system should replace:
- APPLICATION_NAME, APPLICATION_DESCRIPTION, APPLICATION_LAUNCHER, APPLICATION_ICON: values to be substituted by the packager or build scripts
- DESKTOP_MIMES: placeholder for generated MIME type associations
- DEPLOY_BUNDLE_CATEGORY: placeholder for the Categories entry

Other details:
- Terminal=false so the app does not open a terminal window
- Type=Application and StartupWMClass=jabref to help desktop environments match the window
- Keywords include bibtex, biblatex, latex and bibliography

This template enables consistent desktop integration across Linux distributions; ensure the packaging/build scripts perform the appropriate placeholder substitutions before installation.

This pull request simplifies the change scanning mechanism in JabRef when detecting external changes to the bibliography file. Previously, a 3-way merge was used, which compared the last saved file, the current state in JabRef, and the new file state. This approach was complex and potentially error-prone, leading to issues like #5257. The PR introduces a simpler 2-way merge, comparing only the current state in JabRef and the new file state. This should make the logic more straightforward and help resolve the mentioned issue.

However, this change may have a small disadvantage in certain edge cases. For example, if two users modify the same entry in different ways and one user saves the file, the other user will see a less precise merge result. Specifically, fields that were added by one user might appear as removed when the other user reloads the file.

### Changes Made:
- Simplified the `ChangeScanner` class to perform a 2-way merge.
- Updated related classes (`DatabaseChangeMonitor`, `EntryChangeViewModel`, `EntryDeleteChangeViewModel`, `StringChangeViewModel`, `StringNameChangeViewModel`, `StringRemoveChangeViewModel`) to reflect the new merging strategy.
- Adjusted the `BibDatabase` class to use consistent methods for checking and managing strings.
- Added new test cases to ensure the new merging logic works correctly.

### Testing:
- Manually tested the changed features to ensure they work as expected.
- Added unit tests to cover the new scenarios.

### Documentation:
- Updated the CHANGELOG.md to describe the changes.
- Ensured that the documentation remains accurate and up-to-date.

### Issues Addressed:
- Fixes #5257

text:
Improve BibTeX importer encoding detection and handling

Summary
- Enhance BibtexImporter to reliably detect and apply character encodings for .bib files and to record whether the encoding was explicitly supplied in the file header. Added comprehensive tests to verify correct behavior across multiple encodings and scenarios.

What changed
- BibtexImporter:
  - Determine the file encoding by first running charset detection and then scanning the file for a JabRef encoding header ("% Encoding: ..."). If a supplied encoding is present it is used; otherwise the detected charset is used as fallback.
  - Use a CharsetDecoder with onMalformedInput(REPLACE) when reading files so unreadable characters are replaced instead of throwing, avoiding exceptions on malformed input.
  - Populate ParserResult metadata with the encoding and a flag indicating whether the encoding was explicitly supplied in the file.
  - getSuppliedEncoding now parses comment lines robustly (skips BOM, signature lines) and stops scanning when non-comment lines are encountered.

- Tests (BibtexImporterTest):
  - Added parameterized tests that cover files encoded in US-ASCII, UTF-8, Windows-1252 and UTF-16BE, both with and without encoding headers.
  - Verify that degree symbol and umlauts are read correctly for appropriate encodings.
  - Verify that the encodingExplicitlySupplied flag is set correctly depending on presence of the header.
  - Test behavior when an incorrect encoding is declared (malformed bytes are replaced) and that shared database ID is recognized.

Why
- Robustly handling different encodings and declared encoding headers prevents data corruption and parsing errors when importing .bib files created on different platforms or with different tools. The added tests ensure regressions are caught and behavior remains stable across various real-world encoding scenarios.

This PR brings several UI and UX improvements to the main application frame (JabRefFrame):

- Add a background task progress indicator to the toolbar. The indicator is bound to the aggregated task progress and shows a tooltip depending on whether tasks are running. Clicking the indicator opens a PopOver with a TaskProgressView listing running background tasks (with icons).
- Implement drag-and-drop support for opening .bib files. While dragging supported files, a temporary "Open files..." tab appears as a visual drop target; dropped files are opened in new tabs.
- Add and centralize key binding handling for common actions (navigation between libraries, focusing the entry table, starting new entries of various types, search focus, etc.).
- Schedule and show a telemetry opt-in notification shortly after startup if the user was not yet asked; record the user choice in preferences.
- Improve tab & window title handling: unique path parts are computed to disambiguate tabs, tooltips show absolute paths, and updateAllTabTitles keeps titles in sync when databases are added/removed.
- Persist side-pane divider position and react to side-pane visibility changes so layout is restored correctly.
- Enhance quit/close flow: wait for running background tasks before quitting, prompt to save modified libraries, convert/close shared DBs correctly, and shut down autosave/backup managers. Added a dedicated confirmation flow for closing individual tabs.
- Miscellaneous UI refinements: global search bar integration into the toolbar, clipping of the progress indicator to a square, and various internal refactorings to organize menu/toolbar creation and tab lifecycle (add/remove, autosave/backup registration, undo/redo listener registration).

No functional behavioral changes to existing features are intended beyond these UI/flow improvements; the code centralizes and cleans up many window/frame responsibilities.

Summary

Fixes koppor/jabref#521 — allow dragging and dropping of selected bibliography entries from one library tab to another.

Problem

Previously drag & drop only worked for a single entry or did not allow dropping selected entries across different library tabs. This prevented users from moving groups of entries between open libraries using drag & drop.

What I changed

- Updated the drag-and-drop/transfer handling so the currently selected entries are packaged and transferred together when a drag is started from a BibEntry table.
- Adjusted the drop target logic in library tab handling to accept and import multiple entries from another library tab and to treat the operation as a move when appropriate.
- Preserved selection and caret behavior after a successful drop (the newly-imported entries become selected in the target library).
- Added checks to avoid accidental self-drops and to handle cross-database imports correctly.
- Added unit/integration tests covering multi-entry transfer and drop acceptance between tabs.

How to test

1. Open two library tabs.
2. In the first tab, select multiple entries in the entry list.
3. Drag the selected entries onto the second library tab and drop.
4. Confirm the entries are imported into the second library and selected there; confirm they are removed from the source if the operation was a move.

Notes

- This change focuses on improving the user experience when reorganizing entries across open libraries and resolves the behavior reported in the linked issue.

Closes: koppor/jabref#521

text:
Enhance file type inference and download handling for online linked files

What this PR does:
- Improves LinkedFileViewModel's download flow by inferring the external file type more reliably:
  - First tries to determine file type from the server-provided MIME type.
  - If MIME type is not available, falls back to inferring from the URL suffix (using URLUtil.getSuffix + ExternalFileTypes lookup).
  - If neither yields a type, defaults to PDF (StandardExternalFileType.PDF).
- Sets the linked file's fileType to the suggested type name and uses the inferred extension when creating the suggested filename for download.
- Moves the file-type lookup logic into two small helpers: inferFileTypeFromMimeType and inferFileTypeFromURL, orchestrated by inferFileType.
- Keeps progress reporting and task handling: prepareDownloadTask now resolves destination filename based on inferred type, binds downloadProgress to the task, and updates the linked file on success.
- Injects ExternalFileTypes into LinkedFileViewModel via the constructor (already present in the constructor signature) and uses it for lookups.
- Adds error handling for invalid URLs and download failures (dialogs shown on failure).

Why:
- Downloads previously relied primarily on MIME type or defaulted to PDF which could lead to incorrect filenames and file types when MIME was missing. Using the URL suffix improves accuracy for common cases where servers do not provide MIME info.

Testing:
- Manual testing of downloads with known MIME types and with URLs containing various extensions. Confirmed the suggested filename, file type, progress binding, and linked-file update on success. Handled invalid URL and download errors with dialogs.

Notes / Future work:
- Icon inference still uses a fixed PDF icon; a TODO remains to select icons based on file type.
- Additional heuristics (e.g. Content-Disposition filename) could further improve filename/type detection.

Summary:
Enhance the DOI parser so it robustly handles DOIs that include special characters, URL-encoded sequences, and common surrounding noise (URLs, prefixes, and trailing punctuation).

What changed:
- Expanded parsing logic and regex to accept a wider set of characters that appear in real-world DOIs (parentheses, plus signs, percent-encoded bytes, slashes, dots, and other allowed symbols).
- Implemented preprocessing steps: strip common prefixes (doi:, https://doi.org/), trim surrounding angle brackets or quotes, remove trailing punctuation, and normalize Unicode (NFKC).
- Added URL percent-decoding for valid percent-encoded sequences while preserving invalid sequences to avoid accidental corruption.
- Improved normalization so we accept DOIs embedded in URLs or text fragments and return a canonical DOI string.

Tests:
- Added unit tests covering: raw DOIs with parentheses and plus signs, DOIs inside URLs, percent-encoded DOIs, DOIs with trailing punctuation, unicode variants, and malformed inputs to verify fail-safe behavior.

Compatibility and notes:
- No public API changes. Behavior is backward compatible and will accept more inputs than before; some previously rejected but valid DOIs will now parse successfully.
- Be aware that percent-decoding is applied only for valid encodings; malformed percent sequences are left unchanged to avoid data loss.

This change reduces DOI parsing errors observed in the wild and makes our DOI handling much more tolerant of real-world input formats.

- Add a WeakHashMap cache (AUTHOR_CACHE) for parsed AuthorList instances to avoid repeated parsing and improve performance.
- Minor trimming/normalization improvements during parsing and added/prepared cached formatted outputs for various name formats.
- Include/keep unit test (AuthorAbbreviatorTest) ensuring existing formatting compatibility between AuthorAbbreviator and AuthorLastFirstAbbreviator.

Summary

- Ensure repository initialization and pulling behavior are more robust for SLR (systematic literature review) repositories that may not have a remote configured.

What changed

1) jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/slr/StartNewStudyAction.java
- Instead of calling GitHandler#createCommitOnCurrentBranch directly, we now instantiate a GitHandler, call initIfNeeded(), and then create the "Initial commit".
- This guarantees the repository is initialized before appending to the initial commit.

2) jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/git/GitHandler.java
- Added a new method pullOnCurrentBranch():
  - Opens the repository and performs a git pull on the current branch.
  - If no remote is configured, it will perform a local merge (i.e., it no longer errors out when no remote is present).
  - Credentials are set if available, but missing credentials no longer cause an explicit IOException; the method attempts the pull regardless to support repositories without remotes.
- GitAPIException during pull is caught and logged (info) instead of being rethrown as an IOException.

Rationale

- StartNewStudyAction must ensure the repository exists and is initialized before modifying commits; calling initIfNeeded() fixes races or missing initialization.
- SLR repositories used by the application can be local-only (no remote). The previous pull behavior required detecting a remote and enforcing credentials, which caused failures during initialization for local-only repos. The new pullOnCurrentBranch implementation is tolerant of missing remotes/credentials so repository initialization and local merges succeed.

Notes

- The GitAPIException handler currently logs a generic message on failure. This keeps initialization resilient but may hide pull errors; follow-up improvements could refine logging and error handling (and correct the log message text if needed).

Notes for reviewers
- Focus review on the save/merge logic and the test cases that cover both existing records and new saves with keywords.
- No database migrations required; this is a logic fix in the save flow and frontend form handling.

text:
Cleanup and consistency improvements across importers, group logic, custom entry types and OpenOffice integration

Overview
- A set of refactors and minor fixes to improve correctness, readability and resource-safety across multiple packages: importer, groups, model.entry and logic.openoffice.

Key changes by area/files

Importer
- ImportFormat
  - Improved resource handling: reading files/streams with explicit Charset and try-with-resources convenience methods (getReader, getUTF8Reader, getUTF16Reader).
  - Added javadoc and clarifications for format detection and parsing behavior.
  - equals/hashCode and compareTo rely on format name; toString returns format name.

- ImportFileFilter
  - Small helper class wrapping ImportFormat with: descriptive display name generation (using StringJoiner), correct accept() behavior based on format extensions, and implemented Comparable/equals/hashCode for reliable usage in collections and file chooser UI.

Groups
- KeywordGroup, ExplicitGroup, SearchGroup
  - Serialization/deserialization and string representation logic kept intact; parsing and toString handling remains robust.
  - Added/verified equals() implementations to compare meaningful fields.
  - preserved deepCopy implementations and backward compatibility handling (legacy explicit group keys).
  - KeywordGroup: organized search/regex handling, case-sensitivity behavior, and keyword add/remove operations, with clear documentation and safe handling of JabRefPreferences separator.

Model.entry
- CustomEntryType
  - Parsing of custom entry type comments and helper methods for returning required/optional fields implemented with defensive immutability (unmodifiable lists) and capitalization logic.
  - getAsString() helper to produce a textual representation for storage/serialization.
  - compareTo/equals implemented to compare by name.

OpenOffice integration
- OOBibBase, OOBibStyle, CitationEntry
  - CitationEntry: consolidated page-info handling with Optional and change-tracking (pageInfoChanged()), equals/hashCode and compareTo implemented.
  - OOBibStyle: comprehensive parsing of OO bibliography style files (layouts, properties, citation properties and journal lists) with encoding support, defaults, and helper methods to format citation markers and full references. Improved robustness when reading/parsing style files and when converting numeric/textual citation markers.
  - OOBibBase: many routines that manage reference marks, insertion/removal of citations and rebuilding bibliographies; code organizes citation detection, unique identifier handling, refresh logic, and character-format checks in a clearer way.

Other
- General: many places use Objects.requireNonNull, Optional, and String utilities to make code more defensive and easier to reason about.

Why
- These changes tighten up equality semantics and hashing for objects used in collections, improve file/stream reading with explicit charsets and try-with-resources, and make OpenOffice citation/style handling more robust and maintainable.

No behavioral API-breaking changes are intended. The work primarily focuses on internal correctness, safety and readability.

text:
Closes #13031

Summary

This PR adds a small toggle button next to the three file-directory fields in Library Properties (Library-specific, User-specific and LaTeX file directory) that lets users convert the shown path between absolute and relative forms.

User-facing behavior

- New toggle button (icon) is shown next to each directory text field. The icon shows whether the current path is absolute or relative and clicking it toggles the path form.
- Tooltip is shown for each toggle and updates dynamically: "Switch to absolute path: converts the path to an absolute path." / "Switch to relative path: converts the path to a relative path." (localized strings added).
- Toggle buttons are disabled for unsaved libraries (no library file path available).
- When the user selects a directory using the browse dialog, the code sets a relative path if the chosen directory is inside the saved library folder; otherwise it sets an absolute path.
- The icon and tooltip keep in sync with manual edits of the text fields (listen to text changes and update icon/tooltip accordingly).

Implementation notes

- UI: added toggle Buttons, JabRefIconView icons and Tooltips in GeneralProperties.fxml.
- Icons: added ABSOLUTE_PATH and RELATIVE_PATH icons to IconTheme.
- View: GeneralPropertiesView binds new controls, updates icon/tooltip on text change, and disables toggles for unsaved libraries.
- ViewModel: GeneralPropertiesViewModel provides togglePath(StringProperty) to convert a directory value between relative/absolute (relative to the library parent path) and setDirectory(StringProperty, Path) to choose relative/absolute when browsing. InvalidPathException is caught and reported via dialogService.
- Path conversion rules: for saved libraries, if selected directory is inside the library parent folder, store it as path relative to the library parent; otherwise store absolute. togglePath converts the currently shown value to the other form using the library parent as base.

Developer notes / API changes

- Method name changed: librarySpecificDirectoryPropertyProperty() -> librarySpecificDirectoryProperty(). Update call sites if necessary.
- New methods added: togglePath(StringProperty) and private setDirectory(StringProperty, Path).
- Updated files: GeneralPropertiesView(.java/.fxml/.properties/ViewModel), IconTheme, CHANGELOG.md and English localization file.

Other

- CHANGELOG updated to mention the new toggle and the relative-path display behavior.
- Localization entries added for both tooltip messages.

Screenshots

Provided in the issue/PR description illustrate saved vs unsaved library states.

Remove OrdinalsToSuperscriptFormatter from recommended biblatex save actions

Fixes #2596

Summary:
This PR removes OrdinalsToSuperscriptFormatter from the list of recommended save actions for the biblatex profile. It resolves a conflict between OrdinalsToSuperscriptFormatter and LatexToUnicode, which were both recommended for the same fields.

Reasoning:
- LatexToUnicode provides Unicode output suitable for biblatex, which is typically used with UTF-8.
- Having both formatters recommended caused conflicting transformations; removing OrdinalsToSuperscriptFormatter avoids that conflict while preserving correct Unicode conversion.

Impact:
Users of the biblatex profile should see no loss of functionality when working with UTF-8; ordinal superscripts will rely on Unicode conversion via LatexToUnicode rather than the removed formatter.

Summary

This PR adds and configures the repository's CI and automation tooling and ships developer-facing documentation improvements. The main changes introduce/define GitHub Actions workflows for building, testing, deploying and maintaining auxiliary resources (journal abbreviation lists), and ensure the build configuration and docs reflect the developer setup.

Key changes

- .github/workflows/deployment.yml
  - Multi-platform build matrix (linux, windows, macOS) to create runtime images, installers and portable artifacts.
  - macOS code signing, DMG/pkg creation and notarization steps when secrets are present and a tag is pushed.
  - Uses GitVersion to derive versions and renames artifacts accordingly.
  - Uploads build artifacts and, when signing secrets are present, deploys releases to builds.jabref.org via rsync using a deploy job.
  - Concurrency configuration to cancel in-progress builds on ref changes.

- .github/workflows/tests.yml
  - Comprehensive test workflow with multiple jobs: checkstyle, unit tests, database tests (PostgreSQL and MySQL), GUI tests, code coverage upload (optional when CODECOV_TOKEN is present), and gradle wrapper validation.
  - Uses JDK 19 and configures Gradle/Jacoco steps consistently for CI.

- .github/workflows/tests-fetchers.yml
  - Dedicated workflow for fetcher-related tests (triggered on changes to fetcher code and scheduled weekly), using environment secrets for external fetcher APIs.

- .github/workflows/refresh-journal-lists.yml
  - Workflow to refresh journal abbreviation lists by cloning the abbrv.jabref.org repo, preparing the input files, and invoking Gradle's generateJournalAbbreviationList task.
  - Creates a branch and opens a PR automatically via peter-evans/create-pull-request so journal data updates are reviewed.

- build.gradle
  - Adds/maintains tasks for code generation and packaging used by CI, notably generateJournalAbbreviationList (consumes build/journals and writes resources into src/main/resources/journals).
  - Configures jlink/jpackage options and platform-specific packaging behavior that CI relies on.
  - Various Gradle and plugin configurations to keep local builds and CI aligned (JDK 19, JavaFX, jacoco, checkstyle, test tasks, etc.).

- docs/getting-into-the-code/guidelines-for-setting-up-a-local-workspace.md
  - Detailed, step-by-step guide for setting up a local development workspace (IDE setup for IntelliJ/Eclipse, JDK 19, Gradle usage, importing code style and checkstyle, running tests, common pitfalls and troubleshooting).

- README.md
  - Project overview and pointers to builds and installation docs (unchanged functionally but included in context).

Why

- Centralize and standardize CI pipeline: build, test and package artifacts across platforms.
- Automate distribution of development builds to builds.jabref.org when deploy secrets are available.
- Keep journal abbreviation data current by automating the refresh and opening a PR for review.
- Provide developers clear local setup instructions so their environments match CI expectations (JDK 19, Gradle, generated sources).

Notes for reviewers / required setup

- CI depends on several repository secrets for full functionality (macOS signing and notarization, deploy SSH key, API keys, CODECOV_TOKEN). When these are not present, the workflows skip signing/notarization and deployment steps but still build and upload artifacts to GitHub Actions.
  - Expected secrets (examples): OSX_SIGNING_CERT, OSX_CERT_PWD, OSX_NOTARIZATION_APP_USERNAME, OSX_NOTARIZATION_APP_PWD, buildJabRefPrivateKey, CODECOV_TOKEN, SPRINGERNATUREAPIKEY_FOR_TESTS, etc.
- The macOS packaging/notarization path will only run on macOS runners and only if signing secrets are set.
- The Refresh Journal Lists workflow creates an update branch and a PR; ensure the bot/GITHUB_TOKEN has permission to open PRs (the workflow already sets write permissions for contents and pull-requests).

Testing

- CI workflows are defined and ready to run. Verify by triggering workflow_dispatch or by pushing changes to main (or the appropriate paths) to see the matrix build and test jobs execute.
- Local developers should follow docs/getting-into-the-code/guidelines-for-setting-up-a-local-workspace.md to reproduce builds and generate journal resources (./gradlew generateJournalAbbreviationList).

If anything else should be split into smaller PRs (for example macOS notarization secrets or deployment automation), I can split the changes accordingly.

Introduce a reusable WebView pool and switch preview & MathSciNet tabs to use it

This PR adds a dynamic WebViewStore to preload and recycle JavaFX WebView instances to prevent UI freezes when creating WebViews on demand. Key changes:

- Add WebViewStore (logic/util):
  - Provides init(Configuration) and init() overloads to preload instances on the JavaFX thread (via Platform.runLater).
  - Exposes get() to obtain a WebView instance, hasMore() to check availability, and a Configuration record to control preloaded/minimum instance counts.
  - Throws an IllegalStateException if used before initialization.

- Initialize WebViewStore at application startup (JabRefGUI):
  - WebViewStore.init() is called early during GUI initialization so preloaded WebViews are available when needed.

- Use WebViewStore in preview and entry editor tabs:
  - PreviewViewer and MathSciNetTab now obtain their WebView from WebViewStore.get() instead of creating new instances.
  - Navigation is disabled for embedded MathSciNet WebView and preview context menus are disabled to prevent unexpected interactions.

- Preview improvements (PreviewViewer):
  - Search highlighting is handled via injected mark.js logic; when updating highlights we unmark and mark using a safely constructed JavaScript regex.
  - A helper creates a JS RegExp string and properly escapes unescaped forward slashes from Java regex patterns.
  - Ensures theme CSS is applied and anchors in the preview open in the external browser (JabRefDesktop).

Other notes:
- WebViewStore preloads WebView instances asynchronously on the FX thread to avoid blocking the UI during startup.
- Callers must ensure WebViewStore.init() is invoked before calling get(), otherwise an IllegalStateException will be thrown.

Introduce dedicated preferences classes for main table column configuration and main-table behavior, and wire them into the GUI preferences system.

- Misc: helper methods to serialize/deserialize column properties and to construct self-contained export save orders using the current table sort order.

text:
Fix UTF BOM parsing

Background:
The parser did not reliably detect or strip UTF byte order marks (BOMs), which caused incorrect decoding or unexpected characters at the start of files/streams (common with UTF-8, UTF-16 LE/BE). This led to malformed output and downstream failures when reading files containing a BOM.

What this PR does:
- Properly detects and removes BOMs for UTF-8 and UTF-16 (LE/BE) at the start of input data before decoding.
- Ensures the encoding detection/decoding path handles BOMs consistently, preventing extra characters from appearing in parsed output.
- Adds unit tests covering files/streams with and without BOMs for UTF-8 and UTF-16 variants.

Why this change:
- Makes parsing robust across files produced by different tools/editors that include BOMs.
- Prevents subtle bugs caused by leading BOM characters in parsed strings.

Notes:
- Backwards-compatible: inputs without BOMs are unaffected.
- Tests included to prevent regressions.

Files changed: parser and encoding utilities, plus tests.

Summary

Remove unnecessary re-loading of preferences into all ViewModels when saving preferences. The call to setValues (which triggered a full "load" into all ViewModels whenever a preference changed) is not required and has been removed.

Problem

When a preference was changed, the code executed a re-load of preferences into all ViewModels. This was introduced earlier and persisted through a refactor (#10659). This forced redundant updates and could cause unnecessary side effects and performance overhead.

What I changed

- Remove the redundant setValues call executed during preference storing.
- Ensure preferences are written to storage without forcing a global reload of ViewModels.

Why this is safe

- Storing preferences still persists values as before. The change only avoids propagating a full reload to every ViewModel immediately after a save, which was unnecessary and could trigger extra UI updates or side effects.
- No change in persistence format or API behavior for consumers of the preferences.

Impact

- Reduced redundant updates and potential performance improvement when saving preferences.
- Fewer unexpected side effects caused by mass reloading of ViewModels.

Testing & Checklist

- Manual testing of preference changes performed to verify values are saved and effective where needed.
- No user-visible behavior change besides reduced redundant updates.

Notes for reviewers

- This reverts the behavior introduced earlier (see #10659) where a global reload was triggered on each preference save. Please pay attention to places that previously relied on that global reload; if any component expects immediate propagation via that mechanism, it should instead subscribe to preference change events or read the preference explicitly.

If desired, I can add targeted tests to validate no unwanted reloads occur and to ensure preference persistence remains correct.

text:
Fix keyboard shortcuts editing in Preferences (closes #14237)

Summary
- Bug: Key events for editing keyboard shortcuts in Preferences → Keyboard shortcuts were consumed by global application shortcuts and never reached the shortcut editor. As a result, pressing keys did not update the selected shortcut and changes were not persisted.
- Fixes:
  - Add a KeyEvent filter in KeyBindingsTab so the TreeTableView receives key presses and the event is forwarded to the view model (viewModel.setNewBindingForCurrent).
  - Update KeyBindingsTabViewModel.storeSettings() to correctly persist edited shortcuts by syncing the UI repository into GuiPreferences instead of relying on an equality check.
  - Update and add unit tests to verify the behavior and persistence of edited shortcuts.
  - Add a changelog entry noting the fix.

Files changed
- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/keybindings/KeyBindingsTab.java
  - Add KeyEvent import, set an event filter and forward events to the ViewModel so editing works reliably.
- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/keybindings/KeyBindingsTabViewModel.java
  - Implemented storeSettings() to copy bindings into GuiPreferences and add restart warning.
- jabgui/src/test/java/org/jabref/gui/keyboard/KeyBindingsTabModelTest.java
  - Adjusted expectations to match updated repository behavior.
- jabgui/src/test/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/keybindings/KeyBindingViewModelTest.java
  - Added a new test that verifies storeSettings writes changes to preferences and annotated CI-unstable tests with DisabledOnCIServer.
- CHANGELOG.md
  - Note about fixing keybindings editing and saving.

Testing steps
1. Open JabRef → Preferences → Keyboard shortcuts.
2. Select any shortcut (e.g., “Close library”).
3. Press a new key combination (e.g., Ctrl+Shift+L).
4. Click Save and restart JabRef.
5. Verify the new shortcut is shown in the list and works in the application.

Notes
- This change ensures the shortcut editor receives key events before global shortcuts consume them and guarantees the edited bindings are persisted to GuiPreferences.
- Tests added/adjusted to cover the fix; some tests are marked DisabledOnCIServer because they run reliably only locally.

Closes: #14237

Fix file field parser not recognizing online URLs

This PR ensures that the FileFieldParser recognizes and correctly handles online URLs in file fields. Previously URLs exported (e.g. from Citavi) were not detected as online links and could not be imported.

Changes:
- Detect online links at the start of FileFieldParser.parse(...) using LinkedFile.isOnlineLink(value.trim()) and return a LinkedFile constructed from the URL.
- Catch MalformedURLException and log an error (added SLF4J Logger to FileFieldParser).
- Add unit tests to cover a plain URL and a URL represented as a file entry.
- Update CHANGELOG with the user-facing fix note.

This addresses and fixes #7882.

- Manually tested the built-in preview to confirm strikethrough and task lists are no longer rendered and that other preview functionality remains intact.
- No new tests were added (feature removal). Consider adding UI/tests if we want to prevent regressions in rendering behavior in the future.

Notes / Follow-ups

- If users need these features back, they can reintroduce a rendering extension or re-add the removed dependencies, but this increases maintenance and compatibility risks.
- Documentation and changelog: please add a short note to CHANGELOG.md and user docs if desired to inform users about the changed preview behavior.

text:
Closes #14505

Summary

This PR fixes resetting of proxy preferences. It ensures proxy settings are returned to sane defaults when preferences are cleared or when importing incomplete/corrupt preference files.

What I changed

- Added a private no-arg constructor to ProxyPreferences and a static getDefault() factory returning default proxy values (proxy disabled, empty hostname, port "80", authentication disabled, no username/password, do not persist password).
- Added ProxyPreferences.setAll(...) to copy all values from another ProxyPreferences instance.
- Removed hard-coded proxy defaults from JabRefCliPreferences.defaults map to centralize default handling in ProxyPreferences.
- When clearing preferences (JabRefCliPreferences.clear()), proxy preferences are now explicitly reset to ProxyPreferences.getDefault().
- When importing preferences (JabRefCliPreferences.importPreferences(...)), in case of incomplete/corrupt XML the proxy preferences fall back to defaults.
- Refactored getProxyPreferences() to use a new helper getProxyPreferencesFromBackingStore(ProxyPreferences defaults), so values are read from the backing store with fallback to the provided defaults.

Why

Previously proxy preferences could remain in an inconsistent state after clearing preferences or importing a broken preferences file. Centralizing the defaults in ProxyPreferences and using setAll(...) ensures reliable reset behavior and a single source of truth for default proxy values.

How to test

1. Launch JabRef.
2. Open preferences and configure proxy settings (enable proxy, set hostname/port, enable authentication and set credentials, optionally persist password).
3. Verify proxy settings are active.
4. Clear preferences (or use the application action that triggers clearing all preferences) and restart JabRef.
   - Expected: Proxy settings are reset to defaults (proxy disabled, hostname empty, port "80", authentication disabled, username/password empty, persistPassword false).
5. Alternatively, attempt to import an incomplete/corrupt preferences XML file and verify proxy preferences fall back to defaults.

Notes

- This change does not modify keyring behavior for persisted passwords — it only ensures in-memory preference objects and backing-store reads/writes use proper defaults.
- No additional user-visible UI changes except that resetting preferences now reliably resets proxy settings.

Checklist

- [x] I manually tested my changes in running JabRef
- [ ] I added JUnit tests for changes (if applicable)
- [ ] I updated CHANGELOG.md / user documentation (if applicable)

text:
Summary

Adds a new Send to Kindle feature that allows users to send articles to their Kindle devices from the app.

What this PR does

- Adds a Send to Kindle action to the article/share UI.
- Adds a user setting for storing a Kindle email address and an opt-in toggle.
- Implements server-side conversion and delivery pipeline: generates a Kindle-friendly file (EPUB/MOBI), queues a background job, and sends the file to the configured Kindle email via the existing mailer infrastructure.
- Adds rate limiting and validations to prevent abuse (limits per user and per-article checks).
- Adds background worker integration (uses existing job queue) with retry and error handling and stores last delivery status on the article send record.
- Adds tests covering conversion, queuing, email delivery, and settings validation.
- Adds basic UI/UX and accessibility handling for the new setting and Send to Kindle flow.

Why

Users requested an easy way to read saved articles on Kindle devices. This feature builds a lightweight, reliable path to export content for offline reading on Kindle.

Data and config changes

- Database: adds a new column/table for storing user kindle email and delivery records (migration included).
- Env vars: documents required SMTP credentials and optional conversion service API key (if applicable).

How to use

1. Go to Account Settings -> Reading Devices and enter your Kindle email (name@kindle.com) and opt in.
2. Open any article and click Send to Kindle in the share menu.
3. The app queues a job; you will receive the article at your Kindle email. Delivery status is visible in the article send history.

Testing notes

- Manual: enter a test Kindle address, click Send to Kindle, and verify the queued job and outbound email (or local mailer preview) contains the generated file attachment.
- Automated: unit/integration tests added for conversion, job enqueueing, mailer invocation, and settings validation.

Notes and follow-ups

- Conversion quality and formats may be iterated on; current implementation produces EPUB with basic styling converted to MOBI when required.
- We may add a delivery retry UI and per-user send quotas in a follow-up.

No breaking changes expected.

- Manually tested the Save / Save as and Open dialogs in a running JabRef build and verified that filters display the name plus extensions.

Closes #14414

Summary

This PR adds reset functionality for the entry table column preferences so that clearing preferences correctly restores the main table configuration and column layout to their defaults.

What changed

- ColumnPreferences
  - Added a private default constructor that defines the hardcoded default column layout.
  - Added ColumnPreferences.getDefault() to obtain default column preferences.
  - Added setAll(ColumnPreferences) to replace the current values with another ColumnPreferences instance.

- MainTablePreferences
  - Added a private default constructor and MainTablePreferences.getDefault().
  - Added setAll(MainTablePreferences) to replace the current values with another MainTablePreferences instance.

- JabRefGuiPreferences
  - clear() now resets main table and column preferences to their defaults by calling setAll(...) with MainTablePreferences.getDefault() and ColumnPreferences.getDefault().
  - importPreferences(...) now restores main table/column preferences from the backing store with proper fallback to defaults.
  - Replaced the older manual assembly of main table/column prefs with helper methods getMainTablePreferencesFromBackingStore(...) and getMainTableColumnPreferencesFromBackingStore(...), which return defaults when no stored values exist.

Files modified
- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/maintable/ColumnPreferences.java
- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/maintable/MainTablePreferences.java
- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/JabRefGuiPreferences.java

Behavioral notes

- Calling preferences.clear() will now restore the entry table columns to the original default layout instead of leaving them overridden.
- The default column configuration is defined in ColumnPreferences and used as the fallback when no stored column configuration exists in the backing store.

Testing

- Manual testing was performed in a running JabRef instance to verify that clearing preferences resets the table columns to defaults.

This change ensures that preference resets behave consistently and that users who clear preferences will get the original main table/column layout back.

- Add/adjust a comprehensive set of unit tests (FileUtilTest) covering extension extraction, copying semantics, relativization, recursive find, detection of illegal file names, filename shortening edge cases, and the LaTeX-removal behavior for generated filenames.

These fixes make file naming and lookup more robust across platforms and use cases, and add test coverage for previously failing edge cases.

text:
Fixes #6621 — disable automatic synchronization of special fields to keywords by default.

Summary
- Change default preferences so special-field -> keyword auto-sync is disabled by default and special-field serialization default is enabled.
- Update the changelog to reflect the behavior change.

Behavior changes
- New default: AUTOSYNCSPECIALFIELDSTOKEYWORDS = false (was true). This means newly installed JabRef will not automatically sync special fields (ranking, priority, read status, relevance, quality, printed) into the keywords field unless the user enables it.
- SERIALIZESPECIALFIELDS default changed to true.

Refactor and cleanup
- Introduced and used SpecialFieldsPreferences accessors (isSpecialFieldsEnabled(), shouldAutoSyncSpecialFieldsToKeyWords(), shouldSerializeSpecialFields(), plus isKeywordSyncEnabled() which returns specialFieldsEnabled && autoSyncSpecialFieldsToKeyWords) and updated call sites to use preferences.getSpecialFieldsPreferences().isKeywordSyncEnabled() instead of Globals.prefs.getBoolean(...).
- Reduced direct calls to JabRefPreferences.get()/put() in many places; PreferencesService no longer exposes isKeywordSyncEnabled() directly.
- ParserResult: added getPath() returning Optional<Path> and deprecated getFile(). Updated code to compare/use Paths instead of Files/Strings where appropriate.
- Wiring changes: RightClickMenu copy/export actions now receive a ClipBoardManager instead of using Globals.clipboardManager directly; MainTable construction updated for dependency injection.
- Small API/UX cleanups and modernization: replaced many switch statements with Java switch expressions, simplified event handlers, and fixed several minor path/name-handling bugs.

Files touched (high level)
- CHANGELOG.md: documented default change.
- Preferences: JabRefPreferences, PreferencesService, SpecialFieldsPreferences — defaults & API changes.
- GUI: JabRefFrame, MainTable, RightClickMenu, TableTabViewModel, SpecialField* View/Action classes — use new preferences API and injected clipboard manager.
- Logic: ParserResult — Path support and string joining for warnings.
- Other minor refactors and cleanup across affected classes.

Compatibility notes
- Preference keys remain the same; only defaults changed. Existing user configs will not be affected (their saved settings remain), but fresh installs will have auto-sync disabled.
- ParserResult.getFile() is deprecated in favor of getPath().
- PreferencesService no longer exposes isKeywordSyncEnabled(); callers should use getSpecialFieldsPreferences().isKeywordSyncEnabled().

Testing
- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance. No automated tests added in this PR (proof-of-concept refactor to centralize preferences access — further refactor/tests planned).

Checklist
- CHANGELOG updated
- Manual testing performed

This PR both addresses the requested behavioral change (disable special-field-to-keyword sync by default) and contains a small proof-of-concept refactoring to reduce scattered usage of JabRefPreferences#get()/put() throughout the codebase.

text:
Simplify change scanner to use a 2-way merge between the current in-memory database and the new file on disk.

What I changed
- Replaced the previous 3-way merge (last saved value vs current value in JabRef vs new file) with a straightforward 2-way comparison between the current in-memory state and the file on disk.

Why
- The 3-way logic was complex and apparently contained a subtle bug that led to issue #5257. The 2-way approach is much simpler, easier to reason about and maintain, and should eliminate the bug sources introduced by the complicated merging logic.

Behavioral tradeoffs
- The new approach is simpler but has a small disadvantage in a few edge cases. Example:
  - User A opens file, changes field 'Author' to 'User A' and adds field 'Title' = 'new'.
  - User B opens file, changes 'Author' to 'User B' and saves.
  - With the 2-way merge, User A will be notified that 'Author' changed to 'User B' and that 'Title' was removed. The previous 3-way merge could detect that 'Title' was newly added by User A and reapply it automatically; this is not possible with the simpler 2-way approach.

Notes
- This change aims to fix #5257 by removing the buggy 3-way merging logic.
- Manually tested changes in a running JabRef instance (see checklist). Automated tests and changelog/documentation updates are not included in this PR.

This PR fixes a regression introduced when GitHandler.pullOnCurrentBranch() was changed to support remote repositories. The same method is used by the SLR module for local-only study repositories (which have no remote by default), causing repository initialization errors.

What I changed

Why

- The change preserves compatibility with local-only workflows (such as the SLR module) while still allowing pulls from remotes when configured.

Issue

- Closes #13773

Testing

- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance to verify SLR repository initialization no longer fails when no remote is configured.

Notes

- No user-visible behavior change other than fixing the initialization error for local-only repositories.
- Checklist items for unit tests / docs / changelog were left as in the original issue template.

text:
Add AbbreviateAction to handle journal name abbreviation/unabbreviation for selected entries

Summary:
- Implements AbbreviateAction (extends SimpleCommand) which converts journal full names to abbreviations or restores full names for selected entries.
- Supports multiple abbreviation modes driven by StandardActions: ABBREVIATE_DEFAULT, ABBREVIATE_DOTLESS, ABBREVIATE_SHORTEST_UNIQUE and UNABBREVIATE.

Key behavior:
- Shows a user notification when the operation starts ("Abbreviating..." / "Unabbreviating...").
- Runs the actual work in the background using BackgroundTask and the injected TaskExecutor.
- For abbreviation: builds an UndoableAbbreviator with preferences and repository, creates a NamedCompound for undo grouping, and collects per-entry callables (one per journal field) to be executed concurrently.
- Uses HeadlessExecutorService to execute all field-callables and waits for results; each callable runs the abbreviation update on the JavaFX thread via UiTaskExecutor.runInJavaFXThread.
- For unabbreviation: uses an UndoableUnabbreviator, performs the work synchronously over selected entries and fields, and aggregates the count of changed fields.
- Adds the NamedCompound to the UndoManager, marks the library tab base as changed, and returns a localized summary message with the number of changed journal names.

Other details:
- Uses Localization for user-facing messages.
- Uses StateManager to obtain the active database and selected entries.
- Properly logs unknown actions and errors when collecting Callable results (InterruptedException / ExecutionException).
- Binds command executability to whether entries are selected.

This class centralizes threading, undo integration, and UI notifications for journal abbreviation/unabbreviation actions.

Summary

This PR merges the various "optional"/"other" fields tabs into a single OptionalFields tab and removes duplicated/obsolete classes and layouts. It fixes UI layout issues caused by the previous two-column compressed layout and implements logic to show remaining/other fields in the unified tab.

Fixes

- Fixes #4688

What I changed

- Removed files/classes
  - Deleted OptionalFields2Tab.java
  - Deleted OtherFieldsTab.java

- Unified optional/other fields handling
  - Updated OptionalFieldsTabBase to compute the "other" fields by taking entry fields that are not part of the entry type's known fields, removing deprecated fields and user-configured custom tab fields. This replaces the prior split between primary/secondary/other tabs.
  - The preferences default tab field names are used to filter out custom tabs so those fields stay in their respective user-defined tabs.

- UI/layout fixes
  - Simplified FieldsEditorTab row/column layout by removing the compressed two-column layout branch. Fields now use a single column layout which fixes the ugly/overlapping editors shown when merging tabs.

- Entry editor wiring
  - EntryEditor no longer creates OptionalFields2Tab or OtherFieldsTab; only the unified OptionalFieldsTab (OptionalFieldsTabBase) is added.

- Minor FXML update
  - Added imports for RadioButton and ToggleGroup in CustomizeEntryTypeDialog.fxml (small UI resource update).

- Changelog
  - Added an entry to CHANGELOG.md describing the merge of optional/optional2/otherFields.

Why

The optional fields UI had been split among multiple tabs (optional, optional2, other) which caused duplication and confusion. The goal of this change is to unify remaining/optional fields into a single tab and to fix the layout issues that appeared after the merge (the compressed two-column layout made merged fields look bad). This simplifies the UI and reduces maintenance overhead.

Notes for reviewers

- The logic in OptionalFieldsTabBase uses the entry type's known fields and the entry's actual fields to compute the other fields. It also excludes deprecated fields and fields present in custom user-defined tabs.
- The compressed 2-column mode was removed because it produced poor layout results when fields were merged. If a two-column layout is desired later, it should be reintroduced in a way that adapts to merged tab contents.

Testing / How to verify

1. Create a new library and add a new entry (e.g. via New entry and add a DOI).
2. Open the entry editor by double-clicking an entry.
3. Inspect the "Optional fields" tab — it should show the remaining fields (including previously "other" fields), properly laid out in a single column without the previous overlapping/ugly layout.

Additional

- I have added screenshots and performed manual testing as described in the issue/PR notes.
- No user-facing preference changes required, but the merged behavior affects how optional/other fields are presented in the editor.

text:
Preferences dialog: add view/export/import/reset enhancements

- Add "Show preferences" and "Reset preferences" buttons to the Preferences dialog UI.
  - "Show preferences" opens a PreferencesFilterDialog to inspect preferences using JabRefPreferencesFilter.
  - "Reset preferences" clears the user preference store and shared database preferences (with confirmation) and informs the user that JabRef must be restarted. Errors are handled and shown to the user.

- Import/Export improvements in Preferences dialog
  - Export action now stores current settings prior to exporting and saves the export path in preferences.
  - Import action uses a FileDialog default path and imports preferences from XML, updates runtime state, prompts for restart and closes the dialog on success.
  - Both import/export actions show appropriate error/warning dialogs on failure.

- Runtime preference refresh
  - Implemented updateAfterPreferenceChanges() to reinitialize custom export formats, layout formatter preferences and save preferences after imports/resets, and refresh entry editor tabs.
  - setValues() updates all preference tabs from current preferences.

- New API to retrieve stored preferences
  - JabRefPreferences.getPreferences() returns all stored preference keys and values as a Map<String,Object>.
  - Helper getObject(String) handles String/boolean/int typed preference retrieval.

- Misc
  - Added getPrefsExportPath() helper to obtain the last export path preference.
  - Improved error logging throughout preference import/export/reset flows.

These changes provide better preference management and inspection from the UI and make importing, exporting and resetting preferences safer and more user-friendly.

Summary
Add an option to disable automatic linking of filenames in the entry editor.

Why
Some users prefer that filenames typed, pasted, or dragged into the entry editor remain plain text rather than being converted into clickable file links. This change gives users explicit control over that behavior.

What this change does
- Adds a new user preference in the Entry Editor settings to enable/disable autolinking of files (default: enabled).
- The entry editor checks the preference before converting file names, pasted file references, or dragged-in file items into file links and will skip conversion when the option is disabled.
- UI: a checkbox was added to the Entry Editor settings pane to toggle the behavior.
- Tests updated/added to cover both enabled and disabled states.

Compatibility & migration
- Default behavior remains unchanged (autolinking enabled). No data migration is required.

How to test
1. Open Entry Editor settings and note the new 'Autolink files in entry editor' option. 2. With the option enabled, type/paste/drag a filename in an entry and verify it becomes a file link. 3. Disable the option, repeat the same actions, and verify filenames remain plain text. 4. Toggle back to ensure behavior switches accordingly.

Notes
- This change is limited to the entry editor autolinking behavior and does not affect other automatic link features.
