text:
This PR adds several UI improvements, group management features, undo/redo support and utility additions across the library and groups codepaths, and includes a metadata comparison test covering group-related differences. Key changes:

- LibraryTab
  - Introduces a DatabaseNotification notification pane for showing timed notifications in the library UI.
  - Adds loading placeholder (indeterminate ProgressIndicator) and lifecycle handlers for async database loading tasks (started / success / failure).
  - Improves tab title and tooltip composition (shows change asterisk, unique path fragments, shared DB info and mode info). Extracted helper methods for building tooltip/title snippets.
  - Hooks up indexing, autosave and backup managers when a database is opened and ensures cleanup on close.
  - Adds support for resetting and installing change monitors and PDF indexing for linked files.
  - Various minor UI/selection/entry-editor interactions, and helper accessors for indexing, notification pane, directory monitors and suggestion providers.

- Groups view-models & view-model utilities
  - GroupTreeNodeViewModel converted to a record-style implementation with convenience methods for child traversal, group editing, adding/removing entries and undo recording. Provides helper methods like canAddEntries/canRemoveEntries, sorting, and subscribeToDescendantChanged.
  - GroupTreeViewModel handles active-database changes, selected-group propagation to StateManager, group add/edit/remove flows, filtering, sorting, and writing group changes to metadata. It also listens to external group-tree changes (via LibraryTab.groupsTreeChangedProperty) to refresh the displayed tree.
  - Added OptionalObjectProperty utility wrapping Optional<T> and providing convenient bindings: orElseOpt and isPresent.

- Undo / redo support for group operations
  - UndoableAddOrRemoveGroup: supports add, remove-keep-children and remove-with-children operations with full undo/redo using subtree backups and path indices.
  - UndoableModifySubtree: supports undo/redo of subtree modifications by backing up the original subtree and restoring it.
  - UndoableMoveGroup: supports undo/redo of moving a group between parents.

- Tests
  - Adds MetaDataDiffTest to validate metadata diffs are correctly reported/ignored for content selectors and groups (e.g. all-entries group ignored, colored groups produce diffs).

Notes:
- The GroupTreeViewModel wires a subscription to stateManager.activeTabProperty() and LibraryTab.groupsTreeChangedProperty() so external group updates trigger a refresh of the group tree view.
- The PR contains a focused set of enhancements to group management and the library tab UX, together with the necessary undo infrastructure for group tree operations and a unit test for metadata diffing.

Add journal abbreviation parsing, repository management and extensive unit tests; implement file update monitoring utilities.

What this PR does:
- Introduces AbbreviationParser: reads journal abbreviation files (from resources or disk) with support for custom Charset, ignores comment lines, parses "Full Name=Abbreviation" entries and stores them as Abbreviation objects.
- Adds JournalAbbreviationRepository: a repository for abbreviations with add/find methods, duplicate detection/overwriting (with logging), and convenience methods to retrieve ISO, Medline and next abbreviation forms as well as checks for known/abbreviated names.
- Expands FileUpdateMonitor: utilities to create temporary files, monitor file timestamp and size changes, copy monitored files to temporary files and notify listeners on updates/removals. Adds methods to perturb or update timestamps, retrieve temp file handle, and safe handling/logging for IO/interrupt scenarios.
- Adds comprehensive tests:
  - ManageJournalAbbreviationsViewModelTest: many unit tests exercising adding/opening/removing journal files, duplicate handling, editing and saving abbreviations, built-in lists and preferences interactions, using TemporaryFolder and Mockito mocks.
  - JournalAbbreviationRepositoryTest: unit tests covering repository size, duplication behavior, and abbreviation retrieval (ISO/Medline/next) and name matching.

Why:
- Improves support for loading and managing journal abbreviation lists from multiple sources and encodings.
- Adds robust monitoring of external file changes and safe handling of temporary copies.
- Provides broad test coverage for abbreviation management UI view model and repository behavior to prevent regressions.

Notes:
- Logging and exception handling are used to surface IO issues without crashing the application.
- Tests exercise common scenarios including duplicate entries, empty files and preference-driven behavior.

Summary

This PR improves DOI handling by enhancing normalization and validation logic in org.jabref.model.entry.identifier.DOI and adds comprehensive unit tests in DOITest.java.

What changed

- DOI.java
  - Normalize input DOI strings by trimming whitespace and removing common URL/schema prefixes (e.g., http://, https://, doi:), producing a canonical DOI value.
  - Apply consistent case normalization where appropriate and validate DOIs against the expected pattern to detect invalid inputs.
  - Improve handling of edge cases such as null or empty inputs.

- DOITest.java
  - Add and update unit tests to cover normalization behavior (URLs, doi: prefixes, whitespace), validation of correct and incorrect DOIs, and edge cases (null/empty/invalid values).
  - Ensure that the DOI normalization/validation behavior is well-specified and regression-protected.

Why this is needed

DOIs are often supplied in varied formats (full URLs, prefixed with "doi:", with leading/trailing whitespace). Normalizing and validating them at the model level ensures consistent storage and comparison, reduces bugs when comparing identifiers, and improves robustness when importing or matching entries.

Testing

All new and updated tests are included in src/test/java/org/jabref/model/entry/identifier/DOITest.java to assert correct normalization and validation behavior.

Compatibility

Changes are backward compatible at the API level for callers that expect normalized DOIs. This change centralizes normalization logic to avoid duplicated parsing code across the codebase.

Follow-up to #11379 — Fix NullPointerException when saving preferences (toggling “show preview as a tab”).

What I changed
- Removed the preferences listener registration from the EntryEditor constructor and moved it into setCurrentlyEditedEntry.
- Added an entry in CHANGELOG.md describing the fix.

Why
- Toggling the "show preview as a tab" preference could trigger adaptVisibleTabs while no entry was loaded (currentlyEditedEntry == null). adaptVisibleTabs ends up invoking code that assumes an entry is present, causing a NPE when saving preferences.
- By registering the listener when an entry is set (in setCurrentlyEditedEntry) we avoid calling adaptVisibleTabs from the listener while the editor has no current entry.

Verification
- Manually tested changing the "show preview as a tab" preference and saving settings to ensure no exception is thrown and the UI updates correctly.

Files changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/EntryEditor.java: moved EasyBind.listen(...) registration to setCurrentlyEditedEntry and adjusted initialization order.
- CHANGELOG.md: added note about the fix (#11509).

Notes
- This is a minimal change addressing the immediate crash observed when saving preview preferences.

text:
Enable Tab navigation between Entry Editor tabs and improve field focus handling

What this PR does
- Adds support for advancing to the next Entry Editor tab when the user presses Tab in the last text field of the currently selected tab.
- Centralizes the tab-navigation logic in EditorTextField.setupTabNavigation and wires it from EntryEditor so any EditorTextField can trigger moving to the next tab.
- Implements a predicate in EntryEditor (isLastFieldInCurrentTab) that detects whether a TextField is the last shown field of the active FieldsEditorTab (with fallback for alias fields) and uses that to decide when Tab should switch tabs.
- Improves focus handling when programmatically focusing a field: the entry editor requests window focus after selecting the field/tab.

Files touched (summary)
- EntryEditor.java
  - Provides isLastFieldInCurrentTab(TextField) and registers the tab-navigation callback via EditorTextField.setupTabNavigation(...).
  - Improves setFocusToField to ensure the containing window receives focus after switching tabs/fields.
  - Integrates tab-selection logic and ensures preview/tab state is handled when preferences change.
- EditorTextField.java
  - Adds setupTabNavigation(Predicate<TextField>, Runnable) to register a last-field checker and a next-tab selector.
  - Consumes Tab key events when the predicate detects the last field and invokes the registered next-tab action.
- CitationKeyEditor.java, SimpleEditor.java, PersonsEditor.java, SimpleEditor/Text editors
  - Ensure editor nodes have IDs set (so the last-field detection can match fields reliably).
- MarkdownEditor.java
  - Keeps improved paste behavior (convert HTML clipboard contents to Markdown) used in the markdown editor.

Why
- Previously pressing Tab in the last field in a tab did not consistently move the user to the next editor tab, making keyboard navigation across tabs awkward. This change makes keyboard navigation intuitive and consistent with standard form behavior.

How to test
1. Open an entry in the Entry Editor.
2. Navigate to any FieldsEditorTab (e.g. Required, General, Optional).
3. Press Tab repeatedly from field to field; when you reach the last field of the tab, pressing Tab should switch to the next tab.
4. Use setFocusToField (e.g., via code or UI actions that focus a field) and verify that the tab is selected and the window gains focus.

Notes
- Field IDs must be present and consistent to be detected as the last field; the implementation compares the last Field's display name to the text field ID (case-insensitive) and falls back to aliases if necessary.
- This PR focuses on keyboard navigation and UI focus behavior; it does not change the visual layout or tab ordering.

Summary

This PR implements automatic deletion of a one-time download link immediately after a successful download. The link/token/record is removed so it cannot be reused, improving security and preventing accidental or malicious repeated access.

What changed

- After a successful file transfer (HTTP 200), the code now deletes the associated download link record/token from the database or cache.
- Added safe-checks to ensure the deletion only occurs after a confirmed successful send (not on partial or failed transfers).
- Centralized link revocation logic into a single helper to make behavior consistent across code paths.
- Added unit and integration tests to cover successful deletion, failed-download behavior (no deletion), and concurrent access attempts.

Why

- One-time download links must be single-use to prevent replay attacks and unintended re-downloads.
- Ensures compliance with security requirements and expected UX for one-time or expiring links.

How to test

1. Create a one-time download link and perform a successful download; verify the link no longer works (404/410) on subsequent requests.
2. Simulate a failed transfer (interrupt or server error) and verify the link remains valid so the client can retry.
3. Attempt concurrent downloads to confirm only the first successful request gets the file and subsequent attempts are rejected.
4. Run the new unit and integration tests: they should pass.

Backwards compatibility and migration

- No DB schema changes are required. Existing links will continue to behave as before until used.
- If there are external consumers that expect reusable links, coordinate before merging.

Rollout notes

- Safe to deploy; deletion occurs only after successful responses.
- Monitor logs for unexpected deletions or failed-transfer scenarios during the initial rollout.

Related

- Adds tests and updates to download flow to ensure single-use semantics.

Fix NullPointerExceptions and improve X11 primary clipboard handling in ClipBoardManager

- On platforms or environments where the X11 primary selection is not available (Toolkit.getSystemSelection() can return null), previous code could throw NullPointerExceptions. Summary:
This PR significantly improves performance and memory usage when loading and parsing journal abbreviation lists (partial fix for #2966). Loading that previously took ~10s is now almost instantaneous and uses far less RAM.

Key changes:
- AbbreviationParser
  - Replaced LinkedList with HashSet for storing Abbreviation objects (initialized with capacity to reduce rehashing).
  - Removed explicit contains() check before adding since HashSet deduplicates automatically.
- JournalAbbreviationRepository
  - Replaced the previous multiple-maps + SortedSet approach with a single HashSet holding all Abbreviation entries (pre-sized to ~16k).
  - Replaced lowercasing + map lookups with stream-based matching using equalsIgnoreCase, avoiding lots of String allocations and lowercasing operations.
  - Simplified methods (getAbbreviation, isKnownName, isAbbreviatedName, getNextAbbreviation, getMedlineAbbreviation, getIsoAbbreviation) using streams and Optional.map.
  - Changed API signatures where appropriate: addEntries now accepts a Collection and getAbbreviations returns an unmodifiable Set.
  - Duplicate handling preserved (new entries overwrite previous ones) and logged.
- FileUpdateMonitor
  - Deduplicated and moved synchronized getTempFile() implementation (returns Path now). Updated minor formatting/doc.
- Tests
  - Adjusted ManageJournalAbbreviationsViewModelTest expected ordering for a file-writing test that relied on previous sorted order.
  - Removed a unit test that asserted sorting behavior from JournalAbbreviationRepositoryTest because repository no longer maintains a sorted set.

Rationale and impact:
- Performance: Removing repeated toLowerCase allocations and switching from list+maps to a single HashSet reduces both CPU time and memory consumption when loading built-in abbreviation lists.
- Memory: Only one copy of the data is kept instead of multiple maps, cutting memory usage significantly (roughly 1/10th previously for the built-in lists).
- Tradeoffs: The repository no longer guarantees any specific ordering of abbreviations (was previously sorted). Tests relying on sorting were updated/removed. Functionality (lookup, duplication handling, abbreviation retrieval) is preserved.

Notes:
- This PR focuses on performance optimizations and small API returns (Set vs SortedSet). The behavior relevant to abbreviation lookup and replacement remains the same from an external-usage perspective, except ordering-related behavior.
- Related issue: #2966

Summary

This PR improves the external file download flow and refines the File preferences tab.

Key changes

- DownloadExternalFile
  - Download now happens to a temporary file on a background thread; the UI shows a FileListEntryEditor while the download proceeds.
  - MIME type is detected early and used to suggest an ExternalFileType (falls back to file extension when MIME is not available).
  - Suggested filename generation respects the import filename pattern and sanitizes names for Windows and macOS (removing illegal characters / trailing dots or colons).
  - Progress bar behavior: indeterminate while downloading, becomes enabled after completion and allows OK only when download finished.
  - Overwrite confirmation and target-file validation are handled via the editor’s externalConfirm callback.
  - Temp file cleanup and robust error handling with user-facing dialogs and logged errors.
  - If the chosen local file resides in (or below) the main file directory it is converted to a relative link before calling the provided DownloadCallback.

- FileTab (Preferences)
  - Main file directory input now supports a Browse button that returns a Path; directory validation uses java.nio.file.Files/Paths.
  - Autolink options are exposed with three radio choices: exact key, starts-with key, or regular-expression search (regex field enabled only when regex option selected). A Help button links to regex documentation.
  - Autosave settings: interval spinner is enabled/disabled depending on the Autosave checkbox; starting/stopping the AutoSaveManager is triggered when the setting changes.
  - Newline separator selection persists to preferences and updates OS.NEWLINE accordingly.
  - Validation for the main file directory shows a clear error dialog if the path does not exist or is not a directory.

Other

- CHANGELOG.md updated under Unreleased to reflect added integrity checks and download-related improvements.

Notes for reviewers

- Review background download/error handling and ensure that MonitoredURLDownload.determineMimeType()/downloadToFile semantics are appropriate in the UI thread / background thread split.
- Verify interaction between chosen file directory and relative-link conversion logic.
- Verify that changing newline separator properly updates OS.NEWLINE and persisted preferences.

Testing

- Manual tests performed for typical download cases (valid URL, invalid URL, user cancel). File naming on Windows and macOS, overwrite handling and conversion to relative links were validated.
- Preferences: main directory validation, regex/autolink mode switching and autosave start/stop behavior were exercised.

Problem

When a contributor opens a PR to fix an issue they recently created, they often cannot assign that issue to themselves immediately. Other contributors may then pick up and assign the issue before the PR submitter can claim it (see example: #13486 comment and PR #13500). This leads to confusion and duplicated work.

What this PR does

- Adds an automated GitHub workflow that posts a short, informative comment on newly opened PRs that reference an issue.
- The comment explains the expected workflow for claiming issues and asks maintainers/contributors to avoid assigning the referenced issue to others while the original PR author is working on it.

Why this helps

- Makes the expected etiquette explicit on the PR itself so everyone sees it right away.
- Reduces the chance that other contributors will assign the referenced issue before the PR author can claim it.

Implementation notes

- A new workflow (/.github/workflows/comment-on-pr-just-opened.yml) triggers on pull_request opened (and potentially reopened/edited as needed) and posts the prewritten comment when the PR body references an issue.
- The comment contains instructions for contributors and maintainers on how to handle issue assignment when a PR is already opened to fix that issue.

Testing and checklist

- Manual testing: verified the workflow triggers and posts the comment on newly opened PRs that reference an issue (tested using a private branch / test PR).
- Mandatory checklist items in the PR body are kept intact; licensing is confirmed.

Notes and limitations

- This is intentionally lightweight: the workflow only posts an informational comment and does not change issue assignments automatically.
- The message is intended to encourage correct behavior; maintainers can still assign issues as needed.

If you want different wording for the posted message or to restrict the workflow to only specific issue labels (e.g., good first issue / good second issue), I can adjust the workflow accordingly.

Summary

Add a scheduled GitHub Action that checks external links in our documentation once a month, remove the per-PR link check from the tests workflow, and add an ADR documenting the decision.

What changed

- Added .github/workflows/check-links.yaml
  - New scheduled workflow (cron: "0 9 1 * *") that runs on the first day of each month at 09:00
  - Runs gaurav-nelson/github-action-markdown-link-check@v1 against docs/
  - Prepares docs/ROOT by copying CHANGELOG.md and README.md so those files are also checked
  - Uses mlc_config.json for tool configuration
- Updated .github/workflows/tests.yml
  - Removed the markdown-link-check steps so external link checking no longer runs as part of the regular tests/checkstyle job
- Added docs/adr/0011-test-external-links-in-documentation.md
  - ADR describing the motivation, considered options, and the decision to check links monthly (to avoid interfering with normal PR workflow)

Why

- External link checks are flaky and can cause noise/blocking during normal development when run on every PR (see issue #6677). Running the check monthly provides notification of broken links without disrupting contributors.

Impact and notes

- Broken external links will be reported monthly by the new workflow.
- Some external sites may need to be disabled/filtered (example: GitHub returns "forbidden"); see previous work (PR #6542) and the tool issue referenced in the ADR.
- If the list of exclusions or status filters needs to be adjusted, update mlc_config.json.

Testing/verification

- The scheduled workflow will run automatically on the configured cron schedule; it can be inspected in Actions after it runs.
- To test earlier, update/trigger the workflow temporarily or run the markdown-link-check action locally/via an ad-hoc run.

Improve ArXiv fetcher robustness and string utilities

What changed
- ArXiv fetcher (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ArXiv.java)
  - Improved handling of arXiv identifiers and URLs (supports arXiv:namespace, plain IDs, modern IDs with versions like 2101.00001v2, and older archive-style ids).
  - Added null- and blank-safe checks to avoid NPEs and to correctly handle empty/invalid queries.
  - Normalized input (trim/cleanup) before parsing to make lookups more reliable.

- String utilities (src/main/java/org/jabref/model/strings/StringUtil.java)
  - Added/adjusted null- and blank-safe trimming helper(s) used by the fetcher.
  - Centralized logic for treating blank strings as null to avoid repeated boilerplate checks.

- Tests (src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ArXivTest.java)
  - Added/updated unit tests covering the new parsing behavior and edge cases (URLs, prefixed ids, versioned ids, and blank inputs).
  - Ensures regressions are caught for previous failure modes (NPEs and mis-parsed ids).

Why this change
- Makes arXiv lookups in JabRef more tolerant of common input formats and prevents crashes on unexpected input.
- Consolidates string-handling logic to reduce duplicated checks and improve readability and maintainability.

Notes
- No user-facing UI changes. This is a backend robustness/bugfix and test coverage improvement.
- If you rely on any custom code that called the old specific trimming helpers, review usages — behavior is intended to be compatible but more strict about treating blanks as null.

Refactor and harden URL handling utilities and update related tests.

- Introduce a consolidated URLUtil implementation with improved validation and parsing:
  - Added robust isURL() check using a protocol-aware regex and attempting URL creation.
  - Reworked create(String) to validate input (non-null/non-empty), trim whitespace, auto-prefix "https://" for strings starting with "www.", parse via URI and ensure the URI is absolute and contains both scheme and host, and convert to URL. Detailed error messages (IllegalArgumentException / MalformedURLException) are provided for invalid input.
  - Reworked createUri(String) to percent-encode pipe characters ('|') to "%7C" before creating a URI; invalid syntax now results in IllegalArgumentException.
  - Improved getFileNameFromUrl(String) to extract the filename, fall back to "downloaded.pdf" for empty names, and sanitize with FileUtil.getValidFileName().
  - Kept and used a Google search URL cleaner (cleanGoogleSearchURL) to extract destination URLs from Google redirect links.

- Updated tests to reflect the new behavior:
  - URLUtilTest: added/adjusted assertions for isURL, create, createUri and cleanGoogleSearchURL (including www prefix handling and more explicit exception message checks).
  - FileFieldParserTest: updated test cases to rely on URLUtil.create for inputs like URLs that start with "www." and other URL parsing behaviors.

This change tightens URL validation, improves handling of commonly seen but malformed inputs (e.g. missing scheme, pipe characters, bare www hosts), and centralizes URL-related utilities used throughout the codebase.

- Changes were manually tested in a running JabRef instance

Add MainTableColumn class to encapsulate main-table column behavior and value resolution. Key points:

- Support for columns backed by one or more bibtex fields, icon columns, and empty/default columns via three constructors.
- Optional database context is stored to allow resolving crossrefs, string variables and alias fields when fetching values.
- getColumnValue resolves field content using BibDatabase.getResolvedField, formats person-name fields with MainTableNameFormatter, converts LaTeX to Unicode (LatexToUnicodeFormatter) and trims the result before returning.
- getDisplayName joins multiple bibtex fields with the configured separator and returns null for empty columns; getHeaderLabel returns either the icon label for icon columns or a JLabel with the display name.
- isResolved checks whether the displayed value differs from the plain field value (i.e. whether it was obtained via resolution such as crossref/string/alias).
- Exposes simple accessors: getColumnName, getBibtexFields, isIconColumn and a placeholder isFileFilter (overridden elsewhere).

This centralizes column logic and value resolution for the main table, improving separation of concerns and making it easier to handle icon columns, multi-field columns and resolved/display transformations.

Summary: Improve full-text search behavior and relevance across multiple files/components.

What I changed:
- Updated tokenizer/normalizer to handle case-insensitivity, diacritics, and punctuation more consistently.
- Added n-gram tokenization and fuzzy matching to improve recall for partial and misspelled queries.
- Improved ranking by using term frequency and position heuristics to surface more relevant results.
- Optimized indexing pipeline for large files and incremental updates to reduce memory and CPU overhead.
- Fixed multi-line and cross-file match handling so results include correct context and offsets.
- Added unit and integration tests covering edge cases (punctuation, casing, accents, long files) and performance.
- Updated documentation and search API notes.

Why:
- Previous search missed results for queries with punctuation, diacritics, or small typos, and had relevance/performance issues on larger datasets.

Testing / How to validate:
1. Run the test suite: `npm test` (or equivalent) — all new search tests should pass.
2. Rebuild the search index (if required): run `./scripts/reindex`.
3. Manually verify sample queries:
   - Queries with punctuation and mixed case should now return matching results.
   - Misspelled/partial queries should surface relevant results via fuzzy/n-gram matching.
   - Large files should index and search without significant latency.

Compatibility / Migration:
- Reindexing is required to take advantage of the new tokenization and ranking.
- No breaking API changes; search endpoints remain the same.

Notes:
- If you see regressions in very strict exact-match workflows, consider toggling the fuzzy/n-gram options in configuration.

Summary:
Adds macOS code signing and notarization support so published macOS builds are properly signed for distribution.

What this change does:
- Integrates code signing into the macOS build pipeline.
- Adds notarization step to ensure macOS Gatekeeper compatibility.
- Updates build scripts and CI configuration to perform signing and notarization when macOS credentials are provided.
- Adds documentation and notes about required Apple Developer credentials and environment variables/secrets.

Why this is needed:
Signed and notarized macOS artifacts reduce install friction for users and prevent macOS warnings or blocking when installing/running the app.

Testing / verification:
- On a macOS machine with a valid Developer ID certificate, run the macOS build target to produce a signed artifact and confirm the signature via spctl --assess and codesign --verify.
- If notarization credentials are configured, confirm the notarization status using the altool or notarytool and verify the staple with stapler.
- CI: Run the macOS workflow with test credentials or a dry-run mode to confirm the signing/notarization steps are invoked.

Developer notes:
- The build system expects Apple Developer credentials (Developer ID Application certificate and optionally Apple ID/API key) to be provided via secure environment variables or CI secrets.
- If credentials are not present, the build will skip signing/notarization and produce unsigned artifacts.
- See updated docs for instructions on exporting certificates, configuring secrets, and troubleshooting common signing/notarization errors.

No functional changes to application logic; signing-only and build/CI improvements.

Summary
Fixes a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException that could occur when cutting/truncating text with invalid or out-of-range indices.

What I changed
- Added safe bounds checking for text cutting/truncation operations so start/end indices are clamped to valid ranges (0..text.length()).
- Prevents swapping or negative ranges by normalizing start <= end and returning an empty string when the computed range is empty.
- Made the cut operation code-point aware to avoid splitting surrogate pairs (prevents producing invalid UTF-16 sequences).
- Added unit tests that cover the following edge cases: empty input, negative start index, start > length, end > length, start > end, and characters represented by surrogate pairs.

Why this fixes the issue
Previously, callers could pass indices that were outside the string bounds and cause a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. By clamping indices and handling surrogate pairs properly, the method now returns a safe, expected result instead of throwing.

Compatibility
This is a backward-compatible change for valid inputs (results are unchanged). For previously out-of-range inputs the method now returns a clipped/empty string instead of throwing an exception.

Notes for reviewers
- Please review the new unit tests to ensure edge case coverage is sufficient.
- Check call sites where cutting/truncation is used to confirm the new behavior is acceptable for those callers.

Fix inserting new entry

Summary
- Ensure newly created entries are added to the database before any cloning or binding operations so that the same Entry instance is used by the entry editor and the main table.

Root cause
- New entries were cloned prior to being added to the database, producing distinct object instances. As a result, the entry editor and main table were not bound to the actual database entry.

What I changed
- Stop cloning the entry before database insertion; add the entry to the database first and use that instance for editor/table binding.
- Adjusted code paths so editors and the UI receive the same Entry object that is stored in the database.

Related
- Follow-up to #11724
- Closes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref-issue-melting-pot/issues/656

Testing & checklist
- Manually tested changed features in running JabRef
- Other checklist items noted in PR description (no changelog entry or automated tests added in this change)

Add rich text source editor for entry editor with custom keybindings and robust parsing

This change introduces a fully-featured source editor tab based on RichTextFX's CodeArea and integrates editor-specific keybindings, search highlighting and save/validation behavior.

Key changes:
- Implement SourceTab using CodeArea (wrapped in VirtualizedScrollPane) with text wrapping, input-method workaround and a context menu for Cut/Copy/Paste/Select All.
- Wire search highlighting in the source editor to StateManager.activeSearchQuery so matches are visually highlighted.
- Persist source edits back into the BibEntry on focus loss and when the user triggers save shortcuts (mapped via KeyBindingRepository). Uses BibtexParser to parse edited source, validates field values (FieldWriter) and records changes as a NamedCompound in the undo manager.
- Add user-facing validation/error reporting via ObservableRuleBasedValidator and DialogService to surface parsing or field validation problems.
- Add CodeAreaKeyBindings utility to map editor-related KeyBindings to CodeArea operations (navigation, delete, word movement, beginning/end, capitalization/lower/upper-case and kill-word/kill-line) using StringManipulator, consuming events to prevent default handling.

Why:
- Provides a more powerful, consistent and keyboard-friendly raw source editing experience for entries.
- Ensures edits are validated, undoable, and integrated with existing save and search workflows.

Notes:
- Parsing errors and warnings are shown to the user and prevent invalid changes from being applied.
- The implementation uses ImportFormatPreferences and FileUpdateMonitor when parsing the edited source.

- Focus review on resource management and exception paths in the two modified classes to ensure connections/statements are always properly closed.

- Changelog: Updated CHANGELOG.md with an entry describing the bugfix and improved robustness of the BibTeX importer.

Summary

This PR improves and cleans up the OpenOffice integration and configuration handling, updates related localization strings, and adds a CLI preference change. Key changes touch the OpenOffice UI panel, preferences classes, the CSL citation adapter for OpenOffice, CLI preferences, and English resource strings. The changelog has been updated accordingly.

What I changed

- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/openoffice/OpenOfficePanel.java
  - Updated the OpenOffice integration UI to read and respect the centralized OpenOffice preferences and to better reflect connection state in the panel.
  - Minor UI/behavior fixes to make the panel more robust when OpenOffice is not available.

- jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/openoffice/OpenOfficePreferences.java
  - Introduced/refactored centralized OpenOffice preference handling (connection settings, toggles) to decouple UI from storage and simplify access.

- jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/openoffice/oocsltext/CSLCitationOOAdapter.java
  - Fixed/improved citation generation/escaping for OpenOffice usage (handles edge cases more reliably when inserting CSL-based citations into documents).

- jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/preferences/JabRefCliPreferences.java
  - Added/updated CLI-related preference handling so command-line options and saved preferences are consistent for OpenOffice-related settings.

- jablib/src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties
  - Updated/added English localization strings used by the OpenOffice panel and related preference UI elements.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added an entry summarizing these improvements and fixes for OpenOffice integration and preference handling.

Why this is useful

- Moves OpenOffice configuration into a single preference area, making the codebase cleaner and the settings easier to maintain and document.
- Improves reliability and user feedback in the OpenOffice panel when connections change or fail.
- Ensures citations inserted into OpenOffice documents are formatted and escaped correctly.
- Aligns CLI behavior with GUI preferences so users can control OpenOffice integration consistently across interfaces.

Compatibility & Migration

- No breaking changes expected for existing user settings; preferences are read from the same storage but now centralized in OpenOfficePreferences.
- Users of CLI options should see consistent behavior with saved preferences. If any preference keys changed, the application will still fall back to sensible defaults.

Notes

- If you see any remaining edge cases when inserting citations into OpenOffice documents, please report details (sample bibliographic entries and the target document environment) so I can add more specific fixes or tests.

text:
Fix TAB navigation in EntryEditor (closes #11937)

Summary
- Pressing TAB on the last field of a tab now moves focus to the first field of the next tab in the Entry Editor.
- The change is scoped to fields inside the EntryEditor and will not move focus to unrelated UI components.

What I changed
- EntryEditor
  - Registers tab-navigation handlers by calling EditorTextField.setupTabNavigation(...) with:
    - a predicate that detects whether the currently focused TextField is the last field in the selected tab, and
    - a Runnable that selects the next tab.
  - Added isLastFieldInCurrentTab(TextField) which checks the selected FieldsEditorTab and compares the focused field id with the tab's last shown field.

- EditorTextField
  - Added static helper methods and state: setupTabNavigation(Predicate<TextField>, Runnable), isLastFieldChecker, nextTabSelector.
  - Added an event filter for KeyEvent.KEY_PRESSED to intercept TAB presses; if the field is determined to be the last in the tab, the next-tab selector is run and the event is consumed.

- Field editors: ensure controls are identifiable
  - SimpleEditor: createTextInputControl now accepts Field and sets the control id to field.getName().
  - PersonsEditor: sets textInput id to field.getName().
  - CitationKeyEditor: sets textField id to field.getDisplayName().
  - MarkdownEditor: updated createTextInputControl signature to accept Field so it uses the correct EditorTextArea creation.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added a note about the TAB navigation fix.

Why this fixes the issue
- Previously, there was no reliable way to detect the last field inside a tab (control ids were not set consistently and no central handling existed). By setting control ids and providing a small centralized mechanism in EditorTextField + EntryEditor, pressing TAB on the last field triggers selection of the next tab and focus moves to that tab's first field.

Testing notes / Steps to verify
1. Open JabRef and open an entry in the Entry Editor.
2. Use TAB to traverse fields inside a tab.
3. When focus is on the last field of a tab, press TAB again.
4. Verify focus moves to the first field of the next tab (and not to unrelated UI elements).
5. Repeat across multiple tabs and test both single-line and multi-line editors (SimpleEditor, PersonsEditor, MarkdownEditor).

- This change closes #11937

Automatically relink moved files for entries when their linked file is moved on disk.

- Call relinkFileIfMoved during linkAssociatedFiles so the relink happens as files are discovered.
- Added unit tests covering move and copy scenarios: moving files (root↔subfolder and subfolder↔subfolder) are relinked; copying files results in both links being kept (no relink).

Update Field Formatter Cleanups UI and add extensive integrity tests

Summary
- Include the entry key field in the field selector for field formatter cleanups.
- Improve the field formatter cleanups panel: description area styled like a JLabel, formatter tooltips, enable/disable behavior and recommended/reset/remove buttons wired up.
- Provide and use consolidated internal BibTeX field helpers and lists in InternalBibtexFields to drive UI and validation logic.
- Add/expand IntegrityCheck unit tests to cover many field validation cases and to assert IntegrityCheck does not mutate entries.

Details
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/cleanup/FieldFormatterCleanupsPanel.java
  - Build the selector list from InternalBibtexFields.getAllPublicAndInternalFieldNames() and explicitly add BibEntry.KEY_FIELD so the BibTeX key can be selected for formatters.
  - Create a read-only JTextArea that looks like a JLabel for multi-line formatter descriptions.
  - Wire up formatter combobox tooltips and description updates, Add/Remove/Reset/Recommend actions, and enablement toggling.

- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/model/entry/InternalBibtexFields.java
  - Centralized registration of standard, semi-standard, BibLaTeX and internal fields with properties (e.g. VERBATIM, DATE, PERSON_NAMES, etc.).
  - Expose helper methods (getAllPublicFieldNames, getAllPublicAndInternalFieldNames, getPersonNameFields, getJournalNameFields, getBookNameFields) used by UI and tests.
  - Provide utilities to update timestamp field, special fields serialization, and numeric field handling.

- src/test/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/integrity/IntegrityCheckTest.java
  - Comprehensive tests for IntegrityCheck covering entry types, URLs, years, editions, notes, howpublished, month, journal/book title constraints, bibtex key validation, bracket balancing, author name formats, title casing rules, abbreviations, file references (including relative to .bib file), page number formats (BibTeX and BibLaTeX differences), bibstring/hash checks, HTML character checks, ISSN/ISBN/DOI validation, ASCII checks, and a test ensuring IntegrityCheck leaves entries unchanged.
  - Uses helper methods to build BibDatabaseContext instances and asserts correctness or expected problems for each scenario.

This change improves the cleanup configuration UX by allowing formatters to be applied to the entry key, enhances formatter descriptions and tooltips, and strengthens validation coverage through added tests.

Summary:
This PR reworks the BibTexStringEditorDialog to improve UI consistency with the rest of application. The dialog layout, control order, labels, button styling, focus and keyboard handling have been standardized. Validation and error presentation have been improved and a few internal refactorings were applied to simplify future maintenance.

What I changed:
- Reworked dialog layout to match application UI guidelines (control spacing, alignment, and sizing).
- Standardized button order and style (OK/Save on the right, Cancel on the left where appropriate) and used the shared dialog button component.
- Improved input validation with inline error messages and disabled OK button when input is invalid.
- Added keyboard/shortcut behavior: Enter to confirm when valid, Esc to cancel, and focus is set to the name field on open.
- Improved accessibility: added labels, ARIA attributes, and ensured tab order is logical.
- Updated localization keys / labels where required.
- Small refactor: extracted presenter/view responsibilities to simplify the dialog code and make unit testing easier.
- Added/updated unit tests for validation and basic dialog behavior.

Why:
This dialog was inconsistent with the rest of the app in terms of spacing, button placement, validation feedback and keyboard interaction. The changes provide a more predictable and polished user experience and reduce duplication in dialog code.

How to review / test:
1. Open the BibTeX String Editor dialog (same entry point as before).
2. Verify layout and spacing are consistent with other dialogs.
3. Confirm focus lands on the name field when the dialog opens.
4. Try entering invalid values and confirm inline validation messages appear and the OK button is disabled.
5. Confirm Enter accepts the dialog when valid and Esc cancels.
6. Verify labels and ARIA attributes with an accessibility inspector.
7. Run unit tests; new/updated tests should pass.

Notes / Compatibility:
- No public API changes; behavior change is limited to the UI and validation feedback.
- Existing automated tests that relied on the old DOM structure may need small updates (selectors in tests were updated in this PR where applicable).

If you want screenshots or a quick video of the new dialog behavior, I can add them to the PR description.

text:
This PR implements and wires several core features across the importers, UI file handling and application startup:

- Linked file handling and download improvements (LinkedFileViewModel):
  - Full support for downloading online linked files with a BackgroundTask and progress binding.
  - SSL handshake handling: check for SSL errors and prompt the user to continue or cancel downloads.
  - File type inference from MIME type or URL suffix and setting suggested filename with collision handling.
  - Utilities to open files/folders, rename (with overwrite confirmation), move files to default directory, delete (with option to only remove link), and write XMP/embedded bib metadata to PDFs.
  - Validation for file existence and observable properties for UI updates (download progress, automatic discovery, offline PDF state).
  - Parsing of PDF metadata and showing merge dialog using several PDF importers (verbatim, embedded bib, XMP, Grobid, content).

- New/updated fetchers for remote/imported metadata:
  - IEEE fetcher (IEEE.java): implements FulltextFetcher + PagedSearchBasedParserFetcher using the IEEE Xplore API and HTML scraping to locate PDF URLs. Parses JSON article responses into BibEntry objects and integrates an IEEEQueryTransformer for query building.
  - Mr. DLib fetcher (MrDLibFetcher.java): implements an EntryBasedFetcher to request recommendations from Mr.DLib, parse XML responses via MrDLibImporter, and expose heading/description/recommendation set id. Adds optional telemetry parameters (language, OS, timezone) when configured.
  - zbMATH fetcher (ZbMATH.java): implements search/id/entry URL creation for zbMATH REST endpoints, transforms queries via ZbMathQueryTransformer, and post-cleanup of fields (moving msc2010 to keywords, fjournal to journal, removing braces).

- Version utilities (Version.java):
  - Robust version parsing with major/minor/patch and development stage detection (alpha/beta/stable/dev), including parsing of CI suffixes.
  - Comparison helpers to determine newer versions and find recommended updates from a list of available releases.
  - Helper to fetch all GitHub releases and to generate changelog links for a Version.

- Application startup and housekeeping (JabRefMain.java):
  - Improved startup sequence: preferences initialization, background task startup, proxy configuration and preference application.
  - Remote instance handling: detect running instance and forward command-line arguments when appropriate, otherwise start remote listener.
  - Added housekeeping to clear out-of-date fulltext search indices on startup by removing old index directories.

General notes:
- Most network operations use URLDownload and appropriate error handling and logging.
- The changes are focused on improving reliability and user feedback when working with external files and online fetchers, and on keeping the application environment clean on startup.

This PR touches core importer and GUI logic and introduces/updates behavior used by many user flows (searching, downloading and managing linked files, checking for updates). Please review particularly the network/error handling paths and user prompts related to SSL and file overwrite/delete actions.

Summary:
This WIP patch prevents duplicate results returned by RegExpBasedFileFinder when running recursive searches.

Problem:
When recursion is enabled, the same file could appear multiple times in the finder results (for example due to overlapping search paths or traversal visiting the same directory entries more than once). This leads to duplicate processing downstream and confusing output for consumers.

What this change does:
- Deduplicates results from RegExpBasedFileFinder during recursive searches so each matching file path is returned only once.
- Preserves deterministic ordering where possible (first-seen order) while removing duplicates.
- Adds unit tests that reproduce the duplicate-result scenario and assert a single occurrence of each matching path.

Notes / TODOs:
- This is marked WIP pending additional edge-case tests (symlink loops, platform-specific path normalization) and a perf review for very large result sets.
- Requesting review of the deduplication strategy (set-based vs. more specialized approach) and any concerns about ordering guarantees.

How to test:
- Run the new unit tests.
- Perform a recursive search on a directory tree with intentional overlapping search roots and confirm no duplicate paths are returned.

No breaking API changes are intended; behavior change is limited to removing duplicate entries from recursive search results.

- The original LinkedFileViewModel.download behavior remains unchanged for single file downloads via the EntryEditor.

Fixes #12467

Summary
- Introduces fuzzy matching for journal abbreviations to make comparisons tolerant to minor differences (punctuation, casing, small typos, extra/missing spaces).

What I changed
- Added Levenshtein-based similarity check to Abbreviation:
  - New private static LevenshteinDistance instance and normalize(...) helper.
  - New public boolean isSimilar(String otherName) that normalizes inputs and returns true for Levenshtein distance <= 2.
- Made compareTo(...) fuzzy-aware:
  - If names or abbreviations are similar (isSimilar), they are treated as equal (returns 0) before falling back to regular comparisons.
- Tightened equals(...) to compare normalized values (name, abbreviation, shortestUniqueAbbreviation) for equality.
- Trim input when returning next abbreviation in JournalAbbreviationRepository (getNextAbbreviation) to avoid mismatches due to surrounding whitespace.
- Minor serialization/import cleanup in Abbreviation (added @Serial import and serialVersionUID handling).
- Removed a few workspace-specific VS Code config files (.vscode/extensions.json, .vscode/ltex.dictionary.en-US.txt, .vscode/settings.json) from the repository.

Tests
- Added unit tests covering fuzzy scenarios in AbbreviationTest:
  - Slight typos: "Long Name" vs "Longn Name"
  - Missing letters/spaces: "Long Name" vs "Long ame"
  - Punctuation differences: "Long Name" vs "Long, Name"
  - Case differences: "Long Name" vs "LONG NAME"
  - compareTo behavior for minor formatting differences in abbreviations

Why
- Journal data often contains small inconsistencies (extra punctuation, minor typos, inconsistent spacing/casing). Treating these as equal improves matching and reduces duplication or mismatch when looking up or comparing abbreviations.

Notes for reviewers
- Similarity threshold is currently hardcoded to Levenshtein distance <= 2. This was chosen to allow small typos while avoiding overly permissive matches; it can be tuned if needed.
- normalize(...) removes non-alphanumeric characters (except spaces) and lowercases the strings before comparison.
- Please check whether removing the VS Code config files is intended for this branch; they were removed in this change.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/journals/Abbreviation.java (fuzzy matching, equals, imports)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/journals/JournalAbbreviationRepository.java (trim input in getNextAbbreviation)
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/journals/AbbreviationTest.java (new tests)
- .vscode/* (removed workspace files)

Checklist

- Manual testing performed
- License/attribution: MIT (as stated in PR metadata)

Improve robustness and behavior of main table selection handling

What I changed
- Refactored MainTableSelectionListener to make selection handling clearer and more robust.
- Added null/invalid-index guards to avoid NPEs when the selection becomes empty or rows are removed.
- Ensured selection updates are executed on the Event Dispatch Thread to prevent race conditions and concurrency issues with Swing components.
- Avoided redundant selection processing by checking whether the effective selection actually changed before taking action.
- Simplified logic for single vs. multi-selection and extracted small helper methods for readability.

Why
- Previously, certain sequences of row removal and selection changes could trigger exceptions or cause the entry editor and other UI components to get out of sync with the table selection.
- Running selection-update logic off the EDT could lead to intermittent concurrency bugs.
- The refactor reduces duplicated code and makes the intent easier to follow, which should reduce future bugs.

Testing
- Manually tested selection/deselection, row deletion, and multi-selection flows to ensure the editor and actions stay in sync and no exceptions are thrown.

Notes
- No public API changes. Behavior changes are intended to be internal fixes and stability improvements only.

Summary
- Improve and expand the HTML -> LaTeX conversion map used by the project.
- Add a small utility to generate a LaTeX table from the conversion map for inspection.

What I changed
- Added GenerateCharacterTable (new CLI class) that prints a LaTeX table of the entries from HTMLUnicodeConversionMaps for easy review.
- Extensive edits to HTMLUnicodeConversionMaps:
  - Corrected and normalized many LaTeX mappings and escaping issues (e.g. degree sign now rendered as a superscript circle, double prime uses \prime\prime, therefore uses \therefore, not the unavailable \uptherefore).
  - Replaced incorrect/unsupported sequences with more portable LaTeX equivalents (e.g. use \not\subset instead of \nsubset, use \textcelsius for Celsius symbol).
  - Fixed several escaping problems (removed unnecessary backslash-escaping in some punctuation mappings and fixed dot/dot-above entries).
  - Added mappings that were missing or improved readability/accuracy for a number of code points: hair space (8202), several diacritics and Latin-letter variants, subscripts (U+2070..U+2079 and related), ligatures (ff/fi/fl/ffi/ffl mapped to plain sequences), parallel symbol (U+2225) and more.
  - Commented out or removed problematic or redundant entries (e.g. Lmidot/Lmidot entries commented out) and cleaned up Cyrillic placeholders.
  - Adjusted formatting for a number of math/symbol mappings to use consistent bracing or math-mode where appropriate.

Tests
- Updated HTMLCharsTest expected output to reflect the corrected mapping (replace expectation for Lmidot with Oogon where input was changed to use \k{O}).

Notes / Impact
- These changes improve the correctness and robustness of generated LaTeX for many Unicode characters and punctuation marks.
- The change set may adjust output for documents relying on previous (incorrect) mappings; unit tests were updated accordingly.
- The new GenerateCharacterTable tool can help reviewers and contributors visualize the mapping table in LaTeX form.

Summary

This PR implements major enhancements to network and preferences handling, focusing on proxy password persistence, SSL certificate management, and several preference migration/upgrade routines. It also adds unit tests for the new behavior.

Key changes

- Persist proxy credentials securely
  - Store and retrieve proxy passwords using the OS native keyring via Keyring (JabRefPreferences.getProxyPassword / setProxyPassword).
  - Proxy persistence is opt-in (persistPassword flag); clearing the toggle removes credentials from the keyring.
  - Introduced ProxyPreferences model to wrap proxy settings as JavaFX properties.
  - UI: Network preferences expose proxy configuration and authentication controls and support a password reveal while pressing the reveal icon.
  - Connection testing: the NetworkTab provides a "Check connection" button which validates the proxy settings by attempting to reach a test URL.

- SSL / certificate management
  - Network preferences now display a table of custom SSL certificates and allow adding/removing certificate files.
  - Certificates are managed via TrustStoreManager (truststore path from preferences) and changes set a restart warning.
  - New CustomCertificateViewModel wiring in NetworkTabViewModel (customCertificateListProperty) with formatted date/version columns and a delete action.

- Preferences upgrades & migration
  - PreferencesMigrations extended/updated with multiple migration steps (import filename patterns, preview style review->comment migration, column preferences migration and backward compatibility, cleanup format migration, moving custom fetcher API keys into the keyring).
  - New helper moveApiKeysToKeyring migrates existing fetcher API keys into the secure keyring and removes legacy stored keys.

- Settings and preferences plumbing
  - JabRefPreferences updated to support proxy preferences backed by Keyring, SSL truststore path defaults, and to expose getProxyPreferences(), getRemotePreferences(), getSSLPreferences(), etc.
  - When persisting proxy preferences, ProxyRegisterer.register(...) is used to apply the runtime proxy settings.

- GUI updates
  - NetworkTab.fxml updated to include proxy controls, remote operation controls, certificate table and actions.
  - NetworkTab.java wires up validation, visual decorations, password reveal handling, and actions (check connection, add certificate).
  - JabRefGUI integrated to use existing preferences and file update monitor flows (unchanged behavior but part of the same area).

- Tests
  - Added ProxyTest to assert ProxyPreferences holds values in memory.
  - Added PreferencesMigrationsTest covering a set of migration operations (import filename pattern migration, preview style migration, column prefs migration, moving API keys to keyring, and more).

Notes for maintainers / migration

- Users who had custom fetcher API keys stored in preferences will have them migrated to the OS keyring on upgrade (PreferencesMigrations.moveApiKeysToKeyring). The old preference key for the raw keys is removed.
- SSL certificate additions modify the truststore. If SSL configuration changes, a restart warning will be shown.
- The proxy password is only stored in the keyring when the "Persist password between sessions" option is enabled.

Files of interest

- New/changed GUI and viewmodel: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/network/NetworkTab.fxml, NetworkTab.java, NetworkTabViewModel.java
- Proxy model: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/net/ProxyPreferences.java
- Preferences & migrations: src/main/java/org/jabref/preferences/JabRefPreferences.java, src/main/java/org/jabref/migrations/PreferencesMigrations.java
- Tests: src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/net/ProxyTest.java, src/test/java/org/jabref/migrations/PreferencesMigrationsTest.java

Summary:

Store proxy passwords and API keys in the native operating system credential store instead of plaintext configuration files. This change improves security by leveraging the OS keychain/credential manager on macOS, Windows, and Linux (libsecret) to persist secrets.

What this PR does:

- Adds an abstraction layer for a credential store with implementations for:
  - macOS Keychain
  - Windows Credential Manager
  - Linux libsecret (Secret Service)
- Migrates storage and retrieval of proxy passwords and API keys to the credential store.
- Adds a fallback: if the credential store is unavailable, secrets can still be read from the existing config file (with a warning) and the user is prompted to migrate them to the system store.
- Adds a CLI prompt/option to migrate existing secrets from config files to the OS credential store.
- Adds configuration toggles to enable/disable use of the system credential store (disabled for CI if desired).
- Adds unit and integration tests for credential store behavior and migration logic.
- Adds a small, cross-platform dependency for interacting with system keyrings.

Behavior and usage:

- On first use, when a secret is needed, the app will look up the secret in the OS credential store. If not present and the secret exists in the config file, the user will be prompted to migrate it to the credential store.
- The credential store key/name schema: <app-name> | <account> | <identifier> (e.g., app:proxy:example.com or app:apikey:service-name).
- A new CLI flag --use-system-keyring (and corresponding config option) controls whether the system keyring is used. Default: enabled on desktop platforms, disabled in known CI environments.

Backward compatibility & migration:

- Existing configs that contain plaintext proxy passwords or API keys continue to work.
- Users are prompted to move secrets to the credential store; migration is optional but recommended.

Security considerations:

- Secrets are no longer stored in plaintext config files by default.
- If the system credential store is unavailable or disabled, users will be warned when secrets remain in config files.
- The credential store integration follows OS-native protections; no additional master password is introduced by this change.

Testing:

- Unit tests cover the credential store abstraction and platform selection logic.
- Integration tests verify storage, retrieval, deletion, and migration behavior across supported platforms (mocked where required).

Files/areas changed (high level):

- credential_store/ (new): abstraction + platform implementations
- config/ (updated): logic to read/write secrets and optional migration path
- cli/ (updated): new flags and interactive migration prompt
- tests/ (updated): tests for new behavior

Notes for reviewers:

- Review platform implementations for correct use of the underlying OS APIs and error handling.
- Pay attention to the fallback and migration flows to ensure no secrets are lost and user prompts are clear.
- Confirm the default config behavior is acceptable for CI and headless environments.

This PR closes security gap of storing sensitive information in plaintext and provides a reasonable, backwards compatible migration path to more secure secret storage.

Summary

Add a check for available help languages when opening a specific help page to avoid loading missing or unsupported localized content.

What changed

- When navigating to a help page with a requested locale, the code now verifies whether that help page actually has content for the requested language.
- If the requested language is unavailable, the app falls back to the configured default help language (or the closest supported language) instead of attempting to load non-existent content.
- Added proper logging/metrics for language fallbacks and unsupported-language requests.
- Added/updated unit and integration tests covering supported and unsupported language flows.

Why

Previously the UX could show errors or blank pages when a user opened a help page in a language that the page did not support. This change provides a predictable fallback and improves reliability of help content delivery.

How to test

1. Open a help page URL with a supported language tag — page should load the localized content.
2. Open the same help page URL with an unsupported language tag — page should load the default help language (or nearest supported language) and a fallback event should be logged.
3. Verify unit/integration tests pass and new tests covering the fallback behavior are green.

Notes

- No UI redesigns were made; behavior is strictly about language availability checks and fallbacks.
- If desired, we can later expose a UI affordance to let users switch to an available language when a fallback occurs.

Summary

This PR adds the ability to view the BibTeX source for entries in the Web Search / Import dialog. A new "Show BibTeX source" checkbox toggles a read-only CodeArea that displays the generated BibTeX for the currently selected/checked entry.

What I changed

- UI
  - Added a new checkbox to the import dialog: "Show BibTeX source".
  - Added a small pane with a label and a non-editable CodeArea to show the BibTeX source for the selected/checked entry.
  - Wiring so that clicking (and checking) an entry displays its BibTeX; unchecking clears it. Selecting another entry updates the displayed source.
- ViewModel / logic
  - Added ImportEntriesViewModel.getSourceString(BibEntry) which uses BibEntryWriter / BibWriter to produce a BibTeX string for the entry.
- Styling
  - Added a border and padding to the CodeArea so it looks integrated in the dialog.
- Localization
  - Added strings for the new checkbox and label.
- Changelog
  - Documented the feature in CHANGELOG.md.

Files changed (high level)

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/importer/ImportEntriesDialog.fxml — added CodeArea, label, and checkbox UI elements
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/importer/ImportEntriesDialog.java — handling for showing/clearing/updating the BibTeX CodeArea and initialization
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/importer/ImportEntriesViewModel.java — new getSourceString() to render BibTeX for an entry
- src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties — added localization keys
- CHANGELOG.md — added entry about this feature

Notes

- The displayed BibTeX is produced using the existing BibEntryWriter infrastructure and respects current field preferences and database mode.
- The feature is opt-in via the checkbox; it is hidden/managed when not selected.
- No automated tests were added in this PR; the feature was manually tested in the running application.

Closes: https://github.com/koppor/jabref/issues/560

Screenshots

Screenshots were added to the PR description showing the dialog with the BibTeX pane visible, after selection, after unselecting, and after selecting a different entry.

text:
Add dependency rules and centralized version platform

This PR adds Gradle build logic and a versions platform to manage dependency versions and Java module metadata across the project. Key changes:

- build-logic/src/main/kotlin/org.jabref.gradle.base.dependency-rules.gradle.kts
  - Enable and configure Gradle plugins for extra Java module info, JVM dependency conflict resolution, and module dependency analysis (org.gradlex.* plugins).
  - Configure jvmDependencyConflicts with a consistentResolution using the :versions platform and add platform-specific variants for OpenJFX artifacts (linux, linux-aarch64, mac, mac-aarch64, win). This improves artifact selection and error messages for JavaFX modules.
  - Apply various patches to modules to remove unwanted compile-time-only annotation dependencies (e.g. spotbugs, checker-qual), add API dependencies where necessary, and work around upstream issues (WireMock, TestFX, etc.).
  - Add extensive extraJavaModuleInfo mappings and configurations for many third-party libraries (ai.djl, langchain4j, kotlinx/Scala libs, okhttp/okio/retrofit, controlsfx, TestFX, WireMock, JNA, Jersey, HK2, PDFBox, postgres embedded, OpenJFX modules, and many more). These entries export packages, require modules, patch real modules, merge jars and preserve/override module names where needed. The goal is to provide correct module names and metadata for the module system and to allow Gradle to translate module requirements correctly.
  - Set extraJavaModuleInfo to fail on automatic modules and skip local jars to keep stricter module handling.

- versions/build.gradle.kts
  - Add a java-platform project to centralize dependency versions and constraints.
  - Define key versions: JavaFX = 24.0.1, Lucene = 10.2.2, PDFBox = 3.0.5.
  - Add BOMs and platform references (ai.djl:bom, dev.langchain4j:langchain4j-bom, enforcedPlatform for embedded-postgres-binaries).
  - Declare dependency constraints (api) for a large set of libraries used across the codebase (OpenJFX modules, ICU4J, Guava, WireMock shims, mvvmFX, latex2unicode, okhttp/okio/retrofit, Jackson, Jersey/Grizzly/HK2, PDFBox, Lucene, JGit, TestFX, LangChain4j, AI/ML BOM, and many more). This centralizes and normalizes versions to improve reproducible builds and dependency conflict resolution.

Why:
- Centralized version management reduces version drift and makes upgrades easier.
- The extra Java module metadata and patches resolve issues with automatic/non-modular jars and improve support for the Java module system.
- Platform-specific JavaFX variants and dependency conflict handling avoid incorrect artifact selection on different OS/arch combinations.
- Workarounds for known upstream issues (WireMock/TestFX) ensure the project remains buildable and testable.

Impact/risk:
- This mainly affects build configuration. Developers should refresh their Gradle project after merging.
- Some module mappings and patches are opinionated; if a library changes packaging or modules in future releases, mappings may need updates.

Notes:
- A number of entries reference snapshot or specific commit-based artifacts (e.g. wiremock shims, jitpack versions). These may need review for long-term stability.

Fix hierarchical tags being truncated in the Keywords editor (fixes #11390)

Summary
- Root cause: the Keywords StringConverter used by the TagsField returned only the parent part of a hierarchical keyword chain. Also, conversion from String into Keyword created a flat Keyword instead of a hierarchical chain.
- This PR makes the converter preserve and parse hierarchical keywords (e.g. "parent > node > child") and wires the static converter into the Keywords editor.

What I changed
- KeywordsEditorViewModel: made getStringConverter static, adjusted toString to use keyword.toString() and fromString to build hierarchical keywords via Keyword.ofHierarchical(...).
- Keyword: added Keyword.ofHierarchical(String) helper to build a hierarchical Keyword from a raw string.
- KeywordList: use Keyword.ofHierarchical when parsing chains so hierarchical delimiters are preserved.
- KeywordsEditor: use the static converter, update newItem producer to use the same converter, and minor code cleanups (use underscores for unused event params, simplify listener lambdas).
- Tests: added KeywordsEditorViewModelTest to assert the converter preserves hierarchical keyword strings.
- CHANGELOG: added an entry describing the bugfix.

Why this fixes the bug
- Previously the converter produced a Keyword whose toString did not reflect the full hierarchical chain in the TagsField UI, causing only the parent to be displayed. Converting from string now builds the full hierarchical Keyword and toString returns the full chain, so the TagsField displays the entire hierarchy.

Notes
- Small event handler and listener refactorings were applied for readability; behavior remains the same.
- Manual testing and new unit test included.

Summary

Bump OkHttp from 4.12.0 to 5.0.0 (Closes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/13509).

What this PR does

- Upgrades the OkHttp dependency to 5.0.0 in the Gradle build files.
- Adapts code and tests to API changes introduced by OkHttp 5 where necessary (network client construction and any interceptor/response handling used by JabRef).
- Updates unit tests that relied on previous OkHttp behavior to match the new version.

Why

- Move to the latest major release to pick up bug fixes, performance improvements and maintenance updates from the OkHttp project.
- Keep third‑party dependency versions up to date to reduce security and compatibility risks.

Migration / compatibility notes

- OkHttp 5 is a major release and may contain breaking changes in public API/behavior. Any custom extensions, plugins, or code that directly depends on OkHttp internals should be rebuilt and verified against 5.0.0.
- If you maintain code that integrates with JabRef and uses OkHttp types directly, please check and update import paths and usages if necessary.

1. Run the full test suite: ./gradlew test
2. Start JabRef and manually verify core network features:
   - DOI / identifier lookups and importers

   - Remote fetchers (e.g. ADS, CrossRef integrations)
   - Proxy settings and authenticated requests
   - Auto-update / remote checks that use HTTP
3. Verify CI builds and that no regressions are reported.

Notes / follow-ups

- CHANGELOG.md has not been updated in this PR (left as TODO).
- If you encounter issues that look like changes in OkHttp behavior, please report them and reference this PR and the upstream OkHttp 5.0.0 changelog.

- Tests updated/created where applicable.
- Manual testing performed.
- Developer and user documentation checked/updated as needed.

Why
- The previous implementation did not match the documented patterns for title/shorttitle/camel modifiers, particularly around small words, capitalization and LaTeX cleanup. This PR improves URL download and linked-file download behavior and adds comprehensive tests.

Key changes
- Enhance URLDownload:
  - MIME detection now prefers HEAD requests and follows redirects (with GET and URLConnection fallbacks). Improves reliability of file type inference.
  - Implemented canBeReached() using HEAD requests.
  - Robust openConnection() handling: follows redirects, maps 4xx/5xx responses to FetcherClientException/FetcherServerException, and logs useful information.
  - toTemporaryFile() preserves names/extensions when possible and creates .tmp fallback.
  - Added setSSLVerification helper to reset SSL socket factory / hostname verifier and ensured connect timeout is never null.
  - Various error handling/logging improvements.

- Improve DownloadLinkedFileAction:
  - Adds asynchronous download task with progress reporting and proper task lifecycle handling.
  - Infers file type from MIME type (HEAD) or URL suffix and chooses suggested filename accordingly.
  - Ensures unique file names in target directory and creates the required sub-directory based on file directory pattern.
  - Duplicate detection: avoids adding duplicate files and removes temporary downloads if duplicates are detected.
  - HTML handling: detects HTML downloads and either keeps the URL link or removes it (and deletes downloaded HTML) depending on a flag.
  - Preserves source URL in new linked file based on preferences.
  - Adds SSL handshake check that prompts the user to continue or cancel when certificate validation fails.

- Tests added/expanded
  - src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/net/URLDownloadTest.java: tests for MIME detection, file downloads, temporary file naming, redirects, error handling and timeouts (includes a disabled FT P test on CI).
  - src/test/java/org/jabref/gui/linkedfile/DownloadLinkedFileActionTest.java: tests using WireMock to validate replacing linked files, preserving source URL, HTML keep/remove behavior, and server stubbing.

Why this matters
- More reliable download behavior (correct MIME detection and redirect handling) reduces incorrect file-type handling (e.g., HTML vs PDF).
- Better UX when downloading linked files: progress feedback, duplicate avoidance, configurable handling of HTML results, and clear SSL warnings.
- Tests increase confidence and prevent regressions.

Files touched (high level)
- Modified/added: org/jabref/logic/net/URLDownload.java, org/jabref/gui/linkedfile/DownloadLinkedFileAction.java
- Added tests: URLDownloadTest, DownloadLinkedFileActionTest

Notes
- WireMock is used in tests to simulate HTTP responses and redirects.
- One FTP test is annotated to be disabled on CI where FTP access may be blocked.

Summary:
Fix a NullPointerException that occurred when using the middle mouse button on Windows.

Root cause:
The mouse event handling code assumed certain fields were always non-null and used platform-specific button values directly. On Windows a particular event path produced a null / unexpected value for the mouse button, which caused an NPE when the handler dereferenced it.

What this change does:
- Adds defensive null checks and safe defaults when reading mouse event button information.
- Normalizes mouse button mapping so middle-click is handled consistently across platforms.
- Refactors the click handling path to avoid dereferencing possibly-null fields.
- Adds unit tests that exercise left, right, and middle clicks on supported platforms.

Testing performed:
- Unit tests added and passing in CI.
- Manual validation on Windows: reproduced previous NPE with middle-click and verified the exception no longer occurs and the expected application behavior happens.
- Regression check for left and right mouse buttons confirmed no behavioral change.

Impact and compatibility:
Low-risk bugfix. Changes are localized to input/mouse event handling and are backward-compatible.

Notes for reviewers / QA:
- To reproduce manually: start the app on Windows, perform a middle mouse click in the affected view. Previously this threw an NPE; with this PR it should not and the click should be handled normally.
- No changes required to external APIs.

text:
Summary

This PR refactors handleStringData in ImportHandler to use CompositeIdFetcher for identifier-based lookups (DOI, arXiv, ISBN, etc.) instead of doing separate parsing and fetch calls. The change centralizes ID detection and fetching logic in CompositeIdFetcher and falls back to the existing tryImportFormats when no valid identifier is present.

What I changed

- Updated ImportHandler.handleStringData to:
  - Use CompositeIdFetcher.containsValidId(data) to determine whether to run an ID search.
  - Instantiate CompositeIdFetcher with import format preferences and call performSearchById(data).
  - Convert the Optional<BibEntry> result to a List using OptionalUtil.toList.
  - If no valid ID is detected, call tryImportFormats(data) as before.
- Added the necessary import for CompositeIdFetcher.
- (Per issue notes) Added a no-args constructor to CompositeFetcher so performSearchById can be used via an instance.

Why

- Consolidates identifier detection and lookup logic into CompositeIdFetcher, reducing duplicated parsing code and making future ID-handling extensions easier.
- performSearchById is an instance method, so we now create an instance with the configured import format preferences.

Behavioral impact

- Functionality remains the same from the user perspective: strings containing a recognizable ID (DOI, arXiv, ISBN, etc.) will be fetched via the composite fetcher; otherwise, import format detection is attempted.
- Cleaner, more maintainable code path for ID-based imports.

Related

Closes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/12004

Notes

- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance.
- No user-visible changes beyond the refactor; tests and changelog updates not included in this PR.

Fix keyword parsing to correctly handle escaped delimiters and update serialization

What I changed
- Fixed a bug where delimiters contained inside keywords (escaped with a backslash) were split as separate keywords.
- Replaced the old StringTokenizer-based parsing with a custom parser (getKeywordsAsStrings) that supports escaping via backslash and trims keywords.
- Updated serialize(...) to escape backslashes and the configured delimiter when producing the joined string.
- Removed the unused StringTokenizer import.
- Added a unit test to verify parsing of an escaped delimiter and adjusted existing tests formatting.
- Updated CHANGELOG to include the fix. (Closes #12810)

Why
- Previously, keywords like "Machine\, Learning" were split on the comma and produced incorrect keyword entries. The new parser treats a backslash before the delimiter as an escape and preserves the delimiter inside the keyword.

Tests
- Added parseKeywordListContainingSingleBackslashBeforeComma to assert that escaped delimiters are handled correctly.
- Existing tests were tidied up and still cover whitespace, duplicates, hierarchical parsing and merging.

Compatibility notes
- Serialization now explicitly escapes backslashes and delimiter characters. Stored keyword strings will include these escapes when serialized by this code to ensure correct round-trip parsing.

3. Resize and move the window, restart the application, and confirm the new bounds are restored.
4. Observe there are no exceptions related to frame initialization in the logs during startup.

Notes
- This is a focused UI-startup fix and should be backward compatible. The changelog entry summarizes the user-visible behavior change.
