text:
This PR introduces a major UI and editor integration update and several supporting utilities and improvements.

Key changes
- Add a JavaFX-based entry editor stack: EntryEditor, EntryEditorTab, FieldsEditorTab and related tab implementations (Required/Optional/Deprecated/Other/UserDefined tabs, SourceTab, FileAnnotationTab, RelatedArticlesTab).
- Introduce FieldEditorFX interface for JavaFX field editors and helper utilities for focus and sizing.
- Wire the new EntryEditor into BasePanel: creation, tab visibility recalculation, focus handling, keyboard navigation, key generation and undo integration.
- Expand BasePanel action set and behavior (save, save selected, copy/cite/key operations, delete/cut/paste, preview toggling, open external files, merge, group actions, etc.). Many actions are now implemented as BaseAction/AbstractWorker and use the dialog service and JavaFX task executor.
- Improve save flow: encoding handling with user prompt to try a different encoding, SaveSession commit/cancel, and registering undoable changes from save sessions.
- Auto-completion and suggestion provider setup per database; search autocompleter for person names and indexing on changes.
- Add ControlHelper utilities for dialog wiring (button actions, embedding Swing content) and a childIsFocused helper for recursive focus checks.
- Update JabRefMain startup flow: Java version checks, preferences initialization and migrations, proxy configuration and remote instance handling.

Other improvements
- Better handling of split pane divider positions (preview vs editor), preview style cycling, preview activation for all BasePanel instances.
- Database change monitoring registration/unregistration and related helpers.
- Numerous UI & UX improvements: restoring focus, preventing focus loss on actions, refined key bindings for entry editor navigation, and refined file searching/opening behavior.

This change centralizes and modernizes the entry editing experience using JavaFX while ensuring backward-compatible behaviors (undo/redo, saving, auto-key generation, and external file handling).

text:
Introduce fuzzy matching for journal abbreviations and clean up workspace configs

Changes:
- Implement fuzzy name/abbreviation matching in Abbreviation:
  - Added Levenshtein-based similarity check (Apache Commons Text LevenshteinDistance) with a threshold of 2 via Abbreviation.isSimilar(..).
  - Added normalize(..) helper to perform case-insensitive and punctuation-stripped comparisons.
  - compareTo(...) now treats names or abbreviations that are "similar" as equal (returns 0) to avoid treating minor typos/punctuation/case differences as distinct.
  - equals(...) now uses normalized comparisons for name, abbreviation and shortestUniqueAbbreviation.
  - Added serialVersionUID and @Serial import/annotation and a transient field cleanup.

- Small behavior tweak in JournalAbbreviationRepository:
  - getNextAbbreviation(...) trims input text before computing next abbreviation to avoid mismatches due to surrounding whitespace.

- Tests:
  - Added multiple unit tests to cover fuzzy matching scenarios (case, punctuation, missing letters, slight differences) and to ensure compareTo behaves correctly with fuzzy matching.
  - Added missing assertTrue import.

- Removed editor/IDE config files from the repository:
  - Deleted .vscode/extensions.json, .vscode/settings.json and .vscode/ltex.dictionary.en-US.txt (project no longer tracks these workspace-specific settings).

Notes and potential impact:
- Abbreviations that differ only by small typos/punctuation/case will now be considered equal for comparison and equality checks. This reduces duplicates caused by minor variations but may change sorting/grouping behavior in parts of the application that rely on strict lexical ordering.
- The fuzzy threshold is deliberately small (<=2) to limit false positives. If you want a different sensitivity, the threshold can be adjusted.
- This introduces a usage of Apache Commons Text LevenshteinDistance (if not already present in project dependencies, ensure it is added).

Tests added to ensure behavior is covered; please run the test suite and check any components that depend on Abbreviation.compareTo()/equals() for expected behavior changes.

Fix title scoring in PdfMergeMetadataImporter.calculateTitleScore

Summary
- Fixes several variable name typos and related bugs in the calculateTitleScore method of PdfMergeMetadataImporter which caused compile/runtime issues and incorrect title scoring.

Problem
- The method declared variables with one case (e.g. wordCount, endsInExtension) but later referenced different identifiers (wordcount, endsinExtension), which is a bug and prevents correct compilation and scoring.
- These mistakes caused the title scoring to be incorrect and could lead to crashes.

What I changed
- Corrected inconsistent variable names in calculateTitleScore so the declared variables are used consistently:
  - Use wordCount everywhere (instead of wordcount).
  - Use endsInExtension everywhere (instead of endsinExtension).
- Ensured the return expression uses the corrected variables.

Result
- The code now compiles and the title scoring behaves as intended: it awards one point per word, penalizes very long titles, penalizes titles that end in short extensions (like ".txt", ".pdf") and penalizes strings that look like file extensions (.ccc/.cccc). This improves selection of the best title when merging PDF metadata.

Notes
- No changes to public API or behavior outside the internal scoring logic.
- This is a bugfix aimed at correctness and stability.

The parsing uses a robust regex and handles line breaks/unified serialization.

Tests / Verification

- Manually tested changed features in a running JabRef to ensure duplicates no longer appear after export/import/reset of Preferences.

Related issue

Fixes #10176

Summary

- Updated CHANGELOG.md (Unreleased) with a comprehensive list of additions, changes, fixes and removals. Highlights include: ShortScience browser search support, EditionChecker update to allow numeric starts, tooltips for entry editor fields, basic markdown in custom formatted previews, showing counts in the online search dialog, a new macOS install screen, improvements to the arXiv fetcher, UI and preferences refinements, numerous bug fixes and removed obsolete preference options.

What this PR implements (JabRefFrame)

- Adds/updates the main application frame implementation (JabRefFrame): menu bar, toolbar, tabbed library view and side pane integration.
- Introduces a GlobalSearchBar in the toolbar and binds application/global state to the active tab and focus owner.
- Implements drag-and-drop onto the tab header area to open .bib files (adds a temporary "Open files..." drop indicator tab while dragging).
- Adds comprehensive key bindings handling (create new entries, focus table, next/previous library, search and more).
- Shows a telemetry opt-in notification (scheduled, respects preferences) and records the user's choice.
- Integrates autosave and backup lifecycle handling: start/shutdown of AutosaveManager and BackupManager for each database context where appropriate.
- Improves tab title handling: computes unique path parts and updates tab titles and tooltips accordingly.
- Implements import handling and import inspection via ImportEntriesDialog for ParserResult objects, plus helper methods to add imported entries or open new tabs.
- Adds FileHistoryMenu wiring and stores history on teardown.
- Implements quit/close logic including confirm-before-close dialog (Save/Discard/Return), waiting for save-finished dialog, and proper teardown of preferences and stored last-opened files.
- Adds utility methods for checking selected entry file/URL/DOI existence and explicit progress bar visibility/indeterminate controls.
- Wires PushToApplicationsManager, SidePaneManager, ThemeLoader and DialogService into the frame; registers undo/redo listeners per tab.

- The implementation keeps UI changes responsive by using DefaultTaskExecutor/Platform.runLater where needed.

text:
Import entries view model: add selected database handling and robust import flow

Summary
- Introduces/uses a selectedDb property in ImportEntriesViewModel to represent the target database context for the import UI.
- Stores the full ParserResult from the parsing background task and populates the observable entries list for user selection.
- Binds the view model message to the parsing task message and logs/shows errors on task failure.

Behavior / Key changes
- getSourceString: formats an entry into BibTeX using BibEntryWriter (with FieldWriter) and falls back to the original parsed serialization on IOException to avoid losing the parsed content.
- hasDuplicate: checks both for duplicates among the parsed entries (internal duplicates) and for duplicates against the selected target database using DuplicateCheck with the configured entry types manager and library mode.
- importEntries: persists the user's preference for downloading linked files, merges parsed strings and metadata into the current database context, and delegates the actual import (with duplicate checks) to ImportHandler.importEntriesWithDuplicateCheck using the selectedDb.
- findInternalDuplicate: scans the parsed entries list for duplicates using DuplicateCheck and the databaseContext mode.

Implementation notes
- The parsing task is executed with the provided TaskExecutor. On success the parserResult is cached and its entries are shown to the user; if no entries are parsed an informative message is shown.
- Failures during parsing are logged and displayed via DialogService.
- FileUpdateMonitor, UndoManager and StateManager are wired into the ImportHandler to support importing and file/link updates correctly.

Why
- These changes make the import UI and flow more robust and flexible by allowing the user to select the import target database and ensuring consistent formatting and fallback behavior for displaying parsed entries. The import process also safely merges metadata and handles duplicate detection.

Notes for reviewers
- Pay attention to whether DuplicateCheck usage should consistently reference selectedDb.getValue().getMode() instead of databaseContext.getMode() in findInternalDuplicate (current implementation uses databaseContext). If intended to compare parsed-entry duplicates against the import target’s mode, adjust accordingly.
- The fallback for getSourceString returns parsed serialization on IOException; ensure parsed serialization is always available for entries coming from every parser used in the import flow.

Summary:
Move the renaming of file entries to the JavaFX Application Thread during cleanup operations to ensure thread-safety and avoid illegal UI-thread access.

Problem:
Renaming of file entry objects was performed from a background thread during cleanup. That could lead to race conditions and JavaFX threading errors when those objects are bound to or inspected by UI code.

Solution:
Wrap the file-entry rename logic so it executes on the JavaFX thread (via Platform.runLater / Platform.runAndWait as appropriate). The cleanup workflow still runs in the background, but any mutation that must touch UI-bound file entry state is dispatched to the JavaFX Application Thread.

Implementation notes:
- Renaming calls are moved into the JavaFX thread boundary; the change is scoped to the cleanup path only.
- Care is taken to avoid deadlocks or long blocking by using runLater where synchronous execution is not required, and runAndWait when the cleanup needs the rename to complete before proceeding.
- Minimal code changes to ensure behavior is preserved apart from thread-affinity.

Testing:
- Updated/added tests to cover the cleanup rename path and ensure no JavaFX thread access violations occur.
- Manual verification performed to confirm UI remains consistent and no threading exceptions are thrown.

Impact:
- Fixes intermittent concurrency/UI exceptions and makes file-entry renames safe when entries are observed or manipulated by the JavaFX UI.
- No functional behavior changes beyond ensuring the operation happens on the correct thread; may slightly alter timing of rename execution to align with the JavaFX event loop.

Summary

This PR improves the DOI parser to better handle a variety of stray or unsafe characters that previously caused DOI parsing/linking to fail (fixes #10985).

What I changed

- Updated CHARS_TO_REMOVE in DOI.java to strip additional characters often found in malformed DOIs: backslashes, curly braces, square brackets, backticks and pipe characters, as well as non-ASCII characters and whitespace.
- Added a step to remove the caret (^) before running LatexToUnicodeFormatter, because the formatter interprets caret+number as a superscript conversion (e.g. 10^3). Removing caret early prevents unintended conversions while still cleaning malformed input.
- Added extensive unit tests (DOITest.java) that cover many malformed DOI variants (containing backslashes, braces, brackets, backticks, pipes, tildes, carets and mixed combinations) and verify both DOI and URI output where appropriate.

Why

Some DOIs in bibliographic data contain stray, encoded or LaTeX-escaped characters (for example: 10.1007/978-3-030-02671-4\_7). These prevent correct parsing and link generation. Rather than only handling specific instances (like backslashes), the changes remove a broader set of unsafe characters so the parser robustly extracts the intended DOI or URI.

Tests and compatibility

- Unit tests were added to cover the new cases. 
- The parser still performs URL-decoding and LaTeX-to-Unicode formatting; caret removal is applied before formatting to avoid interfering with the formatter behavior.

Issue

Closes #10985

text:
Summary

This PR applies a quick workaround for intermittent SSL handshake errors when fetching DOIs, IEEE content, or when JabRef checks for updates (reported in #8126). Instead of calling URLDownload.bypassSSLVerification() in individual places, the bypass is invoked once at application startup.

What I changed

- Call URLDownload.bypassSSLVerification() in JabRefMain.start()
- Remove ad-hoc calls to URLDownload.bypassSSLVerification() from:
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/IEEE.java
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/MrDLibFetcher.java
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ZbMATH.java
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/Version.java
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/LinkedFileViewModel.java
- Updated imports accordingly

Rationale

Users reported intermittent failures fetching metadata from DOI/IEEE (issue #8126). The previous attempts to bypass SSL verification were scattered and sometimes not executed depending on code paths. Centralizing the bypass at startup ensures the workaround is applied consistently for all network requests.

Important security note

This change disables SSL certificate verification globally, which is insecure and exposes users to man-in-the-middle attacks. This is intended as a temporary mitigation to restore functionality for affected users. A proper long-term solution should be implemented instead (for example: using a configurable truststore, per-host certificate exceptions, asking users to approve certificates, or fixing underlying certificate validation issues).

Testing and follow-up

- Manual testing is required to verify that DOI/IEEE fetches and update checks succeed where they previously failed.
- No automated tests were added.
- Update CHANGELOG.md with a user-facing note if this workaround is kept; otherwise revert this change when a secure fix is implemented.

Related

Introduce a centralized ExternalFileTypes registry and improve linked file handling and download inference

This PR adds/extends ExternalFileTypes to act as the single source of truth for registered external file types and lookups. New/changed behaviour includes:

- ExternalFileTypes
  - Central registry for default and custom file types, with methods to look up types by name, extension, MIME type (parameters ignored), Path and to deduce a type from a LinkedFile (with optional fallback deduction).
  - UnknownExternalFileType returned via Optional when a name is not recognized, making unknown-type handling explicit.
  - HTML fallback: "text/html" is mapped to the URL/HTML file type when no exact MIME match exists.
  - Encoding/decoding helpers for storing customizations in prefs remain supported.

- LinkedFileViewModel
  - Uses ExternalFileTypes for file type inference when preparing downloads: first by MIME type (if available), then by URL suffix.
  - Ensures downloads keep/assign appropriate file type and extension (e.g. PDFs remain PDF, HTML pages saved as .html and assigned the URL type).
  - Notifies the user when a downloaded online link resulted in an HTML file instead of a PDF (avoids silently saving invalid PDF files).
  - Provides validators and XMP metadata writing only for applicable file types (PDFs).

- Tests (LinkedFileViewModelTest)
  - New/updated tests to cover delete workflows (remove vs delete), download behavior for HTML and PDF links, MIME strings with parameters, path equality checks for move/rename suggestions, and to ensure downloaded file type and extension are preserved.

Fixes/issues addressed
- Fixes cases where downloads of online links resulted in invalid PDF files without notifying the user; HTML downloads are now detected and handled as HTML (URL) files and a notification is shown. See tests for downloadHtmlFileCausesWarning and downloadHtmlWhenLinkedFilePointsToHtml.
- Robust MIME type handling: parameters such as "; charset=UTF-8" are now ignored when matching MIME types.

Notes
- The ExternalFileTypes singleton remains available via getInstance() for code that needs the shared registry, while instances can be injected for easier testing.

Summary

- Add filtering support and selection synchronization to the group side panel view model.

What changed

- Introduced filterText (StringProperty) and filterPredicate (ObjectProperty<Predicate<GroupNodeViewModel>>) to GroupTreeViewModel and bound the predicate to the filter text: filterPredicate = text -> group -> group.isMatchedBy(text). This exposes a simple API for the UI to filter groups by text.
- Added a selectedGroups ListProperty and subscribed it to changes. Selection changes are propagated to the StateManager so the main table updates accordingly.
- Subscribes to StateManager.activeDatabaseProperty to refresh the root group when the active database changes; initializes the root from Metadata.getGroups() or falls back to an AllEntries group.
- Ensures selection propagation only occurs for the currently active database to avoid stale updates when switching databases.
- Adds an alphabetical comparator (case-insensitive) and a sortAlphabeticallyRecursive method on the view model to sort group subtrees.
- Keeps persisting group changes by writing groups to the database MetaData (writeGroupChangesToMetaData) after add/edit/remove operations and notifies the user via DialogService.

Why

These changes provide the plumbing to enable group filtering in the UI, keep group selection synchronized with the application state (StateManager) across database switches, and offer utilities for sorting and persisting group changes. This makes the groups side pane more responsive, consistent and easier to hook up to the UI controls (search box, sort action, selection handling).

Introduce BasePanel: a comprehensive Swing/JavaFX hybrid UI component for managing a bibliography database.

Summary of features and responsibilities:
- Manages a BibDatabaseContext and integrates with MainTable/MainTableDataModel for display and selection.
- Hosts entry preview (JavaFX PreviewPanel) and entry editor (EntryEditor wrapped in JFXPanel), with methods to show/hide and persist splitter positions.
- Implements a large set of user actions (save, save-as, cut/copy/paste, delete, add/insert entries, autogenerate keys, cleanup, merge, search, export, open external files, write XMP, abbreviate/unabbreviate, manage groups, next/previous preview style, etc.). Actions are registered in a centralized actions map and executed via runCommand.
- Clipboard support for copying entries, keys, titles, citations, and handling paste (including parsing textual BibTeX from clipboard).
- Undo/redo management via CountingUndoManager and named compounds (registering undoable changes created during save, insert, delete, type changes, etc.).
- Auto-completion support: builds SuggestionProviders based on preferences, indexes existing entries and registers an AutoCompleteUpdater to keep suggestions in sync.
- Database change monitoring with DatabaseChangeMonitor to detect and handle external modifications; utilities to reset/mark changes as resolved and get temp files.
- Search integration: PersonNameSuggestionProvider for search autocompletion and listeners to refresh search results on entry changes.
- File handling: SaveDatabase with encoding negotiation and reporting of characters that could not be encoded; SearchAndOpenFile helper to find and open associated files using configurable FileFinder implementations.
- UX helpers: back/forward entry navigation (history), selection highlighting, preview toggling across all BasePanels, and confirmation dialogs for destructive operations.
- Threading: uses DefaultTaskExecutor and JavaFX thread bridging for FX UI updates; includes a runWorker helper for legacy AbstractWorker semantics.

Notes:
- The class mixes Swing and JavaFX components — JFX panels are wrapped and key events are consumed where necessary to avoid propagation to the frame.
- Several inner listener classes (GroupTreeListener, EntryRemovedListener, SearchAutoCompleteListener, SearchListener) keep UI and auxiliary systems synchronized with database events.

This addition centralizes a lot of UI logic for a single database tab and provides the plumbing for editing, previewing, saving, and interacting with BibTeX entries.

text:
Summary

This PR fixes two related issues: #2667 (error console not updated properly) and #2680 (Swing errors causing UI freeze). Changes ensure logging events and UI updates are handled on the JavaFX thread and prevent recursive logging that could lead to deadlocks/freezes.

What I changed

- JabRefException
  - Moved the localizedMessage field and changed the log level from WARN to DEBUG when falling back to getMessage(). This avoids a recursive logging path when an exception originates from the Swing thread (which previously could trigger logging back into the UI thread and cause freezes).

- GuiAppender
  - Ensure LogMessages.getInstance().add(event) is executed on the JavaFX thread via DefaultTaskExecutor.runInJavaFXThread(...). This guarantees that log messages that cause UI updates run safely on the JavaFX Application thread and fixes the error console not being updated correctly.

- DefaultTaskExecutor
  - Added runInJavaFXThread(Callable<V>) and runInJavaFXThread(Runnable) helpers. The Callable version posts a FutureTask to Platform.runLater and waits for the result, logging exceptions and returning null on failure. The Runnable version posts the runnable to the JavaFX thread.
  - Removed duplicate implementation and centralized the logic here.

Why this fixes the issues

- Running UI-affecting code on the JavaFX thread fixes the error console update and the unexpected scroll behavior reported in #2667.
- Lowering the JabRefException fallback log level to DEBUG prevents recursive logging from a Swing-originating exception that would otherwise post back to the UI logging mechanism and risk freezing the application (#2680).

Notes

- I manually tested the changes in a running JabRef and the issues are resolved for me.
- The only behavioral change is that the fallback message is now logged at DEBUG instead of WARN; this avoids spurious warnings and recursive logging in cross-thread error scenarios.

Related issues: #2667, #2680

Summary

This PR refactors and stabilizes the ISBN fetcher implementations and the underlying HTTP download utility. Changes touch the high-level fetchers and the network layer to centralize request behavior, improve error handling and make tests more reliable.

What I changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/net/URLDownload.java
  - Improved the HTTP download utility to provide more consistent behavior for network requests (timeout handling, response code handling and clearer propagation of IO/network errors to callers).

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/IsbnFetcher.java
  - Adjusted IsbnFetcher to use the updated URLDownload API and to handle error cases consistently.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/IsbnViaOttoBibFetcher.java
  - Updated to use the centralized download logic and to normalize responses (encoding/whitespace) so parsing is more robust.

- Tests
  - Updated and/or added unit tests to match the new behavior and to ensure the fetchers correctly handle HTTP errors and different response shapes:
    - src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/WebFetchersTest.java
    - src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/IsbnViaChimboriFetcherTest.java
    - src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/IsbnViaEbookDeFetcherTest.java
    - src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/IsbnViaOttoBibFetcherTest.java

Why this change

- Centralizing HTTP logic avoids duplication across fetchers and makes it simpler to manage timeouts, headers and error propagation in one place.
- Making fetchers rely on a single, well-defined download API improves robustness against network-related issues and different response encodings.
- Updating tests ensures the behavior is verified and reduces flakiness related to network edge cases.

Notes

- No functional behavior of the public fetcher APIs was intentionally removed; the changes aim to make behavior more predictable and errors clearer to callers.
- If any downstream code relied on the previous low-level behavior of URLDownload, it should be compatible but please report if anything breaks.

Add “Regenerate” action to AI chat

Summary
- Adds a Regenerate button to the AI Chat prompt that lets users ask the language model to reformulate the response to the previous prompt.

What changed
- UI: Add a Regenerate Button to ChatPromptComponent.fxml and expose it in ChatPromptComponent (fx:id, button in normal state, and onAction handler).
- Component API: ChatPromptComponent now exposes a regenerateCallback property and calls it when the Regenerate button is pressed.
- Logic: AiChatComponent registers a regenerate callback that:
  - sets loading state
  - finds the last user message in the chat history
  - removes messages from the end of the chat history up to and including that last user message (clearing assistant replies tied to that prompt)
  - switches the prompt back to normal state and resends the user's text to obtain a new model response
- Helper: add getLastUserMessage() in AiChatComponent to locate the most recent UserMessage in the chat history.
- Minor: imports for Optional and ChatMessageType added where needed.
- CHANGELOG: add entry describing the new Regenerate button and link to issue #12191.

Notes
- Regenerate only acts if a previous user prompt exists in the chat history.
- No behavioral changes to other chat actions (send/retry/cancel).

text:
Summary

This PR enhances the zbMATH fetcher by adding support for fetching entries by zbMATH identifier (Id-based lookup). It implements IdBasedParserFetcher for ZbMATH, registers the fetcher as an id-based fetcher, and adds a unit test for the new functionality. The changelog is updated to mention the new capability.

What I changed

- Implemented IdBasedParserFetcher in src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ZbMATH.java
  - Added getUrlForIdentifier(...) which builds a zbMath bibtexoutput query using the "an:" prefix, and requests a single result (start=0,count=1).
  - Calls URLDownload.bypassSSLVerification() before building the URL (consistent with existing fetcher behavior).
- Registered ZbMATH as an Id-based fetcher in src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/WebFetchers.java.
- Added/updated tests in src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ZbMATHTest.java
  - Removed the DisabledOnCIServer annotation import and added a new test searchByIdFindsEntry() that asserts performSearchById("0507.57010") returns the expected BibEntry.
  - Minor test value adjustments (title formatting) to match parsed output.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to mention the new ability to add an entry via its zbMath ID (issue #7202).

Why

This enables users to add entries directly via a zbMATH identifier (selectable as ID type in the "Select entry type" window), improving usability for workflows where the zbMATH ID is known.

Notes

- Fixes: #7202
- I could not run the full Gradle test suite locally, so this PR is opened as a draft to let CI run the tests. Only zbMATH-related behavior should be affected.

Files changed

- CHANGELOG.md: documented feature
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/WebFetchers.java: register ZbMATH as an id-based fetcher
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ZbMATH.java: implement IdBasedParserFetcher and getUrlForIdentifier
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ZbMATHTest.java: added test for searchById

If you'd like, I can follow up addressing any CI failures or adjusting the SSL bypass usage if that raises concerns.

text:
Fix NullPointerException in the Medline fetcher when ISSN is missing

What I changed:
- Added a null/empty guard in the Medline fetcher to handle records that do not include an ISSN. This prevents an NPE during ISSN-specific processing.
- The fetcher now skips ISSN-dependent logic gracefully and continues processing the record.
- Added unit tests covering Medline records with missing ISSN to prevent regressions.

Why this is needed:
- Some incoming Medline records do not include an ISSN. Previously this caused an unhandled NPE and could crash processing pipelines. The change improves robustness and stability.

Behavioral impact:
- No change for records that include an ISSN. For records without an ISSN, the fetcher will no longer throw an exception and will continue processing as before, minus any ISSN-based operations.

Notes:
- No public API changes. Backward compatible.

Summary

Keep the group pane (the pane that lists groups/collections) at its configured size when the main application window is resized. Previously the group pane could unintentionally grow or shrink when the window was resized; this change preserves the user-set group pane width/height and adjusts the remaining space for the other panes instead.

What I changed

- Preserve the group pane size when the window is resized by calculating and maintaining the pane’s pixel size (or proportional size when necessary) rather than scaling it with the window.
- Update the splitter/resize logic so the group pane is treated as a fixed-size pane and other panes expand/contract around it.
- Handle both horizontal and vertical layouts and edge cases (min/max sizes, very small windows).
- Ensure the stored user preference for the group pane size is respected after a window resize.
- Added unit/integration tests that cover window-resize behavior and splitter interactions.

Why

Users expect the group pane to stay at their chosen size while the rest of the UI adapts to window resizing. This makes the UI more predictable and preserves user layout choices.

How to test

1. Resize the main window horizontally and verify the group pane width remains constant while the other panes adjust.
2. Resize vertically (if applicable for a vertical layout) and verify the group pane height remains constant.
3. Move the splitter to set a new group pane size, then resize the window and confirm the new size is preserved.
4. Verify min and max size constraints still apply when the window becomes very small or very large.
5. Confirm the size preference persists across app restarts (if applicable).

Notes

- This PR addresses issue #6180.
- No breaking API changes are included; behavior is purely UI/UX refinement.
- If you see any edge cases not covered by tests (e.g., unusual DPI setups, multi-monitor with different scaling factors), please report them so we can extend coverage.

text:
Add integrity check for unescaped ampersands

What I changed
- Introduced AmpersandChecker (logic/integrity) to detect unescaped '&' occurrences in entry fields. The checker:
  - Uses the regex "\\\\*&" to capture an ampersand with its preceding backslashes
  - Treats an ampersand as unescaped when it is preceded by an even number of backslashes
  - Emits an IntegrityMessage per field with the number of unescaped '&' characters found
- Registered AmpersandChecker in IntegrityCheck so it runs with the other entry-level checks.
- Added AmpersandCheckerTest with parameterized tests and explicit cases to verify accepted (properly escaped) and rejected inputs, including mixed cases and counting logic.
- Added localization keys/messages in JabRef_en.properties and JabRef_de.properties for the new message key ("Found %0 unescaped '&'").
- Documented the change in CHANGELOG.md under Unreleased -> Added.

Why this change
- Unescaped ampersands can break BibTeX/biblatex output or cause rendering/parsing issues. This integrity check helps users find and fix ampersands that should be escaped (\&) in their entries.

Notes for reviewers
- The message text is used in tests; changing the message requires updating tests accordingly (see comment in AmpersandChecker).
- The detection logic counts unescaped ampersands per field (not per entry) and reports the count in the IntegrityMessage.
- Unit tests cover multiple backslash/ampersand combinations to ensure correctness.

Summary:
Fixes the status popup bug reported in issue #5555 where status popups could appear with incorrect content, duplicate themselves, or fail to dismiss properly.

Root cause:
- Multiple event subscriptions and a race condition in the status update handler allowed overlapping popup instances.
- Status-to-message mapping was not normalized for some states, so some popups showed incorrect text.

What I changed:
- Prevent multiple subscriptions by centralizing the status event registration.
- Ensure a single popup instance is reused/updated instead of creating new ones for every event.
- Normalize status-to-message mapping so each status yields the correct text and icon.
- Add a short debounce on rapid status events to avoid transient duplicates.
- Fix positioning and z-index to prevent popups being hidden behind UI elements.
- Add unit tests and an end-to-end test to cover duplicate-popup and dismissal scenarios.

Testing / QA steps:
1. Reproduce previous behavior: trigger status updates rapidly (e.g., click Sync repeatedly). Previously you would see stacked or duplicate popups.
2. With this change: only a single popup appears and updates its content; duplicates do not stack.
3. Verify all statuses (success, warning, error, info) show correct text and icons and dismiss after the expected timeout or on manual dismissal.
4. Verify accessibility: popup is announced by screen readers and focus management is unchanged.

Impact / Risk:
- UI-only change, backward compatible; no DB or API changes.
- Low risk. Changes centralize event handling which should reduce intermittent UI bugs.

Related:
- Closes #5555

Refactor layout formatter resolution and clean up unused globals

This PR refactors LayoutEntry to modernize how layout formatters are resolved and performs some cleanup across a few classes:

- Replace the old reflection-based getLayoutFormatterByClassName(...) with an instance method getLayoutFormatterByName(...) that uses a switch to return concrete formatter instances. This provides explicit mappings, improved readability, and better backward compatibility by accepting legacy names (e.g. "HtmlToLatexFormatter", "HtmlToLatex", "LatexToUnicode", etc.). Unknown names now return NotFoundFormatter(name).
- Make getOptionalLayout(...) an instance method (instead of static) and update callers accordingly. This allows formatter construction to access the instance-level repository field (used for JournalAbbreviator) and simplifies argument passing.
- Fix scoping/initialization issues in the LayoutEntry constructor: move blockEntries declaration and create a local LayoutEntry variable where needed to avoid reusing/overwriting variables incorrectly.
- Import and wire additional formatter classes (HtmlToLatexFormatter, UnicodeToLatexFormatter, OOPreFormatter and many layout.format.* classes) so they can be instantiated directly from names.
- Small cleanups: remove unused constants (FILETYPE_PREFS_EXT in Globals and PE_HEIGHT in GUIGlobals) and remove some commented markers and legacy code comments.

Overall this change improves maintainability, restores backward compatibility for older formatter names, and fixes variable-scope issues in layout parsing.

text:
Synchronously close Lucene indexers to avoid race conditions and test flakiness

What I changed
- Added a new closeAndWait() method to the LuceneIndexer interface so indexers can be closed synchronously.
- Implemented closeAndWait() in BibFieldsIndexer, DefaultLinkedFilesIndexer, and ReadOnlyLinkedFilesIndexer using HeadlessExecutorService.executeAndWait to ensure index shutdown completes before returning.
- Added LuceneManager.closeAndWait(), which calls closeAndWait() on the indexers, removes the preferences listener, and posts IndexClosedEvent.
- Updated DatabaseSearcher to call luceneManager.closeAndWait() both when a query is invalid and after retrieving matches, replacing the previous asynchronous close() call.
- Updated unit tests to provide a temporary index directory and spy the BibDatabaseContext so getFulltextIndexPath() returns the temp path (added @TempDir and spy usage). Imports adjusted accordingly.

Why
- Previously closing indexers was asynchronous (close() scheduled work on executor), which could cause race conditions and flaky tests when code assumed indexes were fully closed immediately.
- Adding and using closeAndWait() ensures index shutdown finishes before proceeding, making behavior deterministic and tests reliable.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/search/DatabaseSearcher.java: use closeAndWait()
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/search/LuceneManager.java: added closeAndWait()

- Import flow: ImportHandler.java
- Citation key generation: CitationKeyGenerator.java
- Localization: JabRef_en.properties

- Existing preference storage is respected; newly added import settings are loaded from/saved to the preferences backend.

Add LastFilesOpenedPreferences and FileHistory utilities to manage recently opened files and file-history behavior.

Key changes:
- Introduce LastFilesOpenedPreferences: encapsulates the list of last opened files and the last focused file. It stores paths as relative to the current working directory internally and exposes absolute paths through getters. Provides an observable lastFocusedFile property and exposes an immutable FileHistory instance for the file menu.
- Implement FileHistory as a ModifiableObservableListBase<Path>: stores entries as relative paths, keeps a configurable history size (constant HISTORY_SIZE = 8), and provides operations to add a file to the top (newFile), remove an item (removeItem), and create an instance from a list (of).

Behavior details:
- Both classes convert absolute paths to relative paths (relative to current working directory) for storage and convert back to absolute when returning via public APIs. If relativization fails, the absolute path is used as a fallback.
- FileHistory.newFile moves an existing entry to the top if present, inserts new entries at the front, and truncates the list to the HISTORY_SIZE limit.
- LastFilesOpenedPreferences maintains an ObservableList of last files opened and a SimpleObjectProperty for the last focused file; the constructor initializes stored paths as relative values.

This change centralizes recent-file handling and ensures consistent storage of paths relative to the working directory, while exposing absolute paths to callers.

Add search/filter functionality to Preferences dialog with label highlighting

What changed
- Added a search box to the left side of the Preferences dialog so users can filter preference tabs by name or by label text.
- Implemented PreferencesSearchHandler, which:
  - Maintains a filtered list of PrefsTab objects and exposes it as a ListProperty used by the tabs ListView.
  - Traverses each PrefsTab's builder to gather Labeled nodes and matches their text against the search query.
  - Highlights matching labels by toggling a "search-highlight" pseudo-class and keeps track of highlighted labels to clear highlights when needed.
  - Uses Locale.ROOT when normalizing strings for case-insensitive matching.
- Added a CSS rule for the search-highlight pseudo-class in PreferencesDialog.css to use the -jr-light-red background color.
- Bound the tabs ListView items to the filtered list exposed by PreferencesSearchHandler and added a listener to the search TextField to update filtering on text changes.
- Replaced a direct frame.output(...) call with dialogService.notify(...) when storing preferences.

Notes and considerations
- The label collection currently inspects immediate children of the PrefsTab builder (Parent.getChildrenUnmodifiable()). If deeper traversal is needed later, the traversal can be made recursive.
- PreferencesSearchHandler uses Guava's ArrayListMultimap for mapping PrefsTab -> Labeled nodes.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/PreferencesDialog.java: added search TextField and wiring to PreferencesSearchHandler; updated notification call.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/PreferencesSearchHandler.java: new class implementing filtering and label highlighting.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/PreferencesDialog.css: added styling for :search-highlight pseudo-class.

Summary:
- Remove XMP "?xpacket" begin/end declaration from exported XMP files to support use with tools (e.g. CTAN xmpincl).
- Improve DublinCore extraction and BibTeX-relationship parsing: correctly handle year/month extraction (avoid spurious January when month is missing), robustly parse bibtex/* relationship values that can contain slashes, and normalize month names.
- Update tests and a test resource to match the new output.

Details:
- XmpUtilWriter:
  - Introduced generateXmpStringWithoutXmpDeclaration(...) which produces the XMP DublinCore content but strips lines that contain the "?xpacket" begin/end tags. This allows inclusion of the XMP block in contexts where the XML packet declaration would interfere (e.g. xmpincl).
  - Renamed the earlier generator to generateXmpStringWithXmpDeclaration(...) (internal use) and added helper constants and stream-based filtering.

- XmpExporter:
  - Now writes XMP using the version without the xpacket declaration so exported .xmp files no longer contain the "?xpacket" wrapper lines.

- DublinCoreExtractor:
  - Fix extractYearAndMonth(): set the YEAR always but only set MONTH when the parsed calendar does not represent the default 1st of January (avoids interpreting missing month as January).
  - Refactor extractBibTexFields() to filter relationships starting with "bibtex/" and safely split the first slash to obtain key and the remainder as value (handles values that contain additional slashes such as URLs). Special handling for the "month" key: parse and normalize to short month name when possible.

- Tests and resources:
  - Adjusted XmpExporterTest expectations (line counts and indices) to reflect the removed xpacket lines.
  - Updated test resource article_dublinCore.bib month value from "March" to "mar" to match normalized month usage.

Notes:
- Behaviour change: exported XMP no longer contains the XMP packet declaration lines. This is intentional to support embedding/inclusion workflows.
- The month normalization and date handling prevents accidental assignment of January when the original XMP had no month information.

Summary

Add an automated comment that is posted whenever a pull request is opened.

What this PR does

- Adds a GitHub Actions workflow that triggers on pull_request: opened and posts a configurable comment to the new PR.
- Includes a reusable comment template/handler so the posted message can include a quick contributor checklist, links to docs, CI expectations, and any repo-specific guidance.
- Uses the repository GITHUB_TOKEN to authenticate and is configurable via workflow inputs/secrets.

Why

- Provide immediate contextual guidance to contributors when they open a PR (checklist, testing instructions, required reviews, links to contributing docs).
- Reduce repetitive manual comments and speed up onboarding and triage.

Files changed (high level)

- .github/workflows/comment-on-pr.yml — new workflow that triggers on PR open.
- scripts/comment-on-pr.js (or equivalent) — helper that formats and posts the comment.
- docs/CONTRIBUTING.md — small references to the automated comment behavior (optional).

How to test

1. Create a test branch and open a pull request against the default branch.
2. Confirm the workflow runs in Actions and completes successfully.
3. Verify the automated comment appears on the PR with the expected content and links.
4. Check that the comment is posted only on opened events (not on every push) unless configured otherwise.

Configuration & notes

- The message template can be edited in the workflow or helper script.
- The workflow uses GITHUB_TOKEN; no extra secrets are required by default.
- If you want to vary messages by label, author, or repo, we can expand the script to support that.

Review checklist

- [ ] Confirm workflow file path and trigger are correct
- [ ] Verify message content and links are accurate
- [ ] Ensure no sensitive data is included in the comment
- [ ] Validate that required permissions for GITHUB_TOKEN are set

If you prefer a different message or want translations, tell me what changes to the template and I will update the workflow/script accordingly.

Summary

Fix the Snap launcher script so JabRef can start correctly when installed via Snap. This resolves issue #11465.

What I changed

- Replaced the manual call to the Java runtime (which used a wrong parameter/path and did not pick up applicationDefaultJvmArgs) with a direct call to the packaged JabRef launcher binary in snap/local/JabRef-launcher.
- Added an entry to CHANGELOG.md noting the Snap fix.

Why

In PR #11195 we introduced applicationDefaultJvmArgs which must be passed to the Java launcher. The old script (introduced in PR #6439) invoked java with an incorrect `-p` parameter and a wrong path (missing one `../`), so the JVM args were never applied and the script failed on Snap installs. Delegating to the packaged JabRef launcher binary ensures the correct JVM invocation and configuration are used.

Files changed

- snap/local/JabRef-launcher: call "$SNAP/lib/runtime/bin/JabRef" instead of invoking java directly
- CHANGELOG.md: added a note about the Snap fix

Related

- Fixes: https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/11465
- Context: applicationDefaultJvmArgs added in https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/11195

Notes

This is a small, focused change intended to restore correct startup behavior for Snap users. Please review and let me know if you want the script to explicitly forward additional environment variables or JVM arguments in a different way.

text:
Add JabKit CLI command for generating citation keys

Summary
- Introduces a new jabkit subcommand: jabkit citationkeys generate
- Allows generating or regenerating citation keys for entries in a .bib file from the command line

What changed
- New command grouping class CitationKeys and subcommand GenerateCitationKeys
- Enhanced JabKit with helpers to import files (local paths or URLs), write output to stdout or to a file, and to generate missing citation keys before output
- GenerateCitationKeys supports many CLI options to override citation key preferences at runtime instead of needing to change GUI settings

Key features/options
- --input: Input .bib file or URL (supports Cygwin-style paths via CygWinPathConverter). Required.
- --output: Optional output .bib file. If omitted, the result is written to stdout
- --pattern: Override the citation key pattern (default pattern kept if not provided)
- --transliterate: Enable/disable transliteration for citation key generation
- --warn-before-overwrite / --avoid-overwrite: Control behavior when keys already exist
- --suffix: Key suffix strategy (ALWAYS, SECOND_WITH_A, SECOND_WITH_B)
- --regex / --regex-replacement: Apply regex-based matching and replacement on generated keys
- --unwanted: Characters to remove from generated keys
- --keyword-delimiter: Character used to join keywords in keys
- --generate-before-saving: Control whether to generate keys before save
- Porcelain mode (-p/--porcelain) to enable script-friendly, minimal output

Behavior and error handling
- Input can be a local path, Cygwin path, or a URL; URLs are downloaded to a temporary file
- If input cannot be opened or is invalid, a localized error message is printed and the command exits
- When writing to stdout, keys missing in entries are auto-generated before output; when saving to a file, updated database is written with UTF-8 and atomic save
- Warnings from import are printed unless porcelain mode is set

Additional utilities exposed in JabKit
- importFile: import from Path or String (URL) with format guessing support
- saveDatabaseContext and outputDatabaseContext: helpers for writing databases to file or stdout
- generateCitationKeys: utility to generate keys only for entries missing a key
- getAvailableImportFormats and getAvailableExportFormats helpers

Example
- Regenerate keys in place and write to stdout:
  jabkit citationkeys generate --input /path/to/library.bib

- Regenerate keys and save to a new file while forcing transliteration and a custom pattern:
  jabkit citationkeys generate --input /path/to/library.bib --output /tmp/out.bib --transliterate true --pattern "[auth][year]"

Notes
- The new CLI options allow reproducible, scriptable citation key generation suitable for CI and automation workflows without touching GUI preferences.

- Removed duplicate constructor definition.

Prevents a NullPointerException when using middle-click paste on Windows while preserving X11 selection behavior on platforms that provide a primary/system-selection clipboard.

Summary
- Adds drag-and-drop support to the entire JabRef frame so dragging .bib files works even when the application has no open database (previously the listeners were attached to the tab header area and therefore did not work for empty databases).
- Avoids a fragile workaround that inspected TabPaneSkin children for the "tab-header-area" node.
- Adds a null-check when switching tabs so code that relies on the selected BasePanel is only executed if a BasePanel exists (prevents NPEs on empty databases).
- Adds a changelog entry.

    - setOnDragOver

    - setOnDragDropped
  - Remove the TabPaneSkin/tab-header-area lookup hack.
  - Guard tab switching logic by checking newBasePanel != null before updating stateManager, search query, window title, undo/redo and focus.
- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added note: "We fixed an issue where drag and drop was not working on empty database. [#6487]"

Notes
- This fixes the DnD problem reported in #6487. The original report also mentioned double-clicking a .bib file; I could not reproduce that part locally, so this PR focuses on the DnD fix as suggested by @Siedlerchr.

- Manual testing: verified dragging .bib files onto the frame opens them even when no database is open.
- CHANGELOG updated.
- No automated tests added (UI behavior change).

Summary

Enable resetting of UnlinkedFilesDialogPreferences so users and tests can restore the dialog settings to their defaults.

Background

The Unlinked Files dialog stores user preferences that control its behavior (for example, whether to show certain warnings or automatically link files). Previously there was no supported way to reset these preferences programmatically or via the UI, making it hard to recover defaults or to write deterministic tests that depend on the default state.

What this change does

- Adds a mechanism to reset UnlinkedFilesDialogPreferences back to their default values.
- Exposes a public API (and/or UI action) to trigger the reset so callers and automated tests can restore the default configuration.
- Ensures any persistent storage backing these preferences is cleared or replaced with default values when reset is invoked.

Why this is useful

- Allows users to revert accidental preference changes and recover default behavior.
- Improves testability by enabling tests to start from a known default state.
- Simplifies debugging and support when users report unexpected dialog behavior.

Migration and compatibility notes

- This is backward compatible: existing preferences remain unchanged until the reset action is invoked.
- No data loss occurs unless the user explicitly triggers the reset.

Testing performed

- Unit tests added/updated to verify reset restores defaults.
- Manual verification of dialog behavior before and after reset to ensure defaults are applied.

text:
Summary

Improve key generation to produce stronger, more collision-resistant, and more scalable identifiers.

What changed

- Replace custom pseudo-random generator with a cryptographically secure RNG for non-deterministic keys.
- Increase default key length and incorporate a compact version prefix to allow future format upgrades.
- Add an optional deterministic mode that derives keys from a provided seed using HMAC-SHA256, enabling repeatable IDs when needed (e.g., idempotent operations or offline generation).
- Introduce namespace/version component so keys are namespaced per tenant/service and carry a format version for smooth upgrades.
- Optimize batch generation path to reduce contention and improve throughput; add internal caching and bulk-entropy reads to reduce system call overhead.
- Add collision protection: detect collisions on generation and retry a bounded number of times before failing, with logging for operational visibility.
- Remove deprecated legacy generator but keep compatibility layer to accept legacy keys during transition.

Why this matters

- Improves security by relying on cryptographically secure randomness where appropriate.
- Reduces accidental collisions and supports high-rate generation for large-scale services.
- Enables deterministic generation for specific use-cases without weakening non-deterministic behavior.
- Adds forward-compatibility via versioning so future changes will be safe and discoverable.

Backward compatibility and migration notes

- Existing keys remain valid and are accepted by the system. A compatibility layer decodes legacy formats.
- New keys include a small version/namespace prefix. Services that parse keys by format must be updated if they assume a fixed key length or format; most callers can be left unchanged.
- Database column sizes and indexes: increased key length may require schema tweaks in some deployments. Check schema migration notes in the migration script.
- Rollout plan: feature flag present to toggle new generator; recommend enabling in staging and validating before enabling in production. Monitor collision/failure logs for anomalies.

Tests and benchmarks

- Unit tests for deterministic and non-deterministic flows, collision handling, and namespace/version parsing.
- Property-based tests to verify uniqueness and distribution characteristics.
- Benchmarks show reduced latency for bulk generation and lower syscall overhead compared to previous implementation.

Developer notes

- Public API for key generation remains largely the same, with optional parameters for seed, namespace, and version.
- See docs/KEYGEN.md for details on formats, examples, and migration steps.

This change improves safety, scalability, and flexibility of key generation while providing a clear migration path from the old format.

Testing:

- Manual verification performed on representative sample files to confirm compatibility and correctness.

text:
Support latest jpackage changes and adjust Windows installer build

This PR adapts the Windows installer build to the recent jpackage changes (see #5520). The jpackage update changed the location/name of the generated WiX fragment and also introduced a conflict with the --win-dir-chooser option. To make the build work with the new jpackage behavior, the following changes were made:

- build.gradle
  - Temporarily disabled the '--win-dir-chooser' jlink/jpackage option (commented out) because it conflicts with the updated jpackage.

- buildres/windows/JabRef-post-image.wsf
  - Adjusted the path used to open the generated WiX file: the script now reads the WiX file from "${projectDir}/buildres/windows/JabRef.wxs" (jabRefRoot + "/buildres/windows/JabRef.wxs") instead of relying on the installerConfig location.

- buildres/windows/JabRef.wxs
  - Added a copied/adjusted WiX file to buildres/windows so the installer has a stable WiX fragment available during the build. The file contains UI definitions (install-dir chooser, license handling), feature/component declarations, and registry entries required for the Windows installer.

Rationale
- The new jpackage version produces/renames the WiX output in a way that broke the previous post-image script and the use of the --win-dir-chooser option. Including a copy of the Wix file in build resources and changing the script to reference it avoids build failures.

Notes
- These changes affect the Windows installer build only; there are no changes to JabRef's runtime behavior.
- The --win-dir-chooser option has been left commented out temporarily; it can be restored once jpackage no longer conflicts with that flag.
- No unit tests were added; this change was intended to ensure the build completes with the updated jpackage.

It introduces the MergeEntries component and dialogs to let users visually compare and merge two BibEntry objects, wire this into duplicate-import handling, and update the entry-change handling to use merge options when applying modifications.

Key changes:
- Add MergeEntries component (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/mergeentries/MergeEntries.java)
  - Visual diff display of fields with multiple diff modes (plain, word/character diffs, symmetric diffs).
  - Radio buttons per field to pick left/right/none; header buttons to select all left/right.
  - Support for entry-type selection and default radio-button selection mode (DefaultRadioButtonSelectionMode.LEFT/RIGHT).
  - Methods: selectAllLeftRadioButtons(), selectAllRightRadioButtons(), getMergedEntry(), setLeftHeaderText(), setRightHeaderText().
  - Constructors overloads to provide optional column captions and default selection mode.

- Add MergeEntriesDialog (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/mergeentries/MergeEntriesDialog.java)
  - Simple dialog wrapper around MergeEntries returning the merged BibEntry on OK.

- Enhance DuplicateResolverDialog (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/duplicationFinder/DuplicateResolverDialog.java)
  - Integrates MergeEntries to preview/merge duplicates.
  - Persists dialog window state via StateManager.
  - Exposes getMergedEntry() to retrieve the merged result when user chooses to keep merged entry.

- Update ImportHandler import flow (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/externalfiles/ImportHandler.java)
  - importEntryWithDuplicateCheck now uses DuplicateResolverDialog to prompt when duplicates are found during import.
  - Honors user choice to keep left/right/both/merged and handles removal, merging, or abort appropriately.
  - Ensures citation key regeneration, automatic fields, grouping and undo handling remain intact.
  - Import of files continues to run on JavaFX thread where needed; results and undo edits are recorded as before.

- Update EntryChangeViewModel (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/collab/EntryChangeViewModel.java)
  - Uses MergeEntries with custom headings "In JabRef" and "On disk" and DefaultRadioButtonSelectionMode.LEFT for the change preview.
  - setAccepted(boolean) overridden to select either all left or all right radio buttons depending on acceptance state.
  - makeChange() initializes the merge panel (to avoid NPE), applies merge result while preserving the old entry ID, replaces the entry in the database and adds undo edits.

Other notes:
- CitationKeyGenerator and related classes are included in the context but are unchanged; key-generation flows are preserved and used by ImportHandler when regenerating citation keys on import.
- MergeEntries supports multiple diff visualizations and stores the merged result in a new BibEntry returned by getMergedEntry().

Behavioral / UX considerations:
- When resolving duplicates during import, users can now preview and merge fields via the MergeEntries widget before accepting the merged entry.
- EntryChangeViewModel uses the merge UI to let users inspect differences and will automatically switch radio selection when the change is accepted/rejected.
- The merged entry retains the original entry ID (EntryChangeViewModel.makeChange) so references are preserved.

Testing notes:
- Verify merging UI shows correct diffs for different diff modes and that radio-button selections produce the expected merged entry.
- Test duplicate resolution during file import: keep left/right/both/merged decisions must be applied correctly.
- Ensure undo behavior works for inserted/merged entries and that preserved IDs maintain cross-references.
- Confirm no NPE occurs when applying entry changes (EntryChangeViewModel calls description() to initialize merge panel).

text:
This PR improves Microsoft Bibliography (MSBib) export and UNO cross-reference handling.

Main changes

- MSBib conversion enhancements (org.jabref.logic.msbib.MSBibConverter):
  - Preserve original BibTeX entry type in BIBTEX_Entry and map to MSBib SourceType.
  - Export many common fields to their MSBib equivalents (pages, booktitle -> conferenceName, urldate/accessed, journal, address, language -> LCID, ISBN/ISSN/LCCN/MR -> standardNumber, etc.).
  - Better handling for thesis and special entry types (TechReport, MastersThesis, PhdThesis, Unpublished, InternetSite, ElectronicSource, Art, Misc).
  - Patent support: for IEEETran Patent entries, export the NUMBER field as PatentNumber (and clear the generic number field) and write inventors instead of authors.
  - Parse authors/editors/translators using a latex-free value and AuthorList.parse to produce MsBibAuthor objects; preserve corporate authors when wrapped in braces (with a fallback hack for latex2unicode behavior).
  - Minor fixes: build standardNumber from available identifiers and avoid empty strings.

- UNO cross-reference utilities (org.jabref.model.openoffice.uno.UnoCrossRef):
  - Add refresh(XTextDocument) helper to call XRefreshable.refresh() for the document.
  - Implement insertReferenceToPageNumberOfReferenceMark(...) which creates and configures a com.sun.star.text.textfield.GetReference field (set SourceName, ReferenceFieldSource and ReferenceFieldPart) and inserts it at the given cursor to show the target page number. This enables clickable cross-references to reference marks.

- Test resources:
  - Added an example MSBib patent export XML (src/test/resources/org/jabref/logic/exporter/MsBibPatent.xml) demonstrating the expected structure for a patent with inventor information and patent number.

Notes

- Some TODO/FIXME comments remain (e.g. handling of a few MSBib types that are currently unreachable and a latex2unicode-related hack for corporate authors).
- The changes aim to improve fidelity of MSBib exports (especially patents) and to support inserting/updating page-number cross-references in OpenOffice/LibreOffice documents.

text:
Implement BibEntryWriter formatting and field-display handling, plus comprehensive tests

This change enhances BibEntryWriter to reliably serialize BibEntry instances in a consistent, UI-friendly format and adds a full test-suite (BibEntryWriterTest) that verifies behavior across many scenarios.

Key changes
- Write entries in the order: required fields, optional fields, then remaining fields (alphabetically).
- Preserve original parsed serialization when entries are unchanged; reformat only when modified or explicitly requested.
- Introduce alignment of field names based on the length of the longest displayable field name (quick fix for issue #834), so column alignment matches what users see in the UI.
- Ensure non-displayable but writeable internal fields (e.g. __markedentry) are still serialized to the .bib file.
- Field names are written in lower case (biblatex-style) and values are formatted via LatexFieldFormatter.
- Add writeWithoutPrependedNewlines to support writing entries without leading newlines.
- Proper handling of special month syntax (#mar#) and preservation of newline behavior for appended/prepended newlines.

Tests added/updated
- Extensive unit tests in BibEntryWriterTest covering:
  - Basic serialization and expected formatting
  - Serialization of non-displayable writable fields
  - Round-trip parsing and writing (including preserving cite key and fields)
  - Handling of prepended and appended newlines
  - Behavior when entries are modified vs. unchanged
  - Case normalization of field names (camelCase -> lower case)
  - Proper alignment adjustments when a longer field is added
  - Special month syntax and multiple writes without modification

Notes
- getLengthOfLongestFieldName only considers displayable fields to compute alignment; this was chosen to match editor UI expectations. A TODO remains for a long-term fix related to field ordering/formatting.
- Exceptions thrown by the LatexFieldFormatter during field formatting are wrapped to include the field name for easier debugging.

text:
Add PreviewTabView preferences pane for entry preview

This commit introduces PreviewTabView, a JavaFX preferences tab that provides the UI for configuring entry preview layouts. Key features and details:

- New preferences view implementation wired to PreviewTabViewModel via bindings.
- Two ListViews (available and chosen layouts) with ViewModelListCellFactory and multi-selection.
  - Drag-and-drop support to move layouts between lists and reorder within the chosen list (dragOver/dragDetected/dragDropped handlers).
  - Keyboard incremental search: typing focuses and scrolls to matching layout names (jumpToSearchKey).
- Buttons to move layouts between lists, sort chosen items up/down, and reset defaults; their disabled state is bound to selection state.
- Preview pane using PreviewViewer showing a test entry and bound to the selected preview layout and application theme.
- Edit area implemented with RichTextFX CodeArea:
  - Line number gutter (LineNumberFactory).
  - Context menu with Cut/Copy/Paste/Select All actions implemented by an inner EditAction class.
  - Syntax highlighting hooked to the view model (computeHighlighting) and two-way synchronization of source text.

Add JSTOR fetcher (JstorFetcher)

Summary
- Implements a new fetcher for jstor.org that provides both SearchBasedParserFetcher and FulltextFetcher functionality.
- Adds the fetcher to the global lists in WebFetchers so it is available as a search and meta/fulltext fetcher.

Implementation details
- New class: JstorFetcher
  - Builds search URLs (single and complex queries) against https://www.jstor.org/open/search and maps common complex query fields (authors, title, journal, year/from-to) to JSTOR query parameters.
  - Parses search result pages with Jsoup to find citation links, downloads BibTeX from JSTOR's citation/text endpoint and parses entries with BibtexParser.
  - findFullText attempts to extract the PDF/DOI URL from an entry URL page by looking for elements with data-doi and returning the target URL.
  - Declares trust level META_SEARCH.

Tests and documentation
- New tests: JstorFetcherTest covering title search and fulltext resolution. Some year-only search tests are explicitly disabled because JSTOR does not support search by year alone.
- CHANGELOG updated to mention the new fetcher.
- AUTHORS updated to include contributor Johannes Theiner.

Notes and limitations
- Complex-query translation concatenates fields with simple prefixes (au:, ti:, pt:) as used in the site search; edge cases in query syntax could require future improvements.
- Year-only searches are not supported by JSTOR, so those capability tests are disabled.

Closes: #6627

Why
- The previous behavior made the undo stack contain the synchronization compound at the wrong position, which prevented correctly undoing operations affecting multiple entries. By not inserting the compound into the undo manager (the synchronization still runs), the undo ordering and semantics are preserved.

Tests
- New integration test validates undoing a Cut of multiple entries. Manual/automated test should confirm no regressions in special-field synchronization behavior.

Summary

This PR cleans up and improves focus handling and keyboard navigation in the entry editor and its field editors, hardens lifecycles for field editor components, and wires up related key bindings. It also contains minor safety fixes and a changelog entry.

Changes

- Improve focus management
  - Introduced safe focus request utilities in ControlHelper to handle JavaFX focus requests and avoid exceptions when nodes are not yet attached or already disposed.
  - Ensure BasePanel propagates focus correctly to the entry editor when a database/tab is selected.
  - Make JabRefMain initialize and forward initial focus reliably (startup focus tweaks).

- Entry editor and tabs
  - Refactored EntryEditor, EntryEditorTab and FieldsEditorTab to better coordinate focus and lifecycle events when tabs are created, switched or closed.
  - Ensure field editors request focus when their tab is activated and that focus is returned or cleared correctly on close.

- Field editor component robustness
  - Harden FieldEditorFX lifecycle: avoid NPEs and resource leaks by guarding against operations on disposed controls and removing unsafe assumptions about the node hierarchy.
  - Minor API/behavior improvements so field editors behave consistently across platforms and when opened/closed rapidly.

- Keyboard navigation
  - Extended KeyBinding to support navigation-related actions (next/previous field, editor tab switching) and wired these to the entry editor/field editor UI so keyboard traversal is reliable.

- Misc
  - Small cleanups throughout the affected classes to improve null-safety and reduce duplicated code.
  - Updated CHANGELOG.md with a short note about improved entry editor focus and keyboard navigation.

- CHANGELOG.md: add entry describing the improvement
- src/main/java/org/jabref/JabRefMain.java: startup/initial focus handling tweaks
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/BasePanel.java: propagate focus to entry editor
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/EntryEditor.java: focus and lifecycle improvements

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/util/ControlHelper.java: new utilities for safe focus requests and node checks

Why this change

Users reported inconsistent focus behavior when opening the entry editor and when navigating between fields with the keyboard. Rapid tab switching sometimes caused exceptions or focus to be lost. These fixes make focus behavior predictable and resilient, and improve keyboard-driven editing workflows.

Summary

This PR adds an error dialog when problems occur while automatically finding associated files for entries. It refactors the auto-linking flow to surface file search errors to the user and improves result reporting after the operation.

What changed

- AutoLinkFilesAction
  - Now receives DialogService directly (constructor changed) instead of a JabRefFrame.
  - Executes the auto-linking task and interprets a new result object. If any IO errors occurred while searching for candidate files, a warning dialog is shown: "Problem finding files. See error log for details." If no files were found, a warning dialog is shown. Otherwise the number of changed entries is reported via notification and undo history is recorded.

- AutoSetFileLinksUtil
  - Introduced LinkFilesResult (contains changed entries and file exceptions) returned from linkAssociatedFiles(...).
  - linkAssociatedFiles(...) now collects and returns both changed entries and any IOExceptions encountered while locating files instead of only returning changed entries.
  - Some internal fields made final.

- JabRefFrame
  - Passes DialogService into AutoLinkFilesAction instead of the frame.

- Localization
  - Added/adjusted i18n keys in JabRef_en.properties for the new messages:
    - "Problem finding files. See error log for details."
    - "Finished automatically setting external links."
    - "Changed %0 entries."

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefFrame.java

text:
Add automatic detection and display of likely unlinked files in the Entry Editor

What I changed
- Introduced a new preference to automatically search and show unlinked files when an entry is opened in the entry editor. This is enabled by default but can be turned off in Preferences → Entry editor.
- Wire the new preference into the UI (Entry editor preferences tab) and into the preferences model so the setting is persisted.
- When an entry is bound to the Linked Files editor and the preference is enabled, a background task is executed to find files that are likely associated with the entry (but not yet linked). Found files are shown in the linked files list and marked as automatically found.

Why
- Improves usability by surfacing files the application finds on disk that probably belong to the current entry, saving users manual search and linking steps.

Behavior / how to test
1. Open Preferences → Entry editor. The new checkbox "Automatically search and show unlinked files in the entry editor" is present (enabled by default).
2. Open an entry that has an associated file present in one of the library file directories but not yet linked. The Linked Files list should populate automatically with the candidate file(s) (they will be marked as automatically found).
3. Disable the preference and re-open an entry; automatic detection should not run.

Files changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/EntryEditorPreferences.java (added autoLinkFiles property)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/LinkedFilesEditorViewModel.java (trigger auto-find when binding to entry)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/entryeditor/EntryEditorTab.fxml (UI: checkbox)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/entryeditor/EntryEditorTab.java (bind UI to view model)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/entryeditor/EntryEditorTabViewModel.java (expose and store preference)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/preferences/JabRefPreferences.java (preference key, default and persistence wiring)
- src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties (label text)

Notes
- The actual search runs in a background task (no UI freeze).
- Automatically found files are not serialized as linked files until the user accepts/keeps them.
- Default value is true for backward-compatible behavior; users can disable it in the Entry editor preferences.

Summary

This PR integrates Git operations into the "Start New Study" workflow for SLRs and improves the Git handling utility.

What I changed

- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/slr/StartNewStudyAction.java
  - The action that creates a new study now delegates repository-related operations to the Git handler instead of performing ad-hoc file/git steps. This centralizes Git logic and surfaces clearer user feedback on repository creation/clone.

- jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/git/GitHandler.java
  - Extended and hardened the Git handler API used by the UI layer. The handler now provides clearer methods for initializing or cloning repositories, better error reporting, and improved logging. It handles common failure cases (missing Git, clone failures, permission issues) in a way that the UI can present meaningful messages.

Why

Centralizing Git logic in GitHandler reduces duplication, makes the StartNewStudyAction simpler and easier to maintain, and improves robustness when creating or cloning a repository for a new study. It also allows the UI to present clearer progress/error messages to the user.

How to test

1. Open JabRef and use the "Start New Study" flow for SLRs.
2. Choose the option to create a new local study repository (or provide a remote URL to clone, if supported by the UI flow).
3. Verify that the repository is initialized or cloned correctly and that appropriate success or error dialogs are shown.
4. Test error cases: run the flow with Git not installed or with an invalid remote URL and confirm that the UI shows a readable error message instead of a stack trace.

Notes

- No user-visible behavior changes beyond improved Git handling and clearer messages. Existing study files and formats are unchanged.
- If you maintain automated tests that rely on earlier GitHandler internals, update them to use the new public methods.

Add timestamp check when deciding whether a .bak backup differs from the current .bib file.

What changed
- BackupManager.backupFileDiffers now verifies the last-modified timestamp of the latest .bak before doing a byte-wise comparison. If the backup is older than or equal to the current file it is treated as non-different (no warning shown). If timestamps cannot be read, the method will not show a warning (returns false). If an IOException occurs while comparing file contents, the method returns true so the user is prompted to investigate.
- Updated and added tests in BackupManagerTest to cover the timestamp behavior: updated the multiple .bak files test and added bakFileWithNewerTimeStampLeadsToDiff and bakFileWithOlderTimeStampDoesNotLeadToDiff.

Why
This avoids showing a misleading dialog when the .bak is older than the .bib (for example after git operations, cloud sync, or manual edits). This is a follow-up to #9054 and fixes koppor/jabref#597.

Files changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/autosaveandbackup/BackupManager.java
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/autosaveandbackup/BackupManagerTest.java

- New/updated unit tests verify correct behavior for newer and older .bak timestamps.

This PR implements automatic relinking of files when a user moves a file within the file directories monitored by JabRef. The change also integrates this check into the existing linkAssociatedFiles workflow.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/externalfiles/AutoSetFileLinksUtil.java: Added relinkFileIfMoved and wired it into linkAssociatedFiles. Minor imports added.
- src/test/java/org/jabref/gui/externalfiles/AutoSetFileLinksUtilTest.java: Added six unit tests covering move and copy scenarios.
- CHANGELOG.md: Added an entry describing the improved behavior.

- relinkMoveFileFromRootFolderToSubfolder
- relinkMoveFileFromSubfolderToRootFolder
- relinkMoveFileFromSubfolderToSubfolder
- noRelinkCopyFileFromRootFolderToSubfolder
- noRelinkCopyFileFromSubfolderToRootFolder
- noRelinkCopyFileFromSubfolderToSubfolder

Fixes #9798

Notes

Co-authored with Le-Chat-BottE. Feedback welcome.
