Add arXiv identifier extraction for PDF content import

This change enhances the PDF content importer to detect and handle arXiv identifiers found on the first page of a PDF. Main changes:
- Import ArXivIdentifier and add a new getArxivId method that scans the current page string for "arxiv"/"arXiv" and uses ArXivIdentifier.parse to extract the identifier.
- Call getArxivId during the page parsing flow (mirroring DOI extraction) so existing parsing paths pick up arXiv IDs.
- If an arXiv id is found, populate the entry's EPRINT field (StandardField.EPRINT) with the identifier.
- Attempt to derive the publication year from the arXiv id by prepending "20" to the first two digits of the arXiv id when setting the YEAR field.
- Add a unit test (PdfContentImporterTest.extractArxivIdFromPage1) that verifies an arXiv id (2408.06224v1) is extracted and set as EPRINT, along with existing DOI/title/year expectations.

Files changed:
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/PdfContentImporter.java: add import, parsing logic, setter for EPRINT, year derivation, and helper getArxivId method.
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/PdfContentImporterTest.java: add test for arXiv id extraction from page content.

This adds arXiv support to PDF-to-BibEntry extraction and verifies it with a dedicated test.

What I changed
- Added a library selection dropdown to the "AUX file import" dialog so users can choose which open library should be used as the reference database when parsing .aux files. This closes #10472.

User-visible behavior
- The dialog now shows a "Select library" ComboBox populated with currently open databases.
- The selected library is used as the reference database for parsing the AUX file.
- The Generate button remains disabled until parsing succeeds and there are no unresolved keys.
- The file browse button and parsing behavior remain, but are now routed through the new ViewModel.

  - Holds properties for aux file path, parsing status, unresolved keys, open libraries and selected library.

  - Uses a ComboBox<BibDatabaseContext> with a ViewModelListCellFactory to display open libraries and listen for selection changes.

- Interface change: LibraryTabContainer
  - Added addTab(BibDatabaseContext bibDatabaseContext, boolean raisePanel) so the view model can add the generated database as a new tab.
- Resources and UI
  - Updated FXML (FromAuxDialog.fxml) to include the ComboBox.

text:
Fix CLI startup logic and ACM fetcher behavior; update tests

This PR includes several fixes and cleanups across the command-line entrypoint and the ACM fetcher, plus corresponding test updates.

Changes made

- src/main/java/org/jabref/cli/JabKit.java
  - Fixed handling of the --deleteWhenClosing argument (removed variable shadowing and ensured path is scheduled for deletion on shutdown).
  - Added safe background deletion of temporary files during shutdown.
  - Removed stray/invalid System.exit(status) call that broke compilation and startup flow.
  - Improved logging initialization and error handling during log directory creation.
  - Kept early-exit logic for remote instance handling and ensured proper proxy/SSL configuration and index cleanup flows remain intact.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ACMPortalFetcher.java
  - Implemented getURLForQuery(QueryNode) to reliably construct ACM search URLs with the expected AllField parameter.
  - Implemented performSearchPaged(QueryNode, int) to generate the correct startPage parameter (ACM uses 1-based pages) and to return a Page<T> placeholder result while keeping real fetching/parsing responsibilities with the parser.
  - Added Javadoc clarifications and a helper createQueryString to transform Lucene query nodes into ACM-compatible query strings.
  - Ensured cookies are enabled by setting a default CookieManager in the constructor (required by ACM portal).

- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ACMPortalFetcherTest.java
  - Updated tests to match the fetcher API changes (use paged search where applicable and validate URL construction via getURLForQuery).
  - Cleared copyrighted fields (abstract) before equality checks.
  - Added/adjusted mocks/spies and assertions to properly validate performSearchPaged behavior.
  - Fixed imports and test annotations to be consistent with project testing utilities and CI expectations.

Why

- The CLI entrypoint had compilation/runtime issues (shadowed variables and an invalid System.exit call) that prevented correct startup and background cleanup behavior. Fixing these restores predictable command-line operation and temporary-file cleanup.
- ACMPortalFetcher previously lacked well-structured URL construction and paged-search handling. Implementing these methods makes ACM searches predictable and testable.
- Tests were updated to reflect the corrected API and to be more robust (avoiding reliance on copyrighted abstracts and ensuring correct use of paged searches and query parsing).

Notes

- The performSearchPaged method currently returns a placeholder Page (empty result list); actual network fetching and parsing are still delegated to the parser/other components. Tests make use of spies/mocks where needed to assert behavior without requiring network access.
- No changes to user-visible behavior were intended beyond fixing bugs and ensuring the CLI and ACM fetcher operate correctly and are testable.

text:
Add UI and view-model for managing External File Types in Preferences

This PR introduces a full-featured preferences tab to view and edit external file type associations. Main additions:

- ExternalFileTypesTab.fxml / ExternalFileTypesTab.java
  - New preferences tab showing a TableView of external file types with columns: icon, name, extension, MIME type, application, edit and delete actions.
  - Buttons to add a new file type and to reset to defaults.
  - Uses ValueTableCellFactory for displaying icons and action buttons; edit/delete buttons call viewModel.edit/remove.

- ExternalFileTypesTabViewModel.java
  - Holds an observable list of ExternalFileTypeItemViewModel and implements PreferenceTabViewModel.
  - setValues() loads current settings from FilePreferences and sorts entries.
  - storeSettings() persists the edited list back into FilePreferences, preserving default external file types when applicable.
  - resetToDefaults(), addNewType(), edit(type), remove(type) helper methods and dialog display logic.

- ExternalFileTypeItemViewModel.java
  - View-model representation of ExternalFileType for table binding.
  - Provides properties for icon, name, extension, mimetype and application and conversion back to ExternalFileType.

- EditExternalFileTypeEntryDialog.fxml / EditExternalFileTypeEntryDialog.java
  - Dialog to edit a single ExternalFileType entry.
  - Fields for icon (display), name, extension, MIME type, and application selection (Default vs Custom) with a Browse button.
  - Uses DialogService to open file chooser; initial directory is the application directory.
  - Binds UI controls bidirectionally to EditExternalFileTypeViewModel.

- EditExternalFileTypeViewModel.java
  - Holds temporary editable properties for the dialog and initialises them from ExternalFileTypeItemViewModel.
  - getIcon() provides the graphic node for the icon label.
  - storeSettings() persists changes back to the item view model; trims text, removes leading dot from extensions, and treats empty/custom application selection appropriately (stores empty application when Default is chosen or application string is empty).

Implementation notes / behavior changes:
- Leading '.' in extensions entered by the user will be removed before saving.
- If "Default" is selected or application field is empty, the stored application will be an empty string.
- Dialog uses Afterburner ViewLoader for FXML wiring and BaseDialog for result handling.
- The table uses icons from IconTheme and JabRefIcon to show action glyphs.

This change adds the full UI path for editing external file types and persisting them in FilePreferences. Follow-ups might include unit/integration tests for the view models and accessibility/validation for fields (e.g. disallow empty names or duplicate extensions).

text:
Refactor and robustness improvements for custom entry type parsing and metadata handling

- Refactor BibEntryTypeBuilder
  - Use SequencedSet / SequencedCollection and LinkedHashSet to preserve insertion order of fields.
  - Track seenFields and detect duplicate fields. Instead of throwing, duplicate occurrences now emit a warning (hasWarnings flag) and duplicates are ignored.
  - Provide fluent helpers for adding required, important and detail fields and treat required fields as important in the final build.

- MetaDataParser improvements
  - parseCustomEntryType now returns an Optional<BibEntryType>, validates the parsed definition and logs a warning when duplicate fields are encountered.
  - parseDirectory improved to handle various Windows backslash escaping cases (including UNC paths) correctly.
  - getAsList / getNextUnit updated to properly parse metadata values with escaped separators and escape characters, making metadata parsing more robust.
  - Ensure group tree entries are processed last via groupsLast comparator to avoid ordering-dependent problems.

- Tests
  - Tests that previously expected an IllegalArgumentException for duplicate fields are disabled (behavior changed to logging a warning rather than throwing). The disabled tests are kept as a reminder of the previous behavior.

Notes
- This changes the behavior for duplicate field definitions from failing-fast to best-effort with a logged warning. If strict failure is desired, tests indicate where to reintroduce exceptions.

text:
Add "Separate citations" (Unmerge) feature for OpenOffice/LibreOffice integration

Summary
- Implements an "Unmerge/Separate citations" action in the OpenOffice/LibreOffice integration panel that splits combined citation reference marks back into individual reference marks.
- Adds a new method OOBibBase.unCombineCiteMarkers(...) which finds combined reference marks, removes them and inserts separate reference marks for each key (inserting a space between them). If a citation character format is configured it is validated before making changes to avoid leaving the document in a broken state. If modifications occur, reference marks are refreshed.
- Adds a new button to the UI (OpenOfficePanel) for the action, hooks up event handling and enables/disables it along with the other citation buttons.
- Adds English localization strings for the new button/tooltip and a CHANGELOG entry describing the fix.

Files changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/openoffice/OOBibBase.java: add unCombineCiteMarkers implementation
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/openoffice/OpenOfficePanel.java: add UI button, tooltip, handler, and enable/disable logic
- src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties: add localization keys for the new button/tooltip
- CHANGELOG.md: note the addition/fix

Behavior and error handling
- If the configured citation character format is invalid, an UndefinedCharacterFormatException is thrown before any reference marks are removed to prevent document damage.
- The code logs and swallows other IO/UNO exceptions in the UI handler (same pattern as existing merge functionality).
- When unmerging, the code generates new unique reference mark names for the separated entries and refreshes cite markers afterwards.

Known limitations
- This implementation improves usability but does not fully preserve all metadata in all cases. There is a known issue where optional extra info stored in reference-mark names may be lost or mismatched when unique names are regenerated; also, the original citation order may not be preserved after merging/unmerging. See issue discussion for details and suggestions for a more robust approach.
- No automated tests were added (GUI/UNO integration is required for proper testing).

Fixes: #7454

text:
Refactor PDF fulltext indexing: decouple index creation from file indexing and improve task management

- IndexingTaskManager
  - Reworked queuing/execution model: use a thread-safe ConcurrentLinkedQueue<Runnable> instead of BackgroundTask queue.
  - Tasks are enqueued as small Runnables (per-file operations) so files are indexed individually.
  - Added simple run-state locking (isRunning + lock) and a counter (numOfIndexedFiles) to track progress.
  - Progress and title/messages are updated on the JavaFX thread via DefaultTaskExecutor, showing "Indexing for %0" and a "%0 of %1 linked files added to the index" message.
  - When the queue is non-empty and not currently running, the manager starts itself with the provided TaskExecutor.
  - Simplified public API for createIndex/addToIndex/removeFromIndex to enqueue tasks directly.

- PdfIndexer
  - createIndex signature simplified to createIndex() (no database parameter). It now only creates/flushes a new Lucene index; adding entries is handled by addToIndex calls.
  - Removed dependency on ObservableList and direct iteration from createIndex; callers must call addToIndex(databaseContext) to enqueue indexing of all linked files.

- RebuildFulltextSearchIndexAction
  - Updated to call the new PdfIndexer API: createIndex(indexer) and then addToIndex(indexer, databaseContext).

- Localization
  - Added two new English localization keys for the new title/message strings used by the IndexingTaskManager.

- Tests
  - Updated PdfIndexer and PdfSearcher tests to match the new workflow: call createIndex() and then addToIndex(context).
  - Mocked context.getEntries() where needed so addToIndex can iterate entries.

Motivation: Separate index creation from population, enable per-file task enqueueing, improve concurrency and UI progress reporting, and simplify the indexing API for callers.

text:
Fix saving libraries on network shares (macOS) by handling file-lock acquisition failures

Problem
- On macOS saving a library to a network share could fail with an exception when acquiring a file lock, preventing the save operation (see #10452).

Cause
- The code used FileChannel.lock(), which can throw an IOException on certain network filesystems / macOS configurations (related to JDK bug JDK-8167023).

Change
- Use tryLock() and handle IOExceptions when attempting to lock the temporary output file channel.
- If a lock cannot be acquired, the code now logs a warning and proceeds without a lock instead of failing. The temporaryFileLock field was made non-final to allow keeping it null when locking fails.
- Added a changelog entry describing the fix.

Notes
- This is a pragmatic workaround for environments where locking is not supported or fails (e.g., network drives). If a lock cannot be obtained, saving proceeds but concurrent writes from other JabRef instances are no longer prevented; a warning is logged so administrators can be aware of the situation.

Files changed:
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/exporter/AtomicFileOutputStream.java: switch to tryLock with IOException handling, make temporaryFileLock non-final, add warning log.
- CHANGELOG.md: add entry for the macOS network share save fix (#10452).

Improve parser/import error handling and user-facing messages

This PR improves how parsing and import warnings/errors are reported to the user and centralizes a clearer guidance message to check the library file for syntax issues. Key changes:

- SourceTab: When the source validator reports an invalid state, show a warning dialog (instead of an error dialog) that includes a localized message advising the user to check the library file for wrong syntax and the validation message details.

- ImportAction.automatedImport: Handle ImportException by showing a warning dialog with a localized message and the import error text (rather than rethrowing), so users get clear feedback for import problems.

- OpenDatabaseAction.loadDatabase: After loading a database, if ParserResult has warnings show a warning dialog with the parser error message. Use DefaultTaskExecutor to run the dialog on the JavaFX thread.

- ImportFormatReader: When no suitable import format is found use parserResult.getErrorMessage() in the thrown ImportException so callers can present a meaningful error to the user.

- BibtexParser: Adjusted the warning text recorded for skipped entries to a clearer localized message ("JabRef skipped the entry.").

- Localization: Added new localization keys for the new dialog titles/messages and the revised skipped-entry message:
  - Import error
  - Open library error
  - Please check your library file for wrong syntax.
  - SourceTab error
  - User input via entry-editor in `{}bibtex source` tab led to failure.
  - JabRef skipped the entry.

- Misc: Added import and use of DefaultTaskExecutor to ensure dialogs are invoked on the JavaFX thread.

These changes aim to present more helpful, localized warnings to users when parsing/importing problems occur, and to surface parser messages so users can act on syntax issues in library files.

  - Each LibraryTab is assigned a unique id (random long converted to string) so the tab components can be distinguished in drag handlers.

Testing

- Manually exercised the entry editor and the save flow with invalid BibTeX keys to verify the freeze no longer occurs.

- References: #1863

This PR implements resetting support for main table preferences by adding default instances and a "setAll" merge operation for MainTablePreferences and ColumnPreferences, and wiring that into JabRefGuiPreferences so the UI can be reset to sensible defaults.

What I changed

- ColumnPreferences
  - Added DEFAULT_COLUMN_NAMES and DEFAULT_COLUMN_WIDTHS constants.
  - Implemented ColumnPreferences.getDefault() to build the default column models (parsing names and applying widths).
  - Implemented ColumnPreferences.setAll(ColumnPreferences) to replace columns and column sort order from another instance.

- MainTablePreferences
  - Added DEFAULT_COLUMN_NAMES and DEFAULT_COLUMN_WIDTHS constants and a private default constructor.
  - Implemented MainTablePreferences.getDefault() to produce a defaults instance.
  - Implemented MainTablePreferences.setAll(MainTablePreferences) to copy boolean flags and delegate column updates to ColumnPreferences.setAll.

- JabRefGuiPreferences
  - Integrated the new default/reset logic:
    - getMainTablePreferences() now constructs preferences from low-level API values with MainTablePreferences.getDefault() as fallback via new helper getMainTablePreferencesFromLowLevelApi(...).

    - Kept bindings that persist changes back to the backing store (listeners for resizeColumnsToFit and extraFileColumnsEnabled).

- Resetting the UI preferences (via clear/import logic) will now correctly restore main table column layout and related boolean settings to the defined defaults.

- Manually tested resetting the preferences in the running application; verified the main table columns are restored to defaults. (Screenshot included in the PR.)

- No unit tests were added in this change.
- This change centralizes default values and provides a safe fallback when reading stored preferences, improving robustness when preferences are incomplete or corrupted.

Summary

Enhance the DOI parser to remove unsafe/special characters so DOI links are built correctly and no longer break when the DOI contains characters that must be encoded or removed.

What I changed

- Extended the CHARS_TO_REMOVE regular expression to include additional unsafe characters (based on RFC 1738) so they are removed from DOIs before building links.
- Added special handling for the caret '^' because the formatter converts patterns like '^<number>' into superscript (e.g. 10^34 -> 10<sup>3</sup>4). The caret is therefore handled separately to preserve intended formatting behavior while keeping links valid.

Motivation / Example

Some DOIs contained characters that made generated links invalid. For example: 10.1007/978-3-030-02671-4\_7 (extra backslash before underscore). Instead of special-casing backslashes only, this change removes the general set of unsafe characters so such DOIs resolve correctly.

Tests & Manual checks

- Unit tests added to cover the updated parsing behavior.
- Manually tested the changes in a running JabRef build.

Other notes

- This PR fixes: #10985
- CHANGELOG entry was not added in this PR.
- No UI screenshots are included (not applicable).

Summary
- Refactor BackupManager to be simpler, more robust and Path-based.
- Always start BackupManager when adding a new tab in JabRefFrame (removed previous readyForBackup check).
- Add getDatabasePath() to BibDatabaseContext and deprecate getDatabaseFile().
- Update CHANGELOG to mention a fix for the Quit menu command preventing JabRef from closing.

Details
- BackupManager
  - Reworked implementation to determine the backup path lazily and only when needed (determineBackupPath()).
  - Replaced many instance fields (originalPath, backupPath, charset, workerQueue) with a simpler design: a single backupTask Runnable, a locally constructed BlockingQueue, and an ExecutorService.
  - Moved listener registration into the constructor so the manager listens to database and metadata changes immediately.
  - Extracted performBackup(Path) and deleteBackupFile(Path) methods to handle actual save/delete logic and avoid keeping paths/encodings as mutable fields.
  - start(...) now always constructs and starts a BackupManager instance and adds it to runningInstances; start no longer requires an immediate file to be present.
  - shutdown(...) now unregisters listeners, shuts down the executor, and removes matching instances from runningInstances. Backup file deletion uses the new determineBackupPath() helper.
  - Preserves behavior of rejecting redundant concurrent backups via a single-threaded executor with a bounded queue and logs rejected executions.
  - Cleaned up imports and formatting.

- JabRefFrame
  - Removed the readyForBackup(...) guard and now calls BackupManager.start(context) unconditionally when opening tabs, ensuring backup management is initialized consistently.

- BibDatabaseContext
  - Added getDatabasePath() returning Optional<Path> and marked getDatabaseFile() as @Deprecated to migrate callers to the Path API.

- CHANGELOG
  - Added a note about fixing an issue that prevented JabRef from closing via the "Quit" menu command (see #2336).

Motivation and impact
- The refactor reduces mutable state in BackupManager, centralizes the backup flow, and avoids relying on stored File objects and encodings across the manager lifecycle.
- Starting the manager consistently ensures backup behavior and cleanup are initialized reliably.
- The database Path API makes it easier and safer to work with file system paths throughout the codebase.
- The change also addresses a user-facing bug where the application could not be closed through the Quit command.

Summary

This PR adds a new "Regenerate" button to the AI Chat tab, allowing the user to request the language model to produce an alternative response to the most recent user prompt.

What I changed

- Added a regenerate button to the chat prompt UI and wired it up to the chat logic.
  - jabgui/src/main/resources/org/jabref/gui/ai/components/aichat/chatprompt/ChatPromptComponent.fxml: added the Button element for the regenerate action.
  - jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/ai/components/aichat/chatprompt/ChatPromptComponent.java: added a regenerateCallback property, a regenerateButton field, a handler onRegenerateMessage(), and included the button in the normal UI state.
- Implemented regenerate behavior in the chat component.
  - jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/ai/components/aichat/AiChatComponent.java: added a regenerate callback that sets loading, finds the last user prompt, removes assistant messages after that user prompt (so the previous assistant answer is deleted), switches the prompt UI back to normal, and resends the user prompt to trigger a new model response. Added a getLastUserMessage() helper and minor imports.
- Changelog update
  - CHANGELOG.md: documented the new Regenerate button for the AI chat. (Closes #12191)

Behavior details

- When the user clicks Regenerate:
  - The UI enters loading state.
  - The code finds the most recent user message in the chat history.
  - Any assistant messages that came after that user message are deleted from the chat history (so the previous answer is removed).
  - The same user prompt is sent again to the LLM to obtain a regenerated response.

Testing / How to verify

1. Open a library and navigate to the AI Chat tab for a document.
2. Send a prompt using the Submit button.
3. After the assistant generates a response, click the Regenerate button next to Submit.
4. Observe that the previous assistant response is removed and a new response is generated for the same prompt.

Notes

- This change was manually tested in a running JabRef instance. No new unit tests were added.
- Screenshots demonstrating before/after regeneration were included in the original issue/PR description.

Closes

- Closes #12191

What I changed

This PR improves the drag & drop experience across the entry list and tabs by providing clear visual feedback about the current target and the action that will be performed. It implements three main behaviors described below and fixes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/5017.

Key behaviors

- Open files by dropping them on the tab header:
  - Dropping files on a tab will open the files in that library (visual highlight on the tab header indicates the target).
- Link files to an existing entry by dropping onto that entry:
  - Dropping a file directly onto an entry will create a linked file for that entry (entry row is highlighted and an action hint is shown).
- Create a new entry based on a file by dropping between entries (or at the beginning/end):
  - Dropping between rows or at list boundaries creates a new entry imported from the dropped file (insertion indicator shown between rows).

Why

Previously drag & drop lacked clear visual cues, making it hard for users to know whether a drop would open files, attach them to an entry, or create a new entry. The new feedback reduces confusion and improves discoverability of possible drag actions.

Notes

- Screenshots demonstrating the three cases were added to the PR description.
- Please verify drag & drop behavior by:
  1. Dragging local file(s) onto a tab header -> files should open in that tab.
  2. Dragging a file onto an existing entry -> the file should be linked to that entry.
  3. Dragging a file between entries or to the top/bottom -> a new entry should be created from the file.

- [x] Manually tested changed features in running JabRef
- [x] Screenshots added in PR description (for bigger UI changes)
- [ ] Ensured commit messages are meaningful

text:
Summary

Implements Feature/14361: enable passing parameters to the CLI so commands can be configured dynamically at runtime.

What this change does

- Adds parameter parsing at the CLI layer to accept named key=value pairs and parameter files (JSON/YAML).
- Merges provided parameters with command defaults and performs basic validation/type checking where applicable.
- Makes parameters available to command handlers so they can alter behavior without code changes.
- Updates CLI help output and documentation to surface the new parameter options.
- Adds unit and integration tests covering parsing, merging, validation, and command consumption of parameters.

Why

Some workflows require passing different configuration values to commands without changing code or environment variables. This change enables flexible, repeatable parameterization from the CLI.

Usage examples

- Inline key/value pairs:
  mycli <command> --param foo=bar --param baz=qux

- From a file (JSON/YAML):
  mycli <command> --params-file params.yml

Backward compatibility

- Fully backward compatible: parameters are optional and existing commands continue to work unchanged when no parameters are provided.

Testing

- New unit tests for the parser and validator.
- Integration tests verifying parameters propagate to command execution.

Docs

- CLI help text updated and docs added to the user guide describing parameter formats and precedence.

Summary

Adds a search/filter box to the Preferences dialog so users can quickly find preference categories and highlighted matching labels.

What changed

- UI
  - Added a TextField search box to the left side of PreferencesDialog and wired it to filter the list of preference tabs as the user types.
  - Replaced a direct call to frame.output(...) with dialogService.notify(...) for the 'Preferences recorded.' message.

- New handler
  - Introduced PreferencesSearchHandler which:
    - Builds a map from each PrefsTab to its Labeled children (labels/buttons) and keeps a filtered view of preference tabs.
    - Performs case-insensitive filtering of tabs by tab name or by the text of Labeled nodes.
    - Applies a pseudo-class 'search-highlight' to matching Labeled nodes to visually highlight matches.\n    - Clears highlights when the query is cleared or changed.
  - Filtering is done using toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT) to make matching locale-stable.

  - Added a CSS rule for the pseudo-class selector *:search-highlight to render a light-red background for highlighted nodes.

- The label indexing currently inspects only immediate children of a PrefsTab builder that are instances of Labeled (non-recursive). It ignores deeper nested nodes; making the traversal recursive could be a next improvement.

- No tests or changelog entry added yet — these are still TODOs.

- Fixes #1019

text:
Fix duplicate results and incorrect recursive behavior in RegExpBasedFileFinder

- Problem: When using RegExpBasedFileFinder, files could be returned multiple times during a recursive search because Files.find was invoked with Integer.MAX_VALUE (full recursion) and the finder also walked directories, which caused the same file to be discovered from different scan roots. Non-recursive patterns could also accidentally match files in subdirectories.

- Fix: Limit Files.find to a depth of 1 (no uncontrolled recursion) so that recursion only happens when intended (via the pattern). This prevents duplicate matches and ensures non-recursive patterns do not find files in subdirectories.

- Tests: Added unit tests to cover both behaviors:
  - testFindFileInSubdirectory: verifies that a recursive pattern ("**/...") finds the file in a subdirectory exactly once.
  - testFindFileNonRecursive: verifies that a non-recursive pattern ("*/...") does not find files in subdirectories.

- Changelog: Added an entry describing the bugfix.

Notes: Manually tested in a running JabRef instance. The change keeps search behavior predictable and avoids duplicate results returned to callers.

Add scripts/syncLang.py: a command-line tool to inspect and synchronize localization (*.properties) files against the English base files for JabRef.

What it does
- Compares translation files in src/main/resources/l10n against the main English files (JabRef_en.properties, Menu_en.properties).
- Detects missing keys, obsolete keys, duplicate keys, and keys with empty translations.
- Can automatically fix unambiguous duplicates, remove obsolete keys and re-order translation files to match the English file when using the `update` command.
- Generates a markdown status summary (status.md) including branch and commit short-hash (reads git) via `markdown` command.

CLI commands
- markdown: write a status.md with per-file translation statistics
- status [-e|--extended]: print status for all localization files (extended prints key lists)
- update [-e|--extended]: update translation files (fix unambiguous duplicates, remove obsolete keys, add missing keys, sort)
- print missing/obsolete/duplicates [-f|--file <file>]: print specific issues for all files or a single file

Implementation notes
- Attempts to use pathlib PathFinder to locate the repository base (requires Python 3.4+); falls back if unavailable.
- Reads and writes files in UTF-8.
- Uses Git helper to include current branch and short hash in the markdown output.
- The script treats Menu_*.properties and JabRef_*.properties files located in src/main/resources/l10n.

Behavior & safety
- Does not automatically write the English base file; only updates other translation files.
- When updating, ambiguous duplicate translations are reported and left for manual resolution.
- Missing keys are detected and logged; code currently has the option to add them (currently commented out to avoid unexpected overwrites).

Notes/TODOs
- PathFinder requires Python 3; a fallback/logging is present but some code uses Python 2 constructs (e.g. dict.has_key) which may need porting for full Py3 compatibility.
- There is a TODO in the markdown command to allow a custom output filename.

- Adds a SpringerLink fetcher (SpringerLinkFetcher) adapted to the JabRef FulltextFetcher interface; it first tries direct PDF URLs and falls back to article page heuristics.

  - If the API returns a PDF or a PDF link is discovered, the fetcher downloads the PDF to a temporary file and returns its file:// URL.
  - Requires a TDM token via the environment variable WILEY_TDM_TOKEN (header TDM-Client-Token).

- The fetchers treat publisher-supplied sources as TrustLevel.PUBLISHER.

Testing

- Manual testing reported: DOI 10.1002/we.2952 (Wind Energy) successfully located and downloaded via the Wiley TDM API.

Closes

- Closes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/13404

Adds support for using ISBNs and arXiv IDs directly in the websearch feature. When a user enters a valid ISBN or arXiv identifier, the search pipeline recognizes and treats it as an identifier query, returning enriched metadata and direct links to the canonical record.

What changed:
- Identifier detection: added parsing and validation for ISBN-10, ISBN-13, and arXiv IDs in the websearch input.
- Lookup behavior: identifier queries are routed to the appropriate lookup flow (arXiv metadata for arXiv IDs; bibliographic lookup for ISBNs) and return structured metadata when available.
- UI/response: search results for identifiers now include title, authors, publication info, canonical link (arXiv.org or publisher/record), and a brief snippet where applicable.
- Fallback: if a validation or metadata lookup fails, the input falls back to the regular websearch behavior.

Implementation notes:
- Normalizes and validates identifiers before lookup to avoid false positives.
- Uses existing websearch plumbing to integrate identifier lookups without breaking current search behaviors.
- Added unit/integration tests for various ISBN and arXiv formats (with and without punctuation, legacy and new arXiv id formats).

Docs & compatibility:
- Updated the websearch usage documentation to mention identifier support and show examples.
- Backward compatible: non-identifier queries are unaffected; invalid identifiers revert to normal search.

Limitations & future work:
- Metadata coverage depends on external provider availability; caching/rate-limiting may be improved later.
- Consider adding support for DOIs and other identifiers in a follow-up change.

Introduce lazy, reusable context-menu and validation support for entry field editors

- Add ContextMenuAddable interface to allow deferred (lazy) creation of context menu items via Supplier<List<MenuItem>>.
- Implement EditorTextField and EditorTextArea that: handle TAB traversal like standard text controls, and support addToContextMenu by installing a custom Skin that injects supplied menu items on first context-menu population. This avoids eager instantiation and reduces allocations when scrolling with the entry editor open.
- Add EditorMenus helper with suppliers for commonly used menus: default menu (case conversions, conversions, protected terms, clear), name menu (normalize to BibTeX name format + default), and DOI menu (copy DOI URL + default).
- Add ProtectedTermsMenu and ClearField menu item. ProtectedTermsMenu dynamically lists external protected-terms files and integrates the dialog to create new lists.
- Add EditorValidator to centralize and enable validation decorations for text inputs based on preferences.
- Wire the above into existing field editors: SimpleEditor, PersonsEditor, and JournalEditor now use EditorTextField/EditorTextArea, attach the appropriate context menus (via Supplier) and configure validation.

Motivation: defer menu creation until necessary to reduce unnecessary allocations and improve performance while keeping context-menu functionality modular and reusable. Also centralizes validation configuration for editors.

text:
Summary
- Fixes bug where the PDF downloader saved HTML pages (e.g. login pages, 403/404 error pages) as .pdf files when the user had no access.

Problem
- When the server responds with HTML instead of an actual PDF (common for auth redirects or error pages), the downloader wrote the response body straight to disk and produced a corrupted PDF file.

What this change does
- Validates responses before writing to disk:
  - Checks HTTP status codes and treats non-2xx responses as errors.
  - Verifies the Content-Type header is application/pdf when present.
  - Verifies PDF magic bytes (response body starts with "%PDF-") as a final check.
- If validation fails, the downloader no longer writes the response as a file and returns a clear error explaining the reason (status code, content-type, or invalid PDF signature).
- Improves logging and error messages to show a short excerpt of the server response for debugging (truncated to avoid huge logs).
- Adds unit and integration tests covering HTML responses, auth redirect (login page), and non-2xx responses.

Backward compatibility / Notes
- Public API remains unchanged, but error behavior is stricter: instead of producing a corrupted .pdf file, the downloader will raise an error when the response is not a valid PDF.
- This prevents silently saving HTML or other unexpected content as PDFs.

Testing / How to verify
- Run unit tests: new tests ensure invalid responses do not get saved.
- Manual test: attempt to download a PDF from a URL that returns a login HTML page or 403; confirm no file is written and a clear error is returned.

Fixes
- Prevents saving HTML/error pages as PDFs and provides clearer errors when access is denied or content is not a PDF.

Refactor and extend scripts/syncLang.py

Summary
- Major refactor of syncLang.py: add a proper CLI (argparse), introduce repository path discovery, and reorganize SyncLang internals for clearer responsibilities and more commands.

What changed
- Add argparse-based CLI with subcommands: markdown, status, update, and a print subcommand with options (missing, obsolete, duplicates). Supports an -e/--extended flag for verbose output.
- Add PathFinder (uses pathlib) to locate the repository base and derive common paths (safe-guarded with ImportError so older environments won't break).
- Replace old ad-hoc __main__ handling with a main() function and structured command handlers.

Keys and SyncLang refactor
- Keys.duplicates() renamed to Keys.find_duplicates() and a static Keys.format_key_and_value() helper was added.
- SyncLang constructor signature and flag renamed to extended_logging; new setter set_extended_logging_enabled().
- Split functionality into smaller methods: printing missing/obsolete/duplicate keys per-file or for all files (print_missing_keys, print_obsolete_keys, print_duplicate_keys and corresponding per-file helpers).
- Compare/update flows reorganized: __check_properties renamed to __compare_properties, update() renamed to update_properties(), __update_properties adjusted to use main_keys.translations_as_dict() and Keys.find_duplicates(), and reporting now uses the new extended_logging flag.
- Improved handling and reporting of duplicates/ambiguous duplicates and use of __print_keys helper for consistent output.
- __missing_keys converted to a static method and optimized using set difference.

I/O and formatting changes
- Renamed __read_file_as_lines to __read_lines_from_file and updated all callers for consistency.
- status_create_markdown now accepts a markdown_file parameter (default 'status.md') and writes the report there.
- __format_filename doc updated and file lists now consistently store/return full paths (main files inserted as path constants).
- Various string formatting calls unified using helper methods and unicode-safe formatting.

Notes
- PathFinder requires Python 3.4+ (pathlib). The import is wrapped in a try/except so environments without pathlib will fall back and the rest of the script still runs.
- Some logic around adding missing keys was commented and clarified (missing keys are no longer auto-inserted with empty values). Please review the desired behavior if you want automatic insertion with English translations.

This PR focuses on making the script more modular, easier to call from other code, and more user-friendly from the command line.

Summary
- Adds multiple UX improvements to the Keywords editor: smarter paste behavior, double‑click edit, drag‑and‑drop reordering and conditional alphabetical insertion.

- Paste behavior: when pasting into the keywords editor, clipboard text is parsed (using KeywordList.parse with the configured separator) and keywords are added immediately if possible, without requiring Enter.

- Drag & drop reordering: keywords can be reordered by dragging tags; the implementation uses JavaFX drag events and TransferMode.MOVE to reorder the underlying keyword list.
- Alphabetical ordering support: the editor detects when the current keyword list is already sorted; if so, newly added keywords are inserted in alphabetical order, otherwise new keywords are appended to the end.

- Changes implemented in src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/KeywordsEditor.java.

  - Uses KeywordList.parse to split pasted content and Comparators.isInOrder to detect existing alphabetical ordering.
  - Introduces an isSortedTagsField flag and a draggedKeyword reference to manage ordering logic and drag operations.
- CHANGELOG.md updated to mention the new keywords functionality.

Other
- Manually tested. Screenshots provided in the original issue/PR description.
- No automated tests added in this PR.

Closes #10984

Add UnlinkedFilesDialogPreferences and wire it into JabRef GUI preferences

Summary
- Introduces a new UnlinkedFilesDialogPreferences class encapsulating the user-selectable settings for the Unlinked Files dialog: selected extension, selected date range, and selected sort order. The class exposes JavaFX properties and getters/setters and provides a getDefault() factory.
- Integrates the new preferences into JabRefGuiPreferences so the Unlinked Files dialog preferences are persisted to and restored from the backing store.

Details
- New class: org.jabref.gui.externalfiles.UnlinkedFilesDialogPreferences
  - Holds three JavaFX properties:
    - unlinkedFilesSelectedExtension (StringProperty)
    - unlinkedFilesSelectedDateRange (ObjectProperty<DateRange>)
    - unlinkedFilesSelectedSort (ObjectProperty<ExternalFileSorter>)
  - Default values: StandardFileType.ANY_FILE.getName(), DateRange.ALL_TIME, ExternalFileSorter.DEFAULT
  - Provides setAll(...) to copy settings from another instance and getDefault()

- JabRefGuiPreferences changes
  - Adds preference keys: UNLINKED_FILES_SELECTED_EXTENSION, UNLINKED_FILES_SELECTED_DATE_RANGE, UNLINKED_FILES_SELECTED_SORT
  - Adds a backing field unlinkedFilesDialogPreferences and methods:
    - getUnlinkedFilesDialogPreferencesFromBackingStore(UnlinkedFilesDialogPreferences defaults): constructs an instance from stored values (using DateRange.parse and ExternalFileSorter.parse)
    - getUnlinkedFilesDialogPreferences(): lazily loads the preferences from the backing store (falling back to defaults) and attaches EasyBind listeners to persist changes when the properties are updated
  - Ensures clear() resets the dialog preferences to the defaults and importPreferences() resets them to defaults in case of incomplete/corrupt imports

Why
- Centralizes Unlinked Files dialog settings into a dedicated, testable preferences class.
- Persists and restores these settings consistently with the rest of the GUI preferences, keeping UI state across restarts and imports/clears.

No behavior changes to existing features beyond adding persistence for the Unlinked Files dialog settings.

Closes #13868

Summary

This PR adds export functionality for AI Chat conversations and AI Summaries so users can save generated content in Markdown (.md) and JSON (.json) formats. Export controls were added to the AI Chat and Summary UI and the backend implements formatting, file dialogs, and error handling.

What I changed

- Added Gson dependency and module export (build.gradle.kts, module-info.java).
- AI Chat
  - Added an Export MenuButton (Markdown / JSON) to the chat toolbar (AiChatComponent.fxml).
  - Implemented export handlers in AiChatComponent: onExportMarkdown and onExportJson.
  - Implemented generateMarkdownExport and generateJsonExport for chat history + entry data. Chat JSON is serialized with Gson (pretty printed).
  - Uses FileDialogConfiguration / StandardFileType / FileFilterConverter and writes UTF-8 files. Notifications and error dialogs are shown on success/failure.
- Summaries
  - SummaryShowingComponent UI now contains an Export MenuButton (SummaryShowingComponent.fxml).
  - SummaryComponent now passes the BibEntry and DialogService to SummaryShowingComponent.
  - Implemented onExportMarkdown and onExportJson in SummaryShowingComponent and functions to generate Markdown and JSON exports for a summary (including entry BibTeX, entry fields, provider/model, timestamp and summary content).
  - Includes error handling and user notifications.

Files changed (high level)
- jabgui/build.gradle.kts (+gson dependency)
- jabgui/src/main/java/module-info.java (+requires com.google.gson)
- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/ai/components/aichat/AiChatComponent.java (export handlers + generators)
- jabgui/src/main/resources/org/jabref/gui/ai/components/aichat/AiChatComponent.fxml (export menu)
- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/ai/components/summary/SummaryComponent.java (constructor changes)
- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/ai/components/summary/SummaryShowingComponent.java (export handlers + generators)
- jabgui/src/main/resources/org/jabref/gui/ai/components/summary/SummaryShowingComponent.fxml (export menu)

Notes / Implementation details

- Markdown exports include a BibTeX fenced block and the human-readable content (conversation or summary).
- JSON exports include the raw entry BibTeX, a dictionary of entry fields, provider/model metadata, and the conversation/summary content. Chat JSON uses Gson for serialization; Summary JSON uses a small custom formatter to produce a readable JSON structure.
- File saving uses the existing DialogService + FileDialogConfiguration for consistent file chooser behavior and default extensions.
- All files are written as UTF-8. Exceptions during export produce an error dialog and are logged.

Testing notes

Manual tests performed (recommended steps included in the issue):
1. Run JabRef and open the AI Chat view.
2. Create a conversation or generate AI output, then click Export → choose Markdown or JSON.
3. Verify output files: Markdown should be human-readable (BibTeX + conversation/summary), JSON should be structured and include metadata (provider/model/timestamp where applicable).
4. Repeat for the Summary view.

Limitations / TODOs

- No automated unit tests were added (UI-driven feature).
- Summary JSON uses a custom string formatter while chat JSON uses Gson; they both produce readable JSON but could be unified in a follow-up.

This change improves portability of AI-generated content by making it easy to save and reuse outside JabRef.

Introduce a new ProxyPreferences model and integrate proxy handling into the CLI preferences.

Summary of changes:
- Add ProxyPreferences class (org.jabref.logic.net.ProxyPreferences):
  - Encapsulates proxy settings as JavaFX properties: useProxy, hostname, port, useAuthentication, username, password, persistPassword.
  - Provides constructors (including defaults), getters/setters, property accessors, setAll(), equals(), and hashCode().
  - Default values supplied for common proxy configuration.

- Integrate proxy preferences into JabRefCliPreferences:
  - Load and persist proxy settings from/to the java.util.prefs backing store via new helper getProxyPreferencesFromBackingStore.
  - Bind ProxyPreferences properties to the PREFS node using EasyBind so changes are immediately written to the backing store.
  - Securely store proxy password using the Keyring API: getProxyPassword() reads the encrypted password from the key store, setProxyPassword() writes/deletes it depending on persistPassword flag.
  - Respect persistPassword: when disabled, stored proxy credential is removed from the keyring.
  - Ensure clearing preferences or failing imports resets proxy preferences to defaults.

Behavioral notes:
- Proxy configuration is now fully represented as an observable object and synchronized with the persistent preferences store.
- Proxy password storage is encrypted and managed via Keyring; toggling persistence will add or remove the credential accordingly.
- No other preference behavior changes are introduced.

This change centralizes proxy state, improves observability for UI binding, and secures password management.

- No breaking changes to the public API are expected. If you rely on internal implementation details, those may have changed.
- Configuration keys remain the same; however, validation is stricter. If you used invalid/ambiguous config values before, you may now get validation errors that require updating the config to explicit values.

Testing:
- Added unit tests for the new helpers and integration tests for the end-to-end link-setting behavior.
- Ran existing test suite and fixed related failures.

Impact:
- More predictable and reliable AutoSetFileLinks behavior, fewer race conditions, and easier future maintenance.

Resubmit: Properly copy associated PDF files when moving entries between .bib files (fix for #520)

What this PR does
- Implements copying of linked PDF files when entries are copied/pasted between different BibDatabaseContexts. The source database's default file directory is inspected and any linked PDF found there is copied into the destination database's default file directory when pasting entries.
- Adds file-copy behavior to the Copy Files UI action so linked files are actually copied to the selected folder and new LinkedFile entries are added to the BibEntry.
- Ensures CopyFilesTask updates the linked file path after a successful copy.
- Adds logging statements around file copy operations to help debugging.
- Minor whitespace/cleanup in CopyFilesDialogView and CHANGELOG update describing the feature.

Files changed (high level)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/LibraryTab.java
  - Store last copied BibDatabaseContext and, on paste, find linked PDF files from the source database default file directory and copy them into the target database default file directory before importing entries.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/copyfiles/CopyFilesAction.java
  - When copying linked files to a folder, copy files immediately and add updated LinkedFile entries to the corresponding BibEntry. Added logging and exception handling.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/copyfiles/CopyFilesTask.java
  - After a successful file copy, update the LinkedFile link to the new destination path (so the UI/log shows the updated path).
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/io/FileUtil.java
  - Add logging around Files.copy operations.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/copyfiles/CopyFilesDialogView.java
  - Minor trailing newline change.
- CHANGELOG.md
  - Document the new behavior for copying associated PDF files between .bib files.

Notes
- This PR resubmits the changes to the correct repository (original PR was mistakenly placed elsewhere). See and closes issue: https://github.com/koppor/jabref/issues/520
- No tests were included in this PR.
- Logging was added to aid diagnosing file copy failures; failures are logged and do not abort the import/copy operation.

Summary
Remove the field saving options and all related code, UI elements, and documentation. Fields are now persisted using the simplified/default behavior and the old per-field saving configuration and toggles have been removed.

Why
The per-field saving options added complexity, created multiple code paths, and were seldom used. Consolidating to a single, simpler save behavior reduces maintenance and confusion.

What changed
- Removed configuration keys and feature flags for per-field saving (deprecated options and UI toggles).
- Deleted code paths that branched on field-specific save settings and consolidated to the default saving implementation.
- Removed related UI controls and settings screens that allowed enabling/disabling field saving.
- Updated documentation and configuration schema to reflect the simplified behavior.
- Updated unit and integration tests to match the new behavior; removed or replaced tests that relied on the removed options.

Migration / Compatibility notes
- If your configuration currently includes field-saving options or feature flags, you should remove them. They are no longer supported and will be ignored.
- Default behavior is used for all fields now. If you previously used the options to disable saving for specific fields, you will need to implement custom logic outside of the removed configuration to achieve the same effect.
- No database migrations are required.

Testing
- Unit and integration tests were updated to reflect the consolidated save behavior.
- Manual QA: verify that fields are persisted according to the default behavior and that no UI controls for per-field saving remain.

Rollback
- Reverting this PR will restore the removed options and code paths. If you need the removed behavior, revert the merge and follow up with a plan for long-term support or an alternative implementation.

text:
Add BibTeX String Editor UI and supporting infrastructure

Summary
- Introduces a full-featured BibTeX String Editor dialog (FXML + controller + view model + item model) to view, add, edit, remove and save bibtex strings for a library.
- Adds UI styling tweaks in Base.css and EntryEditor.css for consistent look & feel and tooltips used by the editor.
- Adds localization entries required by the dialog (labels, tooltips, messages) in JabRef_en.properties.
- Implements reusable cell/validation helpers (ViewModelListCellFactory and ViewModelTextFieldTableCellVisualizationFactory) to show validation state via pseudo-class and tooltips.

Details
- UI: BibtexStringEditorDialog.fxml provides the dialog layout with a constrained TableView for strings (label, content, actions) and buttons for adding strings and opening help. Uses JabRefIconView for toolbar icons and tooltips for accessibility.

- Controller: BibtexStringEditorDialogView
  - Wires the FXML components to the view model and installs editable cells for label and content using ViewModelTextFieldTableCellVisualizationFactory which presents validation errors as tooltips and applies an "invalid" pseudo-class.
  - Adds duplicate-name protection when editing labels: if a label already exists, the change is rejected and user is shown an error dialog.
  - Binds the Save button to the combined validation state of all rows so saving is only enabled when all rows are valid.
  - Adds convenient behaviour: adding a new string focuses the new label cell for immediate editing; Open Help opens the STRING_EDITOR help file.

- ViewModel: BibtexStringEditorDialogViewModel
  - Loads existing strings from BibDatabase, sorts them and maps them to item view models.
  - Provides addNewString() (creates unique NewString/NexN labels if necessary), removeString(), save() (writes back to BibDatabase), labelAlreadyExists() and validProperty() (combined validation across rows using EasyBind).

- Item Model: BibtexStringEditorItemModel
  - Encapsulates label and content properties.
  - Uses mvvmfx FunctionBasedValidator & CompositeValidator to validate label and content.
  - Label rules: not null/empty, not purely numeric, cannot contain '#', cannot contain spaces. Content rules: not null/empty.
  - Exposes validation methods and a read-only combined valid property for binding.

- Reusable utilities
  - ViewModelTextFieldTableCellVisualizationFactory: provides a TextFieldTableCell that attaches validation tooltips and toggles an "invalid" pseudo-class based on a validation status function. Also focuses and selects the text field when editing starts.
  - ViewModelListCellFactory: constructs ListCell instances from a view model with support for text, graphic, tooltip, style classes, context menus, drag events, and validation pseudo-class handling. Subscriptions are cleaned up on updateItem.
  - Both factories use BindingsHelper to attach pseudo-classes and use fmisc easybind Subscriptions to avoid leaks.

- Styles & Localization
  - Base.css and EntryEditor.css updated/used to ensure the dialog components, icon buttons, toolbars and tooltips follow JabRef theme conventions.
  - JabRef_en.properties: many localization keys are present/added: "Strings for library", "New string", "Add new String", "Remove string %0", validation messages like "Please enter the string's label", "The label of the string cannot contain spaces.", "Must not be empty!", and dialog button labels (Save, Cancel, Open Help page).

Behavior & UX notes
- Save button is disabled while any row is invalid, preventing saving inconsistent data.
- Editing a label checks for duplicates and shows a modal error if the new label collides with another existing label.
- Adding a new string auto-selects the new row and enters edit mode on the label column for quick entry.
- Actions column exposes a delete glyph with tooltip to remove strings.
- The Help button links to the STRING_EDITOR help file.

Developer notes
- Uses de.saxsys.mvvmfx validators and fmisc easybind for validation and property composition.
- Ensure BindingsHelper and IconTheme utilities are available (used by the cell factories and action icons).
- The new pseudo-class 'invalid' is used in CSS to style invalid cells; styles can be added if desired to highlight invalid state visually.

This change adds an end-to-end editing experience for BibTeX strings integrated into the library model, with strong validation and user-friendly editing flows.

Summary

This pull request improves the OpenOffice/LibreOffice citation integration by fixing bugs and making the OpenOffice bibliography style handling more robust. It also updates the CHANGELOG to document the changes.

Changes

- Fix potential NullPointerException and connection issues in OOBibBase
  - Add defensive null checks when accessing the OpenOffice document/bridge to avoid crashes when the connection is lost or not yet established.
  - Improve exception handling and logging for RemoteException and other runtime issues when interacting with the office API.

- Make OOBibStyle parsing and handling more robust
  - Harden style parsing logic to tolerate unexpected or missing properties in the retrieved style data.
  - Ensure fallback/default style is used when the requested style is not available, preventing rendering failures.
  - Minor internal refactoring to clarify responsibilities and make the code easier to maintain and test.

- Documentation
  - Update CHANGELOG.md with an entry describing the fixes and improvements to the OpenOffice integration.

Why this change

These updates reduce runtime errors users experience when using JabRef with OpenOffice/LibreOffice, especially in cases where the office connection is flaky or style metadata is incomplete. The improved error handling ensures the application degrades more gracefully and provides better logging for diagnosing issues.

Notes

No public API changes outside the OpenOffice integration were made. Changes are focused on reliability and maintainability.

text:
Fix UTF BOM parsing when detecting encoding header in .bib files

What I changed
- Bugfix: When a .bib file begins with a UTF BOM, the first character(s) are not '%' so line.startsWith("%") fails to detect encoding header comments. The parser now searches for the first '%' in the line (line.indexOf('%')) and trims from that position, which skips any BOM bytes before the percent sign.
- Tests: Extended and adjusted BibtexImporter tests to cover UTF-8 and UTF-16BE files both with and without encoding headers, and added assertions for whether the encoding was explicitly supplied in the metadata.
- Minor cleanup: Updated imports in the test accordingly.
- Changelog: Added an entry noting the fix for encoding header handling when the file contains a BOM.

Why
- Java may keep BOM characters at the start of the first line; the percent sign that denotes a .bib comment may thus appear at a non-zero index. Using startsWith("%") missed those cases and caused the import to ignore the encoding header. This resulted in wrong encoding detection for files with BOMs.

Files changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/BibtexImporter.java
  - Use line.indexOf('%') and substring from that position to correctly skip BOMs.
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/BibtexImporterTest.java
  - Added/modified parameterized tests to cover UTF-8 and UTF-16BE with/without headers and to verify encodingExplicitlySupplied.
- CHANGELOG.md
  - Note about respecting encoding header when the file contains a BOM.

Tests
- Added/updated unit tests to ensure umlauts and encoding metadata are read correctly for UTF-8 and UTF-16BE files, with and without header lines.

Fixes: #9926

Fixes #10498 — Add ScholarArchive fetcher and query transformer

Summary
- Adds support for scholar.archive.org as a new search fetcher in JabRef.
- Implements a PagedSearchBasedParserFetcher that queries the Scholar Archive API, parses JSON results and converts them to BibEntry objects.
- Adds a query transformer to convert JabRef Lucene-style queries into Scholar Archive query parameters.
- Registers the new fetcher in the global WebFetchers list and updates changelog and tests.

What changed
- New files:
  - ScholarArchiveFetcher: builds search URLs (q, from, size, format=json), sets Accept header, parses the JSON response into BibEntry objects. Maps biblio fields to JabRef fields (title, container_name -> journal, doi, issue, publisher, language, release_year -> year, volume_int -> volume, abstracts[].body -> abstract, fulltext.access_url -> URL, date, contrib_names -> author, issns -> issn). Also maps release_type to a type field and chooses an entry type (Book, Article, InCollection default).
  - ScholarArchiveQueryTransformer: extends AbstractQueryTransformer. Provides AND/OR/NOT operators, maps query fields author/title/journal to the corresponding Scholar Archive keys and handles year and year ranges (publication.startDate range queries).
- Registration:
  - WebFetchers: ScholarArchiveFetcher added to the search-based fetcher set.
- Tests and test updates:
  - ScholarArchiveFetcherTest: basic unit tests checking fetcher name and performSearch behavior (contains a sample bibentry expectation).
  - ManageStudyDefinitionViewModelTest: updated to include ScholarArchive in the list of catalogs and refactored to use a small helper for obtaining the view model.
- Changelog: CHANGELOG.md updated to mention scholar.archive.org as a new fetcher.

Notes and caveats
- JSON parsing assumes the current Scholar Archive API structure (biblio, abstracts, fulltext, contrib_names, issns etc.). The parser will throw a ParseException when the JSON format changes.
- Year handling in the query transformer constructs a publication.startDate range for exact years and parsed ranges; further refinement may be needed depending on Scholar Archive query semantics.
- Tests currently exercise name and basic search. The performSearch test may rely on live API responses; consider mocking network calls for more stable CI tests.

Manual testing
- The new fetcher was manually tested in a running JabRef build.

Request for review
- Please review field mappings (especially date, type and author formatting) and the year range handling in the transformer.
- Any preferences on handling missing fields or alternate JSON shapes are welcome.

text:
Introduce DelayTaskThrottler and use it to debounce expensive/duplicate actions

Summary
- Add a new utility DelayTaskThrottler to debounce scheduled Runnable tasks (cancel previously scheduled task and schedule a new one within a delay window).
- Integrate DelayTaskThrottler into autosave, backup and group hit-count calculation to reduce redundant work and improve performance.

What changed
- New class: org.jabref.logic.util.DelayTaskThrottler
  - Provides schedule(Runnable) and shutdown() methods.
  - Uses a single-thread ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor and setRemoveOnCancelPolicy(true) so re-scheduled tasks replace previously scheduled ones.

- AutosaveManager
  - Now uses DelayTaskThrottler (2_000 ms delay) to debounce posting AutosaveEvent after database change events.
  - Internally posts AutosaveEvent on an internal EventBus so listeners can register/unregister with the AutosaveManager.
  - Uses CoarseChangeFilter to listen to database changes (unchanged behavior) but scheduling is now throttled.

- BackupManager
  - Uses DelayTaskThrottler (15_000 ms delay) to debounce backup writes after database changes.
  - startBackupTask() now schedules determineBackupPath().ifPresent(this::performBackup) via the throttler.
  - Shutdown still unregisters listeners and deletes the backup file.

text:
Add an in-app Error Console dialog and a reusable ListCell factory

This PR introduces a small error-console feature and a utility for creating list cells based on view-model objects.

Files added/changed:
- ErrorConsoleView: FXML-backed dialog wrapper that displays the event log in a resizable alert dialog.
- ErrorConsoleController: Controller for the error console view. Binds the ListView to the shared LogMessages property, sets an icon for the description label and configures a cell factory to show icons and styling per log level. Provides handlers for copying logs and closing the dialog.
- ErrorConsoleViewModel: View model that exposes the LogMessages list, implements copy-to-clipboard for the full log, and implements a GitHub "report issue" flow that opens the new-issue page in the browser and copies a formatted issue body (including build/OS/Java info and the log in a markdown details/code block) to the clipboard.
- ViewModelListCellFactory: New reusable factory to build ListCell instances from simple callbacks (text, graphic, style class, mouse handler). Used to style list rows in the error console based on log level.

Behavior highlights:
- The list of LogEvent entries is bound to LogMessages.getInstance().messagesProperty(), so the dialog shows live messages.
- Log entries are decorated with an icon and a CSS style class depending on the log level (ERROR/WARN/INFO).
- The "Copy log" button copies the whole current log to the clipboard and shows a status message.
- The "Report issue" button prepares an issue title and body with basic system/build information, opens the browser to GitHub's new-issue page, and copies detailed issue information (log wrapped in a markdown details/code block) to the clipboard. IO and URI exceptions are logged.

Utility notes:
- ViewModelListCellFactory makes it easy to specify how items are rendered by providing small callback functions for text, graphic, style class and click handlers.

This change adds a convenient way for users to inspect and export application logs and to report issues with contextual log data.

3. Click 'Copy BibTeX' and paste into a text editor to ensure the entry was copied.
4. Test with results that have partial metadata to verify reasonable fallbacks.

- UI styling follows existing import preview patterns; check responsive behavior.

Fixes an issue in the Keyword editor / TagsField where hierarchical keywords were not converted correctly: only the parent keyword was returned by the StringConverter, so entries with e.g. "parent > node > child" showed just the parent in the Keywords field (and could trigger an assertion).

What I changed

- Corrected the StringConverter/keyword-to-string handling so that hierarchical keywords are represented by their full path (parent > node > child) instead of only the top-level parent.

Why

This fixes the bug reported in #11390 (follow-up to #10910) where hierarchical keywords were being truncated to their parent when shown/edited in the entry editor.

Summary

This PR implements several UI and data-model improvements to the main table and global-search UI:

What's included

- Add Library column to the main table
  - Introduces LibraryColumn which displays the originating library/file name using FileUtil::getBaseName.
  - The column is backed by a new bibDatabasePathProperty() on the BibEntryTableViewModel so each row can show which library the entry belongs to.

- Enhance BibEntryTableViewModel
  - Expose bibDatabaseContext and a ReadOnlyString property for the database path used by the Library column.
  - Create bindings for linked identifiers (URL, DOI, URI, EPRINT, ISBN) and matched groups.
  - Improve handling and caching of special fields and combined field values used by the main table cells.

- Global search UI improvements
  - Add a dedicated GlobalSearchBar component (search modifiers, delayed search, regex validation, autocompletion hookup).
  - Add GlobalSearchResultDialog to show results from open libraries in a separate window with a results table and preview pane.
  - Double-click behavior in the results table: open the corresponding library tab, select the entry in the main table and close the dialog.
  - Persist global search window size and provide a "keep on top" toggle bound to the view model.
  - Use a custom AutoComplete popup skin (reflection is used to obtain the ControlsFX internal popup) to ensure suggestion rendering is integrated with our UI.

- Miscellaneous
  - Improve tooltips and regex validation for the search field, keep search history handling when focus is lost, and wire up modifier buttons to SearchPreferences.
  - Remove SpecialFieldColumn instances from results table in the global search dialog (results are simplified for cross-library view).

Why this change

These changes make it easier to identify which library an entry belongs to in multi-library setups and provide a more powerful, user-friendly global search window that aggregates results across open libraries and lets users quickly jump back to the selected entry in its original library.

Notes / Follow-ups

- The global search autocompletion uses a reflective access to ControlsFX internals to obtain the popup. This is documented in the code as a temporary/fragile measure.
- The PR preserves window size between sessions and exposes options to keep the search window on top.

Summary

Fixes an issue where JabRef would not show the contents of a large shared database library (Fixes #8788). The problem was caused by requesting too many shared entries at once. This change partitions the list of requested shared IDs into batches of 500 and queries the DBMS in multiple smaller calls, preventing the large single request from failing or timing out.

What I changed

- Added partitionAndGetSharedEntries(List<Integer>) to DBMSProcessor which splits the requested IDs into 500-element batches (using Guava Lists.partition) and aggregates results from getSharedEntries for each sublist.
- Updated DBMSSynchronizer to use partitionAndGetSharedEntries when inserting missing shared entries into the local database.
- Added a changelog entry noting the fix.

Why

Large requests for shared entries could fail or not return results when many IDs were requested at once. Partitioning the requests into smaller batches makes the retrieval reliable for large shared libraries.

Files changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/shared/DBMSProcessor.java: new partitionAndGetSharedEntries method and Guava import
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/shared/DBMSSynchronizer.java: use partitioned fetch
- CHANGELOG.md: added note about the bugfix

Notes

- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance with a large shared library; contents are now correctly displayed.
- No unit tests were added in this change.

Fixes: #8788

Fixes an issue where keyboard shortcuts in Preferences could not be edited (closes #14237).

What was happening:
- Shortcut input fields in the Preferences panel could not receive focus or accept edits, preventing users from changing or clearing keybindings.

What this change does:
- Restores focus and keystroke handling for the shortcut input control in Preferences.
- Temporarily suppresses global shortcut interception while a shortcut field is being edited so key events are routed to the input.
- Ensures edited values are validated and persisted to the settings store.

Tests and QA:
- Added tests and manual verification for entering, clearing, canceling, and saving shortcut edits.
- Verified that normal global shortcuts still work outside of editing mode.

Result: Users can now edit, clear, and save keyboard shortcuts in Preferences as expected.

This pull request introduces a series of enhancements and fixes to improve the usability and stability of JabRef. Key changes include:

### Added
- **BibTeX Key Generator**: Added a new field in the preferences for specifying unwanted characters in BibTeX keys. (#6295)
- **ShortScience Search**: Added support for searching ShortScience through the user's browser. (#6018)
- **EditionChecker**: Updated to allow editions to start with a number. (#6144)
- **Tooltips**: Added tooltips for most fields in the entry editor. (#5847)
- **Markdown Support**: Added support for basic markdown in custom formatted previews. (#6194)
- **Import Feedback**: Show the number of items found and selected to import in the online search dialog. (#6248)
- **macOS Install Screen**: Created a new install screen for macOS. (#5759)
- **Integrity Check**: Added a new integrity check for duplicate DOIs. (#koppor#339)
- **Fulltext Downloads**: Implemented an option to download fulltext files while importing. (#6381)
- **Progress Indicator**: Added a progress indicator for background tasks in the toolbar. (#6443)

### Changed
- **arXiv Fetcher**: Improved reliability and removed version numbers from the `eprint` field. (#forum#1941)
- **Group Interface**: Moved the group search bar and "New group" button to a more prominent position. (#6112)
- **Preferences Dialog**: Changed the buttons for import/export/show all/reset of preferences to smaller icon buttons. (#6130)
- **Menu Reorganization**: Moved the "Manage field names & content" function to the "Edit" menu. (#6130)

### Fixed
- **BibTeX Key Issues**: Fixed issues with incompatible characters and dashes in BibTeX keys. (#6257, #6295)
- **Performance Improvements**: Greatly improved the performance of the application and many operations. (#5071)
- **Sorting Issues**: Fixed issues with sorting by priority and numeric cases. (#6222, #6349)
- **File Handling**: Fixed issues with file extensions and overwriting existing files. (#6115, #6174)
- **Windows Installer**: Fixed an issue where the Windows installer did not create an entry in the start menu. (#bug report in the forum)

These changes aim to enhance the user experience, improve performance, and fix critical bugs.

Summary
- Fixes incorrect conversion of Unicode characters that caused corrupted output (mojibake) for accented letters, non‑Latin scripts, combining characters and emoji.

Problem
- Several conversion paths assumed the wrong encoding or used ad‑hoc byte↔string operations that lost multi‑byte sequences. This resulted in characters being misdecoded or dropped.

What changed
- Centralized and corrected bytes↔string handling to consistently use UTF‑8 for decoding/encoding.
- Replaced ad‑hoc conversions with a safe helper that preserves Unicode code points and handles both bytes and str inputs.
- Added NFC normalization where appropriate to make comparisons stable across composed/decomposed forms.
- Updated call sites to expect/return proper str objects instead of mangled byte representations.
- Ensured file/stream I/O opens use encoding='utf-8' where relevant.
- Added unit tests that cover accented characters, non‑Latin scripts, combining sequences, and emoji.

Tests
- New tests added for the affected conversion functions. Tests pass locally; CI should verify cross‑platform behavior.

Compatibility / Impact
- This is a correctness fix; no public API changes were made. Downstream code that relied on previously mangled output will now receive correct Unicode text.
- If any consumer deliberately depended on the old (incorrect) byte sequences, they should be updated to work with proper Unicode strings.

Notes for reviewers
- Pay attention to encoding assumptions in any remaining I/O or third‑party integrations.
- Run the added unit tests and spot‑check file read/write behavior on your platform.

Notes for reviewers
- This is a behavioral change: any code that intentionally relied on injecting HTML into form fields will need to render that HTML elsewhere or use an explicit, reviewed mechanism for trusted HTML.
- No public API changes; will reduce XSS risk and make field rendering consistent.

Testing
- New tests added; all tests pass locally.
