text:
Fix syncLang.py script

Fixes #3573

Summary
- Major refactor and bugfixes for scripts/syncLang.py to make the localization sync script more robust and user friendly.
- Fixed a logical merging issue when synchronizing property files (reported in #3573). The behavior around how missing, duplicate and obsolete keys are detected/handled has been corrected.

Key changes
- Introduced an argparse-based CLI with subcommands: markdown, status, update, and print (with print missing|obsolete|duplicates). This replaces fragile sys.argv parsing and makes the tool easier to use.
- Added optional PathFinder (uses pathlib) to locate repository directories when available; falls back gracefully if pathlib is not present.
- Renamed and reorganized many methods for clarity:
  - Keys.duplicates -> Keys.find_duplicates
  - SyncLang.update -> SyncLang.update_properties
  - File read/write functions renamed for clarity (__read_lines_from_file)
  - Added utility helpers: __missing_keys (now uses set difference), __print_keys, format_key_and_value
- Fixed duplicate/merge handling:
  - Use a canonical format_key_and_value helper to produce consistent output for duplicate reporting and writing.
  - Corrected logic that previously caused incorrect merging of keys when synchronizing; ambiguous duplicates are now reported and skipped, unambiguous duplicates fixed automatically.
  - Missing keys are no longer blindly populated with empty or incorrect values; main translations can be used as a comment in code for future behavior (currently missing keys are left empty/handled explicitly).
- Better logging and extended output handling: extended -> extended_logging flag and the script can print detailed key lists via the new print subcommands.
- Markdown status generation preserved but now driven through the new CLI.

Compatibility
- argparse is used (present in Python 2.7+, and Python 3). pathlib-based PathFinder requires Python 3.4+, but its import is wrapped in try/except so the script remains usable in environments without pathlib.

Manual testing
- Changes were manually tested locally against the repository localization files.

Notes
- The refactor focuses on correctness and usability of the sync script. Additional test coverage and CHANGELOG entry were not included in this PR.
- See discussion and original report here: https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/3573#issuecomment-366490651

Add TestFX UI test for ReplaceStringView (ReplaceStringViewTest.java).

This PR adds a UI test that uses TestFX to load the ReplaceStringView FXML, bring up its dialogPane and perform a sequence of user interactions with FxRobot to verify the replace-string behavior. The test demonstrates that TestFX can be used for our dialogs and provides a starting point for adding more UI tests (#6207) and following the TestFX suggestion from #6089.

Key points:
- New test: ReplaceStringViewTest.java
- Uses TestFX to mock/load the ReplaceStringView FXML, open the dialogPane and simulate user actions to assert the replace behavior.
- Currently the test needs Globals.prefs and Globals.fileUpdateMonitor to be non-null. To prove the concept, Globals.prefs is initialized inside the test. This highlights a dependency in BaseDialog.java (and related code) on global state and suggests a refactor to remove or make these dependencies test-friendly (e.g., dependency injection or safer initialization).

Notes / Next steps:
- Consider refactoring BaseDialog and related classes to avoid relying on Globals static fields so UI dialogs can be tested in isolation without test-side initialization.
- Add more TestFX UI tests following this pattern to increase UI coverage (#6207).

- Tests created: yes
- Documentation checked: yes
- CHANGELOG / manual testing / screenshots updated where applicable.

Fix for #2394 — groups with brackets in their names were not matched correctly.

Problem
- Group names that include square brackets (e.g. "group[1]") were treated as regex character classes when building the matching pattern, causing incorrect matching or runtime errors.

What I changed
- Properly escape group names when constructing regular expressions (use a regex-quoting/escaping utility) so literal characters like [ and ] are matched literally.
- Added unit tests that cover group names containing square brackets as well as other special regex characters (e.g. parentheses, plus, dot) to prevent regressions.
- Small refactor to centralize the escaping logic and make the intent clearer.

Why this fixes the issue
- Escaping special regex characters removes ambiguity between literal group names and regex metacharacters, ensuring group lookup and matching behave as expected for any valid group name.

Compatibility
- This is a bug fix with no breaking changes to public APIs. Existing behavior for group matching is preserved except that names containing regex metacharacters now work correctly.

Testing
- New unit tests included; run the test suite to verify.
- Manually tested matching with names like: "group[1]", "group(2)", "group+3", and "group.name".

Related
- Closes #2394

text:
Add Ottobib fetcher

Summary:
- Introduces a new fetcher that retrieves book metadata from Ottobib (ottobib.com) by ISBN and returns normalized metadata used by the application.

What this PR changes:
- Adds a new module implementing the Ottobib fetcher (src/fetchers/ottobib).
- Registers the Ottobib fetcher in the fetcher registry so it can be enabled alongside existing fetchers.
- Normalizes returned data to the common metadata shape (title, authors, publisher, publishedDate, isbn, identifiers, language, description, subjects).
- Implements network retry and basic HTML parsing resilience to small layout changes.
- Adds caching support (respecting the existing cache layer) to avoid repeated requests for the same ISBN.
- Adds unit tests and integration tests (tests/fetchers/ottobib.*) including success, not-found, and network error scenarios.
- Updates documentation: README (fetchers section) and CHANGELOG with usage notes and configuration options.

Usage / testing notes:
- Example usage is included in the README and in tests; calling the fetcher with an ISBN returns the normalized metadata object.
- Run tests: npm test (or yarn test). Integration tests that hit the live site can be toggled with test flags/environment variables as documented in the updated README.

Compatibility and migration:
- No breaking API changes to existing fetcher interfaces.
- Ottobib fetcher is added as an additional source and can be enabled/disabled via the fetcher registry configuration.

Notes and caveats:
- Ottobib provides data by scraping their pages; resilience is implemented but structural site changes may require updates to the parser.
- Network errors and missing records are handled gracefully and covered by tests.

This PR implements the core functionality and tests; follow-up PRs can add additional fields or refine parsing rules if needed.

Fix ACM Portal author parsing and improve early localization logging

- Fix: ACMPortalParser now handles authors that lack a given name. The parser previously concatenated given + family and could produce incorrect formatting or miss entries when the given name was absent. The code now builds JabRef Author objects (null-safe for "given" and "family") and uses AuthorList.getAsLastFirstNamesWithAnd(false) to produce properly formatted "Last, First" names (and joined with "and"). This resolves an issue where some ACM Portal searches would not return entries when an article author had no given name (see changelog entry and issue #10107).

- Tests: Added testParseBibEntryWithFamilyAuthorOnly in ACMPortalParserTest to cover parsing of authors where one or more authors only provide a family name. The test verifies the generated BibEntry matches expected fields and author formatting.

- Localization: Modified Localization to avoid using the static SLF4J logger during very early initialization. Added @AllowedToUseStandardStreams annotation and write a message to System.err when messages are not initialized. Replaced the removed static LOGGER usages with direct LoggerFactory.getLogger(...) calls for warnings emitted after logger initialization.

- Changelog: Added an entry describing the ACM Portal search fix.

text:
Implemented "Unmerge citations" in the OpenOffice/LibreOffice integration panel (fixes #7454).

What this PR does
- Adds an "Unmerge citations" action to the OO/LO integration panel so users can split previously merged citation markers back into individual references.
- Includes a changelog entry and a screenshot demonstrating the new UI control.

Testing and status
- Manually tested the feature in a running JabRef build.
- No automated tests added for this change (GUI integration tests are not included).

Known limitations and edge cases
- The current "Merge citations" implementation does not persist all information required to reliably restore optional extra info (e.g. page references) stored in document properties. When unmerging, getUniqueReferenceMarkName() may return a different name than the original; this can lead to loss of extra info or, in rare cases, applying it to the wrong entry.
- combineCiteMarkers reorders merged entries by year, which loses the original ordering of entries in the merged citation.
- The current solution improves usability but does not cover all cases. A more robust approach could encode the uniqueness index into the merged marker name (for example, turning "JR_cite_1_XX2000a,YY2010" into "JR_cite_1_XX2000a,1_YY2010") and/or mark original names as reserved when creating merged names so getUniqueReferenceMarkName() can reproduce originals.

Documentation
- The online docs (https://docs.jabref.org/cite/openofficeintegration) do not currently mention the "Merge citations" button. It would be appropriate to document this feature (and the known issues) under the OpenOffice/LibreOffice integration section or the Known issues page.

Screenshots
- Screenshot added: jabref-Unmerge-citations (shows the new Unmerge citations control in the OO/LO panel).

text:
Fix WordKeywordGroup matching and normalize keyword parsing

What I changed
- Fixed the matching behaviour in WordKeywordGroup so that keywords are detected as whole words and are normalized consistently (trimming and case-insensitive matching). This prevents false matches inside other words and handles keywords with surrounding punctuation or whitespace correctly.
- Improved keyword list parsing/normalization logic used by groups to avoid empty keywords and duplicate entries.
- Updated unit tests (KeywordListTest and ExplicitGroupTest) to reflect the corrected behaviour and to add coverage for edge cases (punctuation, surrounding whitespace, empty entries, and duplicates).
- Added a changelog entry describing the fix.

Why this change
- Previously, grouping by keywords could produce incorrect results when a keyword appeared as a substring inside another word, when keywords contained extra spaces or punctuation, or when the keyword list contained empty/duplicate entries. This led to unexpected group membership and flaky behaviour.

How I tested
- Updated and ran existing unit tests; added/adjusted tests in KeywordListTest and ExplicitGroupTest to cover the edge cases addressed by the fix.

Notes for reviewers
- Review the WordKeywordGroup implementation for regex and normalization choices to ensure they meet project conventions for internationalization and performance.
- The changelog entry documents the user-facing aspect of the fix.

  - Remember the source BibDatabaseContext on copy and, on paste, attempt to locate and copy linked PDF files from the source database's default file directory to the destination database's default file directory before importing entries.

- When entries are copied in the Library view, the source database context is stored. - The implementation relies on the default file directory metadata of both source and destination BibDatabaseContext; if the source directory is unavailable the code logs a warning and skips copying.
- Copies use Files.copy with REPLACE_EXISTING; this will overwrite existing files at the destination.
- Additional logging imports and a static copiedBibDatabaseContext field were introduced.

Summary

This PR contains a set of improvements, bug fixes and small refactors across tooling and the jablib codebase. The changes focus on robustness (parsing & IO), better heuristics for PDF/title extraction, improved network download handling, and developer convenience scripts.

Highlights

- Tooling (/.jbang)
  - Added/updated jbang helper scripts: CheckoutPR, CloneJabRef as well as launchers for JabKit, JabLs and JabSrv to simplify local development workflows (clone repo, checkout PRs, run small CLI/servers).

- BibTeX parser (BibtexParser)
  - Improved robustness when detecting newline separator and while reading/purging header metadata.
  - Better handling of BibDesk metadata (plist parsing) and migration of BibDesk static groups into JabRef groups.
  - More defensive parsing for corrupted citation keys and multi-line fields; improved error/warning reporting and attempt to recover from parse errors.

- PDF importer (PdfContentImporter)
  - Improved title extraction using font-size heuristics (TitleExtractorByFontSize) and refined heuristics to ignore noise (footer/header) when picking title text.
  - More robust overall parsing logic for first-page content: streamlined author/title handling, abstract/keywords extraction and publisher/conference detection for Springer/IEEE styles.

- File handling (LinkedFileHandler)
  - Improved logic for computing target paths, handling existing files, renaming to suggested patterns and ensuring uniqueness.
  - Safer move/copy operations and clearer logging when skipping operations because same file already exists.

- Citation key generation (CitationKeyGenerator)
  - Improved cleaning of generated keys: removes unwanted and BibTeX-disallowed characters, replaces special characters with safe ASCII equivalents and enforces whitespace removal.
  - Deterministic appendix generation to make keys unique (a..z, aa.. etc.).

- BST engine (BstFunctions)
  - Refactor and clarifications of many builtin functions (assign, add/concat/substring/formatting operations) and improved validation with clearer error messages.
  - Uses modern Java pattern-matching idioms for clearer code paths where applicable.

- AI summarization task (GenerateSummaryTask)
  - Improvements in chunking and combining summaries; clearer progress accounting and logging for summarization runs and errors.
  - More defensive handling when no linked files or when text extraction fails.

- Network/downloads (URLDownload)
  - More reliable MIME type detection: try HEAD requests with manual redirect following (retries), fallback to GET and finally to URLConnection lookup.
  - Set default Unirest configuration (user agent, cookie management, follow redirects) and encapsulated helpers for toFile / toTemporaryFile / asInputStream.
  - Improved error handling and clearer FetcherException variants for HTTP client/server errors.

- Miscellaneous
  - UnprotectTermsFormatter: safer handling for balanced braces and unchanged output on unbalanced input.
  - NameFormatter: defaults and helper to obtain configured name formatters from preferences.
  - Small logging, internationalization and comment/doc updates throughout the codebase.

Notes

- The PR focuses on making importers, file handling and network I/O more resilient to real-world inputs (malformed BibTeX, complex PDFs, redirecting URLs, file collisions) and provides developer-friendly helper scripts to streamline common tasks when working with the repository locally.
- See inline code comments and logger messages for more details on individual behavior changes.

- Adding unit tests to ensure the parser correctly handles both valid and invalid URLs.

Summary of changes

- Add MSC classification tooltips for keywords
  - KeywordsEditor now loads an MSC codes mapping from msc_codes.json at class initialization and shows a tooltip with the MSC description when a tag matches an MSC code. Loading errors are logged and a safe empty map fallback is used.

- Keyword model and list improvements
  - Keyword: introduced DEFAULT_HIERARCHICAL_DELIMITER, ofHierarchical factory, improved toString/equals/hashCode/compareTo implementations, and added utilities for working with hierarchical chains (getPathFromRootAsString, flatten, getAllSubchainsAsString, addAtEnd).
  - KeywordList: added parsing that accepts an explicit hierarchical delimiter, unified parsing/serialization utilities, merge helper, and other helpers (serialize, parse, merge, createClone, etc.). KeywordList now preserves chain semantics when parsing and serializing.

- ViewModel and editor updates
  - KeywordsEditorViewModel now binds the keyword list property to the editor text using KeywordList.parse/serialize and exposes a StringConverter that preserves hierarchical keywords.
  - Suggestion handling in the view model builds Keyword suggestions and ensures the requested keyword is present at the top of the suggestions.
  - KeywordsEditor (UI): uses the view model converter/matcher, sets up tag cell factory and tag view, supports paste of multiple keywords, keyboard handling, drag-and-drop reordering of tags, and context menu actions (copy, cut, delete). The new MSC tooltip lookup is integrated into tag creation.

- Tests
  - Added KeywordsEditorViewModelTest to assert hierarchical keywords are converted to string as expected.

Notes and compatibility
- If msc_codes.json is missing or fails to load, the editor will log the issue and proceed without MSC tooltips (no crash).
- Keyword/KeywordList API improvements preserve existing parsing/serialization overloads but add richer hierarchical handling.

These changes improve keyword handling (especially hierarchical keywords) and add helpful MSC classification tooltips in the UI.

Summary

This PR restores backward compatibility so users who upgraded to JabRef 5.0/5.1 can safely return to older releases such as JabRef 4.3.1 without losing preferences. It bridges changed preference variable names and converts column preferences back to pre-5.0 formats when needed.

What changed

- JabRefPreferences: renamed the public constants for column preferences to the new mainTable* names (mainTableColumnNames, mainTableColumnWidths, mainTableColumnSortTypes, mainTableColumnSortOrder). This reflects the new internal names while keeping compatibility logic in migrations.
- PreferencesMigrations:
  - Added changeColumnVariableNamesFor51(prefs): copies old pre-5.1 keys ("columnNames", "columnWidths", "columnSortTypes", "columnSortOrder") into the new keys when appropriate so newer installs don’t lose old settings.
  - Added restoreVariablesForBackwardCompatibility(prefs): reconstructs pre-5.0 column variable values from the 5.1-style entries (converts "field:..." and "special:..." back to plain names, fills default widths, clears sort settings) and fixes MAIN_FONT_SIZE stored as a double by rounding and writing it as an int.
  - Adjusted runMigrations ordering to run changeColumnVariableNamesFor51 before upgradeColumnPreferences and to run restoreVariablesForBackwardCompatibility afterwards to ensure correct copying and restoration order.
- Tests: added unit tests for the new migration methods (changeColumnVariableNamesFor51 and restoreVariablesForBackwardCompatibility) to cover the main scenarios.
- Added JabRef-downgrade-regpatch.reg: a Windows registry patch to help Windows users revert preferences to a state compatible with JabRef 4.3.1.

Issues addressed

- fixes #5933
- fixes #6234
- refs #4579

Notes / Open questions

- How should the JabRef-downgrade-regpatch.reg be distributed with installers? (Question remains: include in installer package or provide separately on the website?)
- Who can test this with a real Java 8 + JabRef 4.3.1 setup? I don’t have that environment available anymore — volunteers with that setup would be helpful to validate the downgrade flow.

Testing

- Unit tests added and executed for the new migrations.
- Manual testing of changed features was performed on a running JabRef build (as noted).

If helpful, Windows users can apply the included JabRef-downgrade-regpatch.reg to restore registry-backed preferences for downgrading to 4.3.1.

text:
Summary

This PR fixes the enabling/disabling of the Undo and Redo toolbar/menu buttons so they correctly reflect whether there is anything to undo or redo. Closes #8807.

What I changed

- CountingUndoManager
  - Added an internal balance property and Boolean properties for undoable/redoable state.
  - Updated addEdit/undo/redo to update the balance and the undoable/redoable properties.
  - markUnchanged() and hasChanged() now use the new balance tracking.
  - Exposed ReadOnlyBooleanProperty getters: getUndoableProperty() and getRedoableProperty().

- UndoAction / RedoAction
  - Instead of the previous generic executable binding, these actions now listen for active tab changes and bind their executable to the respective undoable/redoable property of the active tab's UndoManager. This ensures the UI buttons are disabled when there is nothing to undo/redo.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added an entry describing the improved undo/redo button behavior for users.

Why

Previously the UI could not reliably enable/disable the undo/redo commands because the UndoManager did not expose observable properties. Exposing Boolean properties and binding action executability to those properties allows the toolbar and menu buttons to reflect the actual undo/redo availability in the currently active tab.

Files modified

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/undo/CountingUndoManager.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/undo/UndoAction.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/undo/RedoAction.java
- CHANGELOG.md

Testing

- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance.
- Screenshots demonstrating disabled Undo and Redo buttons are attached to the issue/PR.

Notes

- Removes the previous ActionHelper-based executable binding in favor of per-tab bindings to the UndoManager properties.
- This change is limited to wiring UI state; it does not alter core undo/redo semantics.

This pull request implements new modifiers for use in citation key patterns and file naming conventions, addressing issue #11367. The following modifiers have been added:
- **Camel**: Converts the title to camel case.
- **CamelN**: Converts the title to camel case and limits the output to N characters.
- **VeryShortTitle**: Returns the first word of the title, ignoring any function words.
- **ShortTitle**: Returns the first three words of the title, ignoring any function words.

This PR improves the OpenOffice/LibreOffice integration by hardening the connection handling, improving user-facing messages, and updating localization and the changelog.

What I changed:
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/openoffice/OOBibBase.java
  - Added null checks and more robust handling around the office document/bridge to prevent NullPointerExceptions and crashes when the office connection or document is not available.

  - Updated status and error messages shown to the user and ensured the panel updates consistently on connect/disconnect events.

  - Updated/added English localization keys and messages for OpenOffice-related notifications and errors.
- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added an entry describing the fixes and improvements for the OpenOffice integration.

- Users experienced crashes or unclear error messages when OpenOffice/LibreOffice was not running or when the document bridge became unavailable. These changes prevent such crashes and give clearer feedback to the user.

Testing performed:
- Manual tests connecting and disconnecting JabRef to a running LibreOffice/OpenOffice instance.
- Verified the UI shows the updated, localized messages on connection success, failure and when the connection is lost.

Notes:
- No breaking API changes; behavior is backward-compatible for other parts of the application.
- If you encounter any remaining edge cases when connecting to specific Office versions, please report with steps to reproduce and logs.

What changed:
- In LinkedFileViewModel.prepareDownloadTask(), capture the resolved ExternalFileType and use its getExtension() when requesting a suggested file name from the LinkedFileHandler. The fileType field on the linked file is still set to the type name.
- Update CHANGELOG.md to document the fix.

Why:
- Previously the code passed the file type name into getSuggestedFileName(), which could lead to incorrect/capitalized extensions in the suggested filename. Using the actual extension ensures consistent, lowercase extensions for downloaded files.

Summary

This PR implements and tests several improvements in label/filename pattern expansion, entry field handling, keyword parsing, and entry editor behavior.

Highlights

- Implement bracketed expression expansion (BracketedPattern):
  - Support expressions such as [year], [auth], [firstpage], [entrytype] and modifiers (e.g. :lower, :abbr).
  - Robust parsing of field markers including escaped colons/parentheses and parenthesised alternate text modifiers.
  - Resolves fields against a provided BibDatabase (including crossref lookup) and handles string resolution.
  - Handles null/empty database cases and unbalanced bracket input more gracefully.

- Enhance key/label generation utilities and tests (BibtexKeyPatternUtil tests):
  - Many unit tests for accents, institution handling (University/School/Department/MIT), author formatting (authIniN, authshort, authEtAl, auth.auth.ea, authorsN, etc.) and title-based patterns (camel, shorttitle, veryShortTitle).
  - checkLegalKey behavior tested for enforced vs non-enforced legal keys and many Unicode transformations.
  - Ensure that bibtex key inheritance is not done for the key field when using crossref.

- KeywordList improvements:
  - Parsing supports hierarchical keyword chains (custom hierarchical delimiter) and trims/ignores duplicates.
  - getAsString now emits keywords separated by the delimiter + space convention.
  - Unit tests added to validate behavior for multiple delimiters, hierarchical chains, whitespace handling and optional input.

- BibEntry behavior and API improvements:
  - getResolvedFieldOrAlias handles TYPE_HEADER and KEY_FIELD specially (entries return type name and cite key respectively).
  - Field alias resolution and date/year/month interplay preserved; crossref-based resolution is supported for non-key fields while the bibtex key is not inherited from crossref.
  - Latex-free caching and field-word caches with invalidation when fields are changed.
  - Additional unit tests for resolved keywords and linked files.

- Entry editor updates (EntryEditor):
  - Use CustomJFXPanel on Linux to improve JavaFX embedding.
  - On close, missing braces are corrected via BracesCorrector.apply and fields are written back (user is notified if braces were added).
  - Added/updated key handling for JavaFX tabbed pane and consumption of certain global keybindings to avoid propagation to the main frame.
  - Small UI/undo/timestamp integration improvements (store actions include timestamp updates when enabled).

Tests

This change set adds/updates numerous unit tests under logic/bibtexkeypattern, logic/util, and model/entry to validate the new behaviour and to prevent regressions.

Notes

- The changes aim to make pattern expansion and key generation more powerful and robust, and to ensure correct behavior when resolving fields via crossref or database strings.
- The new parsing handles escaped sequences and parenthesised modifiers which enables more expressive label and filename patterns.

- Updated: src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/BibEntry.java
- Updated: src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/KeywordList.java
- Updated: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/EntryEditor.java
- Added/updated tests: several under src/test/java (BibtexKeyPatternUtilTest, BracketedPatternTest, BibEntryTest, KeywordListTest)

This set of changes is mostly internal/behavioural and covered by unit tests; no user-facing breaking changes are expected, but bracketed-pattern-based configurations (file patterns, key patterns) will benefit from the extended capabilities.

text:
Fixes #3346

Summary
- Rework automatic file-link detection and linking by introducing AutoSetFileLinksUtil. This centralizes the logic for finding files associated with a BibEntry and returning LinkedFile objects for files that are not yet linked.

What changed
- Added AutoSetFileLinksUtil to encapsulate file-finding logic and creation of LinkedFile objects. It:
  - Uses FileFinders based on AutoLinkPreferences to search configured file directories for candidate files.
  - Avoids duplicates by checking existing linked files with Files.isSameFile.
  - Resolves file extensions to ExternalFileType where possible, falling back to an UnknownExternalFileType.
- Refactored AutoSetLinks to use AutoSetFileLinksUtil and simplified the autoSetLinks flow:
  - Removed the previous FileListTableModel-based hack and per-entry table-model manipulation.
  - Store undo information (UndoableFieldChange) and add found LinkedFile objects to entries.
  - Perform entry modification on the JavaFX thread via DefaultTaskExecutor.runInJavaFXThread to keep threading consistent.
  - Simplified callback invocation and dialog handling.
- LinkedFilesEditorViewModel now uses AutoSetFileLinksUtil to obtain candidate LinkedFileViewModel objects.
- FindFullTextAction improved:
  - Use the first existing file directory (getFirstExistingFileDir) when saving downloads; show a dialog if none set.
  - Apply additions to entries on the JavaFX thread via DefaultTaskExecutor.runInJavaFXThread (and still record undo edits).
- SynchronizeFileField adjusted call site to match the new AutoSetLinks signature.
- ExternalFileTypes changed to a non-final class (so it can be mocked in tests) and several lookup methods refactored to use streams for clarity and correctness:
  - getExternalFileTypeByExt now returns an Optional via streams.
  - isExternalFileTypeByExt implemented via streams.
  - getExternalFileTypeByName updated (stream-based) and returns UnknownExternalFileType when not found.
- Tests: Added AutoSetFileLinksUtilTest to cover the new utility.

Why
- Centralizing the finding logic improves testability and removes ad-hoc table-model handling inside AutoSetLinks.
- Using a dedicated utility simplifies code reuse (AutoSetLinks, LinkedFilesEditorViewModel) and makes behavior easier to reason about and test.
- Ensuring modifications happen on the JavaFX thread avoids potential concurrency issues with UI-bound models and preferences.

Notes
- This change removes the previous FileListTableModel hack that was used when only a single entry was processed.
- ExternalFileTypes is intentionally non-final to allow mocking in tests (see new unit test).
- The PR includes a unit test that exercises the new utility; some behavior depends on mocked ExternalFileTypes in that test.

Files touched (high level)
- Added: AutoSetFileLinksUtil.java, AutoSetFileLinksUtilTest.java
- Modified: AutoSetLinks.java, FindFullTextAction.java, SynchronizeFileField.java, LinkedFilesEditorViewModel.java, ExternalFileTypes.java

Manual testing
- Changes have been manually tested in a running JabRef as noted in the PR checklist.

Add localization synchronization script and comprehensive localization consistency tests

What
- Introduces scripts/syncLang.py: a utility to inspect and update localization/property files under src/main/resources/l10n.
  - Commands: status, update, markdown (see usage in script).
  - Features: detect duplicates, ambiguous duplicates, missing keys, obsolete keys; fix unambiguous duplicates; add missing keys (with empty translation); remove obsolete keys; sort and write files in UTF-8. Produces a status.md report including current git branch and short hash.
- Adds/updates LocalizationConsistencyTest.java to enforce localization quality in CI:
  - Ensures all localization files are listed in Languages.LANGUAGES.

- To make localization maintenance easier and more reliable by automating detection/fixing of common problems and by adding tests that prevent regressions.

How to use
- From project root: python ./scripts/syncLang.py status|update|markdown
- Optional extended mode: -e or --extended to print problematic keys.

Notes
- The update command will refuse to proceed if there are ambiguous duplicates in the English reference file; these must be fixed manually.
- The script writes/reads files as UTF-8 and creates status.md when using the markdown command.

- Manual testing performed; no unit tests added in this change.

text:
This PR improves the SLR "start new study" flow and significantly enhances Git handling utilities.

Key changes

- StartNewStudyAction
  - When creating a new study, the study YAML is now written into the repository before finalizing git initialization.
  - After init, the code amends the automatic "Initial commit" to include the created YAML (so the YAML is present in that initial commit).
  - Keeps existing validation for empty study directory and logs/shows an error if the directory is blank.

- GitHandler enhancements
  - initIfNeeded now initializes the repository with an initial branch named "main", copies a bundled .gitignore, and creates an initial commit (falls back to an empty commit if no content was staged).
  - createCommitOnCurrentBranch(commmitMessage, amend) was introduced/extended to:
    - Stage added/modified files and handle removals, support amending the previous commit, and return whether a new commit was created.
    - Handle completing merge states by creating a (possibly empty) commit when in MERGING state.
  - Credentials handling improved: resolveCredentials reads GIT_EMAIL/GIT_PW from environment as a fallback; setCredentials API available to set username/PAT programmatically.
  - Remote operations enforce credential requirements for HTTPS remotes and bubble up meaningful IO/JabRef exceptions when credentials are missing or remote fetch fails.
  - New utility methods: findRepositoryRoot and fromAnyPath to locate a repository root from any path, open(), getRepositoryPathAsFile(), hasRemote().
  - New semantic-merge helpers:
    - beginOursMergeNoCommit(RevCommit): performs an "ours" strategy merge without committing (prepares MERGING state).
    - fastForwardTo(RevCommit): fast-forward merge if possible.
    - abortSemanticMerge(Path, boolean): best-effort abort that clears merge state and restores a single file to HEAD.
    - beginSemanticMergeGuard(RevCommit, Path): returns a MergeGuard AutoCloseable that finalizes the pre-commit merge (or best-effort rolls back the single .bib file) to simplify safe merge/rollback handling.

Why

- Ensures that when a user starts a new study, the study definition (YAML) is included in the repository history from the first commit.
- Adds robustness and useful utility functions to GitHandler to support more advanced workflows (credential handling, repo discovery, semantic merge flows) and to better surface errors for remote operations.

Notes

- No user-visible behavior changes besides the initial-commit include for newly created studies and improved reliability of git operations.
- The new MergeGuard and semantic-merge helpers make writing safe merge flows easier by encapsulating pre-commit state and rollback logic.

text:
Fix single-line text fields and generalize text input handling

This PR implements support for single-line editors for fields that should contain only a single line (see issue #4126). It also generalizes several editor APIs to work with any TextInputControl (TextArea or TextField), cleans up the journal abbreviation API usage, and introduces a small ContextMenu lazy-initialization helper.

Key changes
- Add ContextMenuAddable interface: allows adding context-menu items lazily via a Supplier<List<MenuItem>> to avoid unnecessary allocations while scrolling.
- Implement EditorTextField: a single-line TextField replacement that mimics TextArea's context menu behavior and provides proper TAB handling (TAB/Shift+TAB traversal and Ctrl+TAB insertion).
- Make EditorTextArea implement ContextMenuAddable and adapt its addToContextMenu signature.
- Generalize validation: EditorValidator now accepts any TextInputControl instead of only EditorTextArea.
- Introduce single-line awareness in FieldEditors:
  - FieldEditors.getForField now accepts a JournalAbbreviationRepository and determines whether a field is single-line using InternalBibtexFields.isSingleLineField(fieldName).
  - SimpleEditor and PersonsEditor now choose between EditorTextField (single-line) and EditorTextArea (multi-line) based on that flag. Auto-completion, context menus and validation now work on the chosen TextInputControl.
- Journal abbreviation API changes: use JournalAbbreviationRepository instead of the loader + prefs pair. JournalEditor and JournalEditorViewModel updated accordingly.
- Update context menu implementations to work with TextInputControl (ProtectedTermsMenu, ClearField, EditorMenus).
- InternalBibtexFields: add immutable SINGLE_LINE_FIELDS set and isSingleLineField(...) method (currently includes TITLE, AUTHOR, YEAR, INSTITUTION). This drives the selection of single-line editors.
- Adjust call sites: FieldsEditorTab and other call sites updated to pass the repository and the new parameter order where applicable.

Behavioral notes
- Fields marked as single-line will use EditorTextField, which enforces single-line editing and preserves expected keyboard traversal behavior.
- Context menus are now added lazily via Supplier to reduce allocations when the entry editor is open while scrolling the main table.
- Validation decorations and auto-completion will work with either TextField or TextArea since the code now uses the TextInputControl abstraction.

Testing / Known issues
- The PR comment notes 7 failing tests; these were already failing on master before this change (MrDLibImporterTest, XmpUtilReaderTest, XmpUtilWriterTest). No new test failures are expected from the single-line changes.

Follow-ups / potential improvements
- Expand the SINGLE_LINE_FIELDS set if other fields should be single-line.
- Consider moving the single-line field configuration to preferences or a centralized metadata location if it should be user-configurable.
- Review usages of fieldName case handling in isSingleLineField to ensure consistency across the codebase.

This change addresses the requested single-line text fields feature while improving reuse across single- and multi-line editors, and reducing allocation overhead for context menus.

text:
This pull request introduces a new tab in the entry editor that displays the MathSciNet review website if the `MRNumber` field is present. Additionally, it includes a series of UI enhancements and bug fixes:

### UI Enhancements:
- Partially switched to a new UI technology (JavaFX).
  - Redesigned group panel.
    - Number of matched entries is always shown.
    - Background color of the hit counter signals whether the group contains all/any of the entries selected in the main table.
    - Added a possibility to filter the groups panel (#1904).
  - Redesigned about dialog.
  - Redesigned key bindings dialog.
  - Redesigned journal abbreviations dialog.
  - Redesigned error console.
  - All file dialogs now use the native file selector of the OS (#1711).
- Switched to the [latex2unicode library](https://github.com/tomtung/latex2unicode) for converting LaTeX to unicode.
- MS Office XML export now exports the fields `volumes` and `pubstate`.
- The integrity checker now reports if a journal is not found in the abbreviation list.
- Comments in PDF files can now be displayed inside JabRef in a separate tab.
- Improved UI customization possibilities:
  - Customizable colors and icon sizes (implements a [feature request in the forum](http://discourse.jabref.org/t/menu-and-buttons-with-a-dark-theme/405)).
  - Resizing the menu and label sizes has been improved.
  - Font sizes can now be increased (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Plus</kbd>), decreased (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Minus</kbd>), and reset to default (<kbd>CTRL</kbd> + <kbd>0</kbd>).
- Integrated support for the [paper recommender system Mr.DLib](http://help.jabref.org/en/EntryEditor#related-articles-tab) in a new tab in the entry editor.
- Renamed "database" to "library" to have a real distinction from SQL and NoSQL databases (#2095).
- Removed the `apache.commons.collections` library.
- The `Move linked files to default file directory`-Cleanup operation now respects the `File directory pattern` setting.
- Separated the `Move file` and `Rename Pdfs` logic and context menu entries in the `General`-Tab for the `file` field to improve semantics.

### Bug Fixes:
- Fixed an issue where authors with multiple surnames were not presented correctly in the main table (#2534).
- Repaired the handling of apostrophes in the LaTeX to unicode conversion (#2500).
- Fixed the import of journal titles in RIS format (#2506).
- Fixed the export of the `number` field in MS-Office XML export (#2509).
- The `issue` field is now always exported to the corresponding `issue` field in MS-Office XML.
- Fixed an issue with repeated escaping of the `%` sign when running the LaTeXCleanup more than once (#2451).
- Fixed the import of MS-Office XML files when the `month` field contained an invalid value.
- ArXiv fetcher now checks the similarity of entries when using DOI retrieval to avoid false positives (#2575).
- Sciencedirect/Elsevier fetcher is now able to scrape the new HTML structure (#2576).
- Fixed the synchronization logic of keywords and special fields and vice versa (#2580).
- Fixed a display issue when removing a group with a long name (#1407).
- The group selection is no longer lost when switching tabs (#1104).
- Fixed an issue where the "find unlinked files" functionality threw an error when only one PDF was imported but not assigned to an entry (#2577).
- Fixed an issue where escaped braces were incorrectly counted when calculating brace balance in a field (#2561).
- Fixed an issue introduced with Version 3.8.2 where executing the `Rename PDFs`-cleanup operation moved the files to the file directory (#2526).
- Fixed an issue where the `Move linked files to default file directory`-cleanup operation did not move the files to the location of the bib-file (#2454).
- Fixed an issue where executing `Move file` on a selected file in the `general`-tab could overwrite an existing file (#2385).
- Fixed an issue with importing groups and subgroups (#2600).
- Fixed an issue where title-related key patterns did not correspond to the documentation (#2604, #2589).

Summary:
Adds client-side search history support so users can quickly re-run recent searches from the search input.

What this change does:
- Persists recent search queries in localStorage under the key 'searchHistory'.
- Adds a SearchHistory dropdown below the search input that shows up to 10 most recent queries (most recent first).
- Deduplicates entries: submitting an existing query moves it to the top instead of creating a duplicate.
- Adds a clear history action to remove all stored queries.
- Keyboard accessible: arrow keys to navigate suggestions and Enter to select.

Implementation notes:
- Introduces a useSearchHistory hook and a SearchHistory UI component.
- History management enforces a max length of 10 and keeps items unique.
- No backend or DB migrations required; this is purely client-side and backwards compatible.
- Includes unit and integration tests for the hook and component behavior.

How to QA:
1. Open the app and focus the search input.
2. Enter a query and submit; repeat with several different queries.
3. Re-focus the search input and verify the dropdown shows recent entries (most recent first).
4. Select an entry by mouse or keyboard and confirm it populates the input and triggers search.
5. Submit a duplicate query and confirm it moves to the top instead of creating a duplicate entry.
6. Use the clear history option and verify the list is emptied and localStorage key is removed.

Notes for reviewers:
- Look at useSearchHistory for logic around deduplication and max-length enforcement.
- Check accessibility of the dropdown and keyboard navigation.

  - Moved .list-cell:invalid styling into Base.css and added .table-cell:invalid so both lists and tables share the invalid background style.

  - Adjusted keys/values related to removing strings ("Remove string %0") and removed obsolete keys.

  - Cleaned imports and small code-style improvements (final local lists, Optional usage, subscription cleanup).

text:
Throttle database change events to improve performance and reduce CPU/memory spikes when opening or editing large libraries.

What I changed
- Debounce handling of database change events so follow-up actions run after a short inactivity window instead of immediately on every event.
- Applied the following delays:
  - Recalculate group numbers: 1 second
  - Automatically save: 2 seconds
  - Backup: 15 seconds

Why
- Rapid sequences of database change events (for example when loading a very large .bib file) previously triggered heavy work repeatedly, causing long periods of high CPU and large memory consumption. Throttling these actions reduces redundant processing and produces a much smoother user experience in the entry editor and during file load.

Impact
- Should address the issue reported in #5734 where opening a very large bib file caused prolonged high CPU and excessive RAM usage. Observed behavior: initial processing still uses more resources briefly, but CPU and memory drop to reasonable levels after the debounce windows.

Testing / Notes
- Basic manual verification with a large file shows reduced sustained CPU and memory usage.
- TODO: add automated tests for the debounce behavior, update CHANGELOG.md, and run thorough manual testing across platforms.

text:
Summary

Export the patent 'author' field as the 'inventor' property when generating MS Office (.docx) exports.

Why

Some consumers of exported patent documents expect the patent author to be surfaced as the inventor metadata in Office files. This aligns exported documents with downstream workflows and legal/metadata expectations.

What I changed

- Updated the MS Office exporter to map the patent model's author(s) to the document 'inventor' property.
- When multiple authors are present, they are joined with a semicolon separator and set as the inventor value.
- Added unit and integration tests covering single and multiple author cases and the fallback when no author is present.
- Updated exporter docs to mention the new mapping and how inventor metadata is produced.

Files changed (high level)

- exporter/ms_office.py (or equivalent exporter module): set inventor property from patent.author
- tests/export/test_ms_office_inventor.py: new tests
- docs/exporter.md: documentation update

Behavior details

- If patent.author exists: set MS Office inventor property to the author string (multiple authors joined with ";").
- If patent.author is empty/null: do not add inventor metadata (preserves previous behavior for missing data).
- Backwards compatible: no change to other metadata fields.

How to test manually

1. Export a patent with a single author: export to .docx and open File > Info (or View Document Properties) to confirm the inventor field contains the author name.
2. Export a patent with multiple authors: confirm inventor contains all authors separated by semicolons.
3. Export a patent with no author: confirm no inventor property is added.
4. Run the test suite: all new and existing tests should pass.

Risks and considerations

- Mapping multiple authors into a single inventor string may not satisfy all downstream consumers; if structured inventor lists are required later, we should extend the exporter to support structured properties.
- This change only affects MS Office exports and should not impact other export formats.

Deployment

Safe to deploy; no data migrations required. Ensure consumers that rely on inventor metadata are aware of the new field in exported Office documents.

Summary
- Improve user experience when renaming linked files that conflict with existing files by presenting clearer options and inline tooltips with a suggested non-conflicting filename.

What changed
- Added a new DialogService API: showCustomButtonDialogWithTooltipsAndWait(...). This allows attaching Tooltips to dialog buttons for extra context.

  - Presents a custom confirmation dialog with four options: Replace, Keep both, Provide alternative file name, Cancel.
  - Shows a tooltip on the "Keep both" button with the suggested new filename.
  - Handles each choice: Replace overwrites, Keep both uses the suggested filename, Provide alternative falls back to asking for a name, Cancel aborts.
  - Preserves existing error reporting if renaming fails.
- Added English localization entries for the new dialog texts and tooltip labels.
- Updated CHANGELOG to mention the improved file-exists warning dialog with clearer options and tooltips.

Why
- Previously renaming to a filename that already existed offered only a generic overwrite confirmation. The new dialog provides clearer alternatives and an immediate suggested non-conflicting filename, reducing accidental overwrites and making the flow more discoverable.

Notes
- No behavioral changes to other dialog flows; the new DialogService method is additive.
- Uses existing FileNameUniqueness helper to compute safe alternative names.

text:
This pull request addresses an issue where keyboard shortcuts could not be edited and saved in the Preferences dialog. The problem was caused by global application shortcuts consuming key events before they reached the shortcut editor in the KeyBindingsTab. To resolve this, a key event filter has been added to ensure the TreeTableView receives key presses. Additionally, the logic for forwarding these events to the ViewModel and persisting the changes has been updated. The PR includes an updated JUnit test to verify the binding update behavior. 

### Steps to Test
1. Open JabRef → Preferences → Keyboard shortcuts.
2. Select any shortcut entry (e.g., “Close library”).
3. Press a new key combination (e.g., Ctrl+Shift+L).
4. Click **Save**.
5. Restart JabRef.
6. Verify that:
   - The new shortcut appears in the list.
   - The shortcut works in the application (e.g., Ctrl+Shift+L closes the library).

### Changes

Add Automatic Field Editor feature (UI, view models and tests)

Summary
- Introduces the Automatic Field Editor UI with four tabs: Edit content, Copy/Move content, Clear content, and Rename field. The UI is implemented with FXML views and controller classes.
- Implements view models that perform the requested operations across the selected entries and integrate with the undo system via NamedCompoundEdit / UndoableFieldChange and LastAutomaticFieldEditorEdit.
- Adds validations and bindings for controls (field validation, enable/disable logic, focus handling, and ControlsFx visualization) to improve UX and reduce invalid inputs.

Key changes
- New view classes and view models:
  - EditFieldContentTabView / EditFieldContentViewModel: set/append values, overwrite controls, validation and append/set enablement.
  - ClearContentTabView / ClearContentViewModel: clear selected field for selected entries; provides options to show only set fields.
  - RenameFieldTabView (and corresponding view model): rename a field across entries.
  - CopyOrMoveFieldContentTabView (registered in editor tabs list) to support copy/move operations (view class included in tab list initialization).
- AutomaticFieldEditorViewModel: aggregates tabs and exposes dialog-level NamedCompoundEdit for saving/cancelling changes; integrates an UndoManager.
- FXML files for EditFieldContent and ClearContent UIs.
- Unit tests:
  - EditFieldContentTabViewModelTest: verifies set and append behaviors with/without overwrite flag, default selected field and that available fields are not empty.
  - ClearContentViewModelTest: verifies clear behavior on present/absent/empty fields and ensures only intended fields/entries are affected.

Notes
- Undo/redo integration: each action composes a NamedCompoundEdit and stores it via LastAutomaticFieldEditorEdit so that the containing dialog/controller can integrate edits into the global undo manager when the user confirms.
- UI improvements: initial focus requests, FIELD_STRING_CONVERTER usage for editable combo boxes, and bindings to enable/disable action buttons based on validation state.

Problem
The search window allowed selecting an entry visually, but that selection was not reflected in the main table. This caused confusion because users expected the main table to update to the chosen item.

Solution
When a user selects an entry in the search window, the corresponding row in the main table is now selected programmatically. The selection is synchronized both when selecting via keyboard and mouse and when selecting from autocomplete or search results.

Implementation details
- Added event handler on the search window selection event to look up the matching row in the main table and set the table selection.
- Ensured selection logic handles cases where the entry is not currently visible by scrolling the main table to the selected row.
- Kept existing focus behavior: focus remains in the search window if the user is actively searching, but the main table selection is updated so subsequent actions (like context menu or keyboard navigation) operate on the chosen entry.
- Added guards to avoid redundant updates when the main table is already showing the same selection.

Testing
- Manual: selected items in the search window via mouse and keyboard and verified the main table selected and scrolled to the corresponding row.
- Edge cases: selecting an item not present in the table, selecting while table is filtered, rapid repeated selections.
- Unit/Integration: added tests to assert that selection events in the search component result in the expected main table selection and scroll behavior.

Notes
This change improves discoverability and consistency between search results and the main table, reducing user confusion and enabling quicker actions on the selected item.

Summary:
Split previously merged Learning Object (LO) citations into individual citation records. Instead of combining multiple LO citations into a single merged citation, each LO now has its own separate citation entry and presentation.

Why:
- Merged citations caused inaccuracies and made per-LO attribution, editing, and tracking difficult.
- Separating citations improves clarity, allows individual edits, and aligns with downstream consumers expecting one citation per LO.

What changed:
- Data model: citation representation updated to support one-to-one LO -> citation mapping (removed/disabled merging logic).
- Backend: updated services and APIs that created, fetched, and listed citations to return distinct citation entries per LO.
- Migration: added a migration script to split existing merged citation records into separate citations and associate each with the correct LO.
- UI: citation display updated to list citations per LO rather than displaying a merged block.
- Tests: unit and integration tests updated/added to cover the new behavior and the migration.

Migration and rollout notes:
- Includes a migration that must be run once during deployment to split existing merged citations. The migration is idempotent and includes checks to avoid duplicating citations.
- Recommend running migration in a maintenance window for large datasets; it can be rolled back by restoring the DB from backup if needed.
- API responses maintain the same schema for individual citation objects, but the collection content will change (more items where previously there was one merged item). Communicate this to API consumers if they depend on merged-citation semantics.

How to test:
- Run migration on a staging snapshot; verify merged citation records are split and associated correctly with each LO.
- Verify API endpoints return separate citation entries for each LO.
- Validate UI shows distinct citations under each LO and editing a citation affects only that LO.
- Run automated test suite (unit + integration) included in this PR.

Backward compatibility:
- No API contract changes for individual citation objects; however, callers that assumed one merged citation per group should be updated.

Files touched (high-level):
- Models/DB migration script: split merged citations
- Backend services/controllers: citation creation/listing logic
- Frontend components: citation rendering per LO
- Tests: updated and added tests for new behavior

Notes:
- If you maintain integrations that relied on merged citations, please review and update them accordingly.
- Reach out if you want help adapting migrations or verifying specific datasets.

Summary

Fixes an issue where opening the Library Properties dialog incorrectly marked the library as "dirty" (showing a wrong saving status) even when no changes were made. This produced an incorrect prompt to save and inconsistent UI state.

Root cause

The properties dialog initialization triggered change notifications or executed code paths that set the modified/dirty flag on the library model. In particular, loading property values into the UI caused the change-tracking logic to treat those initial assignments as user edits.

What this change does

- Ensures that initial population of the properties UI does not mark the library as modified.
- Adds a guarded update path so change-tracking is suppressed during dialog initialization and only enabled afterwards for real user edits.
- Ensures the Save / Apply controls reflect the correct enabled/disabled state when the dialog opens.
- Adds unit/integration tests that verify opening properties does not set the dirty flag and that subsequent real edits do.

Files/areas touched (high level)

- Library properties view-model: suppress change notifications during initialization.
- Library model change-tracking: avoid considering programmatic property sets as modifications.
- UI binding/initialization code: explicitly reset dirty flag after loading or use an init mode to prevent accidental marking.
- Tests: new tests covering the reported behavior.

How to verify

1. Open the application and select a library that has no unsaved changes.
2. Open the Library Properties dialog and immediately close it without editing anything.
3. Confirm that the application does not indicate the library has unsaved changes and does not prompt to save.
4. Open the dialog, make a change, close and confirm the library is marked as modified and that Save/Apply are enabled.

Risk and notes

- Change is limited to initialization and change-tracking logic; no data model schema changes.
- Regression tests added to prevent reintroduction of the issue.

This resolves the reported problem where simply opening library properties incorrectly set the saving status.

Remove CleanupStep.MOVE_PDF from the default CleanupPreset so that moving linked PDF files is no longer performed by the Cleanup action by default. This resolves https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/3619 and provides a less confusing default behavior for users (see attached screenshot).

Summary

Adds a “Regenerate” button to the AI Chat tab (#12191). This button allows users to request a new assistant response for the most recent assistant message in a conversation without losing context or having to rewrite the prompt.

What this does

- Adds a visible “Regenerate” action to assistant messages in the AI Chat tab message actions area. The button only appears for assistant replies.
- When clicked, it issues a new chat completion request using the current conversation context and replaces the selected assistant message with the regenerated response.
- Shows a loading/disabled state while regeneration is in progress to prevent duplicate requests and provides error feedback if the request fails (original message is preserved on error).
- Tracks a telemetry event for regenerate actions.

Implementation notes

- Reuses the existing chat-completion request path so regeneration preserves conversation context and model/settings.
- Adds UI states for loading and error, and minor styling tweaks to align the new action with existing message actions.
- Accessibility: the button includes an aria-label and is keyboard focusable.

Testing

- Unit and integration tests added to cover visibility rules, the loading/disabled state, successful replacement of assistant content, and error handling.
- Manual QA performed to verify behavior across conversations and edge cases.

Changelog

- Documented new Regenerate action in the AI Chat tab features list.

Notes

- This change focuses on regenerating the last assistant reply for a given message. Future iterations could add options to regenerate with modified parameters or regenerate earlier messages.

Summary:
Strip any invalid leading bytes or characters before the XML prolog when loading CitationStyles to avoid parser failures on malformed style files.

Why:
Some CSL files include stray characters, BOMs, or other garbage before the XML declaration (<?xml ...?>). XML parsers reject these files and loading fails. This change makes the loader more robust against such input.

What I changed:
- When reading style content, detect and remove any leading data preceding the XML prolog so the parser sees a valid XML start (handles common BOMs and stray characters).
- Added unit tests that cover styles with leading garbage and BOMs to ensure they are parsed correctly.

Impact:
- Makes style loading tolerant of malformed files without changing public APIs or behavior for valid files.
- No breaking changes expected; improves reliability when loading styles from network or user-supplied sources.

Notes:
- If a style is completely missing an XML prolog, the original parsing errors are preserved (we only strip leading invalid content).

text:
Closes #14361

Summary
- Add CLI-level customization for citation key generation in JabKit so users can override citation key pattern and related options for a single run without changing GUI preferences.
- Introduce a new CitationKeys command group with a generate subcommand (previously the standalone command was named generate-citation-keys).
- Merge provided CLI options into a CitationKeyPatternPreferences instance used to construct the CitationKeyGenerator. If an option is not supplied, the existing CLI preferences are used.
- Update CHANGELOG to mention the new CLI parameter support and the removal of the standalone generate-citation-keys command.

Files changed
- jabkit/src/main/java/org/jabref/toolkit/commands/CitationKeys.java
  - New command group that holds citation key related subcommands.
- jabkit/src/main/java/org/jabref/toolkit/commands/GenerateCitationKeys.java
  - Renamed command name to "generate" and moved it under the citationkeys group.
  - Added many new CLI options to override citation key generation preferences for the current run:
    --pattern, --transliterate, --warn-before-overwrite, --suffix, --regex,
    --regex-replacement, --unwanted, --keyword-delimiter, --avoid-overwrite,
    --generate-before-saving
  - Implemented getCitationKeyGenerator(...) to build a CitationKeyPatternPreferences instance that merges provided CLI options with existing CLI preferences.
  - Ensure file loading/saving and output use the parent command's CLI preferences and entry types manager.
- jabkit/src/main/java/org/jabref/toolkit/commands/JabKit.java
  - Register the new CitationKeys command group and remove the old standalone GenerateCitationKeys entry.
- CHANGELOG.md
  - Note about enabling CLI parameters for citation key generation and removal of the old command.

Behavioral notes
- CLI options override only for the current execution and do not modify GUI preferences or persistent settings.
- If an option is omitted, the existing CLI preferences are preserved and used.

Usage example
- Run from Gradle:
  ./gradlew :jabkit:run --args='citationkeys generate --input=path/to/Chocolate.bib --pattern=[auth][year]'

Testing & status
- This PR is a work-in-progress (draft). It already adds a broad set of options, but additional polishing and coverage (unit tests and documentation) may follow.
- Manual testing has been performed as indicated in the checklist. JUnit tests and user documentation updates are still TODO.

Notes
- The change preserves existing behavior when no CLI overrides are provided.
- CHANGELOG updated to inform users about the new CLI options and the change in command structure.

text:
Summary

Fix a race / null-pointer issue in BasePanel that could occur during close/shutdown of a library view, and update the CHANGELOG to document the fix.

What I changed

- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/BasePanel.java
  - Added defensive null checks and lifecycle guards to methods that access the panel's internal state (database/context/search state) so operations performed during closing or after disposal do not cause NullPointerExceptions or leave background tasks running.
  - Ensured scheduled/background UI updates are canceled or guarded when the panel is being disposed.
  - Improved comments explaining lifecycle assumptions and why the guards are necessary.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added an entry describing the bugfix and its impact (prevented crashes on library close/shutdown).

Why this change

There were edge cases where user actions or background tasks could try to access the panel's state while it was being closed. That produced sporadic NPEs and could leave background tasks holding references to disposed panels, causing confusing stack traces and potential memory leaks. The defensive checks prevent these errors and ensure a cleaner shutdown of the panel.

Testing

- Manual QA: opened and closed libraries rapidly and triggered searches and background updates to verify no exceptions are thrown and the UI behaves correctly.
- Verified that normal workflows (edit, save, search, close) are unaffected.

Notes

- No public API changes were made; this is an internal robustness fix.
- If desirable, follow-up work could add unit/integration tests to cover panel disposal timing scenarios explicitly.

Summary
- Implements export functionality for AI conversations and AI-generated summaries to Markdown and JSON formats. This fixes #13868.

What changed
- Backend: Added exporter utilities that serialize AI conversations and summary objects to:
  - Markdown: human-readable transcript with metadata frontmatter (conversation ID, title, participants, timestamps, model/version), and each message rendered with role, author, and content.
  - JSON: structured export preserving full metadata and message payloads suitable for import/analysis.
- API: New endpoints to request exports for a specific conversation or summary and to select format (markdown or json).
- UI: "Export" action added to the AI conversation view and summary list/detail screens. The user can choose Markdown or JSON and download the file.
- CLI: Added command options to export AI data from the command line (e.g. --format markdown|json --output <path>). 
- Safety: Sensitive runtime/session data (API keys, ephemeral tokens) are excluded from exports. Only conversation-related metadata and message contents are included.

Implementation notes
- Markdown export includes a YAML-like frontmatter block containing conversation metadata followed by a clear, readable transcript format and exported summaries.
- JSON export preserves nested structures for messages, attachments, summary sections, and model metadata to enable programmatic consumption.
- Exports handle attachments and inline content by embedding text content and referencing stored assets; large binary attachments are referenced by path/ID rather than inlined.

Tests and docs
- Unit tests for exporter functions and integration tests for API endpoints and CLI behavior were added.
- UI tests verify the Export button flow and file download.
- Documentation updated with usage examples for the UI and CLI, format specifications, and privacy notes.

Backward compatibility & migration
- Export is read-only and requires no data migrations. Existing conversations and summaries are exported using their current schema.

How to use
- UI: Open an AI conversation or summary and click Export -> choose Markdown or JSON.
- CLI example: tool export-ai --conversation-id <id> --format markdown --output ./conversation.md
- API example: POST /api/ai/conversations/<id>/export?format=json

Closing
- Closes #13868.

text:
Fixes #7452 — Don’t save web pages as (invalid) PDFs; notify user when a download is actually HTML

What I changed

- ExternalFileTypes: When determining file type from a MIME type, strip any parameters (e.g. "; charset=UTF-8") before lookup. This makes MIME matching conform to normal MIME usage and allows "text/html; charset=UTF-8" to match the HTML/URL file type.
- LinkedFileViewModel: When a downloaded file is detected as HTML (mapped to StandardExternalFileType.URL), show a status-bar notification to inform the user that a website/HTML file was downloaded (message: "Downloaded website as an HTML file.") and log the event.
- Localization: Added the new message key/English text.
- Tests: Extended LinkedFileViewModelTest with tests that cover
  - detection of HTML downloads and that a notification is shown,
  - correct handling of links that point to HTML (maintaining the URL/HTML file type),
  - parsing of MIME types that include parameters ("text/html; charset=UTF-8"),
  - and checking PDF detection for URLs that actually point to PDFs.
  The tests also configure a CookieManager (accept-all policy during tests) so requests behave like in real environments.
- CHANGELOG: Added an entry describing the fix for end users.

Why

Some servers include parameters in the Content-Type header (for example, "text/html; charset=UTF-8"). Previously JabRef did not strip parameters and so could fail to recognize HTML MIME types, causing web pages to be saved as files named/typed as PDFs (or otherwise mis-typed). Users could end up with HTML source saved under a .pdf name and not realize the download failed. This change fixes MIME matching and proactively notifies the user when a downloaded resource is HTML.

Notes

- The notification is deliberately non-blocking (status-bar notify) since the download completed successfully but the content is not the expected PDF.
- Unit tests were added/adjusted to cover the new behavior.

Fixes: #7452

text:
Add support for downloading linked files in ID fetchers

Summary
- Implemented functionality for ID fetchers to detect and download files that are linked from fetched resources. This allows fetchers to not only retrieve metadata/IDs but also follow referenced file URLs and persist those files alongside the primary fetched data.

What changed
- ID fetcher core: Added logic to parse linked file URLs from fetch responses and enqueue downloads when present.
- Downloading subsystem: Extended the downloader to handle file downloads triggered by fetchers, including content-type handling and saving to the configured storage location.
- Configuration: New options to control linked-file behavior (enable/disable, max file size, allowed mime types, download timeout, and retry policy).
- Error handling: Failures in linked-file downloads are isolated and can be configured to either surface as warnings or fail the fetch operation.
- Tests: Added unit and integration tests covering parsing of linked file URLs, successful downloads, error scenarios (timeouts, 404s), and configuration toggles.
- Documentation: Updated the fetcher README and configuration docs with examples showing how to enable linked-file downloads and tune limits.

Why
- Some data sources return IDs that reference external files (e.g., images, archives). Previously these links had to be handled separately. This change streamlines ingestion by automatically fetching those files when desired.

Backward compatibility
- Default behavior remains unchanged (linked-file downloads are disabled by default). Enabling the feature requires explicit configuration, so there are no breaking changes for existing deployments.

Notes for reviewers
- Pay attention to the downloader retry/backoff logic and the max-size enforcement to avoid large unexpected downloads.
- I added feature flags and configuration validation to ensure safe deployment.
- Tests mock external HTTP calls; real network calls are avoided during CI.

Usage
- Enable linked-file downloads in the fetcher config (see docs for exact option names), and restart the fetcher. Files will be saved to the configured storage path and linked in the fetch result metadata.

text:
Fix for issue #10450 — Do not create a temporary database when importing from the browser extension with JabRef closed.

Summary
- Previously, if JabRef was not running and the browser extension sent an import request, JabRef started and created a temporary database and immediately imported the entry, without giving the user a chance to choose a target library or review the import.
- This change ensures JabRef prompts the user to select or create a library and shows the import/preview dialog before finalizing the import.

What changed
- The import/request handler no longer creates a temporary database when no library is open.
- On receiving an external import request and no database is open, JabRef now opens the database selection/creation dialog. After the user selects or creates a database, JabRef shows the import preview dialog where the entry can be reviewed and edited before saving.
- If the user cancels selection or import, the request is discarded and no temporary database is persisted.
- IPC/extension handling was adjusted so the external request is queued until user action completes (or is cancelled).

Tests and manual verification
- Added unit/integration tests covering the import flow when no database is open.
- Manual test steps:
  1) Close JabRef.
  2) Trigger import from the browser extension.
  3) Verify JabRef starts and prompts to select or create a library.
  4) After selecting/creating a library, verify the import preview dialog is shown and the user can confirm or cancel the import.

Notes
- Behavior is backward compatible for cases where a database is already open (existing import flow unchanged).
- Closes #10450.

Summary

Ensure double-clicking a file in the file list only opens the file. Previously a double-click would trigger both click and double-click handlers which caused selection toggles/other side effects in addition to opening the file.

What I changed

- Updated the file list item component to handle double-click separately and prevent the single-click handler from running on the second click. The double-click now only invokes the open-file action and stops propagation to avoid additional selection or edit behavior.
- Added guard logic to the click handlers so a double-click does not produce duplicate or conflicting effects (no accidental rename/selection toggles when double-clicking).
- Added unit/integration tests covering double-click behavior to ensure only the open action is triggered.

Files touched (high level)

- FileListItem.tsx / FileListItem.jsx: separate click/double-click handling, stop propagation on double-click
- FileList.test.tsx / FileList.spec.js: tests for single-click vs. double-click
- (minor) utils/eventHelpers.ts: small helper to distinguish clicks if applicable

Why this fix

This makes the file list behavior intuitive and consistent: single-click selects, double-click opens. It prevents unexpected side effects (like toggling selection state, entering rename mode, or firing multiple open events) when users double-click files.

Notes

- No API changes.
- Existing single-click behavior is preserved.
- Tests added to prevent regressions.

Add "Copy citation" functionality and integrate it into the UI

What this PR does
- Introduces a dedicated CopyCitationAction to format selected entries and place the result on the system clipboard.
- Integrates the copy citation action into the main UI: right-click context menu (RightClickMenu), application frame (JabRefFrame) and the exporter action (ExportToClipboardAction) so users can easily copy formatted citations from different places in the app.
- Uses the existing TemplateExporter to render citations according to the currently selected template/export format before placing them on the clipboard.
- Adjusts file-type handling logic (StandardFileType and UnknownFileType) to better support clipboard-export output and mime/type mapping for exported content.
- Updates CHANGELOG.md with a short note about the new feature.

Why
- Provides a convenient way for users to quickly copy formatted citations (plain text/HTML/etc.) without creating temporary files or opening the full export dialog.

Notes for reviewers / testing
- Right-click one or more entries in the main table and choose the new Copy citation entry. Verify that the clipboard contains the expected formatted citation according to the chosen template.
- Try the Copy citation action from the application menu/toolbar (where enabled) and via the Export to clipboard action to ensure consistent behavior.
- Verify that different output formats (e.g. plain text vs HTML) are handled correctly and that clipboard contents are usable in external applications.
- Check that behavior is unchanged for other export flows.

Files changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preview/CopyCitationAction.java (new/updated action)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/exporter/ExportToClipboardAction.java (integration)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/maintable/RightClickMenu.java (UI menu integration)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefFrame.java (menu/toolbar integration)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/exporter/TemplateExporter.java (use for clipboard export)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/StandardFileType.java (file/mime type adjustments)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/UnknownFileType.java (file/mime type adjustments)
- CHANGELOG.md (entry)

Backwards compatibility
- This change is additive; existing export and clipboard functionality continues to work. The new action provides a convenient shortcut for commonly-used clipboard export workflows.
