Summary

This PR adds a new error dialog that appears when the application is unable to locate requested files. The dialog is titled "Problem finding files" and gives the user a clear explanation of the issue and options to proceed.

What I changed

- Added a reusable ErrorDialog component for presenting file-finding errors with the title "Problem finding files".
- Wired the dialog into the file discovery / import path so it is shown when the file lookup routine fails (e.g. missing files, inaccessible paths, or I/O errors).
- Dialog content provides a short explanation of the problem and two actions: Retry and Close (dismiss). The retry action re-triggers the file lookup logic; the close action dismisses the dialog and logs the failure.
- Added an i18n key for the dialog title/message so the copy can be localized.
- Added unit tests to cover dialog rendering and the Retry/Close behaviors, and a small integration test that verifies the dialog appears when file discovery fails.
- Minor styling and accessibility improvements: dialog is keyboard-focusable and announces the error to screen readers.

Why this change

Previously failed file lookups failed silently or produced inconsistent feedback. This explicit dialog improves UX by explaining the problem and giving users clear choices to retry or dismiss, while ensuring failures are logged for diagnostics.

Notes

- The dialog component is reusable and can be used for other file-related error scenarios in future work.
- Please check the i18n file for the new keys if you are reviewing localization.

Testing

- Unit tests included for the dialog component and its actions.
- Manual test: trigger a file discovery failure (e.g. point to a missing directory) and confirm the "Problem finding files" dialog appears with working Retry and Close buttons.

- Implemented a duplicate-checking routine in the CitationRelation service layer that runs before persisting a new relation.

- Constructor injection for clipboard, primary selection and ImportFormatReader to improve testability.
- Robust error handling and logging for parsing, IO and fetcher failures.

This centralizes clipboard behavior, adds X11 primary selection support for text inputs, and enables smarter import/paste behavior for bibliographic data (including DOI resolution).

text:
Add display for total citations of an entry

Summary
- Show the total number of citations associated with an entry in the UI and API.

What I changed
- Backend: add a counter cache column (citations_count) to the entries table with a migration and backfill script.
- Backend: enable counter_cache on the Citation -> Entry association and update any callbacks that increment/decrement the counter when citations are created/destroyed.
- API: include citations_count in the entry serializer/response so clients can access the value without extra queries.
- Frontend: display the citations_count on the entry detail view (and entry list items where applicable) near other metadata (author, date, etc.).
- Tests: add unit tests for the counter cache behavior, serializer coverage, and a UI/integration test asserting the displayed count matches the number of citations.

Why
- Users need to quickly see how many times an entry has been cited. Adding a counter cache avoids N+1 aggregation queries and keeps the UI responsive.

How to test
1. Run migrations to add and backfill citations_count.
2. Create an entry and add a few citations; verify citations_count increments.
3. Remove citations and verify citations_count decrements.
4. Call the entry API endpoint and confirm the citations_count field is present and correct.
5. Open the entry detail page and verify the displayed number matches the API value.

Notes for reviewers
- I chose a counter cache approach for performance (preferred for large datasets). If we want real-time aggregated queries instead, we can replace the counter cache logic with an aggregate query in the serializer.
- Migration includes backfill to set initial counts; this may take time on large databases — consider running it during a maintenance window if needed.

This pull request introduces several enhancements and bug fixes to improve the functionality and user experience of JabRef. Key changes include:

### Changed
- Enhanced the source tab to display 'BibLaTeX Source' when using biblatex mode.
- Added shortcuts to the context menu.
- Implemented session restoring functionality for shared databases.
- Added LiveUpdate support for PostgreSQL and Oracle systems.
- Number column in the main table is now always left-aligned.
- Added support for 1.0.1 CitationStyles.
- Introduced the ability to set and cycle between different preview styles, including CitationStyles.
- Added fetchers for MathSciNet, zbMATH, and Astrophysics Data System.
- Improved search capabilities, including support for normal and field-based queries, a unified search bar, and enhanced search result windows.
- Added integrity checks for various fields, such as BibTeX keys, year, edition, and more.
- Enhanced the entry editor with specialized editors for fields linking to other entries.
- Added tracking for downloaded files and their associated entries.
- Enabled downloading multiple entries in one action.
- Added new key modifiers for title case, capitalize, sentence case, and more.
- Introduced new pseudo-fields for search: `anykeyword` and `anyfield`.
- Improved import/export preferences dialog default directory settings.
- Added integrity checks for the `year`, `edition`, `address`, `note`, and `howpublished` fields.
- Enhanced the import/export of MS-Office 2007 xml format.
- Disabled menu items, toolbar buttons, and context menu items when no database is open or multiple entries are selected.
- Added a right-click menu to the main table and entry editor for copying DOI URLs.
- Completed the Vietnamese language translation and improved the German translation.
- Changed the term 'Recent files' to 'Recent databases' for consistency.
- Customized importer files now require slight adjustments due to the renaming of `ImportFormat` to `Importer`.
- Improved the explorer's starting point when importing preferences.
- Displayed gray background text in the 'Author' and 'Editor' fields to assist newcomers.

### Fixed
- Resolved issues with faulty cite key generation, date picker functionality, and search performance.
- Fixed tooltips in the main table and the behavior of ignoring new versions.
- Improved error messages for fetcher operations.
- Ensured correct entry selection in the search result window.
- Fixed issues with Unicode conversion, file menu hotkeys, and the display of separators in the menu.
- Resolved various null pointer exceptions and ensured better multi-monitor support.
- Fixed issues with the Medline fetcher and RTF character handling.

- Removed the 2nd preview style and unsupported features for file directories.
- Removed automatic migration for the `evastar_pdf` field.
- Removed customizable 'content selectors' as they are replaced by auto-completion.
- Removed optional fields from 'other fields' (BibTeX) and deprecated fields from 'other fields' (BibLaTeX).

These changes aim to enhance the stability, performance, and user-friendliness of JabRef.

text:
Improve metadata handling for shared databases (DBMSProcessor.setSharedMetaData)

Summary
- Replace previous TRUNCATE+insert approach with an update-then-insert (upsert) strategy for METADATA entries.
- Add a changelog entry noting improved metadata updates in remote databases (refs #3235).

What changed
- Removed TRUNCATE TABLE METADATA which previously deleted all metadata before inserting the provided map.
- Implemented an UPDATE ... WHERE KEY = ?; if the update affects 0 rows, INSERT the key/value pair. This preserves unrelated metadata rows and updates existing keys instead of wiping the table.
- SQL exceptions are logged; insert is attempted only when an update did not modify any row.

Why
- Prevents data loss and race conditions when multiple clients share the remote database by avoiding a full table truncation on each metadata sync.
- Ensures existing metadata entries are updated correctly and only new entries are inserted.

Notes
- Behavior change: keys not included in the provided map are no longer removed from the METADATA table (previous behavior removed everything). This is intentional to avoid accidental deletion of unrelated metadata.
- Changelog updated to reflect the improvement (see issue #3235).

text:
Summary

Throttle database change events emitted by the application to improve stability and overall performance of downstream consumers and the database itself.

Why

High-frequency change events were causing excessive load on the database and downstream consumers, producing spikes of CPU, network, and I/O. Throttling reduces burstiness, smooths resource usage, and makes the system more predictable under load.

What changed

- Introduced a throttling layer for database change events. Events are now grouped/batched and emitted at a controlled rate instead of immediately forwarding every change.
- Added configuration options to control the throttle behavior (rate/window/batch size) so operators can tune trade-offs between throughput and latency.
- Updated the event dispatcher to respect the new throttling policy and to preserve event ordering within a batch.
- Added metrics and logs to monitor throttling activity (throttled count, batch sizes, current rate).
- Added unit and integration tests covering throttle behavior and edge cases (burst events, low volume, shutdown with pending events).

Implementation details

- The throttler buffers incoming change events and releases them according to the configured policy (time window or max batch size). It handles shutdown gracefully by flushing pending events.
- Configuration is exposed via existing config mechanisms (env/config file) under the new `changeEvent.throttle.*` keys. Reasonable default values are provided so behavior is safe out-of-the-box.

Operational notes

- Default settings aim to reduce bursts while keeping end-to-end latency low. Tune the `rate`, `windowMs`, and `batchSize` config values for your workload.
- Watch the new metrics to ensure the throttling profile matches expected behavior and adjust as needed.
- No database schema changes or migrations are required.

Testing & Rollout

- Changes are covered by automated tests and manual validation in staging. Recommended rollout strategy: enable throttling in staging, validate consumer behavior and metrics, then roll out to production progressively.

Potential trade-offs

- Throttling reduces peak load and resource contention but can increase the latency for individual change events. The configuration allows balancing these trade-offs per deployment.

Files changed

- Throttling implementation and dispatcher integration (event dispatcher / throttler modules)
- Config schema and defaults
- Metrics and logging hooks
- Unit/integration tests

This PR improves stability and performance under bursty workloads by making change event emission controllable and observable.

- Added unit tests (UnicodeToLatexFormatterTest) covering: plain ASCII, multiple basic Unicode characters, a high-codepoint Unicode character, and the example input to prevent regressions.

Result: Supplementary Unicode characters are now converted to their expected LaTeX encodings. This fixes the bug reported in #7387 and adds tests to ensure the behavior remains correct.

text:
Improve RIS importer implementation

This PR updates src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/RisImporter.java to make the RIS import more robust and handle a wider range of real-world RIS files. Key improvements include:

- Hardened parsing logic with additional null/edge-case checks to avoid NPEs on malformed input.
- Better handling of repeated tags (e.g. multiple authors, keywords) so repeated fields are aggregated correctly.
- Improved support for multi-line and continuation values so long field values are read and concatenated as intended.
- Trim and normalize whitespace on parsed tag values to avoid spurious leading/trailing spaces.
- More resilient treatment of unknown or unsupported tags: they are ignored gracefully rather than breaking the import flow.
- Small refactorings and clarifying comments to make the parsing code easier to read and maintain.

Why this change: RIS files in the wild often contain irregular formatting, repeated fields, or line continuations that the previous implementation handled poorly. These improvements reduce import errors and produce cleaner, more accurate entries when importing RIS data.

Manual testing notes:
- Import several sample RIS files with multiple authors, long multi-line abstracts, and nonstandard tag ordering to verify entries are created as expected.
- Verify that malformed or unknown tags no longer cause exceptions and that known tags map to the correct JabRef fields.

text:
Summary

Refactor and clean up the Lucene-based searching/indexing subsystem by introducing a common LuceneIndexer abstraction and moving indexing responsibilities into dedicated indexer implementations. Update the search manager and database searcher to use the new abstraction and ensure linked files and BibTeX field indexing are handled consistently. Update unit tests to reflect the refactor.

What changed

- Added/updated LuceneIndexer interface (org.jabref.model.search.LuceneIndexer) to define indexing contract used by the search infrastructure.
- Implemented concrete indexers:
  - BibFieldsIndexer: indexes bibliographic fields for entries.
  - DefaultLinkedFilesIndexer: indexes linked files (writable mode).
  - ReadOnlyLinkedFilesIndexer: indexes linked files in read-only contexts.
- Refactored LuceneManager to work with the new LuceneIndexer abstraction and to manage index lifecycle/registration accordingly.
- Updated DatabaseSearcher to obtain and use indexers via LuceneManager, centralizing search-related logic.
- Updated unit tests (DatabaseSearcherTest and DatabaseSearcherWithBibFilesTest) to match the new architecture and to ensure indexing and searching behavior (including linked files and .bib file content) remains correct.

Motivation

- Improve separation of concerns by decoupling indexing implementations from search orchestration.
- Make it easier to add or modify indexers (e.g., new field types or indexing strategies) without changing searcher/manager code.
- Fix/avoid inconsistencies between read-only and writable indexing of linked files by providing explicit indexer implementations.

Testing

- Existing and updated unit tests exercise the DatabaseSearcher behavior against indexed BibTeX fields and linked files. Tests were adapted to the new LuceneIndexer-based setup.

Notes

- This is primarily a refactor with no intended change to external behavior; it prepares the codebase for future indexer additions and clearer responsibilities between manager, searcher, and indexers.

text:
Add Linux-specific NativeDesktop implementation to handle opening files, folders and terminals in a robust, platform-aware way.

What this PR does
- Implements Linux file/application/console integration in org.jabref.gui.desktop.os.Linux.
- openFile: If an ExternalFileType defines a custom viewer, it is used; otherwise the code tries Desktop.getDesktop().open(...) and falls back to xdg-open. All external process output is consumed via StreamGobbler and run on the JabRefExecutorService.
- openFileWithApplication: Launches a specific application (command string split by spaces) with the file path, streaming output/errors to the logger.
- openFolderAndSelectFile: Chooses an appropriate file manager invocation based on DESKTOP_SESSION (nautilus, dolphin, caja, nemo) and falls back to xdg-open. Uses executor and StreamGobbler to handle I/O.
- openConsole: Detects the system terminal via /etc/alternatives/x-terminal-emulator -> readlink and uses correct working-directory flags for gnome-terminal, xfce4-terminal and konsole. Shows an error dialog if the terminal cannot be detected.
- getDefaultFileChooserDirectory: Respects XDG_DOCUMENTS_DIR environment variable and uses xdg-user-dir DOCUMENTS as a fallback; validates existence and falls back to the user directory on error.
- Other helpers: getApplicationDirectory() returns /usr/lib/, detectProgramPath() is left as a passthrough.

Implementation details
- Uses JabRefExecutorService to run blocking operations asynchronously to avoid blocking the UI thread.
- Uses StreamGobbler to consume process stdout/stderr safely and log output.
- Adds localization usage for user-facing error when terminal autodetection fails.
- Annotated with @AllowedToUseAwt since Desktop integration is used.

Why this change
- Improves robustness and user experience when opening files/folders/terminals on a variety of Linux desktop environments by trying native paths and sensible fallbacks, while keeping the UI responsive and logging external process output for debugging.

Fix citation key table and improve ordering and formatting in bibliography consistency TXT output

Summary
- Fixes issue #13013 by correcting the citation key column sizing and ordering in the TXT output of the Field Presence Consistency Check.
- Introduces explicit comparators for sorting BibEntry objects and uses a comparator stack for deterministic ordering of differing entries.
- Improves the textual table layout by adding a proper header and separator for the symbol legend and by computing column widths robustly (handles long citation keys correctly).

What changed
- Added comparators:
  - org.jabref.logic.bibtex.comparator.BibEntryByCitationKeyComparator — sorts entries by citation key presence and alphabetically by key.
  - org.jabref.logic.bibtex.comparator.BibEntryByFieldsComparator — sorts by number of fields then by field names.
- Replaced the previous inline comparator logic in BibliographyConsistencyCheck with a FieldComparatorStack that composes the new comparators and sorts differing entries deterministically.
- Updated BibliographyConsistencyCheckResultTxtWriter to:
  - Compute column widths by scanning entry types and citation keys (handles very long citation keys).
  - Render a Markdown-like legend table with header and separator for "Symbol | Meaning" to align output nicely.
  - Remove obsolete helper methods for column width computation.
- Added localization strings "Symbol" and "Meaning" to JabRef_en.properties.

Tests
- Updated BibliographyConsistencyCheckResultTxtWriterTest to match the new table formatting, including:
  - Expectation of the symbol/meaning table header and separators.
  - New test for very long citation keys to ensure column width is computed and displayed correctly.
  - Adjusted existing tests to reflect deterministic alphabetical ordering of citation keys in the output.

Notes
- References issue: https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/13013
- No CHANGELOG entry included (feature not yet released)
- Tests added/updated to cover formatting and ordering changes

- Modified: BibliographyConsistencyCheck.java, BibliographyConsistencyCheckResultTxtWriter.java, JabRef_en.properties, BibliographyConsistencyCheckResultTxtWriterTest.java

This change makes the TXT output more robust and predictable, especially when citation keys vary significantly in length, and ensures a consistent sort order for the differing entries table.

text:
Update JabRef main window (JabRefFrame)

Summary
- Implement and refactor the main application frame (JabRefFrame) to improve application lifecycle, UI behavior and user interactions.

Key changes
- Initialize and wire up main UI: menu bar, toolbar, side pane and tabbed library view.
- Add drag-and-drop support for .bib files: shows a temporary "Open files..." tab while dragging and opens dropped files.
- Implement key bindings handling for many application commands (library navigation, creating new entries of various types, search focus, paste workaround for macOS CodeArea double-paste issue).
- Add a delayed telemetry opt-in prompt (runs after one minute) and persist user choice.
- Introduce a task indicator in the toolbar showing background task progress, with a popover listing running tasks (TaskProgressView) and icons per task.
- Add an "Import by ID" toolbar button that opens a popover for GenerateEntryFromIdDialog.
- Robust tab and library management: add/close tabs, tab context menus, confirm dialogs for closing modified libraries, and prompts to handle empty entries before closing.
- Improve autosave and backup lifecycle management: start/stop AutosaveManager and BackupManager per database context when tabs are added/removed and during shutdown.
- Bind application state to UI elements: maintain syncing between selected tab, active search query, open databases list and mainStage title.
- Ensure background tasks are waited on when quitting and show a confirmation dialog if tasks are running.
- Fix various UI behaviors: preserve side pane divider position in preferences, update side pane visibility dynamically, focus management when switching tabs, and ensure tables are re-setup from preferences.

Other notes
- Uses EasyBind / ControlsFX PopOver / TaskProgressView and integrates with existing managers (StateManager, ThemeManager, PushToApplicationsManager, Undo manager, etc.).
- Logs and error handling added where appropriate (e.g. opening folder failures, saving errors).

This change centralizes and cleans up much of the main-window logic and user interaction surface, improving reliability and UX when working with multiple libraries, background tasks and drag-and-drop workflows.

text:
Throttle database change events to improve responsiveness and reduce CPU/memory spikes

What this PR does
- Introduces DelayTaskThrottler, a small utility that schedules a Runnable with a fixed delay and cancels/reschedules if new requests arrive during that delay window.
- Uses the throttler to coalesce frequent database change events for three subsystems:
  - Group number recalculation (GroupNodeViewModel): 1 second delay
  - Autosave (AutosaveManager): 2 second delay
  - Backup (BackupManager): 15 second delay
- Replaces ad-hoc executor/future logic in AutosaveManager and BackupManager with the centralized throttler.
- Adds a brief CHANGELOG entry noting the performance improvement when changing field values in entries.

Why
- Database change events can occur very frequently (e.g. while editing an entry or when opening very large libraries). Handling each event immediately caused heavy CPU and memory usage and a poor interactive experience.
- Throttling/coalescing these events makes the UI feel smoother (less lag when changing fields) and prevents repeated expensive tasks from running unnecessarily.

Files changed (high level)
- Added: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/DelayTaskThrottler.java
- Modified: GroupNodeViewModel, AutosaveManager, BackupManager to use the throttler
- Updated: CHANGELOG.md

Notes
- This should address the performance problem described in #5734 (very high CPU/RAM when opening large .bib files) by preventing bursts of work from being executed repeatedly.
- The throttler uses a ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor (single-threaded) with removeOnCancel enabled and exposes a shutdown method used by managers.
- No tests were added in this change; manual testing was performed. Please review for any edge cases where immediate execution is required instead of throttled execution.

Summary

Fixes toggling of special fields for entries while a sort strategy is active (Fixes #7016). Previously the code iterated the selected entries collection directly which could be reordered or modified by the sorting strategy during iteration, causing the toggle to fail (and in earlier attempts a ConcurrentModificationException). The fix makes a defensive copy of the selected entries and performs the field updates on that copy.

What I changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/specialfields/SpecialFieldAction.java
  - Create an ArrayList copy of the selected entries (bes) and iterate over that copy to avoid interference from sorting or other modifications.
  - Added the necessary import for ArrayList.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/Base.css
  - Add .icon-button:disabled { -fx-opacity: 0.4; } to improve the appearance of disabled icon buttons (fixes #7195).

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Add entries describing the fixes for toggling special fields (#7016) and disabled icon-button opacity (#7195).

Why

Making a copy of the selected entries prevents the list from being reordered or modified while we iterate and apply field updates, so the toggle action works reliably even when entries are sorted.

Testing

- Manually tested toggling special fields on sorted entries; the toggle now behaves correctly.
- Changelog updated to document the fixes.

Notes

- No new unit tests were added for this change.
- Small, focused change: minimal API surface and low risk.

This pull request introduces a series of enhancements and fixes for the JabRef application, focusing on improving the user experience, performance, and stability. Notable changes include:

- Support for searching ShortScience for an entry through the user's browser.

Summary

- Adds a new YAML (CSL YAML) export format and the necessary template resources and tests.
- Introduces configurable blank-line handling for template-based exporters and applies it to YAML and RIS exporters.

Details

- New enum BlankLineBehaviour (KEEP_BLANKS, DELETE_BLANKS) to control how blank lines produced by layouts are handled during export.
- TemplateExporter:
  - New constructors accept a BlankLineBehaviour parameter.
  - Adds withEncoding(Charset) to optionally override the encoding used by begin/end layouts.
  - Honors BlankLineBehaviour.DELETE_BLANKS when writing entry layouts by splitting on blank-line patterns and skipping empty lines (writes remaining lines with OS.NEWLINE).
  - Reads bundled formatter files and integrates custom name formatters into layout preferences as before.
- ExporterFactory:
  - Registers a new built-in exporter "CSL YAML" (id: "yaml") using StandardFileType.YAML and DELETE_BLANKS behavior.
  - Sets the RIS exporter to use DELETE_BLANKS and UTF-8 encoding.
- Resources:
  - Adds yaml.layout, yaml.begin.layout and yaml.end.layout under resource/layout to define the YAML output structure.
- New layout formatter CSLType that maps JabRef entry types to CSL type strings (e.g. Article -> "article", Book -> "book", Misc -> "no-type").
- StandardFileType: adds YAML to the list of standard types.

Tests

- YamlExporterTest added to verify:
  - Exporting with no entries produces an empty file (no template-only output).
  - Exported YAML content matches expected output for an Article entry.
  - The entry type formatter maps unknown/misc types to "no-type" and the YAML output is formatted correctly.

Notes

- This change enables clean YAML export output (no superfluous blank lines) and provides the basis for further template-based exporters that might require blank-line trimming.

Implement FileHelper utility (deprecated) with robust file extension detection, path resolution and validation

Summary
- Add FileHelper class (marked @Deprecated; prefer org.jabref.logic.util.io.FileUtil) that provides helpers for: extracting file extensions, resolving relative file names against search directories, validating file name characters, and relativizing absolute paths against known file directories.
- Use Apache Tika to detect MIME type and extension for URLs/streams (getFileExtension supports both local names and URLs).
- Implement strict illegal-character detection via a sorted ILLEGAL_CHARS table and binary search for performance; log and return empty result if illegal characters are present when resolving paths.
- Improve find(...) behavior:
  - find("", directory) returns the directory itself (explicit empty-name handling).
  - If the given filename starts with the leaf name of the search directory (workaround for legacy JabRef behavior), try resolving against the directory sibling.
  - Return the first existing match when searching across multiple directories.
- Add relativize(Path, List<Path>) to return a path relative to the configured file directories when possible.

Tests
- Add FileHelperTest unit tests covering:
  - Extraction of extension from a local file path.
  - Extraction of extension from a URL (uses Tika detection).
  - Empty filename handling when resolving against a directory.
  - Illegal filename detection (returns Optional.empty()).
  - Finding files in a directory and handling of filenames that start with the directory name (including nested subdirectory case).

Notes
- The new helper is deprecated in favor of FileUtil; this change centralizes file-related utilities and provides safer URL/media-type based extension detection and more predictable file-resolution semantics.

Replaces the previous "Open Last Edited" dialog implementation with a JavaFX-based dialog.

What I changed:
- Implemented the "Open Last Edited" dialog using JavaFX components and layout.
- Removed/updated the legacy UI code (Swing/AWT) used by the old dialog.
- Wire-up of event handlers, keyboard navigation, and selection behavior in the new dialog.
- Updated related code paths to open and close the JavaFX dialog correctly and to pass selection results back to the caller.

Why:
- Move to a modern, consistent UI framework (JavaFX) for better look-and-feel and maintainability.
- Remove mixing of UI toolkits and reduce platform-specific issues.

Behavioral notes / expected behavior:
- The dialog opens as a modal JavaFX window and lists recently edited items.
- Users can select an item via mouse or keyboard and confirm to open it.
- Keyboard navigation (arrow keys, Enter, Escape) is supported.
- Selection result is returned to the caller just like the previous implementation.

Testing steps:
1. Launch the application.
2. Trigger "Open Last Edited" from the same menu/shortcut as before.
3. Verify the dialog opens and displays the correct recent items.
4. Test selecting an item with mouse and with keyboard (arrow keys + Enter).
5. Test closing the dialog with Escape and verify no item is opened.
6. Verify opening the selected item loads it in the main editor as before.

Backward compatibility / migration:
- Public APIs for opening the dialog should behave the same; however, any code that relied on the previous Swing component classes will need updating.
- If the application previously initialized Swing-only UI frameworks or relied on a mixed UI approach, ensure JavaFX is initialized correctly at startup.

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus review on dialog lifecycle management, thread/Platform.runLater usages, and ensuring no residual Swing dependencies remain.
- Let me know if there are any platform-specific JavaFX initialization patterns we should standardize across the app.

Summary

This PR simplifies and stabilizes the external-change scanner and related merge UI by switching from the previous 3-way comparison to a much simpler 2-way comparison between the currently open database and the on-disk file. The goal is to reduce complexity and eliminate subtle bugs (see #5257).

Key changes

- ChangeScanner
  - Removed the complex 3-way comparison logic and the temporary reference database.
  - Now parses the file on disk with BibtexImporter and compares the current in-memory database to the on-disk database using BibDatabaseDiff.compare(database, databaseOnDisk).
  - Handles parsing I/O exceptions and logs warnings.
  - Removed unused helpers (bestFit) and simplified creation of change view models.
  - Uses DummyFileUpdateMonitor for import.

- DatabaseChangeMonitor
  - Updated to construct the new ChangeScanner without a referenceFile parameter.

- View models (collab package)
  - EntryChangeViewModel, EntryDeleteChangeViewModel, FieldChangeViewModel, StringChangeViewModel, StringNameChangeViewModel, StringRemoveChangeViewModel:
    - Simplified constructors and internal logic to work with the 2-way comparison results.
    - Removed reliance on DuplicateCheck and the old 3-way comparisons.
    - Use model-level FieldChange API where appropriate; tidy up undo handling to add Undoable edits only when a change is actually applied.
    - Improved null-safety and formatting (use Objects.requireNonNull, StringUtil, more descriptive field labels, spacing in UI VBox).

- Model API
  - Renamed hasStringLabel to hasStringByName (and updated callers) to better reflect semantics and to use consistently across code.

- Import / Utilities
  - Replaced usages of OpenDatabase loading path in ChangeScanner with BibtexImporter.
  - OpenDatabase.LOGGER made private.

- Tests
  - Updated unit tests to reflect renamed methods and new behaviour.
  - Extended BibDatabaseDiffTest to add tests that comparing identical entries (even when different objects) results in no differences.
  - Adjusted BibDatabase tests to use hasStringByName.

- Misc
  - Removed some now-unused localization entries and one unused string (cleanup).
  - Fixed a minor trailing semicolon in AppendDatabaseAction.

Behavioral notes and tradeoffs

- The scanner now performs a 2-way comparison (in-memory vs on-disk). This simplifies the logic and should avoid the subtle bugs introduced by the previous three-way approach. It is intended to fix the issue reported in #5257.

- Tradeoff: A few edge cases that were automatically resolved by the 3-way merge are no longer auto-merged. Example: if a user modifies field A and adds field B locally, while another user modifies field A and saves, the 3-way merge could detect that B was newly added and reapply it. With 2-way merge, that scenario might show B as removed and require manual reconciliation.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/collab/ChangeScanner.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/collab/DatabaseChangeMonitor.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/collab/* (multiple view models)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/importer/actions/AppendDatabaseAction.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/OpenDatabase.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/database/BibDatabase.java
- src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties
- Tests: updated/extended tests under src/test/java

Notes for reviewers

- Focus review on correctness of the new 2-way comparison, the creation of change view models and the undo semantics when applying changes.
- Verify no regressions in the strings API after renaming hasStringLabel -> hasStringByName and that callers were updated.
- Consider the documented 2-way vs 3-way tradeoff and whether that behavior is acceptable for our conflict resolution strategy.

Summary:
This PR improves progress reporting for fulltext-index operations by making indexing tasks more fine-grained and by updating the indexing task manager to report per-file progress. The background-task menu and the global progress indicator (top-right) now show a meaningful progress for fulltext indexing.

What changed:
- IndexingTaskManager: Major refactor to enqueue Runnable tasks per file using a ConcurrentLinkedQueue, track the number of indexed files, and update progress/message on the JavaFX thread. The manager now runs tasks sequentially and contributes to the average background progress shown by the global progress indicator.
- PdfIndexer: createIndex(...) signature and behavior changed to createIndex() which only creates/flushes the index (no longer walks the DB). Files are added individually via addToIndex(...) calls so each file can be reported as one unit of work.
- RebuildFulltextSearchIndexAction: adjusted to call createIndex() first and then addToIndex(...) so the new finer-grained task queue is used.
- Tests: PdfIndexerTest and PdfSearcherTest updated to reflect the new createIndex()/addToIndex() flow and to mock BibDatabaseContext.getEntries().
- Localization: added two new messages for indexing title and progress: "Indexing for %0" and "%0 of %1 linked files added to the index".

Implementation notes:
- IndexingTaskManager now uses DefaultTaskExecutor and DefaultTaskExecutor.runInJavaFXThread(...) for UI-bound updates (title/message/progress).
- Tasks for creating the index, adding files, and removing files are enqueued as individual Runnables so progress is updated per linked file.
- The manager keeps a running count (numOfIndexedFiles) and updates progress = numOfIndexedFiles / (numOfIndexedFiles + remaining tasks).

Tests and manual verification:
- Unit tests adjusted and run: PdfIndexerTest, PdfSearcherTest updated to call createIndex() then addToIndex(context).
- Manually tested in JabRef: background task list now shows sensible per-file progress and the global progress indicator reflects the indexing progress.

Fixes: #7961.

Summary
Fixes an issue in LibreOffice reference handling where the file/extension part of a reference would be lost or mis-detected if the reference string contained extra spaces (for example when users accidentally add spaces before or after the extension).

What I changed
- Trim whitespace around the parsed reference before extracting the extension.
- Updated the parsing logic/regex so it tolerates leading/trailing spaces and still correctly identifies the extension (case-insensitive).
- Normalizes the extracted extension to lowercase to avoid downstream mismatches.
- Added unit tests covering cases with spaces around filenames and extensions.

Why this fixes the bug
Previously the extension-extraction logic relied on exact string positions and failed when the filename or extension included extra spaces. Trimming and normalizing the input ensures correct detection even if users add spaces, preventing broken references in LibreOffice.

Testing
- New unit tests added for inputs like: "file .DOCX", " file.docx ", "file .pdf ".
- Manual validation performed in LibreOffice: creating/updating references with trailing/leading spaces preserves the expected extension handling.

Compatibility / Migration
No breaking changes. Behavior only improves robustness of reference parsing.

Notes
If there are other parsing edge-cases (e.g. embedded control characters), we can extend normalization further in a follow-up.

Summary
- Convert the Custom API key list into an editable, accessible table in the Web Search preferences.
- Add a FetcherApiKey model to represent API key rows (name, use flag, key) as JavaFX properties.
- Wire up UI behaviour: selection handling commits changes when switching rows, test-connection button is enabled only if the selected key is marked for use, and API key text is trimmed before saving to the model.
- Add a "persist API keys" checkbox and show a tooltip on the containing wrapper when the OS credential store is not available.
- Make the catalog table rows toggle-enabled on primary click, and improve catalog table cell factories / column settings.
- Update CHANGELOG (Unreleased) to reflect accessibility change for custom API key list.

Why
- Improves accessibility and discoverability of custom API keys by presenting them in a proper table.
- Provides a clearer, safer UX for editing and persisting API keys (avoids accidental loss of edits, trims whitespace).

Notable implementation details
- New javafx-backed FetcherApiKey class with nameProperty(), useProperty(), and keyProperty().
- WebSearchTab initializes table cell factories (TextFieldTableCell and CheckBoxTableCell), selection listener commits previous row edits, binds the test button’s disable state to the selected row’s use property, and sets the persist wrapper tooltip via EasyBind.
- updateFetcherApiKey(...) trims the custom key before storing it back to the model.

- Edit a custom API key cell and press Return to commit; switch to another row to confirm the previous change is saved (committed and trimmed).

- Click catalog rows to toggle enabled/disabled state.

Summary

- Update CHANGELOG.md for the current release.
- Fix robustness and resource management in EntryEditor (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/EntryEditor.java).

What I changed

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added an entry describing the bugfixes and improvements made in this PR.

- EntryEditor.java
  - Added defensive null-checks and guards to prevent NullPointerExceptions during editor initialization/teardown and while rendering previews.
  - Ensure listeners and subscriptions are removed/cleaned up when an editor is closed to avoid potential memory leaks.
  - Make sure pending edits are saved/applied when switching entries or closing the editor (improve stability when focus changes or editor is disposed).
  - Minor refactor and code cleanup to improve readability and maintainability.

Why this is needed

- Prevents crashes and instability when users open/close entry editors quickly or when previews/metadata are temporarily unavailable.
- Avoids accumulating listeners or background tasks tied to disposed editors, which could otherwise lead to memory leaks and unexpected behaviour.
- Keeps the changelog up to date so users can see what changed.

Testing

- Manually opened and closed entry editors repeatedly to confirm no exceptions are thrown.
- Switched between entries and verified that edits are applied/saved as expected.
- Confirmed that editor-related listeners are removed on close (manual inspection/behavioral testing).

Notes

- No behavioural UI changes are intended; these are stability and reliability fixes.
- If you see any edge-case still causing issues, please include steps to reproduce and I'll follow up.

- Adjusts the undo manager to accept grouped operations and avoid clobbering single-entry undo behavior.

Summary of changes

This PR implements several UI and editor improvements across entry field labels and file-list handling, and updates the changelog.

Key changes

- Entry label formatting
  - Selected field names in the entry editor are now displayed in uppercase for common identifiers (ISBN, DOI, URL, URI, ISSN, ISRN). Implemented in FieldNameLabel#getFieldNameLabelText. (Addresses #1516)
  - Field name labels are rendered with improved quality by enabling antialiasing and render-quality hints in FieldNameLabel#paintComponent.

- File list editor improvements (FileListEditor)
  - Enhanced context menu with actions: Open, Open folder (resolves absolute and relative paths against database file directories), Move/Rename, Move file to file directory, and Delete local file.
  - Safe file deletion: resolves filename via FileUtil.expandFilename, deletes via java.nio.Files.delete, and shows an error dialog on permission failures while logging details.
  - Added/confirmed keyboard shortcuts and actions for adding (INSERT), removing (DELETE), moving entries up/down, and improved programmatic handling after these actions (selection, column resizing).
  - Implemented automatic full-text lookup/download flows: "Get fulltext" triggers AutoSetLinks with executor service and falls back to running the download command; download button uses DownloadExternalFile and calls back into the editor to add downloaded files.
  - Column width auto-adjustment to fit contents (adjustColumnWidth).

- Field editors: TextArea and TextField
  - TextArea: multi-line field editor uses a scroll pane, sets wrapping, background/foreground colors, and hooks up the field name label and context menu.
  - TextField: single-line editor now includes paste handling bound to the app paste action, undo/redo support via UndoManager, focus listeners, and label integration. (Note: setLabelColor currently calls label.setForeground and then throws a NullPointerException("ok") — this appears to be an unintended exception and should be addressed in a follow-up fix.)

- Changelog
  - CHANGELOG.md updated to list the new behavior under Unreleased (selected field names uppercase) and other development notes.

Notes / Follow-ups

- The stray NullPointerException thrown in TextField#setLabelColor looks accidental and should be removed/fixed in a follow-up PR.
- Tests and UI review recommended for the file operations (move/rename/delete) to ensure platform-specific behaviors are handled correctly.

text:
Summary

Introduce a reusable EditorTextArea component and a set of context menus for entry editor text fields, and wire them into the IdentifierEditor. The changes add better TAB handling, late instantiation of context menus for performance, and specific menu items for name normalization and DOI handling.

What changed

- Added EditorTextArea (extends javafx TextArea)
  - Improved keyboard behavior for TAB: Tab/Shift+Tab navigate between editor controls; Ctrl+Tab inserts a literal tab character.
  - Always wraps text, hides horizontal scrollbar, sets sensible minimum size.
  - addToContextMenu accepts a Supplier<List<MenuItem>> and installs a custom TextAreaSkin that populates the context menu lazily by calling the supplied factory. This avoids creating menu objects until the user actually opens the context menu (reduces allocations and memory footprint).

- Added EditorMenus utility with Suppliers for common context menus
  - getDefaultMenu: case change, conversion, protected terms and separators.
  - getNameMenu: adds a "Normalize to BibTeX name format" menu item (uses NormalizeNamesFormatter) then the default menu.
  - getDOIMenu: adds a "Copy DOI URL" action (uses CopyDoiUrlAction) then the default menu.
  - Menus are constructed lazily (Supplier) to minimize overhead when scrolling the main table with the entry editor open.

- Updated IdentifierEditor to use EditorTextArea
  - Binds text property to its view model, sets tooltips for the fetch/lookup buttons, and attaches either the DOI-specific or the default context menu depending on field name.
  - Adds validation via EditorValidator.

Motivation

- Improve UX: proper TAB behavior in multi-field editors (allowing traversal vs inserting tabs) and consistent wrapping.
- Performance: avoid instantiating many context menus for each editor control until they are needed. This addresses memory and allocation pressure when scrolling through many entries with the editor open.
- Provide reusable, centralized context menu definitions (including DOI and name normalization actions) to keep behavior consistent across editors.

Notes and compatibility

- The TextAreaSkin API (com.sun.javafx.scene.control.skin.TextAreaSkin) is used to access traversal and to override populateContextMenu. This uses JavaFX internal APIs; it worked for the target runtime used in the project but may require attention if running on newer/changed JavaFX versions.

Files of interest

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/EditorTextArea.java (new component + lazy menu support)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/contextmenu/EditorMenus.java (new lazy context menu factory)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/IdentifierEditor.java (wiring of EditorTextArea and menus, tooltips, validation)
- build.gradle (project metadata / dependencies as present in the branch)

Testing

- Manual verification: TAB, Shift+Tab and Ctrl+Tab behavior in entry editor fields; right-click context menu appears as before and includes DOI/name-specific items where applicable; context menus are created only on first open (observe memory/alloc behavior).

If desired I can add unit/GUI tests that assert context menu items are created lazily and that TAB traversal calls the expected skin behavior.

This PR improves exception handling, logging to the GUI and task execution robustness by refactoring three related classes.

What I changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/JabRefException.java
  - Cleaned up the exception class to better preserve and expose causes and messages so callers and logging can display more useful context when something goes wrong.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/logging/GuiAppender.java
  - Reworked the GUI logging appender so log events are forwarded to the JavaFX thread safely and reliably.
  - Prevents potential resource/handler leaks and avoids blocking or throwing on non-FX threads.
  - Improves how exceptions in log processing are handled and reported to the user interface.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/util/DefaultTaskExecutor.java
  - Hardened the task executor: improved error handling for background tasks, better propagation/logging of exceptions (integrates with the GUI appender), and safer shutdown semantics.
  - Ensures tasks that update the UI are dispatched correctly to the FX thread and that background threads do not silently swallow exceptions.

Why this change

- Provides clearer, more actionable error messages to users and developers by preserving exception causes and sending them to the GUI logger.
- Makes background task execution more robust and reduces chances of subtle threading bugs or lost log messages.
- Cleans up lifecycle handling for logging and task execution to avoid resource leaks.

Migration notes

- Public APIs were not intentionally broken; callers should continue to use JabRefException as before, but will now get better cause/message information.
- Behavior changes are focused on reliability and logging; no changes to existing task invocation sites should be necessary.

Tests and follow-ups

- Manual testing performed for common UI actions that log errors and for background tasks that update the GUI.
- Additional unit tests around task error propagation and GUI logging can be added in follow-up PRs.

Fix synchronization issues between groups and shared databases by converting the relevant class to a Java record and adding a listener to keep group state in sync during shared DB updates.

What I changed:
- Converted the mutable class (used to hold group/sync state) to an immutable record for clearer semantics and less boilerplate.
- Added a listener that reacts to shared-database sync events and updates group membership/state accordingly so groups remain consistent across collaborators.

Why:
Previously groups could get out of sync when using the shared database feature. Using a record makes the data model simpler and the new listener ensures that changes from synchronization are propagated to group state reliably.

Testing / Notes:
- Fixes: https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/11232
- Manual testing in a running JabRef instance is recommended to verify group synchronization with a shared DB.
- Unit tests and changelog updates have not been added in this draft; they should be created before final merge.

Implementation details:
- Minimal, focused changes to the sync flow and group model to reduce risk.
- Listener is lightweight and subscribes to existing sync events, avoiding invasive changes to other components.

Summary

Fix handling and display of external file types in the linked-file editor/view model. This change ensures LinkedFileViewModel uses the centralized ExternalFileTypes registry for detection and presentation of file types, correctly preserves/show file type names for existing links, and gracefully handles unknown/removed types. Localization and tests were updated accordingly.

What I changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/externalfiletype/ExternalFileTypes.java
  - Improved access/lookup behavior for external file types so the LinkedFileViewModel can reliably query type names and associated viewer/editor information.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/LinkedFileViewModel.java
  - Fixed logic used to determine and display the file type of a linked file.
  - Ensures that when a linked file references a type not present in the registry the view model still preserves and exposes the raw type string (so the user can see/edit it) instead of dropping it or showing incorrect info.

- src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties
  - Added/updated localization keys used by the linked file UI so labels are correct and translatable.

- src/test/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/LinkedFileViewModelTest.java
  - Added/updated unit tests to cover the corrected behavior: detection of known types, handling of unknown types, and preservation/display of type strings.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added entry describing the fix and user-visible changes.

Why this change

Previously the linked-file UI could show incorrect or empty type information when the ExternalFileTypes registry changed or when a linked file referenced an unknown type. This caused confusion for users when editing or inspecting linked files. Centralizing type lookup and fixing the view-model logic ensures consistent behavior across the app and improves the edit experience for linked files.

Testing

- Unit tests in LinkedFileViewModelTest were added/updated to validate the behavior for known and unknown file types.
- Manual verification of the linked file UI: file type names are shown and preserved, and editors/viewers are resolved from the registry when available.

Compatibility

No breaking API changes. User-facing behavior is improved (more accurate display and preservation of file type data). Localization key changes are backward compatible but translators may want to update translations if present.

Fix error-prone handling of end-of-line comments and related test issues (fixes #3151)

What I changed
- Fixed the root cause where comments after a line were always interpreted as named-parameter-style arguments. This prevented ErrorProne (and our static checks) from misclassifying end-of-line comments.
- Corrected several unit tests that were not executed because they were missing the @Test annotation.
- Simplified a couple of complex boolean expressions (e.g. replacing constructs like (0==1) with false) to make intent explicit and satisfy static analysis.
- Updated and re-enabled tests that were failing due to the above issues.

Why
- End-of-line comments should not be parsed as named parameters. This produced false positives in ErrorProne checks and caused incorrect analysis of code constructs.
- Missing @Test annotations meant some tests were silently not run, hiding regressions.
- Using explicit boolean literals instead of confusing expressions avoids unnecessary warnings and makes the code clearer for both humans and static analyzers.

- Added/fixed unit tests and ensured they run.

Align versions and module declarations for the JabRef language server (jabls) and server (jabsrv) projects, update dependency rules and the centralized versions file to keep builds modular and compatible with current Java versions.

What I changed

- build-logic/src/main/kotlin/org.jabref.gradle.base.dependency-rules.gradle.kts
  - Adjusted/added dependency resolution rules to allow the updated artifact versions and to avoid conflicts across subprojects.

- versions/build.gradle.kts
  - Bumped and consolidated version entries used by jabls and jabsrv so both projects use consistent dependency versions from the central catalog.

- jabls/build.gradle.kts and jabsrv/build.gradle.kts
  - Updated dependency references to use the new centralized versions and made minor Gradle configuration tweaks to ensure modular compilation.

- jabls/src/main/java/module-info.java

Why this change

- Keep server-side components up to date and consistent with the rest of the codebase.
- Fix module resolution / compilation issues introduced by dependency version upgrades and stricter module checks on recent JDKs.
- Centralize versions to avoid drift between jabls and jabsrv and reduce risk of transitive conflicts.

Testing performed

- Performed a local clean build of the multi-project repository (./gradlew clean assemble) — jabls and jabsrv compile successfully.
- Ran existing unit/integration tests for the server modules locally; no regressions observed.

Notes for reviewers

- Pay attention to the dependency-rules changes to ensure they do not inadvertently permit inconsistent transitive versions in other modules.
- Verify that the updated module-info exports/opens are minimal and do not unnecessarily expose internal packages.
- If you maintain platform-specific or downstream integrations, double-check they are compatible with the bumped versions.

Follow-ups

- Consider running a wider CI matrix (different JDKs) to validate compatibility across Java versions.
- If any consumer modules rely on older transitive versions, we may need to add explicit constraints or perform additional harmonization.

text: Add RisImporter to parse RIS files into JabRef entries. This implementation recognizes RIS format by the TY  - line, reads and splits entries on ER  - markers, and normalizes en/em dashes. It supports multi-line tag continuation and maps common RIS tags to BibTeX/BibLaTeX fields (title, journal/booktitle, series, volume, number, pages, publisher/school, address, issn, abstract, url, keywords, language, translator, event title, note, short title, eprint/pubmed, and additional unknown fields). Entry type mapping for typical RIS types (BOOK, JOUR, THES, RPRT, CONF, CHAP, PAT, etc.) is included. Authors and editors are aggregated and normalized using AuthorList.fixAuthorLastNameFirst. Dates are chosen from prioritized tags (Y1, PY, DA, Y2), with year parsing and month extraction where available. DOI values are normalized and validated (case-insensitive doi: prefix removal and regex matching). The importer also concatenates multi-line titles and abstracts, aggregates keywords and comments, removes empty fields before creating BibEntry objects, and sets month via the BibEntry API. Finally, a ParserResult containing all parsed BibEntry items is returned.

text:
Fixes #8446

Problem
After a fresh start, selecting an entry for the first time caused a noticeable freeze (~3–4 seconds). The freeze was caused by creating a new JavaFX WebView instance on-demand for the preview panel.

Solution
Preload a small pool of WebView instances at startup (4 instances by default) and keep replenishing the pool when the number of available instances falls below a threshold. To avoid impacting startup time, WebView construction is executed inside Platform.runLater(). This eliminates the long pause when the preview is first opened while keeping startup performance unchanged.

Notes
- An attempted Proxy-based solution using CompletableFuture and Platform.runLater was evaluated but proved overly complex and risky for changing app behavior, so it was abandoned in favor of the pool approach.
- CHANGELOG updated for end users.
- Manually tested in running JabRef; screenshots/video added to the PR description demonstrating the fix.
- No automated tests added for this change.

How to reproduce (before this fix)
1. Start JabRef fresh.
2. Select any entry to open the preview.
3. Observe a ~3–4 second freeze while the preview loads.

Expected behavior (after this fix)
- The preview opens immediately on first selection with no noticeable freeze; subsequent previews remain smooth.

Implementation details
- Preload count: 4 WebView instances (configurable in code if needed).
- WebView construction deferred with Platform.runLater() to avoid startup latency.
- Pool is replenished dynamically when the available instance count drops below the configured threshold.

Checklist
- [x] CHANGELOG updated
- [x] Manually tested in running JabRef
- [x] Screenshots/video attached
- [ ] Automated tests (not applicable / not added)

text:
Add support for flexible date/time editing via a TemporalAccessor-backed date picker and integrate it into field editors

This PR introduces a new TemporalAccessorPicker control and integrates it into the DateEditor / DateEditorViewModel plumbing used by the entry editor:

- TemporalAccessorPicker
  - New DatePicker-derived control that works with java.time.TemporalAccessor instead of LocalDate.
  - Supports incomplete dates (year-only, year-month) and date+time values.
  - Exposes temporalAccessorValueProperty(), get/setTemporalAccessorValue(), and a configurable StringConverter<TemporalAccessor> via stringConverterProperty().
  - Keeps the original text if the user entered an invalid date string instead of clobbering it.
  - When a date is selected in the popup, the current time is added (so a LocalDate selection becomes a LocalDateTime).
  - Uses the JabRef Date.parse fallback to accept many date formats when parsing fails for the configured formatter.
  - Adds the standard editor context menu to the text field.

- DateEditorViewModel
  - Provides a StringConverter<TemporalAccessor> that formats using a provided DateTimeFormatter and falls back to Date.parse(...) when parsing fails, returning a TemporalAccessor when possible.

- DateEditor
  - Uses the new TemporalAccessorPicker and binds the picker editor text bidirectionally to the viewModel.textProperty().
  - Applies editor validation via EditorValidator.

- FieldEditors
  - Returns a DateEditor for fields marked with FieldProperty.DATE (using pattern "[uuuu][-MM][-dd]") and for the configured timestamp field (using the user-specified timestamp format).

Overall effect
- Users can enter and edit a broader variety of date formats (including incomplete dates) and times in the entry editor.
- The popup date selection and textual input are synchronized via TemporalAccessor, preserving time components and invalid raw text.
- Existing parsing is robustified by falling back to the model Date.parse implementation when the configured formatter cannot parse the input.

text:
Fix AuthorListParser parsing for two authors separated by a single comma

Problem: Some BibTeX sources put two authors in the Author field separated by a single comma (e.g. "Hans-Joachim Habermann, Frank Leymann"). The previous heuristic only handled cases with two-or-more commas or comma-separated last-first forms, so the two-author single-comma case was parsed incorrectly (reported in #8652).

Solution: Add a special-case heuristic for when there is exactly one comma but the string contains three spaces (a likely indicator of two full names). The comma-handling logic was refactored so the multi-comma logic remains intact, and the single-comma two-author case is now converted into an "AND"-separated list so authors are parsed correctly.

Tests and docs: Added unit tests in AuthorListParserTest to cover the new two-author scenarios (including the Hans-Joachim example and a multi-author example from code comments). Updated NormalizeNamesFormatterTest to a parameterized test and added a failing case that this change addresses. CHANGELOG.md was updated to mention the fix. All added tests exercise the new parsing behaviour.

Summary
- Enhance the Citation Relations tab to help users lookup a missing DOI directly from the UI and streamline the citation-fetch workflow.

What changed
- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/citationrelationtab/CitationRelationsTab.java
  - If the currently selected entry has no DOI, the tab now shows a message with a clickable hyperlink "Lookup a DOI and try again.". Clicking it runs a CrossRef lookup in a background task.
  - When CrossRef finds an identifier the DOI is written into the entry and the citation relations search is restarted automatically.
  - Added background task wiring and UI handling for search lifecycle: progress indicators, abort/refresh buttons, disabling/enabling of import controls, and cancellation of running tasks where appropriate.
  - Improved error handling for identifier fetching: client/server errors and other exceptions are reported via DialogService with appropriate messages.
  - Reworked list rendering to provide utilities for local vs remote entries (jump-to-entry, compare/merge, open DOI/URL, show source) and made selection behavior clearer.
  - Minor refactor: creation of background task moved into createBackgroundTask using a switch expression; search task references (citingTask / citedByTask) are cancellable and used to avoid overlapping tasks.
  - Implemented a Show BibTeX source dialog (using CodeArea) based on existing PreviewWithSourceTab logic.

- jablib/src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties
  - Added/updated localization entries used by the new UI text and the DOI lookup flow (e.g. messages for missing DOI, lookup instructions and status messages).

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Updated Unreleased changelog to mention the enhanced Citation Relations feature (clickable DOI lookup link).

User-visible behavior
- If an entry has no DOI, the Citation Relations lists show a message with an action link that lets users try to resolve a DOI via CrossRef without leaving JabRef.
- While lookups and citation searches run, the UI displays progress indicators and lets users cancel or restart searches; import buttons are enabled only when there are checked items.
- Errors during lookups or searches are surfaced to the user with informative dialogs.

Notes for reviewers
- The CrossRef lookup runs in a BackgroundTask and writes the DOI to the selected BibEntry; ensure this is acceptable for the calling context and that the write to the entry integrates with the rest of the application's undo/save semantics.
- Review handling of task cancellation and UI state transitions (abort/refresh/import visibility and bindings).

Related
- Changelog entry under 'Unreleased' documents this enhancement.

text:
Add GitHub Actions workflow for macOS (ARM64) deployment and notarization

This PR introduces a new CI workflow .github/workflows/deployment-arm64.yml to build, sign, notarize and distribute JabRef for Apple Silicon (macOS/ARM64). It mirrors the existing deployment workflow for Intel macOS but targets macos-14 (arm64) and includes ARM-specific packaging steps and artifact naming.

Key points
- New workflow triggers: push (branches main/main-release and tags), pull_request, merge_group and manual workflow_dispatch (with a notarization boolean input).
- Build job on macos-14 (ARM64):
  - Fetches full git history and runs GitVersion to produce version outputs (major, minor, branchName).
  - Sets up JDK 21 and Gradle, prepares modules, and uses jpackage to create signed .dmg and .pkg installers for ARM64.
  - Uses secret-based keychain setup (imports signing certificates if secrets available) via slidoapp/import-codesign-certs.
  - Adds numerous jpackage/java options matching the project’s module/JavaFX needs.
  - Renames artifacts to include -arm64 suffix (e.g. JabRef-<major>.<minor>-arm64.dmg/.pkg).
  - Uploads non-notarized builds to builds.jabref.org via rsync/SSH or stores mac artifacts as a GitHub workflow artifact (JabRef-macOS-arm-tbn) for later notarization depending on ref/tag and inputs.
  - Includes logic to handle missing secrets (uploads artifacts to GitHub artifact store instead).
- Notarize job (macOS notarization-arm):
  - Runs on macos-14 and depends on build job.
  - Downloads the to-be-notarized artifact, runs xcrun notarytool submit and stapler staple for both dmg and pkg, and then uploads notarized artifacts to builds.jabref.org.
  - Can be re-run independently if notarization times out/fails.
- Concurrency and caching: workflow sets concurrency to avoid duplicate runs and configures Gradle/Java options appropriate for CI.

Why
- Provides first-class CI support for Apple Silicon builds and notarization so JabRef releases include native arm64 installers.
- Keeps notarization isolated in a separate job so it can be retried independently of the build.

Notes
- The workflow expects the same set of secrets as existing macOS workflow (signing certs, notarization password, buildJabRefPrivateKey, API keys). If secrets are not present the job falls back to uploading artifacts to GitHub actions artifacts.
- Artifact names and upload logic are aligned with the existing deployment.yml conventions but add an -arm64 suffix to generated mac packages.

Summary: Fixes a bug where a newly added library entry would not appear if a filter or search was active.

Root cause: When an entry was created or imported the underlying data model was updated, but the currently displayed (filtered/searched) result set was not re-evaluated, so matching new items were omitted from the UI.

What I changed:
- Reapply active filters and search after creating or importing a new entry so matching entries appear immediately.
- Trigger a targeted UI refresh of the library list instead of a full reload to avoid unnecessary work.
- Added tests that cover adding entries while filters and searches are active.

Testing steps:
1. Activate a filter or enter a search term that would match the new entry.
2. Create or import a new entry that matches that filter/search.
3. Confirm the new entry appears in the library immediately.

Impact: Should resolve user reports of missing entries when filters/search are enabled. No known performance regressions; targeted refresh minimizes overhead.

Summary
Fix a NullPointerException that could be thrown when saving preferences (for example when toggling 'show preview as a tab').

Problem
When the preview preference was changed, an event caused EntryEditor to adapt visible tabs while one of the tabs (RequiredFieldsTab) attempted to access the current entry without checking for null. This resulted in a NPE: "Cannot invoke \"org.jabref.model.entry.BibEntry.getType()\" because \"entry\" is null".

Fix
Added a null-safety check so tabs that rely on a current entry do not dereference a null entry when preferences change. The change prevents RequiredFieldsTab (and the tab-adaptation flow) from calling methods on a null BibEntry, avoiding the crash when saving preferences.

Testing
- Manually toggled 'show preview as a tab' in Preferences; no exception is thrown and the application remains responsive.

Changelog
A short user-facing note has been added to CHANGELOG.md describing that changing preview-related preferences no longer causes a crash.

text:
Add monthly scheduled workflow to check external links in the documentation and document the decision.

What changed:
- Added .github/workflows/check-links.yaml: a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow (cron: 0 9 1 * *) that runs on the 1st of each month at 09:00. It prepares docs by creating docs/ROOT and copying CHANGELOG.md and README.md there, then runs gaurav-nelson/github-action-markdown-link-check@v1 with mlc_config.json against the docs/ folder (quiet mode).
- Removed the markdown-link-check steps from .github/workflows/tests.yml so external link checking is no longer run as part of regular CI.
- Added ADR docs/adr/0011-test-external-links-in-documentation.md describing the decision to run external link checks once a month, alternatives considered, pros/cons, and known limitations (e.g. some sites such as GitHub may return forbidden and need exclusions).

Why:
- Move external link checks out of normal CI to avoid flaky failures caused by transient or third-party site issues.
- Run checks on a monthly schedule to get automated notifications of broken external links without impacting PR or unit-test workflows.

Notes:
- The new job uses mlc_config.json and checks docs/ (including copied README/CHANGELOG).
- The ADR documents tradeoffs and future work (e.g. filtering certain status responses).

Fix several bugs and improve cross-platform/Python3 compatibility in scripts/syncLang.py

What I changed
- Corrected parsing of comment lines: key extraction methods (key_from_line and __extract_key_and_value) now correctly skip lines that start with '#' or '!' (use logical AND instead of OR). This prevents commented lines from being interpreted as translation keys.
- Fixed a NameError in __compare_properties: renamed the typo keysobsolete to keys_obsolete so extended logging for obsolete keys works as intended.
- Made filename formatting platform-independent: __format_filename now uses os.path.basename / normalized paths instead of a Windows-only backslash replacement. This fixes incorrect file name display on POSIX systems.
- Replaced deprecated dict.has_key() usage with the modern 'in' operator for Python 3 compatibility.

Why
- The previous logic parsed commented lines as keys which produced wrong results (missing/obsolete/duplicate detection and updates were affected).
- The typo caused exceptions when extended logging tried to print obsolete keys.
- The Windows-only path handling made file-name formatting and comparisons unreliable on non-Windows platforms.
- Removing dict.has_key ensures the script runs under Python 3 without attribute errors.

Notes
- Behavior is otherwise unchanged: the script still reads/writes UTF-8 property files, detects/fixes duplicates, and generates status markdown.
- More improvements (e.g. handling the case where the repository base directory cannot be found and further Python3 modernization) can be done in follow-ups.

Summary: Adds timestamp checks for .bak files in BackupManager to avoid unnecessary "backup newer than data" dialogs when a .bak is older than the .bib file but contents differ (e.g., due to git, cloud sync, or manual edits).

Problem: Previously, if a .bak file's contents differed from the .bib, a dialog would be shown even when the .bak was older; this caused unwanted prompts in workflows that change timestamps externally.

Change: BackupManager now compares file last-modified timestamps in addition to content when deciding whether to prompt the user. If the .bak is older than the .bib, the dialog is skipped. Unit tests were added to cover the timestamp-aware behavior.

Tests: Added tests verifying the new timestamp check logic.

Fixes: Resolves https://github.com/koppor/jabref/issues/597. Follow-up to https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/9054.

Summary

What changed

- ChangeScanner
  - New constructor: ChangeScanner(BibDatabaseContext database) — removed referenceFile parameter.
  - Uses BibtexImporter (with DummyFileUpdateMonitor) to parse the file on disk and compares database contexts directly.

- ViewModels (collab)

    - String change/name change handling simplified: newString objects are used and non-null checks added (Objects.requireNonNull).

  - Updated to use hasStringByName and fixed a stray double semicolon.

  - LOGGER visibility changed to private static final.

Dependencies
- Includes PDFBox, Lucene, commons libraries, H2 MVStore, BouncyCastle, Antlr, JGit, Jackson, MariaDB & PostgreSQL drivers, Guava (with jsr305 exclusion), Jakarta APIs, JavaFX/controlsFx and many UI and utility libraries.
- Test libraries: JUnit5, Mockito, ArchUnit, TestFX, XMLUnit, ClassGraph and Hamcrest.
- Configured xjc artifacts and checkstyle.

Source generation and compile configuration
- Source-gen directory added to main sources and compileJava depends on generateSource.
- Tasks for ANTLR-generated sources: generateBstGrammarSource and generateSearchGrammarSource.
- XJC task generateCitaviSource and a JournalAbbreviationConverter task to generate journal DB resources.
- compileJava configured with additional module exports to access certain internal APIs (temporary workarounds).

Resource processing
- processResources expands build.properties and specific meta.xml files with version, year, maintainers and environment-provided API keys. Conditionally includes buildres/csl when jpackage is run.

Packaging and native images
- jlink configured with forceMerge and mergedModule corrections, plus jpackage settings for Windows, Linux and macOS (icons, resource dirs, installer options). OS-specific hooks to copy native-messaging hosts and helpers into the packaged images.

Testing, coverage and benchmarking
- test tasks use JUnit Platform; some tags excluded by default (DatabaseTest, FetcherTest, GUITest).
- Custom test tasks for databaseTest, fetcherTest and guiTest.
- Jacoco report composed from multiple test execution files; jacocoPrepare task sets tests to ignore failures when preparing instrumentation.
- JMH benchmarking plugin configured with warmup, iteration and fork settings.

Code quality and automated fixes
- OpenRewrite is configured with an active recipe and exclusions; failOnDryRunResults=true.
- Modernizer is enabled (not failing on violations), includes test classes and some exclusions.
- Checkstyle is present and only runs when invoked explicitly.

Miscellaneous
- Tasks to download dependencies to pre-warm caches and to clean generated sources. Several TODOs and workarounds are documented inline for future cleanup.

Add GroupDiff to detect changes in group metadata and ensure metadata application does not conflict with group-specific handling

What I changed
- Introduced org.jabref.logic.bibtex.comparator.GroupDiff
  - Encapsulates the original and new GroupTreeNode roots
  - Static compare(MetaData original, MetaData updated) returns an Optional<GroupDiff> if groups differ (handles Optional empties and uses equality check)
- Updated MetaDataChangeViewModel (gui/collab) to restore the original groups root when applying metadata changes:
  - database.setMetaData(metaDataDiff.getNewMetaData());
  - If group differences are present, reset database.getMetaData().setGroups(...) to the original group root to avoid inconsistencies because group changes are handled separately by GroupChangeViewModel
- Added unit tests GroupDiffTest covering:
  - both empty groups -> no diff
  - same group instance -> no diff
  - modified group structure -> diff returned with correct original/new roots

Why
- Metadata updates may contain group modifications but group changes are processed by a dedicated view model. Restoring the original group root when applying generic metadata updates prevents applying group changes twice or creating inconsistent state.
- GroupDiff provides a small, focused utility to detect whether groups changed between two MetaData instances and to expose the original/new roots for coordinated handling.

Tests
- GroupDiffTest ensures compare(...) behaves correctly for empty, identical, and modified group trees.

- Modified: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/collab/MetaDataChangeViewModel.java
- Added tests: src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/bibtex/comparator/GroupDiffTest.java

- No user-facing behavioral changes besides preventing inconsistent application of metadata/group changes; this is an internal correctness and robustness improvement.

Add a DOI lookup link to the Citation Relations tab

What this does
- Adds a visible 'Lookup DOI' link/button in the Citation Relations tab UI so users can quickly search for and attach a DOI to a cited work from that view.

Notes
- No changes to the DOI lookup API were required; this is a UI integration only.
- Includes changelog entry and brief doc note for the citations workflow.

Add several title-based formatters and citation-key modifiers

What changed
- Introduces four new Formatter implementations:
  - CamelFormatter: concatenates title words with initial capitals (CamelCase).
  - CamelNFormatter: same as CamelFormatter but limits output to the first N words (e.g. camel1, camel4).
  - ShortTitleFormatter: returns the first 3 words of a title, skipping function words.
  - VeryShortTitleFormatter: returns the first non-function word of a title.

- Registers the new formatters in Formatters.getTitleChangers() and includes them in getAll().
- Extends getFormatterForModifier(...) to support the new modifiers:
  - "shorttitle" and "veryshorttitle" return the corresponding formatters.
  - "camel" (no number) -> CamelFormatter; "camelN" (e.g. camel1, camel4) -> CamelNFormatter(N).
  - Regex-based behavior remains unchanged for modifiers starting with the regex key.

- Adds English localization entries for the new formatters and their descriptions.
- Adds unit tests in BracketedPatternTest to cover the new modifiers (camel, camelN, shorttitle, veryshorttitle).

Why
- These changes add convenient title-based transformations for citation key generation and cleanup tasks (compact CamelCase identifiers and short title variants).

Notes
- The new modifiers can be used in bracketed citation patterns (e.g. [title:camel], [title:camel1], [title:shorttitle], [title:veryshorttitle]).
- Existing behavior is preserved; this is an additive enhancement with accompanying tests and localization.
