Refactor and harden ImportHandler

Summary
- Refactors org.jabref.gui.externalfiles.ImportHandler to improve readability, maintainability and robustness when importing external files into a library.

Key changes
- Extracted helper methods to simplify the main import flow and reduce code duplication.
- Added defensive/null checks to avoid NPEs when no files are provided or when optional values are missing.
- Improved error handling and logging so failures during import report useful messages instead of failing silently or throwing unclear exceptions.
- Made file filtering/validation more robust (better handling of unsupported file types and directories).
- Ensured import tasks run off the UI thread and that UI updates are performed on the JavaFX thread to avoid concurrency issues.
- Fixed an edge-case bug where attempting to import an empty selection could cause an exception.

Behavior/API
- This is primarily an internal refactor with bug fixes and no intentional public API changes. Import behavior should be more stable and provide clearer feedback on errors.

Testing
- Manual testing of file import flows performed (single file, multiple files, unsupported types, empty selection). The refactor simplifies adding unit tests later.

Notes
- No other files were modified; callers of ImportHandler should continue to work unchanged.

text:
Add MainTable component to display and manage bibliography entries in a TableView.

This commit implements a fully-featured MainTable that integrates with the rest of the UI and application services. Key capabilities:

- Displays BibEntryTableViewModel items, binds sorting to the table comparator and persists visual state via PersistenceVisualStateTable.
- Row factory with handlers: double-click to open editor, context menu creation, drag-and-drop (detected/over/entered/exited/dropped) and mouse-drag selection support.
- Drag-and-drop support for files and local entry moves using a CustomLocalDragboard and DragAndDropDataFormats. Different drop zones (TOP/BOTTOM/CENTER) trigger different behaviors (import new entries vs. link/move/copy files to an entry) via ImportHandler.
- Clipboard support for copying, cutting and pasting entries using Globals.clipboardManager; paste inserts entries into the panel.
- Keyboard shortcuts wired through KeyBindingRepository: ENTER to edit, navigation (select first/last), and clipboard actions (copy/cut/paste) as well as default key propagation.
- Respects user preferences: column creation and sort order from preferences, optional smart column resize policy, and selection mode set to MULTIPLE.
- Registers for EntriesAddedEvent to select newly added entries, and exposes helpers like getSelectedEntries(), getEntryAt(), addSelectionListener(), and clearAndSelect methods.
- Integrates with ImportHandler, ExternalFileTypes, UndoManager, and application state (Globals) for cohesive behavior.

The MainTable is built to be modular and connected to existing services (BasePanel, JabRefFrame, BibDatabaseContext, preferences) and includes logging for drag operations.

text:
Summary

Fix author parsing for ACM Portal results so entries are produced when an author has only a family name. This resolves issue #10107 and is a follow-up to #10137.

What I changed

- ACMPortalParser: Replaced the previous naive concatenation of given + family names with a proper conversion to JabRef Author/AuthorList and formatting using last-first names ("Last, First") and the correct "and" separation. Authors that only provide a family name are handled correctly (they appear as just the family name).
  - Added helper getAuthorsLastFirst(JsonArray) to build Author objects safely when given or family may be missing.
  - Updated imports accordingly.

- Tests: Updated the existing ACMPortalParser test expectation to use last-first name formatting and added a new test testParseBibEntryWithFamilyAuthorOnly that asserts parsing works for an author entry that only contains a family name.

- Localization: Small cleanup to avoid using a static logger during very early initialization:
  - Annotated Localization with AllowedToUseStandardStreams and print to System.err when messages are not initialized.
  - Replaced static LOGGER usage with LoggerFactory.getLogger(...) inline for warnings that occur after initialization.

- CHANGELOG.md: Added a user-facing note about the fix.

Files changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/ACMPortalParser.java
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/ACMPortalParserTest.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/l10n/Localization.java
- CHANGELOG.md

Why

Previously the parser assumed both given and family names were present and concatenated them directly. When an author record lacked a given name, parsing created incorrect author strings and caused some ACM search results (where authors have only family names) to be missed. By using JabRef's Author/AuthorList model and formatting as last-first with proper handling of missing parts, the parser is robust and consistent with other importers.

Tests & compatibility

- Added unit tests covering the family-name-only scenario and updated existing tests to match the new formatting.
- Manually tested in running JabRef; unit tests pass.

Fixes: #10107

text:
Fix JavaFX WebView lifecycle and shutdown issues

Summary
- Prevent crashes and resource leaks related to JavaFX WebView usage during app runtime and shutdown. Ensure WebView instances are created and disposed on the JavaFX Application Thread and the JavaFX toolkit is managed correctly.

What I changed
- Ensure JavaFX toolkit is initialized and shut down in a safe way (JabRefMain, JabRefGUI).
- Centralize WebView creation and lifecycle management in WebViewStore; make creation lazy and always run on the JavaFX Application Thread.
- Make MathSciNetTab and PreviewViewer use WebViewStore for obtaining/disposing WebView instances to avoid illegal thread access and leaking WebView objects.
- Add proper disposal of WebView resources on tab close and application exit to avoid memory leaks and JVM hang on shutdown.
- Update CHANGELOG.md with an entry describing the bugfix.

Why
- WebView must be created and accessed only on the JavaFX Application Thread. Previous behavior could produce IllegalStateException, crashes on exit, or leaked native resources. Centralizing handling makes usage safer and reduces duplicated lifecycle logic.

Notes
- No user-facing behavior changes aside from more robust startup/shutdown and fewer crashes when using Preview or MathSciNet tabs that show HTML content.

Closes #3590

Summary

This change makes Recent Files store project-relative paths instead of absolute paths, improving portability when a project folder is moved or shared across machines.

What I changed

- LastFilesOpenedPreferences
  - Store last opened files and the last focused file as relative paths (relative to the current working directory) when constructing or setting values.
  - When exposing values to callers (getLastFilesOpened, getLastFocusedFile) the stored paths are converted back to absolute paths by resolving relative entries against the current working directory.
  - Added private helpers toRelative/toAbsolute with a safe fallback to the original absolute path on error.

- FileHistory
  - Convert files to relative paths when adding them to the history (doAdd and newFile) to persist project-relative entries.
  - Added toRelative/toAbsolute helpers similar to LastFilesOpenedPreferences.

Behavior notes

- Relative conversion uses Path.of("").toAbsolutePath() as the working directory and Path.relativize()/resolve() to convert between absolute and relative forms.
- If conversion fails, the code falls back to keeping the absolute path to avoid data loss.
- Consumers still receive absolute Paths when reading recent files, so existing usage remains compatible while storage becomes portable.

Testing

Steps to manually verify:
1. Open JabRef and open a .bib file inside a project folder.
2. Close JabRef.
3. Move the entire project folder to a new location (or copy it to another machine).
4. Reopen JabRef.
5. Confirm the Recent Files list resolves and opens the .bib file correctly (relative paths should allow resolving files after moving the folder).

Misc

- This PR closes #3590.
- No JUnit tests added in this change; the conversion logic is straightforward but could be covered by unit tests in a follow-up if desired.

Summary:
This PR improves the change scanner to make filesystem-change detection more accurate, more efficient, and more robust in real-world scenarios.

What's changed:
- Refactor core scanner logic for clarity and extensibility.
- Reduce false positives by better handling of timestamp drift and transient file metadata.
- Detect more types of changes: file renames/moves, permission/ownership changes, symlink target changes, and binary content changes.
- Add an incremental caching layer so repeated scans skip unchanged entries, improving performance on large trees.
- Parallelize file reads where safe to improve throughput on multi-core systems.
- Add configurable debounce/aggregation to collapse rapid successive file events into a single change notification.
- Improve logging and metrics (scan duration, files examined, cache hit/miss) to aid debugging and performance tuning.
- Add configuration options: scan_interval, include/exclude globs, follow_symlinks, detect_permission_changes, debounce_window.

Tests and validation:
- New unit tests and integration tests covering renames, permission changes, symlinks, and race conditions.
- Stress test script added to validate performance and stability on large repositories.

Backward compatibility and migration:
- Public scanner API remains backward compatible. New configuration options are opt-in with sensible defaults.
- No data migrations required.

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus review on the scanner core (scan loop, cache invalidation, comparison heuristics) and the new test cases.
- Pay attention to thread-safety in the parallel read/cache code paths.

How to test locally:
1. Run the full test suite: `npm test` (or equivalent). 
2. Use the stress test script to exercise large trees.
3. Manually test: create/rename/delete files, change permissions, update symlink targets, and verify expected change events are emitted.

This change should reduce noisy change reports and improve scan speed on large file sets while remaining configurable for edge cases.

Summary
- Reworked src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/ClipBoardManager.java to improve reliability and thread-safety of clipboard operations.

What changed
- Centralized clipboard access and clarified responsibilities of the class.
- Ensured clipboard read/write operations are executed on the JavaFX Application Thread to prevent threading issues on JavaFX platforms.
- Added null/empty checks and more robust exception handling to avoid runtime crashes when the system clipboard is unavailable or returns unexpected values.
- Simplified public API for copying and retrieving text (clearer method names and return semantics) to make callers easier to reason about.
- Added informative logging around clipboard errors to aid debugging on different platforms.

Why
- Clipboard interactions were a source of intermittent failures (NPEs and threading-related exceptions) across platforms. Running clipboard calls on the JavaFX thread and adding defensive checks reduces those runtime issues and improves application stability.

Notes for reviewers
- Verify that all existing callers of ClipBoardManager are updated to the new API/semantics and that behavior is unchanged from a user perspective.
- Manual testing recommended: copy/paste various entry formats, empty strings, and try on multiple platforms (Windows/macOS/Linux) to confirm no regressions.
- Possible follow-up: add unit/integration tests that mock clipboard access to exercise error paths.

text:
Summary

This PR adds/updates the project Gradle build configuration (build.gradle) to provide a complete, modernized build pipeline for JabRef including code generation, testing, packaging and code quality tooling.

Key changes / features

- Java/toolchain
  - Sets sourceCompatibility/targetCompatibility to Java 19 and configures a Java 20 toolchain.
  - Disables inferred modularity path (Eclipse workaround).

- Plugins
  - Adds/uses: application, modernizer, jmh, org.javamodularity.moduleplugin, javafx plugin, org.beryx.jlink, test-logger, jacoco, checkstyle, project-report, idea, openrewrite and a custom XJC plugin.

- Code generation
  - Adds src-gen sources to compilation and configures generation tasks:
    - ANTLR tasks: generateBstGrammarSource, generateSearchGrammarSource
    - XJC task: generateCitaviSource
    - generateJournalAbbreviationList to convert CSV to H2 MVStore
    - aggregate task generateSource depends on the above
  - compileJava depends on generateSource and sets the generatedSourceOutputDirectory.

- Dependencies
  - Declares runtime and compile dependencies for PDFBox, Lucene, Apache Commons, BouncyCastle, Antlr, Jackson, JDBC drivers (Postgres, MariaDB, Oracle), Guava (exclusion for jsr305), Jakarta APIs, JavaFX/controlsfx and many others used across the project.
  - dependencyLocking enabled (lockAllConfigurations).

- Testing & coverage
  - Configures JUnit 5 (JUnit Platform), Mockito, TestFX and ArchUnit integrations.
  - Adds specialized Test tasks: databaseTest, fetcherTest, guiTest (tag-based execution).
  - Integrates JaCoCo with combined execution data and generates csv/html/xml reports.
  - Test logging via gradle test-logger plugin (theme and output control).

- Packaging (jlink / jpackage)
  - Configures jlink with various merges/forceMerge workarounds to handle non-modular deps and custom mergedModule directives (provides/uses/require entries).
  - jpackage configuration for Windows, Linux and macOS with OS-specific image/installer options, icons, file associations and resource copying tasks.
  - OS-specific post-processing (copying native host files for distribution).

- Build/resource processing
  - processResources expands build.properties with version, year, maintainers and environment-provided API keys (if set).
  - Adds handling to include buildres/csl when jpackage task present.
  - UTF-8 encoding globally for compilation and javadoc.

- Code quality
  - Configures rewrite plugin with activeRecipe and exclusions.
  - modernizer settings (failOnViolations=false, includeTestClasses=true) and Checkstyle dependency.

- Miscellaneous
  - Adds convenience tasks: downloadDependencies (pre-fetch deps), deleteInstallerTemp, copyTestResources.
  - Applies several moduleOptions and addExports/addOpens workarounds for JavaFX and ControlsFX interop.
  - Many small build tweaks and comments documenting reasons/workarounds.

Testing / Validation

- Run full build: ./gradlew clean build
- Generate and verify sources: ./gradlew generateSource
- Run tests: ./gradlew test (or run databaseTest/fetcherTest/guiTest as needed)
- Create runtime image: ./gradlew jlink
- Create installer image: ./gradlew jpackage

Notes

- The build contains several explicit module export/open workarounds and forceMerge directives to cope with non-modular dependencies; these are documented inline and intended to be removed when upstream dependencies are fixed.
- Sensitive keys are read from environment variables and injected only into the generated build.properties.

This PR centralizes and documents the build setup and packaging steps to enable consistent local development and CI builds, including native installers for Windows/Linux/macOS.

Summary:
Adds observable support for preferences, specifically implementing reactive updates for Language and FileHistory preferences.

What this PR does:
- Introduces ObservablePreference<T> (and concrete implementations) so callers can subscribe to preference changes.
- Adds observable-backed Language preference handling so UI and services can react when the user changes language.
- Adds observable-backed FileHistory preference handling so recently opened files list updates propagate to subscribers.
- Ensures preference changes emit events on set/reset and deliver current value to new subscribers.

Why:
- Makes preference-driven state reactive, avoiding manual polling or ad-hoc event wiring.
- Simplifies keeping UI and background services synchronized with preference changes (e.g., language switching, file history updates).

Compatibility & Migration:
- Backwards compatible: existing synchronous preference getters/setters remain; new observable APIs are additive.
- No data migrations necessary; persisted preference formats unchanged.

Tests:
- Unit tests added for subscription behavior, change emission on set/reset, and initial value delivery.

Notes for reviewers:
- Review focuses: observable API contract (subscribe/unsubscribe semantics), emission timing, and persistence integration.
- Example usage: subscribe to language preference to trigger UI language reload or to file history to update recent files menu.

Files touched (high level):
- preference observable core implementation
- Language preference implementation
- FileHistory preference implementation
- Unit tests for observables and the two preference types

This change enables reactive preference handling while keeping the existing preference storage intact.

text:
Fix freeze on first entry selection after fresh start (#8446)

Summary
- Fixes a noticeable UI freeze (~3-4s) that occurs when selecting an entry for the first time after a fresh start. The freeze was caused by creating a new JavaFX WebView instance on the UI thread when the preview / MathSciNet tabs requested it.

What I changed
- Added a new utility: org.jabref.logic.util.WebViewStore
  - Preloads a configurable number of WebView instances at startup (default: 4) and keeps a small pool available.
  - Uses Platform.runLater() to create WebView instances so preloading does not block application startup.
  - Dynamically enqueues more instances when the pool drops below a configurable minimum (default: 2).
- Initialize the store at startup in JabRefGUI (WebViewStore.init()).
- Use WebViewStore.get() instead of new WebView() in:
  - PreviewViewer
  - MathSciNetTab
- Small cleanup in JabRefMain (removed an extra blank line).
- Added a user-facing changelog entry describing the fix (CHANGELOG.md).

Why
- Constructing a WebView the first time causes a blocking initialization inside the JavaFX WebEngine, which made the UI freeze when the preview was needed for the first time. Preloading WebView instances on the JavaFX thread before they are required avoids that initial blocking cost at the moment the user first selects an entry.

Notes about the implementation
- Default configuration: preload 4 instances and keep at least 2 as threshold. These values are in WebViewStore.Configuration and can be adjusted later if needed.
- WebView construction for preloading is scheduled via Platform.runLater to ensure it happens on the JavaFX Application Thread without delaying app startup.
- WebViewStore.get() will throw IllegalStateException if not initialized; init() is called from JabRefGUI so normal app startup covers this.

Testing
- Manually tested the fix; selecting the first entry after fresh start no longer causes the 3-4s freeze. A video demonstrating the fix was included in the original issue.

Related
- Fixes #8446

Checklist
- CHANGELOG.md entry added
- Manually tested in running JabRef
- No automated tests added (UI behavior)

text:
RIS importer: accept valid DOIs that don't include the "doi:" prefix

What I changed
- In RisImporter.addDoi, if the incoming value does not start with a "doi:" prefix, we now validate the value against a conservative DOI pattern and store it if it matches.

Why
- Some RIS files include raw DOIs without the "doi:" prefix. Previously these were ignored unless prefixed with "doi:". This change makes DOI extraction more robust by accepting properly-formed DOIs even when the prefix is missing.

Details
- The implementation adds a fallback that checks the value against a DOI regex (matches strings starting with "10.", at least four digits in the registrant code, optional sub-registrant parts, a slash, and a suffix that excludes quotes, ampersands and apostrophes). If the value matches, it is stored in StandardField.DOI; otherwise behavior is unchanged.

No breaking changes expected: only additional DOI detection for well-formed DOI strings without the "doi:" prefix.

Summary

Refactor and improve the automatic linking and synchronization of external files in the GUI. This change consolidates the logic used to detect and attach files to entries, ensures consistency with configured external file types, and fixes several issues around file synchronization and the Find Full Text action.

What I changed

- Consolidated auto-linking logic into AutoSetFileLinksUtil and adjusted AutoSetLinks to use the new utilities.
- Updated FindFullTextAction to use the improved auto-set linking behavior and to better handle different file type preferences.
- Improved SynchronizeFileField to ensure file field state stays consistent after file operations (e.g. renames/moves) and to better update the UI.
- Enhanced ExternalFileTypes handling to make type detection and preference handling more reliable when auto-linking files.
- Updated LinkedFilesEditorViewModel to reflect changes in the auto-linking behavior and to ensure UI updates when linked files change.
- Added/updated unit tests (AutoSetFileLinksUtilTest) to cover the main auto-linking cases, including preferred file type selection and edge cases.

Motivation

Users expect automatic detection and linking of local files (PDFs, supplements, etc.) to be reliable and to respect the configured external file types. Previously the auto-linking logic was scattered and sometimes chose incorrect files or failed to update the UI after synchronization. This PR centralizes and stabilizes that behavior.

Behavioral notes

- Auto-linking now considers configured external file types and user preferences when choosing which files to attach.
- Find Full Text will leverage the improved auto-linking flows when saving discovered files.
- SynchronizeFileField will better keep the file field and the UI consistent after file system changes.

Tests

- AutoSetFileLinksUtilTest was added/updated to validate selection logic and to guard against regressions.

Compatibility

No public API changes outside the GUI/utility classes. Existing user data and file links are preserved; behavior for which file gets linked may change to align with external file type preferences.

Notes for reviewers

- Focus on AutoSetFileLinksUtil for the core logic changes.
- Verify that ExternalFileTypes detection still matches expectations for custom types.
- UI should update properly after running SynchronizeFileField and after running Find Full Text.

Summary

Fixes a bug where an empty fallback directory setting was treated as a valid directory, causing incorrect path resolution or runtime errors. This is a follow-up to #9113.

What I changed

- Treat empty or whitespace-only fallback directory values as "not set" instead of a valid path.
- Added defensive checks where the fallback directory is read and used so the code falls back to the normal default resolution (e.g. database directory or system default) when the setting is empty.
- Ensured callers handle the absent fallback directory correctly instead of relying on an empty string.

Why

Previously an empty fallback directory string could be interpreted as a real path and lead to unexpected behavior when resolving file locations. With these changes the application will behave consistently whether the user clears the fallback setting or never set it.

Testing

- Manually reproduced the original failure by configuring an empty fallback directory and exercising the flows that resolve file locations; the issue no longer occurs.
- Verified default resolution still works when a valid fallback is not configured.

Compatibility

No breaking changes or migration steps required.

Fixes

Add new "File" preferences tab to configure file-related options

This PR introduces a dedicated FileTab in the preferences UI (moved out of GeneralTab to resolve space issues) and wires it to JabRefPreferences. Key features and behavior:

- UI elements
  - Main file directory field with a Browse button (uses FileDialog)
  - Options to prefer the BIB file location as primary file directory
  - Automatic file-search and auto-open-browse toggles for linked files
  - Autolink matching mode radio buttons:
    - match files starting with the BibTeX key
    - match exact BibTeX key only
    - use regular expression search (enables an editable regex field)
    - Help button linking to regex documentation
  - Newline separator selector (CR / CR/LF / LF)
  - Backup, autosave (local), and "open last edited databases" checkboxes
  - "Always reformat BIB file on save and export" checkbox
  - String resolution options (resolve for standard fields or all fields + exclude list)
  - Non-wrappable fields and "do not resolve strings for" text fields
  - Help button for autosave

- Persistence & behavior
  - All controls read from preferences in setValues() and write back in storeSettings()
  - When newline separator is changed it is saved to preferences and OS.NEWLINE is updated accordingly
  - Regex expression is only saved if the regex autolink mode is selected
  - Non-wrappable fields are only written back if changed

- Validation
  - validateSettings() verifies that the configured main file directory exists and is a directory; shows an error dialog if invalid

Notes
- The tab uses Localization for labels and HelpAction for contextual help
- The implementation centralizes file options into their own tab and keeps preference read/write/validation logic in the tab

This change prepares the preferences UI for clearer organization of file-related settings and persists all settings via JabRefPreferences.

text:
Improve author name parsing and normalization

This PR enhances the AuthorListParser and the name normalization logic to correctly handle a wider range of real-world name formats and edge cases. Key changes:

- Add handling for name affixes and particles (e.g. jr, sr, von, van, der, zu) to avoid incorrect splitting when parsing comma-separated name lists.
- Better support for semicolon and explicit "AND" separators and mixed separators; correctly convert comma-separated last-first lists into the internal "and"-separated representation when appropriate.
- Improve tokenization to correctly recognize abbreviations, hyphenated names and TeX commands; added TEX_NAMES to properly treat TeX accent commands as name starts/letters.
- Correct detection of token case (including Han script) and token terminators (space vs. dash), preventing wrong partitioning of tokens containing hyphens.
- Fix edge cases such as single-comma inputs, odd counts of commas, and lists that include braces or special characters.
- Add/adjust comprehensive unit tests (NormalizeNamesFormatterTest and AuthorListParserTest) to cover many cases: multi-part names, particles (de la, al-Ṣāliḥ), TeX-encoded names, non-Latin characters, initials and abbreviations, multiple affixes, and mixed separators.

These changes improve robustness of author parsing and name normalization across international names and noisy input formats, and address several previously failing cases in the test-suite.

- Defer initial divider setup to the JavaFX application thread using Platform.runLater so layout bounds are available before setting the divider and removing the listener.

- Persist the side pane size in pixels by subscribing to sidePane.widthProperty() and saving width values, instead of subscribing to the divider position property.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to mention the fix.

Why:
Previously the divider position was set too early (before the SplitPane had a proper width) and persistence used inconsistent units, which caused the side pane width to not be remembered after restarting JabRef.

Testing/notes:
- Verified that the side pane width is restored after restart.
- Resizing the side pane updates the saved width.
- The initial listener is removed after the deferred setup to avoid repeated calls.

Add ACM Portal importer and improve localization bundle handling

- Introduce ACMPortalParser to parse ACM Digital Library search result pages and retrieve BibTeX/BibJSON data via the ACM exportCiteProcCitation endpoint. Key features:
  - parseDoiSearchPage: extracts DOIs from ACM search HTML results
  - getUrlFromDoiList: builds the DOI export URL (properly URL-encoded)
  - getBibEntriesFromDoiList: downloads and parses JSON results into JabRef BibEntry objects
  - parseBibEntry: maps common CiteProc fields to JabRef fields (type mapping including PAPER_CONFERENCE -> Conference, title, container-title -> booktitle, collection-title -> series, DOI, URL, ISBN, publisher, publisher-place -> address, event-place -> location, pages, number-of-pages -> pagetotal, abstract, keywords)
  - Author handling: supports entries with given and/or family names, and family-only authors (produces last-first names when appropriate)
  - Date handling: maps issued.date-parts to YEAR, MONTH, DAY fields
  - Keywords: splits by comma-space, sorts alphabetically and joins with ", "
  - Network and error handling with FetcherException for IO/URI errors

- Add comprehensive unit tests in ACMPortalParserTest covering:
  - parsing DOI search pages
  - building the export URL
  - parsing JSON results into BibEntry instances (including a case with family-only author)
  - end-to-end parseEntries against ACM search URL (integration-style test)
  - behaviour when no entries are found

- Localization improvements in Localization.java:
  - Add lazy initialization guard in lang to warn and fall back to English when localization is accessed before initialization
  - Cache message bundles in LocalizationBundle via createLookupMap for faster access and to support JavaFX inline binding
  - LocalizationBundle now implements containsKey to pretend all keys exist and handleGetObject returns the key if no translation was found, avoiding runtime lookup failures
  - Improved setLanguage to avoid unnecessary reinitialization and to log a warning and fall back to English when an unsupported language is requested

These changes add ACM DL support and strengthen localization robustness. Unit tests ensure parsing correctness and cover edge cases like family-only authors and keyword sorting.

Add GUI logging appender and JavaFX task utilities; support localized exception messages

- Implement DefaultTaskExecutor helpers:
  - runInJavaFXThread(Callable<V>) executes a Callable on the JavaFX thread and returns its result by wrapping it in a FutureTask and using Platform.runLater, handling InterruptedException and ExecutionException.
  - runInJavaFXThread(Runnable) convenience method for async execution on the JavaFX thread.
  - execute(BackgroundTask<V>) launches background tasks on a new Thread and maps the BackgroundTask lifecycle callbacks (onRunning, onSuccess, onException) to a javafx.concurrent.Task, converting Throwables to Exceptions as needed.
- Extend JabRefException to support an optional localizedMessage field and override getLocalizedMessage() to return the localized text when available; otherwise log a debug message and fall back to getMessage().

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/logging/GuiAppender.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/util/DefaultTaskExecutor.java

Summary

This PR fixes issues in the XMP exporter to make exported .xmp files compatible with LaTeX's xmpincl package and improves handling of date/month information extracted from Dublin Core metadata.

Key changes

- Remove XMP packet declaration header/footer from generated Dublin Core XMP content so that .xmp files can be included by the xmpincl LaTeX package.
  - Added XmpUtilWriter.generateXmpStringWithoutXmpDeclaration and XmpUtilWriter.generateXmpStringWithXmpDeclaration.
  - XmpExporter now writes the stripped XMP content to disk.

- Improve extraction of year and month from Dublin Core metadata to avoid misinterpreting default calendar values (PDFBox sets missing months to January 1).
  - Treat a parsed date of YYYY-01-01 as "no month present" to avoid adding spurious January months.
  - When a month is present, set the BibEntry month field using the short month name.
  - Added a workaround to parse and override month values from bibtex/ relationship entries embedded in XMP (some XMP producers put BibTeX fields in relations). This uses a filter/consumer to split bibtex/key/value entries and specially normalizes the month field.
  - This addresses cases where PDFBox's XMP date handling is corrupted; a PDFBox issue is referenced (PDFBOX-4196).

- Tests and resources updated
  - Adjusted unit tests (XmpExporterTest) to new output layout (line counts and affected line indexes changed because the XMP packet tags are removed).
  - Updated test resource month value to the short form (mar) to match month parsing and expectations.

Files changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/exporter/XmpExporter.java
  - Use generateXmpStringWithoutXmpDeclaration when writing XMP files.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/xmp/XmpUtilWriter.java

- Improvements and bug fixes for external files handling and full-text download features.

What changed
- External files
  - Refactored ExternalFilesEntryLinker and AutoSetFileLinksUtil to improve automatic detection and linking of external files to entries. More robust handling of existing links and edge cases (missing metadata, multiple candidate files).

Compatibility and migration
- No breaking API changes expected for public APIs. Internal behavior for external-file linking improved; existing linked files should continue to work. Please test workflows that rely on automatic linking and full-text downloads.

This PR refactors and enhances the main application frame (JabRefFrame) and wires up several UI features and behaviors:

Key changes
- Integrates WelcomeTab: a welcome screen/tab is shown and selectable when no library is open.
- Adds and wires FileHistoryMenu for quick access to recently opened libraries; supports keyboard selection while the menu is open.
- Adds SidePane support: dynamically inserts/removes the side pane into the main SplitPane, persists and restores divider width in preferences, and keeps the side pane non-resizable with parent.
- Initializes GlobalSearchBar and connects it to the StateManager (including auto-completer updates when switching libraries).
- Sets up MainMenu and MainToolBar and composes them into the top of the frame.
- Implements drag & drop handler (FrameDndHandler) initialization for tabs.
- Adds comprehensive key bindings (initKeyBindings) to handle focus switching, library navigation, opening the global search dialog, and many NewEntry actions (article, book, inbook, master/PhD thesis, proceedings, techreport, unpublished, inproceedings).
- Maintains a list of open databases (openDatabaseList) via EasyBind mapping and binds it to StateManager.
- Properly updates StateManager when tabs are selected/closed and ensures focus/selected entries are kept in sync when switching tabs.
- Implements logic to hide the tab bar when the preferences request it and only one library is open (adds/removes CSS class "hide-tab-bar").
- Adds tab context menu creation for library tabs (Library properties, Open database folder, Open console, Close/Close others/Close all).
- Adds robust close operations: close single tab, multiple tabs, close others, close all; ensures requestClose checks and Event firing for Tab.CLOSED_EVENT.
- Introduces OpenDatabaseFolder action to open and select the database file in the OS file manager (with IOException handling).
- Delegates UI commands to the JabRefFrameViewModel via handleUiCommands.

Implementation details
- Uses EasyBind / EasyObservableList for reactive view-model/list synchronization.
- Persists side pane width to GuiPreferences and listens for side pane width changes.
- Uses Injector to provide services (BuildInfo, JournalAbbreviationRepository, UiMessageHandler) and to instantiate some services.
- Keeps mainStage title bound to the current LibraryTab title and falls back to FRAME_TITLE when no library tab is selected.

Testing notes / QA
- Opening and closing libraries should correctly add/remove tabs and update StateManager.activeDatabase and window title.
- When no library is open, the Welcome tab should be shown; selecting it should clear active database state.
- Side pane: adding/removing components should hide/show the pane and persist divider position between sessions.
- File history menu: pressing keys while the menu is open should open the corresponding file.
- Keybindings listed above should trigger the correct actions and focus changes.
- Right-clicking a tab should show the full context menu and actions should behave as expected (including Open database folder error handling).

This change consolidates multiple frame-level responsibilities and improves the startup and tab management UX.

Summary
- Refactor and clean up special-fields, preferences, and clipboard handling. Disable automatic synchronization of special fields to keywords by default.

Key changes
- Default behavior: automatic synchronization of special fields to keywords is now disabled by default (JabRefPreferences default changed). CHANGELOG updated accordingly.
- Preferences API
  - SpecialFieldsPreferences: renamed getters to more idiomatic names: isSpecialFieldsEnabled(), shouldAutoSyncSpecialFieldsToKeyWords(), shouldSerializeSpecialFields(), and added isKeywordSyncEnabled() (computed: enabled && autoSync).
  - PreferencesService: removed isKeywordSyncEnabled() from the interface; import/save preferences now use SpecialFieldsPreferences.isKeywordSyncEnabled().
  - JabRefPreferences now stores/reads using the new method names and changed defaults (AUTOSYNCSPECIALFIELDSTOKEYWORDS -> false, SERIALIZESPECIALFIELDS -> true).
- Keyword synchronization checks updated across codebase to use preferences.getSpecialFieldsPreferences().isKeywordSyncEnabled() instead of the old isKeywordSyncEnabled()/boolean preference checks.

Clipboard & dependency injection
- Replaced direct uses of Globals.clipboardManager with an injected ClipBoardManager in several UI places (MainTable, RightClickMenu, Copy/CopyCitation/ExportToClipboard actions). RightClickMenu.create and MainTable constructors now accept ClipBoardManager.

ParserResult & Path handling
- ParserResult now exposes getPath() returning Optional<Path> and deprecates getFile() (use getPath()). addParserResult now compares database paths against parserResult.getPath().
- getErrorMessage simplified to String.join.

Code cleanups & small refactors
- Replaced many switch statements with modern switch expressions in several viewmodels (SpecialFieldValueViewModel, SpecialFieldViewModel, TableTabViewModel) and used lambda formatting improvements.
- Minor renames for clarity (e.g., be -> bibEntry) and small lambda simplifications (onDragExited handler condensed).
- SpecialFieldAction and other callers updated to pass the new keyword-sync preference through the updated API.
- updateAllTabTitles adjusted to use getFileName().toString() for path comparisons.

Deprecations & breaking changes
- ParserResult.getFile() is deprecated; use getPath() instead.
- PreferencesService had isKeywordSyncEnabled() removed — use getSpecialFieldsPreferences().isKeywordSyncEnabled().
- Several constructors/methods now require a ClipBoardManager parameter (MainTable, RightClickMenu.create and copy submenu helpers). Update callers accordingly.
- Method name changes in SpecialFieldsPreferences (getter renames) require updates if consumed externally.

Notes
- Because automatic special-field -> keyword synchronization is now off by default, users who relied on that behavior will need to re-enable it in preferences if desired.
- Mostly internal/API refactors and code modernization; functional behavior is preserved except for the default sync change and preference default adjustments.

Summary:
This PR fixes a focus-stealing issue in the entry editor that caused the editor to aggressively take focus from the search field or main table (see #5084). As a result users could inadvertently overwrite search text or were unable to navigate entries with the keyboard. The editor no longer automatically restores or forces focus to the first field.

What I changed:
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to mention the bugfix for focus stealing (#5084).
- Modified FieldsEditorTab.java:
  - Removed the activeField field and related bookkeeping.
  - Stopped forcing focus when binding an entry (removed the Platform.runLater focus restore logic).
  - Simplified requestFocus() to directly focus the requested field without updating any active state.
  - Removed handleFocus() override and unused imports (Optional, Platform).
  - Cleaned up selection-detection logic that was used only to restore focus.

Why:
The entry editor previously attempted to restore focus to a field whenever an entry was bound. This caused the editor to steal focus during unrelated actions (searching, table navigation). Removing the automatic focus restore prevents unexpected cursor jumps while preserving the ability to explicitly request focus for a specific field when needed.

Notes:
- Fixes #5084.
- CHANGELOG entry added.
- Manually tested the behavior in a running JabRef build.
- No unit tests were added in this change.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/FieldsEditorTab.java

Fixes issue #6541: opening Library > Library Properties incorrectly changed the library saving status by triggering save-actions-related metadata changes. This PR prevents that by removing the metadata comment that was causing a postChange event.

Problem:
When opening Library Properties a comment block like the following was added to .bib/.sav files and triggered setSaveActions->postChange:
@Comment{jabref-meta: saveActions:disabled; ... }
This caused the UI to show an incorrect saving state and fired unnecessary metadata change events.

What I changed:
- Removed the code that inserts that comment into the metadata (in MetaData#setSaveActions). This prevents the postChange trigger when opening Library Properties.
- No UI changes except hiding the event trigger when opening Library > Library Properties.

Files touched:
- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/metadata/MetaData.java (removed the line that added the saveActions comment / triggered postChange)

Testing:
- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance; opening Library Properties no longer changes the saving status.
- Screenshot demonstrating the fixed behavior is included in the PR description.
- No automated tests added (difficult to reproduce this behavior in unit tests).

Notes for reviewers:
- I removed the problematic comment insertion because it fired postChange. I wasn’t able to find an immediate harmful side effect of removing it, but I would appreciate a review to ensure this change does not cause regressions.
- If there is a desired way to persist saveActions state without triggering postChange, we could consider a more targeted fix later.

- Open the Library tab, change a preference, switch tabs quickly, then save preferences — the app should not throw an exception.

Automated
- New tests cover saving prefs when the Library tab is mounted and unmounted; CI should pass.

Risk and migration

Low risk. Behavior of saving preferences is unchanged for users; this only hardens the code path to avoid exceptions. No data migrations required.

Add option to sync JabRef theme with OS preference

Summary
- Introduces a new preference “Use System Preference” that, when enabled, makes JabRef follow the OS light/dark theme.
- Implements runtime detection of OS theme changes and updates the application theme accordingly.
- Adds the required library and integrates it into the module system and build.

Key changes

  - Preferences → General: added a CheckBox (themeSyncOs) labeled “Use System Preference”. When enabled, the theme ComboBox and custom theme controls are disabled.

- ViewModel / Preference wiring
  - GeneralTabViewModel: added themeSyncOsProperty, bound to the UI, loaded from and stored to WorkspacePreferences.
  - GeneralTab: binds the new CheckBox to the view model.

- Preferences / persistence
  - JabRefPreferences: added THEME_SYNC_OS key (default false) and updated usage of THEME key; persists and loads the new setting.
  - WorkspacePreferences: new BooleanProperty themeSyncOs with getters/setters and included in constructor and factory usage.

- Theme management
  - Added dependency on jSystemThemeDetector and required module declaration (com.jthemedetector).
  - ThemeManager: registers an OS theme listener to update the theme on OS changes. If theme-sync is enabled in preferences, the OS preference overrides the stored theme selection (switching to light/dark accordingly).
  - Minor cleanup of additional stylesheet handling.

- Build & docs
  - build.gradle: added implementation 'com.github.Dansoftowner:jSystemThemeDetector:3.6'.
  - external-libraries.md: documented jSystemThemeDetector dependency and license.

Behavior notes / testing
- Default behavior is unchanged (themeSyncOs = false). If users enable “Use System Preference”, their selected theme is overridden by OS preference and the UI disables manual theme controls.
- Theme changes triggered by the OS are applied at runtime via the detector listener.

Related issue
- Fixes / implements: #8729

- This PR fixes a bug where jstyle validation failed if the configuration began with a default section. Previously the parser/validator did not accept a default section as the first section and reported the file as invalid.

Root cause
- The section detection logic assumed at least one non-default section would precede a default block, so a default section at index 0 was treated as an unexpected token and rejected.

- Adjusted the section parsing/validation logic to allow a default section at the start of the file.
- Ensured the parser sets the default-section state correctly when 'default' is encountered first, without requiring preceding sections.
- Added unit tests that cover the previously failing scenarios: default-only files, default at the start followed by named sections, and default at the start alone.

Testing
- Added tests that assert validity for configurations that start with a default section.
- All existing tests updated to confirm no regressions.

Compatibility
- No breaking changes. Existing configurations remain valid; this just widens accepted input to include default-at-start cases.

How to verify locally
1. Run the test suite (unit tests were added). 2. Validate a jstyle file that begins with a default section; it should now pass validation.

text:
Summary

Fixes intermittent NullPointerException in search tests caused by races when closing Lucene indexes. The index close operation ran asynchronously on a different executor, allowing a subsequent test to access the index while it was still being closed.

Root cause

- Multiple tests shared the same fulltext index path and closing the index happens asynchronously using HeadlessExecutorService.INSTANCE. A following test could start and try to access the index before the previous close operation completed, causing NPEs on CI.
- Using CurrentThreadTaskExecutor in tests did not help because the index close tasks use a different executor.

What this PR changes

- Adds a synchronous closeAndWait method to the LuceneIndexer interface and implements it in all indexer implementations (BibFieldsIndexer, DefaultLinkedFilesIndexer, ReadOnlyLinkedFilesIndexer). These use HeadlessExecutorService.INSTANCE.executeAndWait to ensure index closing is finished.
- Adds LuceneManager.closeAndWait which calls the indexers' closeAndWait and removes the preferences listener, then posts IndexClosedEvent.
- DatabaseSearcher now uses luceneManager.closeAndWait both when the query is invalid and after performing a search, ensuring the close finished before the test proceeds.
- Tests updated to isolate index paths using @TempDir and to spy the BibDatabaseContext so getFulltextIndexPath() returns the temporary directory. This isolates tests from each other and prevents interference.

Files changed (high level)

- Production: DatabaseSearcher, LuceneManager, LuceneIndexer (interface), BibFieldsIndexer, DefaultLinkedFilesIndexer, ReadOnlyLinkedFilesIndexer
- Tests: DatabaseSearcherTest, DatabaseSearcherWithBibFilesTest

Notes

- Using @TempDir alone was not sufficient because the temporary directory could be removed before the asynchronous close completed; adding closeAndWait ensures the close completes before cleanup/test teardown proceeds.
- This is a follow-up to PR #11542 and closes the intermittent failure reported in the melting-pot issue tracker.

Related issues

- Closes: https://github.com/JabRef/jabref-issue-melting-pot/issues/527
- Follow-up to: #11542

Testing

- Updated unit tests now use a temporary index directory and wait for index closing to complete, preventing the race that caused intermittent NPEs on CI.

Summary:
- Implement search history recording so user (and anonymous session) searches are stored for later review.

What this PR does:
- Adds a SearchHistory model and database migration (fields: id, user_id nullable, session_id, query, filters json, results_count, created_at).
- Persists a search history entry whenever a search is executed (backend integration with the existing search endpoint).
- Frontend: captures search events and sends them to the backend. Adds a simple Search History view with pagination and actions to re-run or delete entries.
- Adds a cleanup job to purge entries older than the configurable retention period (default: 90 days).
- Adds tests for model, API recording, UI history listing, delete action, and retention cleanup.

Motivation:
- Allow users to review and re-run past searches, improving discoverability and productivity.
- Provide an auditable history while keeping privacy controls and automated retention.

How to test:
1. Run database migrations.
2. Perform a search as an authenticated user and as an anonymous session; verify SearchHistory entries are created with expected fields.
3. Visit the Search History page; verify entries are listed, pagination works, re-run opens the search with previous parameters, and delete removes the entry.
4. Run the retention cleanup job and verify entries older than retention period are deleted.

Notes & considerations:
- Privacy: user can opt out of search history recording (config flag added). Consider communicating retention policy to users.
- Indexes added on user_id and created_at to keep queries performant.
- Backward-compatible: if search history recording is disabled, no records will be created.

Summary: Fixes an issue where the Postgres instance process would unexpectedly close. This change improves lifecycle management and error handling to prevent premature shutdowns.

What was happening: Under certain conditions the Postgres instance process exited early due to an unhandled error and missing cleanup/restart logic. This led to transient database unavailability and required manual restarts.

Root cause: The process shutdown was triggered by an unhandled exception and by improper handling of connection/child process cleanup. In some cases a terminated child was not reaped and a shutdown path was invoked incorrectly.

What I changed: - Added robust error handling around the Postgres instance startup and runtime loops so unexpected errors no longer cause an immediate process exit. - Ensured proper cleanup and reaping of child processes to avoid spurious shutdown logic. - Introduced retry/recovery logic to attempt a graceful restart when recoverable errors occur instead of closing the whole process. - Improved logging around start/stop events and error conditions to aid future debugging. - Added tests to cover the previously failing shutdown scenario and the new recovery behavior.

Testing: Unit and integration tests added to reproduce the premature close and verify the new recovery flow. Manual testing performed to validate that the instance remains up when recoverable errors occur and that non-recoverable errors still surface appropriately.

Compatibility and impact: Backwards compatible. No database migrations required. This change reduces incidents of unexpected Postgres downtime and should improve overall service stability.

Notes: If you see any remaining edge cases where the instance still exits unexpectedly, enable the enhanced logs and share the trace so we can iterate further.

text:
Closes #12188

Summary

This fixes an issue where LaTeX commands (e.g., \mkbibquote{...}) were retained in generated filenames when using patterns that include the full title (for example, "[bibtexkey] - [fulltitle]"). Previously, filenames could contain transformed LaTeX fragments such as "_mkbibquote_Community_" instead of the intended "Community".

What I changed

- Ensure LaTeX commands are removed when generating filenames from patterns by applying RemoveLatexCommandsFormatter.format() before FileNameCleaner.cleanFileName().
- The change affects the path where filenames are created for linked file renaming (used by LinkedFileHandler -> FileUtil.createFileNameFromPattern()).

Why

FileNameCleaner removed illegal filename characters but did not strip LaTeX commands. Applying RemoveLatexCommandsFormatter first preserves the inner content of commands while removing the command syntax, producing correct, readable filenames.

Example

- Input title: Building \mkbibquote{Community}
- File pattern: [bibtexkey] - [fulltitle]
- Old output: BrayBuildingCommunity - Building _mkbibquote_Community_.pdf
- New output: BrayBuildingCommunity - Building Community.pdf

Tests and checklist

- Tests added to cover the new behavior.
- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance.

Fixes #7016 — Ensure toggling of special fields works correctly for sorted entries

What I changed
- When toggling special fields on selected entries, I now make a copy of the selected entries list and perform the field changes on that copy. This prevents the sort strategy (which can reorder the selection list during the operation) from influencing the result.

Why
- The original implementation iterated directly over the selected entries. That caused a ConcurrentModificationException when the selection was mutated during iteration. Replacing the for-each with a normal for loop removed the exception but still allowed the list order to change during the loop, so toggling could produce incorrect results. Making a copy of the selection before modifying entries fixes both issues.

Notes
- Manual testing of the changed feature in a running JabRef was completed successfully.
- CHANGELOG.md was updated accordingly.
- No automated tests were added in this PR.
- Documentation was checked for relevance.

text:
Summary
Fix a race condition in the abbreviate action that caused incorrect results and occasional exceptions when the action was run concurrently.

Problem
The abbreviate implementation used shared mutable state across invocations (temporary buffers/cache), which was not thread-safe. Under concurrent requests this led to corrupted output and sporadic crashes.

What I changed
- Removed shared mutable fields used during abbreviation.
- Introduced thread-safe alternatives: ThreadLocal for temporary buffers and ConcurrentHashMap for the cache, and guarded cache population to avoid races.
- Cleaned up lifecycle so no per-request state is retained between calls.
- Added logging around the critical path to aid future debugging.

Tests
- Added unit tests that exercise the abbreviate action concurrently (stress test with many threads) to ensure deterministic results and no exceptions.
- Added regression tests covering inputs that previously triggered the race.

Impact
- Bugfix only; behavior is unchanged for single-threaded use and now correct for concurrent use.
- Slight change in memory/perf characteristics due to thread-local buffers and concurrent cache, but this is an intentional trade-off for correctness.

Files changed (high level)
- AbbreviateAction implementation (thread-safety fixes)
- New concurrency/regression unit tests

Notes
This is a non-breaking fix. If you notice any performance regressions in very large deployments, we can tune the cache sizing or buffer reuse strategy in a follow-up.

Summary

This PR adds a new "Send" feature to JabRef that groups two mailing actions under a single submenu: "As Email" and "To Kindle". It implements the requested ability to send selected entry attachments to a configured Kindle e-mail address, and centralizes sending-related menu items under a single Send menu in the main Tools menu and the entry context (right-click) menu. Fixes #6186.

What changed

- UI
  - Introduced a new "Send" submenu in the main application menu and the table right-click menu containing:
    - "As Email" — populates an email body with BibTeX content for the selected entries.
    - "To Kindle" — sends linked file attachments for the selected entries to the user's Kindle email.
  - Added a new text field in Preferences -> External programs to store the Kindle email address.
  - Updated localization strings for the new menu entries and preference label.
  - Updated CHANGELOG with a user-facing description of the added Send menu and Kindle option.

- Code/Behavior
  - Refactored SendAsEMailAction into an abstract base that handles common mailing plumbing (mailto URI creation and Desktop.mail invocation).
  - Added SendAsStandardEmailAction which fills the email body with BibTeX for the selected entries and uses the configured email subject preference.
  - Added SendAsKindleEmailAction which targets the Kindle email from preferences and only enables when selected entries have linked files.
  - Attachments: the implementation collects linked files for selected entries and appends them as "Attachment" parameters in the mailto URI. Because the mailto "attachment" parameter is unofficial and not handled uniformly, the code also optionally opens the folders containing attachments (controlled by the existing preference "Automatically open folders of attached files") to help users attach files in mail clients that don't accept the parameter.
  - New preference key: KINDLE_EMAIL added to store the Kindle address.

Files touched (high level)
- Added: SendAsKindleEmailAction.java, SendAsStandardEmailAction.java
- Modified: SendAsEMailAction.java (refactor to abstract), JabRefFrame.java (menu), RightClickMenu.java (context menu), preferences classes and GUI (ExternalTab.fxml, ExternalTab.java, ExternalTabViewModel.java, ExternalApplicationsPreferences.java, JabRefPreferences.java), localization file (JabRef_en.properties), CHANGELOG.md

Notes

- The Kindle action is enabled only when entries are selected and when those entries have linked files (so there are files to send).
- The standard email action remains available to create an email body containing BibTeX of the selected entries.
- The implementation uses java.awt.Desktop.mail(URI) with a mailto URI and unofficial "Attachment" parameters; because support for attachments via mailto is inconsistent across mail clients, the existing preference to auto-open attachment folders is leveraged to help the user.

Testing

- Manually tested the new menu placement, enabling/disabling behavior, preference persistence for Kindle email, and the mailer invocation on macOS/Windows/Linux desktop environments.
- Screenshots of the changed UI are included in the PR description.

Developer notes

- Localization entries and preference wiring were added so the new preference shows up in the External programs tab and is persisted.
- No automated tests were added with this PR; the feature was manually verified.

Related issue

- Fixes #6186

- This is an internal API change for how context menus are supplied to EditorTextArea; callers in this repo have been updated accordingly.

text:
Closes #12894

Summary

Fixes a bug that caused a library to become hidden when closing a tab located directly to the right of the Welcome tab while two libraries and the Welcome tab were open. After closing a library tab, the tab-selection logic could fall back to the Welcome tab and cause an unintended library disappearance. This change adds a guard that detects when the Welcome tab was selected automatically after closing a library and instead selects the next available tab.

What I changed

- Added a check in the tab-selection logic to avoid automatically selecting the Welcome tab when a neighboring library tab is closed; the next tab is selected in that case.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to note the visible behavior change.

Why this is needed

Without this check, users with multiple libraries open could lose visibility of a library by closing the tab immediately to the right of the Welcome tab. The fix ensures the UI chooses a sensible next tab and prevents accidental hiding of libraries.

Manual testing

- Reproduced the original issue (two libraries + Welcome tab open; close the tab directly to the right of Welcome) and verified the library no longer disappears.
- Verified normal tab closing behavior in other configurations still works as expected.

Checklist

- [x] I license my changes under the MIT license
- [x] CHANGELOG.md updated
- [/] Tests: not applicable / not added
- [x] Manually tested in running JabRef
- [x] Developer and user documentation checked/updated where applicable

How to verify (QA)

1. Open the Welcome tab and two libraries (so tabs order is: Welcome, Library A, Library B).
2. Close Library A (the tab directly to the right of Welcome).
3. Confirm Library B remains visible and no library is hidden; the next tab should be selected instead of falling back to Welcome.

Notes

No behavioral changes beyond the tab selection during close were introduced. If you want, I can add an automated UI test to cover this scenario in a follow-up PR.

text:
Late initialization of context menus to reduce memory usage and improve performance

Summary
- Defers creation of entry-editor context menus until they are actually needed (on first right-click) by using java.util.function.Supplier.
- This avoids instantiating identical small menus for every visible text field while scrolling, reducing allocations and runtime overhead.

What changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/EditorTextArea.java
  - addToContextMenu now accepts a Supplier<List<MenuItem>> and populates the context menu lazily in TextAreaSkin.populateContextMenu.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/contextmenu/EditorMenus.java
  - Menu factory methods (getDefaultMenu, getNameMenu, getDOIMenu) now return Supplier<List<MenuItem>> that build the menu on demand.\u0000
  - Added documentation explaining the lazy-instantiation approach.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/IdentifierEditor.java
  - Updated usage to pass the Suppliers returned by EditorMenus to textArea.addToContextMenu.
- build.gradle
  - Bumped checkstyle toolVersion from 8.0 to 8.3 (allows using {@link ...} in doc comments without checkstyle errors).
- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added an entry describing the late initialization of context menus (PR #3340).

Motivation and impact
- Based on profiling (see issue #3335), eagerly creating context menus for every visible editor field produced significant memory allocations and some CPU overhead when browsing entries.
- By postponing menu creation until the user actually opens a menu, the memory/perf impact while scrolling is essentially eliminated.
- The change is internal to the entry editor; callers that previously passed a List<MenuItem> to addToContextMenu must now pass a Supplier<List<MenuItem>>. All internal usages have been updated in this PR.

Testing
- Manually tested; profiling showed substantial reduction in memory allocations and smaller performance impact when scrolling through entries.

Related
- Issue: #3335
- This PR: #3340

Fixes #8954 — Show number of total citations (times an entry is referenced) fetched from CrossRef

Summary
- Add a new standard field Referencedbycount to store the number of times an item has been referenced by other works.
- Update the CrossRef fetcher to prefer DOI when present for lookups and to extract the CrossRef "is-referenced-by-count" value into the new Referencedbycount field.
- Add and adapt tests to cover the new field and ensure we parse a numeric referenced-by count (tests check the value is present and >= 0).
- Update CHANGELOG.md to document the feature.

What changed (files)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/field/StandardField.java
  - Added REFERENCEDBYCOUNT("Referencedbycount", FieldProperty.NUMERIC).
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/CrossRef.java
  - If DOI is present on the entry, build the CrossRef API path using /works/{doi}.
  - Read item.optString("is-referenced-by-count") from the CrossRef JSON and store it in StandardField.REFERENCEDBYCOUNT.
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/CrossRefTest.java
  - Tests updated to include Referencedbycount in fixtures, and a new test (findTimesExternallyCited) asserts the fetched referenced-by count is >= 0.
- CHANGELOG.md
  - Document the new Referencedbycount field and changes to the CrossRef fetcher.

Notes and future work
- Currently the new field appears under Other fields in the entry editor. Testing
- Unit tests added/updated to ensure parsing and presence of Referencedbycount.
- Feature tested manually in a running instance of JabRef (screenshot included in the issue/PR description).

Introduce a modern Keywords editor and improve keyword model/serialization

This PR implements a new keyword editing UI and supporting view-model + model improvements:

  - Uses com.dlsc.gemsfx.TagsField to render keywords as tag chips with autocomplete suggestions

- Support hierarchical keywords and consistent serialization according to user preferences

Notes
- The new editor uses existing suggestion infrastructure (SuggestionProviders / ContentSelectorSuggestionProvider) so existing autocompletion & content selector entries are available as suggestions.

  - Adds the langchain4j dependency (dev.langchain4j:langchain4j:0.36.2) required for the AI service.

- AiService lifecycle: created at application init, registered in the Injector and closed at application shutdown to avoid resource leaks.

Switch the documentation translation and publishing workflow to use Crowdin. This change centralizes translation management, automates sync between source and translated docs, and replaces the previous manual/localization pipeline.

What changed:
- Added Crowdin configuration and metadata (crowdin.yml and helper scripts).
- Updated README/CONTRIBUTING to document the new translation workflow and how translators should contribute via Crowdin.
- Added GitHub Actions steps (or modified CI) to upload source strings and download translations automatically.
- Removed legacy localization scripts and references to the old workflow.
- Updated .gitignore/other repo files as needed for Crowdin tooling artifacts.

Files of interest:
- crowdin.yml (Crowdin project config)
- .github/workflows/* (CI changes to sync with Crowdin)
- docs/ or i18n/ updates (where source/translated files are organized)
- CONTRIBUTING.md / README.md (workflow documentation)
- scripts/crowdin-* (helper scripts for manual sync)

1. Verify CI passes and the new workflow actions run (upload/download steps should complete without errors).
2. Run the provided helper script locally to simulate an upload or download (see CONTRIBUTING for commands).
3. Build the docs site locally to confirm translated files compile and links are correct.
4. Spot-check several translated pages to confirm string formatting and placeholders are preserved.

- A Crowdin project must be configured and API key added to repository secrets (CROWDIN_API_KEY or similar). See CONTRIBUTING for exact secret name.
- Run an initial sync to import existing source strings and push current translations into Crowdin.
- Remove or archive the old localization service/configuration after the first successful migration.

Impact:
- Translators should now use the Crowdin web UI or Crowdin CLI as described in CONTRIBUTING.
- PRs with translation updates will be managed via Crowdin syncs rather than direct repo edits (unless intentionally bypassing Crowdin).

Notes:
- Ensure repository secrets are configured before enabling CI sync to avoid failed runs.
- Review Crowdin project settings (branch, file patterns, excluded files) to match this repo's structure.

- Represents a group node with displayName (LaTeX -> Unicode), icon, color, children and hit count.

text:
Introduce platform-specific NativeDesktop implementations and a DefaultDesktop fallback

This PR adds/organizes OS-specific desktop integration for file and folder opening, console launching, and directory detection.

Key changes:
- DefaultDesktop
  - Fallback implementation for platforms other than Linux/Windows/macOS.
  - Uses java.awt.Desktop for openFile/openFileWithApplication/openFolderAndSelectFile.
  - openConsole logs an error because consoles are not supported in the generic implementation.
  - getDefaultFileChooserDirectory returns the user home; getApplicationDirectory returns the user directory.

- Linux
  - Uses ExternalFileTypes and user preferences to open files with a configured viewer or falls back to nativeOpenFile.
  - nativeOpenFile tries Desktop integration first, and falls back to xdg-open.
  - openFileWithApplication uses a provided application command or nativeOpenFile otherwise.
  - openFolderAndSelectFile uses DESKTOP_SESSION to choose an appropriate file manager (nautilus, dolphin, caja, nemo or xdg-open).
  - openConsole detects /etc/alternatives/x-terminal-emulator (readlink) and maps known terminal emulators (gnome-terminal, xfce4-terminal, konsole) to start terminals with the working directory; shows an error dialog if not found.
  - Uses JabRefExecutorService and StreamGobbler to handle process IO asynchronously.
  - getDefaultFileChooserDirectory respects XDG_DOCUMENTS_DIR with fallback to ~/Documents.

- OSX
  - Uses /usr/bin/open to open files and folders; supports opening with a specific application using "-a".
  - openFolderAndSelectFile uses "open -R" to reveal files in Finder.
  - openConsole launches Terminal using "open -a Terminal".
  - getApplicationDirectory returns /Applications and default chooser directory is ~/Documents.

- Windows
  - openFile uses explorer.exe to open (or configured application via ExternalFileTypes).
  - openFolderAndSelectFile uses explorer.exe /select, to highlight files.
  - openConsole starts cmd.exe in the given directory via "start".
  - detectProgramPath searches ProgramFiles(x86) and ProgramFiles for the requested executable (appending .exe).
  - getDefaultFileChooserDirectory uses JNA (KnownFolders / Shell32Util) to fetch the Documents folder and falls back to user.home with logging on error.
  - openFileWithApplication launches the specified application with the file as argument.

Notes:
- Several classes avoid static logger instances because logger configuration is performed in Launcher.addLogToDisk; loggers are obtained via LoggerFactory when needed.
- Methods interacting with external processes consume their streams via StreamGobbler and are executed on JabRefExecutorService to avoid blocking the UI thread.
- Use of @AllowedToUseAwt annotations where AWT integration is required.

This improves cross-platform behavior for opening files, folders, and consoles and centralizes platform-specific logic in dedicated classes.

Only show the recovery dialog for .sav autosave files when the .sav actually contains different content than the original .bib file. This prevents JabRef from nagging users on restart when an identical .sav file exists (e.g. after a forced shutdown without changes).

- BackupManager

  - Introduced AUTOSAVE_FILE_EXTENSION constant (".sav") and updated getBackupPath accordingly.
  - If the backup is missing or a directory -> returns false (no dialog). If an IOException occurs during comparison -> returns true (safe default to alert the user).

  - Updated calls to use BackupManager.backupFileDiffers(...) instead of the old checkForBackupFile(...). This affects opening last edited databases, database opening action (OpenDatabaseAction), and related flow.

- Tests and test resources
  - Added unit tests to cover the new behavior: no-autosave (missing .sav), no-changes (identical .sav), and changes (different .sav). Also renamed a test for clarity.

Summary
Fix capitalization for words that contain any dash characters so each dashed segment is capitalized correctly.

What I changed
- Updated the capitalization logic to recognize any dash/punctuation used as a separator (not just the ASCII hyphen) and to capitalize each segment between dashes independently.
- Preserved the original dash characters and spacing when rejoining segments.
- Added unit tests covering single hyphens, multiple hyphens, leading/trailing dashes, and Unicode dash characters (en-dash, em-dash, etc.).

Why
Previously the algorithm failed to properly capitalize segments in dashed words (especially with multiple or non-ASCII dashes), resulting in incorrectly cased text. This change ensures titlecasing behavior is consistent for all dash-separated words.

Compatibility
This is a non-breaking change that improves correctness. No public API changes; existing behavior for non-dashed words is unchanged.

Tests
New tests were added to cover varied dash scenarios and ensure idempotency when running the capitalization function multiple times.

text:
Fixes #2336 — ensure BackupManager shuts down correctly and allow JabRef to quit.

Summary
- BackupManager now registers itself as a listener in its constructor and is always initialized when started. This fixes a case where it was not registered and prevented proper shutdown (resolves issue #2336).
- The backup workflow was refactored: the backup task is now a single Runnable that determines the backup path on demand and performs the save. The ExecutorService/worker queue creation and task submission logic were simplified and encapsulated.
- BackupManager now computes the backup path from the current database path (getDatabasePath) and only performs backups when a path is present. Backup file deletion on shutdown is centralized in deleteBackupFile.
- The static shutdown routine now reliably unregisters and removes running instances.

Other changes
- BibDatabaseContext: added getDatabasePath() returning Optional<Path> and deprecated getDatabaseFile().
- JabRefFrame: BackupManager.start(...) is always invoked when a tab is added (previous conditional was removed so BackupManager can register itself immediately).
- Minor refactorings and cleanup (imports, method reorganizations).
- CHANGELOG updated to mention the fix.

Impact
- Fixes quitting behavior by ensuring backup manager instances are properly registered and shut down, and backup files are removed when closing databases.
- Backwards-compatible API: getDatabaseFile() is deprecated in favor of getDatabasePath().

Notes
- Behavior: a BackupManager is created for each context and will only write backups when the database path is available. Threading/rejection behavior for redundant backup tasks is preserved.

text:
Add copy and reporting features to the Event Log (Error Console)

This PR enhances the Error Console UI and view model to make it easier to copy log content and report issues:

- UI (ErrorConsoleView.java)
  - Added a context menu on each log message cell with a "Copy" action to copy the detailed text of a single log entry.

  - Implemented reportIssue() to prepare system + reproduction + log details, copy the details to the clipboard and open a pre-filled GitHub issue page in the browser.
  - Added safe handling for empty selections and notification popups when copying/reporting.

Why
- Makes it trivial for users to copy relevant log entries for diagnostics, paste them into issues or support channels, and quickly create GitHub issues with the required context.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/errorconsole/ErrorConsoleView.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/errorconsole/ErrorConsoleViewModel.java

Behavior notes:
- Selecting multiple entries and pressing the configured copy shortcut will copy the combined detailed text of the selected entries.
- Using the cell context menu copies a single entry's detailed text.
- "Create issue" copies log details to the clipboard and opens the new-issue page on GitHub; the dialog instructs users to paste the log into the issue body.
