text:
Add comprehensive unit test suite covering core logic and shared components

This PR introduces a large set of unit tests that exercise and validate behavior across multiple modules of the project. No production code changes are included — these tests improve coverage and guard against regressions in parsing, formatting, cleanup, XMP handling, database management and synchronization logic.

Highlights
- bibtex key pattern (BibtexKeyPatternUtilTest)
  - Extensive tests for author-name handling (first/last author, von parts, initials, et al. behaviour, multiple authors)
  - Tests for title handling (veryShortTitle, shortTitle, camel-casing, significant-word capitalization)
  - Tests for keyword extraction and modifiers
  - Many accent and special-latex-character normalization tests, plus checkLegalKey behavior with/without enforcement
  - Page and prefix parsing, first/last page extraction
  - Null/empty input edge cases and exception expectations

- cleanup worker (CleanupWorkerTest)
  - Tests for cleaning and migrating file links (pdf/ps->file), moving files, making paths relative, renaming PDFs
  - DOI cleaning (strip http prefix) and moving DOIs from url field to doi field
  - Field formatter cleanups: normalize month, normalize pages, normalize date
  - HTML/units/latex cleanup formatters and ProtectTerms behavior (ProtectedTermsLoader)
  - Merge of consecutive LaTeX math environments and conversion to biblatex fields
  - Behavior when field formatters are disabled
  - Validation of returned FieldChange lists where applicable

- XMP utilities (XMPUtilTest)
  - Reading and writing XMP metadata to PDF (including raw XMP), round-trip equality checks
  - UTF-8 handling and XML escaping, newline and tab whitespace preservation for certain fields
  - Privacy filter tests to ensure fields are removed according to configuration
  - Tests for Dublin Core and DocumentInformation updates, DC reading/writing, and converting to/from BibEntry
  - Tests verifying read/write for multiple entries and command-line client behavior (XMPUtilMain)
  - Tests for protected (write-protected) PDFs and proper exception behavior with encrypted PDFs
  - Low-level tests reading/writing of metadata streams and schema checks

- core database model (BibDatabaseTest)
  - Tests for entry insertion/removal and duplicate-id/key handling (KeyCollisionException expectations)
  - String (BibtexString) management, resolving #string# constructs, handling circular references
  - Events for insert/remove/change (TestEventListener) and duplication checker counts
  - getUsedStrings helper and preamble handling

- author parsing & formatting (AuthorListTest)
  - Many name parsing scenarios: first/last name order, commas, jr/von parts, braces, hyphens, initials and abbreviation options
  - Formatting for natbib, alphabetization, last-only, last-first, first-first representations and edge cases
  - Caching behavior, handling of company/group authors and relax/braced names
  - Validations of getAuthor, size, isEmpty and expected exceptions on invalid access

- shared DBMS & synchronization (DBMSProcessorTest, DBMSSynchronizerTest, SynchronizationTestSimulator)
  - Parameterized tests across DBMS types (via TestManager) covering setup/teardown, integrity checks and reinitialization
  - Tests for insert/update/remove of shared entries, versioning and optimistic offline-lock behavior (OfflineLockException expected cases)
  - Retrieval of shared entries, metadata get/set, and mapping of shared ID/version
  - Synchronizer tests to ensure local DB sync, event-driven updates and metadata application (save actions)
  - Simulator tests to emulate multiple clients: insertion/update/deletion flows, pull changes and conflict detection

Testing approach
- Uses JUnit 4 tests, Mockito for preferences and mocks where suitable, TemporaryFolder for filesystem isolation, and PDFBox for PDF metadata manipulation.
- Many tests assert both state changes and returned change lists to ensure callers can react correctly.

Why this matters
- These tests lock down complex parsing/formatting logic and shared-database synchronization patterns that are error-prone and critical to correctness.
- They help prevent regressions when refactoring parsing code, metadata handling (XMP), cleanup routines, and DBMS synchronization behavior.

If you want to run the tests locally
- Most tests use standard Maven/JUnit tooling. Some tests are categorized as DatabaseTests and require configured test DBMS instances available to TestManager.
- Tests that operate on PDFs use temporary files and rely on PDFBox; please ensure the environment permits file creation.

Fixes https://github.com/koppor/jabref/issues/577

What this PR does
- Ensures subgroups are placed according to the current alphabetical ordering rules. Subgroups are now inserted/positioned relative to their sibling groups based on the active alphabetical comparison instead of keeping their previous absolute position.
- Implements automatic resorting when a group's name changes so that renaming a group immediately moves it (and its subgroups) to the correct alphabetical place.

Why
- Previously subgroups could end up in the wrong position when alphabetical sorting of groups was used or when a group was renamed. This led to inconsistent ordering in the group tree and surprising behavior for users expecting strict alphabetical ordering.

Other changes
- CHANGELOG.md updated with a user-friendly description of the change.
- Unit tests added to cover subgroup placement and the resorting behavior on rename.
- Manual testing performed in a running JabRef build.
- Screenshots demonstrating the behavior have been included in the PR.
- Developer and user documentation reviewed; relevant documentation issues were created/updated where needed.

Notes for reviewers
- Focus review on the code that determines insertion/placement of group nodes and the renaming flow that triggers resorting.
- The change is backward compatible and requires no migration of user data or settings.

text:
Fixes #9908 — Avoid initializing static Logger instances before tinylog configuration

What I changed
- Replaced static Logger fields with on-demand LoggerFactory.getLogger(...) calls across desktop OS classes to avoid emitting log entries during class initialization.
- Updated usages in DefaultDesktop, Linux, OSX and Windows to obtain loggers at call sites instead of storing a static logger field.
- Adjusted StreamGobbler callbacks to use LoggerFactory.getLogger(Class)::debug where needed and pass exceptions to warn() calls to preserve stack traces.
- Added import references to org.jabref.cli.Launcher and class-level Javadoc explaining why static loggers are not allowed (tinylog becomes immutable once the first log entry is issued via Launcher#addLogToDisk).

Why
- tinylog configuration is applied in Launcher#addLogToDisk and becomes immutable once the first log entry is written. Having static Logger instances can cause logging to be initialized too early, preventing log configuration from being applied. Moving to on-demand logger retrieval defers logger creation until after configuration, ensuring correct logging behavior.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/desktop/os/DefaultDesktop.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/desktop/os/Linux.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/desktop/os/OSX.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/desktop/os/Windows.java

- Functionality remains the same; this change only affects logger initialization timing and preserves expected logging configuration. No user-visible behavior changes expected.

text:
Summary

Add a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow that runs a markdown link checker once a month to detect broken external links in the repository documentation.

Why

The repo contains many Markdown (.md) documentation files that link to external resources. Running link checks on every PR is noisy and interferes with normal development (see issue #6677). To balance notification of broken links with minimal disruption, we run the check on a monthly schedule.

What this PR does

- Adds a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow that runs markdown-link-check on the repository Markdown files once per month.
- Adds configuration for the link checker (ignore list / settings) to avoid known false positives (e.g., GitHub.com returns forbidden) and to make the check practical.

Behavior and rationale

- The monthly schedule prevents the check from slowing or failing normal PR workflows while still providing automated notification of broken external links.
- When the checker finds broken links it will surface them in the workflow run (and can be configured to create an issue or send notifications, depending on repository settings).

Known limitations and future work

- Some external sites (for example GitHub pages or sites that block automated requests) may be reported as broken; these are added to the ignore list as necessary. See the workflow/config for current exclusions.
- A more fine-grained filter of response statuses (to better handle sites returning non-200 codes like 403) is desirable but depends on upstream tool improvements.

Files added/changed

- .github/workflows/check-external-links.yml (scheduled monthly workflow)
- .github/markdown-link-check.json (configuration for the link checker; ignore patterns)

Notes for maintainers

- If a legitimate link is reported as broken, either update the link in the docs or add the URL (or pattern) to the ignore list in the checker config with a short justification.
- This change is intended to improve documentation quality while avoiding disruption of day-to-day development.

Checklist

- [ ] Change in CHANGELOG.md described (if applicable)
- [ ] Tests created for changes (if applicable)
- [ ] Manually tested changed features in running JabRef (always required)
- [ ] Screenshots added in PR description (for UI changes)
- [ ] Documentation checked/updated where necessary

Summary

- Fix BibTeX key parsing and integrity checks to correctly handle a wider range of valid key characters and to avoid false-positive integrity warnings.

What changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/BibtexParser.java
  - Improved parsing logic for BibTeX entry keys so that keys with certain punctuation/characters are handled consistently and leading/trailing whitespace is trimmed reliably.
  - Fixed edge cases where malformed or unusual key tokens were mis-parsed.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/integrity/BibtexKeyChecker.java
  - Relaxed/adjusted validation rules to accept the intended set of valid key characters and to produce clearer messages for invalid keys.
  - Avoids incorrectly flagging valid keys as invalid and improves detection of truly malformed keys.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/integrity/IntegrityCheck.java
  - Standardized integrity check message formatting and severity assignment so that key-related problems are reported consistently in the UI/API.
  - Minor refactor to centralize message creation for better maintainability.

- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/BibtexParserTest.java
  - Added/updated unit tests covering the updated parsing behavior and key validation rules, ensuring previously failing cases are now handled correctly.

Why

- Users reported incorrect parsing/validation of some BibTeX keys which led to false warnings and, in some cases, duplicate-key handling problems. These changes ensure BibTeX keys are parsed and validated according to the intended rules, reducing false positives and improving reliability when importing/exporting bibliographies.

Tests

- Updated unit tests to cover multiple key formats and edge cases; all tests now pass locally.

Compatibility

- This is a backwards-compatible bugfix and tightening of validation rules. Existing valid keys should continue to be accepted; keys that were previously incorrectly accepted as valid may now be flagged if they are truly malformed.

Notes

- No user-facing API changes beyond clearer integrity messages and more accurate validation results.

Summary

This PR implements support for running and managing a PostgreSQL-based metadata backend and includes related refactorings and build/module updates.

Key changes

- Add embedded PostgreSQL lifecycle and cleanup
  - jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/search/PostgreServer.java: New logic to start, stop and monitor a local PostgreSQL server instance used for metadata storage.
  - jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/search/PostgreProcessCleaner.java: Ensures spawned PostgreSQL processes are cleaned up on exit or in failure scenarios to avoid orphaned DB processes.

- Add Postgres metadata writer
  - jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/search/PostgresMetadataWriter.java: Implements writing/reading application metadata to/from the PostgreSQL store.

- Refactor directory handling for DB data and app files
  - jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/Directories.java: Updated to expose and compute appropriate application data directories used by the PostgreSQL instance and other app components.

- Launcher integration
  - jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/Launcher.java: Updated to initialize and shut down the PostgreSQL server as part of application startup/shutdown when configured to use the Postgres metadata backend.

- Module and build updates
  - jablib/src/main/java/module-info.java: Module declarations updated to export/require packages needed by the new postgres-related classes and to satisfy module visibility/reflection needs.
  - jablib/build.gradle.kts: Build configuration adjusted to include the new code and any required dependencies for the embedded PostgreSQL support.

- Changelog
  - CHANGELOG.md: Document the new feature and notable changes for this release.

Migration and operational notes

- If you enable the PostgreSQL metadata backend, the application will attempt to create and manage a local PostgreSQL data directory. The location is determined by the updated Directories utility — check your configuration or data directory if you rely on a custom path.
- The launcher will start the embedded server automatically when configured; the PostgreProcessCleaner ensures PostgreSQL processes are terminated properly on exit.
- Module declarations were updated; third-party tooling that relies on module boundaries or reflection may need corresponding adjustments.

This change lays the groundwork for reliable Postgres-backed metadata storage and safer process management for bundled PostgreSQL instances.

text:
If a file is changed externally, JabRef is doing a 3-way merge between the last saved value vs current value in JabRef vs new value in file.
The way this is done is by first comparing the last saved file with the current (changed) file, and then trying to find additional/other changes in the currently open database. This is really complex and I believe there is some subtle bug in the logic leading to #5257.

With this PR, the change scanner is changed to a to simple 2-way merge between the current value in JabRef vs new value in file. This is way simpler and I hope this PR fixes #5257.
In a few edge cases, the 2-way merge has a small disadvantage. For example, consider the following steps:
- User A opens file
- User A changes field `Author` to `User A` and adds field `Title` with value `new`
- User B opens file
- User B changes field `Author` to `User B`
- User B saves file

At this point, User A gets a message that the file changed with the following changes:
- field `Author` changed from `User A` to `User B`
- field `Title` was removed

The 3-way merge could detect that `Title` was newly added, and thus could automatically reapply this change.  This is no longer possible with the simple 2-way merge.

This fixes #1450 

After changing the preferences the mainTable is using a new `SplitPane` object to divide table and `EntryEditor` - in the course of creating the actual table existing entryEditors are closed which causes a saving of the current `EntryEditor` height in the prefs. As this is calculated based on the (already new) `SplitPane` a wrong value "1" is stored.

To prevent this the previous state of the divider for the SplitPane is restored based on the prefs before the mainTable is recreated.

For the error console, I took the suggestion https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/2667#issuecomment-288742546 by @matthiasgeiger. The freezing after a Swing message occurred since 
̀`LOGGER.warn("No localized message exception message defined. Falling back to getMessage().");`
lead to recursive calls (actually, Log4j has some logic to prevent deadlocks but these don't take effect since the original message is thrown in the Swing thread, while the above "no localized messsage" is posted in the JavaFX thread.). Fixes #8446 

### Problem
After a fresh start; selecting an entry for the first time causes a small freeze of ~3-4 seconds. In short, the freeze occurs when creating a new WebView instance for the preview panel.

### Solution
My solution is to preload a number of WebView instances at startup *(4 instances for now)*. To ensure the preload has no effect on startup performance, I wrapped the web view construction code in `Platform.runLater()`.
Instances are added dynamically when the number of available instances goes under a certain threshold.

### Alternative Solution
I tried a Proxy design pattern; I used a proxy class for `PreviewViewer`; the proxy builds a `PreviewViewer` instance using a combination of `CompletableFuture<PreviewViewer>` and `Platform.runLater()`, then it redirects method calls to `PreviewViewer` by registering callbacks. However, this solution was complex and hard to implement without altering app behavior. 


https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/21198231/160512108-7e79c206-6d7e-439c-9198-71cacff3da5e.mp4

[ #5428](https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/5428) - Issue this PR solves

Gradle was warning about deprecated feature usage. Logs show jacoco append to be the feature that is deprecated.From my understandind the propery is currently ignored.

Removed the Jacoco append property from build.gradle and builds don't throw any deprecation warnings anymore.

The append property in Jacoco is meant to write to the same coverage file. But as mentioned in this [issue](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/issues/5269) setting it to true broke the build caching capability. So starting Gradle 5.0 a breaking change was introduced where they did away with the append property. The default behavior was set to behave as if append is initially false to enable build caching and then append is set to true before passing to the jacoco agent.
This meant that multiple tasks could not use the same coverage file but Jacoco merge is a feature that let's you achieve the same functionality. The gradle for the project does use Jacoco Merge to merge the various .exec file results, so removing the append property should not break coverage.

This fixes an issue where LaTeX commands (e.g., \mkbibquote{...}) were retained in generated filenames using the [fulltitle] pattern.

### Describe the changes you have made here: what, where, why, ...
- When the filename pattern is set to `[bibtexkey] - [fulltitle]`, and linked files are renamed automatically (e.g., during PDF import or when using "Rename file to pattern"), the class `LinkedFileHandler` calls `FileUtil.createFileNameFromPattern()` to generate the new filename.

- Previously, this method only applied `FileNameCleaner.cleanFileName(targetName)`, which removes illegal characters, but does not strip LaTeX commands such as `\mkbibquote{}`. This led to filenames like: `BrayBuildingCommunity - Building _mkbibquote_Community_.pdf`

- To fix this, I added a call to `RemoveLatexCommandsFormatter.format()` before cleaning the filename. This ensures LaTeX commands are properly stripped, while keeping their inner content.

**Example:**
- Input title: Building \mkbibquote{Community}
- File pattern: [bibtexkey] - [fulltitle]
- Old output: BrayBuildingCommunity - Building _mkbibquote_Community_.pdf
- New output: BrayBuildingCommunity - Building Community.pdf

integration panel. 
Fixes #7454(https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/7454)

      No, tests were not created.  Do you have GUI tests?

      There is a known problem: "Merge citations" does not save the information needed
      to find the optional extra info (like page reference) stored in document properties.
      When reestablishing the individual references in unCombineCiteMarkers,
      getUniqueReferenceMarkName() may or may not return the original name.
      When it does not, the extra info may be lost, or even taken from another entry.

      A solution could be to encode the number making the originals unique
      in the merged name: in stead of  "JR_cite_1_XX2000a,YY2010" it would be e.g.
      "JR_cite_1_XX2000a,1_YY2010". Apart from construction and parsing,
       probably marking (or calulating) the originals as "in use" for getUniqueReferenceMarkName()
       would be needed.

       Another problem: combineCiteMarkers orders the merged entries by year  (I am not sure why).
       The original order is lost.

       In summary, the presented solution, although improves the situation, does not cover
       all aspects.

- [x] Manually tested changed features in running JabRef (always required)
- [x] Screenshots added in PR description (for UI changes)

describing the two problems above (or the original, if the proposed changes are not applied)

  Added test coverage for the `preferences` CLI command following the new testing
  framework introduced in #14164.

  ## Changes
  - Created `PreferencesTest.java` with 3 tests:
    - Test that preferences command without subcommand executes successfully
    - Test that import subcommand fails appropriately when missing required parameters
    - Test that export subcommand fails appropriately when missing required parameters

  ## Motivation
  The CLI testing framework was recently added but many commands still lack test
  coverage. This PR adds tests for the `preferences` command.

  ## Testing
  All tests pass locally:
  ./gradlew :jabkit:test --tests PreferencesTest

This PR improves the performance of the journal abbreviation loader/repository/parser and thus is a partial fix for https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/2966.
Previously, loading and parsing the journal repository files took nearly 10 seconds and now almost nothing:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5037600/28175332-3b59e1da-67f4-11e7-9560-f2a504205c0a.png)
Main boost came from using `equalsIgnoreCase` instead of using `equals(text.toLowerCase())` and changing `LinkedList` to `HashSet` as we don't care about the ordering.
I had to adopt two tests which relied on the sorting.

Moreover, only one copy of the list is now stored in memory opposed to the 1 + 4 maps previously (equates to 1/10 RAM consummation). In principle, this makes the journal auto completion slower but I couldn't notice any negative impact.

Adds ignore parameter to `mimeType` and notify the user if the downloaded file is of HTML type, fixes #7452.
  
In the method `ExternalFileTypes::getExternalFileTypeByMimeType`, we added a feature to remove the parameters part
of the `mimeType`, this is allowed in mimeType-specification [link](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Basics_of_HTTP/MIME_types). The previous code didn't consider the parameter part of the mimeType, thus not conforming to the correct enum type in `StandardExternalFileType.java`.

We also added a feature to notify the user if the downloaded link is a HTML file, via the "status bar", because the user might think they have downloaded a PDF while this isn't the case.

### Description

- Pressing TAB on the last field of a tab now correctly moves the focus to the first field of the next tab in the EntryEditor.

- Added static helper methods in EditorTextField to manage the TAB navigation logic.

### Summary
This PR implements a new **Wiley TDM Fetcher** to enable full-text retrieval from Wiley journals using their official Text and Data Mining (TDM) REST API.

### Changes made
- Added `WileyFetcher.java` under `fetcher/fulltext/`
- Integrated it into `FulltextFetcher.java`
- Verified DOI-based PDF downloads work through the Wiley API
- Ensured compatibility with existing fulltext fetchers (e.g., Springer, IEEE)

### Notes
Wiley full-text PDFs require a valid **TDM API token**, which the fetcher can handle via standard API headers.

### Testing
- Tested with DOI: `10.1002/we.2952` (Wind Energy Journal)
- Fetcher correctly identifies and downloads the associated PDF.

Description:
This PR introduces a validation check for user-entered library paths in the Library Properties dialog. It ensures that only valid paths are accepted (Absolute/ Relative), preventing users from saving incorrect paths.

Changes Made:
Real-time Validation:

- When a user types a path, the system checks whether it is absolute or relative.
- If the path is relative, it is resolved against the database’s current directory (getDatabasePath() in BibDatabaseContext).
- If the path is invalid, an error message is displayed in the UI immediately after typing.
- If the path is empty, no validation issues occur.

Validation on Save:

- When attempting to save, if any path is invalid, an error message is displayed.
- Until a correct path is entered, saving will not be allowed for General Tab.

Issue Fixed:
- Fixes [#11840](https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/11840)
- Prevents users from entering non-existing absolute or relative paths.
- Ensures UI feedback is provided in real time to guide users.

Testing:

- Entered valid/invalid absolute paths and confirmed proper validation.
- Entered valid/invalid relative paths and confirmed resolution against the database directory.
- Verified that saving is only possible when all paths are valid.

Search tests sometimes throw NullPointerException (example: https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/actions/runs/10759644260/job/29836573460).

This issue occurs because multiple tests for the same library share the same index path. The index is closed in a background thread, which may lead to subsequent tests accessing the same index before the previous test closing index finishes.

Although the `org.jabref.gui.util.CurrentThreadTaskExecutor` is used to run background tasks sequentially for tests, a different task executor (`org.jabref.logic.util.HeadlessExecutorService#INSTANCE`) is used for closing the index (due to https://github.com/LoayGhreeb/jabref/issues/6).

- Attempt to resolve the issue by using `@TempDir` for the index path.
- Added `closeAndWait` to wait until the task is finished. Using `@TempDir` only didn't resolve the issue because the next test could start, and `@TempDir` would be removed before the closing task finished.


Follow-up to #11542.
Closes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref-issue-melting-pot/issues/527.

```bibtex
@book{9783110702125,

  URL = {https://www.ebook.de/de/product/41373251/hans_joachim_habermann_frank_leymann_repository.html}
}
```

## Previous discussion about removing several selected groups only delete one of them #8390 
> You are prompted to confirm the deletion of one group. After accepting, this group is deleted, but you are not prompted to delete the other groups.
So, while it seems that several can be removed at the same time, groups can be removed only one by one.

## Proposed solution
Fixes #8390 

- When `removeGroupAndSubgroups()` is called, iterate through all selected groups instead of the group that triggers the event handler.
- Popup a confirmation dialog and confirm if user decides to delete:
    - single group
    - multiple groups (if multiple groups selection)
- assign selectedGroups (which is `ListProperty<GroupNodeViewModel>`) to new array to prevent [forEach skips an element when a previous element is deleted](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/17852412/foreach-skips-an-element-when-a-previous-element-is-deleted)

I believe I could bring down the performance impact of the context menus to a bare minimum. I reported this in https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/3335 and @tobiasdiez provided me with the hint how this could work. Against his suggestion to not overshoot, I decided to prove my point that even those small context menus have a significant impact because things will sum up in the end and those menus are newly instantiated for every visible field in the editor.

The starting point was the current master-branch and profiling it by going through only 50 bib-entries. This means that the context menus are instantiated for the visible text fields. This has an impact on performance and memory and, unfortunately, it is not only a tiny fraction. 

## Memory

Notable are the columns "Objects", which are all objects that are created by this method and underlying sub calls and the overall "Size".

![mem1](http://i.imgur.com/pjBJSlF.png)

With almost 40% of the overall memory size, it's definitely something to look into.

## Performance

The performance is with 8% not so large but still noticeable. 

![perf1](http://i.imgur.com/STSGgNj.png)

## Fixing it

By using the `Supplier` interface, we can move the instantiation to the point where the user actually right-clicks into the field. I debugged this, and it seems to work nice. The outcome was as expected. Since no one actually triggers the context menu by just browsing through the list, it vanished altogether. Here is the used memory with this PR created by exactly scrolling through the 50 entries. First the memory footprint

![mem2](http://i.imgur.com/dRrKaxs.png)

and here the performance impact

![perf2](http://i.imgur.com/HgJNhLl.png)

In conclusion, this means as long as the user doesn't need a context menu, we have no memory or performance impact at all.

## Note

I updated the `checkstyle` version in the Gradle built. I like to write comments, and now it doesn't prevent me any longer from using `{@link ...}` in doc-comments to classes that are otherwise not used.

Workaround for #796.
When an undo with multiple entries is undone, each entry is undone one at a time. The Problem herein lies, that when the first entry is undone, the insertion in the database triggers the creation and insertion of an NamedCompund into the UndoManager which kills the main Undo (the one with the multiple entries), which result in just one entry being undone.

With this Workaround each entry has its own NamedCompund which solves the Problem but the user has to call the UndoAction several times (Ctrl-Z for each entry).

# Test external links in documentation

## Context and Problem Statement

The JabRef repository contains Markdown (`.md`) files documenting the JabRef code.
The documentation contains links to external resources.
For high-quality documentation, external links should be working.

Currently we check at each PR (option 2 below), but that is annoying. See https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/6677.

## Decision Drivers

* Checking external links should not cause issues in the normal workflow

## Considered Options

* Check external links once a month
* Check external links in the "checkstyle" task
* Do not check external links

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: "\[option 1\]", because \[justification. e.g., only option, which meets k.o. criterion decision driver \| which resolves force force \| … \| comes out best \(see below\)\].

### Positive Consequences

* Automatic notification of broken external links

### Negative Consequences

* Some external sites need to [be disabled](https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/6542/files). For isntance, GitHub.com always returns "forbidden". A [filter for status is future work of the used tool](https://github.com/tcort/markdown-link-check/issues/94#issuecomment-634947466).

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### Check external links once a month

* Good, because does not interfer with the normal development workflow
* Bad, because an additional workflow is required

### Check external links in the "checkstyle" task

* Good, because no seperate workflow is required
* Bad, because checks fail independent of the PR (because external web sites can go down and go up independent of a PR)

### Do not check external links

* Good, because no testing at all is required
* Bad, because external links break without any notice
* Bad, because external links have to be checked manually

Fixes #9953 

The "working directory" arguments to "gnome-terminal" and "konsole" were incorrect due to slight mis-use of ProcessBuilder, which meant they were badly formed and the terminal loaded in a default directory (most likely the user's home dir).

There are currently no tests at all for any of this functionality at a low-level (i.e., what operating system commands are called and with what args), nor any OS-specific test filtering, etc... probably because it is significant and complex to assert a running terminal's directory, especially from a unit test. Therefore, I have intentionally not attempted to add a test because doing so would require considerable refactoring of existing tests (OpenConsoleActionTest), with not much benefit -- and it still might not be possible to truly prove a terminal opens in a particular directory anyway.

Solution proposal for #4854 

In `FindFullTextAction`, `Task` is now used instead of `BackgroundTask` to be able to show a progress dialog which shows the progress for searching files online.

![lookupDialog](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/24212145/55612578-cabc0800-5788-11e9-92b4-ec4081977b7d.PNG)

Furthermore, the functionality for downloading a file in `LinkedFileViewModel` is split into `download` and `prepareDownloadTask` to be able to define a custom onSucess-action for the background task. This is used in `FindFullTextAction` to add the downloaded file to the entry instead of the URL.

The functionality provided by `LinkedFileViewModel.dowload` remains as it is, so it does not affect the download of a single file via the EntryEditor.

To fix this, we reverted to the original behavior where the method attempts to pull from a remote (if configured), but silently ignores errors when no remote is present. This preserves compatibility with local-only workflows (like the SLR module).

Closes #14237
<!-- LINK THE ISSUE WITH THE "Closes" KEYWORD. -->

I fixed an issue where keyboard shortcuts could not be edited in:
Preferences → Keyboard shortcuts.

The KeyEvent was being consumed by global application shortcuts before reaching
the shortcut editor in the KeyBindingsTab. As a result, pressing keys did not
update the selected shortcut, and changes were not persisted.

This PR adds:
- A key event filter in KeyBindingsTab to ensure the TreeTableView receives key presses.
- Logic to forward the event to the ViewModel (setNewBindingForCurrent).
- Correct persistence of edited shortcuts by syncing the repository into GuiPreferences.
- An updated JUnit test verifying the binding update behavior.

---

### Steps to test

1. Open JabRef → Preferences → Keyboard shortcuts.
2. Select any shortcut entry (e.g., “Close library”).
3. Press a new key combination (e.g., Ctrl+Shift+L).
4. Click **Save**.
5. Restart JabRef.
6. Verify that:
   - The new shortcut appears in the list.
   - The shortcut works in the application (e.g., Ctrl+Shift+L closes the library).

Screenshots visible changes are not required since UI remains the same.

text: Closes #12233 ## Description (UPDATED) As it was pre-requested, I've implemented an option when user is able, using checkbox, to change the formation of the `AI Summary`. If user checks it, `WebView` with formatted into `html` markdown appears, otherwise text stays raw. It is pretty useful new feature that makes `AI Summary` user-friendly for those, who loves to see formatted text, instead of raw `markdown` that besides the text contains "weird", in user's opinion characters. ## How Code Changed and Why? 1. In the issue discussion, I asked questions, and maintainers came up with an idea that we need a simple toggle, so I decided to add into `org/jabref/gui/ai/components/summary/SummaryShowingComponent.fxml` a `CheckBox` that appears one the left below the `AI Summary` 2. This toggle handled in `org/jabref/gui/ai/components/summary/SummaryShowingComponent.java`file's method `onMarkdownToggle()`. Once user checks the `CheckBox` the `TextArea` disappears, and `WebView` come us. 3. `TextArea` was wrapped in `StackPane` to simplify managing and layering of that component. 4. `WebView` programmatically implemented (lazy initialization) to avoid `findMissingLocalizationKeys` and `findObsoleteLocalizationKeys` tests failure. 5. To formate raw text into markdown I used `org/jabref/logic/layout/format/MarkdownFormatter.java` that has been already implemented. ## How to Copy Formatted Content? Press anywhere in `WebView` component press `ctrl + a`/`cmd + a` then `ctrl + c`/`cmd + c`, and paste it in the desired place ^_^ ## Screenshots - Markdown `CheckBox` checked: - Markdown `CheckBox` unchecked: ### Mandatory checks - [ ] I own the copyright of the code submitted and I licence it under the [MIT license](https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/blob/main/LICENSE) - [x] Change in `CHANGELOG.md` described in a way that is understandable for the average user (if change is visible to the user) - [ ] Tests created for changes (if applicable) - [x] Manually tested changed features in running JabRef (always required) - [x] Screenshots added in PR description (for UI changes) - [x] [Checked developer's documentation](https://devdocs.jabref.org/): Is the information available and up to date?
